reviews.title: Excellent Product.
reviews.body: Excellent Earbuds. This is a long-term review. I purchased this brand back in 2023. I have been using them daily for three years at work and at home. I have experienced no problems with them whatsoever. I just purchased a pair Apple AirPods 4 on Amazon with noise canceling, etc. I’m no audio expert, but I did a side-by-side comparison with the music I listen to and these sound just as good as my Apple AirPods 4. I have had no problem with charging, dropped calls or music or either one of the earbuds cutting out. Nor have I’ve heard any static. The sound on these is just as good as the day I bought them. If you need further convincing that these are a great product and a great value, that same year in 2023 at Christmas. I purchased these for my son and a niece and nephew. They all still have their earbuds and they report they still work as well and as good as the day they got them on Christmas Day in 2023. My niece and nephew are in high school and my son is in college. My thinking was if these lasted a year without getting lost or broken, I could still afford to buy them another pair the next Christmas. If you want to test the sound quality of any earbuds or headphones that you purchased listen to the music video by Zara Larson “Ain’t My Fault”. This song has great vocals and a heavy base section and if your headphones or earbuds are garbage, you’re going to be able to tell during this song. I can’t speak to this exact product with all the upgrades in this current version, but I’ve had a great experience with this brand.

reviews.title: Amazing Sound Quality for Listening to Music, and at a Great Price!
reviews.body: Update: So, not even three months after my purchase, the earbuds stop transmitting my voice on phone calls after three to five minutes. I can hear the other party, but they can't hear me. Tried everything I know to fix the issue. They still sound very good for playing music and podcasts, but are useless for extended phone conversations. The Amazon return window has closed, and attempts to contact Jxrev have not been acknowledged. Very disappointed. Initially thought I had found the perfect earbuds, but something broke after a very short time, and no customer support. Initially, I gushed about how great these were, but now, I strongly advise against buying these, based on my disappointing experience. They worked just long enough to get past the Amazon return window, then stopped working. No response from Jxrev, so no after-sale support. Update: Knocked off two stars, may drop another star if I can't find a solution. For unknown reason, the earbuds have stopped working on phone calls after a few minutes. I can hear the other person, but they can't hear me. They work fine for a few minutes, but then suddenly stop transmitting my voice. I've tried every setting I know, can't seem to fix the issue. May well be my phone and not the earbuds (or, more likely, a compatibility issue). Initially, for a few weeks, I had no problems, so something changed. Music sound quality is still top-notch, but occasionally have the same connection issue. Usually stopping and restarting the music player app fixes the issue. But the drop on phone calls seems to be every call now. Still looking for a solution, but they aren't working for me for phone calls. Jxrev J53 Wireless Earbuds: I had bought the (prior) J51 model for a ridiculously low price (Black Friday deal). I liked that so much I was going to buy another but found this newer version, the J53 model. Both have amazing sound quality for listening to music, especially for the (amazingly) inexpensive price. The J53 has an edge on the J51 in several ways. To my ear, the J53 sounds just a bit better, deeper bass, not as bright on the high end and a good balance of sound. The fact that I can say that at all for a sub $20 set of earbuds is amazing. I've tried a number of earbuds, all much higher priced, and returned them all due to poor quality sound listening to mp3 music. (I also have trouble with the kind that press into the ear canal, these sit comfortably in the outer ear.) These really are good. While they aren't 'high fidelity', they sound great. I don't know, but I can't imagine AirPods (or any other overpriced brand) sounding that much better, or worth another $100 or more. Touch controls on the J53 work as advertised (not so much on the J51), though a bit hard to memorize. The (re-charging) case shows how much charge is left as a digital numeric percent (the J51 only has a colored indicator light), and the J53 buds are much easier to remove from the case than the J51. Also can't speak to the phone sound quality on the other end, but I can hear callers just fine, and they seem to be able to hear me just fine. They buds are comfortable, I've worn them for hours while walking or working around the house and I hardly know they're there, except for the crisp music. They stay in place during workouts, so much so that I'm tempted to try them while I swim laps in the pool (haven't got up the nerve...yet, but they are supposed to be waterproof!). As to battery life, I've had them in and playing music for as long as four hours straight and they worked flawlessly, and weren't power drained (not sure yet how long they will play continuously, but at least 4 hours). And, when I put them back in the case, they only took 15% of the remaining case charge to fully re-charge the buds after 4 hours of play. VERY happy with this purchase, I'd say the J53 has the edge on the J51, and, just on music sound quality, both are leaps and bounds above everything else I've tried Great purchase, highly recommend!! I might just buy another set or two as backups, because I haven't found anything even close to the superior sound quality of these, and the price is amazingly affordable. Get 'em while they're still available! These are seriously a great value! They'd be perfect if they added in-ear (or removal) detection and LDAC, the sound quality could probably handle Hi-Res.

reviews.title: Easy to pair and great for calls, but bass is very limited
reviews.body: I picked these up at a really good price and overall there are several things I genuinely like about them. Pairing was quick and easy right out of the case, and the Bluetooth connection has stayed stable without random disconnects so far. The charging case also looks modern and the battery display is a nice feature that makes it easy to check charge levels at a glance. For phone calls, these actually performed better than expected. Voices came through clearly and the microphone quality was solid enough for everyday conversations and work calls. They’re also lightweight and comfortable for longer listening sessions. The biggest downside for me is the sound profile, specifically the bass. I tested multiple songs that normally have deep, rich bass, and it was almost nonexistent. There’s a small amount here and there, but if you enjoy strong low-end sound or listen to bass-heavy music, these may end up feeling a little flat. The highs and mids are decent for casual listening, but the audio overall lacks the fuller sound you get from higher-quality earbuds. At the discounted price, I still think they offer fair value for basic use, especially for calls and podcasts, but music lovers looking for strong bass may want to look elsewhere.

reviews.title: Sehr schöner ausgewogener Sound mit kräftigen Bässen + Angenehm zu tragen
reviews.body: + Soundqualität Das Wichtigste bei jeder Art von Kopfhörern ist natürlich am Ende des Tages immer ihr Klang. Der Sound der Jxrev-TWS-Kopfhörer bewegt sich sehr deutlich ganz am oberen Rand dessen, was man in diesem mittelpreisigen Segment der True-Wireless-Kopfhörer erwarten kann. Die Bässe wummern sehr kräftig und hinterlassen einen spürbaren Schalldruck im Gehörgang, ohne dabei aber die ebenfalls sehr gut wahrnehmbaren Mitten und Höhen zu überdecken. Anhand der Soundqualität könnte man durchaus meinen, TWS-In-Ears einer der großen, bekannteren und teureren Marken in den Ohren zu haben. + Ausstattung und Verarbeitung Bei der Ladeschale ist es geradezu erstaunlich, wie sie derart kompakt ausfallen konnte und dabei zugleich einen ziemlich großen Akku beinhaltet. Das Material und die Verarbeitung wirken tadellos und einwandfrei und die beiden Kopfhörer saugen sich sicher an den Magnetkontakten fest. Das Pairing funktioniert sowohl untereinander als auch mit dem Smartphone oder Laptop stets einwandfrei. + Fazit Es erscheint ziemlich schwierig, für das Geld bessere TWS-Earbuds finden zu wollen.
reviews.body_en: + Sound quality Of course, at the end of the day, the most important thing about any type of headphones is their sound. The sound of the Jxrev TWS headphones is very clearly at the upper end of what you can expect in this mid-priced segment of true wireless headphones. The bass booms very powerfully and leaves a noticeable sound pressure in the ear canal, but without masking the mids and highs, which are also very noticeable. Based on the sound quality, you might think that you are listening to TWS in-ears from one of the larger, better-known and more expensive brands. + Features and workmanship When it comes to the charging cradle, it is almost astonishing how it was able to be so compact and at the same time contain a fairly large battery. The material and workmanship appear flawless and flawless and the two headphones attach securely to the magnetic contacts. The pairing always works perfectly, both with each other and with the smartphone or laptop. + Conclusion It seems pretty difficult to try to find better TWS earbuds for the money.

reviews.title: Works well, until it doesn't
reviews.body: I use this headset daily as I work in construction and it's handy to have 2 so swap one out every day while charging the other. After about 3 weeks one of them completely died. Won't turn on, won't charge, no LED lights of any kind, totally dead. Until that happened I loved the battery life which lasted all day reliably and the sound was good. Just wish it didn't brick itself so fast. Worst part is in order to return it I'd have to send back the other one, which is working, and then since it's a used product the return policy states is likely not get a full refund and replacement wasn't an option. Such a shame. Update 8.26.24 Customer service reached out and offered to make things right by replacing the order or refunding it. I had already ordered the same headset and except for the one that died I have been very satisfied with it so I opted for the refund. They promptly credited back the full amount and I highly recommend this headset now. Solid product and top notch support. Edited to 5 starts!

reviews.title: Good for the price, but quality differs per headphones.
reviews.body: I've had two sets of these now. The older model lasted me 2+ years of heavy and near daily use. I only replaced them when one of the headphone cables finally started cutting out, but I was happy with the cost, battery life, and quality. The second set, which was this newer 'shark' model was a little more disappointing. The audio quality was noticeably worse (way more tinny and lighter on the bass) and the magnets in the ear buds were reversed so they would not keep together and I couldn't stow them. It made it more annoying to bend down and get hit in the eye by the earbuds. I still used them almost daily for hands free calls and general audio, but people I talk to through them do comment that the mic quality is not the best. And now it's been 6 months since I ordered them and one earbud has completely died. I'm torn about ordering a new set. My first set was so good, especially for the price point, that it makes me hope that the second set was just a fluke. On the other hand, the second set is generally disappointing, but the battery life still means I can go several days on a single full charge even when I forget to turn the headphones off and it goes into standby. If you are looking for a cheap set of headphones that can handle some wear, it's hard to beat the price of these. Battery life is great, audio is just okay. Even at it's worse it's mediocre but not bad. The quality of the headphones, in my experience, varies.

reviews.title: UPDATE: SEPT 1, 2023!!! SECOND UNIT HAS FAILED AFTER ONLY 4 WEEKS - JUNK
reviews.body: FIRST UNIT: I COULDN'T GET IT TO TURN ON. I HAD THESE BEFORE WHEN IT WAS MPOW BRAND AND HAD NO TROUBLE. SECOND UNIT - UPDATE: AUG 1, 2023 - THE SELLER "YOSDOM" CONTACTED ME THROUGH AMAZON AND OFFERED TO FIX THE PROBLEM, WHICH THEY DID SATISFACTORILY. IT TOOK A WHILE, BUT IN FACT I DID RECEIVE A REPLACEMENT WHICH WORKS PERFECTLY. THANK YOU TO YOSDOM FOR FOLLOWING UP WITH THESE REVIEWS AND DOING THE RIGHT THING! I WILL VISIT THEIR STORE AGAIN. UPDATE: SEPT 1, 2023 - THIS ITEM HAS WORKED UNTIL YESTERDAY. I HAPPEN TO WALK AWAY FROM MY PHONE (DEVICE THAT THIS HEADSET IS CONNECTED TO) A COUPLE TIMES AND BOTH TIMES THE HEADSET VIBRATED TO LET ME KNOW I WENT OUT OF CONNECTION DISTANCE, WHICH IS GREAT. THE SECOND TIME THIS HAPPENED THOUGH, I WAS NEVER ABLE TO CONNECT TO THE CEVICE AGAIN. I TRIED TO TURN THE HEADSET OFF THEN ON AGAIN, ONLY TO FIND THAT THE HEADSET WAS NOT RESPONDING TO TURN OFF, AND WOULD NOT TURN ON AGAIN EITHER. I ASSUMED THE BATTERY WENT DEAD SO I CHARGED IT OVERNIGHT. THIS MORNING THE RED LIGHT WAS STILL ON WHEN PLUGGED IN. IT NEVER CHARGED, AND I CAN'T GET IT TO TURN ON AT ALL! I FEEL LIKE THERE IS A SERIOUS PROBLEM WITH THE CIRCUITRY OR THE PROGRAMMING OF THE PCB AS THIS UNIT IS BASICALLY DOING THE SAME THING THAT THE FIRST UNIT WAS DOING. SO ESSENTIALLY THIS UNIT IS DEAD AFTER A COUPLE WEEKS. IT HAS SOMETHING TO DO WITH WALKING OUT OF CONNECTION DISTANCE TO THE CONNECTED DEVICE, SEEMS TO MAKE IT VIBRATE TO FAILURE. AGAIN, I'M DISAPPOINTED. I HAD MY MPOW JAWS FOR YEARS!

reviews.title: Fair quality for the price, with a few niggling issues
reviews.body: I've used this style of shark/jaws-style bluetooth headset from a variety of companies since 2018, and this version is my least favorite. The good (compared to other versions): * long battery life * cables feel sturdy The middling: * I'm not a fan of the "fewer-buttons" form factor that was introduced a few years ago. It's a personal thing, but I prefer dedicated volume buttons and separate dedicated track navigation buttons. I've accepted that I've lost that fight at this price point, and pull out my phone whenever I want to rewind, fast-forward, or navigate the track list. I could use the press-and-hold interface to rewind or fast-forward, but each press&hold takes time, especially if I want to shift more than a few seconds. The bad (again, compared to other versions of this headset from other companies): * The "jaws" don't hold the earbuds as well as other versions. The jaws on this version are not as form-fitting as on other versions. A much lighter touch will knock the earbuds out of the jaws, causing them to dangle instead of stay stored away. * The USB-C connection is slightly recessed (normal across all versions), but the size of the indented opening is small. About half my cables can't be inserted correctly because the opening is too small for the protective sheath that's at the end of every USB-C cable. This headset is the only item with this problem - my collection of USB-C cables fit every other device in my house. The supplied cable works, but it's only a foot long.

reviews.title: UPDATED: Newer Version Not as Good
reviews.body: UPDATE 7/2/24: Okay. I'm down to 2 stars. The newest pair of the 10 or so I've tried, lasted from February to July before the left side started to go in and out intermittently. Also, the charging port sucks, the cord will not stay in so you think it is charging and it often just comes loose and isn't. It loses connection for random reasons I don't understand, also it seems the buttons are now super sensitive as my music always gets paused randomly - from my cheek or my neck moving? I think it is time for me to move on from my favorite headphones and I will not be buying another pair. UPDATE 01/17/24: Look, I tried other headphones. I don't want to spend a lot but even if I do, I'm usually not happy. I tried different Bluetooth ones and they fall off my head easily or irritate me. I had a popular brand of one type and was walking through the park one day, and BAM suddenly they were gone! I never even felt them leave my body and I looked everywhere for them. They were decent. At that point, I came crawling back to these headphones. I missed them. I bought them again, and as soon as that high-quality, loud, bass-filled sound hit my ears I was nearly in tears. The long charge. They sit on my neck, noticeably yes, but I know I won't lose them easily either. Stars up again. I just can't quit them. UPDATE 6/10/23: I bought a new set recently, and the newer model seems way worse than the previous one. It constantly disconnects from Bluetooth on its own, has a shorter range than before (two rooms away from music source and loses quality when I could go much further before), and when after charging, sometimes the on and off button doesn't seem to work. I have to plug it in again to get it to work. It also seems to me that the battery doesn't last as long. ************ Original Review for Previous Versions: ******************** I love these headphones so much that I've bought probably 8+ of them over the last 5+ years. But that is just it - they only seem to last about a year or so. To be fair, I wear these headphones almost all day on most days. The magnetic feature of the earbuds typically goes first, and then one side of the headphones always stops working typically. I'm gentle with them. I love how light they are, like a part of my body, and in my opinion, the sound quality is great. The fit is great. I just wish I didn't have to buy new ones every year. Last time I even bought 2 at once to alternate them, hoping they would last a bit longer, but it didn't make much difference. Also, it is hard to know when they're turned off or on (used to love it when it was a switch type button rather than a hold-down type) so often battery will die even quicker.

Meeting audio is crisp, and my coworkers say I sound clear on calls. In terms of comfort, they rival my AirPods Pro, which is fantastic. The only quirk is that they sit in the charging case facing outward, meaning you have to rotate them before putting them in your ears, but that’s a minor adjustment. On the plus side, they connect instantly the moment you open the case, so they're ready to use by the time you put them in. I just wish there was a brief startup chime to confirm the connection. Tap controls work as indicated in the instruction manual (so you'll want to make sure you don't lose it!), but you have to wear/use both earbuds for some functions like increasing or decreasing volume (tapping left decreases, tapping right increases). But being able to gently tap the earbud to play/pause/answer works, once you learn the tap pattern. While the sound quality isn't quite as rich or full-fidelity as AirPods for music, it is perfectly fine for voice calls. If premium, wide-range audio is your top priority, these might disappoint, but they excel for human speech/calls. When paired with my iPhone, there is noticeable sub-second latency with these, so they're terrible when watching videos (audio is out of sync with the video) or playing games, but that's just a warning for buyers if that's something important for you; it's fine for calls/meetings. Charging via USB-C is quick and simple. My favourite feature is the digital battery indicator on the case. It's incredibly handy because you can see exactly how much further you have to go for a full charge. It also takes the guesswork out of knowing when the case's internal battery is running low, so you're never caught off guard by a dead battery. And they last a long time on a charge -- I tested over 5-6 hours listening to podcasts without needing to recharge. Highly recommended for a remote or office setup!

Conclusion : En soi, il est pas mal. Si vous cherchez des Earbuds de bonnes qualités, il reste un bon choix. Il est pratique, les fonctions sont facile à comprendre et assez confortable. reviews.title: Q76 - Un ottimo prodotto
reviews.body: Ho acquistato gli auricolari Rolosar Q76 per usarli durante il jogging: desideravo delle cuffie di qualità che, soprattutto, non si sfilassero dalle orecchie correndo. Secondo me se la cavano benissimo. Come sono fatti Il prodotto è ben confezionato e molto ben costruito; la custodia/base di ricarica funziona perfettamente, senza incertezze, quando si pongono gli auricolari nella culla di ricarica. A sinistra è indicato chiaramente, con un numero, la percentuale di energia residua della batteria di ricarica: a destra, con delle barrette verdi lampeggianti e con il simbolo della batteria, vengono segnalate la quantità di carica residua e lo stato di ciascun auricolare. Nella mia esperienza l'autonomia dichiarata si avvicina moltissimo a quella dichiarata. Quanto sono comodi I due auricolari Q76 sono comodi da indossare: la gomma del supporto che avvolge le orecchie è morbida e non impiccia anche indossando gli occhiali; i gommini in-ear di serie sono disponibili in tre diverse misure, basta scegliere la propria. Usandoli per circa 90/100 minuti per ogni seduta di jogging a me non hanno mai dato fastidio alle orecchie né, alla lunga, si sono rivelati scomodi. Come si usano L'accoppiamento Bluetooth con il cellulare (e anche con il player mp3, come ho fatto io) avviene senza problemi, bastano pochi secondi. Quanto ai controlli, le prime volte in cui ho indossato questi auricolari mi è stato necessario fare pratica per trovare al tatto la zona touch, posta in basso, che permette di controllarli: regolazione del volume, cambio del brano in riproduzione, pausa, risposta alle telefonate ecc. Ma sono bastate poche volte per non avere incertezze. Come funzionano A mio parere l'asso nella manica di questi auricolari bluetooth sport è la qualità del suono: con il player impostato su una curva di riproduzione piatta gli acuti sono brillanti ma mai fastidiosi e le frequenze dei bassi sono a dir poco stupefacenti. Con musica rock e progressive riesco a sentire bassi di una profondità non comune sugli auricolari, in grado di non sfigurare con la riproduzione dalle mie cuffie Grado SR60. Non sono mai invadenti né pompati elettronicamente in stile discoteca. Anche le voci sono ok: presenti e limpide pure nei brani musicalmente più complessi. Onestamente non mi aspettavo un risultato così buono anche se, visto il prezzo (anche scontato) è chiaro che non si tratta di un prodotto basic. Ho apprezzato l'impermeabilità di classe IP7 che si rivela molto utile negli sport – come la corsa - in cui il sudore la fa da padrone; quanto alle telefonate ho trovato efficace la riduzione del rumore Enc, che permette di farmi sentire bene dall'interlocutore senza dover alzare la voce quando mi trovo, per es., in una zona rumorosa. Secondo me A mio parere gli auricolari Rolosar Q76 sono molto ben costruiti e funzionano altrettanto bene: meritano senz'altro cinque stelle. L'unica cosa che mi piacerebbe avessero è la possibilità di ruotare sull'asse verticale le due clip di supporto, quelle che si avvolgono alle orecchie. Infatti, con me, dopo un po' che corro tendono a spostare il gommino in-ear dalla sua posizione ideale, cosa che riduce un poco la profondità dei bassi. Con un paio di cuffie meno fedeli non me ne sarei forse mai accorto. Con queste, invece, le note gravi sono così rotonde e profonde che è un peccato non coglierle in tutte le loro sfumature. Penso che innestando due gommini della misura superiore risolverei, ma preferisco avere nelle orecchie un oggetto che non prema troppo nel condotto auricolare, dunque mi va bene così.
reviews.body_en: I purchased the Rolosar Q76 earphones to use them while jogging: I wanted quality headphones that, above all, did not fall out of my ears while running. In my opinion they do very well. How they are made The product is well packaged and very well built; the charging case/base works perfectly, without hesitation, when you place the earphones in the charging cradle. On the left, the percentage of residual energy in the charging battery is clearly indicated with a number: on the right, with flashing green bars and the battery symbol, the amount of residual charge and the status of each earphone are indicated. In my experience the declared autonomy comes very close to the declared one. How comfortable they are The two Q76 earphones are comfortable to wear: the rubber of the support that wraps around the ears is soft and does not get in the way even when wearing glasses; the standard in-ear tips are available in three different sizes, just choose yours. Using them for around 90/100 minutes for each jogging session, they never bothered my ears nor, in the long run, did they prove uncomfortable. How to use them Bluetooth pairing with the mobile phone (and also with the mp3 player, as I did) occurs without problems, it only takes a few seconds. As for the controls, the first times I wore these earphones I had to practice to find the touch area, located at the bottom, which allows you to control them: adjusting the volume, changing the song being played, pausing, answering phone calls, etc. But a few times were enough to have no doubts. How they work In my opinion, the ace in the hole of these Bluetooth sports earphones is the sound quality: with the player set to a flat reproduction curve, the highs are brilliant but never annoying and the bass frequencies are nothing short of astonishing. With rock and progressive music I can hear bass of an uncommon depth on the earphones, which does not disfigure with the reproduction from my Grado SR60 headphones. They are never intrusive or electronically pumped up in a disco style. The voices are also ok: present and clear even in the most musically complex songs. Honestly, I didn't expect such a good result even though, given the price (also discounted), it's clear that it's not a basic product. I appreciated the IP7 class waterproofness which is very useful in sports - such as running - where sweat is king; as for phone calls, I found the Enc noise reduction effective, which allows me to be heard well by the interlocutor without having to raise my voice when I am, for example, in a noisy area. In my opinion In my opinion the Rolosar Q76 earphones are very well built and work equally well - they definitely deserve five stars. The only thing I would like them to have is the possibility of rotating the two support clips, the ones that wrap around the ears, on the vertical axis. In fact, with me, after running for a while they tend to move the in-ear rubber from its ideal position, which reduces the depth of the bass a little. With a less faithful pair of headphones I would perhaps never have noticed. With these, however, the low notes are so rounded and deep that it is a shame not to capture them in all their nuances. I think that inserting two rubber tips of the larger size would solve the problem, but I prefer to have an object in my ears that doesn't press too much into the ear canal, so I'm fine with that.

reviews.title: Really good value with active noise cancellation
reviews.body: I owned a previous version of the NC9's from 2022 that were a bit different than these, and as often happens with these little earbuds in a small charging case, I recently lost them somewhere, probably in my last hotel room. Beware of spending too much on earbuds - you absolutely will go through multiple sets of them. I was really happy with those earbuds for the price I paid at the time, which was a little over $10. So I figured rather than trying to wade through all the nonsensical marketing-speak on Amazon or the ridiculously overpriced offerings from Apple and other major brands, I'd just get the latest version of the same thing I had. And so far, these are pretty great for the price and a definite upgrade over the 2022 version. Now, I will say that while I'm not an audiophile, I could probably call myself an "audio enthusiast" and I don't think any earbuds from anybody sound all that great either on their own or when compared with decent full size headphones. That's one reason why I refuse to pay anything close to the $200 that's the standard price for major brand earbuds. These are tiny drivers using a low-powered DAC chip and DSP, getting a lossily compressed audio signal over a low-bandwidth wireless codec. It's just the nature of the beast. No earbuds anywhere are worth more than about 50 bucks, and that's with the profit baked in. Anything above that is just a name brand tax. (And these days, maybe a tariff.) But these sound perfectly fine for what they are and basically as good as any other wireless earbuds I've ever used. I did notice some sibilance with the default EQ - like most (all?) modern wireless earbuds, these accentuate bass and treble. But a quick adjustment to the high frequencies in the phone app (something that my older NC9's didn't support) seems to have cured that. There is of course still a bit of extra bass, but I'll leave that alone for now as I don't mind it. I can always adjust it later if I feel differently down the road. One minor quibble with the sound is that possibly because of that extra bass and treble, these don't get very loud. At maximum volume, they're about where I normally feel comfortable in regular listening, but they start to break up a bit before that. My guess is that Tozo has reduced the maximum output to control distortion, which isn't unique to them, but again, don't expect a high-end over the ear headphone experience here for 30 bucks. You just can't listen very loud with a lot of bass through tiny drivers like these without distortion. I don't think most people wearing earbuds listen as loud as I normally like to anyway. If this so far sounds like faint praise in a 5 star review, again, look at the price. You are getting a good value in sound quality, especially when you compare these to much more expensive earbuds that don't sound any better. If Apple were selling these and charging Airpod Pro prices, you'd be looking at a 2 star review. But these are priced fairly given their performance and the limitations of the category. Tozo also sells earbuds without the active noise cancellation but I bought these specifically for that, because it worked well on my previous NC9's and it seems to work at least as well and probably better on these. Keep in mind that noise cancellation in general was specifically developed to counter engine noise on airplanes. And that's still what the technology is best at. The way it works is by pushing out a specific frequency to act counter to the frequency of whatever continuous noise is present. It's not going to be very effective at silencing things like conversations or crying babies that are made up of variable, higher frequency sounds (because countering those would also affect the music you're listening to, not to mention using a lot more processing power, which also uses a lot more battery). That, again, is the nature of the beast. It applies to every set of earbuds that have ANC. But in terms of continuous background noise, such as from a jet engine or a loud fan, these work as well as anything else I've used. And I've used a lot of headphones and earbuds (as well as real aviation headsets) with active noise cancellation. The ANC also does not really alter the sound of the music you're listening to, which my older NC9's kinda did with the ANC on, and it's a pretty common issue with older devices that use ANC. Seems like it's more refined now and I don't really notice much difference, if any, in sound quality with ANC on or off. There was a time only a few years ago when you'd need to spend a few hundred bucks to get ANC at all, and that would have been in a set of wired full size headphones. Now we're talking about how well it works in a $30 set of wireless earbuds. It's kind of amazing if you think about it. I think real ANC alone is basically worth the price of admission here. There are a lot of earbuds in this price range that advertise "ENC" but that is not the same thing - that's for reducing noise on your voice when talking on phone calls. ANC is for listening to music. It's rare at this price, even now. For it to work this well is a huge bonus. Battery life is a definite step up from my older NC9's, although to be fair those were probably also just wearing out by the time I lost them. I intentionally tried to run these down while writing this review and after about 5 hours of constant listening, they were still going strong and when I put them in the charging case, it read 83%. Of course that's the total charge including the case battery, not the buds themselves. I have no idea how accurate that is but if it is correct, then that's probably more battery life than I would ever really need. (You can never have too much, but I can't think of a situation when I'd run out of battery life before being able to recharge.) I read another review where someone said the case on these did not close securely; that is not true. I'd think he must have been using a different version (the reviews here seem to cover all previous versions as well), but I had older ones and that case closed securely too. It's magnetic. The earbuds kind of pull themselves into their little cubbies if you've oriented them the right way, and then the case cover snaps closed with its own magnet. If the case is not closing properly, you're not putting the buds in the right way. They only go one way. You'll get it after a couple tries. Just take note of how they're oriented when you first open the case. Overall I can pretty confidently recommend these. Given that modern phones and many other devices no longer even have headphone jacks, you really need a set of wireless earbuds. Just get these; they're as good as more expensive earbuds and the price is fair. You can't say that about most name brand earbuds.

reviews.title: My New Favorite Earbuds
reviews.body: I actually love these, which was somewhat unexpected given the price tag. I'm not an audiophile, but I can somewhat tell the difference between poor sounding earbuds and decent ones. Trust me, I've purchase a few pairs of the not-so-good earbuds and use them long enough until I can find a better pair. The sound on these is not going to knock your socks off, but for the price, and with the EQ tools in the app, they've got decent sound quality. The fit is actually better than most earbuds that I purchase. My left ear must have a weird shape because a lot of earbuds fall out of that ear pretty easy, especially when I get sweaty or when I'm chewing food. I haven't tried intense exercise with these yet, but they did pass the food-chewing test. In other words, I don't feel the left earbud slowly creeping out of my ear canal while I'm eating, which is what usually happens with other earbuds. The earbud sync up to my iPhone quickly, and the tap controls on the earbuds are very responsive. I like that you can tap the left earbud to activate/deactivate noise canceling. It comes in handy when someone is trying to talk to me through the noise canceling; however, the single tap does switch you to Tozo's "Transparency Mode" instead of "Normal Mode", which mean the earbuds will amplify any exterior sounds which can be grating in loud environments. Just a caution if you have super sensitive hearing already. I can't speak much about how they work for phone calls. In a quiet environment, the person on the other end of the line has said they can hear me just fine. I'd be interested to see how they function in a noisy environment. My basic AirPods are still my go-to for phone conversations, just because I've never had the person on the other end of the line say they're having a problem hearing me, that is if the AirPod will stay in my left ear, which it won't whenever I'm walking around. The noise canceling is probably my favorite feature. I used the earbuds on a plane, and I felt they did an acceptable job of filtering out the plane noise and allowing me to enjoy my music and movies. They worked so well on a 14-hour car ride that sometimes the driver was trying to talk to me, and I had no idea he was speaking unless I was looking directly at him. The battery also lasted the entire car ride, though I confess I only had them on for about a quarter of the trip, and I put them back in the case a few times to recharge them, even though they weren't even halfway close to dying on me. When we arrived out our location, the battery life in the case wasn't even close to being expired. Finally, I can't speak to the longevity, since I've only owned them for a few weeks. I hope they last me at least a few years, at which point, I'll probably buy another pair, if the price is the same. If I get a couple years out of them, then they're definitely worth it. So far, they are my favorite pair of earbuds, out of the four I own

reviews.title: Good enough for the price!
reviews.body: I've been stuck on JLab for years because of their price and quality, but thought I would try these since my preferred ones quality went downhill. They are very easy to connect to my phone, sound great, and my husband can hear me clearly during calls. I like that they have a battery percentage screen on the case. It took some getting used to that they automatically connect as soon as you open the case door. This may pose a problem if you are used to tossing them in a bag with other items that may potentially bump the case door open while you are using the audio on your phone without them. They also sent me black instead of blue. No biggie though, I'll just store them more securely. My only complaint is the shape. If you don't put them in JUST right, they have a strange edge that can get irritating to feel on the bottom of your ear canal. I've provided pictures of this area. Other than that, they are great!

reviews.title: Durable, great noise canceling, great sound quality
reviews.body: I own three pairs of these earbuds in different colors (black, red, sage green) that I've bought over time and keep in different places for different uses. One pair for using while at work, one pair in my bedroom for connecting to my laptop or TV, one pair that I use while riding my motorcycle. The noise canceling on these is fantastic for the price. The helmet I use for riding does have a bit of a wind noise problem and my bike doesn't have a windshield, but while wearing these earbuds on NC mode going 50 mph down the road, I couldn't hear the wind at all, and the music quality is great. I've been a fan of Tozo earbuds for quite a while (used to use the T6s) but this specific model has been my favorite, ESPECIALLY for the great price that they're at. They do stick out of my ears a little bit further than I'd like, which makes getting a helmet on and off with them in very difficult, but obviously these aren't actually intended to be motorcycle ear plugs so that may just be me being picky. I've never had complaints about the sound quality, though I've never tried using them during a phone call so I can't speak to their performance there. I have dropped the earbuds on the ground several times while at work from pretty high up and they have yet to break. I'm a butcher so there's always water and beef blood on the floor, which I've dropped them in, and they still work fine. I lost one of the buds inside a meat freezer for a couple hours and upon retrieving it, it was still working perfectly fine. I don't know how Tozo sells these buds for so cheap when in my experience they are absolute tanks of earbuds. They don't fall out of my ears so all of the dropping was entirely my own fault. Once I put them in I very rarely have to worry about them falling out. If all three of my pairs somehow got lost or ruined, I wouldn't hesitate to order another three to replace them.

I smashed one bud so I decided it's time for a new pair. After reading reviews I decided these looked good and at a reasonable price. I liked the features of noise cancelling ( really works! )) and the app to set an eq band that I prefer or make my own. It really makes a difference if you like boosted bass or high end - whatever. There's many curves available. If you make one yourself, you can save it for others to use And the case which shows the battery level of each bud when in the case. Awesome! There's nothing I would improve. I even like the sound they make when paired with my device (my phone) Get 'em!

reviews.title: Undeniable value for the price and quality you get!
reviews.body: I purchased these earbuds to replace my old Apple AirPods Pro 2’s and Sony WF-1000XM3’s that I used for the past several years. I’ve had these TOZO earbuds for about a month now and so far they’ve well exceeded my expectations. Pros: The audio quality and noise cancelling abilities are far superior to both of my previous earbuds, which are admittedly a few years older and it seems ANC technology is just getting cheaper and better. The earbuds fit perfectly for my ears and are much smaller which makes them feel more comfortable and discrete than my previous earbuds. The companion mobile app offers a lot of control and even has AI translation features where you can speak to someone in different languages while each person wears an earbud and it will translate in the other person’s selected language to each other. Idk if that’s standard these days but it was a fun discovery that there are more interesting capabilities in the app. Cons: The build quality is noticeably inferior to my other earbuds. This was expected but the charging case in particular feels like cheap plastic compared to the metallic or more durable plastic construction on my old Sony’s and AirPod’s. I have dropped it once on a hardwood floor and it survived fine, but it feels less durable than other earbud cases which are already notorious for breaking easily. Bluetooth connectivity between multiple devices. I mainly use the earbuds with my iPhone and iPad and go back and forth between them. The AirPods were always seamless with this and even the Sony’s just had you go into the Bluetooth settings on the device you wanted to pair and select them. With these TOZO’s, there is an extra step if I still have both devices nearby. I have to manually disconnect the old device from Bluetooth first before I can pair the other one. Hopefully this is something that can be fixed later because it is a little annoying to have an extra step in these situations. Overall, even with the cons, these are still 5-star worthy for me at this price point which is literally a fraction of the cost from big brand alternatives. I would happily recommend these to anyone looking for inexpensive earbud options, especially at the sale prices. Even if I just get a year out of these earbuds, I think that’s well worth it to save money and just look at replacing with a similar pair down the road vs paying 5-10x more for earbuds that might last just a few years more if you’re lucky.

reviews.title: Nice overall build quality and solid noise cancellation, but I did not like the sound quality.
reviews.body: I think this company does a lot of influencer peddling to boost it's popularity. I watched multiple "honest review" videos touting how great these are and decided to give them a try as an alternative to my big over the ear headphones. I didn't expect them to outperform full size cans, but figured they should be pretty solid since they are plugged directly into your ears. I was impressed as I unboxed them as the charging case was solid feeling, as were the earbuds. The attention to detail was apparent with the nice packaging and box. They were easy enough to charge up, pair to my phone and came with multiple pillows to fit different ear sizes. Once I played them, that's when the excitement ended. They seem to have a high, harsh peak around 6khz that just irritates my ears. I attenuated them via the app and the sound was less ear piercing, but it wasn't enjoyable to me. It just didn't sound refined or clear. That said, I was very impressed with the noise cancellation. It felt weird to me to suddenly just hear nothing else. If you want quiet on a plane and ok sound to listen to the onboard entertainment, then these seem like they can be a good option. If you are into your music and like punch bass and clear, detailed highs, you won't be happy with these. They are tiny, portable and convenient so they will probably work well for some. I wouldn't advise wearing them jogging or bicycling as you won't hear traffic coming.

reviews.title: Great earbuds at an amazing price
reviews.body: My go-to earbuds have been the Powerbeats 3 for many years. I love the fullness of the sound, although the high-mids can lack some clarity. Last year I decided to get full wireless earbuds and thought I would give one of the cheaper alternatives a try. I got the Tozo T6, and ended up liking them quite a bit. Recently I got the Tozo NC9 to see if there is any improvement, and besides, they are so inexpensive! After tweaking these a fair amount, I finally got a sound I really like that is comparable to the Powerbeats 3. Soundwise, these are not much different from the T6, though I think the T6 have a little more low end out-of-the-box, but this can be adjusted with EQ. The NC9s fit in the ear more comfortably and the ear tips do not protrude as far down into the ear canal. The NC9s practically disappear into the ear and don't have the telltale tail hanging out like Apple AirPods. The NC9s do have noise cancelling, but that is not a feature that I care that much about, so I won't comment on it. I normally wear these on my morning walk or jog. I listen to music on my Pixel 6 Pro and use the PowerAmp app, which has an equalizer. For the Powerbeats 3, I keep the low end fairly flat and boost the upper mids. With the NC9, I use a modified version of the Rock EQ setting in the Tozo app, which is bass heavy, and then also boost the bass quite a bit in PowerAmp as well as a slight high end boost and mid cut. They do not sound quite as full in the low end as the Powerbeats 3, though close, but are crisper in the mids and highs. The low end is perhaps a little punchier. It is crucial to use the correct size ear tips, and also to put the ANC on the Noise Cancellation setting to get the fullest sound. Play around with these settings to see what you like. For me the additional EQ in the PowerAmp app is also essential in addition to the Tozo app EQ. I am very pleased with the overall design and sound of these earbuds. I rarely have a connection problem, and the charging case is wonderful. I am blown away considering the price point. I do recommend using EQ to dial in the sound and am glad that Tozo provides an app for this. I plan on using the NC9 as my goto earbuds considering sound, comfort, and convenience. Update: On a long walk I noticed that the Noise Cancellation mode can produce some subtle artifacts in the sound that bothered me for critical listening. I am now playing around with the custom mode for ANC to see if I can get the fuller sound with no noticeable artifacts. Update 2: I have settled on the Custom Pattern for ANC and am quite happy with the sound I am getting. I really enjoy these earbuds. I will attach some pictures of my settings. For reference, I bought a pair of Beats Studio Buds Plus earbuds, thinking they would improve on the sound of the Powerbeats3 I have and be stiff competition for the Tozo NC9. I was quite surprised, though, that I could not get them to sound full in the low end. The Beats don't come with an EQ, but I did use the EQ in the PowerAmp app. I could not get a full sound. Perhaps the Beats sound much better with iPhones, and not so much with Android/Pixel phones. Anyway, I was surprised, disappointed, and returned them. On the other hand, it makes me even more satisfied with the Tozo NC9 -- better features and better sound at a much lower price!

reviews.title: Fantastico
reviews.body: Sto usando le TOZO T10 da un po’ di tempo e devo dire che mi hanno davvero sorpreso. Offrono un’ottima qualità generale, sono comode e ricche di funzioni che di solito si trovano solo in modelli più costosi. PRO Suono potente e personalizzabile: grazie all’EQ regolabile e alla tecnologia ORIGX 2.0, si possono ottenere bassi profondi e un’ottima resa su ogni genere musicale. Autonomia eccellente: con la custodia si arriva tranquillamente a diverse decine di ore di utilizzo. Perfette per chi le usa tutto il giorno. Bluetooth 5.3 stabile: l’accoppiamento è rapido e la connessione resta solida anche muovendosi per casa. Controlli touch intuitivi: rispondono bene e permettono di gestire musica e chiamate senza difficoltà. Ricarica wireless + USB-C: comodo poter scegliere come ricaricarle. Certificazione IPX8: resistono molto bene a sudore e acqua, ottime per lo sport. Vestibilità confortevole: leggere, si inseriscono bene nell’orecchio e rimangono stabili anche durante il movimento. CONTRO La custodia è un po’ voluminosa rispetto ad altre nella stessa fascia. I controlli touch sono piuttosto sensibili: serve un po’ di abitudine all’inizio. Conclusione Le TOZO T10 sono cuffie affidabili, comode e con un suono di ottima qualità. Offrono funzioni avanzate difficili da trovare a questo prezzo. Perfette sia per l’uso quotidiano sia per l’allenamento o il lavoro in mobilità. Consigliatissime.
reviews.body_en: I've been using the TOZO T10s for a while now and I have to say they really surprised me. They offer excellent overall quality, are comfortable and full of features that are usually only found in more expensive models. PRO Powerful and customizable sound: thanks to the adjustable EQ and ORIGX 2.0 technology, you can get deep bass and excellent performance on every musical genre. Excellent autonomy: with the case you can easily reach several dozen hours of use. Perfect for those who use them all day. Stable Bluetooth 5.3: pairing is quick and the connection remains solid even when moving around the house. Intuitive touch controls: they respond well and allow you to manage music and calls without difficulty. Wireless charging + USB-C: convenient to be able to choose how to charge them. IPX8 certification: they resist sweat and water very well, excellent for sports. Comfortable fit: lightweight, they fit well in the ear and remain stable even during movement. CONS The case is a little bulky compared to others in the same range. The touch controls are quite sensitive: it takes a little getting used to at first. Conclusion The TOZO T10 are reliable, comfortable headphones with excellent quality sound. They offer advanced features that are hard to find at this price. Perfect for both daily use and for training or working on the move. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Suppressed midrange frequencies
reviews.body: I gave these earphones a try for a few minutes after unboxing them and quickly gave up on them. The bass and treble are decent, but the midrange is severely recessed. As a result, vocals sound muffled and distant, while guitars and other mid-focused instruments lack presence and definition. I’ve used countless earphones over the years, and this is one of the most unnatural midrange presentations I’ve encountered. The abundance of five-star reviews honestly makes me question their credibility. Update: I managed to alleviate the issue by using an equalizer to reduce the bass and boost the midrange. Vocals now sound considerably clearer and more present. So I raised my rating to 3 stars.

reviews.title: Very good, improved over previous version (J90).
reviews.body: I had very similar ones which I liked very much besides it being to easy to hit the buttons. I would constantly stop playback when removing an earbud (J90 model). The A90s here have all the good attributes of the previous model but it is harder to hit the touch buttons by accident. I use them at work so always taking one out for a second to talk to someone. As an added bonus the charging case is the same across all these similar models. I lost mine for the J90s but still have the buds. They charge perfectly well in the new case. So now I have a backup. Sound is very good. Not super loud but it's fine. Connection always good. I wear them while cycling at high speed. No issues in loosing one, these are recent but I used the near identical J90s for half a year. They are comfortable and the microphone is decent. I need to talk on the radio to people while cycling with traffic around and most of the time it works. While walking or indoors it should be excellent, high noise environment ok. The last me about 5 hours at full blast with heavy metal. What I like very much is the fast charging. Usually get the battery low warning by the end of my shift but I just pop one in the charger for 10 minutes, while using the other alone and then switch and it's plenty to finish the last hour or so. Full charge is quick too but I like super fast ~1h charge, only takes 10-15 min. What I still don't like, same as J90, you need to increase volume slowly or it counts as a double click and pauses... I don't like that. Half a second would be okay but pausing for a full second between each push is not convenient. Definetly worth the money, I've had fruit branded similar products that were not any better for almost 10X the cost. Depending what you pay. The similar looking models are all similar, so just get the cheapest one. Different brands but likely all made in the same place. Would buy again. In fact I did. Well almost the same. It also feels very much like a premium product, fit in the case and general look and feel is very high quality. Don't loose the charging case!

reviews.title: Great product, even better company.
reviews.body: I was gifted a set of Senso Bluetooth headphones years ago, and used them pretty much every day since then. This included during workouts in which they were jostled about and sweat on profusely, and not really maintained in any way. Eventually they started to show wear, and I purchased another set just so I'd be prepared when they finally gave up the ghost. Unfortunately there was a failure upon the first charging of that new set (which could've been my fault, even though I had the plug turned in the correct orientation). I contacted the company via the phone # in the user manual, anticipating the usual corporate run-around. Instead, I got to speak with a human on that first attempt, sent them the minimal information their warranty department required, and got an immediate written response letting me know that a replacement set was en route. Sure enough, just a few days later, the new set arrived, and is providing me with listening enjoyment as I compose this review. I deal with many different companies in my daily life, and probably like most of you, I find it an increasingly frustrating experience that rarely leads to total satisfaction. Therefore, I make sure to highlight those few remaining companies that actually stand behind their products and still offer excellent, personalized customer service. Senso is one of those companies. My experience with them is akin to those usually found only among luxury brands, yet this product is extremely reasonably priced, offers a quality experience, and is backed by a company that still believes in customer service. I wholeheartedly recommend this product, and would buy with confidence any other product sold by Senso.

Another 2 weeks and they start ignoring me. I give up. UPDATE 10/2020: Let's give credit where credit is due. The replacement headset finally arrived. For the record, I first reached out to Support on 8/28, they agreed to send replacement on 9/6, it was finally shipped on 10/6, and it arrived today (10/10). Let's hope this one will last. Thanks for the replacement. To be fair, I will up it from 2 to 3 stars. UPDATE (07/2021): Another 9 months later, the replacement headset is working great with heavy usage. Give credit where credit is due. Up from 3 to 4 stars. UPDATE (08/2021): Since the 2nd one was good, I ordered 3rd one. Few days after it arrived, left ear on my 2nd set started dying. It goes back my previous belief that there is quality problem.

reviews.title: Would not recommend
reviews.body: Bought these for Teams Meeting calls so I dont have to keep switching headphones or annoying my co-workers or family. You get what you pay for and then still feel kinda ripped off. OVERALL: If you dont care about sound quality, buzzing in ear, ear feel and possibly falling off and dont need the mic, these are fine for 22$ I guess. Anything more than that and I would recommend going to the 40-60$ range or just go the full 100-150$ near the raycon area. (Will update with battery life when I test that out). SOUND QUALITY - TERRIBLE - Even before any audio comes in there is a high pitched buzzing. Eventually it stops, maybe, or I tune it out. If youre audio is loud enough, it will drown out the buzzing. On Teams Meetings, the audio was absolutely terrible. While I can understand what my co-workers are saying, it was the worst sound quality I have heard in my life. EAR FEEL QUALITY - BAD - These do not feel good on/in the ear. Hard rubber, weird feel to the hand, and my not fit too well over the ear unless you have HUGE ears. Would not use for extended periods or active movement. There are replacement earbud rubbers but they still have the same weird feel and hard center. MICROPHONE QUALITY - BAD - They say the closer you are to the device the better the quality.... No, I was maybe 2 inches away from my computer in a quiet room and they barely picked up. I will just use the microphone on the laptop instead. OTHER: micro USB cord - Short also microUSB Carrying case - Meh 10% Off Coupon if you register. 1 year free warranty. LED Indicator not really indicating - Blinks red and blue when pairing, red when charging, is supposed to stay blue when fully charged but just turns off so I'm unsure if its fully charged or just decided to not?

I go to the gym 5-6 times a week and have already been through two pairs of bluetooth headphones and needed a good pair that would last without draining the bank account. A friend recommended these and after reading all the positive reviews decided to give them ago. So here it is. They are very easy to navigate/set up/pair. Pretty comfortable around and in the ear. Fit securely for active working out. Volume level is great. And the price is right on which is very important. Now on to the big flaw. Not sure where the "great sound quality" reviews came from, but for me the sound quality seems terrible. For the price I didnt was expect them to be top notch like Bose or Beats, however these sound so muffled it is like you are listening from the end of a long tunnel. When you up the volume it is even worse. Anyone else experience this? And definitely not noise canceling IMO. Sound quality was never a major concern to me when shopping but these are bad. Not sure yet if I will try to return them, I will probably end up living with them as I don't have an endless budget to spend on headphones and only use them about an hour a day while I am at the gym, but if anyone is looking for great sound quality I would recommend selecting a different set. I would doubt mine are just an outlier I'm thinking this model they are all like that.

reviews.title: Sony WF-C510 -- Good Audio For Cheap
reviews.body: 1) The sound of the WF-C510 is really good right out of the box without EQ. I listen to a lot of music, various genres, and everything is balanced and in control. Punchy bass, treble that's crisp and doesn't make my ears bleed, and decent mids. I definitely trust Sony when it comes to audio products. 2) Fit and comfort are amazing! I can leave these in all day. No joke, after 5+ hours of use, I feel zero discomfort. Not only are these earbuds the most comfortable earbuds of all time, but getting a good in-ear seal is effortless. Just set them and forget them, zero hassle. Just to note, there's no ANC but I don't mind; I use these at home where it's already quiet. Further, there's a feature called Ambient Sound Control, kind of the opposite of ANC, that lets outside noises in (press button on left earbud). Obviously, the volume has to be pretty low for this feature to be useful. 3) I rarely ever use playback controls on a pair of earbuds, as I just use my phone for that stuff. However, the physical buttons on the WF-C510 work like they should and it's always nice to have actual buttons over touch controls, mainly because there's less chance for accidental inputs, a common occurrence on my other earbuds. 4) The battery life seems to jive with Sony's claims of 11 hours in the buds and another 11 in the case. I'm getting a 50% battery level after 5+ hours at a volume level above half with the "Sony Sound Connect" app installed on my phone. I'll admit, the 11 hour battery claim was the #1 factor for my purchase. 5) The app gives you a ton of stuff to play around with. There's a bunch of EQs, 360 audio (more app downloads and payment required, I think), information regarding battery levels, and more. 6) A couple of oddities: The charging case confuses me. Does the orange light turn off when charging is complete or does it stay lit? I've experienced both scenarios and both times the app said the earbuds and case were at 100%. The instruction manual was no help. Also, for some reason I had to re-pair the earbuds to my phone's Bluetooth after shutting it off, which was super annoying. I was testing to see if an older device (without the app) would pair, so to avoid interference I turned off my phone's Bluetooth. The older device paired with the earbuds just fine without the app, so it isn't required. I plan on deleting it; it's probably a major battery hog anyway. 7) Minor issues aside, the Sony WF-C510 delivers premium comfort and pleasing sound. and they're super affordable. Get yours today! lol Update 3/25 -- Checking in to mention that the orange charging light on the case does in fact shut off to indicate that charging is complete and I'm still very happy with my purchase.

reviews.title: Physical buttons + Water resistance = works in heavy rain and shower (unlike ALL capacitive earbuds)
reviews.body: I don't understand the logic behind other earbuds that claim water resistance with capacitive controls. I have tried almost a dozen across various brands and NONE of them work properly when wet. It's not that the water damages them (it doesn't), it's that the capacitive buttons can't tell a water drop from a finger, so they're constantly registering false touches, jumping tracks, changing volume. CAPACITIVE EARBUDS ARE USELESS WHEN WET. (Fine once they dry off.) This WF-C510 pair from Sony, with physical buttons instead of capacitive touch, is the FIRST SET EARBUDS I'VE FOUND THAT ACTULLY WORK IN THE SHOWER or heavy rain. If you're just going for a jog in light mist or some drops of sweat run down your ears, those others do OK, but in a heavy rain or if you want to listen in the shower, go for these. I use earbuds in the shower so I don't wake up my spouse or kids if I get up early. I used to use a suction cup Bluetooth speaker, but that's loud and disturbs the family. Another problem with many capacitive earbuds: if you don't have any audio playing for a few minutes, they'll turn off to save battery... but because the capacitive touch requires power to work, there's often no way to turn them back on without putting them in the case and then removing them. This means if you don't have the case with you, you can't use them at all. I have actually bought extra cases just to leave in the places I often get stuck with powered-off earbuds, but what a waste of money that is! But note that where JBL, for example, sells just extra cases for their capacitive buds, I don't see that Sony does that. While you don't really need an extra case for these because you can turn them on and off via buttons, in the event you do want an extra case, be aware that your only option might be used on eBay. Also, these Sony WFD-C510 earbuds are small (compact, in the best possible way). These are some of the few earbuds I've found that I can wear under ear protection when mowing or doing other loud equipment work. Most other earbuds are bulky in comparison and ear protection pushes against them directly, really digging into the ear. These are so slim, you barely feel them even while wearing ear protection over them. On sound quality, these are great. They're not the best overall, but I think they are the best per dollar (and no earbuds are as good as real headphones if sound quality is the primary goal). They sound amazing for $50 buds. So, yes, overall, I would highly recommend them to anyone, but especially if you care about using them when very wet or under ear protection. Best I've found for those scenarios by a wide margin. To address both issues with a single pair of earbuds is incredible. One of my favorite bits of tech ever.

reviews.title: amazing value
reviews.body: Bought these to replace my favorite earbuds of the past few years, the KZ SKS and was a little disappointed at first. That was until I tweaked the EQ in the SONY app, which these responded wonderfully to. The bass is very lacking out of the box, but it makes for balanced tone. I like a lot of bass and bright highs, so I moved the slider to 7 on bass and adjusted the others accordingly, with no loss in sound quality. The biggest change though, was the exceptional battery life and amazing passthrough mode that I did not expect to like as much as I do. It allows conversations to be carried out while on the phone or listening to music. Even though these are roughly double the price of my $30 KZs, I would actually say they're an even better value with the features and battery life. They're also super light and relatively small, so they won't fall out of your ears. For a 6mm driver (which is supposedly shared with some of their more expensive models), these have an excellent soundstage and really can thump. The ONLY drawback (if you want to call it that), is the buttons are not capacitive, and must be physically clicked. This can be helpful in preventing accidental presses though, which is a plus. Build quality is what you'd expect from Sony. Very good. Will update if these have any drawbacks in the future.

reviews.title: Good Value for the Price, with Some Clear Limitations
reviews.body: I purchased the Sony WF-C510 for around $50 or less, and considering that price point, I am generally satisfied with the product. Below is my experience after a few weeks of use. Sound: For the price, the sound profile is good and well balanced. The bass is present, though not very powerful compared to more expensive models. As a user who has owned higher-end earbuds, I do notice a lack of depth in the low frequencies, but at this price range, that is acceptable. You cannot expect premium bass performance from a budget model, and within those limits, the sound is decent. Comfort: The earbuds are small and lightweight, and after some time you barely notice you are wearing them. They are comfortable enough to use while lying in bed, and if they had touch controls, you could even listen while resting on one side without discomfort. That said, the fit is not perfect for me. They do not feel 100% secure at all times, and I occasionally need to readjust them manually. It is not frequent, but it is an area that could be improved. Buttons: For the price, I did not expect touch controls, but the physical buttons can be inconvenient at times. Pressing them often causes the earbud to move out of position, which then requires readjustment. Microphone: Based on feedback from my wife during phone calls, there was noticeable background noise on my end. I cannot provide a very detailed review of the microphone, but this was the main comment I received during the three weeks of use. Would I recommend them? It depends on the use case. I would not recommend them for intense workouts. If you are very demanding about sound quality or expect a high-end audio profile, these will likely disappoint you. However, for walking, office use, or casual listening—and if you are not very demanding about sound quality—they are a good option for the price. Note: I have used the Jabra Elite 75t for about two years (originally $199) and have been using the Sony WH-1000XM3 for four years. Obviously, this is not a fair comparison, as the difference in sound quality is significant. Still, considering the price of the WF-C510, they are worth it if you are not overly demanding about audio performance. ============================ Update after a few months of use: ============================ After a couple of months with the Sony WF-C510, my overall opinion remains mostly the same, but I can now add a few clearer conclusions. The biggest downside is definitely the microphone. Call quality has consistently been poor. On several occasions during meetings, I had to disconnect them and switch to other headphones to continue the call. Background noise isolation for the mic is weak, and for professional use, they are simply not reliable. The sound profile is still good for the price. It remains balanced and acceptable within its budget category. However, if you are used to earbuds in the $150+ range, these will likely feel underpowered and lacking depth. The difference in presence, clarity, and overall audio richness becomes more noticeable over time. Would I buy them again? Probably not. While they are not bad for the price, I personally prefer stronger audio performance and more depth, even if that means paying more. Overall, my experience is neutral — not bad, not exceptional. They deliver what you would expect from a $48 pair of earbuds, but they do not meet my personal expectations, which are influenced by years of using higher-end models.

reviews.title: Exceptionally good, amazing even, 'buds at a great price
reviews.body: These are amazing. The sound quality is very good. They don't fall out of my ears (all other earbuds i've had, lots of them, don't stay in my ears. Even my AirPods Pro 2 fall out of my ears, but not these. Although they lack noise cancelation, they do significantly reduce environmental noise. The buds form a tight seal, and turning off the Ambient Noise feature makes them effectively noise canceling. BUT, the most impressive feature is the water resistance. I, ummmmmmm, left them in my pants pocket, forgot they were there, and put the pants in the washing machine. Yeah, very much bad not good. The were in there for about 15 minutes total, and 5 minutes into the Wash cycle. So, I remembered that I'd left them in my pants pocket, and that they were in the wash. I fished them out (they'd fallen out of my pants pocket and were on the bottom of the tub, under all the T-shirts, socks, other pants . . . ), and set them on my desk to dry. That night I put them in a UV dryer and cycled it several times. The next morning I tested them AND THEY WORKED. Holy Moly Batman! These are tough buds.

reviews.title: Great Audio, Great Fit, One Big Problem
reviews.body: I purchased these a little under a year ago, and up until about a month ago, I absolutely loved them. Honestly, I would have easily given these 4-5 stars if it weren’t for the charging case issue. Unfortunately, the case has taken a pretty sharp nosedive lately. I now have to charge it almost daily just to use one earbud at a time... which kind of defeats the whole “wireless earbuds” concept. For the price, I expected a bit more longevity. I usually buy cheaper earbuds because I have a talent for leaving them in pockets or sacrificing a single earbud to the outdoors forever, but I decided to splurge for better sound and call quality - and to be fair, these definitely delivered on that front. I also have smaller ears, and these have been some of the most comfortable earbuds I’ve used. They’re lightweight, not made of super hard plastic, and don’t feel enormous or awkward after wearing them for a while. So overall: excellent sound, calls, and comfort... but the charging case aging this badly in under a year is really disappointing.

reviews.title: These are the BEST, really, no joke and comfortable!!
reviews.body: The box was ripped open right where the earbuds were placed in the package. I don’t know if it was someone being curious, or just a shipping machine rip. Either way, I took the earbuds out of package, charged them fully and put them on for a trail. I would put a “mind blown” emoji here. The sound right out of the box was good. Then I downloaded the “Sound Connect” app and I was lost for a good hour and a half, just having fun and listening to music. I was able to quickly use “short cut” way to find what kind of sound I like, as the app just walked me through. I now know, ( by this apps definition) that I like clear bass. There is an equalizer where anyone whom has the knowledge and the skill to set their music to sound just like they want to hear. I have an eclectic range of music. Billy Joel ( older version cd) that didn’t give me the strong clear bass I like, yet it was quite balanced. I listened to Tchaikovsky‘s Swan Lake and that just made me smile. Enter P!nk with “Truth About Love” cd and I could hear parts of the music that I have not heard before. Amazing!! And to end the night with a bang I switched to “Disturbed” Down with the Sickness and I was banging. The sound never got distorted. Everything was clear and I actually had to turn the sound down, as I like it loud!! Mind you, I am not a audiophile, but I do love music, so take my opinion as you choose. The buttons on the buds are easy to use. I used with Alexa, phone call, next song, previous song, and it was seamlessly easy. Functionality is A+. Instructions have a QR Code to take you to a users manual. The buds come with a one year warranty. Just a quick scan tells me I need to keep the box it came in and I am sure there is more that is needed for the warranty. Just read to be safe. The package comes with different size buds inside the package. Now, I can not say enough about how comfortable these buds feel. I have purchased sooooooo many types of earbuds and have NEVER felt buds this comfortable. Every pair of buds, I will not name them, but seriously a LOT, has been uncomfortable. These are just so comfortable and even though I have no noise cancellation, they are sealed so well in my ear that it doesn’t feel like I am missing anything. Long story short, get these!!!!! Sony has always come through and these are no different. Be well.
