reviews.title: Buena calidad de sonido
reviews.body: Tengo los Sony WH-1000XM4 (de diadema) y los Xiaomi Redmi Buds 3 Lite, así que estos serán mi punto de comparación. He leído opiniones de que estos Sony no tienen un volumen muy alto pero para mí el volumen es disfrutable. Los bajos suenan muy bien por el precio, nada que pedirle a las frecuencias bajas de los 1000XM4 (que siendo justos, los bajos de estos audífonos, los 1000XM4, no destacan mucho aún con el ecualizador). El audio en general es más limpio y de mejor calidad en comparación a los Xiaomi. El material sí se siente económico, tanto de los audífonos como del estuche pero nada de qué preocuparse, son económicos pero la construcción es buena y cómoda. Se sienten muy ligeros y no molestan para nada luego de horas. La batería de los audífonos es muy buena, tarda muchísimo tiempo para que baje del 100% (salvo que actives el modo ambiente) y aunque no tienen cancelación de ruido, personalmente siento que en este tipo de audífonos no es realmente necesario porque la goma cierra muy bien el oído. El estuche por otro lado... no dura mucho. En 2-3 días ya había bajado al 50%, pero seguiré revisando (aclaro que yo los uso mucho tiempo al día, cuando no los uso mucho la batería del estuche no baja tan rápido). Si los ves en $800 MXN o menos, me parecen una buena opción, especialmente por lo ligeros y cómodos que son y la calidad de audio en general. Si los ves más caros, buscaría otras opciones. Finalmente, dos consejos: 1. Descarga su app, 'Sound Connect' (de Sony) y usa el ecualizador. El audio que viene de fábrica sí se siente muy plano (tal vez por eso se quejan del volumen), así que usar el ecualizador mejora sustancialmente la calidad de sonido. Si no quieres romperte mucho la cabeza, solo abre la app, registras los audífonos y en el apartado de ecualizador escoge el perfil 'Emocionado' (o algún otro perfil que tenga al menos +7 de Clear Bass). 2. He leído en algunos foros que ciertas personas tuvieron un problema con el estuche: si dejas que la batería del estuche llegue a 0%, este ya no se vuelve a cargar (los audífonos sí, pero el estuche no). En la misma app puedes monitorear la batería de los audífonos y del estuche. De vez en cuando revísalo y trata de que la batería del estuche no baje del 20-30%. No he tenido problemas y no le pasa a todo mundo, pero es mejor prevenir cualquier cosa. Actualización: después de dos meses de uso, el estuche se me ha descargado por completo más de una vez y sigue funcionando, no se asusten por ese tema, pero sí, su batería me dura de tres a cuatro días, a veces un poco menos.
reviews.body_en: I have the Sony WH-1000XM4 (headband) and the Xiaomi Redmi Buds 3 Lite, so these will be my point of comparison. I have read opinions that these Sonys do not have very high volume but for me the volume is enjoyable. The bass sounds very good for the price, nothing to ask for from the low frequencies of the 1000XM4 (which to be fair, the bass of these headphones, the 1000XM4, does not stand out much even with the equalizer). The audio in general is cleaner and of better quality compared to the Xiaomi ones. The material does feel cheap, both the headphones and the case but nothing to worry about, they are cheap but the construction is good and comfortable. They feel very light and do not bother you at all after hours. The battery of the headphones is very good, it takes a long time for it to drop below 100% (unless you activate the ambient mode) and although they do not have noise cancellation, I personally feel that in this type of headphones it is not really necessary because the rubber closes the ear very well. The case on the other hand... doesn't last long. In 2-3 days it had already dropped to 50%, but I will continue checking (I clarify that I use them for a long time a day, when I don't use them much the battery in the case does not drop as quickly). If you see them for $800 MXN or less, they seem like a good option to me, especially because of how light and comfortable they are and the overall audio quality. If you see them more expensive, I would look for other options. Finally, two tips: 1. Download their app, 'Sound Connect' (from Sony) and use the equalizer. The audio that comes from the factory does feel very flat (maybe that's why they complain about the volume), so using the equalizer substantially improves the sound quality. If you don't want to rack your brains too much, just open the app, register the headphones and in the equalizer section choose the 'Excited' profile (or some other profile that has at least +7 Clear Bass). 2. I've read on some forums that some people had a problem with the case: if you let the battery in the case reach 0%, it won't charge again (the headphones do, but the case doesn't). In the same app you can monitor the battery of the headphones and the case. Check it from time to time and try to ensure that the battery in the case does not drop below 20-30%. I haven't had any problems and it doesn't happen to everyone, but it's better to prevent anything. Update: after two months of use, the case has completely discharged more than once and it is still working, don't be scared by that issue, but yes, its battery lasts three to four days, sometimes a little less.

reviews.title: Great value, great sound, almost like noise-cancelling buds.
reviews.body: I thought I needed noise-cancelling earbuds for the gym, but these do the trick at a fraction of the price. Since they fit snugly with the silicone tips (and I have small ear canals), they block out a lot of noise passively. Noise-cancelling probably wouldn't do much better, because it's not optimized for voices and other higher frequencies. If you want earbuds and don't want to pay $300, then these are a great value. Note that I bought them on sale for $68; the current price of $100 is pushing it. The sound is clear and balanced, no excessive treble or bass. No connectivity issues using a Samsung phone and MacBook. Battery life shouldn't be an issue for most people, they last forever. If you haven't used this type of earbud before, just note that when you first put them in, they might not seal well, but just give the silicone a minute to warm up and it will sit better (provided you have the correct tip size installed).

reviews.title: Outstanding Sound Quality and Seamless Samsung Integration

Active Noise Cancellation works very well, and Ambient Mode makes conversations easy without removing the earbuds. Pairing with my Samsung Galaxy phone was quick and effortless. reviews.title: I couldn't imagine paying this much was that much better than ones I used for 1/10th the price
reviews.body: Situation: I couldn't imagine paying this much was that much better than ones for 1/10th the price. This begs the question, Then why did I try them? - I am learning Spanish to be with orphan kids in Colombia. I go to a church to be around them. I have an S24 Ultra that can translate to text or voice. I was wondering if it would be worth getting the S26 Ultra before going to Colombia again. Battery life was the same and the processor was a lot faster. - I expected go for it, but that's not the advice I received. Instead I received your S24 Ultra already has the Galaxy AI Interpreter for face-to-face conversations, Live Translate for phone calls, excellent microphones, and plenty of AI processing power. Samsung's newer hardware improves AI performance, but translation quality is mostly limited by speech recognition (understanding the speaker), translation model quality, context understanding, accents, slang, and background noise, not raw phone speed. Going S24 Ultra to the S26 Ultra might get slightly faster response, smoother offline AI, maybe less delay, but it will not suddenly make Spanish conversation feel like a Star Trek universal translator. Your S24 Ultra is already a monster. For translation, the bottleneck is not your Snapdragon processor, it is capturing clean speech and the AI model doing the interpretation. A better microphone path can help more than a faster phone. The Samsung earbuds Buds4 Pro is what I would recommend. The reason they matter is not that they magically translate by themselves, they improve the whole workflow. The microphones are closer to your mouth, they reduce background noise, you can hear translations privately, and you are not always holding a phone between two people. For example, with Galaxy AI Interpreter, you wear earbuds, the other person talks toward the phone, you hear English translation in your ear, your phone can output your voice translated Spanish. Moreover, if you have a Samsung phone, Galaxy Buds can do some translation tricks too. - It took me some time to overcome feeling stupid for spending 10x as much for something I had that works well, it was unimaginable that they could be that much better, and something I had to guard with my life now. I ordered, then struggled with cancelling, and then let it go on the basis that I also wouldn't know unless I "rolled the dice" to know, and the importance of the mission. The struggle was not the money. It was feeling stupid after I already had some that worked fine. Experience: - Setup surprise: Like all earbuds, they come with various sizes to fit your ears. Unlike the others I have, it has a setup that tests and determines the size that fits your ear. You do not do the determine which size, it does. You get a green check when you get a size that passes. There was only one of the sizes that passed, and they were not the same size for each ear. When I had someone look at my ears and size of the opening, they said they are exactly the same. I tried to trick it by changing its position to have it use the same size for each ear, but it wasn't buying it. I'm guessing it detects how much escapes from the ear to the microphone. Next it wants to do a hearing test like the flight surgeons used to do. This takes a while. Flight surgeons check to see if your hearing is still good. This uses the results of the tests to profile your hearing sensitivity across frequencies to adjust the volumes to make it perfect for each ear. That's more than my ~$1600 flight helmet does. - Comparison: My cheap ones worked just fine, I don't listen to music, and adjusting a mixer to the way I want to hear music just isn't a "duck in my pond". I just want to hear the unaltered sound, clearly, and be understood clearly, that's all I care about. You will not be able to imagine there could be a difference beyond that UNTIL you experience them side-by-side. Then they are very different. According to the scientific tests, the battle is between these and the ones from Apple, which are about the same price. However, if you have a Samsung Phone, it's no contest, which I do, because the iPhone doesn't have the smarts , flexibility, ability to document and record my phone calls automatically, enable you to write scripts to automate things without external approval, or have both eSIM and nanoSIM, as often nanoSIM plans are much cheaper abroad for some reason unknown to me. E.G. The iPhone is a great phone too, but it simply "cannot get there from here". - Features: It has different modes available to control the cancelling of background noise, one of which is to turn off the cancelling when you start talking so you can hear the response of the person next to you without removing the ear buds. There is a mode for driving to hear alert noises. It is much nicer for translation as mentioned in the advice I was given. Like the AirPods, these are also water resistant. You can also track and find them over the Internet from last place used, in Bluetooth range, and you can also find them in the case and turned off locally. There is no tendency for them to fall out of my ears while running. Summary: These are a different ball game than the inexpensive ones. If you have a use case like mine it is, and might also be worthwhile for someone whose hearing isn't the best. What I've written should help you determine if the extra initial cost and cost if you lose them, is worth the advantages they bring for your use case.

reviews.title: So Galaxy Buds 3.5 Pro?
reviews.body: So through extensive testing over the past few months I can without a doubt say these aren't worth the value for your money. Although I'm rating it a 5 star I don't see the value in these headphones. They're practically the same as the old one just smaller in a different chagering box a little more sleeker. However the buttons to turn it up and down or to answer a call are harder to tap and to find. The battery life is just about the same I can get five listens before needing to charge again. What I mean is I take a 20 or so minute drive from my house to my job then at my job I wait 50 or so minutes till I start work. In that time I'm listening to music or a podcast and that's 5 times because I only use it when going to work. The call quality is the same the audio is the same the overall quality is the same. Charging is rather slightly faster. The size is alright if you have big ears if you have smaller ears that might be an issue. They took away the LED lights that used to blink and the sound for when you lose them is still low. The 360 audio for me has been the most pointless feature because I don't hear anything no different and more interrupts my listening with how it sounds. Its neither vivid or immersive. All in all these are the same headphone however made smaller and without the LED lights. I can recommend them if you never had the Galaxy Buds 3 pro however if you have them this is the product to skip.

reviews.title: Comfortable but some problems with features
reviews.body: Better fit for me than the Buds 2 and great sound cancelling. Here's are my pros and cons: Pro: Comfortable for me and stays in my ear better than the Buds 2 and Buds 3. It doesn't feel like it's always on the verge of falling out, or that is plugging up my ear causing pressure in my ear. Pro: The case has a pairing button to make it easier to pair with your laptop and other non-phone devices. Con: When I had 2 devices paired with the Buds 4, it kept losing the connection to my laptop in the middle of use. I suspect there's a software bug. Con: As with all recent Samsung earbuds, the controls are somewhat hidden in the volume setting of the phone now, so non-Android phones and non-phone devices won't have access to many of the settings. There used to be a wearables app that let you access this settings, but that is not the case now so long term usability may also be a problem, as long as Google doesn't change the audio/sound interface in Android. This integrated setting can also be confusing to get to since no other devices integrate this way (that I've seen). I would prefer an app for those controls, personally. Overall, the battery life and sound quality are good. At least as good as other ear buds that I've used over the past 15 years, and the stems do give you some pinch (pause or assistant) and swipe (volume or tracks) controls, like recent Apple'earpods. But here's the one really big negative that earned these 4 stars instead of 5. Live translate. It sucks. I would much prefer to link to Google translate or something else. The Samsung version just doesn't work consistently. I tried it with a fluent Spanish speaker in a quiet room and it missed words, stopped listening mid sentence and was completely unreliable. Do not buy these if you need that feature. These are not a Babble Fish. I would also prefer that the digital assistant was user selectible. I don't want to use Bixby, ever! Otherwise, for listening to music and audio books, having a phone call or Zoom meeting, these are great and comfortable for long periods of time.

reviews.title: Samsung's Best Earbuds Yet – Incredible Sound, ANC, and Comfort
reviews.body: Samsung's Best Earbuds Yet – Incredible Sound, ANC, and Comfort I've owned several generations of wireless earbuds over the years, and the Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro are easily the most impressive pair I've used. Paired with my Samsung phone, they deliver exceptional audio quality, excellent noise cancellation, and a comfortable fit that I can wear for hours. Samsung equipped the Buds 4 Pro with upgraded dual-driver speakers, Hi-Res Audio support, and improved Active Noise Cancellation, and the difference is immediately noticeable. The sound quality is outstanding. Music feels more detailed and spacious, with strong bass that doesn't overpower the mids or highs. Vocals are crisp, instruments are well separated, and everything sounds richer than previous Galaxy Buds models. Whether I'm listening to music, watching movies, or streaming videos, the audio is consistently impressive. The Active Noise Cancellation is another major highlight. It does an excellent job reducing background noise in busy environments while still allowing useful features like adaptive ambient awareness when needed. Calls are also remarkably clear, with microphones that do a great job isolating my voice from surrounding noise. Comfort has been excellent as well. The earbuds stay secure during long listening sessions, and the charging case feels premium while remaining compact enough to carry easily. Battery life has been more than enough for my daily use, and wireless charging support is a nice bonus. Pros: • Outstanding sound quality with excellent clarity and bass • Effective Active Noise Cancellation • Crystal-clear call quality • Comfortable fit for extended use • Great integration with Samsung devices • Premium charging case with wireless charging support Cons: • Some advanced features work best within the Samsung ecosystem • Premium price compared to budget earbuds Overall, the Galaxy Buds 4 Pro have exceeded my expectations. They combine premium sound, strong ANC, excellent call quality, and a comfortable design into one package. If you're a Samsung user looking for high-end wireless earbuds, these are an easy 5-star recommendation and one of the best audio upgrades you can make.

reviews.title: Not Greatest But Decent
reviews.body: I am a lifetime apple user who recently went Android. I am basing this off of my experience with Beats and Apple airpods. These do not have as quick as connectivity as other headphones I have had. The battery life isn't the greatest and noise cancelling does leave something to be desired. The bass is a bit tinny - I cannot enjoy heavy metal music or bass heavy rap without feeling like it is in a tin can. Call quality is okay. They do stay in my ears (I have Eustachian Tube Dysfunction) so it's nice to find something that doesn't hurt my ears or make them feel clogged. The pinch and touch controls do not properly respond as they should and feel a bit clunky. All of this being said. They look good. They don't hurt my ears (HUGE PLUS), and they have yet to fall out of my ears (even when it's been 105.)

title: TOZO A1 Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Light Weight in Ear Headphones
bullet_points: [Ultra-Lightweight Ear Buds Designed for Small Ears] Each earbud weighs only 3.7g and features a compact, ergonomic in-ear design made especially for small ears. Secure, low-profile, and comfortable for workouts, all-day wear or overnight sleeping.The ultra-slim profile sits flush in your ear with no hard edges poking or rubbing, so you can even sleep on your side without discomfort.
[Immersive Stereo Sound with TOZO OrigX Technology] TOZO OrigX tuning delivers clear vocals, balanced mids, and natural stereo sound for music, podcasts, and videos.
[Long Battery Life for Daily Use] Get up to 7 hours of playtime on a single charge, with up to 32 hours total using the charging case—ideal for workdays, commuting, and extended listening sessions.
[Bluetooth 5.3 & Stable Connection] Bluetooth 5.3 provides fast pairing, stable wireless performance, and reduced dropouts as you move around home or office.
[Deep Bass with Clear Vocals] High-performance drivers produce punchy bass while keeping vocals clean and detailed for everyday listening.
[AI-Enhanced ENC for Clear Calls] ENC microphones help reduce background noise like traffic and office sounds, keeping your voice clear on calls and video meetings.
[32 Custom EQ with TOZO App] Use the TOZO app to access 32 EQ presets and adjust bass, vocals, or balanced sound to match your preference.
[One-Step Pairing & Touch Controls] Open the case to pair automatically. Touch controls let you manage music, calls, and voice assistants with simple taps.
[IPX5 Sweat & Splash Resistance] IPX5-rated protection helps withstand sweat and light splashes—ideal for sports, gym and daily activities.
[Made for Calls, Fitness & Daily Comfort] Lightweight, secure, and easy to use—built for daily comfort, clear calls, and an easy fit for small ears.

reviews.title: Really great budget earbuds
reviews.body: I've only been using these earbuds for about two days, so this is definitely an early first impression, but so far I'm surprisingly happy with them. Once they were fully charged, they connected to my phone with no effort at all. I have fairly small ears, and a lot of earbuds end up hurting because they're too large, but I haven't had that issue with these. They fit well and stay comfortable even after wearing them for a few hours at a time. The sound quality, volume, and noise canceling have all been great for me. My favorite feature so far is the call quality. I was constantly disconnecting my previous earbuds whenever I got or made a phone call because no one could hear me. I haven't had that problem with these at all. Calls have been clear, and no one has asked me to repeat myself or speak louder. I haven't had a chance to really test the battery life yet since I usually charge my devices every night, so it may be a while before I know how long they actually last. The only feature I miss from my previous pair is the digital battery indicator on the charging case. Other than that, especially for the price, these have been an excellent purchase so far.

reviews.title: Wireless - Waterproof - Great Sound - Phone App - Mind Blowingly low price point for this quality!
reviews.body: I had been searching for a decent pair of wireless waterproof earbuds where the battery would play music for at least 4 hours on a full charge. I wasn't going to even consider any pair fitting my needs priced below $40, until my daughter told me about these, saying she really loved them and used them until she lost one of them after only a few weeks of use. So I bought them, and have all positive things to say about them, except for one thing. Here goes: PRO's: - They come with 4 pair of different sized rubber fitting tips - Using the pre-installled earbud tips, I was shocked in surprise that all it took was one quick finger press and they fit snugly and better than any other pair I have ever worn. As opposed to having to fiddle with them, twist and turn with a bit of force to make them stay in position. Not these - perfect instant snug fit that stays in place! - near continuous run time playing music or listening to audio books is at least 4 hours! Are you kidding me? For under $15, having 4-5+ hours battery time? Awesome! - When you need to keep using them but a battery dies - This is awesome - One side will always run out of battery before the other. When it does, or better, when it gives the 1st of 3 warning beeps that it is getting low, immediately take it out of your ear and put it in the charge case. OMG. It will charge to 80-90% in 20 mins or so! This means, when one starts to die, put it in the charge case, still listening to the other one. When that dies, even if it's 10 or 20 minutes later, put that one in the charge case, and start listening to the other one that you just put in the charge case a few minutes ago. You will find that it will run long enough for the one you just put in the case to charge to get to a full charge! Doing this, you will always be listening to at least one, but after a couple of times swapping them in/out of the charge case, they charge so fast that you will be back listening to BOTH again for another 1-2 hours, as the charge case if fully charged overnight will charge both earbuds at least 2-3 times. This is amazing - I've had to do this trick of using one while charging the other, but never do they charge fast enough to soon be using both again the same day because of such fast charge times compared to long run times. $15!!! This is an exceptional product and rare to have so many great features for pretty much a cost that makes them disposable but they are anything but!! - Sound quality! OMG! Really nice deep base response, and nothing missing throughout the mids and highs either! - The phone app makes it easy to pick from a huge repository of EQ settings. The phone EQ app isn't just a cheap attempt so they can advertise it as having a 10 band EQ - it is a bonafide 10 band EQ with a 10 DB range (+5 to -5 per each frequency band). You can create as many EQ templates as you like, give them a custom name, save them, even share them. At least 100 or more you can access from other users whose templates show up in the app. -Waterproof! I use them working in the yard (sweating profusely) at the gym, and in the shower blasting hot water from the shower head right on them. CON's: - Just one. As stated, they fit perfectly... until. At some point wearing them for an hour or so, you can feel one starting to get loose - DAMN! There it is on the ground - I hope it didn't break. Whew, it's still fine. It might just be me, but every single day, after wearing them both for at least an hour of a perfect fit - the moment I feel either one starting to loosen up - is when it is falling out. I took Karate, and I;m known for my fast reflexes, but not once so far have I ever been able to stop either one from falling out. Like I said, they fit perfectly, so I don't adjust them. They seem like they never move at all, maybe my ears build up with a thin layer of humidity/sweat, but without notice either one will just pop out faster than I can try to catch it free-falling 6 feet from my head to the ground. So it's been several weeks, so each one has jumped without a parachute to a crash landing on the ground every day, so each one roughly 20 6 foot drops, most of which to cement or asphalt. They both still work 100%, so I am just more surprised than upset at this phenomenon. Perhaps I'll attach a string to them, so when one falls out, I will have time to cup the opposite ear, and it will only fall the length of the string and not hit the ground. Instead of a string, I'll just buy at least one more pair, probably two, so that whenever one breaks, is lost, no longer lasts long after charging, it will become disposable (unless first try to take it apart and see if I can buy a super small rechargable battery and replace it myself, who knows, just a fun "maybe" thing. I completely 100% endorse these earbuds though. Even in the comments, there doesn't appear to be any issue that keeps coming up over and over, a sign of a well-designed product with a rare lifecycle!

reviews.title: Small ear canal fit, all day charged
reviews.body: I love these earbuds! I’m buying my third pair simply due to use and misplacement. Fit: I have small ear canals and jlab and sony earbuds didn’t fit. These come with so many silicon options for your ear. The smallest fit me perfectly! Another bonus is under my snowboard helmet. It truly takes a fingerprint to pause. It has a low profile and when I turn my head, it doesn’t pause from the pressure of the helmet. Charge: I love to listen to audiobooks while hiking. My hikes can range up to 15 hours + multi day. I use one earbud at a time so I can tune into nature as well and can listen all day or multiple days when I’m super into the book. And recharge a bud as needed. They are water resistant, listening through rain, and the case has also been dropped in water and still works. Online calls: I use these paired with my laptop to record videos for my online courses, make phone calls, or zoom. The earpiece focuses well on my voice and dampens out external noise. Noise Cancellation: I also had 2 kids under 2. I relied on the noise cancellation feature during double tantrums to self regulate and be calm for them. I can’t recommend these enough for their price point, fit adjustability, charge life, and water resistance!

reviews.title: Love em
reviews.body: Update 1 year later: I still love these!! They still work great and connect with no problems. They stay connected even when I go to the other side of my house without my phone. The battery has gone down some to where I now get only about 4-5 hrs before having to charge them. I decided a month ago to get another pair of TOZO earbuds with a longer battery life. I got the A-6s. Those worked great but were too big for my ears and wouldn’t stay in place. I apparently have child sized ears! These earbuds fit great and I can wear them all day. There was a sale for a couple days where you could get them cheaper (forget how much), so I now own 4 pairs of these - 2 green, a blue and a black pair! Lastly, my initial pair that I bought a year ago was accidentally washed through a whole wash cycle when I forgot them in my pocket. I was so sad cause I thought they would be totally dead. Opened up the case and popped the buds in my ears; and not a hint of anything gone wrong!! They still work perfectly!! reviews.title: These Sound Way More Expensive Than They Are
reviews.body: Here’s a polished Amazon review that sounds genuine without reading like it was written by the earbuds’ marketing department. Humanity has collectively decided every $30 gadget must claim it’s “life-changing,” so this aims for believable instead. I wasn’t expecting to be this impressed, especially for the price. These earbuds honestly perform like a much more expensive pair. The noise cancellation does an amazing job blocking out background noise, making it easy to focus on music, podcasts, or calls. One of my favorite features is being able to tap the earbuds to skip tracks, pause, or control playback without reaching for my phone. They also come with an app that’s surprisingly useful. You can customize the equalizer, adjust settings, and fine-tune everything to your liking, which is a feature I usually only see on premium earbuds. The sound quality is clear with great bass, they’re comfortable enough to wear for hours, and the battery life has been excellent. If you’re looking for high-end features without paying high-end prices, these are definitely worth buying.

reviews.title: (Le ho ancora dopo 2 anni🤯) Eccezionali per rapporto qualità - prezzo!

Addirittura queste cuffie hanno battuto (in durata nel tempo) le Airpods 3ª Generazione (pagate ben 209€ e usate dal 03/01/2023) queste qua vi posso assicurare che in qualità sonora ovviamente battono le tozo.. ma in durata no!😂 Mi son durate fino maggio-giugno di quest'anno (è una vergogna assoluta che delle cuffie che costano 209€ durino di meno delle cuffie che costano 22,99€🤯). Quando faccio palestra l'allenamento mi dura circa 2h e usando le cuffie 2h la batteria a fine allenamento è ancora a metà!!😍 Invece per la custodia di ricarica dura completamente 3-4 giorni (e ripeto, dopo 2 anni di uso quotidiano, visto che sono una persona che ascolta musica ogni santo giorno, funzionano ancora da dio, senza difetti né niente) anche di quella sono sbalordito! reviews.title: Bon prix, bonne qualité globale👍
reviews.body: J'utilise ces tozo A1 pour écouter principalement des podcasts sur mon lieu de travail, et j'en suis globalement très satisfait. Ils produisent un bon son, même pour la musique, sans être exceptionnel non plus, mais on ne va pas leur reprocher cela à ce prix. Je ne suis pas un audiophile ,mais je ressens quand-même un petit manque de basses... La réduction de bruit est passive et donc incomparable avec de l'a.n.c... c'est quand-même correcte. Franchement ils font le taff, ils sont très agréables à porter, ne provoquent aucunes douleurs pour ma part... Quelques petits détails quand même, le filtre anti poussière à l'air un peu fragile mais bon, n'oublions pas le prix de vente. Aussi, au bout de quelques jours, le volume du son n'était pas le même d'une oreillette à l'autre, sans doute dû à ce filtre... Mais je tiens vraiment à souligner le sérieux et l'excellent travail du service après-vente qui à été à mon écoute et a résolu mon problème de manière efficace et ultra rapide en remplaçant cette paire par une nouvelle... D'une qualité supérieure Svp !! En toute honnêteté, je ne connaissais pas bien la marque Tozo mais je ne peux que vous conseiller de vous orienter vers cette marque très sérieuse et très prometteuse qui prend soin de ses clients !!
reviews.body_en: I use these tozo A1s for mainly listening to podcasts at my workplace, and I'm very happy with them overall. They produce good sound, even for music, without being exceptional either, but we won't blame them for that at this price. I'm not an audiophile, but I still feel a little lack of bass... The noise reduction is passive and therefore incomparable with A.N.C... it's still correct. Frankly they do the job, they are very pleasant to wear, do not cause any pain for me... A few small details though, the dust filter seems a little fragile but hey, let's not forget the sale price. Also, after a few days, the volume of the sound was not the same from one earpiece to another, probably due to this filter... But I really want to underline the seriousness and excellent work of the after-sales service which listened to me and resolved my problem efficiently and extremely quickly by replacing this pair with a new one... Of superior quality Please!! In all honesty, I did not know the Tozo brand well but I can only advise you to go towards this very serious and very promising brand which takes care of its customers!!

reviews.title: Just as Good as the Galaxy Buds FE
reviews.body: Just as Good as the Galaxy Buds FE I previously owned the Galaxy Buds FE and was unsure whether the Galaxy Buds Core would be as good or feel like a downgrade. After using them, I can confidently say that I have found zero noticeable difference between the two when it comes to noise cancelling, overall sound quality, or the experience within the Galaxy Wearable app. The sound is clear and balanced, with good bass and crisp vocals. The active noise cancelling works extremely well and performs just as well as it did on my Galaxy Buds FE. Ambient Sound is also available when you need to hear what is happening around you, and the touch controls make it easy to control your music and switch listening modes. The silicone wingtips help keep the earbuds secure, and each earbud is small and lightweight. They also have an IP54 rating for protection against dust and water splashes, which is a nice feature for workouts and everyday use. Battery life is rated for up to 35 hours with noise cancelling turned off or up to 20 hours with it turned on when using the charging case. The connection has been reliable, and the app provides the same familiar controls and settings that I was used to with the Galaxy Buds FE. Nothing about the Core feels like a major compromise or a step backward. These are fantastic earbuds. For anyone who previously owned the Galaxy Buds FE and cannot decide whether the Galaxy Buds Core are as good, I can confidently say that there is no noticeable difference between the two in the areas that matter most. I am extremely happy with them and would absolutely recommend them.

reviews.title: Best buds for buds+ buddies - but storage case is lacking
reviews.body: I've had the Galaxy Buds Plus for several years. Loved them, but all good things come to an end. I accidentally washed them and now the left one won't work. Can't figure out if it's the bud or the case or both. I wanted something similar - I did NOT want something with a stem. My son has the Buds FE so I tried them. I liked them but they've have been discontinued. What's a girl to do when she likes what she knows and struggles with change? These seem to be the only Samsung buds similar to the old Buds+ and readily available. I dont understand the "latin american stock" part. Reviews seem to indicate the buds will work just fine in the US so I ordered... Mine came with a sticker that says "united arab emirates." Not sure it matters. I'm under the impression that no matter what, buying for a different market than I live in would mean no warranty. I'm hoping since the buds+ never let me down until I washed them, lack of a warranty is ok. Physically they are very similar to the buds+. Almost identical, not quite. The rubbery portion of the core is more front and center and the rubbery portion of the plus is more slanted and to the side. The buds+ might be ever so slightly bigger. The buds+ are also kind of open in the soundhole portion of the rubbery thing whereas with the core, the rubbery thing covers the soundhole and has tiny perforations. The bud+, under the rubbery cover, is kind of metal with small holes, like a colander, whereas with the core it's more like a mesh. If you prefer the open hole rubber cover, it might not be a good idea with these. I'm assuming earwax will get mashed into the mesh but not so much into the colander. Core vs. plus - they feel basically the same in my ears. The left one started to hurt a little after an hour the first time I wore them but they were fine the second time - I think the slight difference in how the tip points requires a slight adjustment in putting them in. It's very minor. The sound is basically what I've been used to with the buds+. I wear these while doing chores or walking. I'm not a music critic or a great judge of amazing sound - I can't tell you if these are up to the task for more demanding things. These seem to block out outside sounds more than my buds+ but if this is something you don't want it's probably something you can change in the settings - I haven't really tried to play around with these yet in the the wearable ap. They're doing what I need them to do right out of the box. Tapping the right core bud pauses and unpauses whatever I am listening to very easily - sometimes I had to fight with the buds+ and in fact sometimes it refused to work at all. Maybe my buds+ got a little finicky with age or maybe these are just better in that regard. I do not like to make calls with earbuds in but I got a phone call while wearing them and the person on the other end was able to hear me just fine. The actual buds are basically perfect - exactly what I want - but I am docking a star for the case. They clearly took some cost-cutting measures with the case. 1. It does not have a light on the inside indicating if the buds are charged, although as soon as I open the case my phone pops up with how much life they have so I can still figure it out. 2. It's very shiny and slippery which makes it easy to drop. The lack of shaping inside the lid for the buds, which most other cases have, bothers me aesthetically but the magnets that hold the buds in to the case are so strong it's not a problem - they're not going anywhere UNLESS you drop the case and it pops open, which I have done. Twice. Everything still works but my buds+ case never popped open like that - in fact the case was still closed tight that horrible day I found it in the washing machine. My son's FEs have gone through the wash twice now and the case has stayed closed (and the buds and case survived). The lid for the buds core lacks a nice tight magnetic closure. If you wanted to go fancier the Buds FE case seems to work and you should be able to buy replacements for those - it has the inner charging light and a stronger closing lid. Of course then you are paying more money. Cheap solution is to get a round zippered earbud case at the dollar store which won't help with the charging light but will at least protect them if they drop. I'm hoping never to find out whether or not these can hold up to washing. Overall I am happy and reccommend these for someone in the market for a buds+ replacement.

When looking at the price of this mouse compared to other gaming mice, this is cheaper, durable, longer-lasting, and has most of the features as the other expensive mice have. I would most certainly recommend any interested buyers looking for a gaming mouse to buy this product. First and foremost, I think that the Redragon gaming mouse is one of the best mice as of right now because it’s cheap and affordable. One of the popular gaming mice that is competing against the redragon mice in the market as of right now would be the glorious model o. reviews.title: Satisfactory
reviews.body: The middle mouse button requires a much harder press to actuate than any mouse I've used. Otherwise it's satisfactory. The left and right mouse buttons as well as the side buttons feel solid and responsive. I'm also pleased to see one of the built-in RGB presets is "off", and so doesn't require downloading software to turn off the lights. Of note, it appears the sensor LED is always at full power, unlike other mice where it dims when the mouse is picked up. Also, you *must* remove the plastic protecting the bottom pads or the mouse will have a lot of friction, and will not glide across any surface (wood or mousepad) as well as expected. The mouse is clearly designed for a palm grip, and will not be as comfortable to use with a claw or fingertip grip.

reviews.title: The best gaming mouse I’ve ever used
reviews.body: I’ve owned and tested many gaming mice over the years, and the Logitech G Superstrike X2 is, without question, the best one I’ve ever used. I don’t play competitively—I mostly enjoy adventure games, action titles, and other immersive experiences—but this mouse has made every gaming session more enjoyable. It combines incredible comfort, premium build quality, and features that genuinely stand out. The biggest highlight for me is the haptic switches. They feel amazing, providing a tactile, satisfying click that makes every input feel deliberate and precise. The feedback is unlike anything I’ve experienced on another mouse, adding a level of immersion that you don’t realize you’re missing until you try it. Combined with the outstanding responsiveness, every click feels fast, consistent, and incredibly satisfying. Another thing I absolutely love is how lightweight it is. It glides effortlessly across the mousepad and never feels fatiguing, even after hours of gaming. The shape is comfortable, the weight is perfectly balanced, and it almost feels like an extension of your hand. The wireless connectivity has also been flawless. It’s fast, stable, and completely reliable, with no noticeable latency or dropouts. It truly delivers the freedom of wireless without any of the compromises that used to come with it. Logitech has once again delivered a premium product. From the build quality to the innovative haptic switches, lightweight design, and rock-solid wireless performance, everything about the Superstrike X2 feels refined and thoughtfully engineered. It’s a mouse that makes you appreciate the little details every time you use it. Overall, this is easily the best mouse I’ve ever owned, and I couldn’t recommend it more. Whether you’re a competitive player or, like me, simply want the best possible experience while enjoying your favorite games, the Logitech Superstrike X2 is absolutely worth it.

reviews.title: Best Mouse I’ve Ever Used
reviews.body: I’ve had this mouse for almost a week now, and I can confidently say it’s hands down the best mouse I’ve ever used. It’s incredibly lightweight, the wireless performance has been flawless, and it just feels high quality overall. I am 35 years old and don't have the best reaction time but this mouse dropped my Human Benchmark reaction time average from 190 ms to around 160 ms. I wasn’t even planning on testing this, but one of my friends told me to try it and see if there was actually a difference. I tested on my old mouse, a Model O, and then back to the Superstrike X2 just to make sure it wasn’t in my head. The difference was still there. Everything just feels quicker and more in control, and the speed and click feel really make a difference. The feeling when you click it is incredibly responsive and smooth. The only thing I can compare it to is clicking an iPhone sleep button. Battery life has been very good also. After about six hours of gameplay, the battery only went from 82% down to 75%, which is impressive for a wireless gaming mouse. Can't recommend this mouse enough to everyone

reviews.title: Really great mouse, but terrible skates.
reviews.body: I absolutely loves this mouse. I usually have stuck to only using razer mice in the past. However I made the switch to this one and its honestly so great. I only really have one complaint and the rest is amazing. Pros: Battery life is honestly amazing. Its really quiet because it no longer clicks, its just haptic feedback like the ps5 controller. You can adjust when it actually clicks which is super cool just like a Hall effect keyboard, because it's the same tech. Mouse just feels great and the included grips are nice, but they do take some getting used to as they aren't what I was expecting. However I have come to like them. Cons: It's vey expensive for a mouse, there's a lot of competition and a variety of mice esp way cheaper. The stock skates are absolutely terrible, that's why I changed them jade's and now its perfect. No complaints after that. However for a mouse this expensive, I was hoping for better skates. I also don't really like the scroll wheel, to be fair I do come from razer mice so that might be why I hate it. It also takes some getting used to as the mouse is front heavy because of the switches on the mouse, but I bet you can fix that if you have a powerplay to balance it out. However I have this mouse for 2 months now and I absolutely love it and I wouldn't switch for another. The only thing I would change if you were buying this mouse today is to also order skates so you can replace them. Would be a 5/5 if it weren't for the terrible skates. TL;DR: Great mouse if purchasing, buy skates as well.

reviews.title: Huge Upgrade!!!
reviews.body: After just a week of using this mouse, I can confidently say this is the best peripheral purchase I have ever made. I initially wasn't in the market for a new mouse, until my scroll wheel broke on my razer mouse. I decided to just pull the trigger on the X2 Superstrike instead of purchasing another razer mouse. The mouse material feel is excellent, and the wheel is great as well. I've also seen some reviews disliking the skates on the X2 Superstrike, however I personally found them to be great. The haptic feedback mouse click seemed a bit gimmicky before I actually used it. Right off the bat, the mouse click feels incredibly responsive and similar to that of any high quality mouse. You get enough feedback and it doesn't feel that much different from a regular mouse click. But, you also have optionality to adjust a ton of settings, like accuation, feedback strength, etc. For gaming, with the right settings, this genuinely feels amazing, and that's before the performance upgrade. As many other reviewers have noted, it noticeably decreases latency on top of all of this. Another huge perk with this mouse I found, was that it's almost dead silent as well. No more loud clicking! My only critique with the mouse are the side buttons and the size. The side buttons are the only part of the mouse that feel "cheap". Because I use the side buttons often in competitive games, I notice it a lot more than probably most people would. I also have large hands, and this is the smallest mouse I have used. I got used to it pretty quick, but the mouse is on the smaller side. Nonetheless, if you are looking to upgrade your mouse and have the money, I would 100% recommend. This feels as impactful as going from a 60hz monitor to a 144hz+.

reviews.title: Side buttons problem
reviews.body: I recently picked up this mouse as my first step into wireless gaming, specifically the Superstrike X2, after using a wired Razer Basilisk V3 for a long time. I’d been thinking about making the switch for a while, and overall I’m glad I did. The main buttons (left and right click) feel excellent — responsive, solid, and satisfying to use. This is clearly where the mouse shines, and it delivers exactly what you’d expect at this price point in terms of core performance. However, the side buttons (the two next to the left click area) are a noticeable weak point. They feel cheap and somewhat out of place, especially when compared to competitors like Razer. Considering the price of this mouse, I expected a higher-quality feel across all buttons, not just the main ones. That said, since the primary clicks and overall performance are what matter most in actual gameplay, I would still recommend this mouse. If you can overlook the side button quality, it’s a strong option for anyone looking to move into wireless gaming. Sorry for the messy mousepad :)

reviews.title: Yes! Beats the G502 Hero (which I liked) and the G502 X (by a lot)
reviews.body: Good god, what a mouse. I mean, it's not perfect; nothing is. But it's so good. I came from years of the G502 Hero; the grips on it were wearing out. I first decided to try a G502 X, as it was supposed to be an improved version of the Hero, essentially. For $25 more than the Basilisk, it pretty much sucked in my opinion. The only thing I could imagine picking it over the Basilisk for is weight. But if you care that much about weight, there are much lighter mice on the market. --- I'll review it as compared to the Hero (and a bit to the X), as that's what I know. They're pretty common, so maybe this will help people out if they're thinking about converting: Initially I wasn't so sure about the grip and the main mouse buttons. The mouse buttons have a rough texture, and I found with my Hero that when my fingers were slightly tacky/damp, they would stick slightly to the surface of the buttons in the same way a clean basketball shoe does to a court (i.e., not "sticky", but grippy). I liked that. But after using it for a while, I think it's totally fine and maybe even better. The feet seem the same to me as the G502 X, which is good. They're white PTFE. Very smooth. The scroll wheel is *fantastic*. Like, it's perfect. It seems to control the mode with an electromagnet, so it makes a cool click sound when the computer is restarted and such. And it even has a setting in the software where you can have it tactile by default, but with a quick flick, it switches to free-spin temporarily. Awesome. And when I move the mouse quickly side to side, there is absolutely no play in the wheel. Nothing. That was one of my annoyances with the Hero. The scroll wheel would wobble audibly and tactilely when in free spin mode with even moderately fast mouse movements. The click noise isn't as nice as I expected, but it's totally fine and better than the X (which was super loud and piercing). I'd put it somewhere between the X and the Hero. It's kind of like if someone built the X and then was like, oh, that sucks, and then made adjustments like a sane human. I believe the Basilisk switches are optical (the Hero is mechanical and the X is hybrid mech/optical), and so maybe that's approximately what happened. In short, I think the Hero is a pretty quiet click, and I think the Basilisk is a very standard click. Sounds like what I'd use as a mouse click if I were a foley artist. The Basilisk's weight is listed at 101g, and it feels quite nice. Not hard to control. I'm sure I'll get even better as we go, though. The palm section is actually quite high! Like, even more than the Hero. It feels pretty good so far. The Basilisk's cable is an absolute work of art. I mean, it's perfect. It's got a soft woven sleeve and is not stiff at all. I had the same kind of reaction to it as I did when I got my current massage shower head and found that no, the tube connecting the head to the spigot doesn't actually have to be stiff at all to do its job. The software is slightly annoying because there's a separate program for the lighting and the mouse (though they're styled identically and could ostensibly be packaged in one app). But its functionality is nice. There are 9 RGB zones around the bottom edge of the mouse, plus one on the scroll wheel and the logo under the palm. They seem rather infinitely adjustable. Neat! --- Hope this helps somebody!

reviews.title: This Mouse Ruined Cheap Mice for Me
reviews.body: I’ve genuinely liked using the Razer Basilisk V3. The first thing I noticed was how comfortable it felt. Some mice are fine for about 20 minutes and then they start feeling like a weirdly shaped brick. This mouse has been much better for longer use, whether I’m gaming or just clicking around online doing whatever nonsense I got distracted by. What I like most is that it feels like someone actually thought about how a hand works. The buttons are responsive, the movement is smooth, and the scroll wheel feels so nice that it almost made reading comment sections worth it. Almost. While this mouse has not been life changing in a dramatic movie soundtrack kind of way, it has changed my expectations enough that going back to a cheaper mouse would feel like using a shopping cart with one bad wheel. Oh, and the customization. I am not out here trying to launch a space mission from my desk, but it is nice being able to set things up in a way that actually fits how I use it. Once everything is dialed in, it just feels easy. Overall, it has been a genuinely solid mouse and one of those upgrades you stop thinking about because it just quietly does its job well. Which, for a mouse, is honestly the dream. It just sits there, minds its business, and makes me slightly more powerful than I probably deserve.

reviews.title: One of my favorite mice and you will love it too
reviews.body: This mouse is just incredibly smooth. Even with its high weight the skates make it super easy to move around and the weight gives it control, resulting in superb aim. The material can make your hands a bit sweaty when death gripping it, but it’s very solid matte surface. You can grip test and throw this mouse across a room without it breaking. The shape this mouse has just fits right in your hand, and the rubber side grips make it super comfortable and easy to use, it’s basically great with any grip type. The skates are super glidey and quiet even when under the weight of this chunker of a mouse. It’s better for bigger hands of course, it’s harder to use with smaller hands but it’s doable. The scroll wheel is the best of any mouse, even the Logitech g502. It has a setting in the software where it can be a tactile scroll wheel when scrolling slowly, but becomes a freely spinning wheel when flicked fast. You can even switch between spinny wheel mode and tactile mode with the click of a button. I loved this mouse so much I upgraded to the wireless version, and I wasn’t sacrificing much leaving wired because the battery life was great on that one. 10/10 mouse.

reviews.title: Good gaming mouse and does what it needs. Just wish it would last longer.
reviews.body: To be honest they don't make mice like they used to. I remember a time where you would buy gaming mice and they would last 5 years minimum. Now a days they last a year if you are lucky. So far this mouse has worked pretty good and seems like it is holding up quite fine. I also want to point out I haven't had this for a very long time and I suspect the build quality of the mouse should last a year if this was anything like my old razor mouse. The scroll wheel is pretty solid. I like how responsive it is. I have never seen a mouse scroll wheel quite like this. Scrolling speed is pretty good. Was able to do a lot of jagged movements and noticed the mouse handled it very well in minecraft. Ergonomic of the mouse are probably the best part. I haven't used a non trackball mouse that felt this great in maybe ever. The programmable buttons I haven't used for anything since I literally have nothing to remotely use them for whatsoever. RGB is decent. Not a selling point for me that is a selling point for some people I guess. With that said I am not sure if I can recommend this just because it seems pretty good but the way gaming mice have been going I don't see this lasting more than a year. I remember a time where mice would last like a decade now they break if you look at them the wrong way. I will say the big pro to a gaming mouse is the fact it is meant for gaming. Yes you are paying a lot of money for something that will break within a year but you pretty much have no choice just because these mice have a sensor in them that is significantly way better than most mice.

reviews.title: Fantastic mouse for those who like it heavy.
reviews.body: I'm an avid PC user and rarely replace my accessories. My mouse especially was hard to replace, as every top end mouse seems to get lighter and lighter. However, after using the Basilisk V3, I can safely say this mouse has been a perfect upgrade from my 2013 Deathadder. It weighs roughly the same, being on the heavier side for a mouse, and that's perfect for me. It's built great, has a fantastic braided cable which is smooth to the touch, it doesn't catch on corners like the older Razer cables, and the RGB is stellar. I really like the ring of RGB that goes around the base, and it's incredibly easy to edit in Razer Synapse. The mouse is also extremely comfortable. I didn't expect a thumb rest to do much, but I'll honestly miss it if I ever have to upgrade. For the price, you really can't go wrong. This mouse is incredible for its price point and well worth investing in if you like to 'feel' your mouse movements.

reviews.title: オススメ出来ると思います。
reviews.body: deathadder v2 proが故障したので買い替えました。 基本的にゲームはしませんが、4Kモニターでdpiの切替を頻繁にするので、切替が手元で出来て、 かつ、ある程度のマクロが割当られる数のボタンが付いたマウスとなると、ゲーミングマウスは最適です。 元々無線マウスだったので、有線になることへの抵抗はありましたが、見た目が太いケーブルは、 思ってた以上に軽く柔らかくなっており、マウスを操作するうえで違和感は感じません。 適度な重さもあり、握りやすさも丁度良く個人的には買い替えて正解でした。 ボタンも一つ増えたので、一番奥のボタンにAlt+F4(ウインドウを閉じる)を割り当ててみましたが、 これが個人的に以外と便利で利用頻度が高いです。 購入してすぐに感じたネガティブな要素(払拭済)として、スクロールホイールの感触が軽すぎる事。 deathadder v2 proはクルクルと回しても、一段一段カチカチと回している感じがあったのが、 本品は殆どフリーなのではないかという位、軽くクルクル回るので、ちょっとなぁと思ってましたが、 SYNAPSE側で設定すると、機械的にホイールの感触が変えられる事が分かり、ちょっと感動。 マウスの進化を感じました。
reviews.body_en: Deathadder v2 pro broke down so I bought a new one. I generally don't play games, but I often switch DPI on a 4K monitor, so a gaming mouse is ideal if you can switch it at hand and have enough buttons to assign a certain amount of macros. Since it was originally a wireless mouse, I was reluctant to switch to a wired mouse, but the thick-looking cable is lighter and softer than I expected, so I don't feel any discomfort when operating the mouse. It has a suitable weight and is easy to grip, so personally, I made the right decision to buy a new one. Since there is one more button, I assigned Alt+F4 (close window) to the innermost button, which I personally find very convenient and use frequently. One negative thing I noticed right after purchasing it (which has already been resolved) is that the scroll wheel feels too light. Even when I turned the deathadder v2 pro, it felt like it was turning one step at a time, but this product spins so lightly that I thought it was almost free, so I thought it was a little weird.However, I was a little impressed when I found out that you can change the feel of the wheel mechanically by setting it on the SYNAPSE side. I felt the evolution of the mouse.

reviews.title: Great mid range mouse option
reviews.body: My previous mice include the Razer Deathadder V2, Razer Basilisk V2 X Hyperspeed, and the Logitech Pro X Superlight. This is easily the most comfortable mouse I've used, the contours feel perfect and the extra button the side is well placed and feels like a natural addition. I've personally not found the weight an issue, though it is much heavier that most other mice, even ones that use a AA battery. I do prefer the external battery as I disliked having to plug in my mouse every so often to charge it, something that became much more frequent as the internal battery lost capacity. The new switches feel excellent, a noticeable improvement from the V2. Performance is good in all areas with the exception of the scroll wheel, which feels like it eats inputs for breakfast lunch and dinner. Basically when scrolling fast the Basilisk V3 seems to skip inputs. My V2 had similar issues and eventually I had to replace it when the scroll wheel started acting haywire and scrolling on its own or backwards. Something to keep an eye on. Appearance is unremarkable. The new RGB scroll wheel is appreciated, but fairly simple in customization. I have it set to static color but you can have it be reactive to clicking, color cycle, breathing, or a few other options with Razer Synapse. One small quirk is that if you have auto sleep on, it takes a bit to actually turn back on when using it again. Whereas the Razer Deathadder V2 was near instant in my experience, the Basilisk V3 takes a few seconds to get going, which sounds like nothing but does make a difference when it happens so often. TL;DR - It's a really good mouse at this price point, good performance and great comfort. Only negative is the scroll wheel and the weight if that matters to you.

reviews.title: Not as good as a 3S, but less expensive. Hopefully better quality switches than the 3S.
reviews.body: I like this mouse, but it could be better. I purchased it to replace a Logitech MX-Master 3S, which is a great mouse except the microswitch for the left button stopped being reliable after less than three years. While that's a reasonable life for some users, perhaps, it seemed inadequate to me. My use case is general pc use for searching the web, writing emails, and managing finances. The Logitech wasn't used every day. The 3S has a higher palm hump, which the Basilisk lacks and I really prefer. The Basilisk is similar in overall size to the 3S, so for the most part it fits my hand sufficiently well. Hump size is the main downside to the Basilisk. That, plus the battery is not rechargeable. What, in 2026?! But I've adapted to it, and battery life so far has been very good. It has the combo BT + 2.4 gHz connectivity with a dongle. Both choices work very well and reliably. I like the center wheel size and action a lot. I like the slip pads on the bottom of the mouse. It has a very handy and perfectly responsive third thumb button that I don't currently use but gamers may find it useful. Only time will tell if Razer's microswitch quality is more durable, reliable, and longer lived than the crap switches Logitech put into the otherwise very good 3S. I have used the Basilisk about two months at the time of this review.

reviews.title: Good stock of beater mice for troubleshooting PCs! Also great for deployment to offices, schools!
reviews.body: I like to fix up and troubleshoot computers in my office, but I always have to use my good mouse to access the system. The Amazon Vine Program pointed me to this 6-pack of bulk wired computer mice, and I thought it would be a perfect addition to my office workshop. This is the 6-pack of wired USB silent computer mice, under the aptly branded "WYQQXZYKJ". It all comes tightly packed together in a small cardboard box. You get exactly what is shown, 6 black computer mice, with about a 4.5ft (or 1.5m) USB wire attached to it. It's an extremely basic computer mouse. You get the essential mouse functions: left click, right click, and scroll wheel. It uses an optical red laser, and 1000 DPI is adequate for basic desktop navigation. It's symmetrically shaped for both the left and right-handed. The most interesting part of the mouse is the silent clicking action, which makes this mouse one step up from an otherwise totally no-frills deal. I'm not going to totally knock the mouse for how basic it is, as it's actually useful for troubleshooting PCs. Sometimes you don't need all the extra buttons, bells, and whistles. I'm tired of using my good computer mice with random computers. I had one incident where I accidentally left the wireless dongle in a PC I sold, rendering a good $100 computer mouse totally useless. When you tinker, work on, and refurbish PCs, it helps to have a good stock of beater mice on hand when you need to get the OS installed and updated, or to work into what's gumming up the system. This bulk pack makes it all ideal for this purpose. The listing advertises itself for home, office, school lab, and PC gaming use in the title (at the time of review), but I find the PC gaming part to be a huge stretch. I wouldn't recommend this mouse for any serious gaming. Beyond troubleshooting PCs, I'd imagine another ideal use for a bulk pack of mice is to deploy them with a fleet of computers, like in an office, library, or school lab setting. Silent clicking makes it incredibly ideal, as you probably wouldn't prefer to listen to loud mouse clicks from dozens of people all day. $14 for a six-pack, along with additional options for 12, 30, 80, or even a 120 pack, is all an excellent deal if you need a bulk supply of basic computer mice. Overall, I recommend!

reviews.title: Great Troubleshooting Spares—Excellent Backup Value for the Workshop
reviews.body: Great Troubleshooting Spares—Excellent Backup Value for the Workshop Sometimes you just absolutely have to use a wired mouse. Whether you are actively troubleshooting a finicky system, working with a legacy machine, configuring a bare-metal OS before Bluetooth drivers are installed, or simply requiring a tactile interface over an integrated trackpad, keeping a basic wired mouse on hand is incredibly convenient. I maintain an office closet with multiple servers running continuously, and even premium wireless hardware—whether running over standard Bluetooth or proprietary wireless dongles—can occasionally suffer from dropped signals or jittery tracking. A basic wired connection, by contrast, connects smoothly and works instantly with almost any architecture. I originally only required two fresh mice for my setup, but this package arrives as a bulk six-pack. While six is more than I strictly needed, the low unit cost makes it incredibly convenient to scatter them around as utility tools—stashing one directly inside a portable system repair toolbox, leaving a couple hooked up to the local server rack, and keeping a spare tucked away inside the main desk drawer. I tested the compatibility across both macOS and Windows environments using a direct native USB-A link as well as a standard USB-A to USB-C adapter, and every unit initialized immediately without any manual configuration. The only minor caveat to note is the overall physical feel: these mice are lightweight and inexpensive and you can tell when you hold it. To provide an exact point of comparison, these units weigh roughly 44 grams, whereas a standard daily driver like the Logi Pebble 2 sits closer to 77 grams. The physical disparity is immediately noticeable in the hand, and the main click buttons feel decidedly hollow and basic. That said, the microswitches registers cleanly and activated successfully every time they were pressed. If you are looking for a premium, ergonomic daily driver for an eight-hour workday, this isn't the right fit. However, if you need a reliable, cost-effective bundle of utility mice to distribute throughout a workshop, tech bag, or server rack, this multi-pack handles the job perfectly. -- How my star ratings work: 5 Stars: Very positive. High quality/design. Fully accomplishes goals. I’d likely buy again. 4 Stars: Positive. Good quality. Accomplishes goals, but there might be better alternatives. 3 Stars: Neutral. Medium quality or design quirks limit its utility. Caution advised. 2 Stars: Low quality. Design flaws make it hard to recommend. 1 Star: Negative experience. Serious flaws or poor quality. Not recommended.

I tested the compatibility across both macOS and Windows environments using a direct native USB-A link as well as a standard USB-A to USB-C adapter, and every unit initialized immediately without any manual configuration. The only minor caveat to note is the overall physical feel: these mice are lightweight and inexpensive and you can tell when you hold it. To provide an exact point of comparison, these units weigh roughly 44 grams, whereas a standard daily driver like the Logi Pebble 2 sits closer to 77 grams. The physical disparity is immediately noticeable in the hand, and the main click buttons feel decidedly hollow and basic. That said, the microswitches registers cleanly and activated successfully every time they were pressed. If you are looking for a premium, ergonomic daily driver for an eight-hour workday, this isn't the right fit. However, if you need a reliable, cost-effective bundle of utility mice to distribute throughout a workshop, tech bag, or server rack, this multi-pack handles the job perfectly. -- How my star ratings work: 5 Stars: Very positive. High quality/design. Fully accomplishes goals. I’d likely buy again. 4 Stars: Positive. Good quality. Accomplishes goals, but there might be better alternatives. 3 Stars: Neutral. Medium quality or design quirks limit its utility. Caution advised. 2 Stars: Low quality. Design flaws make it hard to recommend. 1 Star: Negative experience. Serious flaws or poor quality. Not recommended.

reviews.title: Good Value for Basic Use
reviews.body: For around $14 for a pack of six, I really can't complain too much. These mice definitely feel cheaply made, but considering the price, that's kind of what I expected. They work fine for basic tasks like browsing the internet, schoolwork, or simple office applications. The buttons respond well enough, and they're easy to plug in and start using without any setup. That said, I wouldn't recommend these for gaming or as your primary mouse for everyday office work. They just don't have the solid feel or precision that I'd want if I were using one for hours every day. The lightweight plastic construction makes them feel more like disposable or backup mice than something built for long-term use. Where I think these really shine is in places like schools, computer labs, libraries, or offices that need multiple inexpensive replacement mice. If one breaks, it's not a huge deal because you still have several more in the box. Overall, I wouldn't call them high quality, but I also don't think they're a bad purchase. If you're looking for an affordable bulk pack of basic wired mice, they do exactly what they're meant to do. Just keep your expectations realistic for the price.

reviews.title: The mouse meets expectations and that is about it.
reviews.body: The mouse meets expectations and that is about it. The mouse works, is lightweight, similar shape to the g pro. The mouse is tiny, because I have bigger hands this made it difficult to operate it. That is mainly a me problem but I do want to mention it for others. Because the mouse is 40 dollars it has its drawbacks. Battery needs to be recharged every week or so, but the cable provided is hardly noticeable unlike the g pro. The mouse buttons feel heavy compared to other mice that I had. There is a lot of wiggle room when it comes to how far you have to press to get the actual actuation. (G pro, G pro superlight, g pro superlight 2, g502 x, model O) The mouse is base side heavy. So the weight of the mouse is not spread out. When you hold the mouse you can tell that you not actually moving the whole mouse. This makes fingertip grip harder to use because you really need to engage your palm to more easily move the base. Its still a light mouse so you can really get away with this. I have not needed to use the bluetooth yet so I have no idea how that latency is. The mouse is tiny, because I have bigger hands this made it difficult to operate it. That is mainly a me problem but I did want to mention it. I have had no issues with connectivity when using the USB into my docking station. The plastic case is cheap . I feel like I could easily bend the plastic just by pushing my thumb into it. Overall, I would say save your money and save up for a mouse that meets all of the criteria, but this isn't a bad mouse for $40

reviews.title: A preference based knockout
reviews.body: To begin- I should state that I've been in the mouse community for a few years now and I've purchased mice from many different brands, big or relatively little. I've used Razer, Logitech, SteelSeries, Zowie, Corsair, Glorious, Pulsar, etc. I always seem to find myself coming back to either Razer or Logitech for specific needs that other brands don't necessarily offer. I have a lengthy history with Razer products, and that includes their Viper line of mice. I've owned the original, the mini, the ultimate edition, the 8khz wired release, as well as the Viper V2 Pro. There was one thing that kept my away from these mice for so long- shape. The original Viper mice, while excellent, weren't good for me comfort wise. The hump wasn't pronounced enough, and the curvature on the sides would cramp my hand every single time. I know, I know- why keep buying a mouse with a shape that makes you uncomfortable? Best answer: I like symmetrical mice, and other than shape, the Viper was/is amazing. Enter the V3 Hyperspeed! I was leaning towards 4.5 stars, but since I can't post a half star I'm comfortable rounding up. The V3 boasts a few changes that, in my personal opinion, are upgrades. The sides of the mouse are less aggressive with their curvature and I found them to be much more comfortable for my hands which are roughly 20x11. They've also done away with any worry of your ring finger clipping the side of your secondary click. They gave this mouse the same treatment the Deathadder V3 pro received. Weight isn't bad at all. It's around 82-83 grams with the included alkaline aa battery. I was able to get it down to a comfortable 70ish by using a lithium aaa and a separate aaa to aa conversion kit. This can be reduced even further by placing a small piece of aluminum foil between the battery(+) and the mouse's contact point. And another point to add- batteries. This mouse is NOT rechargeable, and it does NOT come with any included cables. For some this may be a deal breaker, but for me it's perfect. I don't mind rechargeable mice, but with 4K polling becoming the new " standard " I imagine constant charging could be a nuisance. However, there's a kit on here from PowerOwl that contains 8 aaa batteries and a charging system. I paid around $30 for the rechargeable lithiums and the aaa to aa converters in total. The converters came in a 10 pack so that was nice. This mouse is paired with my Hyperpolling dongle which can be purchased separately, or bundled together with this mouse when purchased from Razer. This. Thing. Is. Insane. When it comes to tracking accuracy I have absolutely nothing bad to say. The Focus Pro 30K in this mouse is the same sensor found in their flagships. Kudos to Razer for implementing that into their Hyperspeed line, which is widely recognized as their budget tier lineup. A few grievances of mine are that M2 ( right mouse click ) is considerably light. It might just be a case of heavy finger, but I found myself accidentally actuating the click at times. The side buttons are different in the fact that they are separated and have a bit of space between them. This is a good change, but I utilize M5 ( front side button ) as a Hypershift key, and it makes it a bit more difficult to hit M4 due to that split in distance. If you don't use Hypershift, then this should be of no concern. My copy has no creaking on the shell, no severe rattle, and the clicks are very crisp. I attribute that to the Gen 2 mechanical switches Razer are using in this mouse. For $70 you can't beat this, in my opinion! You're getting an insane amount of performance for a reasonable price. Pair this with a 4K polling dongle, grab some lithium rechargeable batteries, a few converters and you'll be fragging without the worry of cable drag in no time! Final score: 4.5/5 Amazing job, Razer!
