The converters came in a 10 pack so that was nice. This mouse is paired with my Hyperpolling dongle which can be purchased separately, or bundled together with this mouse when purchased from Razer. This. Thing. Is. Insane. When it comes to tracking accuracy I have absolutely nothing bad to say. The Focus Pro 30K in this mouse is the same sensor found in their flagships. Kudos to Razer for implementing that into their Hyperspeed line, which is widely recognized as their budget tier lineup. A few grievances of mine are that M2 ( right mouse click ) is considerably light. It might just be a case of heavy finger, but I found myself accidentally actuating the click at times. The side buttons are different in the fact that they are separated and have a bit of space between them. This is a good change, but I utilize M5 ( front side button ) as a Hypershift key, and it makes it a bit more difficult to hit M4 due to that split in distance. If you don't use Hypershift, then this should be of no concern. My copy has no creaking on the shell, no severe rattle, and the clicks are very crisp. I attribute that to the Gen 2 mechanical switches Razer are using in this mouse. For $70 you can't beat this, in my opinion! You're getting an insane amount of performance for a reasonable price. Pair this with a 4K polling dongle, grab some lithium rechargeable batteries, a few converters and you'll be fragging without the worry of cable drag in no time! Final score: 4.5/5 Amazing job, Razer!

reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised how good it is
reviews.body: For years I have been a fan of the Razer Viper series. I've had a wired version, and now 3 of the original wireless Viper ultimate's, and now this one. I liked the wireless so much even though my wired version still works I bought the first 2 ultimate's to replace it. This is so I had one at home and one at work. Well I lost one of them on a work trip and after years one of them stopped worked (not sure what happened) but it was pretty old at that point). I keep buying the old ultimate version because I like the side grips and don't mind the slight weight increase they bring. The old version is typically cheaper than the newer one anyway and I don't mind the slight weight increase it probably brings. While this version is slightly heavier than my old ultimate and doesn't have the side grips. It's still lighter than many mice out there and still easy to pick up without the side grips. I will spend a little more for the ultimate for my home mouse because I still like it better and it is lighter weight. But for work this is more than sufficient and was much cheaper. The viper series has been known to be one of the top rated mice on the market for years and I will continue to buy it for years to come. Also I don't care about the RGB so its nice this one doesn't come with any. The only downside of that is that its harder to tell when its low on battery. Guess you could say its a double edged sword. The only downside I have to this mouse is I think they removed the side buttons on the right which I frequently used to refresh web pages. But I don't feel the need to do that as often as I used to so I think its a compromise I am willing to make here especially for the price. This is still the most comfortable mice I've ever used, super smooth tracking, built quality is good, and you don't have holes in the mouse which would allow dust to build up inside (let alone if you spilled something in there or had food on your hands. For gaming I'm sure its pretty good although since I use this at the office I haven't tried that yet. But for the price I don't think you can beat this.

reviews.title: The Ultimate Ambidextrous Endgame! 45 Days of Heavy Gaming and Pure Perfection
reviews.body: I am coming back to write this review after putting this mouse through its paces for a solid 45 days. After upgrading my desktop with a premium 8K magnetic keyboard, I knew my mouse setup had to match that elite level of performance. That is why I pulled the trigger on the latest Razer Viper V4 Pro, and after a month and a half of intense daily use, it has completely redefined my gaming experience. If you are looking for the absolute pinnacle of symmetrical gaming mice, this is the endgame. First, let us talk about the design because there is a lot of confusion out there. This Viper V4 Pro is a flawless, perfectly symmetrical shape. It is a completely different beast compared to the older, bulky, asymmetrical right-handed design of the DeathAdder V4 Pro. As someone who prefers a claw/fingertip grip for high-precision micro-adjustments, this symmetrical shell melts into my hand perfectly, giving my thumb and fingers ultimate control. At a mind-blowing 49 grams, the weight distribution is pure wizardry. Combined with the native 8000Hz polling rate and the 50K DPI sensor, the tracking feels like an extension of my own nervous system. In high-APM gaming sessions and chaotic shooters like World War Z or CS2, swapping targets is instantaneous with zero initial drag. Furthermore, it is an absolute dream for massive open-world action games like Where Winds Meet. During high-stakes martial arts combat, dodging, executing flawless parries, and rapidly controlling the 3D camera feels incredibly smooth and responsive. There is absolutely no pixel-skipping or camera stutter, giving me perfect situational awareness. Out of the box and after 45 days of absolute abuse, the build quality feels incredibly solid despite being so incredibly light—no creaking, no flexing, and the Gen-4 optical switches offer a crisp, satisfyingly tactical click that hasn't degraded a bit. If I have to nitpick, running this monster at a full, unrestricted native 8K polling rate does drain the battery significantly faster than standard mice. It is a trade-off for infinite performance. However, the real sweet spot here is the 4K polling rate mode. With about 3 to 4 hours of gaming per day on the 4K setting, the mouse can easily coast for 8 to 10 days straight without even completely draining the battery to zero. This exceptional power efficiency completely eliminates any battery anxiety. Also, the premium price tag might make your wallet sweat, but for a top-tier esports weapon, you absolutely get what you pay for. To sum it all up, the Viper V4 Pro is the undisputed king of symmetrical lightweight mice. It delivers unrivaled performance, unparalleled speed, and an incredibly locked-in grip. It has officially earned a permanent spot as the perfect crown jewel for my high-end setup. Highly recommended! Money well spent!

reviews.title: This is just one of my favorite mice now
reviews.body: TLDR: This is the mouse I keep coming back to. Long story short, I want nothing more when using this mouse. I'm one of those that just collects mice. I have my favorites, and I have some that I have just used once and put away. This is one that I keep bringing out. Simply put, the latest Viper and Deathadder are just some of my favorite mice period. They are built very solid, light weight, and flawless sensors. They have an instant wake up, fantastic battery life, satisfying clicks, great scroll wheel, and great side buttons. They are pricey, but quality-wise, it really doesn't get better than Razer now. And I'm comparing to Zowie, Logitech, G-wolves, Finalmouse, Pulsar, etc etc... Every one of those other brands has something I don't like in the quality alone, a creak, spongy click, or something keeps me from wanting to use those brands since I've used the Viper. Obviously, the shape is subjective, so if you've used the Viper V3 and didn't like the shape, you're not gonna like this. But I love the size shape, and weight. I can't wait to see the next Deathadder shed some weight to around 49g, and maybe implement some analog switches like the Logitech Superstrike. If they ever did that, I just hope they do weight balancing better because the superstrike is pretty front heavy, but I'm perfectly happy with Razer's optical switches because they just feel sooooo good. But I think the haptic analog switches would be very interesting in the Deathadder shape. I really don't know how they could improve on this other than finding more ways to lighten the weight even more. Razer might've perfected the Viper with this iteration.

reviews.title: Great Gaming Mouse for 2026
reviews.body: This is the best gaming mouse as someone who upgraded from a regular stock mouse. The weight, the functionality, and the design of the mouse is perfect. In fact, this mouse, and it features had further fine-tuned my already decent aim. After using this mouse for a while, I have observed my aim became a natural aim bot, where I was even accused of potentially exploiting in a match of BF1. The mouse itself is light, and as someone who came from a heavier mouse it felt a bit weird at first. However, if you can manage it, then it becomes a benefit. It allows you to flick quickly, and track targets consistently, which is where my claim of "natural aim bot" came from. It's not too light where you might find yourself tensing up too much to keep it in place, but if you came from a heavier mouse, then you might overflick your target a few times. The features the mouse offered through Razer's Synapse software such as the DPI and mappings are very useful. You can set different profiles for different games, so there are different DPI's for each game. In addition, you can change the mouse's buttons to be mapped to keys on your keyboard. For example, you can have the side button mapped to 'R', so you can reload through the side button. You can also have the same side buttons run a macro, so if you're playing Helldivers 2, you can instantly input a stratagem through your side button. There are also features like letting the side buttons launch a program. The mouse also features polling rates up to 8k, where higher rates increases the consistency of your cursor's tracking across the screen, and decreases latency. HOWEVER, higher rates can drain the battery life faster, and require specific hardware. Increased polling rates will put higher loads onto your CPU, so ensure you have a strong enough CPU. Otherwise, CPU intensive games will suffer FPS drops, or in general, some games might have issues or do not even support said polling rates. In addition, to notice the different in polling rates, a monitor with a higher refresh rate will be required. Regardless, using 2k and 4k, I haven't really noticed a difference as someone who has a 180hz monitor. It feels the same as 1k polling rate, but if you have the hardware to support it, use it! Regarding the battery life, it's very very good. I have used 2k and 4k polling rates for hours in a day, and the battery only goes down from 100% to like 96%. Whereas if you use 1k polling rate, then the battery doesn't even drain at all till the next day or two maybe (I charge it overnight once the day ends). Upgrading from a wired mouse, and as someone who was a firm believer that wired mice was better, this mouse changed that. I found the wireless mode of this mouse more consistent, than my wired mouse, and offered more freedom in wrist/arm movement. Therefore, I was able to track better. Also, the latency was small on it, perhaps even better. However, you can use the USB cable and plug it into the mouse if you'd like to use it wired. The design of the mouse is comfortable for those who use a claw grip. I typically have my palm touching the mouse, and my fingers in a claw like stance on it. I found no discomfort, and was able to consistently aim. As for other grips, I do not know. If you're upgrading from a stock mouse, then this is worth the upgrade. However, please read other reviews, if you're upgrading from like Razer's Viper V3 Pro mouse, then it might not be worth the money. Since the V3 shares many similarities to the V4 with a few new features. Overall, this might be one of the best mice on the market right now. This mouse ended up being the final piece in the puzzle for me towards perfect aim. Somehow, my peripherals were holding me back, where it is typically the opposite.

reviews.title: The perfect mouse?
reviews.body: I don’t typically write reviews, but this mouse is hands down the best I’ve ever had the pleasure of using, so I feel like I must. The moment my hand gripped the mouse, I knew it was the one. The build quality is fantastic. Everything. From the clicks to the sensor, the scroll wheel and the side buttons. Everything is perfect. The coating on the mouse is high quality and the dongle that comes with it is nicely weighted so it doesn’t slip around on your desk. The stock skates are also wonderful and glide around on my Artisan Zero Soft so smoothly. The size and shape is perfect for my grip style (relaxed claw) so I can handle it comfortably. Since I bought the Razer Viper V4 Pro, I’ve seen a massive improvement in my gameplay. And for that reason I can confidently justify the price of this product. 5 Stars. Genuinely amazing product across the board. Dare I say perfect. 👍 ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

reviews.title: Left me Surprised in a Good Way
reviews.body: This mouse took me by surprise. Coming from the Basilisk V3 Pro, this one is just so lightweight that I almost mistook it for a toy. I seriously can't believe how light this is. The battery life is phenomenal, and the controls are astoundingly tight. The buttons on my Basilisk always felt cheap and mushy, but every button on this Viper V4 Pro is snappy and solid. Getting to the part people care about most, this is probably the most fluid mouse I've ever used. The 50K sensor is a marketing ploy, as I don't use anything over 6400DPI, but you can turn on the 8K polling with a high refresh rate monitor and you won't see any dragging of your cursor across your screen as you will with lower refresh rates, and the higher polling rate shows your mouse's location on the screen more times per second than traditional 1K polling rates. My eyes can see the difference, but only if I strain to see it. I run the mouse at 1K polling rate for optimal battery life and because most games are using that rate the most effectively. It's a sweet spot. So the reasons to get the mouse are simple: lightweight, long battery life, no skipping, truly ambidextrous. The cons: no wireless charging, and no RGB. But those are apparent tradeoffs for that impossibly light 49 gram feel.

reviews.title: Is it worth the upgrade?
reviews.body: The Razer Viper V4 Pro is a flagship-level esports mouse that doubles down on performance rather than reinventing the formula. It features an ultra-lightweight ambidextrous design at around 49–50g, paired with Razer’s Focus Pro 50K optical sensor capable of 50,000 DPI, 930 IPS tracking, and 90G acceleration. It also introduces Gen-4 optical switches, improved wireless performance with an upgraded dongle, and up to 180 hours of battery life. On paper, it’s one of the most technically refined mice available fast, consistent, and clearly built for competitive play. That said, if you already own the Razer Viper V3 Pro, there’s honestly no real reason to upgrade. The improvements here are incremental slightly better battery life, marginally upgraded switches, and small refinements that you’re not going to feel in-game. The V3 Pro is already insanely lightweight, responsive, and accurate, so the V4 Pro ends up feeling more like a spec bump than a meaningful evolution. Unless you’re chasing absolute top-end specs for the sake of it, you’re better off sticking with the V3 Pro. As a stand alone mouse, I give it 4 stars. As a "upgrade" to the previous generation I'd give it one star.

reviews.title: New main. Excellent mouse with a ridiculous battery life
reviews.body: The box didn't have much protection, but it arrived in great condition. As for the mouse itself, it is amazing. I won't talk much about shape because that's highly subjective (I'll just say it fits my hand size and grip style), but everything else is excellent: coating is smooth and grippy, very nice to the touch; main clicks are light and tactile, tho they could have a little less post travel; side buttons are well tensioned and positioned; the wheel might be the weakest aspect, because the scrolling feels a bit off, but it's totally functional; M3 click is very tactile; skates are smooth and fast; build quality is perfect, solid as a rock; performance is top tier, no complaints; and finally, the battery is absolutely insane. I have been using the mouse for 12 days at 1000hz (sometimes 8000, but only for a couple of Apex matches) and it has only gone down to 60%. On top of all of that, Razer has finally made a web software. That means 2 things: 1) you don't have to deal with the bloatware that is Synapse (except for firmware updates); and 2) you can change your settings on Linux, which has been a game changer for me (I dual boot Windows 11 and Bazzite). I think it is worth the price, but only if you don't have a Viper V3 Pro (or even a Viper V3 Pro SE). On paper, the V4 Pro has many improvements, but the only real upgrade that a player will notice is the battery life and the web software. I recommend it to people who have never owned a Viper V3 and want the latest technology and power efficiency. I can recommend it to those who just want to try the shape, but they might also want to take a look at the V3 Pro, since it is cheaper right now.

reviews.title: Worthy of the praise
reviews.body: I have been using it a full week now, and I think it's worth all the praise. It's a safe shape that will work for everyone except if your hands are on the smaller side. Switches, side buttons, scroll wheel, and sensor all feel perfect. My honest favorite thing about this mouse is the battery life is otherworldly good compared to anything I have used. I likely won't have to charge it until about 5-6 weeks of moderate to heavy use at 1000Hz, which is huge when I need to charge my other mice practically after a weekend. The first negative is the price is steep, especially when you could get the V3 Pro Se for like have the price. Two, the M1/M2 switches are on the loud side, but you won't notice them with headphones. You will annoy anyone around you though if they have to listen to you click. Three, the black version is a bit of an oil magnet, but the coating at least feels good. Might be worth using either Razer's provided grips or another brands for long-term use. Overall, it's a very good mouse if it's within your price range, and your hands are moderately large in size. Maybe it's placebo, but I also dropped my first nuke in Call of Duty on keyboard and mouse using it. That might be influencing might personal opinion of it, but I promise it's a great mouse.

reviews.title: G502 X Plus -- A Worthy successor to earlier G502's for FPS games
reviews.body: The 2022 Logitech G502 X Plus was a very pleasant surprise. It is replacing a Logitech G-Pro that is roughly 80 grams weight on a Logitech Powerplay mouse pad (expanded cover for extra space and non-stop charging), primarily used for Overwatch2. Other gaming mice in my collection include earlier G502's, G903, Razer Death Adder + Copperhead, Steelseries Rival3 and Rival600, etc. Generally the best performers in FPS games are the lightest units with the best optical sensors, and the G502 X Plus definitely fits that criteria. Pros: -Comfortable ergonomic shape for marathon gaming sessions -PTFE mouse feet for super-smooth glide across mouse pads -The new optical hybrid switches are incredibly fast compared to the G-Pro's older Omron switches, with a nice crisp click and improved actuation. They will last much longer than conventional mechanical switches and correct double-clicking issues. My last G-Pro's right rear thumb switch suffered from double-clicking issues since they were the old Omron mechanicals that wore out from constant use. -Nice RGB lighting if you are looking for that kind of bling -This mouse wakes from sleep mode instantly (like the G-Pro series). The old G502 Hero Wireless required a full second to wake up, making the old sleep mode feature extremely inconvenient and annoying. -At 106 grams list weight, the G502 X Plus is a tad heavier for a gaming mouse. However, coming from an 80 gram G-Pro, I notice better aim stability without sacrificing flick aim consistency. With the Powerplay charging puck attached and USB receiver stored inside, the G502 X Plus hits 110g on my postal scale. The G502 Hero wireless is 120g with the same accessories. Cons: -No more adjustable weights like its predecessor G502, but to be fair, the whole e-sport industry has shifted competitive user demand to lighter weight mice for the fastest aim flicks possible. -Battery power drains faster with RGB lighting at full settings. This is mitigated by reducing RBG brightness to 85% and shortening idle-mode entry from 2 minutes down to 1. Using a Logitech Powerplay mouse pad, my mouse battery power hovers around 78% to 90% steady with RGB enabled. -The mouse's black finish tends to have shiny oil stains and wear marks over time. This is why I apply blue painter's tape to the areas most prone to this issue. EDIT Feb 2024 - I've replaced the blue painter's tape with automotive carbon fiber vinyl wrap for better visual appeal. Not recommended if you do not like the feel of textured carbon fiber, but it definitely gets rid of those shiny oil stains. Picture attached. -GHub software will not allow users less than 3 DPI presets, and all of these have to be different values at 50dpi intervals. I tried to "lock" my mouse at 1000dpi to avoid accidental DPI switching, but the software would not allow me to do this, so I ended up moving my DPI cycling button to the default profile button up top and removing the up/down DPI adjustment buttons next to the left click. This gave me two additional buttons for other programable functions (like Alt and middle-mouse click since pressing the mouse wheel down can feel awkward). EDIT -- GHUB finally fixed this issue. I can now run with just 1000dpi single setting. -The new hybrid mechanical switches have a different click sound compared to conventional switches -- not really louder, but definitely more metallic. Yes, this mouse is expensive, but the combination of lighter weight + excellent ergonomics + fast/crisp long-wear switches makes this model very hard to beat. If you are looking for a mouse with more weight and heft, then you may not be happy with the G502 X since the latest model has been redesigned for the e-sports crowd. The G502 X now combines lighter weight with an ergo shape, something that most ultra-light mouse offerings lack. NOTE: If you want the best wireless mouse experience, I recommend pairing the G502 X Plus with a Logitech Powerplay for non-stop wireless charging while using the mouse. For those that want a larger mouse pad than what the default Powerplay size offers, check out "Logitech powerplay mousepad expansion mod" on youtube. I have my set-up displayed in the attached images along with actual weight compared to the old G502 Wireless. Update 4/26/2023: The Glorious XL mousepad is the perfect thickness for this Powerplay expansion mod. EDIT: I just read a few other reviews claiming that the G502 X feels "cheap" because it feels too light. The whole point of lowering mouse weight is to minimize mass, thereby requiring less physical energy / effort to move the mouse quickly and accurately. This is how modern e-sports mice are designed, because a lighter mouse is a faster mouse, while a heavier one is a slower boat anchor that is usually on the losing end of an FPS fire fight. The G502 X Plus is only 10 grams lighter than the G502 hero, yet it is much easier to flick-aim than the older G502 Hero Wireless. Also, if you want RGB on the G502 X, you have to get the Plus edition, other wise you get no RGB. Yet one newer review complained about missing RGB LED's on his G502 X non-Plus edition. Going no-RGB is still a valid choice since it saves a few grams, extends battery life, and costs less, but just make sure you know what you are buying ahead of time. ;)

reviews.title: Exactly what you would expect from a direct upgrade.
reviews.body: TBH if your looking for a G502/HERO/Lightspeed replacement there is no complaints in my opinion. Its just a hair bit wider then the previous 502s almost unnoticeable but if you hold them together there is a slight difference. The battery life for it so far has been good for me only been having to charge it like once a week it feels like. It feels like a upgraded 502 lightspeed which is what is. I like that they gave us a option to replace the thumb button with a flat cover that matches the mouse curve so you dont have to have the thumb button for those of us like myself who accidentally press it and never actually use it. Compared to what we paid at launch for the g502 it feels comparable for value and performance. The scroll wheel feels like a nice upgrade from the deep groves to more of a slightly grooved surface thats easy to catch with your finger without issues. The only thing could probably complain about is lack of weights for those who like the weighted options is not super light but its definitely not as heavy as the previous models so people who like the weight of the 502 hero or lightspeed with weights it is gonna be lighter. I like how they changed the charging cable over to the C type charger just like the G733 headphones it still slides it like before but its alot easier to slide in and out and the cable has a good hold when plug in without that feeling like you might rip it if you pull to hard. Other than that software wise minus the RBG change on the body of the mouse it does everything the same as the HERO and Lightspeed models so its pretty much a direct upgrade and replace without having to relearn or figure new stuff out.

reviews.title: Great gaming mouse

The mouse feels very well built and comfortable to use, even during longer gaming sessions. The clicks are crisp, the scroll wheel feels solid, and the sensor tracks flawlessly. I also really like having the extra programmable buttons. They've already become useful for both gaming and general productivity. While I can't speak to the long term durability yet, my first impression has been extremely positive. I honestly don't have any complaints so far. If it continues performing this well over time, it'll easily be one of the best gaming mice I've owned. If you're looking for a high quality wireless gaming mouse that's easy to set up and performs exactly as you'd expect, I'd definitely recommend giving this one a look.

reviews.title: My New Gaming Sidekick: The Logitech G502 X Plus!
reviews.body: Alright, let's talk about the new star of my desk setup – the Logitech G502 X Plus Wireless Gaming Mouse. As someone who spends a good chunk of time in front of the PC, this isn't just a peripheral; it's practically an extension of my hand, and honestly, it feels like it was designed specifically for me. First off, the wireless freedom is a game-changer (pun absolutely intended). Ditching the cable is just chef's kiss for decluttering and those intense gaming sessions where every millisecond counts. And the LIGHTSPEED Optical connection? Flawless. There's no perceptible lag, no hiccups, just pure, unadulterated responsiveness. My old M720 Triathlon is still great for everyday use, and it's my go-to when this beast needs a charge, but for serious pixel-peeping and headshot hunting, the G502 X Plus blows it out of the water. The HERO 25K Sensor is no joke. I'm talking pinpoint accuracy that makes navigating my Alienware 38 Curved and 34 QD-OLED monitors feel like butter. Whether I'm trying to land that perfect shot or meticulously editing a document, this mouse tracks like a dream. And the LIGHTFORCE Switches? Every click feels crisp and satisfying, giving you that tactile feedback that just confirms your action. No mushiness here, just pure, responsive clicks. Then there's the LIGHTSYNC RGB. Look, I appreciate a bit of flair, and this mouse delivers without being over the top. It adds that perfect touch of gaming aesthetic, syncing up with the rest of my setup, like my Gimars RGB Gaming Mouse Pad. It just makes the whole experience feel more immersive and, frankly, cooler. This mouse just fits. The ergonomic design feels great in my hand, even during those extended sessions. It's not too light, not too heavy, and the button placement feels intuitive. It's built for comfort and performance, and you can really tell. In short, if you're serious about your PC experience, especially gaming, the Logitech G502 X Plus is an absolute winner. It's fast, accurate, comfortable, and looks damn good doing it. My gaming setup feels complete with this bad boy. Highly recommend it to anyone looking for a top-tier wireless gaming mouse!

And the LIGHTSPEED Optical connection? Flawless. There's no perceptible lag, no hiccups, just pure, unadulterated responsiveness. My old M720 Triathlon is still great for everyday use, and it's my go-to when this beast needs a charge, but for serious pixel-peeping and headshot hunting, the G502 X Plus blows it out of the water. The HERO 25K Sensor is no joke. I'm talking pinpoint accuracy that makes navigating my Alienware 38 Curved and 34 QD-OLED monitors feel like butter. Whether I'm trying to land that perfect shot or meticulously editing a document, this mouse tracks like a dream. And the LIGHTFORCE Switches? Every click feels crisp and satisfying, giving you that tactile feedback that just confirms your action. No mushiness here, just pure, responsive clicks. Then there's the LIGHTSYNC RGB. Look, I appreciate a bit of flair, and this mouse delivers without being over the top. It adds that perfect touch of gaming aesthetic, syncing up with the rest of my setup, like my Gimars RGB Gaming Mouse Pad. It just makes the whole experience feel more immersive and, frankly, cooler. This mouse just fits. The ergonomic design feels great in my hand, even during those extended sessions. It's not too light, not too heavy, and the button placement feels intuitive. It's built for comfort and performance, and you can really tell. In short, if you're serious about your PC experience, especially gaming, the Logitech G502 X Plus is an absolute winner. It's fast, accurate, comfortable, and looks damn good doing it. My gaming setup feels complete with this bad boy. Highly recommend it to anyone looking for a top-tier wireless gaming mouse!

reviews.title: Avoid. The G-Hub software simply does not work.
reviews.body: Title says it all. I bought 2 of these, figuring I could sync profiles between my desktop and laptop gaming systems. The mouse is mechanically well built, but there are plenty of mice that are mechanically just as good. If you're buying a gaming mouse with all the extra buttons, then you probably play more than one video game... which requires software to change the "profile" or button functions for each different game... and that's where this mouse falls apart. The G-hub software seems designed to do everything Except what you want to do: -You want to change button functions? By Yourself? Gosh, even if you do figure out the interface and psychically intuit that the keys have to be drag/dropped onto the buttons to change them, they still won't change. I mean, why would you need to? We scanned all software on your hard drive and sent the list to our marketing dept, and they auto-set profiles that work great! They promise! -You want to unlock the profile so you can change the button settings? Aw, too bad choom. It's locked because, um, we felt it was necessary to lock the buttons for some reason. Like you might accidentally open this software and accidentally drag/drop functions you didn't really mean to change. Best to leave it locked, for your own good. -You want to change profiles? Oh, sure you can do that. Until you navigate away from G-hub and then it "helps" by auto-changing the profile back to Default! No worries, our marketing team has your back. I mean, they are gaming experts! You should SEE their score on Candy Crush! -You still want to change profiles? Why? I mean, we auto-detect the application for you! Spent a lot of money on that, choom. Why you wanna mess that up? -Want to sync your gaming profiles across two computers? Yeah, we know you tied your G-hub software to your logitech account and thanks so much for that data pipe from your computer to the cloud, but really, our marketing department NEEDS that so they can gather data from your system. You know, to uh... track performance and issues and stuff. We're afraid there just isn't the bandwidth to move your settings to the cloud and over to a whole other device. Sorries, but like we said, our software auto-detects and auto-sets the prefect settinz 4 U! We are soo accurat, and xcelnt qualitee! Promize! So the G-hub software is crap designed by idiots, but don't listen to me. I only have a BA in Computer Science and 24 years experience working in IT, and played video games since Dungeons of Daggorath on the TRS-80. But be my guest and google "Manual for G HUB?" for yourself. Do yourself a favor - buy 3 mice for this price and throw the two worst ones away. You will STILL be money ahead, and have a way better experience. At least until Logitech hires an actual software interface designer.

reviews.title: G502 HERO but less wires. Weight (or lack thereof) could be a pro/con
reviews.body: Fantastic mouse that cleaned up my setup while keeping the in-hand familiarity of the wired G502 HERO, shape and free spinning scroll wheel and all. Battery life is very long subject to personal usage differences of course, I plug it in when the battery indicator turns red maybe for a few hours and it's back up to full and that's maybe one a week or so with moderate to heavy usage. Wireless performance is fantastic, no issues there. The weight of the mouse is *very* light, that can either be a pro or a con: If you want something you can move effortlessly for high speed gaming performance you'll love it. If you're like me and likes a weighted sturdy mouse, and used the G502 HERO with all of the weights installed, you might not be happy. However, there are 3rd party weights you can buy here on Amazon that seamlessly integrate into the magnetic lid underneath for the dongle storage. With one of those installed it's no longer flying off of my keyboard tray and it's just as comfortable as the old version without the limits and mess of a wire.

reviews.title: Leise Maus mit schickem Design und praktischer Akkustandsanzeige
reviews.body: Ich nutze die Maus jetzt seit einigen Tagen sowohl am Laptop als auch am Tablet und insgesamt macht sie einen wirklich guten Eindruck. Was mir direkt gefallen hat, ist das transparente Design – wirkt mal etwas anders als die üblichen Standardmäuse und sieht auf dem Schreibtisch ziemlich modern aus. Im Alltag war für mich vor allem die leise Bedienung angenehm. Die Klicks sind deutlich gedämpft, sodass man auch abends noch arbeiten kann, ohne dass das ständige Klicken nervt. Gerade im Homeoffice finde ich das echt angenehm. Praktisch ist außerdem, dass man schnell zwischen Bluetooth und dem USB-Dongle wechseln kann. Ich nutze sie tagsüber am PC und zwischendurch am Tablet, das Umschalten klappt unkompliziert und die Verbindung war bisher stabil. Auch die Akkustandsanzeige finde ich hilfreich. So sieht man rechtzeitig, wann geladen werden muss, statt plötzlich ohne Maus dazusitzen. Geladen wird per USB-C, was für mich inzwischen einfach Standard sein sollte. Die Form liegt bei meinen mittelgroßen Händen angenehm in der Hand. Sie ist nicht zu schwer und gleitet sauber über das Mauspad. Für längere Arbeitssessions passt das für mich gut. Insgesamt eine moderne und alltagstaugliche Maus mit leisen Tasten und praktischen Funktionen. Ein paar persönliche Vorlieben spielen natürlich immer mit rein, aber bisher bin ich zufrieden.
reviews.body_en: I've been using the mouse on both my laptop and tablet for a few days now and overall it makes a really good impression. What I immediately liked is the transparent design - it looks a little different than the usual standard mice and looks pretty modern on the desk. In everyday life, the quiet operation was particularly pleasant for me. The clicks are significantly dampened, so you can still work in the evening without the constant clicking being annoying. I find this really pleasant, especially when working from home. It is also practical that you can quickly switch between Bluetooth and the USB dongle. I use it on the PC during the day and occasionally on the tablet. Switching is easy and the connection has been stable so far. I also find the battery level indicator helpful. This way you can see in good time when it needs to be loaded instead of suddenly sitting there without a mouse. It charges via USB-C, which should be standard for me by now. The shape fits comfortably in my medium-sized hands. It's not too heavy and glides smoothly over the mouse pad. This works well for me for longer work sessions. Overall, a modern and everyday mouse with quiet buttons and practical functions. Of course, a few personal preferences always come into play, but so far I'm satisfied.

reviews.title: Phenomenal value
reviews.body: I was really blown away with this mouse to be quite honest. For what you pay, you get awesome value which is something that is lost today in most consumer of products. This mouse is a tad bit smaller than the Superlight 2 in width and length, and has a slightly lower hump in the back. I haven had any issues with sensor spin out or misclicks with M1 & M2. Pre and post travel aren't too bad most of it I attribute to flex. The side buttons are on point and feel great, I really disliked the side button implementation in the original G-Pro because they were too squishy IMO, these however don't feel that way. Like I said for what you pay ~ $40 vs $160 for the Superlight 2, I can day without a doubt that the Superlight 2 is not 4x better than this mouse not even 2x.

reviews.title: Review after 4 months of use.
reviews.body: I genuinely love this mouse. At the time of the review, I had this mouse for about 4 months and had no problems. The style, functionality, and setting are great. Accuracy is pretty good, but note that the mouse is heavier than a standard computer mouse. The bottom of it is metal with the insert for the sensor and stand charging pins. Clicks feel good. Personally, I chose this mouse because of its big size and weight, as my previous mouse was a clicker that broke. The mouse will feel good in the hand of the 6-foot-tall male, and even with a fast moving does not lifts up from the mouse pad. I tend to use lower dpi, so I move the mouse more. The charge lasts for about 3-4 days with 5-8 hours of daily use(I do not charge it until it is about 10%, and I do not turn it off). When charging, I tend to turn it off, put it on the charging stand, and it takes about 1-2 hours to be charged to full. But note that for the first few days you vrist might tire out a bit, but eventually it will get you used to its weight. I love this mouse and recommend it especially for people looking for a computer mouse that is bigger and heavier then standar market ones.

reviews.title: Cheap switches you will have to replace. I wish Asus would have done better with this product.
reviews.body: Here is the deal I have with this mouse: brand new out of the box and already have double-clicking going on. Two weeks of use. While they do include a spare set of switches, this still does not account for the fact they are cheap. No wonder it's designed so one can replace switches so easily. For the price, Asus should be ASHAMED. For me, I just ordered proper switches to replace what this product came with. Not a big deal as they are dirt cheap. But still, as I stated, for a $100+ mouse, the switches should not be this cheap. This is a heavy mouse. If you use a cloth mouse pad, you are not going to like this mouse. You feel the friction and the weight of this mouse on this material. I switched to my Logitech G440 hard-covered mouse pad, and it slides like a dream. I was going to order glass skates. Glad I did not. If you install new states, you will be unable to use the dock mount. I do like the fact that there are 6 side buttons. Using a glass mouse pad or hard cover allows me to play FPS games with ease. I like the 5 DPI settings, but, again, for the price, they could have added a few more possibilities. For a few dollars more, you can have a G502 with superior hardware but a lack of side buttons. I operate in an entire Asus ecosystem; I have an Asus motherboard, PSU, AIO cooler, 5080 GPU, & 3 monitors, so I already have Armory Crate installed on my system. If you buy this mouse, you HAVE to install Armory Crate to make use of this mouse in any good way. That being said, Armory Crate is notorious for being known as bloatware. Which, in my opinion, it is. There's really no need for it to be running and eating up system resources like this app does. So buyer beware. I would have brought a Razer instead, but that mouse too requires that you install their software to work their mouse. The lesser of two evils for me was this mouse. The construction, meaning the mouse shapes and material, feels robust and tank-like. But I dare not drop it. It feels like a smartphone: it looks built for durability and day-to-day use, but one drop and it's broken. Mainly because of the weight of this mouse. It's like dropping a brick from 2'. So take care of your equipment or at least get the protection. I know this review sounds bad, but it's really not. I do enjoy this mouse; I like the fit in my hand (I have mid-size hands), I love the ring finger resting point, and the scroll wheel is smooth. My issues are stated: It should come with better switches; one needs a hard surface area to really be able to move this mouse without muscle failure, and the bloatware just to use this. It should be a $60 mouse, because in the end, you will be buying upgraded switches and looking for a mouse pad that will work well with this mouse. As far as gameplay, it does take some getting used to, but it's doable. Back in the day, gamers used to play FPS with ball mice. While this is 1000% better, a lightweight/gamer mouse would be a better pick. The 6 side buttons are the lifesaver for this mouse for me. While it takes a little time to set up profiles so they do work in the games you are playing, once it's done, you are golden. Windows does not support any more than, like, 3 or 4 side buttons, so you have to program the unsupported ones to bind to keys, then in-game, bind that key to your mouse. All in all, a good, solid mouse as long as you don't mind the 'little' headaches that come along with it. 3 stars because there are better mice out there & for a company like Asus, I would expect better from them. EDIT (PLEASE READ!): I really wanted to love this mouse. The shape and the heavy chassis feel fantastic in the hand, but for the premium price tag, the internal hardware is an absolute nightmare. The biggest issue—and the reason I had to abandon it—is the mechanical microswitches. I bought this in April, and within a few months of normal gaming, it developed a severe double-clicking issue and started dropping window drags. It got to the point where it was actively sabotaging my gameplay; I would press the rear middle side button (which I use for missile lock-ons or grenade throwing), and the switch simply wouldn't register the input. ASUS tries to market their "push-fit hot-swap switch sockets" as a feature, but it's really a band-aid for their use of cheap, outdated mechanical parts. I tried fixing it myself by buying three different sets of replacement mechanical microswitches. None of them held up, and the mouse continued to miss clicks and fail. This proves the issue isn't just the switches themselves, but a fundamental flaw in the PCB, the socket design, or the firmware relying on 1990s-era mechanical contacts. The side buttons are also prone to sticking, even after a thorough cleaning, making them unreliable in crucial gaming moments. Furthermore, you have to deal with Armoury Crate, which is a bloated mess; their own updates ruined the mouse profiles I had set. Did it 3 times, and the constant fear that a speck of dust or a stray cat hair will get inside the chassis and ruin the contacts. If you are a serious gamer looking for a reliable, long-term peripheral, look elsewhere. Do not buy a mouse at this price point that still uses mechanical switches. Save yourself the headache and buy something with modern optical switches (like the Razer Naga V2 Pro or Corsair Scimitar) that physically cannot double-click. Thankfully, Amazon Customer Service was amazing and granted me a one-time return exception because of how quickly this hardware failed. I took that refund and immediately bought a mouse with optical switches.

This proves the issue isn't just the switches themselves, but a fundamental flaw in the PCB, the socket design, or the firmware relying on 1990s-era mechanical contacts. The side buttons are also prone to sticking, even after a thorough cleaning, making them unreliable in crucial gaming moments. Furthermore, you have to deal with Armoury Crate, which is a bloated mess; their own updates ruined the mouse profiles I had set. Did it 3 times, and the constant fear that a speck of dust or a stray cat hair will get inside the chassis and ruin the contacts. If you are a serious gamer looking for a reliable, long-term peripheral, look elsewhere. Do not buy a mouse at this price point that still uses mechanical switches. Save yourself the headache and buy something with modern optical switches (like the Razer Naga V2 Pro or Corsair Scimitar) that physically cannot double-click. Thankfully, Amazon Customer Service was amazing and granted me a one-time return exception because of how quickly this hardware failed. I took that refund and immediately bought a mouse with optical switches.

reviews.title: Just Not Enough For An MMO Mouse
reviews.body: Wanted to love this mouse so badly! I went back and forth on returning it for days because I love the charging dock, the response time, the price, the quality, battery life, and the large size of this mouse. It is extremely comfortable, but I have a few complaints that resulted in its return: - Not enough buttons. Most MMO mice have up to 12 programmable buttons as most MMO's have an action bar of that size. You'll find a few that have less like ESO though. Most MMO mice have a grid pattern for their side buttons whereas this one is asymmetrical with buttons located in other places which is great if you want that. Unfortunately the Corsair Darkstar MMO Mouse also has this but more buttons to work with which is what I needed. I sadly ended up going with that mouse as I needed more function over form. - Side buttons are super low quality. The buttons move around when you push them and they have a cheap, unsatisfying click to them. I could probably look past this if the mouse had enough buttons but can't in this case and is worth mentioning. - Although very minor, this mouse is only 1000Hz versus the 2000-8000Hz that competitors offer. In the grand scheme of things, that's not going to be very noticable and would take a hit on the battery. Overall this wouldn't have swayed my decision on keeping the mouse like the two former issues but also worth mentioning for those that might want to know.

reviews.title: One issue and it ruined my experience
reviews.body: I have many Asus products as a start. I want to give a list as a start to give some understanding as to my knowledge and user experience with this brand. Rog Spatha X Rog Zepherus g14 2025 Rog Zepherus G16 2020 An Asus 34 “ wide screen gaming monitor Rog Strix Scope II Rog Rakiri Pro Rog Delta II I have long since been a fan of the brand and by the brand so I can try and have compatibility without issue. Most of my experiences have been good other than some Armoury Crate and Aura Sync which are general and common. I like the mouse for its weight, button placement, the feel it has in the hand and when using it. I like being able to switch DPI’s and the RGB is nice. Overall this is a well balanced mouse and I even think for my hand, which is smaller, the size is great. The issue is the construction of the mouse and misfires that occur because of either a bad design choice, bad manufacturing choices, faulty parts, software issues, or the labeling of products as new when the where actually refurbished by the manufacturer and relabeled. (that seems to be a practice used with tech retailers like best buy) the mouse wheel on my spatha misclicks the back switch of the mouse which about an inch apart for the user to accidentally misclick. I tested using a mouse remapping tool and as i rolled the wheel, the back switch of the mouse fired like a machine gun. the only option was to remap and disable the function. No reset the mouse, and its firmware. I downloaded firmware packet after firmware packet. This should be a great mouse. Honestly I would give this product a 9 if not a 10 without this issue. However this “small” issue makes watching my a youtube video and scrolling down the page IMPOSSIBLE, functionally it makes using the scroll wheel IMPOSSIBLE. It also seems like my only option is to speak to a rep who wants to watch me explain the issue and team chat, then make me pay to send in my mouse which they don’t know if they can fix, so they may just send me a new one and I actually like this mouse so I want to use it NOW, so for me it’s easier to disable the function than deal with customer support. That being said, Asus still delivered a broken item and I’d rather use my Logitech G 502 X now because the situation paint my head anytime I pick up the beautiful piece of equipment I saved up for. So I guess I also had a issue with the process of trying to find a solution with Asus when their product has defects.

reviews.title: Excelente qualidade, alto investimento
reviews.body: O mouse é fabuloso. Já estou usando-o a várias semanas. Para quem gosta de mouses grandes. A base de carregamento é também o dongle wireless, então não é adequado para quem quer trocar rapidamente entre computadores. A bateria dura o suficiente para ate dois dias de uso moderado (configurado o modo de hibernação). Se deixar o mouse na base durante a noite, não vai acabar a bateria durante um dia inteiro de uso constante. Vem com botões extras para reparar, e aparentemente é possível abri-lo com certa facilidade. Usar o Armoury Crate, o programa de gerenciamento da Asus, é indispensável. Então considerar isso. É o mesmo usado para placa mãe Asus e outros componentes da marca. O preço é alto, mas se estiver disposto a compra-lo, é uma excelente opção. Possui 6 botões configuráveis, além dos 3 botões de clique padrão e os 2 de avançar e retornar, então são 11 botões ao total para interagir com o computador, sem contar o botão de DPI. Não é possível conectar via bluetooth. Conexão wireless é confiável, mas não flexível.
reviews.body_en: The mouse is fabulous. I've been using it for several weeks now. For those who like big mice. The charging base is also the wireless dongle, so it's not suitable for those who want to quickly switch between computers. The battery lasts enough for up to two days of moderate use (hibernation mode is configured). If you leave the mouse on the base overnight, it won't run out of battery during a full day of constant use. It comes with extra buttons to repair, and it appears to be possible to open it quite easily. Using Armory Crate, Asus' management program, is essential. So consider this. It's the same one used for Asus motherboards and other brand components. The price is high, but if you are willing to buy it, it is an excellent option. It has 6 configurable buttons, in addition to the 3 standard click buttons and the 2 forward and return buttons, so there are 11 buttons in total to interact with the computer, not counting the DPI button. Cannot connect via Bluetooth. Wireless connection is reliable but not flexible.

reviews.title: ROC is the Best!
reviews.body: Endlich das ROC-Setup komplett und auch von der Maus bin ich begeistert, sehr hochwertig, fühlt sich gut an die Materialien und zum Glück keine gummierten Tasten! Wie einige hier schreiben, das einige Daumentasten nicht richtig auslösen, das Problem kann ich nicht bestätigen, jede Taste funktioniert wunderbar, das einzige ist, das die Daumentasten etwas leichter gehen könnten, es braucht schon viel Druck im Daumen um diese auszulösen aber das ist mein persönliches empfinden. Das ist auch das erste mal in meinen Leben, das ich nach 30 Jahren Kabelmaus ohne Kabel Zocke und was soll man sagen, es läuft einfach super, genau wie mit Kabel also ab jetzt nie wieder Kabel und die Ladestation ist auch extrem gut verarbeitet, schwer und hat sogar eine Status-LED für den Akku ... absolut Top!!!
reviews.body_en: Finally the ROC setup is complete and I'm also thrilled with the mouse, very high quality, feels good, the materials and luckily no rubberized buttons! As some people write here, some thumb buttons don't trigger properly, I can't confirm the problem, every button works wonderfully, the only thing is that the thumb buttons could be a little easier, it takes a lot of pressure in the thumb to trigger them, but that's my personal feeling. This is also the first time in my life that I've been gaming without a cable after 30 years of using a cable mouse and what can I say, it works just great, just like with a cable, so from now on I'll never have to use cables again and the charging station is also extremely well made, heavy and even has a status LED for the battery... absolutely great!!!

reviews.title: I loved my Logitech. This is a viable replacement!
reviews.body: I am a user, and fond lover, of the G502 and G600. When I saw V3 Pro and the feature set, I really wanted to take a dive into the Razer ecosystem and give it a whirl. reviews.title: I don't like Razer, but this mouse slaps
reviews.body: I was really, really contemplating rating this less because of Razer Synapse 4. I couldn't get button remapping to work in any game at the start, it would only work after I closed Synapse entirely. Profile switching also didn't work. The software took so much finagling and trial and error manually deleting Synapse and re-installing more than once--I even tried deleting Synapse data online from my account via the Privacy Center to no avail. Midway through, I almost just resorted to keeping things on onboard memory and manually switching between games. It was brutal. Thankfully profile switching started working and button remaps followed suit. I don't know how I got it to work, but it works! It handles so well that the pain setting up the software can be forgiven. This is everything I wanted out of my old Logitech G600s, of which I've had several and daily drove for the better part of a decade. I'd always try but ultimately return other MMO mice because I'd always miss ring-finger button. I know I'm not the only one that felt this! It seems like Razer heard our cries and implemented it on this new Naga V3 Pro, even adding the two additional buttons by the left-click button like on the V2 Hyperspeed. My only gripes are that the side buttons aren't as pronounced and contoured as the G600, and the left- and right-mouse clicks are just obnoxiously loud. Travel distance and weight per click as well I'd say aren't great either--maybe better for older MMOs where each click needed to be more deliberate, but a lighter switch would be better for modern MMOs. I guess I'll get used to them. Despite all of that, the fact that in addition to the extra buttons this is wireless AND I can swap plates for other non-MMO games? I can learn to live with this. Logitech really missed out.

reviews.title: Perfect for my setup
reviews.body: I had to find a fast affordable replacement after my cat suddenly decided that my previous mouse was actual prey and absolutely demolished it. This one is a pretty good weight, which will hopefully save this one from an early demise. It goes to sleep fairly quickly to extend the battery life if you're using it wirelessly like I am, but there's no noticeable delay when you move it again and it wakes up. I have arthritis and typically use a palm grip as opposed to a claw grip on the mouse and it fits in my hand perfectly, plus the little grippy side where the thumb sits helps with control pretty well. The RGB default lighting actually matches the setup I have now, so I don't feel the need to change it unless I decide to change my lighting theme for my whole desk, but there's a little program on the redragon website that's pretty easy to set up and change what the buttons do and the lighting if you so choose. RIP old mouse, long live the redragon. Edit: Purchased July 2024 — Currently August 2025. For the past month or so, the mouse battery has been dying faster and faster. In the beginning, I really only had to charge it once a month with VERY heavy, daily use. Now, I've rarely been playing video games, mostly just using my computer for email and school, and I have to charge it at LEAST once a week. It's such a shame, it was such a good mouse. On the bright side, my cat can't knock it off very easily. RIP redragon too, I guess.

reviews.title: Excellent all-rounder mouse
reviews.body: This review is for the Razer Cobra Pro (wireless ver). Razer built a feature rich mouse that can do it all with excellent build quality (no creaking, side flexing or M1/M2 wobble) compared to the mice from other brands. A lot of critics wanted an ultra lightweight ~50g Viper mini, not this. But for the people who care about having a feature rich mouse with excellent build quality, ability to cycle between multiple devices using different connections (Bluetooth, 2.4GHz wireless, wired), this is a great mouse that also happens to have the latest and greatest tech for top tier gaming performance. There's a profile button on the bottom of the mouse that allows you to cycle between different profiles, which is useful if you wanted to have a profile for your laptop that turns off the RBG lighting, reduces the poll rate to 500 Hz (save battery) etc. The mouse has on-board memory, so you can save your profiles and settings, then uninstall Synapse if you so please. The only con is that the RGB settings are still not saved with the on-board memory profiles (c'mon Razer). The M1/M2 buttons have a crisp, slightly higher than normal audible click and the side buttons are placed well and feel great. The rubber side grips are molded into this model, so you cannot remove them. This is not great if they wear down, as they cannot be easily replaced like grip tape. The shape of the mouse is 99% the exact same as it's predecessor, the Viper mini. From a technical perspective, this mouse is capable of 4K Hz polling rate, but only if you purchase the HyperPolling dongle or the Dock Pro from Razer, otherwise it defaults to 1K Hz polling. The mouse is not as heavy as everyone is lamenting online, as it weighs in at ~76g. If you take off the dongle cover on the Razer Cobra Pro, you can get the mouse down to ~74g and which improves the balance in my opinion. For reference, here is how much some popular mice weigh among the big two: - Logitech G305 which is similar in size, weighs 99g. - G Pro Wireless is 80g - G Pro SuperLight is 61g - Razer Viper Ultimate is 74g - Razer Viper V2 Pro is 59g Battery life: - 170 hours on Bluetooth - 100 hours on 2.4GHz wireless (1K Hz polling) - 33 hours on 2.4 GHz wireless (4K Hz polling) Overall, I really like this mouse from Razer and personally, going up in weight from ~50g hasn't had any impact on gaming performance, I adjusted very quickly and actually don't mind the extra bit of weight (high sens). In the future, a lighter V2 with no rubber side grips would be ideal. --TLDR-- Pros: - Excellent build quality (no creaking, flexing or M1/M2 wobble) - Top tier sensor from Razer - Multi-device capable (Bluetooth to your laptop, 2.4GHz dongle in your desktop. even wired) - Gen 3 Razer optical switches (no double clicking like mechanical switches) - Mouse wheel is rubberized, feels great - Medium weight mouse at ~76g (74g if you remove the dongle cover) - USB-C connector - Top tier 2.4GHz almost zero latency wireless connection Cons: - Built-in rubber side grips (if these wear down, you're stuck with it instead of just replacing grip tape) - RGB settings aren't stored in the on-board memory, so you'll have to keep Synapse installed if you care about specific RGB settings - 4K Hz polling rate requires the additional HyperPolling dongle or Dock Pro (sold separately) - could be lighter (~60g range), but not a deal breaker Bonus review: The wired version of the Cobra is almost an exact replica of the Viper Mini wired, but with improvements to the sensor for LOD (lift off distance) and now has the Gen3 optical switches. Try this mouse and be the judge for yourself!

reviews.title: The best mouse out of 20 that I tried, my replacement to Razer Abyssus Essential
reviews.body: Wow.....this is such a good mouse! I tried the Razer Cobra wired version, but this wireless is even better. It has been one of the few mice I have tried where the wireless version is an actual upgrade, apart from the wireless function. The sides of the mouse have a much better grip than the wired version, and the buttons feel snappier and especially the scroll wheel feels very accurate & doesn't slip at all. The mouse is extremely light and has very customizable sensor settings in Razer Synapse. I did read online that quite a few people say that the rubber side grips will wear out over time and that they aren't replacable or removeable. I did see also, though, that people recommend using the Razer Grip Tape (or other simlar mouse grip tapes) to put over the side grips when they wear out. I think that is what I will do, as I am choosing this mouse to replace my Razer Abyssus Essential. This mouse was the best out of 20 mice that I tried, including beating out barely the Cooler Master MM711. This mouse was just a little more accurate for me and more comfortable with the solid shape without holes, especially on the side grip, which I didn't enjoy as much after testing for 30 minutes or so. Overall, a very very good mouse, maybe a 9.5/10.

reviews.title: Provides the power requirements of your USB devices while extending the available ports.
reviews.body: I had a problem. My monitor array at home includes a Thunderbolt hub that includes two DisplayPort and one VGA connector, and my laptop at home includes one HDMI and one additional VGA connector, but this totals only 6 screens when my laptop's primary screen is added in. My monitor array, on the other hand, includes yet another 6 screens (all but two of them are 1080p). These screens are driven by a set of mostly DisplayLink display adapters, although I have a few others that required manually installed drivers (with varying success), and some that don't advertise DisplayLink but whose drivers installed automatically anyways. Six USB-A Display adapters require a lot of power, and I ran into the limit of my workstation and Thunderbolt hub's power capacity at only 4 additional displays, and every single USB-A and USB-C port on my laptop and my dock were used up, leading to a messy snarl of wires and cables that wire ties just didn't resolve. What I like: 1. It allows me to connect my entire array of video extenders and power my entire array of monitors. It substantially cleans up the mess of cables connected to my laptop and hub by putting many of them in one place. 2. Its aluminum finish looks good on my desktop. 3. Its power supply is rated for 65w, telling me I can connect more devices before its capacity is exhausted. 4. It has a sturdy construction. What I don't like: a. Ummm, that's a tough one. Maybe it takes up additional desk space and there are a lot of cables connected to it, but hey, that's kind-of the intent. Nah, I can't say I dislike that. Caveats: - Your results may vary if you plan to use this to drive a large array of screens. My laptop has 64GB RAM and a second video card with another 6GB video RAM. I have a newer laptop at work with 128GB RAM and a second video card with 16GB video RAM that can't run my home array without overheating.

reviews.title: Performed well until it didn't, but replaced promptly without hassle.
reviews.body: This USB hub worked well for 9 months then it started intermittently not communicating, then it would reconnect. All I had connected at those disconnect times were Logitech dongles for a keyboard and trackball. Difficult to diagnose, I thought the screen was freezing, perhaps a graphics card issue. Occasionally Windows issued the "USB device not connected." When the hub completely failed, the diagnosis was easy. I contacted intpw via email as suggested on their website, after a couple of efforts at diagnosis they agreed the unit was defective and replaced it promptly through Amazon. The service tech suggested that Logitech dongles should be placed as far apart at possible on the hub, they are known to interfere with each other if too close; don't know that I've ever had that problem, but took the advice. So yeah, it would have been nice if it didn't fail, but stuff happens and they replaced it. This thing is really well made, an aluminum extrusion with the board rigidly mounted inside, shielded and physically protected.

reviews.title: Low profile, fast, and stylish
reviews.body: There is not much to say about this. It has a low profile and lets you expand how many USB ports you have. The first four USB A ports, starting from the left, have 5Gb/s speeds. The next two have 10Gb/s speeds. What you should know is that of the three USB C ports on the right, the first one has 10Gb/s speeds, the next two are just for power and do not handle data. If you have a phone or tablet that lets you charge it through a USB C port, you can plug it into one of those ports and it will charge. What you should know is that you need to plug this into a high-speed USB 3.2 port to get the fast speeds. It comes with a USB C to USB C data cable for plugging into your computer. Since it only gives you one USB C data port, you're not gaining any additional USB C ports since you use one from your computer and only get one in return. The cable isn't that long, so you'll be limited in where you can place it unless you invest in a longer cable. But the price is good, it looks nice, and is very functional.

reviews.title: Solidly built powered USB hub (with a few wrinkles)
reviews.body: This hub has a very Apple-esque design and appears to be very solidly built. So far, it seems to perform well and as expected based on its specs. A couple of things though that are not made clear to purchasers based on the description provided: 1. The hub is provided only with a US 2-pin mains power lead. In other countries you’ll need to use a plug adaptor, else provide your own native mains cord with an IEC-C7 “figure 8” connector on the other end. At least the power brick uses that style of connector, the mains plug is not hard-wired. 2. The instructions warn you that WiFi dongles (such as those used to communicate with wireless mouse and keyboards) should not be plugged into the hub due to the risk of interference. Meaning one port on your laptop/PC will have to be used for such dongles if you have them. Not a dealbreaker, but it would have been nice to know this prior. 3. The instructions say only one HDD or two SSDs can be connected to the hub (presumably for power draw reasons). The maximum load is 900 mA (4.5 W) but it’s not clear if that is per data port (the USB standard) or in total across all data ports. This hub provides only one USB-C and two USB-A 3.1 Gen 2 data ports (10 Gbps). That’s a bit light-on these days. The remainder are USB-A 3.0 ports (5 Gbps). The two “power delivery” (non-data) USB-C ports are handy for charging devices, total power delivery max 45 W. So all up, a rating of 4 stars.

reviews.title: I don't know how I ever lived without it.
reviews.body: I'm very happy with this device. My laptop doesn't have an ethernet port and only has one USB-C SuperSpeed port, so I bought an ethernet to USB-C cable to connect my ethernet switch to the Anker and into my laptop's USB-C port, and it works great. I don't need a fast internet connection for the things I do, so my service is only a 50mbps symmetrical up/down connection, and that's what I get even while transferring files from my external between other devices, charging my phone, and using composite devices. I bought the Anker 100W Compact and Foldable USB C Charger for it and it charges my S24 extremely fast. It's very well built, yet super lightweight. I love the sleek, slender design. It's the perfect size to easily slide into a pocket, store in a desk drawer, or keep handy in a laptop case or backpack. Using it is easy. Just plug it into your computer and plug your devices into it. Just make sure you have a power supply for it if you're charging or powering other devices, using external storage, or running anything else that taxes USB power. I have had ZERO connectivity issues with it — no random disconnect/reconnect blips, no failed transfers for huge amounts of data that have taken up to 45 minutes, no static his or crackle when my headset is running through it... no problems at all. It's actually kind of spooky now that I think about it... I can't recall a time I've ever had a similar device that didn't have some nuance that got under my skin, like a loose connection, random disconnections, having to reinstall the drivers all the time, or having to troubleshoot just to get it connected for the first time. The most stress I've put it through was with my keyboard connected, ethernet running through it, my S24 charging and transferring about ~20gb of pictures and videos to my 2T external HD at the same time that my laptop was transferring about ~500gb of media and documents to the HD, too, and I was surprised by how warm it DIDN'T get. My only complaint is trivial and unique to my situation — I wish output cord was longer. About six inches would do. My laptop sits up on an adjustable stand that clamps to my desk, and the end where the output cord is hangs a few inches off of my desk. This puts extra stress on the USB-C port and can wear it out faster or damage it. I haven't had a use for the HDMI port yet, but I eventually will. I use all of the other ports for my work and personal devices, though. These include: a 2tb external hard drive; a Poly Blackwire 3320 Series headset; a dongle for a wireless mouse/keyboard combo or a wired keyboard and a dongle for a wireless mouse; my Galaxy S24 charges and transfers files through it super fast; I have several thumb drives ranging from 20gb to 512gb that I regularly use; I recently bought an RCA/S Video-to-USB converter to digitize old home movies I plug into it, too.

reviews.title: A sleek, full-size hub that finally got everything right for my laptop setup

The build is solid—aluminum shell, clean finish, and it matches my laptop’s aesthetic nicely. Plugged it in and it immediately recognized every device: external monitor, USB-A hard drive, flash drive, mouse, and power all at once. No compatibility headaches, which is already a huge win. The performance has been great. The 4K HDMI output works flawlessly with my external monitor, offering crisp picture quality and no weird dropouts or lag. The 90 W Power Delivery means my laptop charges even when I’m using it hard (video editing + screen output + USB devices), which used to be a pain when using lesser hubs that throttle the charging or heat up quickly. The USB-A ports feel robust and haven't failed or lagged with connected accessories, and the entire hub remains cool under load. It hides neatly behind the laptop and stays connected without getting pulled out accidentally. If you work with laptops, external screens, and multiple devices—and want something streamlined that won’t get in the way—this Anker hub is absolutely worth it.

reviews.title: Good Basic USB-C Hub, Just Not Designed for My More Demanding Setup
reviews.body: I originally purchased this Anker 5-in-1 hub for my iPad-based DJ cart. Although it ultimately wasn’t up to the demands of that particular setup, I still think it’s a well-made hub for normal everyday use. For basic HDMI and USB expansion on a laptop or iPad, it works well and feels like the quality I’ve come to expect from Anker. My problem was that my DJ system needed to handle several higher-demand connections at the same time, including video, audio, and charging. For that application I eventually learned that I needed a more advanced powered/smart hub rather than a basic USB-C adapter. I didn’t return this one because there’s nothing actually wrong with it. I kept it as a handy way to add an extra HDMI connection or additional USB ports to my laptop or iPad when I need them. It just wasn’t the right tool for the job I originally purchased it for.

reviews.title: Updated - Absolutely awesome, if it would have only worked longer than one day and this one did!
reviews.body: This is an update to my original review. The first one had a few issues of which are in the original review at the bottom of this one. I was sent a replacement that works! It does exactly what I needed, data transfer with USB C support, nothing else. No there is no video capability, but there are so many hubs and docking stations out there that do have that capability it became a problem in my configuration. I have more video connections than I could ever use, but was left high and dry on USB C. I also use a wheel device and external keypad in my workflow that wouldn't work with another product I tried. It works with this just fine. It also is the first part of a chain linking two other hubs together with the first product I tried at the end of that chain. The price...it solved a problem with it being the only solution I could find and is one of the less costly parts of my entire setup as well leaving me more room for expansion. I would call that a bargain. This was exactly what I needed, did exactly what I needed it to do for one whole day. The second day is when things went whacky. I couldn't access any of the connected drives which at that moment there were three. So, I shut everything down and just tried unplugging everything and then plugging it back in. Start the computer back up and nothing. Once again, I shut everything down and swapped cords around this time starting in the ports I hadn't used. What were in the new ports worked, the one drive that was in one of the others didn't work. What's kind of odd is the third problem port. sometimes will work if I plug something in while with everything on, but it's not seen on a reboot. It's built well and is really the best solution I have found for my setup. I gave it 3 stars when as it is now, doesn't deserve any, but they are sending me a replacement. A fully working version of this, that works longer than one day and hopefully for a long period of time is definitely a 5 star buy. Hoping this was just a fluke. Once I get the replacement and if it performs as it should I will update this review to where it should be. If not, I will downgrade it to also where it should be.

reviews.title: Slow, Unstable, and poor quality. Highly not recommendable.
reviews.body: I bought this USB C Hub for my laptop and was very disappointed. Upon opening and connecting via USB C 3.2. port on my laptop, I noticed the connection felt very mushy and loose. Not secure at all and comes out easily, tested on multiple ports. The device was not recognized right away and I had to play around with the connection to get any sort of connectivity. The Power delivery is also finicky and does not always work. I performed several disk speed tests with the USB C Hub using my portable SSD, and also by directly connecting the portable SSD to the laptop. When portable SSD directly connected, I had read and write speeds around 1000 MB/s. When portable SSD connected to the USB C Hub, I had read and write speeds of around 40 MB/s. Also while connected to the USB C Hub, the speed test was extremely unstable, and freezing. The quality is poor, and functionality is mediocre. Save yourself some time and skip this one. It's a huge waste of money and definitely not getting any value from this product.

reviews.title: Compact aluminum USB‑C hub with true 4K60 and fast ports
reviews.body: This little Yottamaster hub turned out to be a genuinely useful addition to my setup. It’s compact, lightweight, and feels sturdier than most of the plastic hubs in this price range thanks to the aluminum casing. That metal shell isn’t just for looks either — it helps keep the hub cool during long sessions, and even when I had multiple devices plugged in, it never got hot enough to worry about. The port layout is simple but well thought out. You get two USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports for fast transfers, a USB 2.0 port for a keyboard or mouse, a dedicated USB‑C PD port, and the HDMI output. The USB 3.2 ports really do hit the advertised 10Gbps speeds — moving large files to an external SSD was quick and smooth. The slower USB 2.0 port is clearly labeled “480 Mbps,” which is actually helpful so you don’t accidentally plug fast storage into the wrong spot. The HDMI port supports full 4K at 60Hz, and the picture quality is sharp and stable. It’s worth noting that your device needs to support DP Alt Mode for the video output to work, but once connected, the hub handled an external monitor without any flicker or handshake issues. I used it for both extended desktop and mirrored display, and it behaved exactly as expected. Charging performance is another strong point. The PD port supports up to 100W input, with 90W passed through to the laptop and the remaining power used to run the hub itself. Being able to charge while using all the ports at once is a big convenience, especially if you’re working with a single USB‑C port on your device. It’s also nice that the PD port is charge‑only — no confusion about whether it carries data or video. In day‑to‑day use, everything just works. No drivers, no fuss, no random disconnects. It’s small enough to toss in a laptop bag and forget about, and sturdy enough that I’m not worried about it getting banged around. For travel, office setups, or even a future mini‑PC build, it’s a clean, reliable way to expand ports without clutter. Overall, it’s a well‑made, technically solid little hub that punches above its price point.

reviews.title: A nearly weightless port replicator that works very reliably.
reviews.body: The Yottamaster 5-in-1 USB-C docking station is a stylish lightweight port expander. The aluminum exterior closely matches my MacBook Pro. I love the added flexibility it provides for my laptop that only has two usb c ports. It has two USB-A ports rated up to 10Gbps, great for fast external drives, file transfers and other high-speed accessories.
