reviews.title: Anker Has Been Assigned Custody of All My Cables
reviews.body: I bought this because apparently owning a laptop now requires purchasing a separate device so you can plug things into the laptop you already purchased. Fine. We live in strange times. Fortunately, this little Anker dock understood the assignment. I plugged it in, connected my monitors and accessories, and everything just worked. No troubleshooting pilgrimage. No unplugging things seventeen times. No crawling under my desk questioning every decision that led me to this moment. Now one USB-C connection handles the mess that used to look like my laptop was receiving life support. The dual-monitor support works great, the ports are actually useful, and the whole thing is small enough that it doesn’t become yet another piece of equipment occupying valuable desk real estate. The best part is disconnecting my laptop. One cable. That’s it. I unplug one cable and walk away like a person who has their life together. I do not have my life together. But for approximately four seconds after disconnecting this dock, the evidence suggests otherwise.

reviews.title: Not great for long-term set up
reviews.body: 1. Doesn't come with the wall plug to allow charging. You have to have your own USBC cord to connect to the wall to allow charging while using. So this is best if you don't want to charge your laptop while you have it connected to two monitors. 2. I ordered two. One I use in my home office, the other at my business office. I've had them for about a month or so and I'm noticing that both screens do not stay connected continuously at either of my offices. Each docking station has w monitors connected via HDMI to my laptop via usbc. I always lose connection of one or both screens throughout the day. Especially when my laptop times out. It doesn't automatically connect both screens. I have to manually disconnect the 2 monitors then reconnect in order for it to pick up the signal again. Probably best for one additional screen vs two.

reviews.title: Almost perfect- headset difficulty’s
reviews.body: I’ve been using this Acer USB hub for a few weeks now, and overall I’m really happy with it. I bought it mainly because my laptop doesn’t have enough USB ports for all my schoolwork gear and gaming accessories, and this hub has made things so much easier. Setup and use Right out of the box, it was completely plug-and-play — no software, no setup. I just plugged it into my laptop and started connecting my devices. The size is perfect for portability; I toss it in my backpack when I go between school and home, and it doesn’t take up much space on my desk either. Performance For most of my devices, the hub works flawlessly. My mouse, keyboard, flash drives, and external hard drive all connect instantly and run smoothly. File transfers are quick, and I didn’t notice any lag or drop in performance. The USB 3.0 speeds feel solid, which is great when I’m moving large files for class projects or videos. Build quality It feels well-made for the price — not cheap or flimsy. The cord is thick enough that I’m not worried about it bending or breaking easily, and the ports hold connections snugly. It’s clearly built to handle everyday use. The one issue The only thing keeping this from being a 5-star review is my headset. For some reason, when I plug my USB headset into the hub, it either doesn’t get recognized or the microphone cuts in and out. When I plug it directly into my laptop, it works perfectly fine. It’s not a huge deal since everything else works great, but it’s a bit annoying since I use the headset for both online classes and gaming. From what I can tell, the hub might not deliver enough power or stability for certain audio devices, which isn’t uncommon for smaller, bus-powered hubs like this one. Final thoughts Aside from that minor issue, I’m really happy with this hub. It does exactly what I need — adds a few extra ports, keeps everything connected, and is simple to use. For everyday accessories and school use, it’s a great buy. Just be aware that some more sensitive or high-power devices (like headsets or external hard drives) might work better plugged directly into your computer. Overall rating: 4 out of 5 stars Would I recommend it? Definitely — especially if you just need more USB ports for regular devices and don’t plan on using it for audio or power-hungry gear

I mainly use it for work and do a lot of typing, so it was important to me that it be comfortable as well as nice-looking, and so far it has completely met my expectations. When I bought it, I didn’t realize that the letters were printed on the front of the keycaps rather than on top. It only took me a few hours to get used to it, though, and now I actually like it because I think the lettering may wear off more slowly. The only thing I didn’t like is that it doesn’t have a dedicated “Home” key. It has an “End” key, but not “Home.” That said, the software makes it incredibly easy to remap keys and customize their functions, so it works perfectly for me anyway. I also like that you can choose from several colorful lighting effects, although I usually keep the lights turned off because I find them a little distracting while working. The keyboard is somewhat heavy, so I would consider it more of a desk keyboard than something you would want to carry around, which is completely fine for my use.

reviews.title: 10/10 would buy another one, perfect gift
reviews.body: The AULA F75 Pro isn’t just a keyboard — it’s a life upgrade. From the moment I unboxed it, I knew this thing was built different. The build quality feels premium in a way that makes everything else on my desk feel insecure. The weight, the finish, the layout — chef’s kiss. But the sound? Oh man… pure mechanical ASMR. Every keystroke is a buttery, creamy “thock” that makes typing feel less like a task and more like a treat. It’s so smooth and satisfying I found myself typing things I didn’t even need to type — emails, notes, grocery lists, lorem ipsum paragraphs — just to hear it sing. Key layout & switch orientation: One thing I absolutely love is how the keys are south-facing, sitting slightly inward instead of pointing outward toward you. It gives the whole board a cleaner, sleeker look and makes the RGB shine through in a softer, more premium way. Wireless performance: flawless. Zero lag, zero hiccups, zero drama. It connects instantly and stays rock-solid whether I’m gaming, working, or just vibing on YouTube comments. Battery life: absurdly good. I swear this thing runs on wizard energy because I keep checking the percentage and it keeps refusing to go down. RGB: The lighting is vibrant without being over-the-top, and the multi-function knob makes switching effects, brightness, and colors stupidly satisfying. One smooth twist and you can go from a calm ambient glow to full-on gamer neon. It’s intuitive, responsive, and makes controlling the RGB feel extra premium without the need of a software which is a plus. Overall? This keyboard is elite. Legendary. A masterpiece of clicky, thocky engineering. If you want something that feels incredible, sounds incredible, and looks incredible, the AULA F75 Pro is the one. I absolutely, genuinely loved this product.

reviews.title: Unbelievable quality on this thing
reviews.body: Just, WOW! This thing is HEAVY but feels like it was made out of butter. The exterior casing is made out of what feels like dense '90s style plastic which doesn't show fingerprints. If I didn't know better I thought it was metal covered in some kind of coating. The keys on this thing are the smoothest I have ever felt in my life. Just pure buttery smoothness, but a really nice clickety clack when you start typing. There isn't a spring sound like a lot of old keyboards from the '80s up to the mid '90s, but the clacking sound is still very satisfying and retro in its own way. The lighting patterns are just out of this world. I expected it to just light up, but it has quite a few different patterns like rippling, pulsing, and my favorite is some kind of mode that makes the colors jump around. The fact that the lettering is on the front of the key instead of the top is really cool. So far the Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz connections have both been really good, I haven't tried it plugged in but I'm sure it would be good. Seriously, the quality on this thing is unreal and exceeds my expectations by several miles. I thought I was just getting a fairly decent plastic keyboard that would weigh about the same as most others and have springy sounding keys. This thing reminds me of some kind of professional music gear. If you aren't sure, just get one, this is seriously one of the highest quality items I have ever received from Amazon from a non-top-tier brand.

reviews.title: Very Impressive
reviews.body: I'm impressed. Coming from a 4 year old Corsair mechanical keyboard with cherry mx switches, I had high hopes that this keyboard would get the job done. It lacks dedicated media keys, but you still have media keys by using the function key. The battery is excellent to start; I hope it lasts just as long as my Corsair did. The weight is a little beefy despite it being mostly plastic and thicc. The size is perfect if you intend to use it on your lap or TV tray. There are many different LED modes as well, which is nice, as well as the fact that you can set these modes without having to install some sort of app to control them. While I primarily use the 2.4 connection, I do like the fact that it supports 3 bt devices. The response rate is very good and on par with the Corsair. You will have to get used to the arrow key layout with end, pg up, pg dn, and delete being in one single vertical row. Probably the most intriguing thing that made me want to even look at it was the front etched keys, which were perfect for my use case. I usually rest the keyboard on a shelf slightly higher than my shoulder when I sit so the keyboard is closer to my eye level than my hands. These keys make it easier to quickly see and press some custom commands I have instead of having to pick up the keyboard, sit it on my lap or tray, and then use my commands. The key presses are also very muted from the cherry mx switches, which is a plus and slightly more satisfying. Overall, I'm Impressed. (update as of 3-15-26) Nearly a year later, the battery's lifespan has decreased to about 50% of its original capacity.

reviews.title: So, awesome I’m jealous!
reviews.body: I bought this keyboard for my husband and switched the keycaps to fit his aesthetic as well as so he can read a bit better. (He’s new to the computer club used to be console and he’s got bad eyesight from the military.) so in the picture the keycaps are changed but not the switches! The original keycaps it comes with is a grey with the letters, symbols, and words on the side. Even though I swapped them out I want to state they are absolutely excellent quality, super soft matte feel, and low profile. I kept the keycaps for future use instead of tossing them or offering them up to my family. Which is what I usually do with manufactured keycaps. So, that’s how good they are! That and they honestly are an absolutely gorgeous color in person despite just being greytones. Now onto more of the benefits this keyboards the forth of fifth I’ve customized (I just customize as a hobby for friends and family) This one though is the first of this brand and oh my gosh do I regret not buying this brand sooner! Mainly for myself because of all the bonuses with this keyboard. Haha. Firstly, the keyboard came in awesome packaging and when I realized it can be used wirelessly too! Absolutely fantastic! I didn’t check for that before purchasing so it was a super awesome surprise! And the quality too my husband has absolutely loved getting to use his new keyboard and he got so giddy with the RGB too. I feel like building wise too this is a great keyboard for beginners. If you want a nice keyboard that has easy hot-swappable capabilities this is definitely where to start! And the volume button is such a bonus too. It makes accessibility count with this keyboard. That along with how compact it is too it takes such little space. To put into retrospect his desk is only I think 38 inches width and he still has plenty of room on each side of his desk for his snacks and drinks because of how little space the keyboard is. Literally no issues have come from the keyboard, it even with his wonky usb ports (a custom built computer composed of old/used parts.) it works well and doesn’t have any connectivity issues. So, to put all the perks together: -compact and comfortable -easy to swap keycaps around and switches —switches it came with are the perfect click for those who don’t like it to be an overbearing sound. —perfect for beginners of customizing keyboards. -Volume nob to control volume with easy access rather than fighting around your desk to get to the speaker control. -has wired, Bluetooth, and dongle capabilities which cleans up wire management. — Battery life is great so charging doesn’t happen as often and it lasts even longer with rgb turned off. - I almost forgot: also, has amazing presets of rgb colors that are fun and is perfect for zoning out to when you are having writers or artist block. Now, for the jealousy caption. I need to save up to get me one too! Because, this keyboard is everythingggg and I am definitely in need of an upgrade from my wired keyboard as well as all the perks of this keyboard. Definitely, looking forward to customizing one for myself down the line! This company is for sure my go too for keyboards. I highly recommend! For now I’ll just enjoy seeing the smile on my husband’s face every time he looks at his keyboard while we game together! The best Christmas purchase I’ve ever made!

reviews.title: Excelente calidad por el precio, el mejor teclado que he tenido
reviews.body: Primero que nada, si no tienes mucho conocimiento de teclados mecánicos y quieres empezar con este teclado, es una muy buena opción. La calidad se siente desde el momento de sacarlo de su caja, es un teclado pesado y no por eso es malo, se siente muy bien escribir en él, además el sonido es bastante diferente a un teclado que normalmente viene con una computadora nueva o que simplemente compraste uno barato en un Walmart o en internet, suena firme y bien al teclear. Comparado con teclados más baratos, estos switches mecánicos son muy sensibles, no me refiero a su duración, si no a la fuerza necesaria para pulsarlos ya que es mínima la fuerza necesitada, lo que lo hace menos pesado en jornadas largas en la computadora. Cuenta con varios modos de iluminación RGB, por mi parte solo lo tengo en color blanco y a un brillo moderado, porque sí, el brillo que tiene la retroiluminación es bastante. Otra de las cosas que me gusto es que puedes checar la batería del teclado con la combinación de teclas: FN + B. Cosa que es muy útil ya que no cuenta con otro indicador de batería. Solo para concluir, es un excelente teclado que vale mucho la pena, y si lo encuentras en descuento no dudes en adquirirlo.
reviews.body_en: First of all, if you don't have much knowledge of mechanical keyboards and want to start with this keyboard, it is a very good option. The quality is felt from the moment you take it out of the box, it is a heavy keyboard and that does not mean it is bad, it feels very good to type on it, plus the sound is quite different from a keyboard that normally comes with a new computer or that you simply bought a cheap one at a Walmart or on the internet, it sounds firm and good when typing. Compared to cheaper keyboards, these mechanical switches are very sensitive, I am not referring to their duration, but to the force necessary to press them since the force needed is minimal, which makes them less burdensome for long days at the computer. It has several RGB lighting modes, for my part I only have it in white and at a moderate brightness, because yes, the brightness of the backlight is quite a bit. Another thing that I liked is that you can check the keyboard battery with the key combination: FN + B. Which is very useful since it does not have another battery indicator. Just to conclude, it is an excellent keyboard that is very worth it, and if you find it at a discount, do not hesitate to purchase it.

reviews.title: Great keyboard, definitely happy with the purchase - great price too.
reviews.body: Easily the best keyboard I've ever bought, and I've bought some high-tier brands in the past for over a hundred dollars. It comes with a keyswitch tool, extra switches, and does not feel cheap in quality. It also sounds nice when typing. It's that kind-of "muted clack" sound. Hard to describe such things but that's my best shot at it. The size is standard array and my fingers feel good on it. I was able to switch out my keycaps for WASD (I prefer circular key caps for those) and the caps do not clash with the other caps what-so-ever. The wireless bluetooth and plugged in modes both work well; I was able to use it wirelessly for about 3 days of near-constant use before having to plug it in. Honestly, I just left it plugged in since then so not sure how well the battery is on a recharge. The lights are appealing, the keys look nice; the color scheme is kinda abstract but I'm not mad about it. Overall, great keyboard, and it's held up for a couple months now with no degradation. Thanks Redragon. Appreciate a good product.

reviews.title: Bought both keyboards so I could compare
reviews.body: (TLDR): The “LED” one (less expensive) works/sounds just as fine, the only real difference is the “QWERTY” one has brighter and more vibrant backlighting. If you just care about functionality/affordability, get the cheaper one. If you care more about aesthetics, spend a lil more! - - - - - I have two fellow gamer friends who desperately needed new keyboards, and since I already bought them keycaps, I decided to look for affordable mechanical keyboards for them. Amazon recommended these, reviews seemed promising, but I had another issue.. what’s the difference?? Why is one $10-15 more?? Nothing really explains the difference here and Google couldn’t help me with wtf LED vs QWERTY was (I thought they both were?? 🤨 Idk still learning about keyboards, bear with me here) A few reviews said one was brighter than the other, but other than that, I was unsure why one cost more. One friend only cared about functionality as they work from home, but the other friend very much cares about aesthetics and has a nice gamer setup. So figured, I’ll just get both! So here’s a breakdown of all the notable but pretty settle differences: RBG LED (White Logo) On Box: Sindri Red Dragon Price: Cheapest Option (great for what you pay for, best affordable option) Sound: Red Switches, not “silent” imo but not too loud either (I think this one sounded SLIGHTLY clackier, but friends couldn’t tell difference, maybe I just watch a lot of keyboard videos to notice lol) Base: Black “Metallic” appearance (bottom keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly lighter, not all that noticeable though Lighting: Not nearly AS vibrant, but still bright enough (top keyboard in dark pic) When you first plug in, the light is stagnant. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for casual gamers or work use RGB QWERTY (Red Logo) On Box: Rudra Red Dragon Price: Slightly Pricier (still great for what you pay for tbh) Sound: Red Switches, same, not “silent” imo but not too loud either Base: Black Plastic appearance (top keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly heavier. Lighting: Much more vibrant (bottom keyboard in dark pic, pic doesn’t do justice, it was significantly brighter) When you first plugin, the light is flowing. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for gamers and work use - - - - - My review is already long af, but I’ll have my friends update me on overall usage overtime. The “aesthetics” friend plays way more games on their PC, so I’ll be able to tell heavy gamer use for the QWERTY one. While the “functional” friend will be using it for work, as they work from home, so I’ll tell more daily use for the LED one. 👍 I’ll ask more about the settings as well as time goes on, for now, they’re just happy with their new keyboards!
reviews.body_en: (TLDR): The “LED” one (less expensive) works/sounds just as fine, the only real difference is the “QWERTY” one has brighter and more vibrant backlighting. If you just care about functionality/affordability, get the cheaper one. If you care more about aesthetics, spend a lil more! - - - - - I have two fellow gamer friends who desperately needed new keyboards, and since I already bought them keycaps, I decided to look for affordable mechanical keyboards for them. Amazon recommended these, reviews seemed promising, but I had another issue.. what’s the difference?? Why is one $10-15 more?? Nothing really explains the difference here and Google couldn’t help me with wtf LED vs QWERTY was (I thought they both were?? 🤨 Idk still learning about keyboards, bear with me here) A few reviews said one was brighter than the other, but other than that, I was unsure why one cost more. One friend only cared about functionality as they work from home, but the other friend very much cares about aesthetics and has a nice gamer setup. So figured, I’ll just get both! So here’s a breakdown of all the notable but pretty settle differences: RBG LED (White Logo) On Box: Sindri Red Dragon Price: Cheapest Option (great for what you pay for, best affordable option) Sound: Red Switches, not “silent” imo but not too loud either (I think this one sounded SLIGHTLY clackier, but friends couldn’t tell difference, maybe I just watch a lot of keyboard videos to notice lol) Base: Black “Metallic” appearance (bottom keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly lighter, not all that noticeable though Lighting: Not nearly AS vibrant, but still bright enough (top keyboard in dark pic) When you first plug in, the light is stagnant. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for casual gamers or work use RGB QWERTY (Red Logo) On Box: Rudra Red Dragon Price: Slightly Pricier (still great for what you pay for tbh) Sound: Red Switches, same, not “silent” imo but not too loud either Base: Black Plastic appearance (top keyboard in light pic) Felt slightly heavier. Lighting: Much more vibrant (bottom keyboard in dark pic, pic doesn’t do justice, it was significantly brighter) When you first plugin, the light is flowing. Functionality: No lag so far, smooth typing, perfect for gamers and work use - - - - - My review is already long af, but I’ll have my friends update me on overall usage overtime. The “aesthetics” friend plays way more games on their PC, so I’ll be able to tell heavy gamer use for the QWERTY one. While the “functional” friend will be using it for work, as they work from home, so I’ll tell more daily use for the LED one. 👍 I’ll ask more about the settings as well as time goes on, for now, they’re just happy with their new keyboards!

reviews.title: Decent for a deal, but could be more durable.
reviews.body: I wouldn't buy this keyboard for more than thirty dollars, but it goes on sale enough that I believe it's worth buying for the twenty or so dollars the bring the price down to. I've had this keyboard for over a year, and it's worked flawlessly for most of that time. There's not much to say about it, functionally. It's a standard full-sized mechanical keyboard. It's not quiet, but I like how clicky it is, personally. Now, for the reason I don't recommend you buy this for full price. About nine or ten months into owning this item, the keys started to behave finicky. The 'R' key no longer lights up and the 'A' key has a problem with double inputs. I'll give the keyboard this, I use it a lot. I'm a writer and a gamer, so I've really put it through its paces. I'm also not as anal about maintenance as I probably should be. If you regularly dust and clean under the keycaps, it would probably last you a good deal longer. If your like me, someone who puts your keyboard through heavy use, I would go with something more durable. If you only intend to game with it, it should be fine for about a year, which for twenty dollars is a fine deal.

reviews.title: Never thought I'd love a keyboard so much...
reviews.body: It's taking a little getting used to the slightly different arrangement of some keys but man... overall, this keyboard KICKS TAIL!!! I love how it lights up, I'm always working in low light or the dark and my eyes aren't what they used to be so I just can't tell you how much of a difference it makes. I also feel like the key symbols won't/can't wear out because they're backlit. Typical keyboards have letter and words wear off over time, but I don't see how that's possible with this keyboard. It's not a "gamer keyboard" it's just a great basic keyboard with all the functions you need. Keystrokes feel amazing! Not sure how to describe but when you're typing it just feels really nice. A real quality built product and worth every penny. I'm considering buying another before they don't make them anymore... LOL Oh, the battery lasts forever on this thing too. You can turn it OFF when you're done for the day and you can set the keyboard to pair/work with multiple computers (even have keys configured differently if you like). The backlight shuts off when you remove your hands from the keyboard or stop typing for about 5 seconds, but its got this really cool "motion detection" feature that once you put your hands over the keys again or start typing it lights right back up! I'm telling you if you're in the market for a new BLUETOOTH keyboard and are willing to pay a little more for a NICE one... this is the board to have!!! I really love it. I'll give you the 1 thing I didn't like about it as I began using it... The FUNCTION ROW of keys has no space above the NUMBERS or Number pad, etc. So it's super easy to hit the wrong keys sometimes. I'll often go to use the "home" key and end up hitting the key to switch between machines, or the biggest one is the "lock" key the farthest top right key over the number pad's "minus/dash" key. I often go to hit the "minus/dash" key and end up locking my windows (having to sign in again). HOWEVER, using the Logitech software that is used to configure the keyboard I was able to just disable that lock key. I don't need a KEY for that anyway. When I want to lock my Windows session (log out) without shutting down, I'll just do it the normal way with my mouse (Start > Power > Lock). No big, been doing that forever anyway. Anyway, this keyboard is awesome. Especially, once you get used to it. Most times I get a new keyboard and have to get used to the key arrangements and different spacing anyway. Might as well do it with a great keyboard. 😊👍🏻 P.S. I have always been a Microsoft keyboard/mouse kinda guy. I didn't think much of Logitech until I got the MX Master 2 Mouse, which is now also my favorite ever. This keyboard goes with that mouse it's sold in bundles they're of the same product set.

reviews.title: Satisfying typing experience
reviews.body: I love this keyboard. I use the same monitor for my gaming PC and for my work Surface Pro. I had a wired keyboard which I had to unplug from the gaming PC and plug into the docking station every morning and then do the reverse after my work hours. It became tedious after a while, so I decided to upgrade to a wireless keyboard that can switch between multiple devices without having me crawl under my desk to do so. This one seemed not too expensive, had full width, and reviews were decent. I'm very pleased. Switching between devices is handled with 3 dedicated buttons for this specific purpose, no crawling required. I used the dongle to pair it with the gaming PC, and Bluetooth to pair it with my work computer. Now I can work from the kitchen or the yard if I want to. It's slightly louder than I expected, but is by no means clickety like some others I've used. Typing is now completely satisfying. The texture of the buttons is soft and the feedback is addictive and makes me want to type forever. As an unexpected bonus, I was able to connect the keyboard to my phone and type in mobile apps with a full keyboard!! What a novel and refreshing experience. The only complaint from my daughter is that it doesn't have colored backlight. It's just plain white.

reviews.title: Beautiful keyboard
reviews.body: So I just received and began to use this keyboard today. I am pretty blown away by how nice it looks, how good it feels, and just the experience overall. Compared to my previous keyboard, I already like this a fair amount more. For reference, I was using the Corsair k57 RGB wireless. Also a quite nice keyboard, but this has a much more premium feel. It's also much more professional looking, which is why I chose it as I plan to use this in an office environment. Some thoughts below. -The clicks are super nice, I've never used a "clicky" switch with feedback like this before and I quite enjoy it. Probably my favorite feedback I've had from just typing on a keyboard. The various corsair boards I've used in the past I typically chose a quiet and/or a linear switch. -Overall a very nice, professional look. I wouldn't expect any weird looks with a keyboard like this in a professional environment. -Pairing was easy, plugged in the receiver and it instantly connected; no other input needed. Even the sister product to this never did that for me, the MX master 3S mouse. I had a bit of a struggle trying to get that to pair using the included receiver, as I recall. (Otherwise one of my favorite mice, also coming from a mostly corsair brand background). There is also bluetooth pairing, if preferred. (or if the receiver refuses to work, like my MX master 3S.) One minor negative is the backlight. The first problem was even getting the keyboard to light up at all. The keys for the keyboard backlight simply did not seem to function at all, no matter if I had the FN key held or not. Puzzled, I installed logitech's software and looked for options there. No luck. A bit annoyed at this point. Luckily, their software offered me access to an upcoming beta version of their software, "Logitech Options", so I downloaded that to poke around and see if there were more settings there. As it turns out there were. Oddly, they didn't work though. The keyboard refused to light up, the keys meant to dim or brighten it doing nothing at all. As I began a search to see if this was a common issue, the backlight finally came on. No idea what changed. Pretty standard white LED backlights. Lots of pissed off customers on forums about it though. Apparently, Logitech has been pretty silent about the issue. I'd be pissed too, if my $200 keyboard didn't have a functioning backlight due to software issues. With that rambling anecdote, the backlight itself is just fine, about what I expected for a professional keyboard like this. Just clean white LEDs. In summary, a very nice looking, nice feeling premium keyboard. Pretty unassuming in a professional environment. Easy setup. Quite happy with it. Edit: The backlight does not seem to remember brightness settings between use sessions, so if you will get super annoyed or angry about having to hit brightness up each time you use, that's something to consider. Most annoyingly, if the room is deemed "too bright" by the sensor, the backlight will not turn on at all. Understandable, but I'd still like the option.

reviews.title: Very disappointing for a $150+ keyboard.
reviews.body: I was very disappointed when I started using this overpriced keyboard. First of all, the build quality is inexcusable for a $150+ keyboard, especially from a brand like Logitech. The space bar and the backspace keys squeak horribly every time I press them. I understand that can be fixed by applying some white silicone grease, but I shouldn't have to do that with an expensive keyboard right out of the box. In addition, the rubber foot across the back of the keyboard has already started to peel off. I purchased the tactile (quiet typing) version, and while it isn't the loudest keyboard I have ever typed on, "quiet" is not at all how I would describe it. Someone in the next room or cubicle would definitely be able to hear you typing on this. I wonder how loud the "clicky" version is... And now, to address the backlight issue: Several reviews have mentioned problems with the backlight. It seems to function "as intended", but the design choices really make me scratch my head. The backlight will turn off just a few seconds after you stop typing, and doesn't turn on again until you press a key. That means that if you aren't constantly typing, the backlight will be turning on and off in a way that is very visually distracting at the bottom of your vision. If you take your hands away from the keyboard, you will not have the keys illuminated to help orient your hands when you start typing again. In a dark room that means you can't see anything on the keys. Even the timing of the backlight is inconsistent. Sometimes it turns off while I am still typing, sometimes it stays on for a minute or two with no input, like it got stuck. At first I thought I just had to adjust the timeout settings on the Logi Options+ app. Nope! No options! Just a couple of annoying, distracting backlight animations (like, random keys illuminating, why would anyone want that?!). I'm not sure who signed-off on the design for this thing or what they were thinking. Furthermore, the caps lock key has a distracting blinking whenever it is on, especially annoying if you are gaming and caps lock is set to something like toggle run/walk. The keyboard is Bluetooth only, which seems to work fine. But I would have liked to have the option to plug it in like a normal USB keyboard. As far as I know the USB plug is only for charging, but also leaves an always illuminated and fairly bright "charging" LED, very obnoxious if your computer is in your bedroom. In short: Don't waste your money on this. I will be returning mine.

reviews.title: Beware the USB dongles
reviews.body: Original review: It's a keyboard an it works After hearing people rave about mechanical keyboards, I decided to get myself one. I am not sure how representative of mechanical keyboards this one is, but I find it to be very similar to everything I have used before. The keys don't feel "clicky" at all. In fact, I am constantly running into an issue of resting my hands on the keyboard, and "mushing down" a key by mistake (in other words, "wwwwwwwwwwwwwwwww" because my finger pressed a key without me even noticing). I think I can get used to pulling my hands away from the keyboard to keep that from happening, but I find it weird that I now have to do this. I assumed the keys would be harder to press, not mushier than the cheap-o keyboards I have had. Another issue I have had is that the keyboard is not flat. I have tested it on multiple surfaces, including a glass table. I ended having to prop one side up with some paper. Not too happy about that. For whatever reason, this does not have a print screen key. Luckily you can remap it using the Logi Options+ software. Honestly, at this price, I am not sure I would recommend this keyboard. Ok, so why 4 stars? It does have some positive points. First, it looks pretty sharp. Second, aside from not sitting flat, it feels solid / well-built / quality. It is small, yet it is heavier than most keyboards. I am used to keyboards lasting "forever", so I will update here if/when I run into issues. Third, switching between different machines works flawlessly. Fourth, it allows me to bring my settings to all computers (e.g. remapping the screen capture key). Fifth, it has a rechargeable battery and it lasts long enough that I never have to worry. I do have a charging cable right on my desk, so every once in a while I just leave it plugged in, so I have never seen it go below 85%. What else can I say, it is a keyboard and it works. ----- Updated review: beware the USB dongles. Logitech mouses and keyboards (e.g. "MX Mechanical", "MX Master 3s", "MX Anywhere 3") connect either via Bluetooth, or via a USB dongle. However, the USB dongles are not all the same. For example, the "MX mechanical" keyboard only connects to a "bolt" dongle; and the "MX Anywhere 3" mouse only connects to a "unifying" dongle. Unfortunately, there is no clear guide / summary for which devices go together. You just have to check each device before buying to see what dongle it uses. Devices in the same generation are *not* guaranteed to use the same type of dongle. Here is my experience: I setup for myself a MX mechanical keyboard + MX Master 3s mouse and everything works fine. Both devices connect to a "bolt" dongle, so I have a "bolt" dongle on my laptop, and another "bolt" dongle on a desktop computer. I can switch between laptop and desktop with a press of a button. The keyboard/mouse itself is fine, the review can be seen above. My wife saw my setup and wanted the same, but she didn't want the MX Master 3s mouse ("it is too big"), so I got her a this same "MX Mechanical" keyboard and a pink "MX Anywhere 3". As it turns out, the mouse does not come with a "bolt" dongle, it comes with a "unifying" dongle. So now I have one "bolt" dongle which connects only to the keyboard, and one "unifying" dongle which connects only to the mouse. Thus, to "fix" this situation, I either need to use Bluetooth for everything (which I was trying to avoid to begin with), or I need to purchase 1 extra bolt dongle and 1 extra unifying dongle, so that each computer has both a "unifying" and a "bolt" dongle. Let's hope I have enough USB ports, or I will also need a USB hub. Even if you are aware that different dongles exist, you still need to be careful. If you buy a "MX Anywhere 3", you get a "unifying" dongle, but if you buy a "MX Anywhere 3 for business", then it has a "bolt" dongle. This is, by the way, how I ended up with a "unifying" dongle - while browsing the products, I opened up two tabs, one with a black MX Anywhere 3, and one with a pink MX Anywhere 3, except one of them was "for business" and the other was not. You might think this mess would warrant giant disclaimers ("DOES NOT HAVE A BOLT CONNECTOR"), or some kind of guide for which devices go together, but nope. For extra hilarity, Amazon bundles a "MX mechanical mini" (bolt) with a "MX Anywhere 3" (unifying). The whole thing is confusing, misleading, and just terrible user/customer experience. If I could start over, I would just get something else.

reviews.title: Best office keyboard to date
reviews.body: This keyboard is pretty amazing. I own a HHKB, and a Pok3r. I build and customize my own keyboards. I bought this mainly because of the Logitech Flow feature. But first, I wanted to talk about the keyboard itself and why I think this is the best office keyboard to date. The build quality is amazing. It's sturdy, and the internals are very tight, which means, no rattling, no added noise or reverbiation. As a result, this is a very quiet mechanical keyboard (I can only speak for the brown switch version). The keycaps are made out of recycled plastic, but they don't feel cheap. They are quite smooth and easy to type with. The typing experience is very consistent and smooth (see type test photo). My typing speed is consistent with my other keyboards, but for me, it's definitely feels much better to type with tactile silent switches compared to my other keyboards. Even though this keyboard is a low profile keyboard, there are flip up feet at the bottom of the keyboard to lift it up a little more to get a better angle if that's what you prefer. The lights are nice, but what makes this keyboard really stand out is when it doesn't use the lights at all. Without the backlights on, this keyboard can do 10 months on 1 charge, which is completely unheard of for a mechanical full size wireless keyboard. I've had this keyboard for a couple of days on the whole time, and by now, my other wireless 60% would have died and required a recharge. There is only one issue with this keyboard which is customization. For Macros, only some of the keys (F Keys and Cursor Targeting Group) can be customized vs what I am used to, which is being able to customize every single key. For customizing the physical look itself such as changing the switches or the keycaps, this keyboard cannot be customized like that. The spacebar doesn't use standard stabilizer stem widths. You can replace every key cap except for the spacebar. You also cannot change the switches unless you know some soldering which is not recommended. As for the reason why I bough the keyboard. I absolutely love it! The logitech flow option allows me to move from my multiple computer setups with only one keyboard and mouse. I often multitask, I have a computer running 24/7 as my "smart tv" as well as my personal laptop, and my work computer. Considering how I can flow through all those computers from one set of mouse and keyboard without having to physically switch the mouse to use that specific computer is absolutely game changing. I feel like I am using one computer, even though they are all completely seperated. Whenever a product can make someone's life easier, is when you know you have something truly revolutionary. For work and every day use, this is absolutely the best office keyboard to date.

reviews.title: Excellent keyboard with a few minor issues
reviews.body: This keyboard is a solid little keyboard. It’s very well built and has a satisfying feel and noise while typing. I really like how easy it is to switch between different computers. I have it set to use both my desktop PC and my MacBook Air when I dock it on my desk. It knows which is which and changes the keyboard layout accordingly. Everything just works. The battery life is excellent and it charges up really quickly over usb c. The Logitech Options app is really easy to use with everything laid out in such a way to just make sense. Also; the back lighting is simple but still nice. Ok onto my complaints. First I wish the key caps were a better material. They get glossy really quick from the slightly dirtiest fingers. I dunno if that’s due to the dark grey colour or the material itself. But for the price it should have better key caps. Second; I wish this thing had full rgb backlighting. The white is nice; but full colour would be better. Ok that’s it. So overall this is a great desktop keyboard that you could also take with you if you wanted to use your laptop or iPad on the go with it. It’s great for multi device use and the typing experience is really nice!! If you’re coming from the keyboard that came with your Mac or PC… or want something small and portable; this is definitely for you!

reviews.title: Light, bright, responsive, and with a wonderful profile layout
reviews.body: Best keyboard I've ever owned. Sturdy case, sleek profile, the layout makes this keyboard incredibly easy to clean without the need to dismantle the keys in the process. The White LEDs are bright and easy to see in the dark, unlike many backlit keyboards that can make it harder to read the keys. The responsiveness both in typing and in the tactile feel of every key clacking on release is a delight. As a friend has been using a slightly different G4 model for 5 years, I have every expectation that I will be using this keyboard for years to come. Very happy customer.

reviews.title: Worth 60 bucks easy, on sale it's an absolute bargain.
reviews.body: I ordered one of these after my place of employment got tired of keyboards failing constantly. After several months of outright abusive use by my co-workers, they still performed flawlessly with a lovely sense of tactile feedback, soda spills aside. One failed only after half a thermos of coffee was spilled into it, but that's to be expected from anything not waterproof rated. After ordering one for myself to use at home, I LOVE typing on it. It's my first true mechanical keyboard, and it's pleasant to just tap away, typing whatever I feel like. Each key feels like it's got two levels of depression (almost like me): First a clear 'catch' when the key activates and types, and then another more firm one when you reach the bottom of the key well. I've yet to have it double-type anything even when my clumsy fingers wanted to, although it hasn't saved me from butterfingering my keystrokes in games. As far as gaming goes, it's not PERFECT. It does make an audible noise when typing, so when you are frantically spamming the strafe or jump keys, it's going to sound like clicking the mouse over and over, but it's really no worse than your average mouse. If you're wearing headphones and blasting your speakers, you won't notice it. If you're in a silent small room, you can't avoid hearing it. Find your medium. Its clearly more meant for office work, but I find it good for gaming, and it's sturdy and heavy enough it doesn't move around at all or feel like it'll die if I drop my phone on it.

reviews.title: Not the best choice for Mac; satisfying click but not for quiet environments
reviews.body: I can't tell you how well this works for gaming, but if you're looking to buy this as a Mac keyboard for standard daily use, definitely read on. This keyboard is far better for a PC. It doesn't have matching keys for a Mac keyboard, so you'll have reduced functionality with key commands. These are differences I've come across so far: - Instead of a CMD key on both sides of the space bar, this keyboard has only one on the left of the spacebar that functions that way, and it's not in the position of the usual Mac CMD key. (see my pic) - There's no volume control on this keyboard, so you'll have to have your Mac keyboard available to change volume unless you keep volume control visible on your menu bar. - Screen dimming requires holding this keyboard's fn key and then using F1 or F2. - Some special function keys on this keyboard don't do anything on a Mac. Here's what I do like about the keyboard: - Satisfying click. The keys are like old school keyboards with large keys that actually had feel to them. The volume of the click is kind of loud though, so if you need to maintain a quieter environment this keyboard won't do. - The attached 10 key is nice to have. - It's corded so no batteries required. - The keyboard is sturdy feeling with just-right weight to it - The key backlighting is adjustable - No quick trigger keys means no accidental double lettering - Because the keyboard rises high off your desktop compared to modern keyboards, make sure you have a seating position that lets you keep your hands lower than normal. Overall this keyboard is probably great for gaming or for PC users who don't have to keep it down while using it. If you're a Mac user, especially one who needs a quiet environment, you should look at different models.

reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.body: Bought this for my wife’s WFH setup. She fell in love with the Creamy Switch craze on TikTok and this was a reasonably priced keyboard that fit the bill. I found a cute sakura themed keycap set to replace these, but she said she’d have been happy with the blues and purples that came preinstalled. It looks great, feels and sounds fantastic, and does everything you’d want from a keyboard. She loves the size, specifically that it includes the number pad. Not enough decent keyboards do these days. People want minimalism in everything, but the functionality of a dedicated number pad is hard to beat. Connecting is super easy. We’re using the hardwired USB-C option, but I was able to use Bluetooth on my laptop at work while I was testing and installing the other keycaps prior to giving this as a birthday gift. She loves that it’s such a lightweight feel of typing, even noticeably so to someone without the heavy handed typing of myself, having grown up on IBM and Alps switches which allow for some decent banging. I’m not a keyboard snob or really a deep enthusiast, but some of my friends and coworkers that care more than I do really loved it as well. It’s a crowd pleaser, and that wonderful little subdued THOK on each tap is soothing as foretold.

reviews.title: Bought it for my husband and now it's mine
reviews.body: First I want to say that I initially bought this for my husband as he had bought a walmart clicky brand keyboard and was finally growing tired of the clicky sound lol. Well as the keyboard enthusiast I suggested this one as it was simple and a few of the review videos had sounded promising. When it arrived the first thing I noticed was the heft, this was made with durable material and not light weight at all, which put some ease to my mind that it wasn't just made of cheap plastic. The size was just perfect, I couldn't be happier, and when I typed for the first time the creamy and thocky sound just itched the right place in my brain. I could not get enough of it. I love that there are 3 types of way that you can connect, BT; Dongle or wired. I always prefer wired. The keycaps are nice, although I prefer rounded keycaps to the sharp square ones, I did replace the factory keycaps and I just fell in love with this more. The switches sound nice and deep and honestly, this is almost perfect for me, I'll be playing around with this keyboard especially since it's hot swappable and I might try other switches. For those just starting out with interest in the keyboard area, this is a great first start with a not too expensive price point! I did end up having to buy another keyboard for my husband since I stole this one, it was definitely worth it though! Can't wait to mod this one a little more!

reviews.title: Great keyboard for the price
reviews.body: The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests. It has linear switches meaning there's no "bump" or clickiness to them, I'm not 100% sure what exact switches they are because there is some conflicting information online. I think mine has "Star Vector" switches? Regardless, the switches are quite light on force and very quiet, which brings us to the sound. This keyboard sounds great for the price. It's a little on the clacky side, but the switches have no scratchiness to them and are obviously pre-lubed, and there appears to be some kind of sound-deadening material inside the case as there is none of that hollow pinginess you get from something like a cheap Logitech mechanical. Overall it is a massive improvement from the Logitech keyboard I had previously to this one. The case is plastic but seems to be fairly high quality. The keyboard is surprisingly heavy which is very confidence inspiring and gives you a very stable feeling typing experience. It also has RGB lighting on all of the keys but the keycaps are not shine-through meaning the lettering doesn't light up. If that's a big deal to you, I'm sure you could swap them out for something else later as it does come with a keycap and switch puller, which also means you can change the switches if you want. It also has 3 different connection modes: "Wired" which uses a USB-C port on the board for connection (and it does come with a USB-C to A cable in the box), "2.4 GHz" which uses a little wireless dongle that sits in a little slot on the top edge of the board when not in use, and it's also able to connect via bluetooth. I haven't tested the battery life as I use this keyboard at my desktop computer with the wired connection, but having the different modes and a physical switch to change between them means you could have this board connected to multiple different devices and switch between them whenver you want which is cool and useful if you need that. I'm fairly new to the world of mechanical keyboards, this is only the second one I've ever owned, the first being a Logitech board that didn't sound or feel nearly as good as this one. As I type this review out on this very keyboard, I find myself liking the sound and feeling more and more. I'm sure there are things about it that someone with more knowledge and experience could pick apart and criticize, but overall I am very happy with this keyboard and would definitely recommend it to anyone who's not an expert and is looking for something better than the offerings from companies like Logitech and Razer.

title: AULA F75 75% Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, Hot Swappable Creamy Keyboard, Pre-lubed Linear Switches, 2.4GHz/Type-C/BT5.0, RGB Backlit Gaming Keyboards(White&Brown)
bullet_points: Tri-mode Connection Keyboard: AULA F75 wireless mechanical keyboard supports BT5.0, 2.4GHz wireless and USB wired connection, can connect up to five devices at the same time, and easily switch by shortcut keys or side button. F75 computer keyboard is suitable for PC, laptops, tablets, mobile phones, PS, XBOX etc, to meet all the needs of users. In addition, the rechargeable keyboard is equipped with a 4000mAh large-capacity battery, which has long-lasting battery life

Hot-swap Custom Keyboard: This custom mechanical keyboard with hot-swappable base supports 3-pin or 5-pin switches replacement. Even keyboard beginners can easily DIY there own keyboards without soldering issue. F75 gaming keyboards equipped with pre-lubricated stabilizers and linear switches, bring smooth typing feeling and pleasant creamy mechanical sound, provide fast response for exciting game

Advanced Structure & PCB Single Key Slotting: This thocky heavy mechanical keyboard features an advanced structure, extended integrated silicone pad, and PCB single key slotting, better optimizes resilience and stability, making the hand feel softer and more elastic. Five layers of filling silencer fills the gap between the PCB, the positioning plate and the shaft,effectively counteracting the cavity noise sound of the shaft hitting the positioning plate, and providing a solid feel

16.8 Million RGB Backlit: F75 light up led keyboard features 16.8 million RGB lighting color. With 16 lighting effects to add a great atmosphere to the game. And supports 10 cool music rhythm lighting effects with driver. Lighting brightness and speed can be adjusted by the knob or the FN and key combination. You can select the single color effect as wish. And you can turn the backlight off if you do not need it

Professional Gaming Keyboard: No matter the outlook, the construction, or the function, F75 mechanical keyboard is definitely a professional gaming keyboard. This 81-key 75% layout compact keyboard can save more desktop space while retaining the necessary arrow keys for gaming. Additionally, with the multi-function knob, you can easily control the backlight and Media. Full-key macro programmable, you can customize the function of single key or key combination function through F75 driver to increase the probability of winning the game and improve the work efficiency(Driver download: bit.ly/m/AULA). N key rollover, and supports WIN key lock to prevent accidental touches in intense games

Multi-function Control Knob: This AULA 75% wireless gaming keyboard is equipped with functional knob to switch gaming mode or office mode. In gaming mode, you can rotate the knob to adjust the brightness of the lights, and click the knob to switch the lighting effects easily; in office mode, rotate the knob to adjust the volume, and click the knob to play or pause. Long press the knob for about 5 seconds to switch modes

reviews.title: LOVE my first mechanical keyboard

If you type really fast it sounds like pebbles in the creek ^.^ I did some research before getting a keyboard since i wanted something of a good quality but was prepared to drop $100+ on it. Very pleased with the quality of t his one - it feels very sturdy, the keys have just enough resistance to effortless typing. With the knob you can switch different color modes and adjust the brightness or control volume. It also allows pairing with 3 devices (and switch with a brass of a button, well, 2 buttons but u get it) via Bluetooth and it’s very convenient since i can use it with my computer, iPad and steam deck. I use Mac book and the translation from cmd , option and, control buttons are a bit confusing since the keyboard is for windows, but once you get used to it it’s ok. All my friends without mechanical keyboards now want one and all my friends with one approved the buy =DD Oh, and I obviously replaced the keycaps - now the light mode really looks magical.

The 75% layout is a great balance between compact size and functionality. It keeps the important navigation and arrow keys while taking up considerably less desk space than a full-size keyboard. The wireless connectivity is also convenient and makes for a cleaner setup. The hot-swappable design is a major plus for anyone who enjoys customizing their keyboard. Being able to change switches without soldering gives you plenty of options to personalize the typing experience later. The keys feel responsive and consistent, whether I'm typing or gaming. The overall construction also feels solid, especially for the price. Overall, this is an excellent mechanical keyboard with a smooth typing experience, useful wireless functionality, and plenty of customization potential.

reviews.title: AULA F75 Review Glacial Blue Reaper Switches
reviews.body: I’ve been using the AULA F75 keyboard as my main keyboard, and it has been a great upgrade from my previous one, especially considering the price. I mainly use it wired, but I also tested the Bluetooth connection and it worked perfectly fine with no issues. The overall connectivity has been excellent, and I haven’t had any problems using it with my games. The RGB lighting looks really nice and adds a lot to the keyboard’s overall appearance. I do wish there were more RGB customization options and selections available, but the included effects are still enjoyable and look great. The Reaper switches feel and sound amazing. In person, the keys have a really creamy sound profile, while in videos they seem to come across as a bit more thocky. The typing experience feels smooth, satisfying, and enjoyable. The multifunction knob is one of my favorite features. I mainly use it for controlling volume, and having quick access without needing keyboard shortcuts is extremely convenient. It’s a small addition, but it makes everyday use much easier. For gaming, this keyboard has been great for me. Everyone has different preferences when it comes to switches and keyboard feel, but personally, I really enjoy using it while gaming. The responsiveness, comfort, and connectivity have all been solid. Overall, the AULA F75 is an excellent upgrade at its price point. I’m very happy with it so far, and I’m definitely interested in trying out other versions of this keyboard in the future. For now, this has been a fantastic choice, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a quality mechanical keyboard without spending a lot.

Ele é bem mais pesado que meu antigo teclado (que não tinha toda essa construção do AULA), as teclas parecem ser de uma ótima qualidade, essa cor é muito bonita e, apesar da minha preocupação de não enxergar direito as letras pelo azul ser claro, elas são bem visíveis. It is much heavier than my old keyboard (which didn't have all this AULA construction), the keys seem to be of great quality, this color is very beautiful and, despite my concern about not seeing the letters properly because the blue is light, they are very visible. Its RGB is very beautiful, even though you can't see the keys in the dark and I had no problem installing the software. The only thing I didn't like very much was that the extra switches are not the same as the ones that come with the keyboard, but I'm trusting in the quality of the leobog so I don't need to change them anytime soon (the sound is super satisfactory). Anyway, to be a top of the line keyboard the only thing missing was the aluminum construction, but for the price it's worth a lot, even more so if it's on sale. 10/10

reviews.title: Works. Just okay
reviews.body: This keyboard is adorable, has great soft (not super quiet, but soft feeling) key presses, its responsive, and it has great connectivity options. Its a happy medium between a full size keyboard versus a compact layout, and it's so easy and smooth to type on. That said, the RGB backlighting does not work for me. I've followed the instructions sent with the keyboard, followed the troubleshooting instructions from AULA and from Amazon, used AULA's software for this keyboard, tried factory resetting, and googled for help videos or anything I could find. Reached out to AULA's support, and they were unwilling to assist and just directed me to Amazon. All I could find on Amazon was the seller's support information. At this point I'm just accepting that it's a defect and something must be wrong within the keyboard, and I'm not savvy enough to diagnose their hardware issues nor do I have the time or will to demand a refund or replacement. The keyboard works great without RGB, but it was a big feature for me when purchasing this as it was mostly an aesthetic purchase. Yeah, I could have picked other options, but I chose this because of the price and I wish I hadn't. So, knocked two stars off for me. TL;DR - it's just a keyboard that you can use on multiple devices. If you just want simple for a good price, this is for you, cause it's a solid option. reviews.title: Budget HE keyboard that gives you all you need...
reviews.body: AULA WIN68 HE is my first ever HE keyboard, after years of being in the world of mechanical keyboards and exclusively favoring the brown switch (tactile) I always watched many videos and people praising HE keyboards and the edge they give to you in gaming primarily. We all know of the famed Wooting 60 HE which started this trend in gaming world both the price and being only 60% give's it only a small and competitive market for a few individuals that can afford it or need it for professional e-Sports. As primarily a single-player gamer I was blow away with how much HE switches changes your experience of playing and gives you for the first time ever something that gamepads had over keyboards, and that is you don't need to push the key all the way for it work, both only a slight push fulfils the given command that you want (MMOs and racing games benefit from this the most). The web software is one of the best features of this keyboard and it allows you to customize every single key however you want it, every key supports rapid trigger as well as customizing the dead zone as well as primarily the sensitivity of the keys. The standard version that I have allows you to customize the sensitivity from 0.8mm to larger if you prefer (default being 1.70mm, while mechanical boards clock at 2.1mm). Keyboard is hot swappable and you can change your magnetic switches really easily. Brightness and RGB is also good with no complaints in that department (you can customize it in the web software). The build quality is also good and think that board was upgraded to PBT switches since when typing on them the feel sandy and rough, sound quality is quite since magnetic switches are linear switches (both better in every way), and the keyboard is wired only which I prefer since I am using it on my personal PC and have no need to use it elsewhere. HE keyboards are definitely the future and every professional or enthusiast e-Sport gamer simply must have this keyboard because it gives them and edge in every way that mechanical keyboard simply cannot give at the moment! I recommended this board for anybody who is on the fence over coming to the HE world.

Considering the overall quality, sound, build, lighting, and features, this keyboard delivers an impressive experience for such a budget-friendly price. Overall, I highly recommend this keyboard to anybody looking for a budget-friendly gaming keyboard! I've attached a picture with my Logitech G305 mouse for a scale reference.

reviews.title: Best board for the price, BY FAR !!
reviews.body: Great board especially at this price point. This really raises the bar for entry level products and makes it much more accessible. This thing will impress most seasoned enthusiast. I could see this thing attaining a similar status to the Aula F75. You get really good acoustics, great switches (lubed BSUN Purples), gasket mounting AND hotswap. I've been typing on it for a few days and the sound tests you see online are very accurate, board sounds very creamy and poppy, which makes for a very satisfying typing experience. The RGB on this board is really bright and has some cool preset animations. Definitely NOT office friendly, I took this thing to the office one day and had to swap it for a normal keyboard because it is quite loud. I enjoy the sound but I don't think my coworkers did. lol Unfortunately I did notice that the space bar seems to make a really loud thunk which doesn't match the sound of the rest of the board, but you can fix this pretty easily with a rubber O-Ring or some foam inside the space bar. And sadly I did not get any spare keycaps with my order, as I've seen other buyers receive in their reviews :( Overall though, really good board and significantly raises the bar for entry level products. This thing will outperform boards that cost twice the price. I am very happy with my purchase and will be buying one for my gf too

reviews.title: Super impressive for the price.
reviews.body: I'm shocked at the quality of this keyboard for the price. The main case is plastic but a is very good quality plastic. Obviously, it's not going to be aluminum at this price. The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time. I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect. It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate. My only complaint whatsoever about this keyboard is that I'm not too crazy about the switches, but that's really a personal preference thing. They're certainly not terrible and I can definitely see other people with different preferences liking these, as actually a lot of other reviewers did really like the switches. But I'll probably be swapping them out, which is another great thing about this keyboard is that they are hot swappable. For those wondering about the sound - the stock keyboard is clacky rather than thocky.

The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time. I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect. It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate. My only complaint whatsoever about this keyboard is that I'm not too crazy about the switches, but that's really a personal preference thing. They're certainly not terrible and I can definitely see other people with different preferences liking these, as actually a lot of other reviewers did really like the switches. But I'll probably be swapping them out, which is another great thing about this keyboard is that they are hot swappable. For those wondering about the sound - the stock keyboard is clacky rather than thocky.

reviews.title: It's pretty good!
reviews.body: Chances are, you've found this keyboard after reading a number of Reddit threads or watching a review or 2 on Youtube, and I can confirm they're all very correct to recommend this keyboard. It's kind of obvious that it's not trying to be high-end, as evidenced by the all plastic build, basic and other creature-comforts that are left out, like volume knobs and little near-useless LED screens, but it is still a solid, well built keyboard with a decent-enough feature set. But, it's a keyboard, so if we're being real, its the tactile feel of typing on this thing along with it's really nice, satisfying "creamy" sound (at least that's what I've heard it called, though I still don't quite get why) that makes you want mechanical keyboard like this and this one does the thing real well while also looking pretty dang nice at the same time (I got the gray gradient version with side-printed keycaps. The battery life using the included USB 2.4G wireless dongle is exceptionally good and it also has RGB backlighting with 20 preprogrammed lighting modes, if you're into that thing, but I've got it set to a static color and it looks good enough for me. All of that at this price point makes this a really, really, really good option and one that I can absolutely recommend.

reviews.title: The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.
reviews.body: This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable. My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.

reviews.title: Buen sonido y calidad por el precio, pero software y patas mejorables
reviews.body: El teclado superó mis expectativas en lo esencial: sonido “thock” muy placentero, pulsaciones firmes y tres modos de conexión que funcionan sin problema. La construcción se siente sólida; el plástico es grueso y limpio al tacto, de mejor calidad que en otros modelos de su rango. Puntos a favor: Excelente sensación y respuesta lineal. Sonido grave-cremoso desde fábrica, sin necesidad de mods. Muy buen valor por el precio: se acerca a prestaciones “custom” de gamas más altas. Puntos a mejorar: El software de administración fue inútil en dos PC. La página es confusa, y aunque el teclado fue reconocido, no ofrecía opciones reales de configuración. La parte trasera utiliza un plástico más sencillo, y las gomas antideslizantes están pegadas con cinta doble faz que comenzó a despegarse desde el primer día. Me preocupa que se pierdan o necesiten ser reemplazadas pronto. No incluye numpad: ideal para gaming y escritura, pero puede ser limitante para quienes usan mucho la entrada numérica. Conclusión: Una excelente puerta de entrada al mundo “custom” por su sonido, tacto y conectividad, siempre que no dependas del software ni necesites un teclado completo. Nota aparte (no influye en la calificación del producto): el rastreo tardó cuatro días en actualizarse; el paquete llegó sin daños, pero el proceso logístico, la comunicación y el profesionalismo por parte del vendedor pueden mejorar.
reviews.body_en: The keyboard exceeded my expectations in the essentials: very pleasant “thock” sound, firm keystrokes and three connection modes that work without problem. The construction feels solid; The plastic is thick and clean to the touch, better quality than other models in its range. Pros: Excellent feel and linear response. Bass-creamy sound from the factory, without the need for mods. Very good value for the price: it is close to “custom” features of higher ranges. Points for improvement: The management software was useless on two PCs. The page is confusing, and although the keyboard was recognized, it offered no real configuration options. The back uses a simpler plastic, and the non-slip rubbers are glued with double-sided tape that began to peel off from the first day. I'm worried they will get lost or need to be replaced soon. Does not include numpad: ideal for gaming and writing, but can be limiting for those who use numerical input a lot. Conclusion: An excellent gateway to the “custom” world for its sound, touch and connectivity, as long as you do not depend on the software or need a full keyboard. Side note (does not influence product rating): tracking took four days to update; The package arrived without damage, but the logistics process, communication and professionalism on the part of the seller can improve.

reviews.title: Absolutely Impressed!
reviews.body: I upgraded my home gaming setup with this keyboard after considerable research, and it’s been a joy to use for both gaming and typing. Strengths: Premium typing experience: The pre-lubed cream linear switches and gasket mount deliver a “thocky” feel and satisfyingly smooth keystrokes. Typing and gaming are both quiet and comfortable, with five layers of foam dampening any hollow sounds. Customization: The included software lets me remap keys, create macros, and adjust more than 20 dynamic RGB lighting modes quickly. I loved being able to easily tweak the look and functionality. Build quality: PBT double-shot keycaps with an MDA profile feel sturdy and resist wear; they’re grippy and comfortable for long sessions. The detachable aluminum volume knob is a treat for instant control. Layout: The 98-key layout keeps the numpad and arrow keys but eliminates wasted space—a space-saving solution perfect for both gaming and work. Universal compatibility: Works perfectly with Windows and Mac out of the box, and includes both a 2-in-1 keycap/switch puller and extra switches for future customization. Bottom Line: This is an exceptional value for anyone who wants a customizable, quiet, and responsive keyboard for gaming, work, and creative projects. The smooth switches, full-featured software, and premium build make it a standout in its price range. Highly recommended for enthusiasts and everyday users alike.

reviews.title: Where sound, price, and comfort meet.
reviews.body: Absolutely worth the money, and even got it on sale! As I was looking for a replacement for my Logitech G512 that had finally started to show its age, after nearly 5 years of daily wear and tear from both games and general typing, I stumbled upon this board after seeing the shop it was inside of. I've been using it now for close to a week, and it has sealed the deal for my desire to build a keyboard once I have the means to do such. Each keycap having a small variance in its elevation by just a few millimeters may not sound like much, but it allows for a much smoother flow in typing and touch feel as you move through the keys. Additionally the sound the keyboard makes with the lubed switches below each key, effectively a quiet thunk-click is just beautiful. Its also much quieter than the G512 was, and is less noticed by people when I am speaking with them over the phone for work. So major win there! Solid 5/5 stars, if you need a keyboard for a good price and solid function - fully recommend.

reviews.title: Légère fatigue mais très qualitatif
reviews.body: "+" - Injection qualitative des plastiques de touches, - Apparence flatteuse et châssis robuste, - Branding peu agressif, - Super réactif, - La définition du rétroéclairage RGB est excellente et les scénario LeD sont bons, - Format 98% vraiment cool. - Peu de vibration parasite, - Excellent rapport qualité/prix, - Jeu de remplacement de quelques switch et touche de remplacement de la molette si besoin. "-" - Certaines touches (Shift, Caps Lock, Tab) gigotent un peu, - Molette de son est lisse et difficile à tourner. Pourtant, elle est pourvu d'un mécanisme de haute qualité. - Le clavier est haut, sans repose poignet une fatigue est inévitable. - Toute tentative de nettoyage est vaine : démonter le clavier par strate est difficile. "i" - La distance d'activation est très courte, ma main au repos au dessus du clavier peut suffire à déclencher des commandes. C'est un moyen efficace de rendre le clavier réactif mais diminue le confort d'usage selon moi. - Le son "creamy" n'est pas de tous les goûts, mais c'est un bon compromis entre feeling mécanique et discrétion. Il est plus bruyant que des cherry brown ou les touches "brown" des claviers mécaniques logitech. J'aime beaucoup l'esthétique et la sonorité de ce clavier, je le recommande aux acheteurs éclairés ! :) Ma note était de 4/5, mais la marque m'a spontanément contacté pour mieux comprendre mon retour. Je pense qu'ils ont un service client absolument exemplaire.
