reviews.title: MAJOR DESIGN FLAW DO NOT BUY
reviews.body: DO NOT BUY THIS!!! Purchased and came very quickly like next day but the UBar clasp design is so poor it broke when I tried to switch wrists after about a day wearing the decice, when I put it back on the UBar that secured the device was bent so that it wouldn't secure properly to my wrist. The entire wearable is held onto your wrist with a UBar attachment that is secured on either side by 2 millimeter (no exaggerating) size holes. These will inevitably fail and after wearing for a total of about 29 hours and simply attempting to switch once it's a major design flaw. It was difficult to figure out how to secure to the wrist and charge from the beginning and while relatively comfortable to wear, wasn't giving the readings I would want without an upgrade. The customer support is essentially an AI that responds via email and then eventually redirects you back to Amazon. Also this is membership based that auto renews annually and is several hundred dollars. I was willing to give a try and see if it was worth the renewal since the 1st year was included with the device and I felt like I could simply change to another wearable if I didn't feel it was worth it. I finally got a real person to respond who redirected me back to Amazon for refund because they couldn't provide any alternative to the band flaw. Super disappointing I was excited to try this and bought for myself for my birthday and will have to do more research on what actually works for wearables because this is NOT a good product

It was difficult to figure out how to secure to the wrist and charge from the beginning and while relatively comfortable to wear, wasn't giving the readings I would want without an upgrade. The customer support is essentially an AI that responds via email and then eventually redirects you back to Amazon. Also this is membership based that auto renews annually and is several hundred dollars. I was willing to give a try and see if it was worth the renewal since the 1st year was included with the device and I felt like I could simply change to another wearable if I didn't feel it was worth it. I finally got a real person to respond who redirected me back to Amazon for refund because they couldn't provide any alternative to the band flaw. Super disappointing I was excited to try this and bought for myself for my birthday and will have to do more research on what actually works for wearables because this is NOT a good product

Reviso mi Recovery y HRV cada mañana, y eso me ha ayudado a tomar decisiones más informadas sobre cuándo exigirme y cuándo bajar el ritmo. Lo que más valoro es cómo se volvió clave para mejorar hábitos generales: sueño, energía en las mañanas y alimentación. El Journal te deja agregar tus propios factores personalizados, así que puedes cruzar tus datos con lo que realmente te importa a ti, no solo con lo genérico. Punto en contra: algunas funciones como Advanced Labs (exámenes presenciales) son exclusivas de EE.UU., así que si vives fuera no podrás usarlas del todo — aunque sí puedes subir tus propios resultados de laboratorio sin problema. reviews.body_en: I purchased the WHOOP Peak looking to better understand my stress and energy level on a daily basis, and it has exceeded my expectations. I review my Recovery and HRV every morning, and that has helped me make more informed decisions about when to push myself and when to slow down. What I value most is how it became key to improving general habits: sleep, energy in the morning and diet. The Journal lets you add your own custom factors, so you can cross-reference your data with what really matters to you, not just the generic. The initial setup takes a little time (multi-day calibration, setting goals, notifications), but it's worth it once it's set up properly. Cons: Some features like Advanced Labs (in-person exams) are exclusive to the US, so if you live abroad you won't be able to use them at all — although you can upload your own lab results without a problem. Overall, highly recommended if you are looking for real data to make better decisions about your health and well-being on a day-to-day basis.

reviews.title: Whoop has some good stats, and some fake hype too
reviews.body: WHOOP will be at you day and night; the device is very frisky when it comes to telling you your basic health stats and behaviors. However, I would like to add a few caveats: 1) The AI or algorithm that they use SOUNDS like it's personalized to you, but the conclusions and statements the device makes are based on collected, aggregated, and thoroughly-predigested data. That's not to say its inaccurate, but it's not "personal" in a real sense--the sense that a series of physiological and blood tests would deliver. that would be specific to you. You are more likely to get recos based on standardized data. 2) The app is really busy. There are so many charts and data points and subcategories that it becomes difficult (for me, anyway) to find precisely what I'm looking for. I have to ASK (query) to get to see my running stats, for instance; I can't seem to find them otherwise. 3) The loads of data and so-called personal recos are designed to keep you interested and committed, andf that's basically a good thing, but it's also to hook you into paying an annual fee FOREVER. Compared to a high-end sports watch (Garmin, Suunto, or even Apple) you will be paying ad infinitum for something others offer for free. That said, I've only had my WHOOP for about a month, so I'm expecting a fresh batch of data when I hit the 30-day point, and perhaps I'll find more of it useful when I get there. Right now it's a pleased enough with the info provided, though I do wish it "agreed". more with my watch. Not quite sure whose stats to believe! ***UPDATE*** A few days short of two full months. I DO like their AI; when I correct it ("No that wasn't a run I was digging in the garden / walking the dog") it accepts and adjust response accordingly. Nice. Though I still find the data provided kind of scattered around the site, with no simple menu to help locate something. And WHOOP is OBSESSED with "Strain;" even after reading their explanations I still can't compute their approach. Accuracy still a big ? mark, as it only occasionally matches what my Garmin watch reports. Who to believe??

reviews.title: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
reviews.body: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

reviews.title: The best fitness tracker I've used
reviews.body: I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone. Compared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. I had gotten used to Apple's smooth interface, built in microphone and speaker for voice commands, and often useful apps that can be used without needing to get my phone out. That being said, after a few days I can confidently say that I don't need them. I would argue that Garmin knows what this is and what it is not - it's a fitness device first and foremost, and everything else comes second. And on that basis they nailed it - the fitness tracking has been excellent and noticeably better than the Apple Watch especially in sleep tracking. I also much prefer their approach to goals, which tracks exercise over the course of a week rather than focusing specifically on individual days. Whenever I was sick or had a down day I would feel guilty if I didn't close all of my rings on my Apple Watch, but I don't feel that same pressure with the Garmin. I do miss being able to use voice commands with my watch, but I could have gotten a more expensive Garmin if I really wanted that, and I don't think it's worth it for me. The second thing I noticed: not having to charge your watch every day is a game changer. This was easily my biggest frustration with the Apple Watch since it's marketed as a device you wear 24x7 and yet needs to be charged every day. And considering how long it took to charge my Series 5, this was a major annoyance. I couldn't charge it overnight, because I wanted sleep tracking. I couldn't charge it in the morning, because I like to start off my day with exercise and it doesn't charge fast enough to do it after a workout and before work. And if I charged it in the evening, I would often forget to put it on before bed and miss out on the sleep tracking. The Garmin is a breath of fresh air by comparison - I charge it about once a week, and with my relatively light usage it can probably go close to two. I took a multi day trip recently and I didn't once have to worry about charging my watch, which was a pleasant change. reviews.title: I love this thing. Not the least expensive, but probably the best bang for the buck.
reviews.body: I’m someone who really really did not want a watch of any sort, especially not an Apple Watch or anything else that is bloated with unnecessary hardware that needs to be charged every single day. Charging a phone every day is enough of a pain without needing to add any other junk, so no thanks to the useless gimmick-loaded “smart” watches. But I really needed to do fitness tracking because without some sort of gadget I just have zero idea how lazy or not lazy I’ve been lately and whether or not I need to get at least some minimal exercise. And my #1 must have feature is week-long battery charge life. This watch is good enough, even though the battery life might be more like 5 days in some cases if you’re using it for activities a lot where the gps is turned on. But for those not running with the gps every day or constantly tinkering with it a full battery charge seems to last a week. That is, charge it for an hour on Sunday and no need to charge it again until the same time next Sunday. You could get the battery to last longer if you’re willing to shut off absolutely everything that might use more power. I started out with a Garmin vivosmart 5 because I didn’t think I needed anything beyond that, but I have sleep problems and decided I needed better sleep tracking. So I ended up with this one even though I don’t really care about random silly “apps” on a watch. Overall this watch has been excellent. It has a very good UI and the fitness tracking features a quite good. The sleep tracking is decent, but still has its issues that hopefully Garmin will fix with software updates. In particular the “nap tracking” doesn’t seem fully baked yet, and things like laying back in a recliner reading a book or watching TV can get falsely detected as a “nap”. Then there’s no way to delete a false nap on the watch or in the Garmin Connect app. There are still a few minor bugs that some people will run into but they seem to be things that can be fixed with firmware updates and I haven’t run into anything completely feature-breaking. If you feel like messing with it you can also install some “apps” like custom watch face designs or sunset/sunrise times, more detailed weather and such. But even without installing anything the watch does everything needed for health and fitness stuff. Almost all of the apps that come with the device can be uninstalled, so if you don’t need “women’s health tracking” for example then you can just remove that to free up space. Their mobile app is pretty well designed and only awkward in some parts of the configuration. The watch reliably synchronizes as long as you leave the phone app running in the background and I’ve never had any Bluetooth connection failures, lag, or lost pairings. Things that the watch is not good for are things that you’d typically use a phone for like communication, turn by turn navigation, maps, games, and such. But I don’t want a watch to do any of that stuff and I’d rather have it save its battery charge so I don’t have to charge it constantly. So overall, this is “the” watch you want if you want as little nonsense as possible and don’t want to worry about battery charge all the time but still need full health and fitness tracking stuff beyond what the $75-150 models offer. And there are also no subscriptions required.

reviews.title: Nice watch, has some flaws
reviews.body: Just received the watch today, it’s nice but I have some concerns. For starters the band is completely silicone and plastic- the buckle piece is plastic, even the case around the watch is plastic. For $200 you’d think it would at-least be metal. The setup was easy- but came with very little instruction for other things like changing watch faces, setting up apps, etc. Learning how to use the watch and what the buttons all do is pure guessing. The charger is USB-C- if it wasn’t for my laptop I would have no way to charge the watch. Should have come with a compatible block. UPDATE: After using the watch for several days I do like it. While the overall construction (plastic casing) could be better, the overall operation works great. Steps and heart rate seem accurate. The display looks nice, customizable, and the watch is comfortable. The stress levels don’t seem to be accurate. I get “high stress” alerts when all I’ve been doing is laying in bed all day. Just add a titanium casing to the surrounding of the watch and provide more thorough instructions on overall use + updates for accuracy on certain apps and it would be perfect!

reviews.title: Super produkt w super cenie
reviews.body: Opinie piszę po około 3 tygodniach od zakupu, więc zdążyłem już dobrze zapoznać się z zegarkiem. Produkt jest rewelacyjny i spełnia moje wszystkie oczekiwania, a nawet więcej. Świetne wykonanie, zegarek jest lekki, a pasek bardzo miękki, dzięki czemu praktycznie nie czuć go na ręce. Rewelacyjny wyświetlacz, na którym wszystko idealnie widać nawet w pełnym słońcu. Przy ciągłym pomiarze tętna, włączonych powiadomieniach ze smartfona, rejestracji kilku aktywności i dokonywaniu nim kilku płatności dziennie, zegarek wytrzymuje na jednym ładowaniu 7 pełnych dób i zazwyczaj jeszcze jest około 20-30% baterii. Jak dla mnie wynik rewelacyjny. Świetne modyfikowalne tarcze, które możemy za darmo pobrać ze sklepu Connect IQ. Zegarek sprawdzi się w przypadku osoby która chce mieć nieduży i lekki zegarek z płatnościami zbliżeniowymi, z ciągłym monitorowaniem stanu zdrowia i rejestrowaniem aktywności. Oczywiście dla wyczynowych sportowców Garmin ma lepsze urządzenia, jednak dla amatorów jest to bardzo dobry wybór.
reviews.body_en: I'm writing this review about 3 weeks after purchase, so I've already gotten to know the watch well. The product is amazing and meets all my expectations and even more. Great workmanship, the watch is light and the strap is very soft, so you practically don't feel it on your hand. A fantastic display that shows everything perfectly, even in direct sunlight. With continuous heart rate measurement, smartphone notifications turned on, recording several activities and making several payments a day, the watch lasts 7 full days on a single charge and usually has about 20-30% of the battery left. For me, it's a fantastic result. Great customizable dials that can be downloaded for free from the Connect IQ store. The watch will be perfect for a person who wants a small and light watch with contactless payments, continuous health monitoring and activity recording. Of course, for professional athletes, Garmin has better devices, but for amateurs it is a very good choice.

reviews.title: This watch is an Amazing buy!
reviews.body: I am beyond happy with my new watch! You get the luxury without the cost. It has so many amazing features using the "Glory Fit App," which is very user-friendly. I'm able to take calls, make calls, and text from the watch. Listen to music by connecting via bluetooth. It allows you to customize countless features like temperature units, weight, and metrics. You can choose between multiple digital face diplays in your watch settings. You can also set the length of time display stays lit before it disappears. It features: training plans, goal setting and allows you to connect with friends. The watch straps are interchangeable so that you can attach different colors or styles. You can monitor your heart rate, blood oxygen levels, sleep, step count, weight, and more! It has a voice assistant and alarm clock as well. You can also sync most of your Apps on your paired device (I did my my phone), so that you can receive notifications and even use the same functions on your watch simultaneously. For example, I paired my youtube account so that whenever I receive a notification in the Youtube App of a new video, it shows that notification on my phone as well. I can even listen to YouTube using the play, pause, and stop buttons from my phone. I also synced our security camera device so that I can receive those notifications as well while away from home. I am able to select any number of applications I want to individually sync or not. This is great so that I can be selective and not have my watch going off every second of the day. It helps me to stay motivated as far as my fitness goes because I'm able to set goals - it sends you an achievement reward notification, which sounds once a goal has been reached. It has so many features that I haven't even begun to tap into. There is a slight learning curve, as with sny smart device, but it's very user-friendly after you patiently program and customize each feature to fit your needs and get the hang of it. I love the color selection options. I chose the black and light pink/rose gold color (for him & her), I also ordered (from another seller) face covers for protection. The covers were very easy to slip on (see in photos & video). It comes with a convenient USB, and the watch is packed in its own individual box. Note: THE BOX HAS (2) WATCHES PICTURED BUT ONLY COMES WITH ONE WATCH. I just want to mention it because my pictures & video show (2) watches, but it's only because I bought them separately in those exact colors pictured on their box. I took multiple pictures to help display some of the features and to demonstrate the ease at attaching a face cover (sold separately via another seller). This is an amazing buy, and it makes the perfect gift. Be sure to check out the video ~ hope this helps!

reviews.body: Good watch for the money. You do have to download an app. It is not overly complicated to navigate. I struggled some getting it to connect with the app but I’m not tech savvy. Battery life was good. It would last for two days. It charged quickly. It didn’t track my sleep well, which was one of the reasons I bought it, but it does have to be in constant contact with your wrist and I don’t like my watches that tight. It did do a decent job on vitals and had charts to show weekly levels. The negatives were you had to change your settings to a certain exercise to get a more accurate result. Especially on steps. Since I’m up doing a lot of walking, lifting, bending and sometimes crawling when cleaning the house I found you get a better representation of steps if you changed the setting to indoor walking. 😁 The drawback on any of the exercise settings I would forget to switch back to normal. Which is a negative on me. The next one is a very personal preference. I really wanted to be able to change the bands. I like sparkles and my daughter likes blues. I couldn’t find any that would fit the watch. We ended up making a few cuts here and adjustments there to get them to fit but I don’t think most people would want to do that. My husband bought me an apple watch for my birthday and my daughter didn’t like having anything on her wrist so I gave them to the grandsons 10 & 9. They are obviously not gentle with them but they are still going. I would place that into the sturdy column.

reviews.title: Works ok for the price
reviews.body: Im at little on the fence about this watch. For the price it is great and when I first got it I was in love. Now that I've had it for a few weeks and have been able to use it I'm not sure how I feel about it all the time. It adds steps randomly, like even when I'm sleeping (I don't move in my sleep) I wake up and it'll say i took like 400 steps. The heart rate monitor and blood oxygen monitor seem to work just as intended. I got this watch to help track my sleep and this is where I keep having issues. Sometimes it won't register that I slept, or doesn't record it properly (and i have even started wearing the watch backwards so that the sensor is on my wrist so it can get a better read). Today it said I slept for 3 hours while I was out running errands. I also accidentallyet the watch die the other day (it lasted a few days without charging), but it seems like since then I've been having a lot of issues with the Bluetooth, the call features, tracking and notifications. The app is also pretty basic. Sometimes it's hard to find the settings your looking for and they don't give you many options to begin with. When I go in to look at my sleep it shows a graph which is nice, but if you want to try to see the times you have to press on this tiny sliver and most of the time it highlights the wrong thing and doesn't really break anything down for you. I know I got this watch at a great price, but I will be honest I have been looking for a different one similarly priced, considering sending this back. I guess if my opinion changes I'll update my review.

reviews.title: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
reviews.body: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!) The one potential “glitch” I thought I had finally discovered with my Vivoactive 5, but which turned out not to be an issue, occurred when I was flying internationally. I was returning from Europe to the US on an evening flight where the time in the US was six hours earlier. So both my FITBIT and my Garmin thought that when enough flight time had elapsed, they went past midnight and started their metrics over as a new day - meaning steps completely zeroed out and started over. But not long after I landed at 7 pm US time, my Fitbit picked back up with the previous day’s step tally, but my Garmin still showed the reduced step count tallied as a “new day”. I was disappointed with this until I checked the metrics in the Garmin app and noted that the “two day tallies” indicated on the watch itself were actually (appropriately!) counted and displayed as a single day step counts in the app. So yes, I am sold on the Garmin. But I do still have to wonder why if FITBIT - even early versions - could have successfully addressed ALL of the issues I have found with so many competitor brands, why can’t all the others? Maybe I shouldn’t have been so wary of Google taking over Fitbit when I started investigating other Smart watches, but I learned a lot about different brands and their bogus IP 68 and 5 ATM ratings! So to reiterate, Garmin is exactly what it says it is, and Fitbit is as well. Do your comparisons!

reviews.title: The best fitness tracker I've used
reviews.body: I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone. Compared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. I had gotten used to Apple's smooth interface, built in microphone and speaker for voice commands, and often useful apps that can be used without needing to get my phone out. That being said, after a few days I can confidently say that I don't need them. I would argue that Garmin knows what this is and what it is not - it's a fitness device first and foremost, and everything else comes second. And on that basis they nailed it - the fitness tracking has been excellent and noticeably better than the Apple Watch especially in sleep tracking. I also much prefer their approach to goals, which tracks exercise over the course of a week rather than focusing specifically on individual days. Whenever I was sick or had a down day I would feel guilty if I didn't close all of my rings on my Apple Watch, but I don't feel that same pressure with the Garmin. I do miss being able to use voice commands with my watch, but I could have gotten a more expensive Garmin if I really wanted that, and I don't think it's worth it for me. The second thing I noticed: not having to charge your watch every day is a game changer. This was easily my biggest frustration with the Apple Watch since it's marketed as a device you wear 24x7 and yet needs to be charged every day. And considering how long it took to charge my Series 5, this was a major annoyance. I couldn't charge it overnight, because I wanted sleep tracking. I couldn't charge it in the morning, because I like to start off my day with exercise and it doesn't charge fast enough to do it after a workout and before work. And if I charged it in the evening, I would often forget to put it on before bed and miss out on the sleep tracking. The Garmin is a breath of fresh air by comparison - I charge it about once a week, and with my relatively light usage it can probably go close to two. I took a multi day trip recently and I didn't once have to worry about charging my watch, which was a pleasant change. Overall I think this watch is a great fit for a more casual user who isn't running marathons but wants to track fitness and sleep and get some extras like smartphone notifications and see the weather at a glance. If you want something with more smart features and better build quality (i.e. more metal and less plastic), then the Venu might be a better fit. Or they have the Forerunner if you do run marathons. Or a bunch of other models for more specific use cases. But I would highly recommend giving this watch a try if you're looking for the same things that I am.

Garmin Vivoactive 5 has not caused any skin irritation! I am pleased with the metrics it gives. The app takes some getting used to, but it isn't complicated to navigate...just different from fitbit. So far the battery charge lasts for at least 7 days. It charges quickly. I like the screen size, metrics and words are easy to read. The screen reacts well to touch even with a screen protector on. It is easy to access the watches features. I like the wake up summary. It gives me prompts to move and stretch. It gives sleep advice and measures body battery throughout the day. The watch is comfortable to wear and looks great with everything. I swap between a nylon band and leather band. I would highly recommend.

reviews.title: I love this thing. Not the least expensive, but probably the best bang for the buck.
reviews.body: I’m someone who really really did not want a watch of any sort, especially not an Apple Watch or anything else that is bloated with unnecessary hardware that needs to be charged every single day. Charging a phone every day is enough of a pain without needing to add any other junk, so no thanks to the useless gimmick-loaded “smart” watches. But I really needed to do fitness tracking because without some sort of gadget I just have zero idea how lazy or not lazy I’ve been lately and whether or not I need to get at least some minimal exercise. And my #1 must have feature is week-long battery charge life. This watch is good enough, even though the battery life might be more like 5 days in some cases if you’re using it for activities a lot where the gps is turned on. But for those not running with the gps every day or constantly tinkering with it a full battery charge seems to last a week. That is, charge it for an hour on Sunday and no need to charge it again until the same time next Sunday. You could get the battery to last longer if you’re willing to shut off absolutely everything that might use more power. I started out with a Garmin vivosmart 5 because I didn’t think I needed anything beyond that, but I have sleep problems and decided I needed better sleep tracking. So I ended up with this one even though I don’t really care about random silly “apps” on a watch. Overall this watch has been excellent. It has a very good UI and the fitness tracking features a quite good. The sleep tracking is decent, but still has its issues that hopefully Garmin will fix with software updates. In particular the “nap tracking” doesn’t seem fully baked yet, and things like laying back in a recliner reading a book or watching TV can get falsely detected as a “nap”. Then there’s no way to delete a false nap on the watch or in the Garmin Connect app. There are still a few minor bugs that some people will run into but they seem to be things that can be fixed with firmware updates and I haven’t run into anything completely feature-breaking. If you feel like messing with it you can also install some “apps” like custom watch face designs or sunset/sunrise times, more detailed weather and such. But even without installing anything the watch does everything needed for health and fitness stuff. Almost all of the apps that come with the device can be uninstalled, so if you don’t need “women’s health tracking” for example then you can just remove that to free up space. Their mobile app is pretty well designed and only awkward in some parts of the configuration. The watch reliably synchronizes as long as you leave the phone app running in the background and I’ve never had any Bluetooth connection failures, lag, or lost pairings. Things that the watch is not good for are things that you’d typically use a phone for like communication, turn by turn navigation, maps, games, and such. But I don’t want a watch to do any of that stuff and I’d rather have it save its battery charge so I don’t have to charge it constantly. So overall, this is “the” watch you want if you want as little nonsense as possible and don’t want to worry about battery charge all the time but still need full health and fitness tracking stuff beyond what the $75-150 models offer. And there are also no subscriptions required.

reviews.title: Garmin vívoactive® 5 Health & Fitness GPS Smartwatch
reviews.body: The Garmin vívoactive® 5 has been a great watch to help monitor my daily activities, sleep, heart rate, and so much more. I wasn't so interested in the idea of connecting to my phone but rather the health benefits. It was a great purchase. The screen size is not too large for my small 5 inch wrist, but also large enough that I can clearly see the screen. The watch was easy to set up, make adjustments to as I learn about the various functions, and was easy to connect to my phone and work benefits. I like that I am able to select which features I would like to use. Garmin is very compatible with many fitness programs. I don't have good success wearing a silicone strap so I did purchase other bands which were simple to remove and connect to the watch head. I believe Garmin was a very good choice for a first health and fitness watch for me.

reviews.title: Nice watch, has some flaws
reviews.body: Just received the watch today, it’s nice but I have some concerns. For starters the band is completely silicone and plastic- the buckle piece is plastic, even the case around the watch is plastic. For $200 you’d think it would at-least be metal. The setup was easy- but came with very little instruction for other things like changing watch faces, setting up apps, etc. Learning how to use the watch and what the buttons all do is pure guessing. The charger is USB-C- if it wasn’t for my laptop I would have no way to charge the watch. Should have come with a compatible block. UPDATE: After using the watch for several days I do like it. While the overall construction (plastic casing) could be better, the overall operation works great. Steps and heart rate seem accurate. The display looks nice, customizable, and the watch is comfortable. The stress levels don’t seem to be accurate. I get “high stress” alerts when all I’ve been doing is laying in bed all day. Just add a titanium casing to the surrounding of the watch and provide more thorough instructions on overall use + updates for accuracy on certain apps and it would be perfect!

reviews.title: Super produkt w super cenie
reviews.body: Opinie piszę po około 3 tygodniach od zakupu, więc zdążyłem już dobrze zapoznać się z zegarkiem. Produkt jest rewelacyjny i spełnia moje wszystkie oczekiwania, a nawet więcej. Świetne wykonanie, zegarek jest lekki, a pasek bardzo miękki, dzięki czemu praktycznie nie czuć go na ręce. Rewelacyjny wyświetlacz, na którym wszystko idealnie widać nawet w pełnym słońcu. Przy ciągłym pomiarze tętna, włączonych powiadomieniach ze smartfona, rejestracji kilku aktywności i dokonywaniu nim kilku płatności dziennie, zegarek wytrzymuje na jednym ładowaniu 7 pełnych dób i zazwyczaj jeszcze jest około 20-30% baterii. Jak dla mnie wynik rewelacyjny. Świetne modyfikowalne tarcze, które możemy za darmo pobrać ze sklepu Connect IQ. Zegarek sprawdzi się w przypadku osoby która chce mieć nieduży i lekki zegarek z płatnościami zbliżeniowymi, z ciągłym monitorowaniem stanu zdrowia i rejestrowaniem aktywności. Oczywiście dla wyczynowych sportowców Garmin ma lepsze urządzenia, jednak dla amatorów jest to bardzo dobry wybór.
reviews.body_en: I'm writing this review about 3 weeks after purchase, so I've already gotten to know the watch well. The product is amazing and meets all my expectations and even more. Great workmanship, the watch is light and the strap is very soft, so you practically don't feel it on your hand. A fantastic display that shows everything perfectly, even in direct sunlight. With continuous heart rate measurement, smartphone notifications turned on, recording several activities and making several payments a day, the watch lasts 7 full days on a single charge and usually has about 20-30% of the battery left. For me, it's a fantastic result. Great customizable dials that can be downloaded for free from the Connect IQ store. The watch will be perfect for a person who wants a small and light watch with contactless payments, continuous health monitoring and activity recording. Of course, for professional athletes, Garmin has better devices, but for amateurs it is a very good choice.

title: Smart Watch with Alexa Built-in, 1.83" HD Bluetooth Calling Fitness Tracker
bullet_points: Bluetooth 5.3 Call and Message Notification: Cillso smart watch features an advanced single-chip processor and sensitive microphone, enabling direct call making and answering. When you enable the "VeryFit" App to receive messages, notifications will be displayed on the smartwatch. Get all your messages and notifications (Facebook, Twitter, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, Linkedin,Skype etc.) sent straight to your smartwatch with intuitive customizable vibrations

Built-in Alexa Voice Control: This smartwatch integrates Amazon Alexa's intelligent voice assistant, delivering a comprehensive hands-free experience directly from your wrist. Simply speak commands to instantly access news, weather, and calendar updates, set reminders, control smart home devices, and manage music playback. This full suite of voice-activated functionalities streamlines daily routines, enhances multitasking efficiency, and keeps your hands free for the moments that matter most.

1.83" HD Display and Personalized Customization: IDW26 smart watches for men women feature a 1.83-inch HDdisplay paired with 3D tempered glass, boasting a resolution of up to 320×385 for excellent image quality and high touch sensitivity. The 4-level adjustable brightness ensures clear visibility even under bright sunlight. Through the "VeryFit" app, users gain access to over 130 stylish watch faces and the ability to create custom designs, allowing for personalized expression

120+ Sport Modes and IP68 Waterproof: Fitness tracker supports 120+ professional sport modes, covering diverse indoor/outdoor activities like running, cycling, and soccer to suit all fitness levels. Equipped with high-precision sensors, fitness watch accurately tracks steps, distance, calories burned, and workout duration to help analyze performance and optimize training plans. With an IP68 rating, it's resistant to sweat, rain, and handwashing (Not for swimming or hot showers)

All-Day Health Monitoring: Android smart watch is equipped with a high-precision optical sensor that supports 24h real-time heart rate monitoring, helping you stay informed about your physical condition. It also intelligently analyzes sleep quality, accurately identifying deep sleep, light sleep, and awake phases to help improve your sleep habits. Paired with its dedicated app, you can view long-term health trends and receive personalized insights to gradually develop a healthier lifestyle

Long Battery Life and Multi-Functionality: Sports smartwatch is powered by a 300mAh battery with a low power design, providing up to 5-7 days of usage and up to 30 days of standby time, with just 1.5 hours of charging. It is widely compatible with smartphones using Bluetooth 4.0, Android 5.0, iOS 9.0, or later versions. Additionally, activity tracker offer various practical features, including an alarm, stopwatch, timer, phone locator, camera control, and more

reviews.title: Not Built for the Water
reviews.body: It’s honestly a decent smart watch/exercise/step tracker, and connectivity on land is pretty good (I can go a fair distance in open space away from my phone before the watch disconnects). Battery life is pretty good, and it does receive texts and allows you to control your music. I am writing this review as someone who works in aquatics-specifically spending a lot of time in the water. While the watch does have good water resistance, the connectivity under water is non existent and it also tends to react as though I’m manipulating the screen (I am aware that all these complaints are normal with water). All in all, it’s not what I was looking for. One other MINOR complaint. The app that comes with the watch gives you the ability to personalize your home screen (which is genuinely fun/a great feature). A lot of them come with a “current outside temp” reading, but I can never get this part of the home screen to connect properly regardless of the home screen in question. A petty complaint but a complaint nonetheless XD All in all, it’s probably great for on land day to day/exercise, but definitely not for water related activities.

reviews.title: Ideal para uso diario
reviews.body: Este reloj inteligente con Alexa y pantalla de 1,83″ me ha sorprendido para bien, especialmente por lo completo que es para su precio. Ya desde el tamaño de la pantalla se nota que puedes leer notificaciones y ver información sin forzar la vista, y con Alexa integrada se siente más “inteligente” que otros relojes básicos. Al abrir la caja encontramos: El propio reloj un cable magnetico para cargar y un folleto a modo de manual de instrucciones. Lo primero es ponerlo a cargar y luego escanear con el movil el codigo QR para obtener la aplicación Veryfit. Lo que más me ha gustado: La integración con llamadas y notificaciones funciona fluida y hace que no tengas que sacar siempre el móvil. Los modos deportivos (más de 110) son muy abundantes para el precio, y te permiten registrar desde caminatas hasta actividades más específicas que falta me hace... Las funciones de pulsómetro, podómetro y monitor de sueño están ahí y hacen un buen trabajo para uso diario (aunque no sean del nivel médico, te dan una buena idea general). El hecho de que sea IP68 resistente al agua es un plus para el día a día — te olvidas de quitártelo incluso en la ducha o cuando llueve. La esfera DIY es divertida: puedes personalizarla, lo cual da un toque más personal. La sensación general: Se siente sólido, bien integrado con Android/iOS, y tiene funciones que normalmente esperarías en relojes más caros. reviews.title: Large, multi-function, need to check HR and spO2 are not 100% accurate
reviews.body: This watch is a reasonable price, and tells time, date, weather, etc. The face is rather large - wider than my wrist - and the strap is long. Probably owing to the gender-neutral style of the watch. There are numerous choices for the watch face display, but most are truly awful. I wanted it for the oxygen and heart rate measurement. I compared with my pulse oximeter, and the watch overestimates oxygen saturation by 4-5%. Not unexpected, and easy to account for once known. Heart rate seems more accurate. Note that you will need a USB-c adapter to charge the watch, as it only has a (short) USB-a cable. I have no idea how it measures 'sleep' - it told me I sleep over 8.5 hours, when it was actually more like 6.5. Not bad looking if you don't mind the shiny black block appearance. You also have to download the app on your phone, which I'm not sure about - don't like the idea of sending my data to China.

reviews.title: Getting the basics right
reviews.body: I have used the forerunner 55 watch for over a year now and I have been very pleased. It’s got most of the features that you would want and nothing too flashy or useless. The big selling point for me was the 2 week battery life and I’m happy to say that it has held up pretty well. I use this to track my sleep, mountain biking, gym workouts, and any other random I activity I get into. I went down the rabbit hole of all the fancier watches they have and realized I don’t need them. Sure it would be nice to have a touch screen, but do I really need it? Having a touch screen instead of 2 week battery life is not something I would swap out. And I prefer the buttons over a touchscreen because it just works better for me anyway. I like the size of it cause it’s on the smaller side and the buttons are placed well and useful. Overall, this watch has been great and I probably will stick to the forerunner series when I need a new watch in a couple more years. If you are getting a watch for a specific activity, maybe look at one of the more niche watches but if you just need a good all around watch for a moderately active lifestyle, this might be just what you need.

reviews.title: 3 years and counting!
reviews.body: *** I've been using this watch for 3-years (& 1-month) now. It still works great and I still have zero regrets! I even got one of my sons to buy the same model. *** ------------------------------- Original 11-month review: Thanks to this watch, I was able to drop the 20+ pounds I put on during my post-covid depression. It got me moving again and whereas the original daunting number of 10k steps in a day made me nervous, I now walk around 23k steps daily without even thinking about it. The challenges on the app have helped me move from my former weight loss goals to my present toning ones and suffice it to say, all of this has helped tremendously with my mental health as well. As for the watch features, I was looking at all sorts of brands and all kinds of models and settled on this one and never looked back. I needed a time teller, a pedometer and a heart rate monitor, in no specific order. I received all of those and more with this wrist decor. Not only does the watch look nice and feel weightless on my skin when adjusted correctly, but it works so well at everything it was made to. The heart rate monitor is very accurate when compared with other heart rate monitoring devices. The watch is simple to clean although I was afraid of damaging something whilst attempting to clear out the 'gunk' around the plug-in site. I didn't purchase the watch for the sleep related feature but it is an interesting bonus. After roughly 9-10 months of continuous 24-hour use, I finally started noticing it act up during my treadmill workouts. My heart rate would drop to 0 and at one point I saw it jump to 248. Since I wasn't dead or dying during any of these times, I thought I'd start turning it off at night and I haven't noticed the issue since. It could have just been an error that required an update but like I said, I didn't buy for the sleep feature anyhow. The battery life is pretty good I'd say. When I told my husband one day that I should 'charge my watch tonight because it's been a couple weeks' he was really surprised. I keep track on my exercise calendar whenever I feel the need to plug in, which I do during the night so it doesn't interrupt my steps during the day. I normally charge once it hits somewhere in the 10-19 percentile. This takes (me specifically) about two weeks to accomplish, with roughly an hour and a half, minimum, of recorded activities at least five days a week and the watch otherwise just being turned on consistently. Of course, there are extra outings that warrant using the start button once in a while and yet I still find my charge schedule to remain the same. You can choose from a variety of watch faces that come standard but I definitely have enjoyed looking through the Garmin store at other options. The background I've used for quite some time now shows the moon in its current phase and as a lifetime star gazer, this is a face I was more than happy to throw money at. I spent just a few dollars and received something around 10 different looks, several animated such as plants or flowers that grow or open as you complete your steps for the day- amazing, if you like that sort of thing, turns out I do. Overall, I love my watch and I hope it lasts me a good, long time but if and when it finally dies from time cancer, I'll be sure to replace it with another Garmin!

This takes (me specifically) about two weeks to accomplish, with roughly an hour and a half, minimum, of recorded activities at least five days a week and the watch otherwise just being turned on consistently. Of course, there are extra outings that warrant using the start button once in a while and yet I still find my charge schedule to remain the same. You can choose from a variety of watch faces that come standard but I definitely have enjoyed looking through the Garmin store at other options. The background I've used for quite some time now shows the moon in its current phase and as a lifetime star gazer, this is a face I was more than happy to throw money at. I spent just a few dollars and received something around 10 different looks, several animated such as plants or flowers that grow or open as you complete your steps for the day- amazing, if you like that sort of thing, turns out I do. Overall, I love my watch and I hope it lasts me a good, long time but if and when it finally dies from time cancer, I'll be sure to replace it with another Garmin!

reviews.title: Fit for my purposes
reviews.body: Wanted a simple wrist device for heart rate monitoring at the gym and while walking, with or without a HRM strap but definitely without all of the current smart phone connectivity clutter. No, I don't care about texts, emails or other messaging when working out--I want to escape that noise. Struck out at REI. The days of simple HRM watches with straps seem to be over. But this device seems to fit the bill, albeit at a higher price point. I have tested the HR accuracy against my combination Polar HRM and Garmin high end cycling computers (1040/1030) and it tracks with remarkable accuracy --remarkable given its reliance on technology that does not include a chest strap. Variation to the Polar chest strap 1030 or 1040 combination did not exceed 3%, when it was not spot on. Quality seems good. As with any of these devices, operation becomes more "intuitive" with increased use. It may be that some of the cheaper knock-off smart watches available on Amazon perform well as well. IDK and am not going to speculate. All I know is that this one is fit for my purposes.

reviews.title: Excellent watch functionality but some tweaks recommended
reviews.body: I had a sports watch and polar chest strap monitor 25 years ago for Concept 2 rower training. Technology has improved enormously since then. I chose the Garmin Forerunner 55 because I wanted simplicity as well as multi-functionality. It fulfils both needs. Above all the Garmin sports watch is accurate. I am now 71 and have just started training prep for another C25K with my daughter - hence the need for an accurate heart rate monitor. The things I like about the watch and app follow plus some suggested tweaks. On the positive side customisable heart rate zones are useful, and it is easy to develop warm up, walk, run, repeat x8 workouts, which can then be modified in subsequent weeks. However, I had to use AI to pose a dozen or so technical questions about how to set up specific procedures and to analyse and interpret some of the performance data that the Garmin produces. The written Garmin instructions in multiple languages don’t touch the sides of what the app can do hence using Google Gemini to pose detailed questions. Another user tip - the Garmin app can be integrated with the Chronometer app which monitors food and exercise expenditure. This combination of apps is a really sophisticated tool to record data, if you are of a scientific disposition. For example, if your Adjusted Baseline Activity hits zero, it indicates that your Garmin has accounted for every metabolic "tick" above your resting BMR. The wider screen of an Apple Mac is much more accessible to see all the post exercise Garmin data. The IPAD version of the Garmin app is actually a scaled mobile app and it is difficult to escape from a page as the menus are obscured. A workaround is to reset your IPad display to ‘more space’, but I would recommend using a laptop and the Garmin website which have no technical issues.

reviews.title: Solid Watch! Worth it if you're debating!
reviews.body: This is a solid watch! I didn't want to spend money on a fitness watch that I was mostly paying for a brand name.. This does everything a fitbit does and most everything the lower end Garmins do. I really like how lightweight it is! I haven't had it long enough to test out the two week battery life but so far it was a quick charge and has been at 100% all day even after wearing it all night and having the sleep and heart rate on, steps seem accurate maybe off one or two steps but nothing is going to measure perfectly even fitbits and Garmins aren't 100% accurate. I like all of the features! However, the Zepp app has too much going on but it's not as difficult to navigate as I was expecting from the other reviews. It's a fitness watch first so those features are great... Call and text is just okay. I gave it 5 stars but I almost just did 4 because it's geared towards men; the design, watch faces, the app etc.. Are all very Male "coded" Which is fine if you don't care I just happen to like a more feminine aesthetic and I think they could do better to have more feminine options or even more neutral options would be great but that is just a nitpicky personal preference. Overall this is a good watch! I did a lot of research and I would say if you're debating it just get it! It is far less expensive to try this and not like it and get something else then it is to try a $300-$800 watch that you hate but you already spent $$ so you feel stuck. UPDATE EXACTLY 1 WEEK LATER: Still a really solid fitness watch but not everything it promises I turned off most of the notifications and app features that don't make sense for my goals and the battery lasts a week. To be fair though I have only taken it off to shower and wash dishes I have worn it day and night for the entire week and currently it's at 10% A week is pretty solid still though. I also bought a screen protector that was pink and a new purple band and it did change the aesthetic for me.

reviews.title: All the features; a fraction of the cost
reviews.body: I am so pleasantly surprised by the quality and feature availability of this affordable off-brand watch. After switching to Android, i needed a watch to replace my Apple watch. I didnt want to get reinvested in an over-priced flagship like Samsung or Garmin, so I looked for something budget but feature rich. This was a SOLID choice and i am so happy with it. Pros: Price. Its hard to beat the low price of this watch. Battery. My apple had to be charged every day or so and it drained rapidly. The Amazfit lasts me at least 5 days with normal use. But here is the best part - its still doing pretty much everything my apple watch was! Im honestly shocked how long the Amazfit battery lasts while still giving me all the features i need. Notifications. The Amazfit integrates with the phone via the Zepp app. You will still recieve all your necessary phone, messages, email, socials, etc notifications to your watch. Integration with Android. This watch works great with Android via the Zepp app. Screen size. Another big surprise was how large the screen size is. I cant believe i paid a third the price of Apple but i got 3-4x battery life and huge screen. Cons: Cosmetic weakness. The metal edge around the screen is already getting some very small dings. I dont really care and it is purely superficial. Theres really not a lot bad i can say about this watch. Im so pleased with the value and capability at the very low price point relative to apple. Other features: Tracks sleep, heart rate, sends movement alerts, has routines, offers a daily biocharge tracker (think battery but its your body's remaining daily charge), tracks steps, movement, calories.

reviews.title: Decently solid value fitness band
reviews.body: Okay, I bought this for Christmas, so I've been using it for about 6 months now. I do believe that this is a good value for your money. It does most of the things I want it to do. It looks good, and I found compatible bands (the original band cooked my skin, and I had to remove it and put on a fabric band). I like its functionality, and the battery lasts a long while (not 14 days but still a good while). The only really negative thing I've found about it is that it will NOT keep notifications turned on from the Zepp app that goes with it. Because I forget to turn it on when it goes off, it's almost never sending me notifications, which is one of the things I bought it for. This is a big issue that I think Amazon needs to correct, or maybe more specifically, they need to correct on the connected Zepp app. No matter how many times I tell it to allow notifications, it'll work for a few days and revert back to none. Then, I go days without noticing it and have to turn it back on again. I've checked Reddit to see what others are saying, and it's definitely a known issue that needs to be addressed.

reviews.title: Amazing Amazfit - Excellent so far.
reviews.body: Edit (06/10/25): Now about 8 days into the Bip 6. After a week of use, the watch was sitting at 50% charge. I charged it up to 96%+ in about an hour. I'm using a USBC charger which I think provides about 2A. Can't say for sure as it's a charger built into a lamp in my bedroom that has both USBC and USBA; the "C" charger shows my Pixel phone charges "rapidly" whereas the "A" plug charges normally (slower but fast enough for the phone to hit 100% sometime during the night). I did try the "A" port (with an A-to-C cable) but it is slower. Still totally happy with the Bip 6. More feedback in a few months. Early days but I thought it might be helpful for those trying to decide between a Fitbit and this Amazfit Bip 6 (a truly unfortunate name). I had been using a Fitbit Charge 5 for a couple of years. The first week I wore it, the Charge 5 detected Afib and that probably saved my life. So I wanted to really like the Charge 5 and continue using it. However, I discovered it was terribly inconsistent in providing a sleep score and HRV; perhaps 40% of the time it just failed. A month or so ago (after 2+ years of use), it would just go "black screen" if I did anything with the Charge 5 other than simply looking at the screen. The battery also didn't last very long and the charger "connection" (magnetic) was hit-or-miss so it was time for a new watch. After deciding against another Fitbit (reviews have gotten worse over the years and Google has already said Fitbit will soon no longer be supported properly), the choice was either an expensive Garmin (and they're all expensive), a Samsung Galaxy watch (also $$$), or one of these "cheap" Chinese brands. (Can't use an Apple watch as my phone is of the Android variety). This Amazfit seemed to have the best reviews of the cheap smartwatches so I bought it with the 3-yr warranty for under $100 total. Amazon delivered it the next morning. Followed the prompts and set it up in a few minutes so it syncs with my Pixel 6a with the Amazfit Zepp app. I charged it using the provided charger "puck" (you must provide your own USB-C cable, remember this!) and, once it reached 100% (a couple of hours maybe), I strapped it on and configured the watch both with the watch's preferences and the Zepp app. I have most of the integration with the phone switched off; why did I need to answer my phone with the watch when I have my phone on my hip all day? I just wanted the watch to keep track of my steps, heart health, and sleep (the latter the most important point). So here we are after three nights and the watch seems to be 100% accurate in sleep tracking and heart health reporting (and it keeps perfect time, of course). As I indicated above, these are still early days but I'm thrilled with this Bip 6. I even am dabbling in the watchface creation app on the web and even that works! Why would I want to use that? I hate tiny type on a large screen so why not make a watchface that really shows off how large all the information can be presented? Great stuff. I am not going to test how waterproof the watch might be; I remove it before showering or swimming and am careful otherwise. BTW: There's a function on the watch where you can "eject" any water that might have found its way into the speaker. (Yes; the watch can play music and you can speak through it to your phone but I'm not going down that patch.) The only downside I can see (and it's not for me) is the length of the band; I have a small wrist but the fourth hole in the strap makes the watch fit properly; I would have expected a longer strap for larger wrists. However, using that fourth hole leaves about 1.75" beyond the buckle (.75" of which tucks back inside the band and that's fine). I would recommend to Amazfit that they provide a longer strap for larger wrists (much like how Fitbit does it). Oh, yeah; one more thing. One of the included apps on the phone is a compass! I set it up so one of the buttons on the side of the watch launches it. You know when your GPS starts off by saying "head east"? Who knows where that is without a compass? Now I know. I'll report back in a few months with more info.

reviews.title: Feature-packed smartwatch for an incredible price—if you’re willing to tackle the learning curve!
reviews.body: This watch is fantastic! I love being able to make and receive calls, plus get text and email notifications right on my wrist. The offline navigation is a standout feature—I downloaded maps for my hometown and neighboring cities, and navigating without cell service is seamless. It’s especially convenient during workouts. Whether I’m playing pickleball or lifting weights, I can leave my phone in my bag and still catch important notifications without interrupting a match or set. I’ve used sleep tracking since 2022 (upgrading from a Bip 3 that finally gave up the ghost), and the accuracy on this model is solid. Given everything it offers, the price-to-performance ratio is hard to beat. The Drawbacks: Poor Documentation: Setup and configuration were frustrating. The official guides provided little help, so I had to rely on influencer tutorials and trial-and-error to get everything dialed in. Stock Band: The included strap is mediocre. I swapped it for a 22mm magnetic braided nylon band, which completely resolved my comfort issues. If official video tutorials or better documentation were provided, this would easily be a 5-star review.

reviews.title: Brilliant Smart Watch
reviews.body: Im super impressed with the AMAZFIT BIP 6. I got it for my house mate as her FITBIT Versa 3 died on her. So i initially came across a YouTube review of this smart watch and it caught my eye being the tech nerd i am and i was super impressed, so i continued watching different reviews and they just got better and better so i recommended this to my house mate who knows NOTHING about tech lol, and we got it. Set up was SUPER easy and from set up i have got to say it has not missed a beat. It pretty much has got and does almost everything my 🍎 watch ultra 2 does, plus a few little things i like better, like you can set a time for AOD to turn on at 8am and turn off at 10pm i think this is awesome and it also puts the watch in to DND mode so it doesnt disturb you whilst your alseep. It has 4 or 5 standard AOD watch faces to chose from or you can use your actual chosen watch face for AOD. Has great fitness features and another thing i love is it has a toggle which you can press and ALL your stats come up without having to go into each one individually like HR, STRESS, FITNESS ( Activity) your breathing, etc. The Watch is Bluetooth of coarse and it has a super stable connection as mentioned has not disconnected once & has great range away from your phone, it can take calls and you can also make them. You can also send and recieve text messages and even has quick replies. The display i think is awesome can get super bright and no issues seeing details on a bright day. It actually gets so bright my housemate keeps it on the lowest level of brightness. It has all your toggles like DND, PING MY PHONE, TORCH, AirPlane Mode, etc. Its a really nice looking watch as well and this one we got is a beautiful colour. It takes just about most 22mm bands with quick release pins, so changing bands is easy and pretty much most 3rd party bands fit. The watch lasts a good 7 days if you dont have much activity going on and my house mate has been charging it up approx every 6 to 7 days, with more activity it will still last 4 to 5 days. My only little gripe is the battery charging puk, it doesnt come with a cable in the box. You have to be extremely careful not to loose the charging puc and also i been trying to look for a holder or stand for the puc and just cannot find one for the Bip 6 unless you spend a small fortune for the stand that fits the Puc made specifically which is a shame. She'd like to have some sort of puc stand so that she doesnt accidently loose the actual charger, would be nice if you could get your hands on more 3rd party ones ? Bar that this is an EXCELLENT smart watch and with my housemate using it over the last month or so she has been thoroughly impressed by it and so have i to be honest. Its also not that expensive for EVERYTHING this smart watch does plus more. If your looking for a good all round Andorid smart watch then this is the one, look no further, you will be pleasently surprised with it, if not overly. It does also work with IOS but all features work better with Android. Also the App is so functional, you can do so much on it and its super easy to navigate and understand and it even has a watch face market where you can get a heap of watch faces for free with more getting release FREE weekly and some paid faces end up being free so a HUGE range to choose from. You do have to set up an account to use the App but that to is simple to do HIGHLY RECOMMENDED SMART WATCH 😀👌⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

reviews.title: Previous Apple Stan Here- this watch is amazing
reviews.body: I have always been an Apple Watch person. I’ve had one since probably 2017 and I was sick and tired of the horrific battery life Apple Watches have. Let me tell you on battery life alone this watch is leaps and bounds ahead. It’s been 8 days since I got this new watch, it came 96% charged and it currently has 45%. My Apple Watch battery wouldn’t last me 12 full hours. It’s overall easy to use, coming from Apple there was a slight learning curve but it’s not bad. Very easy to setup. It seems accurate steps wise. I have a very small wrist so I wish it came with a smaller band. This one fits but the left over strap wraps around almost all the way. I still get the needed notifications from my phone and can control my music. This is an incredibly functional watch. My husband kept telling me just to buy a new Apple Watch because I use it for work primarily but I couldn’t bring myself to pay that high of a price again for just a slightly better battery and I know Garmin is worth it but I’m not active enough to make the price worth it. I was skeptical with this only being $45 at the time but it has definitely proved its worth. We shall see how long it actually lasts though. Crossing my fingers for at least a year because I love this thing.

reviews.title: Here’s an honest review for ya!
reviews.body: I was honestly considering returning this, but now I’m a bit undecided. Maybe I’ll write this review and it’ll help me decide. For context, I’m a big watch person - especially for workouts - so I set a budget of $50 max and decided to give this one a try. It was right on the money. When it arrived, I’ll admit the packaging made me a little skeptical. Usually, presentation says a lot about the product, and this didn’t give the best first impression. AT ALL. After opening it, the watch itself did feel a bit flimsy at first (see photos), but surprisingly, the actual build quality turned out to be better than expected. It feels fairly sturdy, which was a nice surprise. I tested it at the gym this morning for the first timr, and it definitely held its own. The workout tracking exceeded my expectations - it offers a wide variety of activities you can easily select, which is a great feature! The battery life is exceptional! It lasts for a very long time which is ALWAYS a plus! I also liked that I could customize the watch face with a personal photo. However, there’s a downside: if you upload your own image instead of using one from the app’s store, you’re very limited in what data can be displayed. Instead of showing time, date, steps, calories, etc. all together, it only allows you to display one or two items. In my case, I could only show the time and date, which was disappointing. Cons: The app is probably the weakest part of this product. There’s a “Find My Phone” feature, but it disconnects every few minutes. You have to reopen the app to reconnect before using it again, which defeats the purpose - especially if you’re trying to locate your phone when it’s lost. Not sure how someone is supposed to find their lost phone but need their phone and watch need to be connected to the app before using this tool. Make it make sense??? You can’t lol. It also claims to support notifications from apps like Snapchat, Facebook, and Instagram, but despite enabling everything, I haven’t received any of those. Not a single one. I only get basic notifications like calls, texts, and a few random apps. I work in software, so I’m prettyyyy comfortable with tech. If I’m having trouble getting these features to work properly, that’s something to keep in mind if those functions are important to you. Please be aware of this if you’re searching for a watch solely for this reasoning. Another downside is that the wristbands aren’t interchangeable - there’s no easy way to swap them out, which is limiting. Which really sucks. Overall, for $50, it’s decent. But honestly, for an extra $20–$30, you could probably find something much better without all the disconnection issues this one constantly gives you. I’ll give it a few more days before deciding whether to keep it or return it. More than likely I’ll be returning to get something more reliable but I’m writing this review for those who wants to stay in a reasonable price range, while giving them the honest review they deserve before spending their hard earned money. Hope this helps!! EDIT 5/24/26: I ended up keeping the watch. The more I used it, the more features I was discovering both in-watch, and in-app. However, I’m still keeping it as 3 stars because of the Cons I’ve listed still being an issue. reviews.body_en: I was honestly considering returning this, but now I’m a bit undecided. Maybe I’ll write this review and it’ll help me decide. For context, I’m a big watch person - especially for workouts - so I set a budget of $50 max and decided to give this one a try. It was right on the money. When it arrived, I’ll admit the packaging made me a little skeptical. Usually, presentation says a lot about the product, and this didn’t give the best first impression. AT ALL. After opening it, the watch itself did feel a bit flimsy at first (see photos), but surprisingly, the actual build quality turned out to be better than expected. It feels fairly sturdy, which was a nice surprise. I tested it at the gym this morning for the first timr, and it definitely held its own. The workout tracking exceeded my expectations - it offers a wide variety of activities you can easily select, which is a great feature! The battery life is exceptional! It lasts for a very long time which is ALWAYS a plus! I also liked that I could customize the watch face with a personal photo. However, there’s a downside: if you upload your own image instead of using one from the app’s store, you’re very limited in what data can be displayed. Instead of showing time, date, steps, calories, etc. all together, it only allows you to display one or two items. In my case, I could only show the time and date, which was disappointing. Cons: The app is probably the weakest part of this product. There’s a “Find My Phone” feature, but it disconnects every few minutes. You have to reopen the app to reconnect before using it again, which defeats the purpose - especially if you’re trying to locate your phone when it’s lost. Not sure how someone is supposed to find their lost phone but need their phone and watch need to be connected to the app before using this tool. Make it make sense??? You can’t lol. It also claims to support notifications from apps like Snapchat, Facebook, and Instagram, but despite enabling everything, I haven’t received any of those. Not a single one. I only get basic notifications like calls, texts, and a few random apps. I work in software, so I’m prettyyyy comfortable with tech. If I’m having trouble getting these features to work properly, that’s something to keep in mind if those functions are important to you. Please be aware of this if you’re searching for a watch solely for this reasoning. Another downside is that the wristbands aren’t interchangeable - there’s no easy way to swap them out, which is limiting. Which really sucks. Overall, for $50, it’s decent. But honestly, for an extra $20–$30, you could probably find something much better without all the disconnection issues this one constantly gives you. I’ll give it a few more days before deciding whether to keep it or return it. More than likely I’ll be returning to get something more reliable but I’m writing this review for those who wants to stay in a reasonable price range, while giving them the honest review they deserve before spending their hard earned money. Hope this helps!! EDIT 5/24/26: I ended up keeping the watch. The more I used it, the more features I was discovering both in-watch, and in-app. However, I’m still keeping it as 3 stars because of the Cons I’ve listed still being an issue. I’d say give it a try yourselves and see how you like it. You can read all the reviews but it’ll affect everyone differently.
