reviews.title: This Review is the only one you need to read! This watch DOES IT ALL!!!!!
reviews.body: This will be the only review needed to know this is the Smart Watch to purchase!! I have at this point probably purchased and returned more than 50 smart watches because I wanted notifications to have an audible tone and not just vibrate. With Bluetooth 5.2 it was an automatic with most of the accompanying apps you had to partner the watch with but when 5.3 came out, it became vibrate only on all apps with the exception of ONE…VeryFit. Additionally, VeryFit is the ONLY one which will register notifications from LITERALLY EVERY SINGLE APP you have which sends banner notifications to your phone, not just the 10-15 options typically seen in the other apps like Gloryfit, DaFit, FitCloudPro, HBand, etc. In order to receive these Push Notifications on an iPhone, which is what I have, you need to go into Settings, Bluetooth, touch the “i” in the circle and check off “Show Message Notifications” and “Share System Notifications”. You must then go to the App List, find VeryFit, make sure Background App Refresh is checked and Notifications are mirroring the ones I’ve captured in my images. The other important piece of info is the watch volume is set low when it first arrives. Make a phone call from the watch and touch the speaker icon key to allow for raising the volume. In the VeryFit app itself, go to Device, click Notifications, be patient and wait a few seconds and the screen will expand - check off “Sync Phone Notifications” and this is where all the excitement is! As notifications come to your phone, they will also become listed here on this page (and your watch will get the alert for them at the same time) and this is where you can Allow or Turn Off the specific notification. I have also captured this in my images for reference. As you can see, I get notifications for everything I receive on my phone. If you need more assistance, do as it says and tap the “i” in the circle on that page and you will get the detailed instructions just as I have given you now. I have also captured those in my images for you to reference as well. This tracks sleep, stress, energy, blood oxygen level, heart rate, gives you weekly averages on all. It can track your cycle for females and ones weight. It has suggested programs to help with better sleep habits, managing weight, stress, breathing exercises etc. It has every possible physical exercise activity one could imagine. It’s waterproof, has excellent options for watch faces - many are free or you can opt to pay for some if you choose not to become a Community member and if you do, those become free then as well. You can share your progress within the community to help stay motivated if needed. You can contact customer service if you have additional questions at anytime by tapping the little blue operator floating on the page within the app as well. There are screen protectors available, watch cases are shown available but they are too big, so don’t bother, you can change out the bands - there’s nothing you can’t do with this watch and the battery life is also fantastic, lasting me a week so far, even with all the many notifications I receive!! Obviously, I highly recommend it!! You won’t regret the purchase! The only thing I am now in need of is finding its twin in rectangular form because I like to switch between that and round; should I find it, I will update this review with the information! I hope this review has helped!

reviews.title: Good watch if it lasts — You won’t regret this purchase
reviews.body: Update 6/3/26, company responded to my email and sent a new watch asap. I will report back in a couple months if it keeps working. Update 4/20/26, just short of 2 months. My watch has been acting up, the screen has not lighting up for me and the charge going from 100% to zero in just a couple minutes, and now the screen won’t turn on and Bluetooth will not connect to my phone. I have added a video of the issue that is causing me to update my review. Not the update I wanted to give as I loved this watch, but I felt compelled to come back and give an update to others so they were aware of what i experienced. I typically don’t write reviews, but I had to for this product. I used to be a Fitbit owner and very much enjoyed the fitness tracking. I was ready to move to a different style, I wanted one that looked more like a watch. I searched and reviewed garmin and nowatch. I didn’t love garmin due to the size of the watch face on my smaller wrist and the one I liked the best was around $500. The nowatch brand is beautiful but along with the expensive price, I didn’t love that you couldn’t look at the watch and see steps. So I landed on, why not give this product a try?? The watch face size was smaller which was better for my wrist size, the price was better than right and it had all the features I wanted, plus more. Once I got this watch I wore this watch and my Fitbit together to compare stats, believe it or not, this watch was closer to the miles walked measured on my treadmill compared to the Fitbit, the sleep stats were similar. Love the ability to answer calls and make calls in this watch. The weather tracking and all notifications come through well. And the screen is amazing. I did swap out my band (20mm), just for personal preference, the one that came with it was durable. Battery lasted 7 days, I used a decent amount and tracked fitness each day. 100% would recommend!!

reviews.title: Klasse Produkt... 👍👍👍
reviews.body: Angekommen in einer flachen weißen aber dennoch edlen Box/Schachtel. Innendrin die Uhr, das Ladekabel und eine Kurzbeschreibung – völlig ausreichend. Ausgepackt und erstmal gestaunt. Das Gehäuse ist aus Metall gefertigt und sieht in der rosegoldenen Färbung absolut edel aus. Das Armband aus weichem samtigem Kunststoff schmeichelt sich regelrecht um das Handgelenk. Eine absolut gelungene Smartwatch in einer edlen Aufmachung und sehr angenehmen Haptik. Die erste Herausforderung: Stelle die Verbindung zum Smartphone her, aber auch hier – keine Probleme. App wie in der Beschreibung auf das Smartphone herunterladen, installieren, die Berechtigungen freischalten und Schwupps hat sich die Uhr auch schon mit dem Smartphone verbunden. Die Telefonfunktion funktioniert top und das mit einer glasklaren Verbindung zum Gesprächspartner. Die Auswahl der kostenlosen Hintergründe/Uhrendisplays ist meines Erachtens völlig ausreichend und die kostenpflichtigen Displays sind auch nicht teuer, wenn man unbedingt noch etwas anderes brauchen sollte. Für Sport und andere Aktivitäten hat der Hersteller so ziemlich alles an „üblichen“ Sportarten in die Software gepackt. Nach vielen enttäuschenden Erfahrungen mit dieser Art von Uhr im günstigeren Preissegment, bin ich diesmal absolut begeistert. Es muss tatsächlich kein teures Produkt wie ein „angebissener Apfel“ sein um eine Menge Spaß mit einer Smartwatch zu haben. Spaß der auch noch einen klasse Preis hat. Beide Daumen 👍👍...
reviews.body_en: Arrived in a flat white but elegant box/box. Inside the clock, the charging cable and a short description – completely sufficient. Unpacked and was amazed at first. The housing is made of metal and looks absolutely elegant in its rose gold color. The bracelet made of soft, velvety plastic really flatters the wrist. An absolutely successful smartwatch with an elegant design and a very pleasant feel. The first challenge: establish the connection to the smartphone, but here too – no problems. Download the app onto your smartphone as described in the description, install it, activate the permissions and presto, the watch has already connected to your smartphone. The telephone function works perfectly and with a crystal-clear connection to the person you are talking to. In my opinion, the selection of free backgrounds/clock displays is completely sufficient and the paid displays are also not expensive if you absolutely need something else. For sports and other activities, the manufacturer has packed pretty much all “usual” sports into the software. After many disappointing experiences with this type of watch in the cheaper price segment, this time I am absolutely thrilled. It actually doesn't have to be an expensive product like a "bitten apple" to have a lot of fun with a smartwatch. Fun that also has a great price. Both thumbs 👍👍...

reviews.title: Perfect size if you feel the Active 2 is too small
reviews.body: I previously had the Amazfit Active 2, but felt it was a bit small for my wrist. This however is perfect. Easier to see the heart rate info and whatnot with the larger screen. Plus the battery life is way longer than the 10 days claimed on the Active 2 and while it's not a huge deal to charge, it's still much more convenient to have extra battery life. One thing I was a little unsure of was the thickness. The photos kind of make it look like a beast. While it is thicker than the Active 2 it's not obnoxious and it's given me no pause whatsoever in terms of look and feel. Brightness is excellent, though I haven't had it long enough to test it on a sunny day outdoors. **Edit** Have been out in full sun with it and no problems seeing the screen The strap is very comfortable and is the same type of quick release strap with the pins that other smart watches have. Doing some googling it's a 22mm strap which shouldn't be a problem to find. One thing worth mentioning is some peoples skin is sensitive to silicone straps. My skin is not, but I've also had nylon with velcro and can recommend that if you want to use a different strap. Also there's no more tucking the tail of the strap down between your skin and under the strap, it's now routed the way most other straps are, on the outside. I'll update this review if I have any issues, but if you're up in the air between this and the Active 2 and you don't have tiny wrists I'd definitely go with this. Edit 1/22/26: Zero issues to report. One thing worth mentioning is that the face is not completely flat. The edges at the bezel curve down slightly. This means a flat 1.5 inch screen protector won't work; the edges would come off or there would be bubbles that you can't remove. I'm currently using the same screen protector I had for my Active 2. It doesn't cover everything but it does cover the flat part and vast majority of the screen completely and without any raised edges or bubbles. You can view my profile to see which I used. There seem to be some tempered glass screen protectors here on Amazon that curve down at the edges (with the bezel markings to match), but since this is so new I haven't bought one yet.

reviews.title: Perfect in many ways
reviews.body: It’s been a week now since the purchase and I can honestly say this is an excellent smart watch! Build Quality: Excellent, well thought out and very good quality controls. Arrived well-packaged with good protective packaging. There is a very small font but well written manual. The screen is of very high definition and very bright. Functionality: Excellent and very responsive. Easy to pair with my IPhone and the alerts are instantaneous, both the phone and the watch receive, emails, alerts etc at exactly the same time and the watch doesn’t show any lag at all. I would say, it beats my Apple watch in receiving the same alerts from the phone! If you’re very active and do all kinds of sports, you’re in luck. The watch is loaded with functions for any sport imaginable. These functions can be turned on or off / customized to suit your life style. Zepp app: The Zepp app is used to set up / pair / customize the watch and it is an excellent app actually! Customization: Also excellent. The watch can be customized in dozens of ways. There are countless watch faces that are free as well as ones that one could purchase. But honestly, the free ones are truly good! Cons: Nothing serious. The band would be much better if the connections are like Apple’s (slide in and lock in place) instead of using pins. The instructions manual really requires a magnifying glass. But it is so intuitive that one may not need the manual and the magnifying glass! In summary: This is a terrific smart watch. I am wearing it more frequently than my Spple watch that cost 3x more! I highly recommend it , especially when on sale!

reviews.title: Runners Watch
reviews.body: I used coros pace 3 for almost 2.5 years until there was hardware issue with crown and touchscreen. I had two amazfit watches previously, GTS and BIP. But I liked my coros pace 3 the most because of its accuracy, battery life and training modes. I didn’t expected it would end this way. It was an expensive watch so I decided to go with a budget watch this time and purchased crossbeats armour pro. I returned it the next day as it wasn’t able to sync with Strava. Next I decided to go with Amazfit watch because i had good experience with my GTS and BIP. Scrolling around I came to know about newly launched Active Max. I just ordered looking at the reviews and ratings on amazon although I didn’t expected much from this one. After using coros pace 3 i was not expecting much from this watch but to my surprise it surpassed my expectations. It did everything what my coros pace 3 did and at not so expensive price tag. It is pretty accurate in distance, heart rate, calories tracking. The calling feature is amazing and speaker and mic are crystal clear. So many good features like quick notifications, bt calling, offline and online music control, AI coaching, Always on display and not to forget it has a very strong gps connection. Gps locks up very fast, within few seconds and doesn’t loose signals throughout the run. 16K is Great value for money for this all in one accurate and precise, premium, feature rich bundled watch.

reviews.title: Fits comfortably on my wrist, easy to read bright colored perfect size screen
reviews.body: Arrived quicker than scheduled so that was a nice surprise. I love the soft pink color and I also like the larger screen. My last fitness tracker was smaller screen. This looks similar to a well known expensive brand watch. I just got it today and got right to programming it so I could start wearing it. I can't rate it on durability or accuracy yet but I sure hope it will be more reliable than my last fitness tracker which I won't mention the brand. I like the brightness of the screen which I find easier to read outdoors. UPDATE: Samsung Galaxy Fit 3 (2024) review continued: I'm quite pleased with this item as it seems to actually work each day! Imagine a fitness tracker that actually works and doesn't randomly stop mid day!! Another plus that I discovered by accident is my watch reminds me when I'm out of range of my phone. This helps me to remember to not leave my phone behind if I'm working outside or over at my son's house. I have gotten home and realized an hour later that my phone isn't in my bag. This watch vibrates right away when the phone isn't in range. As an older person this is a help for me. I want to have my phone nearby in case I have a medical issue. I also love the bigger screen and the watch is very responsive which was another frustration with my last fitness tracker. I love the long charge battery life. I doubt I'll ever go back to my prior fitness tracker as it was so maddening to NOT be able to figure out the issues and sometimes it would "wake up" and start working again. This Samsung Galaxy Fit 3 is easy to wear and provides the health tracking numbers that matter to me. Thumbs up.

reviews.title: Love at first sight
reviews.body: This watch is honestly almost perfect. Literally like a 9/10. The design is sleek, the watch face is not too big for my tiny wrist, has a vibrant and attractive display, and the watch band is really nice and soft! I had a fit bit charge 4 before this one and it finally quit on me. I wanted a low budget option because I haven't been consistent and don't have 300 dollars to waste for it to sit around if I end up not staying consistent. For 50 dollars this beauty fits nearly all my needs. Paired to my samsung phone immediately when I pulled it out of the box. Super easy to set up, and tons of different ways to customize the watch face. Have I mentioned its so pretty?? I don't typically wear a watch but I wanted the health metrics to track my heart rate and steps. This is one of two mild caveats. It doesn't actively track your heart rate. Every couple minutes or so it pings your heart rate to get more of a time line than a live feed. No worries, it pings often enough you get a good idea. Only mildly sucks because I use the live feed heart rate monitor to help clue me in to if I might have a panic attack or if I'm overreacting. Another thing. I have been using google health to track my calories and set specific goals for some of my macros I'm trying to hit. Unfortunately, the samsung health app doesn't get this specific and just gives you the suggested daily intake as a metric rather than letting you set your own. What sucks more is that these two apps don't sync with each other. So now I have 2 seperate apps to track my health. All in all. Its really a fantastic little gadget. For $50 I would 10000% buy it again if they came out with a newer version. Will update again after I've had it a few weeks.

reviews.title: The fitbit killer
reviews.body: My wife and I have been fitbit fans since the Charge 2 (2016).  Before the google purchase, fitbit was a strong leader in lower cost fitness trackers.  It did concern us that our fitbits would die frequently (nearly each one we had died within a year from the Charge 2, 3, 4). However after talking with customer service they would send us replacement.  So, ok, we can deal with that.  (Even though in the past few years you had to provide a ton of documentation including, IIRC, your drivers license.) I had a fitbit 6 that I got for Christmas 2024.  Wow, a color screen.  LOL.  I needed a replacement as the screen on my Charge 5 kept getting dimmer, and dimmer, to the point when I could not read it outdoors and barely indoors.  So I was gifted the Charge 6 and it was big step up.  But it took me a few months until I realized that the floors option was gone, not just not working, but removed, to make space for other features I could care less about. So I looked around in late June and discovered the Fit 3.  So I bought one.  I am SO GLAD I did.  What do I need?  Step counter, heart rate, floors, distance, calories.  Oh, and the kicker for me was AIRPLANE MODE.  I study various energetic sciences including BioGeometry and the EMF coming from our devices is not benign.  I don't wear a tracker to sleep, don't want anything live, and keep my blue tooth turned off unless I am actively syncing. This is what I see comparing Fit 3 to Fitbit Charge 6.   What the Fit 3 has as an advantage:  Larger screen, airplane mode, beautiful faces, much cleaner UI on the watch and in the android app(s) (I am using this with a Pixel 7 phone).  The ability to sync only turning on bluetooth.  A few years ago fitbit/google basically said we aren't syncing your fitbit unless you have both location/GPS and bluetooth turned on.  Sometimes you could get the fitbit to sync with location off but this was tricky/spotty. What advantages did the Charge 6 have for me, personally.   None really.  It cost about 3x the amount for the Charge 6 compared to the Fit 3.  That's ridiculous. In a head to head comparsion of measurements this is what I see.   Fitbit Charge is often slower to start your step counts and the Fit 3 is quicker on that.  So you steps counts are going to go up and perhaps the Fit 3 does count some arm motions as steps when it should not.  But the Fit 3 is still very close (within 1-3%) with the Charge 6.  The Fit 3 tends to undercount calories compared to the Charge 6, I can't tell which is more accurate.  On the Charge 6 bluetooth syncing was always a laborious pain taking sometimes minutes to get the past few days of data and often having to turn bluetooth off/on and/or restarts to get it to sync.  The Fit 3 is very fast *most* of the time.  I did have one instance where the Fit 3 was not syncing in the Health App and I had to open the Wearable app and trigger a sync from there, which worked. The big thing is battery life.  I have automatic activity tracking turned on and except when syncing in the evening I keep it on airplane mode.  I charged it overnight last Thursday/Friday before I first put it on.  It's now Wednesday evening, nearing 6 complete days of use and my battery level is at 55%.  That frugal energy use is really good and is on par with the earlier monochrome fitbits. I am very pleased with my Fit 3 purchase.  Back in the early to mid 2000's I was very excited about Timex was doing just in digital watches (Iron Man, etc).  The Fit 3 harkens back to those kind of days for me when you could get a very full functionality wrist device that looked good, worked great, and was a good deal.  This is definitely worth a close look if you don't need an higher priced fitness/communication device that is emitting EMFs into your pericardium meridian 24x7.  Well done.

reviews.title: Nice fitness tracker
reviews.body: I've had a long line of Fit Bits and when I found out Samsung has a non-smart watch tracker, I decided to give it a chance. (I don't want to pay smart watch prices.) Out of the box, the Fit 3 was in Spanish, but when I put it on the charger, it reverted to English. It stayed English until I got a new phone and had to reset the tracker in order to pair it with the new phone. The tracker reverted to Spanish and putting it on the charger did not change that this time. I pressed the top option on the device's screen and got to choose from a whole list of languages. I chose English, but this is where someone who wants another language will find it. The charge on this item is supposed to last up to 13 days. I've had this device for 3 months, and I got 6 days out of each charge (7 if I let the device die) for the first 2 months or so. Now, it last 4-5 days. I don't have the display always on and I don't consider my use of this device heavy by any means. 6 days is what I got out of my most recent Fitbit. My Fit 3 charges from 20% to 70% in about 20 minutes and to 100% in about an hour. The trick is to get the charger properly seated, because the first couple of times, I don't think it was on correctly, as I got the main display, not the charging percentage display, and it took about 2 hours to reach 100%. I wore the new Fit 3 side by side with my old Fitbit Charge 6 for 24+ hours to compare - 2 nights and one active day. The first night, the Fit 3 recorded 20 more minutes of sleep and the second night, the Fitbit recorded 20 more minutes. I don't know how either determines when I am asleep and not quietly reading, so I figure the results are comparable. The Fit 3, while behind on step count early in the day, ended the day with almost 1,500 more steps than the Fitbit. Both counted activity (cleaning, for instance), not just pure steps. I'm OK with this - I figure any movement is better than no movement. There are many more features that I don't use. I may in the future, but I'm happy with what I do use. I tried taking photos on my phone (also a Samsung) with my Fit 3 as a remote shutter button. I like that feature! Text notifications come to my Fit 3, but not all of them. When I am using my phone, notifications do not go to the tracker (I have found that this is the default and I can change it if desired). Group texts never do (they will go to my car, so I don’t know why they won't go to my Fit 3), and random regular texts don't. I found in the Health app where I can pick and choose which apps will send notifications. All told, I like this device. It’s not perfect, though. I miss the feature that Fitbit has that reminds me to move each hour. I'm now forced to choose between step count, floor count (I assume that means how many stairs I climb), or active hours. I like counting steps, so that's my main goal. I like seeing the hearts light up throughout the day as I get closer to my goals. I also have active minutes and active calories burned as goals, but I don’t care as much about those.

reviews.title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Cute, sleek and does everything I need — obsessed with it!
reviews.body: I picked up the pink one and it looks absolutely gorgeous on the wrist. The colour is a soft, subtle pink — not loud or plasticky at all — and the slim band sits really comfortably without feeling bulky. I've worn fitness trackers before that felt like a brick on my arm, but this one is so lightweight I genuinely forget I'm wearing it sometimes. The screen is bright and clear, easy to read even in sunlight, and swiping through the menus feels smooth and responsive. Setting it up with my phone was quick and straightforward — no technical headaches, just paired it and it was ready to go. For day-to-day tracking it covers everything I need — steps, heart rate, sleep, calories, stress monitoring. The sleep tracking in particular is really detailed and I've found myself actually paying attention to it and adjusting my routine. The battery life has also genuinely impressed me. I charge it maybe once a week which is so convenient compared to smartwatches that need charging every day or two. reviews.title: A Simple and Affordable Fitness Tracker
reviews.body: I purchased the Xiaomi Mi Smart Band 10 after comparing it with several other fitness trackers, and the value for the price was hard to beat. After watching multiple YouTube reviews, I felt confident it was the right choice. The Smart Band 10 is simple, clean, and not overly flashy. The setup process was straightforward, though you do need to pair it with the Mi Fitness app, which requires creating an account. Once set up, the device tracks heart rate, sleep, steps, and provides handy notifications like incoming text messages. It covers all the essential features most people need. The Smart Band is pretty light weight and sometimes I don't feel it on the wrist which can be worrisome as you may bump it into things around, which I've done a few times but no scratches just yet but that's something to take note of. The battery life is truly impressive. I fully charged the device on November 22nd, 2025, and as of writing this review, it has been running for 14 days straight on that single charge and is sitting at 45% battery. With power-saving mode, you can extend it even further. However, there are a couple of downsides to consider. The most noticeable is the lack of physical buttons, which you can see in the product photos. You can power the Smart Band 10 off from the settings menu, but the only way to turn it back on is by connecting it to the included charging cable. This hasn’t caused any issues for me yet since I haven’t needed to turn it off, but it's something potential buyers should know. I also question the accuracy of the calorie and step counters at times, as the numbers don’t always feel consistent. Overall, if you’re looking for a simple, affordable, and reliable fitness tracker, whether for personal use or as a gift, the Xiaomi Mi Smart Band 10 is a solid choice. **Update on December 13, 2025, the Xiaomi Mi Smart Band 10 is currently on 19% of charge after a 21 day period going off one charge cycle. The Smart Band estimates that it could last for 4 more days. This device has been really impressive so far.

reviews.title: Truly Impressed!
reviews.body: I previously owned the Fitbit Charge 6 and was constantly disappointed. Its step‑tracking data was inconsistent, and the wristband felt heavy and uncomfortable for all‑day wear. Switching to this Xiaomi smart band has been a night‑and‑day difference, and I am truly amazed by its performance. Its step counting stays accurate during daily walks. The 1.72‑inch AMOLED screen is much bigger than the small display on the Fitbit Charge 6, with tons of free watch faces for full customization. It includes many practical tools that Fitbit does not have, such as real‑time weather updates, a handy flashlight, stress monitoring, and my favorite feature: remote camera control. I can take self‑shots easily by using the band to trigger my phone camera, which works perfectly for taking photos alone. Battery life is outstanding. A full charge lasts up to 21 days, while my Fitbit Charge 6 needed charging every seven days. Best of all, this tracker costs far less, with no mandatory subscription fees for health analysis. This lightweight, well‑designed fitness band gives fantastic value for money. I absolutely recommend it.

reviews.title: Nice watch at a good price
reviews.body: Update (July 7, 2024): I have used many watches like this and all had a feature to update the firmware. I never, ever received a firmware update before this watch. It actually updated and fixed the one thing I didn't like (the snooze feature)! Yay! I am adding the extra star for this! Now my favorite watch. -------------------------- I got this FitPolo smartwatch when it was listed at $24, a very nice price. It is almost identical to my go-to watch. It looks good, very apple-ish. It has the 'stem' button that turns on the screen, takes you to the features or, when held, calls up Alexa. Awesome! You can make calls from the watch via an on-screen dial pad. You can answer calls on the watch. You can read headers to your emails, and most of a text message. You can set quiet time so as not to be disturbed at night. The usual wake-on-wrist-turn is here too, with the advantage that it turns off when you put your arm down. You can set how long the screen stays on. I am almost a week in with the watch and I still have 44% left on the first charge. A feature I really like is that you can do many things, like setting new alarms, right on the watch. All other models I have used required that you use your phone to do this. One feature this has that my other watch does not, is a snooze feature. Some might like this, but I find it a problem. The issue is that pressing the stem button is snooze. You have to look at the screen and select the right button to turn the alarm off without snooze. I suppose that really wakes you up, but I would like the option to disable the snooze feature. There are many, many faces to choose from both free and paid. It was easy to pick out some I love. The strap is a traditional watch strap. I would swap it for a velcro sport strap. This is a well designed watch well worth the $50 listing. Since it also had a $15 coupon, it was outstanding! Nice!

Twice it tried to call 911 just because I rolled over in bed. Then when I actually fell, it did nothing. I turned off the fall detection as it's useless. But other than that, it is a great little watch for those who want a simpler life!

(Since I don't sleep with it, I stretch it to weeks) What it lacks from a full smartwatch? Payments (I don't need), answering calls plus some fancier health tracking like ECG or VO2max. But for the price, who cares? I wear it and don't worry about it. I would prefer I could set the watch without phone and also use standard watch straps, but hey the price! The Samsung app is one of the best for general health tracking. Best by far for nutrition tracking. Serious fitness enthusiast may find it a bit lacking. Shame the watch doesn't work with iPhone. This is a highly recommended device unless you are CERTAIN you need all the fancy features of a Galaxy or Pixel.

reviews.title: Phenomenal(ESPECIALLY IF YOU USE A DIABETIC CGM!)
reviews.body: The negative: Qi wireless charging removed with the watch 8 generation. That means you can't charge the watch from a power-sharing compatible phone(like my S23 Ultra). ....really, though, that's all the negative. Power-sharing has always been fiddly anyway. The neutral: I get about 1.5 days per charge, with battery protection on(max charge @ 90%), and ALL the bells and whistles(including always-on display). If you want it for sleep tracking every night, have a charger at your desk during the day to keep it topped-up. Slightly smaller screen/chassis ratio than expected. The body feels like they COULD have made the display a smidge bigger, but ymmv. That would have impacted weight, durability, and battery life, so it's probably for the best. The good: Feels good. Substantial. Beefy, but not clunky. Get a metal band to replace the sweaty faux-leather/rubber one. Fast. Responsive. Voice commands using google. Built-in digital compass. Gestures(shake your hand in a...suggestive fashion to clear notifications because...um...you're busy...feeding geese 0_o ). The rotating bezel is back, absent on the other variants of the watch 8 generation(and a deal breaker for me). Best of all, though, as an insulin dependent diabetic, the ability to check my blood sugar without unholstering my phone is PURE GOLD. If this applies to you, Google "gluroo watch app". Recap: Not perfect, but it still phenomenal. Not cheap, but I've worn it every day for a month. Every day, I think to myself: "WORTH IT".
reviews.body_en: The negative: Qi wireless charging removed with the watch 8 generation. That means you can't charge the watch from a power-sharing compatible phone(like my S23 Ultra). ....really, though, that's all the negative. Power-sharing has always been fiddly anyway. The neutral: I get about 1.5 days per charge, with battery protection on(max charge @ 90%), and ALL the bells and whistles(including always-on display). If you want it for sleep tracking every night, have a charger at your desk during the day to keep it topped-up. Slightly smaller screen/chassis ratio than expected. The body feels like they COULD have made the display a smidge bigger, but ymmv. That would have impacted weight, durability, and battery life, so it's probably for the best. The good: Feels good. Substantial. Beefy, but not clunky. Get a metal band to replace the sweaty faux-leather/rubber one. Fast. Responsive. Voice commands using google. Built-in digital compass. Gestures(shake your hand in a...suggestive fashion to clear notifications because...um...you're busy...feeding geese 0_o ). The rotating bezel is back, absent on the other variants of the watch 8 generation(and a deal breaker for me). Best of all, though, as an insulin dependent diabetic, the ability to check my blood sugar without unholstering my phone is PURE GOLD. If this applies to you, Google "gluroo watch app". Recap: Not perfect, but it still phenomenal. Not cheap, but I've worn it every day for a month. Every day, I think to myself: "WORTH IT".

reviews.title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 Classic (2025) 46mm — A Worthy Return to Form ★★★★★
reviews.body: After putting the Galaxy Watch 8 Classic through its paces over the past few weeks, I can confidently say Samsung nailed the comeback. The rotating bezel is back, and honestly, that alone made me hit "buy" — but there's so much more to love here. Build Quality That Feels Premium The 46mm stainless steel case has real heft without feeling clunky on my wrist. The brushed finish looks sharp whether I'm in a t-shirt at the gym or wearing a button-down to a meeting. The sapphire crystal display has shrugged off everything I've thrown at it — no scratches yet, despite my best (unintentional) efforts. The crown bezel clicks with that satisfying tactile feedback Samsung fans have been begging for since it disappeared. That Display, Though The Super AMOLED screen is gorgeous. Bright enough to read in direct Florida sunlight, vibrant when scrolling notifications, and the always-on display sips battery rather than gulping it. Colors pop and text is razor-sharp. Health Tracking Is Genuinely Useful The upgraded BioActive sensor is the real star. Heart rate tracking is accurate compared to my chest strap, sleep tracking finally feels reliable (with actually actionable insights instead of just data dumps), and the new wellness features — including the energy score and vascular load metrics — give me a real sense of how my body is recovering day to day. ECG, blood oxygen, and body composition all work as advertised. Performance and Battery Wear OS with One UI Watch is snappy. App launches are instant, transitions are smooth, and I haven't experienced the lag that plagued earlier generations. Battery comfortably gets me through a full day with the always-on display enabled, and closer to two days if I turn it off. Fast charging tops it back up while I shower. Fitness Tracking GPS lock is fast and accurate on outdoor runs, workout detection actually catches the workouts I forget to start, and the suite of supported activities covers basically anything I do. The running coach feature has been a pleasant surprise. The Ecosystem Bonus If you're in the Samsung world, this watch is a no-brainer. Pairing with my Galaxy phone was seamless, Samsung Pay works flawlessly, and notifications mirror perfectly. It also plays nicely with non-Samsung Android phones, though you'll lose a few features. Minor Nitpicks The proprietary band connector means you'll want to budget for first-party or compatible straps. And while battery life is solid, power users tracking long workouts with GPS will still want to charge nightly. Bottom Line The Galaxy Watch 8 Classic is the watch Samsung should have been making all along. The rotating bezel transforms the experience, the build quality justifies the premium price, and the health features have genuinely changed how I think about my recovery and sleep. If you've been waiting for Samsung to bring back what made the Classic line special, the wait is over. Highly recommend.

I've tried other less expensive smartwatches in the past but this one hits all the marks for me. I am well pleased so far.

reviews.title: Amazing device! Battery life is not an issue for me.
reviews.body: My five years old Galaxy Watch 4 was giving me signs. It was time to replace it. I bought the Watch 8 Classic because there is no Watch 9 Classic. I have it tweaked to my liking and I am blown away at what it can do. Battery life is an issue for some users, but not for me. I spend an hour on my PC flying my RC helicopter simulator every day. I charge the watch while I practice, and it is fully charged when I'm done. I have disabled the features that I don't need or use, and I have no issues or "charge anxiety". The rotating bezel is the bees knees. My Watch 4 had the software bezel, but the metal bezel is much much better. The build quality is excellent, and I have no problem with the size and weight. I am surprised at how lightweight it is despite the size. I got some strap adapters so that I can use my Watch 4 straps. Yes, it is a bit pricey, but you get what you pay for! It is a good investment in my opinion. The only time I take it off is when I shower. I have no trouble sleeping with it. The gestures feature is waaay cool. I'm very pleased with it; no buyer's remorse here. I watched several YT videos to help me to set it up. I highly recommend this watch.

title: Garmin Forerunner® 970, 47mm, Carbon Gray DLC Titanium, Black/Whitestone
bullet_points: Our brightest AMOLED touchscreen display with button controls, a lightweight titanium bezel and sapphire lens, plus a built-in LED flashlight for greater awareness in the dark during early morning or late-night runs
Up to 15 days of battery life in smartwatch mode and up to 26 hours in GPS mode for a more complete picture of your training and recovery

Understand your overall energy efficiency with running economy, and see how much you’re slowing down when your foot hits the ground with step speed loss (HRM 600 monitor required; sold separately); running tolerance helps you understand the real impact running has on your body so you can adjust your training to avoid overload and improve

Train for an event, achieve a milestone, or improve your fitness with Garmin Coach training plans; these running and triathlon plans are personalized to you and adapt based on your performance and recovery

Built-in microphone and speaker let you make and take phone calls from your wrist when your watch is paired to your smartphone — and you can even use your smartphone’s voice assistant to respond to text messages and more

Confidently run any route by using full-color, built-in maps and multi-band GPS; with dynamic round-trip routing, you can break off the path, and your watch will develop a new route that will get you the same mileage

Training readiness score is based on sleep quality, recovery, training load and HRV status to determine if you’re primed to go hard and reap the rewards (data presented is intended to be a close estimation of metrics tracked)
ECG app can record your heart rhythm and check for signs of atrial fibrillation (not available in all countries; for people 22 years or older)
Multisport auto-transition detects sport changes between swim, bike and run in multisport activities — so you can focus on the race and let your watch take care of recording splits

Get wrist-based running dynamics, including cadence, stride length, ground contact time and more, plus wrist-based running power, which gives you a continuous measurement of how much power you’re applying to the ground

reviews.title: The Ultimate Triathlon Watch
reviews.body: I use the Garmin Forerunner 970 every single day, and buying it has been one of the best investments I've made. As a triathlete, it has everything I need for swimming, cycling, and running—and much more. The training and performance metrics are outstanding, and the sleep tracking has been incredibly useful. Coming from the Apple ecosystem, I was especially impressed by the battery life. It lasts so much longer than I expected, making it easy to wear 24/7 without worrying about charging. Despite all of its features, the watch is incredibly lightweight and very comfortable to wear all day and night. I barely notice it's on my wrist. Paired with the Garmin HRM-Pro Plus, it becomes an exceptional combination for running and swimming metrics, and overall training analysis. I highly recommend it to anyone who is serious about running or triathlon.

reviews.title: One of the best smartwatches as a Triathlete
reviews.body: One of the best smartwatches I’ve used as a triathlete. Comes with a built in triathlon function that can track all 3 sports + transition times. Battery life lasts pretty much 2 weeks and recharges while I’m in the shower. Garmin also syncs all data from the Forerunner 970 with the Edge bike computers and connects with their heart rate straps and if you use a Wahoo/Zwift trainer everything syncs together as well. Display is super bright and comes with an always on display now + built in flashlight at the top which is probably one of the best things about the watch. I’ve also seen zero scratches on the display so I can attest the sapphire display they use is definitely more durable than my last Apple Watch’s display glass. It takes some getting used to compared to how easy Apple Watches are to pick up immediately but everything just makes sense once you figure it out.

reviews.body: As a recreational runner, the Garmin Forerunner 970 has proven to be a tremendous gadget that has truly transformed my training. The amount of data it collects is impressive, allowing me to monitor my progress with professional-grade accuracy. The device stores and translates complex metrics into a simple format, making it easier to make decisions to improve my fitness. I must admit that, at first, it is complicated to understand so much information and navigate through all the features it offers. However, once you get past the learning curve, it becomes indispensable. It is a powerful tool that, while offering elite-level functions, perfectly adapts to those of us who run for passion and health. A high-quality investment that keeps me motivated to keep clocking in miles!

It's also really cold you can download and customize your watch faces. If you buy this watch you won't be sorry!

My old Venu 2 Plus was very clunky and everything was buried deep in a chaotic menu structure. That watch, however, is still running strong. Other than theses points and the basic high quality of Garmin devices, the biggest advantage is the phenomenal battery life! I am getting 10-15 days depending g on how I use it. I have a Galaxy Ultra which I absolutely love but it needed to be charged everyday, even when not using workout features, which is why I was looking for replacement in the first place. If you can take the price hit, this is the beast to get.

reviews.title: Muy recomendado pero actualicen su dispositivo
reviews.body: Había comprado el forerunner en blanco para un regalo a mi novia y le encantó mucho así que me intrigo comprarme uno pero en color negro para mí pero al usarlo notaba que cambiaban las configuraciones solas, el idioma etc, lo devolví y lo cambié por otro y lo mismo al cargar mi respaldo, y compré otro más sencillo el instinct 3 pensando que ese si funcionaría mejor pero igual la batería se consumía en una semana, así que me puse a investigar y mi app de Garmin Connect no estaba actualizando mis dispositivos, así que estuve buscando información y descargué Garmin Express que está tanto para windows o macOS y al conectar tu dispositivo te lo actualiza sin ningún problema, actualicé el forerunner 970 y me va de maravilla, siempre que adquieran un producto Garmin actualicen mediante pc para su mejor funcionamiento, Ahora resuelto el problema lo eh usado para correr y gimnasio y la verdad que me da muy buenas métricas y la batería va mil veces mejor que un Apple Watch Ultra
reviews.body_en: I had bought the forerunner in white as a gift for my girlfriend and she loved it a lot so I was intrigued to buy one but in black for myself but when using it I noticed that the settings alone changed, the language etc., I returned it and changed it for another one and the same thing when charging my backup, and I bought another simpler one, the instinct 3 thinking that that one would work better but the battery still consumed in a week, so I started to investigate and my Garmin Connect app was not updating my devices, So I was looking for information and I downloaded Garmin Express, which is for both Windows and macOS and when you connect your device it updates it without any problem. I updated the Forerunner 970 and it works great for me. Whenever you purchase a Garmin product, update it via PC for better performance. Now the problem is solved, I have used it for running and the gym and the truth is that it gives me very good metrics and the battery is a thousand times better than an Apple Watch Ultra.

reviews.title: Excellent product, best sports watch available.
reviews.body: Fantastic item, worth the expense. Lots of running data (probably more than I need, would be enough for an elite runner). Upgraded from a Forerunner 165 mainly for the maps (which are excellent, almost OS map quality) and the ability to plot courses on the watch. Music and lap times through bluetooth headphones. The watch also has a speaker to give times and warnings about pace (too slow/fast) which are useful during races when I don't wear headphones. Also has inbuilt torch which is good enough to assist when running after dark, and suprisingly useful at other times (think searching in dark cupboards, examining fuse box, etc). Battery normally lasts me about five days, with running everyday and on a fairly bright setting. Would be less if you used the "always on" setting. Screen bright and easy to read, even when racing (without my reading glasses!), and the screens are all customisable whether you are interested in pace, distance, heart rate, time in heart zones, ascent/descent, etc. The watch has metrics for loads of other sports, including cycling, swimming, snowboarding, etc, which I cannot comment on, but for a distance runner this is probably the best sports watch available today.

reviews.title: Fantastic Smart Watch for the price, AMAZING battery life!
reviews.body: UPDATE after 2 weeks of owning this Smart Watch for Women: WOW! It's been a week and a half since I last charged this smart watch, and it is only down to 16%! The battery in this watch is AMAZING! SO much better than the Versa2 I had before! [Earlier] So far, I am very impressed with this smart watch! (I previously had a Versa 2 and after about a year the battery barely lasted 2 days, which became very annoying, and then it just stopped charging at all) This Smart Watch for Women is VERY user-friendly. Its time, date, timezone, heart rate, steps etc all work extremely well. And it does much more than my Versa 2 ever did. This smart watch also receives AND sends calls, and did it seamlessly! I haven't yet used the text function to send, however, it has received all my texts and alerted me. It works well with the app, which was easy to download and set up. The BluTooth works well also. I'm also happy that this watch is waterproof (up to a certain depth) because I will be paddleboarding this summer, and swimming. The watch came with two bands from which to choose, which is nice. And it came with its own charging cord, proprietary at one end, but USB on the other. It seems to charge quickly. I would definitely recommend the Smart Watch for Women, especially for those who want a lot of the functions of an Apple Watch, but don't want to pay that exorbitant price! This watch is SO much more reasonable, AND it looks very nice on.

reviews.title: It’s alright
reviews.body: Had this watch for a couple of weeks now. This watch is not bad, it is also not the greatest. I don’t think it accurately measures steps and heart rate is hit and miss, seems like it depends on how you hold your wrist or how tight you wear the watch. The phone locater feature doesn’t always work either, and you can’t customize the watch face with your own photo or answer text messages. That being said, the workout features that track distance and speed, etc. are great. The sleep tracker works well and just about all the other watch features are pretty cool. I do like that you can answer your phone and talk through the watch because there’s a microphone which has the ability to connect to Siri. All in all I would say 3.5 stars. Oh and the charge does holds well, just like with anything though it depends on how much you play with it. Update: After writing this review I was contacted by Nora from the company’s customer service team and offered either a replacement or refund of the watch that I purchased. It was super unexpected but highly appreciated, and gave an undoubting sense that this small company cares about their products and the reception they receive. The interaction and level of customer service alone is enough to give the watch a higher rating, as it’s obvious the company cares and that’s more than most places these days. I would overall recommend

reviews.title: Great googly-moogly the choices!
reviews.body: So realistically, I have gone through 4 (yes this is my 4th) smart watch this year (I think?! Might be 3 but anyways) and thos one by far has FINALLY given me everything I've been looking for. Well, almost everything. Still cant text out on it but, it is what it is. So, some interesting things about this watch compared to the others ive had are the accuracy of the biometrics taken, the screen quality, and overall battery life. I am even liking that when I misplace my phone is actually rings MY ringtone and not some weird built-in one from the watch company. I even love that you can change the notification tone ON the watch itself too. Pretty snazzy there. Now here's some downfall in my opinion (this is my personal opinion, use its information as you see fit). Firstly, the paid membership app im not thrilled about and its not for the price, thats fair across the board. Its the lack of knowing the time frame parameters used as well as this being noted in the listing itself. Another is, the lack of it being fully customizable (i.e. you make it your very own) backgrounds as well as the limited number you can have (4 is the max). But again, this is my opinion and im one who likes fully customizable things as I like to be different. Only other "flaw" is that it only has 1 button which sticks out a fair ways for my liking and digs into my wrist... Do wish it was a little more, sleek if you will in that department. But ive added photos to show the level of things offered as well as how it does look very asteticly pleaseing. Which is nice little bonus! So maybe im nitpicking on some things, oh well! All in all though, its beyond worth getting. Not had a connection issue like past ones, and the band it even came with wasnt just silicone (oddly wearing that causes my skin to "eat" itself so I cant wear them). So I hope this helps someone out there!

reviews.title: Recommended, lots of pluses, a few caveats
reviews.body: I've come to really like this rose gold smartwatch that I bought as a replacement for a Fitbit Charge 4. I have narrow wrists so it's big in comparison but as said, I'm getting used to it. I love being able to read it at a glance without squinting. The screen is sharp, crisp, gorgeous color and easy to read. Set up was initially easy but when I started using the watch, customizing screens, layout of icons and grant it the permissions it needs, I had to turn to googling "IDW28" and found most of the answers i needed. I am fairly tech savvy and after a lot of frustration, I could only solve my issues this way. (The companion app was no help.) The biggest problem was the watch would compete with my ear buds, phone or bedside speaker to take over Bluetooth control, and attempt to direct the audio to the watch. Audio would cut in and out as it repeatedly tried to take control. I finally figured out what was wrong when I realized a phone call I received was switched to my watch. I had a Dick Tracy watch! 😂 Lol and the audio is not nearly loud enough to make calls on our listen to music. Overall the watch with its phone app is exceptional to monitor steps, heart rate, sleep patterns, exercise sessions, stress level, water intake, weather and control your phone's music app, camera and much more. It also alerts you to notifications of messages and emails. Essentially it's the same notification that your phone displays (not the whole email or text) and you cannot respond. It does not measure blood pressure as some reviews suggest. It will connect to your AI asst but I don't need that. I do wish for a way to enter water intake in the watch but for now that has to be done on the phone app. It charges fast and is easy to hook up. The battery lasts about a week but you're mileage may vary depending on your settings. I would definitely recommend buying if you are looking for an easy to read screen that is a giant step up from something like a Fitbit. If you want to send messages or emails, respond to them, see images attached in same then look to spend 5-10 times the price. Me? I'm happy with the purchase. I don't need to make calls on a watch or compose replies to texts and emails on my wrist. I really hope they solve the problem competing for Bluetooth as I'd like to turn on some of the features I had to give up to solve the problem.

reviews.title: Can't complain...much
reviews.body: Hello there, future watch owners. If you're like me, you've spent wayyy too much time agonizing over which knockoff smart watch to buy, and have probably read every review ever written. So, here is a list of every observed helpful and unfortunate aspect of this quality timepiece. I've been using it about a month. Pros: It looks nice. The screen is large enough to read and navigate easily, without feeling like you have a tablet on your wrist. The responsiveness is decent and the picture is clear. The swipe-right shortcut saves your most recent selections. There are lots of options for what it can do. Workouts, music, phone, calculator, stress, sleep, O2, heart rate, water intake, and something I found especially helpful as someone who leaves their phone lying around, Find My Phone. I've used most of these but have barely scratched the surface on the sports/workouts. Notifications show up with a red dot rather than a large icon, which I like and are easy to read and clear. I really like being able to adjust the brightness on the screen, and having a shortcut for the wake gesture; it's easy to turn off at night - because it's bright enough to burn your retnas - and back on during the day. The flashlight function is very helpful and almost absurdly bright. The alarm works well. The battery has been fantastic. I probably have less notifications set up for social media and email than some, but it easily lasts me a week+, which is way more than my poor, retired 4 year old Versa Lite ever did. Cons: The app sucks. It's like they tracked daily notifications with "app unpaired from device" and forgot to fix it. I am re-pairing every couple of days. It links up quickly but I wish it would stay linked. There are no screen protectors available that I've found and as a result, there is already a scratch on the face. There is also a chip off the wrist sensor already, which makes me wonder about the longevity, and my skins safety. I wish that when you pressed the side button from a selection, it would take you back to the menu, rather than back to the home screen, but that's minor. I also haven't found replacement bands. I don't care for the cloth band but I like the silicone. Eventually it will wear out and I would like to be able to replace it. I haven't braved the water with it yet because I'm afraid of drowning it, so I can't speak to that. I think that for the price-point, it is worth it. I threw the extended warranty on it, so I'm basically covered for three years if something messes up and then I just get a new one. Rant over, enjoy your day 🙂 hope it helps!

reviews.title: Great value smart watch with tons of features
reviews.body: This is a great budget smart watch for someone who is maybe interested in trying one and doesn't want to spend hundreds of pounds on a top branded one. This watch offers you a wide variety of apps and facilities that you would find on a top branded watch It has lots of health apps such as heart rate, sleep, blood oxygen levels and stress levels. It also has a wide variety of fitness apps included which can help you begin your fitness journey with things like walking plans and running plans, or to continue in a journey with more advanced features. The display is large and clear, colours of vibrant and it's a very sensitive screen allowing you to easily navigate your way through the various menus and settings. You will download an app indicated in the instructions, this will allow you to fully personalise your watch as well as store your data - obviously your watch has a limited memory and you will need to store data externally. It charges using a special magnetic USB cord which attaches to the back of the watch. Charging is fast. It's incredible how much you get in this watch for such a low price, it's fantastic for people on a budget or someone just wanting to test the water to see if a smart watch is for them.

reviews.title: Packed with Features and Surprisingly Polished
reviews.body: This smartwatch delivers far more than I expected at its price. It’s stylish and comfortable to wear, and the pink gold version looks particularly refined without feeling too flashy. The screen is clear and responsive, and basic navigation feels smooth. Bluetooth calling has worked well, and the battery life has easily lasted a full week with moderate use. I like the health features, especially the heart rate and sleep tracking, which seem reasonably accurate for general wellness. Notifications come through reliably, and I’ve found the hydration reminders and camera shutter function more useful than expected. The included extra strap is a nice touch, and the ability to swap bands with standard 22mm ones adds even more versatility. While I didn’t dive deep into the fitness modes, the range of options is impressive for anyone with an active routine. The app has room for improvement, especially in reducing clutter and simplifying customization, but it does what’s needed once set up. Overall, this is a very capable smartwatch that gets a lot right, especially for everyday tracking and light communication needs.

reviews.title: Ottimo prodotto ricco di funzioni ed adatto ad ogni occasione!
reviews.body: Questo smartwatch della AEAC si è dimostrato un prodotto davvero valido e qualitativamente ben fatto. Arriva a casa in una scatolina carina bianca con l’immagine di un orologio e la scritta smartwatch. Aprendo il packing troviamo lo smartwatch con cassa quadrata di colore dorato con un cinturino in silicone di colore rosa già montato. In dotazione abbiamo poi il cavo di ricarica usb con attacco magnetico e il libretto di istruzioni con la lingua italiana. L’orologio, che è un articolo da donna, si presenta molto elegante e adatto ad ogni tipo di occasione. Presenta 1 pulsante al lato che serve per accenderlo/spegnerlo e per navigare nei vari menù e sottomenù, in alternativa al touch screen che risulta comunque preciso e sensibile. Una volta acceso compare la schermata iniziale ed effettuando swipe si scelgono le varie funzioni. Le cose che questo smartwatch può fare sono davvero tante: per le sportive ci sono tutte quelle funzioni relative al benessere del corpo dovute a più di 100 attività tra le quali nuoto, trekking, corsa etc.etc. Ci sono anche molte funzioni più o meno utili come contapassi, cardiofrequenzimetro, monitoraggio ossigeno, monitoraggio del sonno e misuratore di pressione. Poi ci sono le funzioni di un orologio classico come la sveglia e il datario e le funzioni smart che attraverso un collegamento bluetooth ad uno smartphone ci permettono di leggere messaggi da app social come instagram e facebook o da applicazioni come messanger o whatsapp. La connessione ci permette anche di utilizzare le varie play list presenti sul device o di utilizzare la fotocamera dello stesso senza bisogno di prenderlo. L’orologio ha un quadrante rettangolare LCD da 1,8 pollici con una ottima risoluzione di 240x280p in full HD e luminosità, che può essere ulteriormente modificata attraverso le impostazioni. La chiusura del cinturino risulta molto forte e resiste anche a strattoni abbastanza violenti. La connessione con il cellulare è immediata ed è stabile fino a 10 mt circa dal dispositivo (in presenza di ostacoli come porte o muri ovviamente è minore). L’orologio comparirà nella sezione del bluetooth del dispositivo con il nome IDW19 BT. Se tutto questo non bastasse Il costruttore ci mette a disposizione un app gratuita di nome “Very fit” anche in lingua italiana che completa ulteriormente questo smartwatch. Quest'app è davvero utile in quanto una volta scaricata e abbinato l’orologio ci permette di rispondere e chiamare senza prendere il cellulare con una qualità audio sufficientemente buona per conversare anche all’aperto in mezzo ai rumori del traffico. L’app fornisce ulteriori possibilità di settare lo smartwatch nelle sue funzioni e scaricare tanti quadranti diversi o utilizzare una foto personale come sfondo ed ovviamente scaricare eventuali aggiornamenti. Sempre con l’aiuto dell'app possiamo avere un data base dei nostri progressi nelle varie attività sportive e nel monitoraggio delle funzioni corporali ed è possibile anche importare vari contatti telefonici, quelli che magari si chiamano più frequentemente, cosi da non prendere affatto il cellulare. Il costruttore asserisce che questo orologio è impermeabile infatti ha la certificazione IP68 però io il bagno o la doccia con l’orologio eviterei di farlo in quanto il vapore potrebbe danneggiare la batteria. Può essere collegato a dispositivi che hanno android 6.0 o superiore o iOS 9.0 o superiore. Le mie impressioni su questo prodotto sono davvero ottime. Menu e sottomenu sono cosi facili ed intuitivi che non c’è alcun bisogno di vedere il libretto di istruzioni. La batteria al litio è di buona qualità con una durata superiore ai 6/7 giorni utilizzandolo in maniera normale con una ricarica che non dura più di 2 ore. Il cinturino in silicone sembra di buona qualità morbido e flessibile risulta molto comodo e anche dopo averlo indossato una intera giornata non porta prurito o rossore. Vedremo con il tempo anche la durabilità. La lunghezza totale di questo smartwatch è di 25 cm circa il che significa che può essere indossato da persone con una circonferenza del polso che va da 15 cm fino a 20 cm e oltre. Questo tipo di smartwatch non permette di installare applicazioni aggiuntive, non è fornito di GPS integrato per un eventuale navigatore e non da la possibilità di scrivere messaggi o vedere foto. Io l’ho regalato a mia moglie e devo dire che le è subito piaciuto. Lei non è particolarmente affine con la tecnologia ma ha subito imparato ad usarlo, almeno nelle sue funzioni principali. Lo indossa tutto il giorno anche quando lavora e mi ha detto che è cosi leggero che a volte dimentica di indossarlo. Il prezzo di questo al momento della recensione non è disponibile quindi non posso fare una comparazione ed una eventuale valutazione in merito. In conclusione questo è un prodotto di cui sicuramente ne consiglio l’acquisto anche per un eventuale idea regalo appena ritornerà disponibile alla vendita. Spero di essere stato utile nell'esporre tutte le caratteristiche di questo prodotto che mi è stato proposto tramite il programma Vine di Amazon, in cui cerco di dare sempre valutazioni oggettive ed obiettive dei prodotti offerti e testati. Resto comunque a disposizione per chiarire ulteriori dubbi sul prodotto.

reviews.title: Durable Case with a Great Built In Kickstand
reviews.body: This case has been excellent for my iPhone 15 Pro Max. The fit is perfect and feels very secure without adding too much bulk. One of the standout features is the MagSafe magnet strength, which is incredibly strong and holds accessories firmly in place without slipping. I also appreciate that the clear material has stayed clear and has not yellowed from regular handling or oils from my hands, which has been an issue with other clear cases I have used. It was easy to install on the phone and has held up very well with daily use. The built-in kickstand is also a really nice addition and works well for watching videos or using the phone hands-free without feeling flimsy. Overall, it feels durable and well-made, offers great protection, and still shows off the phone’s design.

It's well built, all the buttons line up perfectly and can be pressed easily. The magnet on the back is super powerful. It attaches really well to any mounts or stands or other attachments. The built-in stand around the upper camera part is really nice. I got my phone in blue and wasn't thrilled at the idea of covering it with a case, so I really like that this case is clear (mine is ringed in black and looks really nice with the blue phone). I've also dropped my phone about 100 times since I started using this case and it's still in perfect condition. Highly recommend! I also want to mention I've had to contact ESR for a couple issues I've had over the years and they always respond and fix the issue.

reviews.title: It's from ESR, so you know it's GOOD!
reviews.body: Since I posted this review, and used the case on my new iPhone, I realized that while I love the case, I don't honestly love clear cases. So I have now purchased the case in Frosted Orange, which for me is just a more pleasing color combination. The buttons are still clicky, the case just as protective and I LOVE LOVE the Stash Stand. If there was one thing, I'd change, I would like the buttons to be separate, not built into the case itself. Building the buttons into the case, leaves an opening above and below the button, which could let dust get in between the case and your iPhone, but this isn't unusual and isn't really an issue. Otherwise, I just LOVE this case, even more so in Frosted Orange. Here is the original review I wrote: OK, so Apple hasn't even formally announced the new iPhone's coming, but I know I'll be getting the Pro Max version and I like to be prepared for a new iPhone well in advance of it's arrival. I was very pleased to see ESR already offering them for the 2025 models (likely to be called iPhone 17), so I went ahead and ordered a Pro and Pro Max in clear as we'll get both when we can preorder them. The case appears very well made as you'd expect from ESR as they are one of the really good case makers for iPhone. It's your typical Polycarbonate back, with TPU sides, which are grippy. ESR buttons are usually very clicky, but I won't know how they work on the new phone till it's in hand. I currently own iPhone 16 Pro Max and when they first came out, I bought a couple cases, none of which had a dedicated Camera Capture button built into the case. But when I got a case with a dedicated Camera Capture button, I realized that for me, it's mandatory on ALL future cases. And this case from ESR indeed has a Camera Capture button built in. ESR says this case is scratch resistant and that's really good as scratches do annoy me. But its certainly NOT scratch proof, so keep that in mind if buy this case. They also suggest the TPU sides of the case are anti-yellow, which is an added benefit. Only time will tell on that as eventually, TPU will yellow. Also built into this ESR case is what they call a Stash Stand. It actually surrounds the camera surround and is made of Zinc Alloy. It hides seamlessly, but when you pull it out, it turns into a stand you can use to prop your phone in either landscape or portrait orientation. The only question I have overall with the case is the camera surround is completely made of Polycarbonate, with precise sized openings for the cameras themselves. Not that this is a problem, but if dust get inside the area, it might be annoying as I'd need to remove my phone from the case to blow any dust out. Again, time will tell on this. Otherwise, while there are surely going to be lots of case options for the new phones this year, I can say without question that buying one from ESR is always a great choice in a case which is better made than lesser priced cases and it will provide excellent protection for an expensive iPhone with 3X Military Grade Protection.

reviews.title: Protective case that isn't very heavy, with handy stand.
reviews.body: I recently upgraded to the iPhone 17 Pro Max which is the nicest iPhone I've had to date, and I've had them all. I knew I wanted to get strong protection but was worried because even on its own, this is a large, heavy phone. I have the iPhone a little over a week, and have tried at least 10 cases, all different price ranges. And I already had to replace the screen protector because I dropped it without a case on 😡. My last iPhone had an ESR case I liked and used throughout its life so I wanted to try this brand again for the 17 Pro Max. I got both the Classic and Cyber to compare them. reviews.title: Great MagSafe Hold & Premium Look without the Premium Price Tag
reviews.body: Finding a solid case for an iPhone SE that actually includes strong, reliable MagSafe compatibility can be a bit of a hunt. I picked this up looking for an everyday protective cover that wouldn't break the bank, and straight out of the box, it delivered exactly what was advertised. It offers an incredible value compared to high-end name-brand cases that cost three to four times as much. Real-World Details & Performance The fit on the phone is absolute perfection—it snaps on snugly and feels almost like a factory-custom cover with no loose edges or awkward alignment. The translucent matte finish gives the phone a very clean, high-class aesthetic that looks much better in person than standard clear TPU cases. Functionally, the MagSafe magnets are surprisingly strong. Magnetic chargers and accessories lock into place firmly with zero slipping. It has already survived a few accidental drops around the house without a scratch to the phone or the case itself. While I've only had it for a short time—so long-term durability over months of heavy use remains to be seen—the initial build quality feels remarkably sturdy. Pros & Cons Pros: Strong MagSafe Hold: Magnets align perfectly and grip chargers securely. Custom Fit: Wraps precisely around the phone without bulk or gaps. Classy Aesthetic: Translucent back gives it a sleek, high-end look. Unbeatable Value: Delivers the protection and features of expensive cases at a fraction of the cost. Proven Drop Defense: Handled initial drops smoothly with great corner protection. Cons: Unproven Long-Term Wear: Too early to tell how the TPU border and translucent back will hold up against daily friction and yellowing over time. Final Verdict If you need a reliable, attractive daily case and aren't putting your phone through extreme hazard environments (like heavy construction or intense outdoor sports), this is an absolute winner. I would easily buy this again or pick one up for my kids' phones. Highly recommended for anyone wanting full MagSafe functionality and sleek style on a budget!

While I've only had it for a short time—so long-term durability over months of heavy use remains to be seen—the initial build quality feels remarkably sturdy. Pros & Cons Pros: Strong MagSafe Hold: Magnets align perfectly and grip chargers securely. Custom Fit: Wraps precisely around the phone without bulk or gaps. Classy Aesthetic: Translucent back gives it a sleek, high-end look. Unbeatable Value: Delivers the protection and features of expensive cases at a fraction of the cost. Proven Drop Defense: Handled initial drops smoothly with great corner protection. Cons: Unproven Long-Term Wear: Too early to tell how the TPU border and translucent back will hold up against daily friction and yellowing over time. Final Verdict If you need a reliable, attractive daily case and aren't putting your phone through extreme hazard environments (like heavy construction or intense outdoor sports), this is an absolute winner. I would easily buy this again or pick one up for my kids' phones. Highly recommended for anyone wanting full MagSafe functionality and sleek style on a budget!

Is this case perfect or the best?! Not even close, but is it more than enough for some like me and a good fit for the 8? Yes, especially if manufactured correctly!

reviews.title: Good value
reviews.body: This case looks much better in front of you than a picture can render. I have the Product Red iPhone XR and this is the red case. The color comes very close to the color of the aluminum frame and looks like part of the phone. At first glance it doesn't look like there is any case at all! The red color is a shiny, metallic red as opposed to the matte red color of the iPhone frame. It does not clash where the phone's color can be seen in the cutouts and it nicely compliments the color on the back of the phone! Contrary to what another reviewer said, this case does indeed have a lip for basic screen protection. If you lay your phone face down on a perfectly flat surface with this case on, the screen will not contact anything. That being said, it is minimal by design. If you think you may be tossing your expensive phone around in places where the screen could be impacted perhaps you would be better served with a more robust case. This case is a great value for what it is! It complements the phone's styling. It will protect your phone from scratches on the back and sides. I had an iPhone 6 Plus with no screen protector installed on the glass for four years. The only protection was the lip provided by the various cases I used. The glass never got more than the most superficial, barely visible marks in that length of time. Totally worth it to me for the arguably better user experience of the naked glass screen. Even the most pricey tempered glass screen protectors do not match the buttery smooth touchscreen experience in my opinion. My fingers do not slide the same way. Anyway, the glass on the iPhone XR is significantly tougher than previous phones and I don't anticipate a problem. I offer that information only to illustrate that, with proper care in handling, you can rock an inexpensive, minimalist case with no issues. It should be noted, as another reviewer has said, that the back of this case is NOT perfectly clear. The phone can be seen but there is a pattern or texture which is noticeable if you hold it to the light just right. Not a deal breaker at all for me. You can still showcase the beauty of your XR with this case but it could be an issue if you require a perfectly clear back. I think this pattern may have something to do with durability and I doubt it will be an issue to most users. There is a color coordinated lip to protect the camera lens and I love the custom color coordinated cutout for the flash and mic modules in the back. So many XR cases simply have a huge opening that looks like it was designed for a dual camera setup. I like the extra attention to detail. One caveat: The fit is snug. If you are like me and frequently take you case off for thorough cleaning or want to rock a different case for that day, care should be taken when removing this case. The iPhone's aluminum frame is slippery and you could launch your phone out of your hands! I bought several cases together to compare. The Ranvoo case is nearly identical to this one. That one is much easier to remove because it is ever so slightly thinner. It has the same attention to detail in the cutouts and the same pattern in the "clear" back. The tradeoff is there is virtually no raised lip to protect the screen which is why it's easier to remove. Both products are good for what they are. This Torras case is a remarkably nice product for the money. With proper care it could be the only case you need but at this price, it will be a nice option in your iPhone's wardrobe.
