reviews.title: Looks Great!!!
reviews.body: Snug fit with my iPhone 17 Pro so it protects my phone quite well and I’m quite happy with it. Seems to be durable as I have dropped my phone a couple of times I’m very surfaces and so far, I haven’t seen a crack anywhere. Quality seems to be solid so far but only time will tell. Feels very slick and smooth, but maybe too smooth as it has been known to slide quite easily. There is a protector for the front screen (which I did not purchase), but I decided against it as I have discovered front screens reduce the phone‘s ability to detect commands with my finger after time has progressed and dirt/detritus builds up behind the screen after a certain length of time. I was concerned at first that the edge of the case on the back where the lenses are located would raise the phone too high and not allow charging when the phone was laying down on a charge mat, but that was not the case. Although, I did discover that exact positioning is important as just laying it down doesn’t always mean the phone is charging. So, I had to make sure to watch the screen when I wanna charge to make sure the mat and the phone aren’t position to charge when needed. All in all, this is a pretty solid product and I haven’t seen any yellowing in the plastic case as of yet, but it’s only been a couple months since I’ve been using it so maybe after a year I’ll reassess again. If there was one thing that would bug me about this case, is the raised lip of the back of the case surrounding the lenses. There was already a raised area on the phone for those lenses and this case just makes it that much more pronounced. I can only guess that the raised lip area on the back of the case is to further protect the lenses, but that also makes it harder for easy positioning for charging, and makes the phone bulkier when being placed into a pocket or bag. Still, this protects my phone and does what I want it to do so the raised area on the back is a minor issue that I can live with for now. Would I get another one? Hmmmm, maybe. Too early to tell at this point. But I won’t say no if something better comes out on the market.

Overall I would 100% recomend this case, Otterbox has again outdone themselfs.

reviews.title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
reviews.body: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

reviews.title: Amazing (typical) Otterbox performance
reviews.body: I work in trades so I wanted something that would protect my phone but not make it feel like I have a scrap 2x8 in my pocket. Also being in trades it has gone through its fair share of abuse and after having this for a little over a year now the only damage I can report is some cosmetic scratches, dings, a small non important piece of plastic as well as the rubber flap that goes over the charging port ripped off (though I'm to blame on most of that...). Long story short I told myself I would get a new phone when my current iPhone 8 dies. In desperate attempts to speed that up without being too blatant (as I've now had this phone for easily 6-7 years now and I'm ready for a new one) I've thrown this thing across rooms, out of second story windows, off roofs and ladders, etc. I think you get the point... Fortunately (or unfortunately) it has protected my phone through it all. The only things I have against it though is that the opening for the charger does give some trouble to the thicker aftermarket chargers (e.g. I have a Ryobi lightning charger that's thicker to supposedly protect it but it still charges with some "convincing"). In an attempt to handle that I ripped off that rubber flap that I mentioned before (no, that solved nothing but I felt better in the end). NOTE: It actually was starting to rip off slowly through use about 6 months in but I just expedited that process. The other point is that after a year of use (and abuse) its texture has gone pretty smooth so the grip isn't anything to marvel at but it does its job. I somewhat handled this by cutting a bunch of grooves with a utility knife but I can understand others not wanting to follow suit. TL;DR - Doesn't impede in screen or button usage. Great protection in a smaller and sleek design. May have some problems with charger clearance if you have really bulky aftermarket chargers. Notes for the picture: Mostly here to show the missing rubber flap that would usually cover the charging port. There was a think plastic piece that would go right below it and create a hole that the flap would fit into but that broke off as well. Most damage is through my abuse (for example the bottom left corner) but for the most part it's still in working condition. You can also see my "custom texturing job" I did on the back lol. Does it look pretty? No. Is that my fault? Absolutely.

reviews.title: Great, not too bulky, yet very protective case - Just avoid Amazon shipping!!
reviews.body: For the money especially, this is a great case. Unlike the defender series or others like it this doesn’t have the P.I.T.A. two-sided case that locks together and is difficult to remove. Some reviews say it’s hard to put on, they’re clearly doing it wrong as it’s VERY easy. It’s a 2 part design, so while it comes together, it’s key to put the rubber part on the phone before snapping the hard plastic cover in place. No doubt people saying it’s a tight fit tried both at once. That’s more difficult and puts strain on the plastic. I’m the worst about dropping my phone. ai must have dropped it (iphone 8) at least 75-100 times minimum, and I don’t even worry about breaking anything anymore. The lip of it sticks out just enough to protect the screen, and the dual layering is ultra shock absorbent. It’s also pretty thin considering the amount of protection. I gave a 4 for durability and sturdiness as over time the outer plastic snapped on me and the inner rubber cover has a few worn areas, but at $20, replacing wasn’t particularly bothersome and it certainly lasted a good 6-9 months of hard use - better the case than my screen! Still a 5 in total as sometimes something has to break, and so perhaps it’s better being a little less sturdy. To anyone asking, of course it fits a 7, there is no big difference in the shape of 8 and 7. Idk if the lip would protect the plus as well since the screen is bigger, but that’s an overall risk the Plus phones have. Finally, I wish I could rate Amazon delivery separately. If you live in a city apartment building or even a house and won’t be home, they don’t bother reading delivery instructions (which always has info to access my mail room / lobby). It’s probably Amazon’s fault for having impossible schedules, but the drivers will *sometimes* try to buzz once (not always), then ignore the delivery instructions and leave the box outside if you’re not home or can’t answer. When I wondered where my replacement case was, a quick review showed some lady walking by, noticing the pile of boxes left, and took a couple small packages on top before walking quickly off, one of course was mine. Almost more infuriatingly, customer service put it down to “delivery error” and said they’d blame the shipper.. yet Amazon is the shipper. So they blame themselves and do nothing to fix it, and outsourced customer service means people that can only answer a few basic questions before they get confused and off script. This time they promised me they were working with delivery drivers to fix the problem, yet it’s been happening for at least 2 years. If my neighbors didn’t look out for each other and bring in anything left outside, much more would have been stolen by now. And still they have my sensitive door access info, which I don’t give out lightly.. and never use it. How it’s cheaper to replace these items than just fix the problem is beyond me. My advice, if 1-day delivery is an option, is to buy it alone so as not to make the $35 minimum and let UPS handle it, since their drivers would never leave packages out on a city street (they also take note of info like door codes, how crazy). It’s to the point where if I see Amazon shipping I dread it and have to try to stay home. At the very least a notification saying the package is outside for anyone to take would be a start. That’s enough about Amazon shipping, just on my mind since the first order got stolen. UPS safely brought the replacement though

reviews.title: Great case, but watch your charging cable.
reviews.body: I see the case has undergone a slight re-design since my original one. It come with in soft inner rubber shell with an outer hard rubber shell. I guess that's to better absorb impact. The original one they were molded together. Now the inner shell appears to be removeable. That said, it seems to be well made. It's a tight fit to get the phone in. The buttons line-up where they should, so they are functional. Someone mentioned in another review that they liked the dust cover for the charging port. For me, it's a a love/hate relationship. I love the idea of keeping it closed when not charging, but since the "hinge" part of the flap has a strong reflex to close, I have to keep my phone motionless while charging or the pressure the lid has will cause the cord to pop-out just enough to stop charging without visual queue to know it happened. I actually get better results on a cheaper and thinner cord, but then it wears out the cord faster. So, for sturdiness, I give this 5 stars. But overall, due the the aforementioned charging issue, I give it 4 stars. Also, the outer case is a bit slippery, I wish it had better hand grip material, but workable if you know that.

reviews.title: Great clear case with a ring stand.
reviews.body: This is the 3rd Torras case I have bought for my 17 Pro Max and I think this one will be the keeper. The clear has a very different texture to what I imagine the black and blue cases with opaque plastic sides feel like. It has more grip. The clear looks really nice with a silver 17 Pro Max. And the ring stand has so far held up very well. It’s the first time I am using the O style instead of Q style 360 stand. It is not as stiff as the Q style which is a bit of a bummer, but a big plus is you basically can’t accidentally try to close this the wrong way and break the stand. Anyone who has used the other style will understand what I mean. I’ve had several small drops with this case on and my iPhone 17 Pro Max remains flawless so it is at least good for some drop protection. It isn’t the slimmest case but it is slimmer than the non-sports versions of this case. The back is hard pc and the sides are tpu but it is a very hard tpu. It feels almost the same as the back but not quite and has that very slight bluesh tint which I believe is a sign that Torras is using some type of anti-yellow tech here. No idea how long it will last but it looks great several weeks in. (Edit: we are now several months in and the case still looks as good as the day I bought it! Absolutely no yellowing) I do wish Torras offered better colors for this exact style (with this tpu vs the opaque plastic sides). On their website the only other options for this style are wacky colors I don’t think any sane person would want. I’d happily buy a fourth Torras case if they offered this style in a dark purple or even just the whole thing smoke grey (again with tpu sides).

reviews.title: Fabulous case and stand, ring grip is not for me
reviews.body: Positives: I really wanted to like this case, but I'll be returning it. It's well made, felt durable and protective. The bumpers on front and back felt like they'd protect my screen and cameras from drops onto flat surfaces. I liked the ring for the kickstand ability, and LOVED it for the magnet! It was strong enough to stick vertically on my fridge, and I have confidence it could stick well on chargers or car holders. Easy to install and easy to use. The 360° ring is fabulous. Negatives: My big hangup was the ring. I've used a PopSocket for years, and have gotten used to holding my phone passively for long periods of time. The ring was very difficult to adjust to, and I really tried. It was uncomfortable no matter how I entangled or rested my fingers. The ring is thin, so I guess it was the concentrated weight of the phone that dug into my skin. TLDR; Would recommend if you're wanting to use your phone more for watching videos, or resting against a table top. But if you plan to hold it a lot, might not be for you either.

reviews.title: Trust the Drop Rating, Don't Test It. TESTED: Bike drop tested. Perfect.
reviews.body: I bought this case because of the shock-absorbing rubber material integrated into the frame, and hopefully that will work out when I eventually drop my giant, heavy phone. Reminded me of Mous cases with that shock material, and even better this clear case isn't $85+shipping. The only thing keeping me from giving this case a 5-star review is I don't necessarily trust the durability because the case is so thin, it doesn't pass the eyeball test. However, I do trust that the product will keep my phone in tact, I just don't want to find out. EDIT: Riding my bike through a parking lot, hit a speed bump, it flew out of my jersey pocket and tumbled onto asphalt. Totally works. Hit all 4 corners, no scratches, no cracks even on my screen protector. Changing review to 5 stars. This thing is thin, and also the real deal. Almost want to buy a 2nd one in case they ever stop making it. Great news to prevent drops, all outward materials are very grippy and have a reliable feeling in the hand. The button action is very nice too, very easy to press both the power and volume buttons; you don't feel like the phone is going to rocket out of your hand when you try and turn your phone on, like the Speck Presidio case I returned. The main reason I tried so many cases was button action, and this case is great. Floating buttons FTW. Also, the camera is further protected than most cases with a little extra material in the lip. The ridge goes far enough past the 3-lens array you can visually see it protruding past the cameras, unlike other cases I've tried so far where it looked questionable. No question here, you're not putting your cameras down on the table. Keep in mind, we're talking like an extra 0.02" of material making the difference here. Don't worry, it doesn't show up in your ultrawide. The blue is also a great compliment to the Pacific Blue phone. It's close enough that it blends in spectacularly, my favorite part being the blue on the frame showing through the clear outer coating. It reminds you of the true color of your phone, which you lose if you get a case with black edges. I don't only want to see the blue when I put the phone down, I want to see the blue when I'm using the phone too. I'm already covering up the blue stainless steel frame of the phone itself. Overall, great case with shock-absorbing material around the frame. A little thin, but very grippy and protective of the camera. Button action is tremendous. You'll be very happy with the blue case if you have a Pacific Blue phone.

reviews.title: same quality as always
reviews.body: As someone who has a history of accidental phone drops (and let's be honest, who doesn't?), investing in solid phone protection is not just a preference, it's a necessity. The OtterBox phone case I recently purchased has once again proven why this brand is synonymous with top-tier durability and peace of mind. This case is an absolute tank, and if you value your phone's survival, look no further. Design & Build Quality (5/5): My OtterBox case feels incredibly robust and well-engineered right out of the box. The multi-layer design, typically combining a hard outer shell with a softer inner slipcover, provides excellent shock absorption. Despite its protective qualities, it doesn't add excessive bulk, maintaining a surprisingly comfortable grip. All ports, buttons, and cameras are precisely cut, ensuring full functionality without compromise. The materials feel premium and durable, built to withstand daily wear and tear. Protection (5/5): This is where OtterBox truly shines. I've had several unintended "gravity tests" since putting this case on my phone – drops on concrete, tile, and even a minor tumble down some stairs. Each time, my phone emerged completely unscathed. The raised edges around the screen and camera offer crucial protection against direct impacts when laid flat. The sealed port covers (on some models) are also fantastic for keeping out dust and lint, which can be a common issue. If you're prone to dropping your phone, or if your lifestyle demands extreme durability, this case is an absolute must-have. It shrugs off impacts that would shatter an unprotected phone. Ease of Use & Accessibility (4/5): While the protection is phenomenal, the case is snug (as it should be for protection!), so taking it on and off isn't a five-second job. However, once it's on, it's on to stay, which is precisely what you want. Buttons remain tactile and easy to press, and access to the charging port and speakers is unobstructed. Wireless charging also works perfectly with the case on. Value for Money (5/5): An OtterBox might seem like a significant investment compared to flimsy, cheap cases, but consider it an insurance policy for your expensive smartphone. The cost of replacing a cracked screen or a damaged phone far outweighs the price of an OtterBox. It's an investment that pays for itself the first time it saves your phone from a catastrophic drop. Overall Impression: The OtterBox phone case delivers exactly what it promises: unparalleled protection. It's a rugged, well-built, and highly effective guardian for your device, giving you complete confidence that your phone can handle whatever life throws at it. If you prioritize durability and want to avoid the heartache (and expense) of a broken phone, I wholeheartedly recommend an OtterBox. It's a small price to pay for genuine peace of mind. Pros: Unrivaled drop protection: Seriously tough! Durable, high-quality materials. Precise cutouts for ports, buttons, and camera. Excellent shock absorption. Good grip, despite its sturdy build. Protects against dust and debris (on models with port covers). Great long-term value, saves on costly repairs. Cons: Can be a bit bulky for some preferences (a trade-off for protection). Not the easiest to remove/install frequently. If you want your phone to survive, get an OtterBox. It's that simple.

reviews.title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
reviews.body: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

It feels great in the hand, with a solid overall build and grippy sides that help prevent accidental drops. The magnetic hold is also strong and works perfectly with MagSafe accessories. While that makes it easier to slip into a pocket and more comfortable to carry, it might not offer quite as much protection as the thicker models. That said, it still feels durable and well-made. reviews.title: Great rugged case. Need Yellow option
reviews.body: Nov 26 2023 Update: Ive had and used this case exclusively for over 4 months now. Im a guy who carries there phone everywhere and I work alot in dirty, sandy, wet areas. This case still looks new. HINGE PROTECTOR: Still funtions as new. FRONT DISPLAY COVER: Still functional althogh it has some marks on it. HOLSTER: I dont use the holser as much as I thought I would but it has functioned well when used. PROTECTION: GREAT I've dropped my phone a few times with no signs of damage to the phone or the case. Dirt intrusion inside the case has been minimal, this has been a problem with other cases in the past. COLOR: PLEASE, PLEASE MAKE A BRIGHT YELLOW COLOR AVAILABLE. Us working guys need a bright yellow option so when the phone is dropped on the work site it can easily be found, also great for those with impaired vision to find where they put their phone down. GENERAL OBSERVATION: I've seen a comment here that states this case is slippery, that has not been my experience at all. The case has a textured design that makes holding it effortless. I dislike those rubbery cases because it's been my experience they are very difficult to get out of the front pocket of my jeans, they don't last and they let dirt and sand get into the case interior. FINAL COMMENT: This case is well worth it price, buy it. ORIGINAL REVIEW: 12 2023 Received my Flip5 few days ago along with samsung ring case. Was not pleased with the ring case as unlike the Flip4 ring case the ring only attaches to one side-the back side of the case, offers no hinge protection at all and relies on two sided tape to hold front on. Might be fine for some but not for really active users. This Beatle case was not cheap $36 but it seems well designed and of good quality. FIT: The Flip5 fits in it well. Phone functions well in it, all buttons work well, USB C cables all fit. PROTECT: Good corner and camera protection. Much easier to keep a grip the phone. HINGE: covers the entire hinge, sturdy but dose not automatically close when the flip5 is folded. It's a ez movement of the index finger to snap it closed, and it seems to stay closed until the phone is opened. OPEN-CLOSE: The phone opens and closes easily, in-fact more easily then with out any case as it's easier to get a grip with this case on it, however unlike the original Motorola DPC500 Microtac flip phone, the Flip5 can't be easily opened one handed with or without this case, although it can be done with this case, it's takes a little practice and nimble fingers. KICKSTAND: Kickstand works well with phone when vertically oriented but not as well when horizontally as the hinge protector interferes and makes it rock a little, it still works only will be a little lopsided. FRONT SCREEN PROTECTOR: touch still works well however the screen protector plastic seems a bit soft. Mine already had some small marks on it when it arrived, hopefully the screen protector can be ordered separately and easily replaced from Supercase. Another reviewer here wrote that he put a tempered glass screen saver on the front display and removed the one from the supercase, sounds like a good workaround. HOLSTER: again seems well designed and well manufactured. The Flip5 fits well in it when oriented with the front screen inward toward the hip and the usb port down. Easy to get the phone in and out of the holster and it seems quite secure when in it. While I can remove the phone from the holster one handed its not a fluid movement, where it is a simple task when using 2 hands, quick, simple and effortless. Returning the phone to the holster is a simple one hand operation, it snaps in and you know it's secure. The belt clip is robust, the clip rotates and is about 1" wide, should accommodate a belt of 1-5/8" wide, seems easier to use with the clip towards the front, but gives you the choice of any position 360°. I don't think anyone will need to worry about the phone falling out of the holster. Also seems comfortable to wear even if you have some belly roll, Dwane Johnsons abs not required. OVERALL FIRST IMPRESSION: I like this case, I'm glad I purchased it, I'd buy it again. I was concerned about it being to big, it's not. Good Job Supercase!

reviews.title: Great protective case option for Galaxy Z Flip 5 but could use more improvements.
reviews.body: This case worked for me balancing design and protection for my Galaxy Z Flip 5. Love the carbon fiber and sturdy design. How the case will hold up only time will tell. Only concern is the flap for the hinge protection and how it will handle a drop. Overall, I feel this case should provide adequate protection for accidental drops from my hand or desk should it ever happen. My biggest dislike is the plastic front small screen protector. It does not have glass like clarity and does not handle cleaning well. It build up oil, dust, and grime overtime that I cannot remove thoroughly with alcohol as they adhere to the plastic screen which drove me nuts. I removed the front screen plastic protector and installed a tempered glass screen protector in place to complete this case to my tastes. Also note, I was concerned this case would not fit with the camera tempered glass protector that came with my glass screen protector but to my surprise it did and looks even better as it filled in the gaps when I installed it around the camera lens without the camera lens glass protection installed. With this case, some of my durable type Anker USB-C cables could not plug in all the way, but my Ugreen USB-C cables worked. Be aware not all USB-C cables will work with this case. Likes: - Carbon Fiber look and Tough Design Aesthetics - Protection - Integrated Kick Stand Dislikes: - Front cheap feeling screen plastic protector that does not hold up well to oil, dirt, and cleaning overtime - Kickstand works, but has sharp edges that pokes. Would prefer if corners and edges were smoothed out - Not all USB-C cables may be able to plug in to charge with the case installed - Hinge flap protection feels vulnerable to breaking if dropped at certain angle as it is kept closed by a spring and not magnets. Only time will tell.

reviews.title: It does the job very efficiently, I'll gladly trade damaging a $30 case over a $1000 phone any day.
reviews.body: I can't believe that there are one star and two star reviews when the phone case does its job - protect the phone when dropped. Drop it far enough or hit it the right direction and any case will break! The trick is to NOT have the phone break! Plus the complaint about having to flip the hinge protector down. I just opened and closed my phone now and my hand on the back automatically closed the hinge cover. It's really a non-issue, yet listed as a complaint. I've never left it open. I've dropped my phone a few times without any damage to case or phone. Here is my evaluation after a year of use. The Beetle cover makes the phone a bit thick when in pocket, but that's part of the price of having some protection, like the 1980s big bumper blocks for the 5 mph crash thing. I could live without the stand, which could thin the case a bit. Still it does its job. Still better than having one of the giant phones that no longer can fit in one's front pants pocket. The Flip fits about any pocket, even with the Beetle case. I need that as a motorcyclist. But no way I'm having even the smallest phone fit comfortably in the side pocket and no way I'm sticking my phone half hanging out of a back pocket. So the Beetle does the job as well as possible. The case also is just wide enough making it not fit in my ProClip phone holder in my vehicle, almost but not quite fitting. But that's more of an issue for the ProClip than the phone case. Nice part is that the lower portion of the Beetle case is that it slides off easily and the phone fits the ProClip then. So I can live with the situation decently. Again, the stand could go away for me, maybe a case that doesn't have it, but I know that features like that sell others on the case. I forgot that it was even there, never using it. I've recently tossed the belt clip thing, not having ever used it either. Be nice without the extras for my use. So, in spite of minor issues, it does deserve a five star for the past year I've had it. I sure hope if I drop my phone that the case will break first. I'll trade $30 for $1000 damage any day.

reviews.title: Great case until the stand breaks.
reviews.body: I bought the green case in September 2023. It is now May 2024. I've only dropped my phone two or three times since having it in this case, and I must say that it does do well for protection from a fumbling drop. However, I expected the stand to last longer than it has. The little plastic thingies that attached the stand connector to the bottom of the phone case have both broken off and now that part is just in the way to where I can't use my stand now. I'm really disappointed because this is advertised as such a tough case that can handle anything. This hinge is the Achilles heel of this case. So instead of spending more money on the same case, I'm just going to use my hot glue gun to glue that little flap up to the stand so that I can still use the stand part, but it won't be in the way now. All in all, this is a great case until that hinge breaks and renders your stand basically useless. Quite the disappointment for what I paid for it.

reviews.title: Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!
reviews.body: If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. I’ve tested a lot of MagSafe cases, and this one feels like it was engineered, not just manufactured. Protection That Isn’t Just Marketing The first thing you notice is the Air-Guard corners. They aren’t just decorative; they create a visible cushion that actually absorbs impact. I’ve already had one "heart-stop" moment where my phone slid off a high counter onto a tile floor, and it literally bounced. Not a scratch on the phone or the case. The "Military-Grade" label actually feels earned here. The MagSafe Connection (HaloLock) ESR’s magnets (they call it HaloLock) are notoriously strong—often stronger than the official Apple cases. • The "Snap": When you bring it near a charger or car mount, it grabs hold with a very secure click. • Reliability: I use a heavy MagSafe power bank and a wallet attachment; neither budge even when I’m walking or the car hits a bump. It’s rated for 1,500g of holding force, and you can definitely feel that extra "tug." Design & Utility Depending on the model you get, many of these come with the Stash Stand around the camera. This is a game-changer: • It protects the lenses when closed. • It’s made of a high-quality zinc alloy that doesn't feel flimsy. • It works in both portrait (for scrolling/FaceTime) and landscape (for videos) without blocking the MagSafe ring. The Build Quality The back is a hard, scratch-resistant polycarbonate that stays clear much longer than cheap TPU. The sides have a nice matte grip that prevents that "slippery soap" feeling. It adds just enough "heft" to make the phone feel protected without doubling its thickness. Pros: • Superior Magnets: Best-in-class MagSafe strength. • Corner Protection: Air-Guard tech is legit for drop safety. • Tactile Buttons: They remain clicky and responsive, not mushy. • Raised Edges: Significant lip around the screen and camera for "table-top" protection. Cons: • Tight Fit: It’s a very snug fit, so it takes a little effort to get the phone out if you swap cases often (but that’s also why it’s so protective!). Final Verdict: This is the "Goldilocks" of cases—it’s tougher than a standard clear case but way sleeker than a traditional bulky rugged case. If you value your phone's trade-in value and use MagSafe accessories daily, this is an absolute no-brainer. 5/5 Stars.

reviews.title: Case That Feels Like a Favorite
reviews.body: I picked up this tortoiseshell case when I wanted something protective for my new iPhone 15 Pro but with a vibe that fits my Hawaii laid back style. I liked that it uses sustainable materials and still looks chic rather than plain. The goal was to have something practical that would shield the phone and still feel good in daily life. In everyday use it holds up well. It fits snugly, buttons and ports are easy to reach, and the grip feels secure without being bulky. The built in magnets keep MagSafe charging reliable and compatible with accessories, which makes a lot of sense for me since I use wireless charging most days. What stood out is how the look stays stylish without shouting, and the case resists scratches while handling minor bumps. The texture helps me grip the phone more securely, and the pattern hides fingerprints better than I expected. A small caveat is that it does add a bit of heft and a touch more bulk than ultra slim options, so it takes a moment to adjust when slipping the phone into a pocket. Still, the trade off is worth it for the protection and the easy MagSafe use. Overall I’m really happy with this case and I’m giving it five stars for the combination of style, practicality and peace of mind.

reviews.title: Yes, Some Of Us Still Use the iPhone 13 ;)
reviews.body: I am still using an iPhone 13, which is kind of funny considering we are getting close to the iPhone 18 generation. I do not see much reason to replace a phone that continues to do what I need, especially when a decent case helps keep it looking almost new. This magnetic case has been a good match for that purpose because it protects an older phone while adding features that make it feel a little more current. The fit around my iPhone 13 is precise, and I like the coverage around the edges and corners. After years of owning the phone, keeping scratches, dents, and other everyday damage away from it matters to me. A case cannot stop every possible accident, but this one gives me enough protection that I am comfortable carrying the phone throughout the day without treating it like something fragile. When I take the case off, the phone underneath still looks remarkably good for its age. MagSafe is another reason I enjoy using this case. My magnetic chargers and other accessories connect without having to remove anything first. The magnetic hold feels secure during normal use, and charging has worked as expected. Being able to continue using newer MagSafe accessories is especially useful because it keeps my iPhone 13 compatible with the way I use my other devices today. The kickstand may actually be my favorite part. I watch videos, news, and other content on my phone fairly often, and being able to set it down instead of holding it the entire time is convenient. I can place it on a desk, table, or countertop and watch hands-free while doing something else. It is also handy during longer videos when holding a phone eventually becomes annoying. The case feels substantial without making the iPhone unnecessarily cumbersome. The buttons remain easy to press, and I can reach the ports without fighting against the case. It gives an older phone a refreshed appearance while preserving the familiar size and feel that made me keep the iPhone 13 in the first place. Overall, I have been very satisfied with this case. We may be approaching the iPhone 18 era, but my iPhone 13 is still going strong, and this helps me keep it that way. Between the protection, MagSafe support, and kickstand, it gives me several reasons to continue using a phone that still has plenty of life left in it. Pros: • Helps keep an older iPhone 13 looking remarkably well preserved • MagSafe support works nicely with magnetic charging and accessories • Kickstand is extremely useful for watching content hands-free • Worth the value Cons: None

reviews.title: Good basic phone case, with stand and see-through backing.
reviews.body: The case I have is for the iPhone 13/14, and it is currently installed on my personal iPhone 14. It fits snugly and is thinner and less bulky than the one it replaced. The back of the case is mostly made of translucent plastic, so you can see the Apple logo, and the base color of the phone case (mine is black, so no real whoop there). I like that it is a bit slimmer than the one I previously had, and it fits a bit better in my pocket now. This case also has a small flip out stand (see photos below), so it can be used to stand the phone at an angle for hands-free viewing. My third-party Qi wireless charger also works fine with this case. The hole for the Lightning charging port is a decent size and still allows use of a Lightning cord for charging. It is a bit snug, but seems slightly more roomy than the previous case (I do not have to fiddle as much to get the plug inserted (like the last case). The case has a slight ridge around the face of the phone, and a raised lip around the camera section on the back side of the phone. This is to prevent the screen and the camera lenses form coming into contact with the table surface. The front ridges are smaller than my previous case, but good enough as long as the table surface is not rough or too uneven. This case is nothing outstanding, but it does work well and fits the need for a basic protective case for the phone.

reviews.title: Deciding between the Belkin and Anker Charger? Get the Belkin!
reviews.body: Over the past few months, companies like Anker and Belkin have introduced new charging stations that support Qi2.2 charging at 25 watts. Unfortunately, these products come with an extremely high price tag, as is common when they are first introduced. When spending such an exorbitant amount of money on a 3-in-1 charger, you want to make certain you carefully research all the available products to make the most informed choice. I bought both the Belkin MagSafe charger and the Anker Prime 25-watt charging station. In the end, I returned the Anker and kept the Belkin. The Anker was the most tempting purchase, given its unique design that included a display screen built into the stand that provided data on the exact charging wattage of each device. The screen also includes a clock and information on the current cooling level. I must admit, Anker's unique overall design and incorporating a screen make for a highly innovative product. The problem is, the Anker did not perform as expected. While charging my Apple Watch Ultra, it would only charge between 0.5-1.0 watts. My AirPods would only charge at about 3.4 watts max. Both these devices should be charging at 5 watts, but they never reached that level. Anker claims that "For watch models that support fast charging, the power can reach 3W - 5W when the battery is low. However, the power fluctuates during the charging process and does not remain at a high level continuously." However, even when my Apple Ultra Watch was near empty, it never reached 5W charging while on its stand. Despite the absence of a built-in screen, I noticed that the Belkin MagSafe Station charged my watch at a faster rate. My iPhone 16 Pro Max charged at a variable rate, which is normal for these chargers. You should only expect 25-watt charging when the phone is below 50%. Any charge above that will be slower. Another thing that I like about the Belkin over the Anker is its elegant design and small footprint. The stand looks very classy, has a padded charging base, and doesn't move when quickly grabbing and removing my phone. Anker also remained in place under the same circumstances. A win for both products. At the time of this review, the Anker costs $40-$100 more than the Belkin. I wouldn't mind paying more for the Anker if it performed as well as the Belkin, which, for me, did not. Furthermore, I had several frustrating issues dealing with Anker support when returning my unit and obtaining a refund. What I learned here is that just because a company puts out what appears to be a high-tech product with a pretty screen doesn't make it the better choice. If it doesn't perform as advertised, the consumer loses. I am having a much better experience with the Belkin. It's a solid charger that works as promised.

reviews.title: Worth the price!
reviews.body: I had 3 less expensive generic 3-in-1 chargers for just over a year... they worked okay, but I was never completely happy... then about a month ago the weak magnets started to cause my Apple watch to start off charging but then lose the connection and let the watch die overnight. So I started looking for better solutions and found this one. First, I generally believe that "brand name" vs. "generic" is often just an excuse to charge more. I really balked at $129 for a charger. In the end however, I decided to take a chance and took the plunge. WOW! What a difference! First, the magnets are much, much stronger... dropping connectivity will likely not be something I ever worry about again. And because the connection is so much better, and coupled with the huge (power wise) 45 watt adapter... all 3 of my devices (iPhone, Apple watch and AirPods) all charge much faster and reliably, even with all 3 on the charger at once. Second, the information I found regarding the cooling fan and a "hum" appears to be overblown... I can't hear a thing! (But I also have other devices nearby that I can hear so it could just be drowned out; except, even with my ear right next to this charger I could not hear anything. So, don't let the fear of a fan scare you off. The only negative thing I can think of is that the arm for the phone is adjustable, you can lay the phone completely back to 90 degrees so that the screen points up (or very close to 90 degrees) if you want. It seems to be a friction kind of adjustment, I do not see any way to tighten or loosen it... it holds position pretty well so far, but I could see this becoming an issue later. And the folding arm for the phone will be useful if I ever travel with it... fold it down for compactness and through it in a suitcase... perfect. Overall, not the least expensive by far... but so far, the quality is the best I've found. I'll wind up with one or two more over time most likely (unless something even better comes along).

The only charger I still reach for when I need the absolute fastest charge is Apple’s 45W charger. It’s excellent for an office setup and helps keep everything organized. Setup was simple and the build quality feels durable and well made. A couple of downsides: the magnetic connection can feel a little loose at times, and you have to get your phone centered just right or it may slide off. It also makes a bit of noise, which can be distracting when you’re trying to focus and get work done in a quiet office. It’s definitely on the expensive side, but for the convenience of charging three Apple devices at once, I think it’s worth the price. If you’re invested in the Apple ecosystem and want a clean, all-in-one charging station, this is a solid choice.

reviews.title: Great charger, but weak MagSafe magnets hold it back
reviews.body: This Belkin charger is a great product overall, but it has one significant drawback that I don’t think should be overlooked. First, the positives: my Apple Watch Ultra 3 fast charges as advertised, and so does my iPhone. The charger itself is lightweight and compact, and it comes with a 45W charging brick and a nice rubber-overmolded cable that feels high quality. From a charging and build-quality standpoint, I’m very happy with it. Unfortunately, there’s one issue I can’t get past: the magnetic strength of the MagSafe phone mount. The magnets simply don’t feel strong enough. It doesn’t take much of a bump to knock the phone off the charger, and that’s something I think potential buyers should be aware of. I believe the weaker magnets may actually be an intentional design decision. Because the charger itself is so lightweight, stronger magnets could cause you to lift the entire charger when trying to remove your phone. I can understand the reasoning behind that tradeoff, but I still think the magnetic hold is too weak in practice. Belkin appears to have tried to compensate for this by adding a silicone surface to the charging area to provide additional grip against the back of the phone. Unfortunately, it doesn’t provide enough friction to make up for the weaker magnets. Personally, I would have preferred a heavier base combined with stronger magnets, even if it added some weight to the product. If Belkin had addressed this, I genuinely think this would be a 10/10 charger. As it stands, I’d give it a 7/10. The charging performance is excellent, the included 45W power adapter and cable are nice, and the overall design is very good. The weak magnetic hold is really the only thing keeping me from loving it. You may think this won’t bother you, but I would seriously consider it before buying. A surprisingly light bump can cause the phone to fall off the charger, and for something you may use every day for years, that matters. If you’re comparing this with the Anker Prime, which costs roughly $30–$40 more, the additional cost may be worth considering if it provides a more secure magnetic connection. Over several years of daily use, $30–$40 isn’t much of a premium to avoid an annoyance you’ll potentially deal with every day.
reviews.body_en: This Belkin charger is a great product overall, but it has one significant drawback that I don’t think should be overlooked. First, the positives: my Apple Watch Ultra 3 fast charges as advertised, and so does my iPhone. The charger itself is lightweight and compact, and it comes with a 45W charging brick and a nice rubber-overmolded cable that feels high quality. From a charging and build-quality standpoint, I’m very happy with it. Unfortunately, there’s one issue I can’t get past: the magnetic strength of the MagSafe phone mount. The magnets simply don’t feel strong enough. It doesn’t take much of a bump to knock the phone off the charger, and that’s something I think potential buyers should be aware of. I believe the weaker magnets may actually be an intentional design decision. Because the charger itself is so lightweight, stronger magnets could cause you to lift the entire charger when trying to remove your phone. I can understand the reasoning behind that tradeoff, but I still think the magnetic hold is too weak in practice. Belkin appears to have tried to compensate for this by adding a silicone surface to the charging area to provide additional grip against the back of the phone. Unfortunately, it doesn’t provide enough friction to make up for the weaker magnets. Personally, I would have preferred a heavier base combined with stronger magnets, even if it added some weight to the product. If Belkin had addressed this, I genuinely think this would be a 10/10 charger. As it stands, I’d give it a 7/10. The charging performance is excellent, the included 45W power adapter and cable are nice, and the overall design is very good. The weak magnetic hold is really the only thing keeping me from loving it. You may think this won’t bother you, but I would seriously consider it before buying. reviews.title: Nice looking charger with very annoying quirks/bugs
reviews.body: It's cool that this is the "official" charging dock that Apple endorses. When it works, it works well and it feels quality, with all hinges feeling sturdy. Time will tell after folding it hundreds of times whether the hinges will hold up, but I feel optimistic. This is one of the few options you have unfortunately for 25W charging if you have a newer iPhone, as they tend to be really expensive. Watch charging works fine and reasonably well, but it seems like the pad doesn't shut off and the watch continues to get warmer as it sits fully charged. Phone charging doesn't seem to have this issue, but it might be whatever cooling tech they have keeping it room temp-ish. The part I hate the most about it is the airpod charging area. It has an annoyingly bright white LED that lights up when you put it on the charger, and it takes forever to start charging, if it even does that. I've woken up contless times to my airpods not having charged at all, even though I put it down as correctly as possible. Even when I move it back and forth on the charger it takes forever to finally register the airpods are on there and frankly it's a really poorly functioning charger that tarnishes an otherwise decent dock. Even when it does successfully charge, it does the same thing where the charger doesn't shut off after fully charging and the airpods are really warm when I pick the case up. All in all, a decent charger but don't expect the airpods charger pad to work well. Frankly, I expected better for almost $100 and I'm pretty disappointing overall.

reviews.title: Heavy, but powerful charger
reviews.body: This is a somewhat heavy (weighs about a pound), but powerful battery. I don't mind the weight, I expect that from a 20k battery. It feels solid and well built. I like the display and how it shows the negotiated voltage and amps so you can see what it is doing. I also like that it has a trickle charge mode for lower power devices like my watch and earbuds. Most batteries will shut off because there isn't enough of a power draw, in trickle charge mode the battery will not shut off for 3 1/2 hours. Please note that they recommend that you use a minimum 65 watt charger to charge the battery. You can use less power, but the battery will take longer to charge. With the more powerful charger it takes a little over an hour to fully charge. One day my M4 MacBook Air was down to around 25% and my phone was around 40%. I plugged both into the battery at the same time. I charged my phone to 80% and computer to 100% and the battery was down to about 10% remaining charge. The computer was drawing around 60 watts the majority of the time. One thing that has left me curious is that I have yet to see it either receive or draw more than 3 volts @ 20 amps since it says it is capable of 5 volts. Both my charger and computer should be capable of 100 watts, but I also know that devices negotiate with the charger so it doesn't bother me that it is less.

reviews.title: Travel Essential- Great Value Purchase!
reviews.body: I originally purchased this portable charger for an upcoming camping music festival, but I’ve ended up using it far more often than I ever expected. It’s small enough to fit in my purse, so I find myself grabbing it all the time. It has saved me in airports while traveling, at hotels when I forgot a wall charger, and even during nights out when my fiancé realizes his phone is almost dead. I’ve even used it to recharge a portable speaker after it ran out of battery one evening. The built-in charging cables are probably my favorite feature because we no longer have to remember extra cords. It has connectors for both my iPhone 14 and my fiancé’s iPhone 17 Pro, and those are the only charging ports we use anymore. I also like that the battery pack itself can be recharged in multiple ways, which makes it even more convenient. Pros: * Holds plenty of charge for multiple devices * Fits easily inside a purse or small bag * Built-in charging cables eliminate the need to carry extra cords * Works with both my iPhone 14 and my fiancé’s iPhone 17 Pro * Can also charge other devices like portable speakers * Great for travel, hotels, concerts, festivals, airports, and everyday emergencies * Multiple ways to recharge the battery pack itself * Excellent value for the price Cons: * Takes a very long time to fully recharge (at least half a day, sometimes longer) * Slightly bulkier than some ultra-compact battery packs Overall, this has become one of those products I never realized I needed until I had it. It has bailed us out on so many occasions that I now keep it in my purse almost all the time. The long recharge time is definitely its biggest weakness, but once it’s fully charged, it lasts a long time and has been incredibly reliable. For the price and convenience, I would absolutely recommend it.

reviews.title: A Game-Changer for On-the-Go Charging
reviews.body: This power bank stands out for its practicality and well-thought-out design. Right from the start, the packaging gives a premium feel, and it’s great that a USB-C cable is included for charging the device itself. Small details like this make a difference, as not all power banks come with the necessary cables. One of the features that impressed me the most is the built-in cables. They sit completely flush against the body of the power bank, which means they don’t stick out awkwardly. This is a huge plus, as it prevents them from catching on things when placed in a pocket or bag. This also makes carrying the power bank much more convenient, as you hardly notice it’s there. The LED display is another standout feature. Unlike power banks that use tiny LED dots to indicate battery levels, this one has a clear and easy-to-read digital screen, showing the exact percentage of charge remaining. This removes any guesswork and makes it much easier to know when it needs recharging. It’s a small but extremely useful detail that makes a big difference in daily use. Build quality is excellent. The power bank feels robust and secure in hand, with a well-constructed design that doesn’t feel flimsy or cheap. A feature that I particularly appreciate is the curved edges. It might not seem like a big deal at first, but having owned power banks with sharper edges in the past, I can say that those can be uncomfortable to hold, especially when using the phone while it’s charging. The rounded design of this one makes it comfortable to grip and prevents any discomfort when carrying it around. Performance-wise, it delivers exactly as advertised. reviews.title: One of those products that just quietly works
reviews.body: I bought this charging station for my wife as she is deep in the Apple ecosystem (I'm on the Android side), and she’s been using it for about 6 months now. She's happy with it. It’s one of those products that just quietly does its job every single day without any issues. The design is clean and modern, and it looks great on her nightstand. The MagSafe thingy holds the iPhone securely in place, even with a case on, and the Qi2 charging is surprisingly fast and reliable. She usually puts her phone on at night, and it’s fully charged by morning without fail. It also charges her Apple Watch and AirPods at the same time. It’s so nice to have one sleek unit instead of three separate chargers and a mess of cables. The non-slip base is a nice touch too, though I wish it stuck to the surface a bit more, sometimes it doesn’t keep the whole thing as steady as I’d like. Maybe the whole stand is a bit too lightweight... Just for fun, I tried putting my Samsung Buds on the bottom charger, and it actually worked! So it's not limited to Apple devices, which is a nice bonus. If you’re deep in the Apple ecosystem (or live with someone who is), this is a fantastic addition to your/their setup. Highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Easy to use, great product!
reviews.body: When you move into the apple ecosystem, it is usually done first with an iphone, then with airpods and finally with an apple watch. When it gets to that stage you usually have two or three cables to charge all these devices, which is no longer convenient. Before buying the product I was a little unsure, as it is an expensive product. But it was totally worth it, just for the ease of being able to charge the three products, which I mentioned above, quickly and easily, without having to be handling two and three cables (even without the need to handle multiple outlets) which greatly simplifies the cable management for those who seek visual simplicity. The only thing not convenient is the material of the base with which the product is made, as it tends to "absorb" dust, dirt, grease etc etc in a very easy way, it is not an easy product to clean but with a little patience can be left as new. If I had to improve something it would be the above mentioned and additionally in the black version I would also try to leave the Magsafe Pads in black color, for those who have a dark palette of colors on their setup. In my case I used the product with an Iphone 13 (normal), Airpods 3 and a watch series 8 and it charges these three devices without problems. The convenience here is that since it is a product that allows you to charge these gadgets so easily, this allows me to rarely run out of battery or forget to charge any of them.

reviews.title: Works as intended
reviews.body: So I just bought a brand new one two years, but it’s because I never registered the warranty for our first one. This is basically a one piece kit that is a great starter for battery charging for most kinds of automotive and marine batteries. It’s very simple to use, and the one reason our last one stopped functioning is because of built in fail safes. In this case: my wife and I were washing our camper and this got wet and then got some dirt on it, it got through the water resistant seal and the charger could detect this. The great news is the charger will literally cease to function if it has become damaged. It will give a flashing red light, and you cannot put it into Force Charge mode. The only downside is unless you have a multimeter, you may not know that it has become damaged internally. I figured it out because of the mode not working, and it wouldn’t charge any batteries. The fuse was fine. So make sure you register this when you get it. It does the job and the only way you know it’s working is because of the status light, as it is beyond quiet. It’s basically a plug with the clamps for the battery terminals, so it is easy to store and carry around. I highly recommend this charger if you need something simple without a lot of functionality, just don’t leave it exposed to the elements.

reviews.title: Little Miracle
reviews.body: Okay, I did NOT expect this little thing to work, but it did and might for you IF you have patience. My Grandfather who was MoAT (Mechanic of All Things) owned back in the day what I thought were REAL chargers, they were so big and heavy they had to be put on wheels and rolled around, they had giant switches that'd illuminate and while I'm probably purely imagining this they were plugged into 220-volt outlets. This thing fits in the palm of my hand, just as pictured, smaller than most mobile phones. "Huh," I said, "this should be comical." I hooked it up and, as others have said, figuring this thing out is NOT straight forward, the instruction manual is weak to say the least, the good news is, as I found, there are many intrepid experimenters who, like me, bought it on a whim and did some trial and error which it'd seem 99% of them got the thing to work to their needs, just like me hence, I'm taking the time to write this review. What this lacks in coherent features or instructions it makes up for it in the end by eventually (boy I mean eventually) getting the job done, for that honestly I'm giving it a generous five stars, because it did what I wanted it do against all odds, just like the Phil Collins song. ("Just take a look at my car now, 'cause it's finally starting here.") To get the to point, this took TWO WEEKS to charge a completely dead battery in a completely dead system. If it'll help anyone I own a 2000 Lexus RX300 that is, in fact, drinking age, if I could find a small ute-friendly bar to have a couple with me of which, in terms of trusty old friends, this boring beige over beige has been one of my best now with over 270,000 miles with no reason, per the Lexus dealer, to give up the ghost before 300,000. Toyota quality and then some with only wearables and maintenance needed BTW, the car has only had one issue, eating car batteries every four or so years. Being a cheap bastard and Lexus parts are pricy I've chosen battery over a slightly-off generator which brings us to the recent hullabaloo and the need to be the Noco Genius, though it'd prove not straightforward as I hoped. Hooking up the Noco Genius you get a slowly blinking light, like a heartbeat, that will tell you nothing really. Also there's a force-charge setting where you hold the button (there's only one button on the whole thing, this thing is basic) it supposedly will force a charge into a battery... this doesn't work, at all. After some digging it supposedly only does this if a battery is below some arbitrary limit which, my battery was completely dead, kaput, nada, force charge only made the 6V light go on which, apparently, is what others experienced. Point being, don't hold you breathe. I kept trying to charge the battery but it didn't budge, didn't budge, didn't budge, then I had a thought and said to myself "self, what if I unhook the battery, THEN charge it?" As in, is it because it's also hooked to my car hence current is going other places? Mind you, this thing is only one (1) amp, that's very little, if you're looking for a quick charger or something to charge and jump your car, this ain't it, have you seen the size of this thing? reviews.title: Seems pretty good so far
reviews.body: I have two of these. They are not exactly the same model (I think one of them is an older version of this model). The older one, I have had in the garage for several years to keep the batteries in the cars up when they are not driven very often. Some people say these are not for car batteries and I won't argue with them but the one I have out there definitely keeps the battery in my 2001 Corolla charged. And in fact, we had an incident where someone left a dome light on in that car and drained the battery to the point to where there was absolutely no response from anything electrical in the car. We started the car with a jumper pack, pulled it in the garage and connected it to the Noco and let it do it's thing. That's been at least a year and that battery is still going strong in that car. I purchased this one off Amazon to use on various SLA batteries I have around. I have two jumper packs with 18 AH SLA batteries in them. One of them had been sitting in the garage for several years due to the fact last time I tried to charge it, it wouldn't charge. I was going to order a new battery for it from Amazon but I figured I kind of needed an extra charger for SLA batteries anyway and this Noco unit was less than the price of a new battery for the old jumper pack. I figured it would be a long shot to try and charge that old battery and get any more life out of it but I thought it would be interesting to see what would happen. Can't be a tougher challenge for a SLA battery that's been sitting in a garage dead for years. Well, that jumper pack doesn't exactly have easy access to the battery but after some fighting with it, I got it open and popped the clamps on the terminals. The charging light began to pulse and after about a day, went green (was still pulsing but was pulsing green). It finally went solid green. I left it plugged in a few days. I have one of those miniature inverters that plugs into a cigarette lighter (that particular jumper pack doesn't have a built-in inverter but does have a cigarette lighter plug). So I plugged it in and tested it with a clamp light. So far, seems to be working about as well as you'd expect for a jumper pack battery that is probably approaching ten years old now. Or maybe better than you'd expect. It's only a 12 watt LED in the clamp light but my main goal was to get every last bit of value from any SLA batteries that I can. I'd definitely have a use for a small inverter like that in a power outage and if you have an extra battery that you can plug it into, so much the better. I believe the built-in charger on that jumper pack just may have died or was not up to charging it's battery for whatever reason. Remains to be seen how much more life I can get out of such batteries but it's definitely worth the price paid.

reviews.title: Reliable. Battery was ready when needed
reviews.body: In January 2026, the temperature dropped to -25°, without wind-chill, over 3 days. The electricity went out. I needed to start my emergency generator, and the battery was dead. I start the generator every month and run it for 1 hour to maintain the battery. This battery was only 7 months old. I was lucky. I had a battery for the sump pump in case of emergency, and I was able to use it. Here it is the end of August 2026, and we've been experiencing thunderstorms daily. Last night the electricity went out. I've had the battery on the NOCO Genius 1 since January. I installed it and the generator started right up. The battery has been on the charger for 7 months, so if there was a problem with the charger, I'd know by now. The charger is reliable and it protects the battery. Choose the right one by amperage of your battery.

reviews.title: Works with a REALLY low battery
reviews.body: My wife has a 1995 Mercedes SL320 that she did not drive all winter and well into the new year... when she opened the garage door and tried to start it the battery was dead, drained by MANY months of the old style mechanical clock running without the car being started so the battery could charge My (brand name withheld) several year old 10 amp 'smart' charger would not work because the battery was too low to be detected So, I looked for a different charger with a FORCE mode to get a dead battery to start charging... I connected this one at about 7PM at night (it never would go into force mode, since the battery had 'just enough' charge to be detected) and when I get in the car at 7AM the next morning the battery had enough of a charge for the dash lights to come on, but not enough to run the starter The PDF I downloaded shows that this 1 amp charger will take 'about' 23 hours to charge a 30 AH battery... the battery in her SL320 is a 100 AH model, so I will let the charger run for another full day before I try to start the car again (or maybe 2 days to get the charger enough time to work) So far, this charger is doing exactly what I need (I thought about a larger model to charge quicker, but decided that slow charging was good enough... she hasn't driven her car since last Fall, so she can now wait a day or two)

reviews.title: Very easy to use, but it should include printed instructions
reviews.body: Very easy to use, but it should include printed instructions I bought this because my car battery had gone dead after the car had been sitting for a while. I wanted something I could connect and leave charging rather than just jump-starting the battery again. So far, I’ve been impressed with how simple it is to use. I connected it to the battery, selected the appropriate mode, and it began charging without any fuss. The indicators make it easy to see what it’s doing, and at the moment it seems to be working exactly as intended. My one criticism is that there is no conventional instruction manual included. Instead, you scan a QR code and go online for the instructions. That worked fine for me, but I don’t think it’s a particularly good choice for a product like this. Not everyone has a smartphone readily available, and battery chargers may be used in garages or emergency situations where having basic printed instructions in the box would be useful. Other than that, my first experience with it has been very positive. It’s compact, straightforward to connect, and remarkably easy to operate.

reviews.title: Works perfectly, just a nerrow range of uses
reviews.body: First, this charger is fantastic at charging fast. I have had no problems with charging any phone fully in half the time my old wireless charger took. The caveats: The charger has two states. It is either fast charging, or it is off. It will not work at all in a car because it doesn't supply enough amps. It won't work with wall plugs under 25 watts (5v, 5A). It doesn't just refuse to fast charge, it won't even power up. So this only works if you have a high-amperage adapter, or a high power computer port. The other issue is weight. The device is small and surprisingly light, but that means if you pick up your charging phone, the charger comes with it. Great in a car, but it won't work there. Terrible on a nightstand or desk. I'm constantly prying off the charger just so I can use the phone. So great in any situation where the above two issues don't matter.

So this only works if you have a high-amperage adapter, or a high power computer port. The other issue is weight. The device is small and surprisingly light, but that means if you pick up your charging phone, the charger comes with it. Great in a car, but it won't work there. Terrible on a nightstand or desk. I'm constantly prying off the charger just so I can use the phone. So great in any situation where the above two issues don't matter.

reviews.title: No more fluff in the port excuses
reviews.body: I’ve always found charging my phone overnight a bit annoying – constantly trying to get the cable in the right position, and still waking up with a low battery more often than I should. This MagSafe-style charger has completely removed that hassle. Now it’s just a case of placing the phone down and letting it attach magnetically, which feels a lot more reliable than fiddling with cables in the dark. Since using it, I’ve stopped waking up to a nearly dead phone, which is exactly what I wanted from it. It comes as a simple package with the charger itself, a USB-C cable and a USB-A converter, so you’ve got a bit of flexibility depending on what plug or setup you’re using. The magnetic alignment is strong enough that the phone stays in place easily, even if you move it slightly on the bedside table. What stands out with this set is having two chargers. It makes it easy to keep one at the bedside and the other in another room or take it for travel, so you’re not constantly unplugging and moving things around. It also supports faster wireless charging, so it doesn’t feel slow compared to wired charging overnight, especially when paired with the right adapter. It’s more than enough for overnight use and day-to-day top ups. Case compatibility is decent too. It works through most standard slim cases without issue, but for the best magnetic hold you’ll want a MagSafe-compatible case or one with built-in magnets. Thicker cases do weaken the snap-in feel a bit. Price wise seems to be normal for the price of 2. Overall, it’s a small change that makes a big difference in day-to-day use. No more cable faff, no more guessing angles – just put it down and it charges. Exactly the kind of simple upgrade that makes life easier.
