reviews.title: Carga rápida, tamaño mínimo y magnífico precio. Totalmente recomendado
reviews.body: Si estás buscando jubilar los dichosos cables de una vez por todas y te llama la atención el nuevo estándar de carga inalámbrica Qi2 y tienes dispositivos que aceptan la carga inalámbrica, quédate por aquí porque te voy a contar detalladamente mi experiencia real con este pack de 2 cargadores magnéticos. Después de estar trasteando con ellos a diario, usándolos tanto en el escritorio de casa como llevándomelos de viaje, aquí te dejo mi análisis a fondo, sin rodeos, con lo bueno, lo genial y también con esos pequeños detalles que conviene saber antes de lanzarse a por ellos. 📦 ¿Qué nos encontramos en la caja? De primeras, lo mejor de este producto es que es un pack doble. Te vienen dos bases de carga inalámbrica magnética de color violeta oscuro (tampoco es demasiado oscuro). Visualmente llaman la atención ya que tienen un perfil ultra delgado (apenas unos 5 milímetros de grosor) y pesan poquísimo (unos 54 gramos). El chasis es metálico, lo que le da un toque premium muy limpio, y el cable viene integrado con conector USB-C y un acabado trenzado que se nota bastante resistente al trote diario (dobleces, tirones en la mochila, etc.). ⚠️ Un detalle crucial de inicio: El pack no incluye los adaptadores de pared (los enchufes). En la caja solo vienen las dos bases con sus cables. ⚡ Rendimiento y Velocidad: ¿De verdad carga a 25W? Aquí hay que ponerse un poco técnicos, pero de forma sencilla. Estos cargadores cuentan con la nueva certificación Qi2 / Qi2.2, que es básicamente la evolución universal del sistema MagSafe de Apple. Promete hasta 25W de potencia máxima. En el día a día, con los teléfonos compatibles más recientes, la velocidad se nota un montón. En apenas 30 minutos te puede plantar la batería en torno al 50%, siendo notablemente más rápido que las típicas bases inalámbricas antiguas de 15W. Pero ojo, que aquí viene el "truco" de la potencia: 1. El enchufe importa: Para exprimir esos 25W de punta, necesitas conectar la base a un adaptador de pared de 30W o superior con salida de 12V (el típico cargador rápido potente que uses para la tablet o el portátil). Si lo conectas a un enchufe antiguo de menos de 20W, la velocidad caerá en picado. 2. Carga desde el portátil: Si eres de los que, como yo, viaja mucho y conecta la base directamente al puerto USB-C de tu ordenador portátil en una reunión o cafetería, la potencia real se verá limitada por la del ordenador (suele dar entre 10W y 15W). Sigue siendo comodísimo para mantener el móvil con energía mientras trabajas, pero no irá a su velocidad punta. 🧲 El imán y el ajuste magnético: El cargador lleva internamente imanes de neodimio N52. En dispositivos de la manzana o teléfonos preparados nativamente para alineación magnética, la experiencia es súper cómoda: acercas el teléfono por la parte trasera, se "pega" solo en la posición exacta milimétrica y empieza a cargar. Es ideal para la mesita de noche porque no tienes que andar tanteando a oscuras a ver si ha encajado en la bobina. Dado que es mucho más pequeño (aproximadamente la mitad) que las bases de carga inalámbrica, si tu dispositivo no tiene la alineación magnética has de asegurarte que realmente está bien colocado, ya que además no tiene ningún led que indique que está cargando, sólo puedes saberlo por lo que te indica tu dispositivo. A tener muy en cuenta con Android y fundas: • Si usas dispositivos como los últimos Samsung Galaxy o Google Pixel, o incluso si llevas el iPhone con una funda convencional, necesitas obligatoriamente que la funda sea compatible con MagSafe/Qi2 (las que llevan el anillo magnético integrado). • Si intentas usarlo con una funda de plástico normal o de piel gruesa sin imanes, el agarre se debilita muchísimo y el teléfono se soltará con cualquier movimiento. En algunos terminales Android sin funda o con carcasas inadecuadas, el imán puede sentirse algo flojo, así que el secreto para que no se mueva nada es una buena funda magnética. 🥶 Gestión de temperatura y seguridad. Al ser tan sumamente compacto y delgado, la disipación del calor es puramente pasiva a través de su carcasa metálica. Durante las cargas rápidas intensas, vas a notar que el cargador y la trasera del teléfono se calientan bastante. Es un comportamiento normal en la carga inalámbrica de alta potencia, aunque en ciertos modelos de teléfonos más pequeños o compactos (como ediciones SE o similares) esa sensación de calor puede ser un poco más acusada de lo esperado. Por suerte, incluye chip inteligente con protección contra sobrecalentamiento y detección de objetos extraños, por lo que corta el flujo si detecta anomalías. 🔍 Lo que se echa en falta (puntos a mejorar) Para ser totalmente honestos, hay un par de detalles de diseño que podrían haber redondeado el producto: • Sin indicador LED: El disco no tiene ninguna lucecita que te confirme visualmente que está pasando energía. Tienes que fiarte del pantallazo o la vibración de tu propio móvil al colocarlo. • Tamaño reducido: Como el disco es tan minimalista y delgado si no usas una funda que guíe el imán de forma automática, al principio te puede costar un par de intentos centrarlo perfectamente sobre la zona de carga trasera a la primera. ⭐ Conclusión: ¿Vale la pena? Rotundamente sí, sobre todo por la versatilidad del pack de dos unidades. Por el magnífico precio que tiene, es ideal para dejar uno fijo en tu zona de trabajo habitual (el escritorio de casa o la oficina) y meter el otro directamente en la mochila o el neceser de viaje. El color violeta oscuro es super original y elegante, rompiendo con el aburrido monopolio de las bases habituales de siempre. Si tienes claro que necesitas un adaptador potente en casa para sacarle los 25W y usas fundas magnéticas adecuadas (o tu dispositivo tiene alineación magnética), este kit te va a dar una comodidad muy importante en tu rutina diaria, ahorrándote el engorro de andar buscando y rompiendo cables físicos a cada momento. Una compra de lo más práctica y recomendada.

reviews.title: Great if your charge port has commitment issues
reviews.body: I use this with my iPhone 8 because sometimes the charge port is finicky so I have to use wireless charging, and I gave the second one in the 2 pack to my cousin who has an iPhone 14 Pro Max. The magnet connection is strong, it snaps on tight and doesn't shift. The slim design is great for when it's stuck to the back of your phone and you're using it so it's not bulky in your hand. For my iPhone 8, there's no magnets in the phone, so it doesn't attach, but it works fine as a normal Qi pad if I centre it and it doesn't make my phone hot. It charges my phone at 7.5W. That's an iPhone 8 limit, not the charger's fault. My cousin's 14 Pro Max gets 15W, since 25W Qi2.2 only works on iPhone 15 and newer. No wall adapters are included so you need a 25W+ USB-C PD brick to get fast charging on phones that support it. With my iPhone 8, a basic 10W brick is enough. If you use a weak adapter with a newer phone, charging will be slow. For the price of a 2 pack, it's good if you need a backup for port issues or want Qi2.2 speeds on a newer phone. The strong magnet is great for MagSafe phones, and it still functions as a standard wireless charger for older models.

reviews.title: Good value. Good product
reviews.body: I've gone through more charging stations than I'd like to admit, and most either take up too much room or require a tangle of cables. This one keeps everything much cleaner by charging my phone, Apple Watch, and earbuds in one compact unit. What impressed me most is how portable it is. When folded, it's small enough to slip into a backpack or carry-on, making it a great travel companion. I especially like that the charging cable retracts into the base instead of becoming another cord to wrap up before packing. The magnetic phone charger holds my phone securely, even in StandBy mode, so I can use it as a bedside clock while it charges overnight. My watch and earbuds also charged consistently without having to fiddle with positioning them over and over. The built-in lighting is a nice extra. I normally don't care for RGB effects, but it's easy to switch off if you prefer a darker bedroom. It's nice to have the option instead of being stuck with lights that stay on all night. The only drawback I found is that the built-in power cable isn't very long. If your outlet is tucked behind furniture or far from your nightstand, you may need to rearrange where you place the charger. A slightly longer cable would have made it even more versatile. Overall, this is a well-designed charging station that reduces clutter and travels well. It feels sturdy, charges reliably, and combines several useful features into one compact package. I'd recommend it to anyone looking to simplify their desk or bedside setup.

reviews.title: Great Angle Adjustment, and turns my phone into a clock
reviews.body: The adjustable angle on this charging station is what really sold me. Once your phone is set on it, you can tilt it just right so the display is easy to see, and I've actually started using it as a nightstand clock. When I wake up in the middle of the night, the motion wakes the phone display and shows me the time without me having to pick it up or fumble around. That angle adjustment is mainly what I use it for, though I can also see it being handy for propping up your phone to watch something while it charges. The flip up piece for the watch works great too. My older Apple Watch 6 fits on it fine and charges reliably every time. I've also used the front part to charge my AirPods, and that works well even with a small silicone case on them. Charging speed is right in line with other wireless chargers I've used, nothing faster or slower than expected. It folds down into a small cube that's easy to toss in a suitcase, so you have one single charger covering all your devices when you travel. Overall this is a great value since you're getting three charging stations in one, and I'm already thinking about picking up a few of these as gifts for some of the older kids later this year.

reviews.title: Decent bedside multi-device charging station for home or travel. Light is a bit bright/distracting.
reviews.body: The ANTBOOK Model Z1 charging station is a great space-saver that consolidates multiple cords and chargers into a single, compact unit for your tabletop or nightstand. While its built-in retractable USB-C cable makes it highly convenient for travel, it could be a bit short, extending only to a maximum of 25". The included 33W PD power adapter performs reliably. Thanks to a rubberized base and most of its 285g weight concentrated at the bottom, the station remains highly stable and stays firmly in place, though I do wish the magnet was a bit stronger to offer a more secure hold on my iPhone 11 (with MagSafe case; should be very adequate for iPhone 12 and up due to integrated magnets). The capacitive switch on the front, which allows you to turn on/off the light, is also not very responsive (at least on the unit I received), which can be frustrating (see my video). The USB-C output port on the back is a handy extra for charging a watch with its own attachment or another accessory, though it's noteworthy that the output is fixed at 5V and does not support 9V or 12V fast charging. For storage and transport, the station folds down into a cube. While it is not the most compact travel charger on the market, it is still very manageable. It supports MagSafe-compatible phones in both portrait and landscape orientations. It also features a built-in light, activated by a touch-sensitive toggle, which can serve as a nightlight or a charging status indicator -- showing an animated RGB effect when idle and a pulsating solid color while your phone is actively charging (strobing green while charging AirPods, blue while charging iPhone, or alternating between green and blue when both are charging). Unfortunately, the brightness is not adjustable, and I found the light to be too bright/distracting for a dark bedroom, though it does thankfully turn off automatically once your phone reaches a full charge, or you can just turn the light off altogether, as I've done. A slightly annoying quirk is that it goes back to the animated RGB effect in the event of a power failure, but maybe that's a helpful behaviour. Overall, the station functions as expected, simultaneously charging an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods wirelessly. While I am not certain it delivers true "fast" charging, it is more than adequate for overnight use. During my testing with an iPhone 11, AirPods Pro, and Apple Watch all charging at the same time, I noticed a current draw of barely 1A at 9V, which does seem a bit low, but it still gets the job done by morning.

reviews.title: Convenient travel charger with a clever cord, but has a few quirks
reviews.body: I grabbed this three-in-one charging station hoping to clear up the wire clutter on my nightstand and have an easier time packing for trips. It definitely succeeds at saving space, reliably charging my phone, watch, and earbuds all at the same time. The foldable design is incredibly compact, and the built-in retractable power cable is a fantastic idea that means I never have to remember to pack an extra cord. It even comes with the wall adapter, which is a great touch. That said, the execution isn't entirely flawless. The retractable cable can be a bit stubborn and occasionally needs some wiggling to wind all the way back up into the base. It also features a built-in light that defaults to a bright rainbow effect. While you can thankfully turn it off, the touch button can be a little unresponsive, and the light itself is just too bright to use as a bedside nightlight since you can't dim it. It also won't give you the absolute fastest charging speeds on the market, but for an overnight charge, it does the job perfectly fine. reviews.title: Compact 3-in-1 charger with a built-in nightlight
reviews.body: This 3-in-1 wireless charging station can charge an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods all at once, and folds down to a compact size that works well on a nightstand or for travel. It also has a 10W USB-C output port on the back which is useful for charging devices that do not support wireless charging. Phones can be charged at up to 15W, earbuds up to 5W, and watches up to 3W. There's a light built into the bottom of the unit that is operated with a touch button on the front. It can be changed from a night light mode to wireless charging indicator mode (blue for phone charging and green for earbud charging), when nothing is charging the light cycles between the colours. The USB-C cable is built into the unit and retracts when not in use, so there's no worry about forgetting to bring the cable. A 30W AC adapter is also included. The base has a non-slip finish to keep it from sliding around. The phone magnetic strength works okay with my phone case and holds it in place. A practical all-in-one charging station that charges up to four devices at the same time and I like the built-in retractable charging cable. I've used it on my nightstand and it helps keep it very tidy. It will also be great to travel with instead of having to take a number of cables and adapters.

reviews.title: A Versatile, Compact Charger With Great Feature Set
reviews.body: I’ve been using this for a little while now and it’s been a solid upgrade from the pile of chargers I used to have on my nightstand. The main reason I got it was to charge my iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods at the same time without dealing with three separate cables. It does that without any issues. I’ve tried it with an iPhone 15 and an older 13, a Series 9 Watch, and AirPods Pro, and everything sits properly and charges consistently. Nothing super fast, but reliable enough for overnight or desk use. The retractable cable is one of the better features. You pull it out to reach the outlet, plug it into the included 30W adapter, and then retract it when you’re done so there’s no loose cord hanging around. Keeps the whole setup looking a lot cleaner than what I had before. There’s also a small RGB light that you can change colors on or dim. I mostly leave it on a low warm setting at night so it acts like a soft night light without being distracting. You can turn it off completely if you prefer. Overall it’s compact, does what it’s supposed to, and the safety protections give a bit of peace of mind. Not the flashiest thing I’ve owned, but it solved the clutter problem and I haven’t had any problems with it so far. Happy enough with the purchase.

CHARGE DEAD BATTERIES — Charge batteries from as low as 1 volt, or use Force Mode to manually charge completely dead batteries down to zero volts. Perfect for recovering deeply discharged or neglected batteries.

reviews.title: Perfect for a second car that doesn't get driven often
reviews.body: I was hesitant to buy one of these because of the reviews about fires. Don't pay attention to those reviews. This little trickle charger keeps your car battery at full and in brand new condition. I read somewhere online that if you put a brand new AGM battery in your car like I did and keep this NOCO Genius10 hooked up, the battery can theoretically last up to 10 years because the NOCO will continuously keep it charged and repaired. It seems that my battery was not the problem with my car as the starter relay on the clutch needed replacing so now my car starts again. But I put in a new AGM battery anyways and won't have to worry about replacing it for another 7-10 years as long as I keep the NOCO attached when not driving the car for long periods of time. As for the NOCO functionality itself it has a couple buttons, one to choose what kind of battery you are using, regular 12V, AGM, or Lithium Ion. The other button I believe is for what kind of charge you want(trickle, decharge, repair) but since I have a brand new battery I simply keep it on trickle charge. The cord length is not very long so in order for my NOCO to reach my car battery and the wall socket in my garage I used a decent gauge extension cord. The instructions say not to use an extension cord but there is no other way since my wall outlet in my garage is too far away from the car battery. I keep a smoke detector next to the NOCO and battery just to be safe. I got the NOCO on sale during Prime Day so it is definitely a good value for the money. So far so good.

reviews.body: Purchased the NOCO Genius charger in hopes it would resurrect my battery. Un fortunately, it did not save my battery, but I cannot blame that on the charger. The only complaint I have is the lack of instructions. They were not minimal, there were none at all provided with the unit. Luckily, able to look on line and find plenty of videos, however, this does not negate the need for an instruction and care pamphlet. The unit feels solidly built and works as expected. While it did not resurrect my battery as it claims it can do (not in all situations), mine was 5 years old, lead acid and probably just to far gone for help. However, it is doing a great job charging my marine battery and using it to keep it charged until used again. I like it. Much more compact than the older styles and easily able to mount to a wall or post as a charging station. I would definitely buy again.

reviews.title: Pretty neat device, very capable as well
reviews.body: I have a battery charger made in the 1970s, inherited from dad that passed away in 2011. It was time for another one, and I was going to buy another Schumacher that weights about 15 Lbs. Was ready to pull the trigger and decided to see if something better was out there, thus buying a Genius 10 instead based on YouTube reviews. The Genius 10 was much larger and heavier than how it looks in the picture. The build quality is really good in my eyes, looks like tough ABS polymer, very nice cords with that good feeling wire jacket insulation. The new clamps are nice looking and very practical to me. It's heavy and awkward to store, so I bought the Noco case as well; I thought the other case was too small in size. I ran some test with it, on a 12V Honda Lead Acid and Group H8 AGM battery and was happy the results. It was more intuitive than the 1970s version I have with 30 amp boost that is scary to use. What I like with Noco or Genius, it's several tools in one unit, so every 3 or 4 months, I can use the Genius to check the status of all my batteries, well that is the plan at least. One neat thing, using the 12V output to keep a battery online while changing a battery, so the cars computer keeps running and doesn't reboot from removing the battery causing weird things to happen. I have no regrets in my purchase and bought the case to enhance it more. I think the price is reasonable as well considering what a $100 buys today.

reviews.title: Saved me from buying a new battery!
reviews.body: EDIT 2/26/24: I am now the blocks "AAA". Been helping people start their cars when jump starts with cables have not worked. Definitely handy to get other people out of an otherwise expensive pinch. I have a car battery that I purchased around 2016 (date of review 1/3/24). The car itself does not get driven much, at most 2-3 times a week no longer than 15 minutes one way. Throughout the years I've drained it by leaving the car lights on. Its always required a jump start after that to get going again. Recently I've been an idiot and been leaving my lights on more frequently. Eventually it required me to jump start everytime I wanted to turn on the car. It was becoming a hassle and I was about to call it quits and purchase a new battery until I came across Project Farm's review on battery chargers. This was at the top of the list so I figured to give it a shot. I was not disappointed! I charged it for 4 days straight, put it in my car, and it started right up. Not surprised considering it was just charged but the real test laid ahead. I was going to be out of town for two weeks and leave the car sitting. I came back two weeks later and the car started up, no hesitation whatsoever, as if it was a different battery! The NOCO Genius 10 saved me about $150-200 at least in a brand new battery. On top of that, I can now use it for other batteries in the event of any similar issues. The instructions on the other hand are a bit confusing and had to rely on YouTube comments to piece it together. For those who are confused at what to do, I did not do a 12V repair (function which this unit has) as it requires the battery to be completely charged first. All I did was charge it straight for 4 days uninterrupted. When first put on battery to the charger it will be in standby mode. You push (or hold depending on what you need) the MODE button to select your desired option. I was charging a lead acid battery so I selected 12V. The meter at the top slowly advanceD from each of the four bars until the final bar was pulsing green which indicates its charging to full (over 80% I believe). The green charging light continued to slowly pulse even on the 4th day but I took a gamble and disconnected it from the battery. For the battery to be 100% charged, the green light should stay solid. That means my battery worked 2 weeks later after sitting and it wasn't even at 100%. The unit can also force a charge on batteries that are extremely under voltage. Thats a separate setting that I haven't had to use yet. It can also charge AGM and Lithium but I believe the 12V repair function is only for lead acid. Unfortunately I had to go through 3 separate orders because the first two were from Amazon Warehouse and I encountered issues with both, consecutively. I ended up getting frustrated and just purchased a brand new charger. Pros: Solid build quality Excellent cable connections with weather covers Compatible with a wide variety of batteries Repair and Force charge batteries Cons: Poor instructions Charge is slow BUT I think thats how these chargers work TL;DR Try this first before rushing to get a new battery it is a good investment that can save you a lot of money

reviews.title: Funcionó muy bien en mi acumulador AGM (770CCA y 70AH)
reviews.body: El cargador llego en un día, el precio en Amazon esta elevado comparado con otros sitios sin embargo la recepción en un día me favoreció. Me lo recomendó un amigo que se dedica a la mecánica automotriz, mi camioneta apenas encendía, especialmente los lunes después de no usarla sábados y domingos, las primeras dos fotografías muestran el estado del acumulador (LTH AGM 48, 760CCA y 70AH) antes de usar el NOCO Genius10, básicamente parecía que el acumulador estaba bien cargado sin embargo se bajaba rápido y le faltaba potencia de arranque, después de conectarlo al Genius10 y dejar que realizara una carga completa (aproximadamente unas 4 horas y hasta que el led verde dejo de parpadear), para después correr el reparador por aproximadamente 4 horas más la batería quedo completamente restaurada, como se puede ver en las dos siguientes fotografías. Ya instalado de regreso en mi camioneta el arranque es inmediato y sin esfuerzo. La batería ya se había cargado antes con otros cargadores diferentes, pero no funcionaba bien casi de inmediato daba problemas en el arranque de nuevo y el SOH (state of health) seguía en los 80,s ahora es del 100%, así mismo el estado de carga (SOC) nunca llegaba al 100%... este cargado rehabilito mi acumulador con alrededor de dos años de uso, y que por descuidos míos se había dejado descargar al dejar accesorios prendidos en la camioneta en varias ocasiones. Lo recomiendo ampliamente.
reviews.body_en: The charger arrived in one day, the price on Amazon is high compared to other sites, however the reception in one day was in my favor. It was recommended to me by a friend who is dedicated to automotive mechanics, my truck barely started, especially on Mondays after not using it on Saturdays and Sundays, the first two photographs show the condition of the accumulator (LTH AGM 48, 760CCA and 70AH) before using the NOCO Genius10, basically it seemed that the accumulator was well charged however it went down quickly and lacked starting power, after connecting it to the Genius10 and letting it perform a full charge (approximately about 4 hours and until the green LED stopped flashing), and then the repairer ran for approximately 4 hours plus the battery was completely restored, as can be seen in the following two photographs. Once installed back in my truck, the start is immediate and effortless. The battery had already been charged before with other different chargers, but it did not work well almost immediately, it gave problems starting again and the SOH (state of health) was still in the 80s, now it is 100%, likewise the state of charge (SOC) never reached 100%... this charge rehabilitated my accumulator with around two years of use, and due to my carelessness it had been allowed to discharge by leaving accessories on in the truck on several occasions. I highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Reliable Smart Charger That Brought a Neglected Battery Back to Life
reviews.body: I purchased the NOCO GENIUS5 to maintain the batteries in vehicles that don't get driven regularly, and it has been one of those tools that quickly proves its value. Setup was straightforward. The included connectors are easy to use, and the charger automatically detects the battery and selects the appropriate charging mode. I especially appreciate that it can be left connected for maintenance without worrying about overcharging, which gives me peace of mind when storing a vehicle for extended periods. One of the batteries I used it on had been sitting for quite a while and was struggling to hold a charge. After connecting the GENIUS5 and allowing it to complete its charging cycle, the battery recovered enough to reliably start the vehicle again. While no charger can fix a battery that's physically damaged or completely worn out, this unit did a good job recovering a battery that I initially thought might need replacement. The charger itself feels well-built and the display indicators are easy to understand. I also like that it supports both lead-acid and lithium batteries, making it useful for multiple vehicles and equipment around the house. A few things prospective buyers should know: The 5A charging rate is ideal for maintenance and general charging, but it isn't the fastest option if you're trying to charge a large, deeply discharged battery in a hurry. The indicator lights are simple and functional, though some users may prefer a charger with a more detailed digital display showing voltage and charging status. Overall, this is a dependable smart charger that is easy to use, versatile, and well-built. Whether you're maintaining a seasonal vehicle, motorcycle, lawn equipment, or simply want a charger that can safely stay connected long-term, the GENIUS5 is a worthwhile investment. Helpful tip: If you're using it for battery maintenance, consider installing the included quick-connect lead permanently on the battery. It makes future charging sessions much faster and more convenient.

reviews.title: NOCO Genius5
reviews.body: I bought the Genius5 after neglecting a relatively new battery in my motorcycle. Due to weather and travel, I often have long gaps between rides. Unfortunately, one of these gaps was long enough to damage the battery. I didn’t realize that batteries need a minimal charge to avoid sulfation, and mine had become severely discharged. Although my NOCO GB40 starter worked fine, the battery wasn’t holding a charge even after a day of riding. Instead of immediately replacing the battery, I decided to try saving it with the Genius5. After charging the battery with the Genius5, I tested it with a battery analyzer, which reported it as damaged. I then ran the desulfation process, and afterward, the analyzer showed the battery was in good condition. I repeated the tests several days later to be sure, and the battery still appeared to be in good health. Now, I keep the Genius5 connected to my motorcycle whenever I’m not riding for more than a week, and I haven’t had any battery issues since. I still carry the GB40 in my panniers, just in case, but I haven’t needed to use it lately. Some notes on the desulfation process: The desulfation process seems to send voltage peaks, and you may hear some bubbling inside the battery. This happened to me, and from what I’ve read, it’s normal as long as there’s not too much bubbling and no vapors, heating, or swelling of the battery. The entire process takes a while, so it’s unrealistic to monitor it the whole time. However, I recommend watching it for the first 20 minutes to ensure the battery noises aren’t increasing. After that, you can leave it running while staying nearby, just in case something goes wrong. A final note on this process: because of the voltage peaks, I didn’t run it with the battery connected to the motorcycle to avoid any potential damage to the circuits. For regular maintenance charging, I do keep the battery connected. The Genius5 is designed to work with standard batteries, gel, and even lithium ones. The one I used was a Gel Yuasa, and I’m pleased with the results. I also purchased the NOCO cables (GC002 X-Connect M6) to make it easier to connect the charger without removing the seat. The cables were a bit expensive but seem well-constructed and are quite convenient. Final thoughts: If you have a vehicle that sits unused for extended periods, and this happens frequently, then this charger is ideal for you. However, if you only need it once a year or less, it might be easier and cheaper to disconnect the battery from the vehicle while you’re away to prevent discharging. For my use case, the Genius5 has been worth it, and I’d definitely buy it again.

reviews.title: Resurrected a dead battery overnight
reviews.body: My interstate battery went completely when I went returned from a 6 week trip. Tried jump starting by using my other car but failed. Noco is one of the few chargers that can charge a completely dead battery. Watched a project farm youtube video on car battery chargers ( see chart at 18m29s of the video) before buying. I purchased the 5A one due to time constraint ( charged 75% in 8 hours ). You can buy the 2A version or 1A version if you have all the time and just want to keep batteries fully charged. I let it charge overnight and had a fully functional battery in the morning. This happens to me whenever I go on long trips ( 4 weeks + ). With a rechargeable jump starter, you are limited by the battery life of the starter which is only 3-4 years after which most batteries fail. The wall charger hopefully will last a long longer. Saved me a lot of time - No need to drive the car around after jump starting to get some charge into the battery. Just charge overnight and done. Love it.
reviews.body_en: My interstate battery went completely when I went returned from a 6 week trip. Tried jump starting by using my other car but failed. reviews.title: Yeah so don't mix up your fused alligator cables if you buy different models
reviews.body: I bought a Genius1 and Genius5. The latter failed on first use due to my mistake mixing up the alligator clips during unboxing. I didn't look closely enough to notice that the 1 and 5 aren't just feature levels but are current ratings in Amps. The proprietary connectors are identical but the 1A unit has a 2A fuse and the 5A unit has a 10A fuse, and they're on the battery side of the connectors not the device side, so obviously the 2A fuse correctly blew when I tried using the 5A unit. They work fine after fixing my careless mix-up, but I'd like these better if the device or fuse holder were marked with a recommended fuse rating, or the connectors couldn't mate with the wrong device, or the fuse holder were on the device side of the proprietary connector, or the unit came with spare fuses, or the fuse ratings were included in the online user guide, or the user guide were included in the box, or the safety guide were printed in a typeface legible to adult human eyes. Anyway, keep your cables together with the devices and don't mix em up.

reviews.title: High quality at a reasonable cost
reviews.body: This charger/tender worked well to "revive" a ~80Ah lead acid battery that sat in a low state of charge for nearly a year. After an initial 2.5 hour cycle in repair mode, followed by a higher amp charge from an older/larger charger, a noticeable improvement in battery performance was observed. A shorter repair cycle, about 30 minutes total, restored some capacity on another lead acid battery still in use. There are cheaper desulfator-only options, of questionable reliability/longevity, so the additional features offered on this model were cost-effective for my intended usage. While I have not yet used this as a tender/maintainer for any length of time, the cabling to and from the charger are long enough to reach from one side of a car to the other. This unit did not seem to produce much heat in repair mode with ~75F ambient temp. In auto charge mode between 25% and 75%, it was warm to the touch. I'll have to try a longer charge period to see if it heats up further. UPDATE: after using repair & charge mode on a flat battery for a few hours, this unit can get fairly hot. Using this on a flat surface so air can get underneath is a good idea. This product did not come with a manual in the box, just the warranty booklet. Tracking down a user manual on the manufacturer's site did not require much effort. The 6V and repair mode are not activated by quick presses of the single button. Pressing & holding for a few seconds activates these extra modes from standby. Some form of documentation in the box would have been more convenient than going to the website, but I digress.

reviews.title: Revived my battery
reviews.body: I bought a used 2022 Honda Ridgeline with ~7,000 miles on it some months back. It was a "dealer demo car" and was well-maintained as a result. Now, it's got around 12,000 miles on it. One day, I left the lights on too long with the ignition off, and had the radio playing. Stupid on my part, but my battery didn't have enough charge to deliver the amps needed to turn the engine over. I bought a Noco GB40, and it worked well - it'd start my truck when needed. Yesterday, it didn't. I guess the battery had degraded too much, so I was shopping for new batteries when the sticker shock hit me. Given the age of my truck, I thought it would be silly to replace the battery. Someone recommended the Noco Genius5, so I gave it a shot. Amazon's same-day delivery got it to me quickly, and I basically hooked it up to the battery, plugged it in, set it to AGM mode, and let it go to work. I waited several hours for the charger light to show "solid green", indicating it was fully charged. I started up my truck; it sounded better than the day I bought it. However, on the dash, it had a note about an "emissions problem". My scan tool showed a permanent code with the Transmission Control Module and a bunch of other temporary codes. Since I didn't have any codes before, I figured I may have freaked out the electronics by charging the battery while the battery was hooked up to the truck, or maybe by touching the terminals out of sequence when removing the cables. Either way, I removed the battery from my truck, hooked up the Genius5, and set it to "repair mode". My truck had low mileage when I bought it, at about a year old, which likely meant that it say for a while when not in use. Maybe that could have led to sulfation or stratification, which could have meant it wouldn't charge as effectively from the alternator. I also wanted to remove the battery to allow the computers to reset in the truck. If it was still throwing codes after that, I'd bring it into the dealer. This morning, when I woke up, I noticed the Genius5 was in standby mode, meaning the repair mode had finished. I started the Genius5 back up, and set it to AGM mode again -- it took about a minute, but it said the battery was good to go with a solid green light. I Installed the battery back in my truck, fired it up, and I kid you not, it sounded better than ever -- less strained, more powerful, and all of the codes were gone. My truck had a freakout -- not due to this device, I'm sure, but likely due to me doing something stupid. It's rare for me to review a product so quickly. This thing is amazing, has lots of neat accessories available for it, and saved me money. I'll continue using it to prolong my batteries and save me money in the long-run. If you're on the fence, this little device is absolutely legit. 10/10 would recommend.

If you want an affordable, simple webcam that’s easy to use, this one gets the job done. Helpful tip: Make sure the webcam is plugged directly into your computer rather than a USB hub—this can help keep the video feed stable.

reviews.title: Well-designed, well-built, well-supported
reviews.body: I bought one of these for my wife after using one myself for several years. I teach online so my camera gets constant use. The image quality is terrific, especially after using the setup software to increase the camera resolution. The camera is plug-and-play, requiring no setup in either Windows or Ubuntu Linux. The only minor complaints I have are that images are dim in low light (make sure your face is well-lit from the front!) and that it occasionally re-focuses spontaneously and causes a few seconds of blurred video. But 99 percent of the time the image is excellent. Audio quality is very good too, but the microphone can be overdriven, causing distorted sound. This is seldom a problem for voice calls but if you're using it for something louder like an acoustic instrument you should turn down the microphone gain in either the camera setup or the application itself, and make sure from the person on the other end that they're not hearing distortion. With the mic properly set you get decent audio fidelity, no matter what your sound source is. My biggest complaint about this webcam has nothing to do with the device itself. It's too popular. It's almost always sold out at the Logitech store, and when they do make some available, they are snapped up by resellers who scalp them at a $15-$30 premium. It would be helpful if Logitech would limit the number people could buy to give more people a chance to get this great camera at a more reasonable price.

It automatically adjusts to make sure my face is well-lit and clear. I didn't have to buy expensive key lights or ring lights to look good on camera, which saved me a ton of money. This camera is Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Logitech MX Brio: A Stunning Leap Forward
reviews.body: ## **Logitech MX Brio Ultra HD 4K: The New Gold Standard for Video** If you haven’t upgraded your webcam in a few years, the **Logitech MX Brio** is a startling reminder of just how far imaging technology has come. Gone are the days of grainy, "good enough" video calls. We are officially in the era of ultra-crisp, professional-grade production sitting right on top of your monitor. ### **Crystal Clarity & Visual Fidelity** The jump to **Ultra HD 4K** is immediately noticeable. The clarity is staggering—it picks up textures and details that older 1080p sensors simply smudge away. Whether you’re in a high-stakes board meeting or recording content, the image looks expensive. It handles difficult lighting with ease, ensuring you don't look washed out when the sun hits your desk or like a shadow when the lights are low. ### **Pro-Grade Audio** Usually, webcam microphones are an afterthought, but the audio here is surprisingly **clear and crisp**. It manages to isolate your voice while minimizing that hollow, "bathroom" echo common in cheaper units. While dedicated mics still have their place, for 95% of users, this audio quality is more than enough to sound professional and authoritative. ### **Total Software Control** Where this camera really shines is the **Logitech G HUB or Logi Options+** integration. The level of control is deep: * **Fine-tuned adjustments:** You can tweak ISO, shutter speed, white balance, and exposure. * **Field of View:** Crop in for a tight headshot or widen it out to show your workspace. * **Show Mode:** A clever bit of tech that lets you tilt the camera down to show your desk, automatically flipping the image so your viewers can see your sketches or notes correctly. ### **The Verdict** It’s incredible to see how much technology has shifted in just the last few years. We’ve moved from "webcams" to "miniature cinema cameras." The **Logitech MX Brio** isn't just a tool for Zoom calls; it’s a high-performance piece of hardware that brings professional studio quality to a plug-and-play format. If you value how you show up in the digital world, this is the upgrade you've been waiting for.

reviews.title: Expensive but worth it (if you actually need it)
reviews.body: This is a great device with clear video and sound. Installation was easy, only down side is the cord is too short. I had to use an extension to allow the camera to reach the back of my computer, which sets on the ground, right below the monitor. (make sure to get a USBC 3 or higher). Downside is you have to deal with logitech software and website. The description of the logi options software is described by Logitech for use with mouse and keyboards. It doesn't mention web camera. And there is a recommended "hub" software that is not needed, and just becomes bloatware. If you want to manage the device Logi Options is mandatory, but easy to navigate. Autofocus is very quick and the camera is almost too bright and clear. I turn down the resolution from 4k as I thought it was too bright, and who wants to see the pores on a persons skin. Its sits well on monitor and find I did not have to use the stick pad. I just left the cover strip over and having no issues. As for value, this thing is expensive. I am not sure it is priced right for the person who needs an occasional web meeting. But it great if you do lots of meetings and want the best. I am told the sound is crystal clear and the AI noise reduction seems to block out all the background noise of my air purifier and printer.

reviews.title: The best “professional work” webcam I’ve personally used, especially for virtual backgrounds
reviews.body: I bought the Logitech MX Brio after spending years using a mirrorless camera setup (Lumix GH3 + prime lens) as my desk webcam. I work remotely full-time and spend most of my day in video calls (99% in Microsoft Teams), so my priorities are a little different from the average streaming-focused review. What I wanted was: • excellent image quality at normal desktop distances • reliable performance in Teams • strong virtual background segmentation • stable autofocus/exposure • easy to set up For my use case, the MX Brio has honestly been excellent. The biggest surprise was how good the image looks in real-world meetings. Yes, my GH3 (and other mirrorless cameras) can still produce a more cinematic image in ideal conditions, but in Teams specifically (where video is heavily compressed and usually capped at 1080p), the practical gap is much smaller than people think. As far as the camera is concerned, what matters most is consistency and signal quality, and this camera delivers both. The MX Brio handles exposure transitions smoothly, autofocus has been reliable, and image sharpness is very good without looking overly processed. Logitech also seems to have improved color handling compared to some older Brio models that could occasionally look harsh or over-sharpened. Where this webcam REALLY shines is virtual background and portrait segmentation. I use a virtual background almost 100% of the time, and this camera consistently gives cleaner edge separation than several other webcams I’ve tested. Good lighting absolutely helps, but the MX Brio seems to provide a very clean image feed that works well with Teams’ background processing. A few other things I appreciated: • solid low-light recovery without becoming a smeary mess • flexible field of view options • sturdy physical build • built-in microphone • easy mounting and positioning There are a couple tradeoffs worth mentioning: • Logitech’s software ecosystem is still a little fragmented (Logi Tune, G Hub, etc.) • if you are primarily a streamer/content creator, there may be better options depending on your workflow • this camera, like any, benefits significantly from proper lighting and good positioning. It's worth it to invest in a couple lights and proper mounting system But for a professional desk setup focused on video meetings, presentations, collaboration, and hybrid work, I think Logitech understood the assignment here surprisingly well. This is the first dedicated webcam I’ve used where I no longer feel tempted to drag a mirrorless camera back onto my desk.

reviews.title: DO NOT BUY A LOGITECH WEBCAM!!!
reviews.body: Is it possible to leave less than one star?? Seriously, Logitech is the worst... I bought this Brio webcam as a REPLACEMENT for an earlier model webcam that I just could not get to focus on my face during TikTok / YouTube livestreams, no matter what I tried... So, I invested ANOTHER $170 on this one (Logitech now has $350 of my hard-earend money), and this one has the exact same problem. I have spent HOURS with AI, Logitech's website, Logitech's tech support, support groups, etc., and here is what my image looks like consistently on livestreams (see attached screenshot). Logitech: How many hours do you expect your customers to spend getting YOUR product simply to work properly?? The latest round: I tried to get a refund on Amazon, but I'm past the window for returns/refunds. So, I have been reaching out to Logitech. Last week, their tech support spent quite a bit of time with me (which includes MY wasted time), and they couldn't solve it. So, they PROMISED I'd hear back from their next-level-up tech support by end-of-day Thursday. I'm typing this review on Saturday, and still not a peep from Logitech. I suspect they're hoping I just disappear, since they can't seem to solve my webcam issue. And, yes, I've done it all: Switched from WiFi to a direct connect to my router; downloaded Logitech's software and tried manually focusing, etc.; closed all my other apps to ensure my laptop memory was as freed up as possible; etc., etc... and, yes, the lens is spotless clean. So, I'm done. Logitech has my money, but that's all they're ever going to get from me. I'm now purchasing a EMEET S600 4K Webcam, which costs $110 less than this piece-of-junk Brio; this is the webcam my livestream partner is using....

reviews.title: Excellent camera - corrected lighting issues that other cameras could not
reviews.body: My home office has dark wood paneling, and natural light comes in from one side. This setting has meant that half of my face is as pale as a sheet and the other side is almost unrecognizable. I tried several cameras (mostly Logitech), and none of them were awesome. Until this one. This camera is great for adjusting to different lighting conditions. And the picture is sharp as well. I had to do very little in terms of set up. It just works. During one of my first video meetings with the new webcam, a colleague who I had met with a several dozen times over the last few years asked me whether I was using a virtual background. He hadn't noticed the nice wood paneling before. Tells you how bad the situation was. I was so pleased after using this for a day I ordered a second one for my regular office. I've struggled with lighting issues there as well -- there is a large window right behind me when sitting at the desk. I'd often look like a dark shadow. This camera remedied the situation there as well. Anyway, highly recommended.

Plug&Play Connectivity, Guaranteed Privacy - Simply connect this USB 2.0 Webcam to any device with a Type A port and start your video communication instantly. With no need for drivers or cloud storage, it offers a controlled environment that maintains data locally. It is ideal for professionals and settings that demand privacy.

Designed with stability, the PC camera boasts a robust swivel connection between the lens and its stand, uses an internal rubber material that grips securely to computer, and firmly integrates into the device with a 1.5m fixed cable.

reviews.title: It actually works for Windows 10!
reviews.body: I was super excited to purchase this 4K webcam to help myself have crisper, clearer video chats when teaching online. Since changing from an established workplace to freelance, I had to return my previous company computer, and that left me with my old 2012 HP running Windows 10. The built-in webcam on my laptop is terrbile! At my brother's recommendation, since I needed something better (and since simply using my cell phone wouldn't work for the long-term), I began looking into external webcams. I asked Google's AI to help me find something suitable for my laptop in particular, and somehow this 4K camera came up. However, when it came in the mail and I plugged it in, my computer didn't seem to recognize it at all. No blue light! Anyway, I was beginning to wonder if I'd have to return it, but I had already attached the "privacy" adhesive over the lens and was concerned that this might mean I couldn't send it back. Also, I really wanted it to work! So I did a ton of troubleshooting, updating things on my computer here and there, installing drivers, etc. Nothing worked. I then bought an external USB 3.0 hub since my laptop's hubs aren't powerful enough for a 4K webcam evidently. Plugged everything in. Still, nothing! Then finally, I asked AI for recommendations regarding that particular webcam and my specific laptop, once again. The final recommendation it gave me was to "install Native EMEET Software." I had read earlier that everything would be supplied automatically as soon as you plug it in, but it turns out that's not always the case. I went onto the website, and there's a place listing "downloads" where you can get the needed software for either Windows PC or Mac. So, I downloaded the Windows one ... and voila! At long last, after installing that software, the camera worked! Apparently it's still not perfectly displaying in 4K, but no matter! The quality is is a step down from that, since my computer cannot quite support 4K. What it can display though is still a MASSIVE upgrade from what I had before! The low-light performance is excellent, and you can adjust the camera settings (contrast, saturation, etc.). I've never used an external webcam before so to me this is pretty cool. Plus, I can always use this camera on a newer laptop whenever I'm able to purchase one, and then I can have perfect 4K. But for now, attached to the laptop that I have, this camera quality is still beyond "good enough"; it's great. I'm glad I didn't give up and send this back. So it's completely worth it -- just know that if you have an old computer running Windows 10, you might have to jump through multiple hoops first before getting it to work. ;)

reviews.title: Video streaming is your job = PASS ... Casual video for mtgs/life = BUY IT -- checks all the boxes
reviews.body: If video streaming is a way you make money, do NOT buy this. This webcam + microphone is not for professional level video streaming. If you need a webcam + mic device that is good enough, and performs better than most/all laptop integration webcams, then just buy this and call it a day. There are a lot of options, but I promise that unless you are a really particular human, you will be happy with this product. a) WfH business person taking video calls for work = YES b) private individual streaming to connect with friends/family = YES c) a recreational streamer = YES Detailed review notes below.... **MOST IMPORTANT THING TO KNOW** The camera can only go so far, but a lot of what determines the final video quality is what YOU do to create a good video streaming environment. Read: If you are in a windowless cave 50' below Earth's surface with no artificial lighting, poor video quality is on you, not the device. Lighting and distance of the camera from your face are THE MOST IMPORTANT VARIABLES in determining whether this camera performs well or not. I posted a photo of my specific camera placement and lighting and desk situation, and have tested out four different lighting scenarios (listed below) to show the impact of lighting on the video quality. **REVIEW NOTES** Each number 1-4 below has a matching image that I have attached to this review: 1. Only natural light from my office windows (indirect sunlight) 2. #1 + clip-on desk lamp with warm colored LED *MY FAVORITE SETUP* 3. #2 + recessed ceiling lights (3" white colored LEDs with 8' ceilings) 4. Natural light from windows + recessed ceiling lights (NO desk lamp) *NOTE*: Each image was taken via Windows Snipit tool while waiting to join a Google Meeting BOTTOM LINE, you have to mess around with your lighting and camera distance to get the sweet spot for your specific environment, and may require additional lighting sources (e.g. lamp) to get it right. The EMEET app is super easy to install and provides decent enough picture settings to tweak the image quality without being overkill. No login/account/signup required. I recommend keeping the "white balance" on AUTO at all times.

reviews.title: A great 4K cam with Sony sensor
reviews.body: The box for this is quite sturdy although not very visually impressive. Acer should put more effort into their packaging, particularly on a premium product like this. These are my main likes and dislikes for this product: Like: Sony 1/2 “ sensor 4K HDR Premium lenses Full metal body Compact and portable Good overall build quality Fully Plug & Play Dislike: Expensive at £79.99 rrp Lens cover falls off too easily As you can see there is a lot I like about this webcam. The image it produces look very natural, being not too colourful or contrasty, with just the right balance. The sharpness at 4K is a noticeable improvement over 1080p or even 1440p, as long as you have a monitor good enough to see the difference of course. The Sony CMOS sensor is good at controlling signal noise, so the fuzziness is kept to a minimum in low light, and is far better than a standard webcam with a generic cheap sensor. The autofocus is surprisingly good, again this is due to the sensor and chip combination. Tracking actually works in most instances, which I have not seen on a webcam before. The dual mics work very well and remove background noise almost completely. Voices are clear, even multiple voices can be heard perfectly within about six feet of the camera. Installation was a few seconds, as it is plug and play. This is being used on Windows 11 but it should also work on Apple Macintosh computers. The lens cap is a bit of a disappointment, it is not strong enough and is easy to knock off when handling the camera. A more powerful magnet is needed. The current price for this is £66 which I think is reasonable, and at that price it’s going to get a solid five stars.

reviews.title: A little differrent
reviews.body: The product listing on Amazon is brilliant and exciting, with many promises. Is some ways, the actual product exceeds the claims but in other ways it is "different". Skip down to " * " for the good news The little cardboard box it comes in is function but visually generic or industrial. No blame, but underwhelming for the magic of the promise of studio-quality visuals, making it ideal for gamers, educators, and professionals seeking streaming camera​ precision. The claim is that the USB cable is "5.9in" when, in fact, it is close to 57 inches or 1.4 meter. The claim is that it is USB plug-and-play when, if fact there may be some issues. On this Windows 10 computer, the device manager reports this as a 4K camera but with the caution "was not migrated due to partial or ambiguous match" I don't know. Some APPS can't find it but the important ones ( like ZOOM ) like it a lot. Don't bet on instant installation. The low-light performance is adequate. Kind-of OK but not outstanding. However, the auto-focus really goes nuts in very low light. It "hunts" and cannot resolve prime focus though it tries and tries. Works good with adequate light. The instruction manual is microscopic but well written, in good English, somewhat optimistic: claims OS compatibility with Window XP / Vista 7/8/10/11 Linux2..6.24 or later / Ubuntu ( ?? not IOS ? ) Again, don't bet on it. And why would you think that poor old Windows XP doesn't need a driver. * - the good news The form factor is small and pleasing. Maybe 2-1/2 inches wide and rather graceful, not aggressively rectangular like most. The image quality is exceptionally good, Snapshots indicate 3840 x 2160 resolution. FYI: this is considered 4K UHD (Ultra High Definition) — 3840 × 2160 pixels,as used in TVs, monitors, and consumer devices The activity light is actually an oval around the lens that slowly changes colors when the camera is active. It is interesting and a good excuse to keep looking directly into the camera - resulting is a better sense of "presence" in online meetings compared to appearing "off camera" and disinterested. The privacy flap is very small and easily overlooked - resulting in a dark, black picture of course - but handy and effective The camera HAS AUTOFOCUS ( some apps turn it off ) and can focus sharply down to 3 inches. Almost macro. I would keep it just for this feature. The mount is a ball attachment giving 360 degree rotation, about 90 degrees vertical and great latitude in how the clamp is positioned. The clamp-mount has a high quality metal insert for a 1/4-20 tripod screw The sound quality is very good. It is claimed to have AI properties and noise suppression. You will have to make your own determination. My video space has good acoustic qualities. I would have to test it in a tiled bathroom or a noisy coffee shop before I could comment on AI since everything, maybe even toilet paper, is now "AI". At a competitive price-point, this may be best among equals. If you purchase this camera, you will get to like it as part of your Zoom or Teams setup. note: pictures are selfie in a mirror ( maybe 4 inches away or less ) and a US quarter resting on the product box

reviews.title: Works well and has privacy cover
reviews.body: This is a straight forward plug and play webcam. There’s no setup involved other than putting it on top of your monitor and connecting the USB cable. It’s 1080p so it’s not going to be as sharp or as clear as some of the other ones on the market. For example, the gold standard for me has been the instalink 360. Super detailed and clear and most importantly, it gets skin tone right. Compared to that, the Xoclon is just okay. It’s a bit darker, or a bit too light when it attempts to focus. But does it make sense to compare it to a $200+ webcam? No it doesn’t. What this Xoclon is good for is as a camera for your kid for remote learning or for your home office to use in a pinch. Not everyone cares about the quality and skin tones anyway. The microphone works well and doesn’t muffle my voice either. There is also a privacy flap for the camera lens itself. Now it’s worth mentioning that there is no hardwired privacy switch or button for the microphone and to be fair, most webcams don’t have that. There is also a light strip that indicates when the camera is in use. It’s purely to let you know when you’re using the camera and won’t do anything to illuminate your face or anything like that. For a plug and play camera that is about the cost of a fancy salad bowl, yeah this will do nicely.
reviews.body_en: This is a straight forward plug and play webcam. There’s no setup involved other than putting it on top of your monitor and connecting the USB cable. reviews.title: Easy Plug-and-Play 4K Webcam With Colorful Activity Lights
reviews.body: I recently picked up this webcam and have been pleasantly surprised with how well it performs for its size and price. Setup was about as easy as it gets. I connected the webcam to a Microsoft Windows 11 laptop, and there were no drivers to download or install. Simply plug in the camera to any USB-A port and it should be recognized as both a video and audio device. Windows Settings>Bluetooth & Devices>Cameras and Settings>System>Sound>Input configuration menus allow further adjustments if needed. I found it easiest to start with the Windows Camera app to preview and tweak the image. Windows 11 shows the highest 16:9 resolution for the webcam is 8.3 MP (3840x2160). The camera image was quite good when there is adequate light. The sound quality is certainly very usable. The listing mentions "Smart Noise Cancellation," but I was not able to verify that feature specifically during my testing. Physically, the camera is very small compared to my old Logitech webcam. It also has fun lights that rotate through many colors when the camera is in use. This is a great visual reminder that the camera is active. For privacy, there is a physical lens cover that can be folded down to ensure no video can be captured. This adds real peace of mind beyond just relying on the colored lights being off. One minor gripe is that the lens cover can be a little difficult to flip up if you have larger fingers, since there is no handle to grab to flip it up. Overall, this is a nice camera for use with Windows video capture, video conferencing applications, live streaming, and general everyday use. If you want an easy plug-and-play webcam with solid image quality, this one is definitely worth considering.

reviews.title: Honest Review
reviews.body: I don't like giving misleading reviews so I'm going to keep this as real and grounded as possible. I bought this product close to a month ago as a quick solution to use on discord calls with a freshly set-up gaming pc. Since I wasn't going to be using this for anything professional, I wasn't a stickler for the quality. That being said, I was pleasantly surprised to find that it did look better than the built-in webcam I had been using on my gaming laptop previously. I don't use the webcam microphone at all, so I can't speak for any of the audio-related aspects of this device. I was worried about it's ability to fit on my monitor before purchasing, but the clip mechanism is surprisingly easy and universal across the 3 monitors I've mounted it on. I would say as long as your not rocking a CRT, this should fit on any flat-screen monitor. It was also a bonus that the clip design allowed me to slide the webcam from one end of the monitor to the other. The length of the cord was just under 5ft, I loosely measured 4'10". It helped that I already had a usb extender on-hand, since it wouldn't reach my middle monitor while plugged in. For any privacy enthusiasts, it does not have an LED indicator for when it's in use, and doesn't come with a built in cover either. reviews.title: Interviewing remote? BUY THIS.
reviews.body: I'm in the process of interviewing for a new job and want that first impression to make an impact. I remember when I interviewed for my current job years ago they later commented on how good my streaming quality was. I used my school's AV room which had excellent webcams, mics, and a studio booth. I'm on the job market again and need an AV setup that won't break the bank. This camera fits the bill perfectly because it's cheap enough for just a few uses but still delivers an excellent picture. As with any camera, always learn how to connect and adjust software settings before going live; that aside, I didn't have any issues connecting and making adjustments (mirror, brightness). You'll need to download their app to make adjustments. Very intuitive from there. Seems to be forgiving of lighting technique so long as you simply have adequate lighting. White balance is dead on (5000k Walmart light bulbs), just be ready to adjust light source angles and brightness settings. Microphone works, but any monitor-mounted camera mic won't be great. I bought a $30 lavalier mic and it made a huge difference. You can have excellent video quality, but if the audio sucks it's all for nothing. If I could nitpick I wish it shot in 24 FPS. 60 is nauseating, and luckily most streaming services will knock it down to 30 anyway. More fps is not better. It just looks unnatural and consumes more resources in doing so in the process.

reviews.title: Excellent Webcam For Its Purpose.
reviews.body: This is an excellent camera for its intended purpose- web conferencing in much better resolution than most built in laptop cameras or conferencing monitors. It's not really meant for streaming (you'll want a DSLR setup for that). It suits its purpose very well! The biggest plus is that it can do 1080p FHD in 60 fps. There are cameras 2x-3x the price that still only shoot 1080p in 30 fps. The camera is very solidly built, and the twist-to-open privacy shutter isn't flimsy like many are. The camera also has 45° of swivel on its mount, very handy for compensating for angled dual monitors, or for keeping unwanted objects out of the background. The retro tubular "This is a camera" shape also looks cool! There are 2 inbuilt microphones, which would be useful if you're using a desktop that lacks an inbuilt speakerphone or a monitor that has one. I have an external microphone so I only used the feature to test it. It's better than most conference monitor mics, but not an external dynamic or condenser microphone. The Emeet Link software is very basic, and resolution is altered in your camera settings instead of the app. The only complaint I have is the lack of a manual focus option, but considering the features for the price, and the use case, it is forgivable. Overall, it does everything I want it to, the price was right, and it works. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Solid Performer – Clear Image, Great Audio & Smart Design
reviews.body: I’ve been using this webcam for almost 12 months now and I honestly can’t fault it. It’s well designed, reliable and performs exactly as expected for video calls and streaming. The camera mounts securely on top of my monitor, with a clever design that allows it to sit flush and hug the screen without slipping or wobbling. It feels stable and unobtrusive, which is ideal for day-to-day use. A standout feature is the built-in privacy cover—a physical lens flap you can close when not in use. This is a must-have in today’s digital environment and offers peace of mind in the unlikely event your system is ever compromised. When closed, you’re completely protected from any unauthorised access to your webcam feed. It connects via USB-A to USB-C, while it does come with a cable (I believe around 1m long), I opted to purchase a 2m extension with a right-angle USB-C plug. The angled plug was important to me, as it allows the cable to sit neatly without jutting out from the back of the camera—especially helpful for keeping things tidy and adjusting placement when your PC isn’t close to your monitor. As for performance, the image quality is excellent for a webcam, especially considering the price. It delivers a sharp, vibrant picture with fast autofocus and smooth frame rates, particularly noticeable at 1080p @ 60fps. It’s absolutely up to the task for Zoom meetings, live streaming, or content creation. The built-in microphones were a pleasant surprise too. I had a separate desk mic on standby assuming the webcam mic would be subpar, but so far I haven’t needed it—the onboard mic does a great job and captures audio clearly with minimal background noise. All in all, I highly recommend this camera. Between the thoughtful design, impressive performance, and practical privacy features, it’s a well-rounded piece of kit that’s been a great addition to my setup. 5 stars without hesitation.

reviews.title: OBSBOT Tiny 3 mit leichten Schwächen die sich sicherlich per Update beheben lassen.
reviews.body: Kleine und gute Kamera die tut was sie soll. Sie hat eine ausgezeichnete Video- und Audioqualität. Die Kamera wurde von dem PC mit Win 11 sofort erkannt. Zur Nutzung muss man jedoch die App des Herstellers laden. Diese ist etwas Gewöhnungsbedürftig, das Einstellen der gewünschten Parameter ist nicht sehr inuitiv. Ein, für mich, zweites kleines Manko ist die Ausrichtung im Modus mehrere Personen und Nachverfolgung. Mann muss schon sehr genau in Richtung Kamera sprechen, damit diese dann auf die entsprechende Person wechselt. Das schwenken ist dann langsam. Es besteht zu befürchten, bei Personen mit einer ähnlichen Stimmlage, das die Kamera durcheinander kommt. Bei dem Folgen einer einzelnen Person hat die Kamera jedoch keine Schwierigkeiten. Das geht zügig und ohne Probleme. Da hat die Kamera voll überzeugt. Ich gebe der Kamera 4.5 Sterne (aufgerundet 5). Die Probleme mit den mehreren Personen lassen sich sicherlich per Update beheben, genauso wie die App und deren Bedienung. Für mich als Webcam funktioniert sie super, an die App gewöhnt man sich. Die Kamera ist für Ihre Größe relativ schwer, was sich dann bemerkbar macht wenn Sie sich dreht. Es sind keine Ruckler zu sehen. Außerdem hat der Fuss einen Anschluss für ein Stativ mit Normschraube. Alles in allem eine Kaufempfehlung für diesen Preis. Geliefert wird die Kamera in einem stabilen Karton, inkl Unterlagen und USB Kabel. Ein Netzteil ist nicht mit im Lieferumfang.
reviews.body_en: Small and good camera that does what it's supposed to do. It has excellent video and audio quality. The camera was immediately recognized by the PC with Win 11. To use it, however, you have to download the manufacturer's app. This takes some getting used to; setting the desired parameters is not very intuitive. A second small drawback for me is the alignment in multiple person and tracking mode. You have to speak very precisely towards the camera so that it then switches to the relevant person. The panning is then slow. There is a fear that people with a similar voice pitch will confuse the camera. However, the camera has no problems following a single person. This happens quickly and without any problems. The camera was completely convincing. I give the camera 4.5 stars (rounded up to 5). The problems with multiple people can certainly be fixed with an update, as can the app and its operation. For me it works great as a webcam, you get used to the app. The camera is relatively heavy for its size, which becomes noticeable when it rotates. There are no jerks to be seen. The base also has a connection for a tripod with a standard screw. All in all a purchase recommendation for this price. The camera is delivered in a sturdy box, including documents and USB cable. A power supply is not included.

reviews.title: Great for big monitors, but overpriced for what you get
reviews.body: Solid monitor light, but probably not worth the price unless you have a huge screen This has been a nice addition to my desk setup. I chose it because, as you can probably tell, my monitor is massive (49 inches), and I needed something that would actually cover a decent portion of the screen. Pros: Brightness: This light really helped brighten up my space. My office tends to be pretty dark, so it’s been great for overall visibility and eye comfort. Size & Flexibility: I love how large it is and that I can move it around to get the angle I want. Quality: It feels well-made and doesn’t look cheap at all. (To be fair, this is the only monitor light I’ve tried, so I don’t have a ton to compare it to.) Cons: Price: Even though the build quality is solid, I still don’t get how this costs over $50. It’s just white and warm light with brightness adjustments. No RGB, no standout features. If you don’t have a large curved monitor like mine, I’d say go with a cheaper one that offers more features. Remote only: This part is wild to me. There are zero controls on the light itself. Everything depends on the remote. So if you misplace it, you’re basically out of luck. Final thoughts: Overall, the light works well, and the size is perfect for my ultra-wide monitor. I just think it’s overpriced for what it is. If you specifically need the large size and basic lighting, it’s a good pick. But if not, there are more affordable options out there with better features.

reviews.title: Visually appealing, nice size, sensible controls that remember your previous settings!
reviews.body: First of all, I really appreciate a desk lamp that can simulate the warm glow of an incandescent lamp (this is 3k, not 2.7k which is close enough for me). The harsh white/blue colors of many LED lamps don't do it for me but if that is what you want, you can get that here too! In addition, I think it is nice to have a consistent light color throughout the entire house and the warm color is consistent with the rest of my home. I also really appreciate that I can turn it on/off and have it come back on at the LAST SETTINGS that I had previously!! I don't have to re-set my preference every time I turn on the lamp which is not uncommon (I have other lamps that I have to press the button 3-4+ times to get it to the intensity and/or color that I want every time I turn it on). Once you set your preference, it remembers it! It is somewhat of a minimalist design, just enough equipment to do what it needs to do. The black color matches the other things on my desktop. It does have quite a lot of brightness levels which I also appreciate. I find the height to be about right. If it is too tall, it can get in the way, and if it is too short, it may not be flexible enough for enough circumstances. I have my lamp behind the computer monitor, but then position the light over and towards the desktop in front of my screen. I can then reach underneath or around the monitor quite easily to turn the light on/off. Overall good value and nice, thoughtful, functionality.

reviews.title: Flexible reading lamp with adjustable brightness/warmth
reviews.body: This desk lamp is very versatile for many different applications. The main stand rotates 135°, there is a hinge about 3/4 of the way up and another hinge where the lamp attaches. Additionally, the lamp head can rotate 280°. This flexibility makes it easy to direct the light exactly where you need it. The brightness and temperature of the light can been adjusted using the buttons on the lamp stand or the included remote (2 AAA batteries required). The remote has two preset options for reading or computer video, which is really convenient. You can quickly switch modes and create a natural lighting look for video calls instead of harsh overhead fluorescent lights. The lamp also has an automatic shut off option for 30 or 60 minutes. The base is flat and heavy to prevent tipping, and has pads on the bottom so it won’t scratch your desk or table. The only downside is that it uses kind of a bulky AC adapter plug rather than a USB or small size plug. So you have to have enough clearance to plug it into the wall or a power strip. The cord is pretty long though so that is helpful (about 6 ft or just under 2m) Overall this is a nice desk lamp and I like the flexible options in directly the bright light where you want it, or just giving some ambient lighting.

reviews.title: Great light diffusion
reviews.body: I really like the different light levels and color temperatures this lamp provides. It works particularly well as a desk lamp because you can adjust the lighting to suit what you're doing. I've primarily been using it for soldering, where the bright light makes it much easier to see what I'm working on. My daughter also commented that it would be great for the artwork she does (and that she is likely to steal it from my desk)... The touch controls work very well. It comes with a remote, but I haven't needed to use it much since the touch controls are sufficient for me. The remote does provide some additional control, though, including independently adjusting brightness and color temperature up or down. The touch controls essentially cycle through the available settings. The remote also includes reading-light and conference-light modes. The lamp uses a wall power adapter ("wall wart"), with a barrel connector on the cord about 12 inches from the lamp base. According to the specifications on the adapter, it's rated at 24V × 0.75A, or exactly 18 watts. What could be improved The biggest limitation is the range of motion. The base rotates only about 100 degrees, and the first joint allows roughly 90 degrees of front-to-back movement. I'd like to see it swing farther forward because, starting from the vertical position, it can only lean forward about 20 degrees. The middle and upper joints have considerably more range of motion. I suspect this limitation was intentional to help prevent the lamp from tipping over. At its furthest forward position, the lamp does feel like it could potentially tip, although it hasn't done so. A slightly heavier base would probably allow for a greater range of motion without sacrificing stability. The joints themselves are nicely stiff. The lamp stays where I position it, and I don't have to worry about it gradually sagging or shifting over time due to gravity. Overall, I'm very happy with it. The adjustable brightness and color temperature are the biggest selling points for me, and the excellent lighting makes it especially useful for soldering and other close-up work.
