reviews.title: A well-designed reading lamp...and more!
reviews.body: Give this little light a try; I think you'll really like it. The box arrives mostly assembled, so you should have it up and running within five minutes. At first, I was a bit disappointed thinking that the lamp could only be controlled with a remote. With dozens of remotes scattered throughout my house, the last thing I needed was another one for a simple lamp. However, I was pleasantly surprised to find that you can adjust everything that you would normally control with the remote using some conveniently placed buttons on the bottom stem of the lamp. These controls allow you to change the color temperature from warm white to cool white and adjust the brightness level, from mood lighting to super bright. There are also a couple of presets for reading light and ambient lighting, along with an on/off switch. A quick note about the on/off switch: you need to press the button briefly. If you hold it down, the lamp won't respond, which initially led me to believe I had a defective unit, but that wasn’t the case. If you’re looking for a small, well-built lamp that offers complete flexibility, you’ll be hard-pressed to find a better option, especially at this price point.

reviews.title: Excellent early impression.
reviews.body: 1. The controls are at the base of the vertical riser. They do not get obstructed by other items on the desk. Controls are very intuitive except for the 45-minute shut-off timer. No silly remote control to lose. 2. The base is about 6" by 6" and is made out of steel plate. It is large enough and heavy enough that the lamp is very stable. There is a soft, non-skid pad on the bottom that protects the table surface while keeping the lamp from being inadvertantly pushed around. I specifically wanted a lamp with a base such as this rather than a clamp-on type. 3. There is enough vertical adjustment to clear the top of large monitors. 4. The arms and lamp came pre-assembled. The only assembly requirment is to slip the upright post onto the base and plug in the power supply. 5. The power supply transformer plugs into a standard 120 VAC outlet. The cord is over 6 feet long so placement is not an issue. 6. Color temperature and brightness adjustments are easy. The lamp is sufficiently bright for reading printed material. 7. The light diffusion is quite uniform and has a wide dispersion angle. I originally was looking for a unit with a light bar ("wings") but this has proven completely adequate. I hope that it lasts for quite a while. The manufacturer states that there is an 18-month waranty but that is hard to count on with Chinese manufacturers. Really happy with this lamp, especially for the price.

reviews.title: Excellent lamp for use with tall monitor configurations
reviews.body: After purchasing an Omorepa lamp to place behind my Dell UltraSharp U5226KW monitor, I discovered it was not quite tall enough to position properly without shining directly into my eyes. I ended up returning it and trying the LitONES desk lamp instead because it was slightly taller and, importantly, allowed the lamp head to rotate independently. That flexibility turned out to be exactly what I needed. I initially bought one lamp just to test the setup and quickly realized I had finally found the right solution. The lamp is tall enough to work well behind the 26.5-inch-tall Dell monitor, and the adjustable head makes it easy to angle the light over the monitor and down onto the keyboard and work area without glare. The light itself provides a soft white glow and the brightness can be adjusted easily. Because the monitor is extremely wide, I eventually purchased a second lamp and positioned one on each side behind the display. The only minor inconvenience is that each lamp must be turned on separately since there is no remote control. But honestly, that is a very small complaint — I can lean over and switch them both on in about five seconds. A pretty good sign that I may be a little spoiled at this point. If you have a tall monitor and prefer placing lights behind it so the illumination projects over the display onto your workspace, these lights are definitely worth considering.

reviews.title: Recommended. Could be improved but good as is.
reviews.body: TL;DR: Recommended but could be improved. I'm using this lamp in my living room to illuminate a bluetooth keyboard in the evening. The gooseneck keeps the lamp where I put it and feels like it's well made and will last. The lamp has 3 color settings - white, amber and off-white(?). I'm not sure why they choose off-white rather than red, which is useful when you don't want to compromise your night vision any more than you have to. The lamp seems to be quite efficient; I've been running it on an old no-name (and over-rated IMHO) 30,000 mA USB power bank for about 12 hours, and I've got 87% of the battery left. It's wide enough to illuminate a full-size keyboard, but the LED strip is designed so it's easy to keep glare off the screen. I've got two power banks, neither of which start when the lamp is plugged in; you must push the button on the power bank to turn on the output. This is because the lamp (and other devices) don't draw enough current when the lamp is off for the power bank to notice it's connected! As a result, if I turn the lamp off (such that the lamp's blue standby light comes on) the power bank thinks nothing is connected and shuts down after a few seconds (and thus losing my dimmer adjustments). The lamp has a wide illumination range; it gets quite bright, and dims to a very low level, such that I can keep it on when I'm not using it and it isn't distracting. This is important because WHEN HE LAMP LOSES POWER IT FORGETS HOW MUCH I've DIMMED IT (for which I have deducted a star). To compensate for this, when I turn the light on for the evening I set the default (white) light to the level I need to view my keyboard; I set the other two colors to the lowest level. When I want to take a break and watch TV for a bit, I select the amber color and I can dim the light is enough that I don't notice it. Then when I want to type some more I switch to the white color and I'm in business. I have one other nit: The lamp's gooseneck threads onto the top of a stiff upright tube, which screws into the desk mount. This tube is long enough that I can barely position the lamp perfectly (due in part to my setup - others may not find it too long). This could be solved by shipping a 2nd tube about half the length of the current tube. This way I could use the short tube and it would give the gooseneck more 'reach'. Some may find it useful to use both tubes for added height.

reviews.title: DualBeam FocusCraft 18W
reviews.body: I put this LED dual‑head desk lamp to work in my Waikiki home office and immediately appreciated how well it performs once the 360 degree gooseneck settles into position and the wide light bar floods my workspace with even, shadow‑free illumination. The functionality is excellent because the stepless dimming and five color temperatures let me shift from warm evening reading to bright task lighting without ever feeling locked into a preset, and the gesture control is surprisingly responsive when my hands are busy with tools or paperwork. Usefulness is high whether I’m working across dual monitors, doing detailed craft projects, or lighting a larger desk surface since the extended bar covers far more area than a traditional lamp. My British Retriever likes them in her own way because she always curls up beside the soft glow and seems soothed by the flicker‑free light instead of harsher overhead fixtures. Accuracy is solid because the brightness, color range, and gooseneck flexibility match the published specifications, and the lamp stays stable on the base without wobble. For the money, the value is strong since it delivers wide‑area lighting, thoughtful controls, high CRI performance, and a versatile design that makes everyday work feel more comfortable and precise.

reviews.title: Excellent Desk Lamp With a Slightly Overeager Motion Sensor
reviews.body: I have been very pleased with the Syrinx LED lamps, and this model fits my desk particularly well. It provides bright, broad illumination without taking up much working space. The stepless dimming also makes it easy to adjust the output for anything from general computer work to detailed close-up tasks. The arm has a very good balance. It takes only a light touch to reposition, yet it holds the selected position without drifting or sagging. That makes it easy to direct the light exactly where it is needed. The hands-free control is a double-edged sword. It is genuinely convenient when you want to turn on the lamp quickly without fumbling for a switch, especially when your hands are occupied. However, the sensor can also interpret an innocent stretch or arm movement as a command and unexpectedly switch the lamp off. Despite that minor annoyance, this is a bright, versatile, and well-designed desk lamp that I enjoy using.

reviews.title: Everything was great except...
reviews.body: I've been using this LED desk lamp, and it's been a great addition to my workspace. The 16-inch wide light provides ample coverage, eliminating shadows and ensuring uniform lighting across my entire desk. What I really love is how super bright and glare-free it is. No more eye strain or squinting under harsh lighting! Plus, it’s flicker-free, so I can focus for hours without distractions. The lamp's versatility is another big win. With five dimmable levels and adjustable color temperature from 3,000K to 6,500K, I can easily customize the lighting to suit my needs. The high Color Rendering Index (CRI) of over 90 ensures accurate color reproduction, which is perfect for detailed work. The flexible gooseneck design allows me to position the light exactly where I need it, whether it’s direct illumination on my work surface or ambient light in the room. The heavy base keeps the lamp stable, so it doesn’t tip over or move around during use. As much as all functionality of this lamp is great, I have to subtract one star for the build quality. The build quality leaves a lot to be desired for. The materials feels cheap, and may easily break if accidentally falls or tips over. Overall, this LED desk lamp has significantly improved my workspace, making it brighter and more comfortable. If you don't mind the build quality, then this should be fine for the most part.

reviews.title: A decent desk lamp
reviews.body: I like that this desk lamp has a small footprint and can be placed off to the side, out of the way, but then using the gooseneck the light can be brought in where it is needed. I also like that it is quite bright and can be dimmed from low light to full output. The light color itself can be adjusted between 3 levels, warm, cool or a mix of warm and cool. I personally prefer the white cool light as it seems like a better color for a work light. I don’t use the ambient sensor function so can’t comment. The base is heavy and holds the lamp without tipping even when the gooseneck is cantilevered far out. There is a light diffuser on the end of the lamp shade which can be removed if you want the full blast harsh light, which may be more useful in some situations. There is a usb charger port. The dimming control is a little funky and the click stops were not expected. I would rather have a smooth silent dimmer than one with detents. Also the range of lowest light to highest light is not very wide. Nevertheless, at this price point there isn’t much to complain about. This is a nice bright lamp with more functionality than one would expect at such a low price and seems well made. It is recommended.

reviews.title: Just what I was looking for!
reviews.body: I'll be honest. I was looking for something in my local brick and mortar stores. Target, Walmart, Home Depot, Lowes... every place let me down because they all had the same unimaginative junk. And certainly not in store so I can just go get it. I have a pretty deep computer desk with dual 27" monitors on moving arms. I also have a separate soldering table. I wanted good, shadow free illumination on both and nobody had anything that would work. Lo and behold, I stumble across this on Amazon. I love when someone has a good idea and turns it into a great product. Unboxing is just ridiculously easy. There is no building. All you have to do is screw clamp it to your surface and plug it in. It seems it'll fit a pretty thick surface too. 1 1/8" (almost 3cm) thick shelf stock for a desk and it has enough space for another inch or so. No flickering that I can see. It's clean smooth light. The color temperature options are plentiful and you can cycle through presets of both temp and brightness or do a smooth transition to what you want. The side panels are separately turned on and off (together) and can fold down 90° (if you really wanted to) or all the way up to upside down on top of the main lamp. It's all folded together in the box, so just unfold and use. Only real issue is there's no telescoping function. So if you have a small desk and want it mounted at the back AND close to your surface, you might have to get creative. The auto brightness is interesting... it gets brighter when the ambient light goes down. I expected the opposite. But maybe this makes sense. I prefer manual control anyway. Overall, very great product for anyone working at a desk, writing, making, what have you. I love this thing already. There's a really good video review that will show you all you need to know. I bought two right then and there (for both tables) and I do not regret my decision at all.

reviews.title: It's Mostly Wonderful
reviews.body: This is a fun-to-use desk lamp with a clamp. It doesn't have the stability of a lamp with two side-by-side arms, however, when I type, it only wobbles a little. I've gotten used to it, so it isn't really a distraction. My favorite part of the lamp is the side arms that swing up or down, depending on where you want to put the light. For more focus on your desk; swing down. To illuminate the ceiling, or the entire room, swing up. You can control the brightness or illumination of each type of element, so that the arms that are pointed up can have light, while the ones pointed down can be dimmed or turned off altogether to prevent glare. The brightness starts as very dim and goes all of the way up to very bright (with some glare), and many steps in between. Nice! All in all, I've had this lamp for over a month now, and haven't noticed any defects or bad design, except for the slight wobble. It's great if you like to have a room for computer use while having the ability to light the whole room without glare. That's why I give it a '5'.

reviews.title: ABSOLUTELY LOVE IT
reviews.body: OMG I love this. I got a second one for me and one for my son for his room. Pretty much good to go out of the box, very easy to put up, stays where I want it, and good range of motion. IME these touch button devices usually default to off if you unplug/replug them, so they can't really be used with smart plugs. That is a HUGE plus for me. The one issue, if you can even call it an issue, is that it feels like it should rotate where the main lamp part is connected to the arm, but it doesn't. I've done that a couple times and heard a bit of a crack, but it doesn't seem to be broken. Which actually goes in the plus column now that I think about it. It's pretty sturdy, even against stupidity, LOL.

reviews.body: The first one I bought lasted less than an hour, then the light went out and it stopped charging my phone (that was the only extra thing I had plugged into it). I was disappointed because it was a perfect lamp for my needs. I almost just returned it for a refund but it was too good not to try one more time. I'm glad I did. The second one was sent to me about a month ago and it's worked perfectly since. I use this on my desk at work so on average it's used, either as just a charger or a charger and a lamp, for an average of 40ish hours a week for a month with no issues. The light brightness is adjustable so it's as bright as you want it to be (very bright on its highest setting). The neck adjusts in 2 spots so you can easily get it to the angle you need. The charging ports all work great and I use those every work day, as many as 3 at a time (there are 4). I haven't used the plugs much because I haven't needed them but they all work. If you think this fits your needs then definitely buy it. Just use it way before the return date in case you happen to get a dud like I initially did.

reviews.title: Bright adjustable desk lamp that really helps with detailed work

The two adjustable heads flood the work area from different angles so shadows are minimal and the five colour temps with ten brightness steps make it easy to find a comfortable setting for reading, painting or computer work. The touch controls are simple and the memory function means I get the same light each time I turn it on. The lamp stays cool and I had no flicker during long sessions, and the joints held position reliably. Two practical notes, the small pen holder is more decorative than useful and if you plan to run the USB port and the lamp at once use a good quality 5 volt 3 amp adapter to avoid flicker. Overall it met my expectations for flexible, eye friendly task lighting.

reviews.title: Well built and very stable; modern and minimalistic
reviews.body: This desk lamp certainly isn’t your typical desk lamp. The first thing I thought is that it looks like something straight from a science fiction movie. It’s not the prettiest lamp, but it has more of a clean, modern design with a black matte finish and slender profile. In my opinion, it’s just a more modern version of the swing lamp from back in my day. It obviously has more functionality when it comes to temperature and brightness levels, but to be honest, I find the height and angle adjustments to be a bit clunky. I suppose it’s because the arms are so long, not that they’re hard to turn. I like the slender profile of the lamp, though, because I can place the long, top light over my work space, and it brightens the area without getting in the way. I would say that the LED lighting is on par with most lamps of this type. I can adjust the brightness and temperature that’s suitable for my tasks: warm light for computer work, natural for crafting or writing. As you can see in the video when I turn off the lights, it casts a nice bright light over the desk area, but the rest of the room is fairly dark. Of course, you can adjust the angle of the light if needed, but it’s not going to brighten the entire room like a regular lamp could. But I suppose that’s why it’s called a DESK LAMP, not a table lamp. Concerning the build, unlike a regular lamp (and the old-timey swing lamp), the base is nice and flat, which means it doesn’t take up space. It can be used to hold a cup of coffee, your phone, or whatever else can fit on there. The base is not heavy, either, but it works well to counterbalance the lamp arms. The bottom post that’s connected to it is a little wobbly, though. Even so, it doesn’t seem to affect the stability. This lamp looks like it would be very tippy, but it’s surprisingly stable, even at the craziest angles. The design was obviously planned out well. Other than the post being a bit wobbly, the craftsmanship is good, too. So far, I’ve used this lamp almost every day since I received it. I might actually personalize it a little by putting a small plant on the base or put some pretty stickers on it. For now, it’s doing what I need it to do, and it doesn’t tip over easily, so I’m happy with it.

reviews.title: Build Quality Doesn’t Match the Great Lighting
reviews.body: The light itself does a good job and has a lot going for it, but the overall build quality left me wanting more, especially considering the price. It is made of metal, but it uses a very thin gauge that feels hollow and doesn’t give the impression of a premium desk lamp. The biggest drawback is the articulating arm. The pivot and rotating joints are extremely stiff and don’t move smoothly, so adjusting the lamp usually takes two hands and more force than it should. Making small positioning changes can be frustrating because the movement isn’t fluid. On the positive side, the lighting is excellent. It gets plenty bright, offers multiple brightness levels, and lets you switch between warmer and cooler color temperatures depending on what you’re doing. The slim, low profile design also looks nice on a desk, and the base is sturdy enough to keep the lamp stable even when the arms are extended into different positions. Overall, it performs well as a desk lamp and the lighting quality is hard to complain about. I just think the mechanical design and build quality should have been better at this price.

reviews.title: Highly useful sturdy metal lamp with true-to-life color lighting!
reviews.body: I needed a desk lamp that would work well for both desk work and artwork such as sketching. So far, this lamp has been excellent for these activities. The lamp is sturdy and well made, with a solid metal construction that feels durable without being too heavy to move around. One feature I really like is that it sits on a flat base rather than using a clip. That gives me more placement options, and the flat base doesn’t take up much desk space. The lamp has two adjustable joints that allow me to position the light exactly where I need it, or I can extend it fully upright to function more like an area lamp. It also provides a wide coverage area and can be adjusted quite high when needed. For art projects, I appreciate that it is designed to reproduce true-to-life colors. According to the description, it is flicker-free, glare-free, and emits no blue light, making it easier on the eyes. It offers five brightness levels and four color temperature settings ranging from white to warm white. The timer function is a unique feature, although I’m not sure how often I’ll use it. One thing that confused me initially was the power adapter, which looked like it might charge the lamp. So far, I have only been able to use the lamp while it is plugged in. My only real issue was that the top and middle sections arrived assembled in the wrong orientation. At first I thought the design was unusual because one section pointed up while the other pointed down. Fortunately, I was able to unscrew and reposition the sections correctly, and everything worked fine afterward. Overall, this is a sturdy, versatile lamp with excellent adjustability, wide light coverage, and features that make it especially useful for desk work and art projects.

I'm sure if you just wanted something for a gentle ambiance to compliment or help with a laptop then this is for you.

reviews.title: Perfect for all types of work!
reviews.body: I bought this out of necessity for working at home during the winter. I was expecting this lamp to be a lot bigger than it actually is. It comes in amazing compact box. The box could fit through your letter box (in its own box not the amazon one on top). Nicely packaged and very easy to expand to the desired height. The clamp has a good range of widths to fit a variety of surfaces. Even on a thin desk top it clamps really well i did not have to add any additional wood or anything to balance it. As light position is important to me as i suffer from migraines now and then. I was able to position this neatly behind my dual monitors to provide light on my desk without hitting my eyes. It looks smart and professional and easy to angle and adjust to suit. Lighting from it is fantastic. The different settings to choose are amazing. Warm, Daylight and Cool Light and adjustable light levels! Not only can you adjust the colour preference you can adjust how bright it is! Powering the lamp with USB IS THE BEST THING EVER! reviews.title: GREAT for dual side mount full desk lighting
reviews.body: Love this light. Only mounted for my hobby desk a few days. I had previously intended to make a 'Light Arch' to maximize lighting across the desk. While shopping planned area updates including clamp on lighting, this store had a picture of these light bars on both ends of a desk, and that was the spark I needed. Desk top is 65 inches wide. with lights adjusted as pictured, there is about 1 inch gap between ends of the heads. In CAD I modeled a simple rectangle tube with limit ridges for ends of heads. This tube acts as a coupler, so the hanging light bars not only help support each other, but also exhibit almost no wobble when the desk is jarred. Lights are wonderfully bright. I can adjust warmth to my liking. Construction is solid and high quality. The remotes are a great touch. Both sides of clamp come with non slip pads already attached. The control design is not particularly intuitive, but I give a pass for that given the memory to return lighting to previous state when turned on. Worst case, I turn on and touch the reading/writing button for maximum illumination. Improvement recommendation: adjust remote programming so touching reading/writing (MAX) button turns all lights on to that state, without needing to turn on first. I enjoy these lights for my purposes and am pleased 2 of them were my optimal solution as intended

reviews.title: Needs a heavier base for maximum positioning. Good desk light.
reviews.body: This is a lightweight desk lamp. The base of the lamp is covered in a felt material. The head of the light can be easily rotated so it can swivel left and right and the flexible arm is coated in a soft silicone material and bends easily. It also maintains the position you bend it into and doesn't sag since the head of the light is relatively light. The button controls are not individual buttons, they're plastic bubble buttons. Once the flexible arm is connected, it cannot be removed. The back of the lamp is just a plastic housing, no metal there to help dissipate heat, but even so I found that the back of the light only got slightly warm even at maximum brightness. Not even warm enough to be used as a hand warmer. The light has 5 brightness levels and the light is a very even diffuse light pattern and a wide cast area. The light output at maximum is quite bright, but not bright enough to over saturate printed material which would make it unreadable. The night light mode provides a much dimmer light output than is achievable with the brightness controls. It works very well as a night light. By default when pressing the night light button, the color temperature is warm. You can cycle through the other color temperatures after selecting night light mode. In order to get out of night light mode, you need to increase the brightness. When you turn the light off and turn it back on, it will remember which mode it was in last and use the same mode as it was in when it was turned off, this also applies to the night light mode, not just the brightness and color temperature. The brightness of the light isn't controlled via PWM, so it is flicker free. The 4 LEDs on the base illuminate to tell you which timer setting you're on. Due to the fact that the base is very lightweight and doesn't have any heft to it, you cannot move the head of the light too far away from the base. If you do, the imbalance of the weight will just cause the light to fall over. Also accidental bumps can knock it over easily. A heavier weighted base would help a lot here to allow for maximum range of positioning. I have another old fashioned halogen bulb desk lamp and it has a very heavily weighted base even though the head is lighter than this unit's head and it has very good stability as a result. The remote is a wireless remote and not an IR remote so there's no need to point it at the lamp to use it. I tested it, and it has very good range, going through 3 walls with ease. The base has a felt layer on the bottom providing some grip to keep it from easily sliding around. Although there is a USB-A and USB-C ports on the back, you need to provide your own cables. Included is a 12V/2A barrel connector power adapter, however it isn't UL or ETL certified, but then again neither is the lamp.

By default when pressing the night light button, the color temperature is warm. You can cycle through the other color temperatures after selecting night light mode. In order to get out of night light mode, you need to increase the brightness. When you turn the light off and turn it back on, it will remember which mode it was in last and use the same mode as it was in when it was turned off, this also applies to the night light mode, not just the brightness and color temperature. The brightness of the light isn't controlled via PWM, so it is flicker free. The 4 LEDs on the base illuminate to tell you which timer setting you're on. Due to the fact that the base is very lightweight and doesn't have any heft to it, you cannot move the head of the light too far away from the base. If you do, the imbalance of the weight will just cause the light to fall over. Also accidental bumps can knock it over easily. A heavier weighted base would help a lot here to allow for maximum range of positioning. I have another old fashioned halogen bulb desk lamp and it has a very heavily weighted base even though the head is lighter than this unit's head and it has very good stability as a result. The remote is a wireless remote and not an IR remote so there's no need to point it at the lamp to use it. I tested it, and it has very good range, going through 3 walls with ease. The base has a felt layer on the bottom providing some grip to keep it from easily sliding around. Although there is a USB-A and USB-C ports on the back, you need to provide your own cables. Included is a 12V/2A barrel connector power adapter, however it isn't UL or ETL certified, but then again neither is the lamp.

reviews.title: Simple lamp with a great selection of colors.
reviews.body: I see a lot of confusion about this product. The directions aren’t very descriptive, . 1. This product does have different color lights . 2. You can turn the color cycling off so that it stays on whatever color you desire. 3. You are able to adjust the brightness, there are three levels The thing to keep in mind is you navigate this one button device with the timing of your button presses. A long 3 second tap will turn it on and off. The default when you turn it on is the white color. The white is not too cool, nor too warm. You can adjust the brightness and at the highest level it is plenty bright if you need to find something in the room. I don’t think it will adequately light a large dark room on its own. But you can read using this light if you are within a few feet of the lamp (for most people). . If you want to change to the color setting, then a quick one second tap after the device is turned on. At this point, you will be on the color cycling mode. if you do nothing, the device will cycle through various shades of green, blue, red, yellow, etc. For example, you will see a turquoise blue, a cornflower blue, a hot pink, a pale green, etc. If you want to select a particular color, wait until it cycles to the color you like, and use a one second tap to select. This will pause it on the color that was lit when you tapped the button. If you want to turn the device off, just press the button for three seconds. You will have to repeat the process every time you turn the device on, It isn’t very resource-intensive so I wouldn’t let that deter you unless you are picky and this is a dealbreaker. I’m sure more expensive units have more robust memories, settings, and remote controls with more than one button to navigate. Only two items come in the box, the lamp (which is roughly 7” tall, and 4” wide at the base) and the power cord (which is not infuriatingly short) so setup is easy.. There’s no charging or batteries required. So far I like it and plan to keep it. I have insomnia, and read about light therapy. When I’m ready to sleep, I plan to change the color to an Amber/orangey/pink color to mimic the sunset to tell my body it’s time to get tired and go to sleep. I just received it, so cannot speak to longevity. I always come back and edit reviews if anything changes. If it stops working, I’ll update with a date so you’ll know how long mine lasted. Hope this helps! Edit : 6/1/24 I wanted to amend this review to specify that the color portion of this lamp is not dimmable. This may present an issue if someone is trying to use a color To fall asleep as I mentioned I was using this for. I agree that the lamp is very bright for colors. To fix this, I use a Small canvas bag I received with another product over it. I can still see the color and the lamp but it is much less less bright. If I didn’t have that bag I would use a scarf or some other type of lightweight fabric over it to use it for nighttime.

reviews.title: This lamp has a secret feature (a glowing review)
reviews.body: This lamp was purchased on 12/6/2025 for $18.99. The quality is more than adequate, but the lamp is very lightweight and definitely not what I would consider a premium product, however it looks good and functions well for the price that I paid. On the lamp that I received which is the model with a cord (not rechargeable) I can touch and hold the top control panel when the lamp is off, and it will come on in an ultra low mode which I absolutely love! Other than that if you were just to tap the top when the lamp is off there there are 3 brightness levels to cycle through with each tap: Low, Medium and High. The light that emits from this lamp is soft, the color temperature is pleasant and leans warm which for me is a great thing. To get to the colored mode you must press and hold on the top of the lamp while the white light is on and then tap the top to start/stop it from slowly cycling through the spectrum of colors, ie once it lands on your favorite color give the top panel a tap and it will freeze there on that color. The lamp also remembers that color too so the next time you enter color mode by holding down on the top panel it will come on directly to that last color which was used. I wish the brightness could be controlled when in the color mode but it cannot. I would guess that the brightness when in color mode is factory set to be somewhere around Medium and is not dimmable or adjustable in any way when in color mode which could obviously appear brighter to your eye depending on which color you have landed on or that the lamp is currently cycling through (if you just leave it continually and slowly flowing from one color to the next in a mostly smooth and seamless fashion). So far this is a nice, cheap and attractive bedside lamp.

reviews.title: Great light coverage
reviews.body: I use a 6ft by 3ft dining table as a desk because I need to be able to have textbooks and notebooks open while I also use the computer and take notes, and I was having trouble seeing print well without shuffling everything around as I went along with just the regular desk lamp. This lamp is clamped to a long side, and it doesn't take away from the valuable work space. It illuminates the entire tabletop nicely, and at full brightness, I can read everything around me easily. I keep it at about half brightness for a comfortable illumination when I'm not reading/writing, and that is slightly brighter than my other lamp was. The arms adjust easily, and allow for more light in specific areas if needed. The included remote control is very handy, and has several preset brightness/color settings, but also easily adjusts each manually, and includes a timer feature. Batteries are not included, though; it takes 2 AAA. My only reason for taking off one star is because the assembly, while it was essentially simple, was slightly harder because the connector at the top of the flexible arm was on the wrong side of the arm to easily connect to the light bar, and I had to finagle it a while to get it to be able to connect. Overall, I am very pleased with it and would buy again.

Highly recommend.

reviews.title: I'm 35 or 36 and I love this lamp ☺️🥰😅
reviews.body: 😃🥰 This thing honestly cheers me up every day☺️ its only been 1 week and im still gushing over how cute and fun this lamp is😃 PROS: • Clean, modern, smooth curves. I love that the branding logo is at least blended in nicely and not tacky.. pretty minimal. Not tacky. • I LOVE the DIY functions. Choosing your own colors from the color wheel is awesome. There are many colors to choose from ! #1 reason for buying this lamp was the DIY functions 🥰 • Price was okay, but still a bit steep. I bought 2 for a total of 162$ ... (you got a deal if you bought 2) 80 bucks is a bit steep still... even with all this lamp does. I would not pay more than 80 for this lamp... especially because it's not cordless like the updated one. • I love that they update the app with new options for preset scenes! I didn't even expect that and then I saw new ones appear one day. • I love that you can dim the background color in the DIY Sketch section. Helps a lot with night time chill time... plus looks great paired with bright colors in contrast to the dimmed background. I'm an adult female and I have so much fun playing with this lamp. All in all I LOVE this lamp. The cons/improvements I list below, are just me being very critical of the color limitation. CONS / Improvements • I wish you could get deeper colors.. like a deep striking red, a basic 'green crayon' green, a forest green... etc but it's just not possible. The greens are lime green to aqua. The reds aren't red, they are hot pink to coral pink even on the reddest setting. • The lamp is very bright, even on its lowest 1% setting. I can't have these on at night when I'm sleeping... which is kind of a bummer. Sometimes we have to turn them off when we're watching tv at night too, because theyre just so bright. Even the various sleep preset scenes that do have darker dimmed colors.. it's still quite bright. *** Correction though ... I found in the DIY Sketch that you can actually dim the main background color. Huge plus ! Now night time wont be so bright and I can really make other colors pop against the dimmed background. • Wish it were cordless of course, but I am sure they will make a cordless version since they already did with the Table Lamp Pro JBL speaker one. Hopefully they keep these ones smaller like they are but make them cordless. • For the preset 'scene settings' ..... you can't actually change the colors to anything you want. For the ones you CAN customize (there are a few you 100% can not) There is a list of 8 different color "combos" to choose from. If you don't like a color used in any of those 8 color combos, you cant do anything about it. So for my favorite scene settings, I can only use that scene if I use one of the 8 pre set options provided for that scene. This is shown on one of my review photos. However, I have recreated some of the "preset scenes" using the DIY/Sketch function. That enables me to use whatever colors I choose.. but still there are limitations around this. For example, the "Fire" Preset Scene, you can't choose other colors for that fire movement scene at all. Which sucks. It would look very cool in other colors. *** EDIT --- I stand corrected after exploring some more. In the DIY section, you do have "fire" as an effect and you can change the color of it... including various colors it will morph into. It just doesnt show on the actual 'fire' preset scene. Very happy to have realized this ☺️ • The Ai function is super cool.. and I know it works awesome on their other products such as their light panel or curtain lights... this one has limitations only because of the inability to use darker or duller color. For example in my last photo you can see I asked for a moody greyish blue sky... slate grey/slate dull blue would have been awesome with white clouds... but it can't do those colors (slate greyish blue). HOWEVER now that I know I can dim the background significantly in the DIY section, I can maybe pull this off. Finding a way to realllyy have "millions" of colors to choose from would be great. I'm being really picky here lol I do love the color options it does have. 😍🥰 With most variations of any color on the DIY color wheel, outside of the most obvious variations, the difference is barely barely noticeable, even if on the app they show as very different shades or tints of blue, there is barely a difference once on the lamp...... Though there often IS a difference. You can see the slight change when you switch back and forth, for the most part. You get a lot of pink, since the entirety of the red are variations of pink.. plus the actual entire pink section. Much of the "purples" are actually fuschia pink. You have to go very blue to get a regular "purple". There are way less variations of green, purple, yellow. Green for example, there is only lime green and quickly goes to aqua, or yellow on the other side. Basic green crayon color would be awesome. Purple usually looks more blue or fuschia.. depending what colors you pair it with it or whether purple is totally by itself. Or if you dim the background color, your 'purple'(fuschia) will probably turn more towards actual purple. When I use a red background, (which shows hot hot reddish pink to orangey red.. never real red).... i can get a purple heart on it by making the heart blue. It then shows up purple. So there are tricks. ☺️ I am really happy with the custom colors though despite these few limitations haha I'm making it sound worse than it is. It's an awesome lamp. 🥰 I wish I could draw/sketch white and grey mountains... like light grey with contrasting dark grey and slate grey, with white tips mountains. I will play around with it some more though, because in the DIY "Fire" effect, I see some 'slate' greys possible be used. So it seems possible? Another example of this limitation: 🎅🎄Christmas colors.. there are none. ... Since red is hot pink and green is lime green. So the preset christmas scenes do not give christmas vibes at all. Same with the Halloween... purple is never purple enough unless you have zero colors near it... or place enough blue next to fuschia to turn the fuschia a nice purple. The halloween presets that have orange and purple next to eachother, the purple never shows well enough to look Halloweeny. In my opinion. St Patricks Day Preset Scenes are capable of lime green only... Other than that, These lamps are so awesome. 😁 I'm totally buying more Govee products 😏😛 I ordered the Uplighter off their website just days after I bought these lamps😛 One small annoyance is I ordered from the Govee website 5 days ago and my uplighter still isnt here. I went through the website bc it was on sale for 170 + an extra 8$ off coupon code....... 5 days later today the lamp is here on Amazon on sale for 160..... So I could have got the lamp within 24hrs had I been able to use Amazon but they lagged 5 days on matching their amazon store sale to their website sale. Hopefully it arrives today.

reviews.title: GOVEE is where it's at it seems
reviews.body: I have several Govee products and I have watched a lot of growth over the years. What brought me back to Govee was not only their string lights, but the customer support is amazing. And they probably would win the popularity vote if there was one. Now it is getting to the point that when Govee releases another product, I want to buy it whether I need it or not. This table light is no exception! I wanted it just because it's Govee and who doesn't want a table side light that can do a heck of a lot more than just be a light. The scenes are amazing and there are so many to choose from. So not only can it be a white light that you can change the brightness but it can be programed to similate a sunrise when you get up or a sunset when you go to bed or any other combination in between. I had a night light with a smart bulb in it and was quite happy with it. But the Table light seemed like it would be the perfect companion. No matter what, I like this light, but there are a couple of things that could use help. This goes for just about every light strip that Govee has and it has to do with the music feature. For the most part it syncs well enough to most beats, but what bothers me and a ton of others is that when there is no sound, it still dances with light. So it's not exact. One day they will address this issue. reviews.title: Surprisingly Premium Monitor Light — Great for Daily Work and Low-Light Days
reviews.body: I’ve been using this monitor light, for several weeks, on an Acer display for daily work, and overall it’s been a really solid addition to my desk setup. Installation was straightforward — it mounted easily and felt secure once positioned. No complicated setup or tools required, which I always appreciate. The lighting itself is where this really shines (no pun intended). The adjustable color temperature range from warm to cool is useful depending on what you’re doing. It can give you more of a relaxed desk lamp vibe in warmer tones or a bright, focused work light when you need better visibility for detailed tasks. There’s also an auto-dimming feature, but I personally prefer setting a static brightness level once and leaving it there. The included remote control is a nice touch and honestly makes the product feel more premium than the price point would suggest. Build quality feels better than expected — not cheap or flimsy. I use this every day for work, and it’s especially helpful during gloomy weather or late afternoons when natural light drops off. It reduces the need for overhead lighting and keeps the workspace evenly illuminated without glare on the screen. My only real complaint is the articulation adjustment. The mounting design doesn’t provide quite enough tension, so adjusting the angle sometimes requires two hands to keep everything aligned. It’s not a dealbreaker, but it’s an area that could be improved in a future version. Overall, this has been a great upgrade for my workspace and something I didn’t realize I needed until I started using it consistently.

reviews.title: Excellent monitor light at a great value!
reviews.body: I'd been considering a monitor desk light for some time now, but I could not justify the price tag giong as high as $200 on the BenQ "original" that sorta started it off with these types of lights. This was a couple years ago now and clearly today there are many different versions of similar monitor lights on the market, the Quntis being among them, and which appears to be a fairly close copy of the BenQ light. I found this one on Amazon, priced around $40 for the non-remote (remote being rather superfluous in my opinion) version and did a little comparison research to see if this might be a good fit. There are many similar monitor lights out there, some cheaper and going as low as ~$25 and some obviously more expensive. I figured the Quntis was a good middle ground price-wise and took a shot to see if this would fit the bill. Indeed it does! Whether or not, or how close a copy to the BenQ the Quntis is I don't know for sure, as I've never seen the alternatives, but I can say this one is very well designed and well constructed, some plastic and also some metal in the construction and on close inspection the quality is definitely there. The mounting system is simple and functional and adapted perfectly to my HP Omen gaming monitor, which I would say has a somewhat non-standard profile shape and thickness, at least at the top where the light mounts. No problem, the mount is easily adjustable and rests perfectly and securely on my top monitor edge with full confidence that it's not going anywhere, or is any way unstable or wonky. The light controls on top of the light are easily accessible, operated by touch and the tactile "buttons" are shaped so they can be easily felt when operating the light. There are stepless controls for brightness and color temperature, as well as a sort of "auto" button that adjusts the brightness based on the ambient light in the room, which is nice. The lightbar throws a very nice pool of light on your keyboard and desk space in front of, and not directly ON, your monitor - right where you need it - without any glare, or being too harsh. Again, the quality, brightness and temperature of the light is easily adjustable to your liking. The monitor mounting system is sensible, simple, highly adjustable and highly functional. Lamp is powered by USB and in my case plugs right into a USB port on my monitor and totally invisible, hidden behind. Anyway, I guess I might have got a little carried away with this review, but tldr; the Quntis is an excellent monitor light and if this is something you've been looking at, I don't think you can go wrong with this one.

reviews.title: Perfect... in most keys
reviews.body: I got this lamp to use on a grand piano at church. The arm reaches across reasonably well from the side (though it doesn’t extend far enough to be fully centered over the music desk). The multiple color temperatures and brightness levels are very helpful for accommodating the preferences of various users, and all our pianists seem to like it. It works smoothly and perfectly... in most keys. BUT if you like to play in D-flat, beware! I just discovered that the resonance point of the casing appears to be a D-flat (138.591 Hz). The plastic started buzzing quietly when playing strong tonic chords in that key. This was, of course, horrifying. I assume the same disturbing outcome holds true when playing in C-sharp major, since the identical notes are used, but I only had sheet music in D-flat today. More testing would be needed to determine whether the issue extends to enharmonic keys, but this didn’t seem urgent to share here, since: • I didn’t want to go into too much detail that isn’t relevant to the average consumer (because we all hate that), and • Only psychos play in C-sharp major anyway. I realize this acoustic phenomenon may not affect all potential buyers of this lamp, but it seems like this particular harmonic bug could be mentioned somewhere in the description—if not in the product title itself—just so that members of the five-flats-loving community have some warning. Oh, also, the buzzing stopped as soon as I moved the arm slightly, so there’s that.

I've wiped it down here for the photos, but do realize that it is a dust/fingerprint/cat hair collector. Smudges show up, so if you're not willing to wipe it down every now and then you might be disappointed with it's overall aesthetic look. Pro tip: I keep a pack of Pledge multi-surface wipes ( Pledge Multi Surface Everyday Wipes Fresh Citrus, 25-Count (Pack of 4) ) in a drawer near my desk to wipe both it and the lamp down - takes a few seconds and looks as good as new. I mostly use this lamp at its lowest setting, as it provides a nice ambience to my work area. Each of the preset light levels can be brightened and dimmed. If I'm going to be doing real work, the light gets bright enough by itself to make reading from a textbook or paperwork comfortable and without strain. Usually one of the reading or middle settings is as bright as I'll go for reading actual pages from a book, and I only use the brightest settings if I'm struggling to see something small like jewelry or I'm fiddling with some component or part of my computer. It does get quite bright. I haven't used the timer function, but there is an automatic 60 minute timer included. Overall, it's a versatile little lamp. I got mine on sale at Christmas during a flash sale, for thirty something dollars, and I think it's well worth it. The listed price, however, is complete rubbish - total waste to pay full price regardless of how well it works, as it is simply made up of plastic and LED bulbs. Wait for a sale and you'll be happy with it. I've included photos of the lamp with various light levels and in different positions.

reviews.title: All Good except 1 Big Thing
reviews.body: TLDR: Solid build, good light quality, useful brightness and color controls, and a swing arm that does most of what you want. The big catch is that it does not behave the way modern smart home users will expect, and the mounting geometry has some real-world limits the listing photos do not show. Four stars, with caveats worth knowing before you click buy. Let me lead with the good, because there is plenty of it. The light itself is genuinely nice. Plenty of brightness for working, reading, or close-up tasks, and the color temperature options give you warm yellow, neutral white, and a cooler white-blue depending on what you are doing. Eleven brightness levels is more granularity than I expected. The arm extends and folds well, and the head pivots to put light right where you want it. It runs on USB, the wall adapter is included, and the wattage is low enough that you can power it from a laptop port if that is convenient. The clamp mount is solid and holds tight once you have it in place. A note on installation. The clamp wants a specific amount of mounting surface, and my location had less than the lamp wanted in one direction. I pulled out a Dremel and shaved a small relief into the underside so the clamp could sit properly. Not a complaint, just a heads up if your desk has a thick lip, a beveled edge, or a rounded corner where you want this to live. Now, the big thing. This lamp does not default to on when power is restored. If you turn it off and walk away, fine. If your power blips, or if you have it on a smart switch that cuts power, the lamp comes back off. To turn it back on you have to walk over to the lamp and press the little button on the inline cord controller, which sits close to the base of the arm and is not always easy to reach. This matters because the listing advertises a memory function, and modern buyers, especially anyone with a smart home setup, are going to read that and assume something it does not actually mean. Here is what is happening. The memory function does work, in a narrow sense. When you press the on button, the lamp comes back at whatever brightness and color mode you used last. It does not have to be reset every time. That is real and it is useful. What the memory function does not do is preserve the on/off state across a power cut. The reason is that this is a soft-touch push button rather than a mechanical switch. The lamp's electronics have to be powered to know they are on, and when power is removed and restored the default state is off. A traditional mechanical switch physically holds the circuit closed and is why your bedroom lamp comes back on when the power flickers. This one does not, by design. If you live in a fully manual lighting world, this is a non-issue. You will press the button and life goes on. If you have your office lights on a smart switch, or you have ever said the words "Google (or Alexa), turn on the lights," this is going to be an ongoing minor annoyance. I had assumed, like most lights, that I could plug this into the same smart switch as the rest of the room and have it come on with everything else. Instead it sits there dark while everything else lights up, waiting for me to walk over and poke it. The other thing worth flagging is the arm geometry. The first segment, the one closest to the clamp, is not designed to swing forward. It folds up and back, which is fine on an open desk where you have empty wall behind you. If you are mounting this on the back edge of a desk that sits against a wall, on the lip of a hutch, on top of a shelving unit, or inside a cubicle, you are going to discover that the elbow needs room to bow outward behind the lamp. The listing photos all show the lamp on an open desk with nothing behind it, so this is not obvious until you have it in hand. Plan your mounting location with that in mind. There is also a 45 minute auto-off timer button on the controller. Apparently aimed at bedtime reading. I have not used it but it is there if you want it. Four stars. The light is good and the build is good. The memory function exists but means something different than a smart home buyer will assume, and the mounting flexibility has limits that the listing does not show. If you can live with those, this is a nice lamp at a fair price. If you were hoping to drop it into an automated lighting routine, you are going to want to know about the default-off behavior before you order.

reviews.title: An Excellent Lamp with a Small Caveat
reviews.body: This is a great lamp. It is VERY bright, and has lots of cool color and warmth settings. It's a very light sheet steel construction, and folds up neatly with a convenient hand screw for quick removal and installation. The boom, arm, and light mantle are highly flexible and have a solid range of motion, and keep their position very well. The light strip is VERY large, with LOTS of LEDs and casts a very significant amountt of light. In it's highest setting, probably several thousand lumens across each LED. It is powered by USB, and draws close to 15 watts. The manufacture rates the light at 12 watts, however, they only supply a 10 watt, 5-volt @ 2-amp USB wall adapter. The supplied wall adapter started to cut in-and-out after about 3 months of regular nightly use at 80%+ brightness plus warmth settings. If you don't run the light past roughly 75%, you won't have any problems. Otherwise, I'd recommend upgrading to a 5-volt @ 3-amp USB wall adapter to save the hassle. For that I'm deducting a star. Your mileage may vary. I paid about $36 in December of 2025. It was worth the money. I do structural engineering and CAD, and like to see my keyboard while up at night. TL;DR: Worth the money, well built, and very bright, but needs at least a 5-volt @ 3-amp USB wall adapter to work to it's full capacity, as the supplied 2-amp adapter is not substantial enough for light levels above 75% plus warmth settings. Pictures coming ASAP.

I get tired of having to keep turning it on, so I bought this desk lamp. It’s a good lamp. The color and brightness choices are good. I agree it’s a little bit light-weight, but that is not an issue for me. I bought it because I liked the cordless charging dock, and the pen holder is a nice addition. reviews.body: I ordered this for better lighting for miniature painting as well as lighting up my desk area. The simple minimalist look is sleek and contemporary meeting almost any desk or setup universally. The lamp feels sturdy and solid but you can tell the material is not all metal but some pressed plastic or much cheaper thin alloy material which is non-magnetic, maybe thin aluminum. The buttons are touch sensors not actual clicky buttons so that could put some folks off but non-issue for me. The lighting has color adjustments so you can light to you preference whether warm, cool, or cold and even has an automatic brightness and stepping feature built in. Honestly I though the brightness feature was a gimmick however using it as a back light in my office has improved my eye comfort from long periods at the computer for work. While the lamp is very easy to adjust and stays in place when moved the information presented makes it seem like the lamp head would rotate 180º which it does just not in the direction expected, meaning the lamp must always be parallel to the surface it is placed on no exceptions. I dinged it a star because of this as the image shown seems to be a bit misleading whether intentional or not. It uses a power adapter with barrel socket to the lamp so is not portable and does not charge, has no remote though there are auto stepping and brightness features you must manually activate the lamp.

reviews.title: Lovely desk lamp for my mini office.
reviews.body: I ordered this desk lamp off of Vine for my office because I needed one and was remodeling. I was using just a regular light that is on my ceiling and it was creating a glare on my Monitor that was hard on my eyes. This one is much better. It is adjustable. Bendable, Dimmable and has eye saving features with different colors of light. A White neon type. A medium light and a Warm light that is very easy on the eyes. Setting it up was pretty easy. So you can keep it horizontal looking or pivot them to the front for when working on things. reading documents or need to see fine details. The clip was nice and sturdy on my desk. No bends or breaks. I hooked it on pretty tight to. Solid build quality all the way through. All in all I really like it. I think this lamp makes a great office light and can also be a very good workshop light. Or lab light. Or even just a reading lamp for your room. The retail price was more then fair and it just works. No complaints. I love it and can recommend it. Thanks a ton.

reviews.title: Long LED heads, super bright, high and flexible stand
reviews.body: This is a double-head LED lamp that is very bright and raised high on desk edge. The head lights are two LED panels that can rotate 90 degrees horizontal between front and side. It doesn’t have a lamp stand on desk. It has a desk edge mounting bracket that can be mount to a variety of thickness of desk. A fixed metal pole attached to the mounting bracket. Then a flexible goose neck attached to the metal pole which then hold the LED heads. The goose neck can be adjusted to any angle of your choice. Both the metal pole and the flexible goose neck bring the LED heads very high over desk that you can place monitors underneath the LED heads. Both LED panels can independently rotate at axis of the center of the LED heads. On top of the center of LED heads there are 4 touch buttons: power on/off, light color temperature, dim and brightness. These buttons are very sensitive and responsive. In addition to the control buttons on the LED heads, the desk lamp comes with tiny remote control for convenience. It has exactly the same 4 buttons as those on the LED heads. The desk lamp comes with a special power adapter which provides 24V/1A power for the lamp. The wire attached to the LED heads can be inserted into the slots of the goose neck and metal pole, so that it is not visible. A very detailed design. Excellent. The bottom screw plate of the mounting bracket is kind of small compare to the weight of the lamp that it needs to hold. Not sure if it will be strong enough and durable. So far so good. Very good desk lamp. Highly recommend.

reviews.body: Review of LED Desk Lamp for Office Home & Battery Operated Lamp Rechargeable Lamp Foldable & Portable Light, LED Desk Light Strip, 3 Brightness Dimmable Small Desk Lamp Wireless Reading Lamp (White) I needed a smaller, lightweight, bright and flexible LED desk light to use for reading and when taking some closer pictures with my phone. With my existing lighting, I had difficulties in getting the lighting correct and without shadows. After looking at several items on Amazon, I opted for this one. The price was better for me too. I ordered the white one but thought that I had received a pink one upon receipt since the one pictured on the box was pink. Apparently, the boxes all show pink ones, I suppose. This is made in China (pictured). Likes: This light is quite flexible and allows different angles. Obviously, if you extend the arm with the light out too far, this will fall forward since it disrupts the center of gravity too much. If I needed it to extend farther, it would not take something of much weight to be placed on the base to keep it from tipping over. The light is quite bright. It has 3 settings of brightness. The easy-to-work single button facilitates on level 1, then level 2, then level 3, and then back off (I tried to show the different levels of lighting in my pics). The button is very easy to operate. The light came charged enough to try. The instructions suggest going ahead and charging it, which I did. A small light near the charging port illuminates red to show it is charging and turns green when completed. The charging cable is a standard USB A to USB C. I like the fact that it is rechargeable. I found this to be a reasonable price. It has a small footprint and easily folds away for storage. It's aesthetically pleasing. There are small pads on the bottom of the base to keep it from sliding around. These would make nice and inexpensive gifts. Dislikes: I really don’t have any dislikes at this time. Neutrals: Some reviewers reported the light not lasting very long, both battery life and functionality. Time and usage will be the judge. I will try to update this review accordingly if necessary. My wife immediately clamped it onto her pottery worktable and declared it perfect. As it turns out, she was right. The adjustable arms make it easy to position the light exactly where it's needed, and it does an excellent job of filling in the shadows on cloudy days or late afternoons when natural light isn't cooperating. The light is bright, even, and makes it easier to see texture, details, and surface work without constantly repositioning pieces. It's not the most conventional-looking lamp I've ever seen, but after watching it in use for a while, I stopped noticing how it looked and started appreciating how well it worked. In the pottery studio, that's about as high a compliment as a tool can get.

reviews.title: Best light I have found
reviews.body: I have searched for and bought so many different kinds of lights for my sewing machine station. None of them have been satisfactory until this light. There are two important properties I need. Brightness and flexibility. First Brightness: I am 80 and need a lot of light where the needle is stitching. Yes there is a sewing machine light that turns on when the machine is running but even though it gets hot enough to burn skin, it is frustratingly dim. This desk light has 4 color temperature settings from warm to cold controlled by one button and 4 brightness levels controlled by another button so 16 different choices in all. These are regulated by lightly touched buttons on the lowest arm and the highest brightness out shines any other light I have tried. AND there is no flicker like many LEDs. So many lights have claimed amazing brightness only to be completely useless. Flexibility: A sewing machine is a very challenging lighting problem since the needle (where the work is happening) is hidden under the mass of the machine. The light has to be mounted on the right side of the machine so it doesn't block the movement of fabric. The right side of the machine is also solid and won't let any light pass through! Ideally it has to be located between the sewer and the machine so the sewer does not throw a shadow. This desk light offers EXTREME flexibility with 4 joints which all articulate in multiple ways but once the arms are set where I want the angles do not slip. The light might look very awkward in its placement on my table (and please excuse the mess!) but the outermost arm is throwing light exactly where I need it. The fabric can easily move underneath it. The other two arms are lighting up the overall table nicely. It is very well made and the clamp keeps the light steady even with such a long reach. I love this light.

reviews.title: Ambient light
reviews.body: I'm obsessed with these lights—I own two now, one in my bedroom and another in my living room. The only reason I'm not giving it five stars is the night light feature, which ironically is the setting I use the most. It can't be configured through the app, and activating it directly on the lamp is frustrating. You have to turn the unit off and lightly touch both the top and bottom at the same time, which isn't intuitive and doesn't always work on the first try. I also found the preset mood scenes to be somewhat underwhelming. Aside from setting schedules, there isn't much room for customization, so they don't add a lot of value in my opinion. That said, if you're looking for a stylish lamp with excellent ambient lighting and tons of options, I still highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Great Smart Lamp
reviews.body: I looked all over for an actual LAMP that worked with Alexa. Everything else seems to be a lamp with an included smart bulb. The issue begins if you can't really use the app nor can verbalize Alexa commands. Since my mom is able to do neither, she didn't really have a reliable way for the lamp to be turned off at night other than a lamp's physical switch. The issue there is that means there's no power to the smart bulb to have Alexa turn it back on. With this lamp, not only are we able to have her turn it off at night, but I can also have it timed to turn on in the morning with 'sunlight' level light to help her wake up, as well as have it timed to turn on a bit before sunset so her room is lit for when she wants to do things there in the evening. Overall, this is a great lamp, and I am fully happy with the purchase and after setting it up. I will note that there are other features I didn't mention, like different types of light (soft light for reading, 'daylight' for helping wake up, etc.) as well as multiple colors of light available.

reviews.title: Best Lamp I've Owned
reviews.body: It is without a doubt the best lamp I've had the privilege of buying. It feels, looks, and functions at a premium and high quality. The neck of the lamp is what I'd consider nearly perfectly balanced between flexibility and sturdiness. With the adjustable angles of the light bars themselves, as well as the neck, it will unquestionably meet your positional needs. The touch controls are practically flawless. They work every time they are pressed, as inputted without fail. They are positioned as such you can easily identify and press them at any time without having a clear visual of them. I was extremely satisfied with the quality of light itself. The range of warmth/cool strikes a node of nostalgia and comfort for me that is difficult to explain. They are arranged perfectly, and can satisfy any particular need for a specific light task by task throughout your day. The brightness levels do not fail to complement this standard, there are a satisfactory amount of levels ranging from beautifully ambient dim to possibly light up the room. A more niche comment, my desk has oddly positioned metal framing that goes underneath in a rectangle. It is often difficult for clamp based items to function on my desk because of it, but the size of this clamp was so good it still managed to clamp all the way up and firmly onto the edge of my desk. I saved plenty of space with this lamp. I have literally 0 complaints. I'd buy it again.

reviews.title: Great execution of a novel designed and versatile LED desk lamp
reviews.body: This desktop lamp is BRILLIANT! Most items I see from Amazon ads are gimmicky and often overpriced. Such nonsense does not apply to this versatile LED desk lamp. Was shopping for better lighting than the clip-on ring light I have, which is harsh on my eyes and does not provide illumination for my desk. Saw this lamp popped up in my search for webcam lighting. Checked the reviews and was pleasantly surprised on the positive feedbacks. It's a creative design yet priced as the same cost as simple non-harsh webcam/video streaming lighting. Works really well and has plenty of color shades (5) and brightness levels to suit a variety of light settings. Wide enough to handle my home office setup with a laptop screen plus 34" main screen of an external monitor. Dual tilt function means I can cast enough light on my profile on video conferencing calls and rotate back to original position when I am off calls and typing away on the daily grind. Truly happy with the purchase and rarely am I bothered to write a review, but here I am giving the lamp some high raves.

reviews.title: Exactly what I needed.
reviews.body: Unboxing: Everything was in the box with no missing parts. Instructions were included. Assembly: Not hard to assemble at all. Took about 5 to 10 minutes. As usual I suggest reading the instructions and following along. Not difficult to understand or follow. Function: Everything has worked as expected. The clamp connected fine to my desk and after setting it up I have not needed to move or change the clamp in any way. Holds nicely and does its job without issue. The bendable arm is easy to move and holds the lights in place. Even when changing the positioning of the lights themselves it does not change the bendable arms position. Its also nice that when I want to adjust the position of the bendable arm it is not difficult to do so. The lights themselves are sufficiently bright for day or night use. I find it particularly helpful to be able to change the light color along with brightness. Rotating the lights with near 360 degree rotation is also helpful. It works great with a web cam. I can easily tilt them to face me to provide better lighting for web meetings and then tilt them down to be out of my eyes when just working. I would purchase it again given the chance and have no regrets thus far.

reviews.title: Nicer than I thought it would be. Recommend.
reviews.body: This lamp is much nicer than I expected. It lights up my entire desk, and it's very well made. The light doesn't produce any glare, either. The assembly is easy, with one screw at the base you screw in with the included screwdriver. I like the multiple light colors that you can pick, based on lighting conditions or just your mood at the time. The controls are touch operated, there's blue tiny LED by the power button that indicates the lamp is plugged in. This blue LED turns off when the lamp is on, so it won't shine in your eyes, which is good design. Also, the lamp automatically returns to the previous color and brightness settings you had when you turned it off, which is very convenient. The lamp gooseneck seems to be high quality, and the lights swivel a full 180 degrees. The housing is nice aluminum, and the gooseneck is a nice rubber-like material. The cord properly runs through the lamp, hidden, unlike cheaper models of this lamp. Overall, I highly recommend this version over the others. I searched, and it seemed to me this was the best version. It might not be the absolute best, but it seems to be high enough quality and of a good design to last a long time. Recommend.

Don’t think that’s the case. Room for improvement perhaps!

reviews.title: Recommended. Could be improved but good as is.
reviews.body: TL;DR: Recommended but could be improved. I'm using this lamp in my living room to illuminate a bluetooth keyboard in the evening. The gooseneck keeps the lamp where I put it and feels like it's well made and will last. The lamp has 3 color settings - white, amber and off-white(?). I'm not sure why they choose off-white rather than red, which is useful when you don't want to compromise your night vision any more than you have to. The lamp seems to be quite efficient; I've been running it on an old no-name (and over-rated IMHO) 30,000 mA USB power bank for about 12 hours, and I've got 87% of the battery left. It's wide enough to illuminate a full-size keyboard, but the LED strip is designed so it's easy to keep glare off the screen. I've got two power banks, neither of which start when the lamp is plugged in; you must push the button on the power bank to turn on the output. This is because the lamp (and other devices) don't draw enough current when the lamp is off for the power bank to notice it's connected! As a result, if I turn the lamp off (such that the lamp's blue standby light comes on) the power bank thinks nothing is connected and shuts down after a few seconds (and thus losing my dimmer adjustments). The lamp has a wide illumination range; it gets quite bright, and dims to a very low level, such that I can keep it on when I'm not using it and it isn't distracting. This is important because WHEN HE LAMP LOSES POWER IT FORGETS HOW MUCH I've DIMMED IT (for which I have deducted a star). To compensate for this, when I turn the light on for the evening I set the default (white) light to the level I need to view my keyboard; I set the other two colors to the lowest level. When I want to take a break and watch TV for a bit, I select the amber color and I can dim the light is enough that I don't notice it. Then when I want to type some more I switch to the white color and I'm in business. I have one other nit: The lamp's gooseneck threads onto the top of a stiff upright tube, which screws into the desk mount. This tube is long enough that I can barely position the lamp perfectly (due in part to my setup - others may not find it too long). This could be solved by shipping a 2nd tube about half the length of the current tube. This way I could use the short tube and it would give the gooseneck more 'reach'. Some may find it useful to use both tubes for added height.

I just hate having to reset it every time I adjust the TV.

reviews.title: Compact Air Purifier Best Suited for a Bedroom, Home Office, or Smaller Open Layout Condo
reviews.body: DREO recently updated their Air Purifier line for 2026 with the release of both the 539S and this model, the 338S, which offers max room coverage up to 856ft² vs. 1176 ft². Otherwise, these models offer very similar operation and performance, so do consider the room size and square footage you are looking to cover. Build quality-wise, the 338S is another solid device that is compact in size at just over 14"H x 9"W and weighs under 6lbs. Unlike the 539S model with a transparent lower section of the cylinder style that reveals the 3-in-1 HEPA filter, the 339 opts for a solid white style from top to bottom, with the filter hidden inside. Personally, I prefer this look, but you do have to make a point of opening the unit to inspect the filter regularly for maintenance or replacement. The display is clear and easy to read, along with the 4-colour gradient visual, both of which can be turned off so they aren't a light source in a bedroom. This is a WiFi-connected device that you can also control via the DREO app, which is free and easy to use. It actually has to be one of the easiest apps I've ever used in terms of getting a device connected and set up, in minutes, literally to DREO's credit. This device can also be integrated into either Google Home or Alexa for voice control. I like the real-time monitoring, history and ability to schedule the operating times as well. The app is also your source for upgrading the firmware, when applicable. In terms of performance, the 338S operates relatively quietly and goes about its business of monitoring and cleaning an average-sized room every 15 mins or its max coverage every hour. Like the 539S model, the fan is quiet at level 1-2 and only starts to be more audible above 3. It really isn't too noticeable unless the air particulate matter suddenly worsens from cooking or smoke, which unfortunately has become more of an issue due to summer wildfires each year now. Overall, if you are looking for a compact air purifier for your bedroom, home office or a small condo, the DREO 338S may be the model for you. If you need to have coverage closer to 1,200 ft², then the DREO 539S may be more suited for your needs, but both models perform very similarly based on my time testing them both for review. Price-wise, there is only a $20 difference, so you may want to opt to upsize, so to speak. Both are a recommended buy, and hopefully you'll also perhaps catch either on a deal.
