reviews.title: I really like the Core Sonic 1.0, but there are a few annoyances
reviews.body: The Core Sonic electric toothbrush looks like a premium toothbrush. From the moment you unpack it, you see a really nice box. In the theme of sustainability, most of the packaging is made of cardboard, but it looks so much nicer than your usual cheap plastic packaging. There is nice colored printing showing everything that is included. The items are neatly stored and there are manuals included. Everything just screams quality. If I were just going by packaging, this would be a 5 star. Inside the box is your electric toothbrush, one plant-based brush head, a magnetic (mirror) mount with adhesive backing, and a magnetic stand/charging cable. The toothbrush is attractively colored and I like the fact that there are different colors to choose from when buying. It is not bulky and would be perfect for traveling (unfortunately, no case included though). There is only one brush head included and at time of ordering, there are replacement heads being sold in a 3pk for around $19. It seems a little expensive, but given that they are plant based, I can understand the pricing. The brush cover is a snap on type. It does not cover three back of the toothbrush though, do you may want to use a different cover if you are traveling. The magnetic mirror mount seems like a good addition, but I don't want to want to attach adhesive to my mirror and my mirror is also a good foot higher than the counter so I wouldn't trust using it personally. Next comes one of my cons. The included charger is proprietary, so you are reliant on the manufacturer's charger. The stand is magnetic, but since it is lightweight, the toothbrush can easily be knocked off balance accidentally. The cable is also non-removable so if it is damaged, you need to replace the entire base. And while the cable is USB C, this requires you to have an open USB C charging brick. I have a bunch of USB C cables, but I don't actually have many open USB C chargers. I would have much preferred just a USB C port so I can use my own USB C cable so I can easily connect it to one of my many open USB C cables. I guess the built in cable helps with waterproofing, but it is a bad inconvenience. Luckily, the battery is supposed to last about a month, though I am not sure how accurate that claim is. As for usage, there is only one button, so it can't get any easier to use than turning it on. You turn it on and then you can press the button again for a stronger brush. The toothbrush will remember the last used setting. And there is supposed to be a pressure sensor to tell you if you are brushing too hard. I don't have this problem so I can't comment on how well this feature works. During brushing, it will pause a bit at 30 seconds and then turn off at 2min, so pretty standard compared to other electric brushes. The bristles are a good stiffness and not overly soft. The brushing is also at a good level for me. So I really have no complaints about the usability during brushing. I will say that the handle is a little on the skinny side, so if you have larger heads, you might fumble around a bit as you adjust during brushing. Overall, I really liked this brush and would recommend it as a travel brush due to its compactness.

reviews.title: Excellent budget friendly toothbrush
reviews.body: This is a review of the SURI NEW Core Sonic Electric Toothbrush, currently listed at $75.00. This is a new release from SURI offering a budget-friendly version of their popular SURI Pro 2.0. As a longtime user of Oral-B electric toothbrushes, I was completely surprised by this SURI. It cleans differently. At least it feels and sounds like it cleans differently. My Oral-B does an excellent job; this SURI does an excellent job also. I've used the SURI exclusively for the last 2 days, and my teeth feel very clean. I chose the Nightfall Blue color, which is a deep blackish blue. I charged it overnight before first use and installed the magnetic mirror mount so it would be ready to hold the brush once charged. The mount is very sturdy, and the brush attaches magnetically and securely. It's a great way to keep the countertops clear and the brush from getting splashed whenever I wash my hands. Other factors that make this a good choice for me: - Sleek, lightweight case -Recyclable brushheads -Travel brush cover -Travel lock button (so it won't accidentally turn on in your bag) -4 week USB C rechargable battery I cannot attest to battery performance at this point. I will update this review if the length between charges differs dramatically from the 4-week claim. At this point, I am very pleased with the SURI, intend to keep using it, and find it a good value.

reviews.title: Even better than the first version
reviews.body: I've had the SURI 1.0 for over a year and love it! I don't expect anything less from this model! Even though this is the slightly less "lux" version, it hits all the high notes... Smooth, sleek modern lines, no bulky mouth feel like with older electric toothbrushes. It charges pretty quickly and keeps a charge for weeks!! The charger works well and has a very small, compact foot-print. I bought the 1 0 with travel case for over $100, so to me this new model at $75 is a pretty good deal. It doesn't have the cleaning travel case--but that makes this brush great for a back-up brush, or weekend home or gym-bag brush, etc. I do prefer the more earth friendly body of the pro 1.0--which is aluminum and the replacement heads are minimalistic and color coordinated, which looks more high-end to me--but they last a while last a while either way--its pretty eco-conscuous, generally speaking! The bristles are also sturdy but gentle and there are two modes of vibration to choose from, to suit your comfort level. I love this brush! It also doesn't hurt that opening the box is a gift experience in itself! Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Great clean and excellent for travel
reviews.body: I’m really impressed with this electric toothbrush. It gives a noticeably deeper clean than a traditional manual toothbrush, and the sonic vibration makes brushing feel quick and effortless. The pressure sensor is helpful for making sure I’m not brushing too aggressively, and the built-in two-minute timer makes it easy to stick to the recommended brushing time. The battery life is a major plus. Being able to go weeks between charges makes this especially convenient for travel, and USB-C charging is easy and familiar. I also really like the compact travel cap and magnetic mirror mount. The mount keeps the toothbrush off the counter and saves space in the bathroom. The brush itself is lightweight and comfortable to hold, and the bristles have a nice balance of softness and firmness. I also appreciate the focus on more sustainable materials and the recycling program for used brush heads. Overall, this is a thoughtfully designed electric toothbrush with great cleaning performance, convenient features, and excellent battery life. It feels like a significant upgrade from a basic manual toothbrush.

I like the travel cover for the brush head, which keeps the bristles clean at home or on the go, making it easily portable. It seems to do an effective job of cleaning and is good quality. This toothbrush thoroughly cleans my sensitive teeth without irritating my gums. It comes with a stick on magnetic toothbrush holder which is a handy feature, but I probably don't want to put a sticker on my mirror. It has an appealing appearance - I ordered the Haze Green. It comes with a c charging cord on which users will recharge it standing up on the charging base - it does not include a c block for plugging it in so users will have to provide their own. It is a fair value for the money.

reviews.title: Fantastic Cleaning Performance with Incredible Battery Life
reviews.body: The SURI Core is a phenomenal sonic toothbrush with an incredible battery life. Having already used the SURI 2.0, the Core feels just as capable, with the cleaning performance and power seemingly just as strong. If there is any difference in power between the two, it certainly isn't noticeable during everyday use. The long battery life is another major advantage, making it easy to forget about charging for weeks at a time. The only real annoyance I've found is the charger compatibility. Unfortunately, the Core doesn't appear to work with our existing SURI 2.0 charger because the shape of the bottom is different, meaning two separate chargers need to be kept around. It would be great to see SURI develop a more universal charging solution across its range in the future. Aside from that inconvenience, this is an excellent toothbrush that delivers fantastic cleaning performance and battery life.

reviews.title: Best electric toothbrush I've used
reviews.body: Unsurprisingly this Suri brand toothbrush is now the top brand in the UK. This is my second one (accidentally left my last one in a hotel abroad:( ). If you’re looking for a top British electric toothbrush, this brand is a great choice. I see that it now boasts 17,000 verified Trustpilot reviews, so it’s clearly well loved and comes with clinically tested dentist-approved design. I really like the slim handle and the sonic cleaning is powerful, helping remove significantly more plaque than a manual brush, and the pressure sensor plus 2-minute timer make brushing simpler. Battery life is impressive too, giving up to four weeks per charge, and USB‑C charging makes it easy to keep going. It’s also light and travel-friendly, with a plant-based travel cap and a tidy Magnetic Mirror Mount for your bathroom. I also really like the brand's eco-focused approach,from its recyclable heads to its bio-based handle and B Corp certification. Trust me - you'll probably agree in a short time that this is the best toothbrush out there.

reviews.title: A Report from the Front Lines of Oral Hygiene
reviews.body: Dateline: A Bathroom Sink, Under the Unforgiving Glare of the Vanity Lights. For years, the act of brushing your teeth has been a sleepy, half-conscious affair. A dull, buzzing ritual performed on autopilot before you either face the horrors of the day or collapse into bed. You thought you knew what an electric toothbrush felt like. You were wrong. You were living a lie. I am here to tell you about the Philips Sonicare 4100. And I am here to tell you that it is a different beast entirely. It sits in your hand with a comfortable, substantial heft—a proper tool, not some flimsy, skinny wand. The handle is sturdy, the build quality immaculate. It feels like a serious instrument for a serious job. I applied the paste, brought the brush to my teeth with the casual indifference born of long habit, and thumbed the power button. And was immediately jolted awake by a profound, high-frequency thrum. This was not the gentle back-and-forth of a lesser brush. This was a jump scare. A sudden, powerful hum that felt like I was holding a swarm of microscopic, hyper-caffeinated jackhammers against my teeth. This is the "sonic" part of the name, a technology that vibrates with a speed and intensity that is both shocking and deeply, profoundly effective. You can feel the difference. It's a sensation of being deep-cleaned, of having years of coffee stains and bad decisions power-washed into oblivion. There are smart features, of course. A pressure sensor that gently chides you if you're pressing too hard, a built-in coach to keep you from savaging your own gums. A timer that dutifully guides you through the quadrants of your mouth. The included cap for the brush head is a simple, welcome touch of practical genius. But we must address the one, single, baffling decision that holds this marvel back from pure, unadulterated perfection: the charger. In a world that has finally, blessedly, begun to standardize around the glorious, universal USB-C port, Philips has chosen to tether this futuristic cleaning wand to a proprietary, old-world charging base. It is a strange, frustrating relic, a small annoyance that requires its own dedicated spot on your counter, unable to join the happy family of your other modern chargers. Even so, that one grievance is a whisper in the face of the roaring, high-frequency hurricane of cleaning power this toothbrush provides. The Sonicare 4100 is an impressive, powerful, and brilliantly effective piece of technology. It transforms the most mundane of daily chores into a high-performance event. A five-star champion that will leave your mouth feeling cleaner than you ever thought possible.

reviews.title: Lasted 12 years before I had to buy it again! Superior clean without the hefty price.
reviews.body: After an incredible 12-year run with my first Oral-B Pro 1000, I finally bought it again! The battery on my original brush finally bit the dust, and toward the end, it would only stay charged enough to get me through 24 hours of teeth brushing (if I was lucky) before dying. However, I loved the performance so much over the last decade that replacing it with the exact same model was an absolute no-brainer. Here is why this brush is a classic: Hygienist Approved: My dental hygienist once told me that it really doesn't matter how fancy or expensive an electric toothbrush is—any solid electric toothbrush is far superior to a manual brush. This model gives you that elite, professional clean without making you pay for unnecessary, over-hyped tech features. The One Minor Con: If I have to name one downside, it is the noise. Even brand new out of the box, it does sound a bit like it might be powered by hamsters while it is working. But just because it doesn't sound whisper-quiet doesn't negate the fact that it is a remarkably solid, heavy-duty toothbrush. A Note on the Color: The color is fun, but the listing is a bit misleading. I thought I would be getting a mint green, but instead, it is definitely a powder blue. I much prefer green to blue, but eh, whatever—it still cleans my teeth perfectly! If you want a proven, durable electric toothbrush that will last you for years to come without draining your wallet, this is the one to get. Highly recommended!

reviews.title: Crooked, Overcrowded, Yellow Teeth
reviews.body: Let me start this review by saying that when I was younger, much to my parent's dismay, I neglected to brush my teeth. I would brush them but not as often and as thoroughly as a child should. This was partly due to my very bad gag reflex and partly due to the fact that it felt painful (?). Anyway, I've had yellow teeth my whole life (I'm 29) because of it. I never got braces (thanks again gag reflex) but my parents tried everything to get me to have better oral hygiene and to have a more aesthetically pleasing smile. Now that I'm well into adulthood, my smile being so yellow, and also very crowded, was starting to bother me. I knew I had to give in and fix one or the other. (To be clear if you have crooked teeth don't feel like you have to change yourself just for society - after 29 years, I can say that I truly wanted to change the yellowness purely for myself). I've gotten healthier in almost all other aspects of my life. I decided to make the plunge and buy this in hopes it would help get my teeth cleaner and help reduce plaque buildup. Not just for aesthetics, but for actual oral hygiene. So, I've used it twice a day for 3 days so far and my brother commented on how "white" my teeth look yesterday evening. That felt very good to hear, not gonna lie. I think this toothbrush is amazing for the price. I love how tiny the head of the brush is. It fits into my small, overcrowded mouth perfectly. I was worried that it would take forever to brush my teeth since I wasn't doing the work, the toothbrush was. However, it takes about 2 minutes and 30 seconds or 3 minutes if you're extra thorough. It allots 30 seconds to each section of your mouth, it will do a variation in the vibration to let you know when the 30 seconds is up and to move to the next portion of your mouth. It doesn't automatically shut off after 3 minutes (that I know of) if you want to go back and do another section of your mouth, which is nice. As for the pressure sensor on the toothbrush, mine does not work. It doesn't indicate any color or anything. It just appears to be a normal electric toothbrush. I may have gotten a "bad" toothbrush since it's not working, but to be honest, I truly just wanted something that would do a deep clean and this toothbrush does that. However, all the other reviews mention the sensor working so if that's something you're looking for, I would still highly recommend this toothbrush. I think mine might just be a dud in that department. The charging took several hours to be full on the first day. I keep it on the charger to ensure that it is always fully charged. If you don't have your charger with you and you need to rely on it without it, I'm told the battery lasts up to a week. Which, is very impressive for a $50 toothbrush. Amazon says that it has Bluetooth connectivity but I do not see any indication of that on the boxes or in the manual. My parents bought me an electric toothbrush when I was little, but I was too young to appreciate it. Now that I'm older, I think this is a great option for any person of any age. I do recommend it!

reviews.title: A great value that comes with power
reviews.body: This is the most powerful electric toothbrush I have ever used! I ordered this toothbrush to replace a manual one that I had. My dentist recommended an electric one so I picked this one up. This is amazing! My teeth have never felt so clean When you first get it, it will come with no charge, so make sure you charge it. In the box, it includes the toothbrush and a charger. You don’t get any extra heads so make sure that you order some. When you do use it though, you will love how clean your teeth get! My teeth have never felt so clean! I use it every day. It is waterproof, so you can take it in the shower, which is perfect for me since my mornings are rushed. It is enjoyable to use and to hold, it’s terrific! One thing I really enjoy about it is the two minute timer. It keeps me accountable to actually brush my teeth for a long enough time, and it doesn’t allow me to brush for a longer time than I have to. It pauses every thirty seconds, so you can brush each quadrant of your teeth for thirty seconds, so you can give one section of your teeth the attention it deserves. With the pros out of the way, I do want to talk about a few cons. There are way too many settings to use. I know that it’s nice to have many options to choose from so we can pick what we want, but you don’t need three different ways to brush your teeth. Most of the time I just click the on button and don’t bother with the other settings and turn it off when I’m done. The other settings aren’t even that different. You can see that in my included video The battery life is also not the best. Some people have reported getting a week or two’s worth of battery, but I’m finding I have to charge mine every five days, which isn’t a dealbreaker, but I travel a lot, so it’s not ideal. Speaking of not ideal, they use a proprietary charger which really makes this toothbrush not travel friendly. You need to take so many chargers with you for your phone and laptop. Those might have the same charger, like USB-C, but this doesn’t. So, you need to take this charger separately. Another thing is that you need to really keep the toothbrush, charger, and any surface it touches, clean and dry. Otherwise, wherever you put this, bacteria will start to build up. If you don’t clean your charger every other day, bacteria will start to build up and it’s gross. The included picture doesn’t do it justice, and that’s just on my sink. Despite my complaints, I really enjoy this toothbrush. It’s relatively inexpensive compared to other electric toothbrushes, it has lasted me a long time, and it’s powerful. I do recommend it!

reviews.title: Great cleaning, versatile options for brush heads, charge lasts, but only 1 speed setting
reviews.body: One of my best purchases. I used to clean my teeth with a manual toothbrush, thinking that if I spent enough time and diligence, it would provide the same level of cleaning as an electric toothbrush. I was wrong. After my very first cleaning with this device, I felt a level of clean teeth only experienced when I leave the dentist's office after a cleaning. And it wasn't just a subjective feeling. When I returned for my 6 month cleaning the next time, there was barely any tartar or plaque build up - all had been removed by this toothbrush. I also noticed that my level of bad breath and tonsil rocks declined significantly. Turns out a manual cleaning is nowhere near as good as this machine. I have purchased this toothbrush for familty and friends, telling them it has changed my life. I wish I had this device as a child! The toothbrush comes with interchangebale heads, so that you can pick the one that works best for you - sensitive teeth, hard brush, whatever. Oral-B makes these products available, but you can also purchase no-name brands as well. It does create quite a bit of vibration in your head that I found a little scary at first. However, despite having sensitive teeth and gums, the toothbrush never harmed them. The toothbrush ahs a pressure sensor that stops once you put it too tightly against your teeth to prevent this. There is supposed to be 3 levels of speed for the brush. Mine doesn't seem to have them - has shown in the video. It's not that I don't know how to operate it - the toothbrush I purchased for my family (in white instead of pink) had those features, as advertized. In the end, I don't feel that having those 3 levels are important, except perhaps to get used to the sensation of vibration in the initial phases of use. The toothbrush comes with a plug and charger. It seems t o keep its charge for 4-5 days (I only use this toothbrush once a day for 4 min). Then the little light at the bottom of the toothbrush turns from green to red, alerting me that it is time to charge it (so I can usually travel without the toothbrush charge if it is for a trip that is less than a week). The charge itself happens very quickly - it seems to be charged within 20 min. I highly recommend this spinning toothbrush. It has changed my mouth's health!

reviews.title: Best Electic Toothbrush You Can Get
reviews.body: My dentist told me that I needed to switch to an electric toothbrush so I found the specs and review to this one to be good. The brush head isn't too small like the other ones I saw, and it has two power speeds. It may be uncomfortable to use on your teeth at first if you switch from a manual toothbrush. But let me tell you, that your teeth will get so much used to it and after a while, it won't even bother you. I find that my teeth are just as clean as if coming from a dentist's office. My teeth feel so smooth and I can tell that it has gotten rid of any plaque or bacteria I may have. I have permanent retainers on the bottom of my teeth which can be a pain to clean and floss. But with this electric toothbrush, I can tell that it's cleaner than it has ever been as I glide my tongue around the area. I just visited the dentist and the hygienist was going about how clean my teeth are and how well I take care of them! And how I have absolutely no plaque, and I am doing the right things, and that I should keep doing what I'm doing. I was using a battery-powered brush that was cheap from Walmart but having to replace the batteries is a hassle. The fact that this is rechargeable and the change holds for a VERY long time is what I think is the best thing about this toothbrush. It may not come with a wall adapter, but you can contact Sonicare and they can send one in for you to use. Their idea is to conserve the environment by doing so which is fine by me. I just used a wall charger I've had and it does the job. If you're on the fence about buying this one, or any electric toothbrush-don't be. Its the best investment you can make for yourself and your oral health and I have not looked back on buying this. 10/10 recommend.

reviews.title: Wish I had purchased it years ago
reviews.body: I've been using a manual toothbrush for years. I never felt like I could get my teeth clean enough with them, but I didn't want to shell out the money for a pricey electric toothbrush. After having gum recession from brushing too hard, I decided to try an electric toothbrush out. I bought it for $55, and honestly, I love it so much I would've paid $85 for it. It works great, it's comfortable to hold, super easy to use and it gets my teeth so nice and clean. It makes brushing so much easier, and I love the pressure sensor, it stops me from brushing so hard. The heads are a wee bit pricey to replace, but they only need to be swapped every 3 months, and all of the Philips ones are interchangeable. I've been using it for about 3 weeks and only had to charge it once so far. I love the pink colour, and I love that it doesn't have any nooks or crannies to trap water and grow mold like toothbrushes 15 years ago had. Highly recommend, it's the best purchase I've made all year.

reviews.title: Not as weak as they say
reviews.body: This is my 1st electric toothbrush. I ordered it over the oral b smart 1500 because it's cheaper and I found more people who swear by it than oral b. Later on, I read comments where people who have this 4100 for 10+ years say that the newer 2021 version has only half the power of the old version. Someone on reddit showed images of the inside of the new and old versions and the new version has a small plastic toy-like motor, while the old version has a big copper-wrapped motor and an old version user said "now I understand why the new version is lighter and less powerful". I was disappointed on the new version and tried to cancel the order but I couldn't. Once it came, I decided to try it and to my surprise, it brushes my teeth way better than my manual soft-bristled and hard-bristled toothbrushes(I use both manual brushes daily compared to my daily usage of the electric toothbrush 4100 C2 head of medium bristles. If you have gum sensitive issue, buy the S sensitive or G2 optimal brush head. If you want hard-bristled, buy W diamondclean brush head). I don't know how good the old version was but this newer version definitely brushes better than any manual toothbrush unfortunately it doesn't not come with a travel case. Update 5/16/2024: I bought the Oral B smart 1500 because it was on sale and I wanted to see how better it is compared to the sonicare. The oral B package looks nicer and bigger than the Sonicare but upon opening the smart 1500 package, I saw hair all over the toothbrush. I did read many customers saying on reddit that their Oral b toothbrush were repackaged, but I can't believe I'm a victim of this nastiness. It also took 2 weeks to reach me from Hawaii and since it says "made in China", I think the seller is located in China. I'll return this and I'll advise you to buy the Sonicare instead of the oral b if you don't want to be cheated receiving a used-repackaged toothbrush. Update 05/22/2024: On 05/17/24, I bought the Oral b smart clean 360 which has exact power as the smart 1500 that I returned but the smart 360 has 5 modes and a button to change the mode while the smart 1500 has 3 modes and no button to switch between the modes. The advantage of the oral b smart clean 360 is that the brush heads cost is cheaper than the Sonicare 4100 and I find it better at whitening my teeth than the Sonicare. That's all the advantages there. The things that I don't like with it are many, so I'm just going to name the most annoying ones: 1) The brush heads are too big compared to the Sonicare(see picture): Putting Oral b brush heads in my mouth is like putting a golf ball in my mouth(my head and mouth are wider than the average US male). 2) The brush heads have holes(see pictures) that trap saliva+toothpaste and creates more noise when the brush handle needle rotates in the presence of the liquid mixture, and moisture will be also trapped easily in the holes(most customers complain about Oral b brush heads design. Oral b corrected the needle issue with the IO version but the IO introduced a shallow hole which now traps moisture in the brush handle). When I'm using the Oral b with no choice but to have my mouth wide-open, it forces my mouth to produce more saliva which gets mixed with the toothpaste and enters the brush head and creates more noise. 3) Rattling noise: The Oral b smart clean 360 isn't as noisy as people say. It's the quality of the noise the problem. It's a very unpleasant rattling noise as if you're hearing an old car engine with broken parts in it. That noise gets worse when liquid enters the brush head holes. 4) The charger is not round like a perfect circle: You must put the Oral b brush handle in a specific position to charge it and if you place it wrong, it'll fall and might break. 5) The Daily Clean mode is rough and combined with the big brush head the experience is bad, but the smart clean 360 has more mode which make it smoother and better than the smart 1500 but not as good as the Sonicare 4100. 6)It has no auto-stop mode: You keep brushing without knowing how long you have been brushing your teeth. To summarize, the oral b non-IO brush heads are cheap but very badly designed for a pleasant toothbrushing. I won't recommend it if you're shorter than 6 foot tall or have a small mouth.

reviews.title: Replaced my old Series 2 Sonicare with this one and can highly recommend this 4100 Model.
reviews.body: I was replacing my "old" Phillips Sonicare, specifically the HX6240, which was a series 2 model. Loved it. I found newer brands of electric toothbrushes seemed to be including 2 features I did not want, sending my data; and, reminders to brush a new area every 20 sec for 2 minutes. The latter called Brush Pacer results in 6 reminders. I prefer 4 reminders, the Quad Pacer Timer, 4 - 30 sec increments. Easier to keep track of where I already brushed. This new 4100 had the Quad Pacer, was not info invasive, and I could use the same brush tips I liked. The Lithium Ion battery on this new one lasts longer than the old NiMH one. It can sit on a "similar looking" charging base to the old one. But the new model is charged via a USB type A cable base and cord. You can use any standard USB charger you already own for phones or tablets. This model includes 2 Pressure sensitive settings, which is all I need. It is lighter and has a slimmer profile. One unexpected thing is that you can actually charge the new model on the older model's base. My spouse still uses the older model, and when we have extended travel together we take just one charger. Its turned out to be the perfect replacement electric toothbrush for me. (Photos: Older Model is on your left.)

reviews.title: minor accidents and there goes your 3 digit electric tooth brush
reviews.body: Sonicare loses cleaning power after minor drops I’ve now gone through three Sonicare toothbrushes in about two years. In my experience, even a minor drop can make the vibration much weaker. The brush still turns on and vibrates, but the power drops so much that it no longer feels like an effective electric toothbrush, even with a new brush head. That is the most frustrating part: it does not completely fail, so at first glance it seems fine, but the cleaning performance is clearly reduced. At that point, the main advantage of using an electric toothbrush is basically caput.. This has happened to me twice, and it makes the product feel far less durable than it should be for normal real-world household use. For a premium toothbrush, I expected better resistance to minor drops and better long-term reliability. I still think Sonicare is a great product, but after this repeated experience I would strongly advise buyers to be very careful with handling and not assume it can tolerate everyday bumps or falls. Planned obscolecence? Sad if it is. I am sure it should not take more than a minor cushioning, internal or external to make the product more rugged.

reviews.title: True longevity & happy to purchase 2 more
reviews.body: Oral-B Pro 1000 Rechargeable Toothbrush has not disappointed me. I’ve had my own since 2019. It still functions beautifully. The one thing I’ve noticed is the battery charge doesn’t last as long as it did when it was new. I could go 2 weeks or more without charging. Now it’s about 1 week & I need to charge. I do brush morning & night for the full 2 minutes. I love everything about it. I don’t have sensitive teeth thus my teeth can handle the deep cleaning it provides. I really don’t recommend this if you do have sensitive teeth as I feel it would be too harsh. The timing function works wonderfully for it tells me when to move onto the next area of my mouth. ••To prevent a yukky mess that drips down I have learned 2 things: I thoroughly run water under the brush while it’s running to fully clean it. This, however, doesn’t prevent yuk from your brushing from forming down where the brush head meets the toothbrush. I became tired of a toothbrush that had dried toothpaste on it even though I thought cleaning the head was enough. Unfortunately the yuk does collect at that area & begins the mess. To prevent that I do now take the head of the brush every time I use it now. I just sit in to side in a dry cloth. Hence a clean brush. Since my purchase I’ve purchased 2 more. One for my husband who was told by his Dentist he needed an electric toothbrush because he was developing gingivitis. He loves it because it’s so easy to brush now. The toothbrush does all the work. At first he was doing the brushing & ruined the head a little. So a reminder this does the brushing for you. You only need to move the brush around your mouth. Since having mine I haven’t had one cavity. One thing my hygienist did mention when I first got it was I wasn’t getting high enough to my upper gums. Now I make sure I do. I also purchased one for my 15yo Son as his Pediatric Dentist said it was okay & recommended that he start early with an excellent choice in toothbrushes. For $50- the price hasn’t changed since 2019 - this is well worth getting. For multiple reasons as I feel I thoroughly cleans my teeth. Once I began using this my mouth felt clean & fresh & it does every time I use it. I also feel using an electric toothbrush has saved $ I’d be spending on dental bills. The cost always swayed me away from making the purchase but I’m glad I did. Obviously since mine still works since 2019 there’s definite genuine quality with Oral-B. The box does state it comes with a 2 year limited warranty & there is a 60 day risk free trial. The paperwork details are in the box. For all I’ve written I highly recommend this Oral-B electric toothbrush & I don’t feel you’ll be disappointed. ••I do not purchase genuine Oral-B brush heads. From the beginning I’ve purchased a generic version from Amazon which have worked perfectly. My pictures reflect how nicely it’s packaged upon its arrival.

reviews.title: Does a very good job on plaque
reviews.body: I have always used a standard manual brush. I was skeptical of electric because it seemed like the little head only moved in short back and forth spins (instead of complete circles) making it less effective. In addition, I assumed that you could not apply any pressure, or the head would stop moving. My dentist recommended I try one to help with plaque build up that I seem to accumulate quickly on the inside of my lower front teeth. So, I bought this one (my wife has had one a few years). Some observations: - It does a very good job keeping plaque off. I actually started using this brush halfway between dentist appointments. I found that it could not remove already present plaque (at least not what I had), but that once removed by the dentist, this brush does a great job keeping it off. Much better than a manual brush. For that alone I am sold. - The small size is very good for getting around back teeth / wisdom teeth. It also gets you to focus on a tooth at a time (vs. the sawing motion across many teeth) - which actually took no more time. Overall, a session might take very slightly longer than manual, but is certainly more thorough. - You can press down pretty hard, and the brush keeps oscillating. Although, in my experience, there is no need. I tend to use less pressure than a manual brush. While the brush head is doing a short back and forth spin (vs. a total 360), that seems just as effective (perhaps more so, since you get both directions of spin very quickly on all surfaces). - The brush does a pulsing vibration after 2 minutes. You can just ignore it and keep brushing. It also does much lighter pulses every 30 seconds, to help you time your session into groups of upper front, upper back, lower front, lower back. Again, you can ignore all this and just brush at your own pace. - If two people in the same bathroom are using this type of brush, there are two good options. One, have both people use the same base, and just switch out the head (they are color coded for this reason). Or two, give each person their own unit, but keep just one charging base out. The charge need is so infrequent, that its easy to just leave one brush standing on its own, and the other on the charger; then just switch out when a charge is needed. This clears up counter space and cords. - We have purchased the generic (and less expensive) replacement heads. In our experience, they were identical to the originals in materials and make. I am sure there is a lot of quality variation, but it was not hard to find good options. - My wife and I have what appear to be identical models, except we did one black, one white to make them easy to keep separate. Mine, the white, only turns off by pressing the off button 3 times (since it cycles through modes using the on/off button). This is the only thing I really do not like. The black one turns off with one click. Perhaps it is a setting, but we can find no way to change it. So, I find myself holding the brush in my mouth (to stop splatter) while finding the button (see below), and pressing 3 times. - The on off button is a little hard to press. It is flush and shallow. I always manage to get it on and off, but sometimes it is surprisingly hard. Recently, it would not turn on, and I thought it must have lost its charge. Turns out I just had to press very firmly. This can be a challenge when turning the unit off. You tend to keep it in your mouth (to prevent splatter), and so finding and pressing the button is sometimes a little harder than you would think. I think for most people, this is just a negative to be accepted. But for people who are older, or not dexterous in the hands, I think this would actually make the brush impossible to use. Overall, I am happy with it, because it prevents plaque, end of story. If I could change one thing, it would be a single press, easy press on\off button.

reviews.title: Excelente cepillo
reviews.body: Este es mi segundo cepillo eléctrico oral-b, me encantan, ya no regreso a los tradicionales. Siento los dientes más limpios y es más sencillo el cepillado de dientes. Un tip para mantener la base del cargador y el cuerpo del cepillo limpios es que al terminar de lavarse los dientes no pongan el cepillo directo al cargador. Primero separen el cabezal y el cuerpo del cepillo, enjuaguenlos bien, sequelos y ya después ponen solo el cuerpo del cepillo en el cargador. Actualización (12/sep/2024): a ya casi dos años de la reseña, mi cepillo y el cargador siguen en excelentes condiciones. Solo es cuestion de cuidarlo y mantenerlo limpio.
reviews.body_en: This is my second oral-b electric toothbrush, I love them, I won't go back to the traditional ones. My teeth feel cleaner and brushing my teeth is easier. A tip to keep the base of the charger and the body of the brush clean is that when you finish brushing your teeth, do not put the brush directly on the charger. First separate the brush head and body, rinse them well, dry them and then put only the brush body in the charger. Update (Sep 12, 2024): almost two years after the review, my brush and charger are still in excellent condition. It's just a matter of taking care of it and keeping it clean.

reviews.title: A Nice Upgrade From My Oral-B Pro 100
reviews.body: I recently upgraded from my old Oral-B Pro 100 to the Oral-B iO Series 3, and I can definitely tell the difference. The brushing experience feels much smoother and quieter, and my teeth feel noticeably cleaner after each use. One of my favorite improvements is the pressure sensor. It helps me avoid brushing too hard, which is something my old toothbrush didn't have. I also like the different cleaning modes they're simple to switch between and let me choose what feels best. The brush head glides comfortably over my teeth, and the handle feels solid and well-made. Battery life has also been great so far, lasting several days before needing a recharge. If you're still using an older Oral-B model like the Pro 100 and have been thinking about upgrading, I think the iO Series 3 is well worth it. It feels like a much more refined brushing experience, and I'm really happy with the purchase.

reviews.title: I love this toothbrush!
reviews.body: I always forget to write reviews after I buy stuff on Amazon. I should try to do it more because it is helpful when you find a review that is real. So, I bought this toothbrush to replace another brand that I bought about a year and a half ago. The old toothbrush just wasn't doing a good job at cleaning my teeth. I have always had problems with cavities and plaque build-up. The only sure-fire way of getting all of the plaque for me was to use Plax prior to brushing. Still, I find myself in the dentist's office every six months with a hygienist jack-hammering my mouth with water pick to get my teeth clean. It's embarrassing and it makes me feel anxious about my gum health. I saw the Oral-B iO Series 3 here on Amazon and it was discounted. According to Oral-B it is really good at getting rid of plaque. I took the manufacturer at their word, and bought it. Holy crap, ya'll! This thing is amazing! The iO3 has a round brush head similar to the polishing tool your dental hygienist uses. I've used cheaper Oral-B electric toothbrushes that also have round heads, but they weren't as robust as the brush head on the iO3. The bristles aren't hard, but they are dense and arranged in a way that they can hug your teeth while brushing. You can get that brush on every surface of each tooth (except directly between the teeth, of course). The motorized handle has a pressure sensor that changes color based on how hard or soft you are pressing. If you get it just right, it lights up green. The iO3 also helps you time your brushing so that you the recommended two minutes. It pulses when it's time to change to a different quadrant. It doesn't automatically shut off when the two minutes are up, however. That's fine with me as I will just continue brushing other parts of my mouth like my tongue and the roof of my palette when I'm done with my teeth. There are supposedly three types of brushing settings to choose from, but I have only used the default cleaning setting. The other two setting are supposed to be for sensitive teeth and whitening. The default works just fine for me. The build is solid and feels good in my hands. I like that the handle comes with two brush heads, a travel case, and case for the brush heads. I like to take my brush head off and put it in the case after I'm finished just because I'm paranoid about having a toothbrush exposed in the bathroom. It's nice to have the option to shield it from germs. So, TLDR, this is a great electric toothbrush. My teeth haven't felt this clean since the last time I went to the dentist. Oral-B did a fantastic job of designing a product that makes brushing easy and will almost certainly result in you having a positive visit at the dentist, and may help reverse gum issues and prevent cavities. I definitely recommend you buy this product if you are in the market for an electric toothbrush.

reviews.title: Best toothbrush I've ever owned
reviews.body: This is by far the best toothbrush I have ever used! Thinking that was better then just using my regular manual one. My husband bought this in black about a month ago and liked it and it was on sale so I decided to jump and get it as well. I've been using it for a week now and my mouth still feels as clean as it did the day I came home from the dentist with a cleaning. It was a little strong on the vibrations at first but after the week of using it consistently it no longer bothers me. Its not loud at all and I love the 30 second interval vibrations it gives you so you know to move on to the next quadrant in your mouth. Over all the best thing I've bought all year. Would recommend it to everyone.

reviews.title: La meilleure brosse-à-dents électrique
reviews.body: Après deux mois d'utilisation, je peux le dire, il s'agit de la meilleure brosse-à-dents électrique que j'ai utilisé. En voyant ce nouveau type de brosse pourtant, je me demandais au départ s'il ne s'agissait pas d'une autre façon d'attirer le consommateur, mais non. Le système de nettoyage me paraît bien différent de ce que j'utilisais auparavant, y compris chez Oral B. POURS : - Le système de vibration / rotation de la brosse est tout simplement très bien pensé. C'est très doux à l'usage, cela paraît également très précis et le résultat est vraiment bon. - Le voyant qui permet de savoir si l'on appuie trop sur la brosse est très visible, c'est assez simple d'adapter la pression exercée. - J'aime également la vitesse de vibration. CONTRES : - Un peu dispendieux. Sur du long terme, si la brosse-à-dents reste toujours aussi fiable, cela pourrait compenser son prix. Conclusion : C'est un coup de cœur pour la brosse Oral B iO ! En espérant que cela dure plusieurs années.
reviews.body_en: After two months of use, I can say, this is the best electric toothbrush I have used. When I saw this new type of brush, however, I initially wondered if it wasn't another way of attracting consumers, but no. The cleaning system seems very different to me from what I used before, including at Oral B. PROS: - The vibration/rotation system of the brush is simply very well thought out. It's very smooth to use, it also seems very precise and the result is really good. - The light which lets you know if you are pressing too much on the brush is very visible, it is quite simple to adapt the pressure exerted. - I also like the speed of vibration. CONS: - A little expensive. In the long term, if the toothbrush remains as reliable as ever, this could compensate for its price. Conclusion: We fell in love with the Oral B iO brush! Hoping it lasts several years.

title: Lumineux Teeth Whitening Strips, Peroxide Free, 9 Treatments (1 Month)
bullet_points: WHITENING THAT RESPECTS ENAMEL – Intentionally designed to visibly brighten your smile while supporting enamel health, so you never have to choose between whitening and long-term oral care.

A SMARTER ALTERNATIVE TO PEROXIDE – Peroxide whitens by bleaching teeth, which can weaken enamel and lead to sensitivity. Lumineux works differently - helping gently lift stains caused by coffee, tea, & wine without damaging enamel.

DENTIST-FORMULATED & CLINICALLY-PROVEN – Developed by a dentist who believes stain removal should never come at the expense of enamel health, Lumineux brings a science-driven approach with clinical support and over 70 peer-reviewed studies.

CLEAN FORMULA, GENTLE ON TEETH & GUMS – Comfortable & effective whitening made with mineral-rich, coconut oil-based actives & free from peroxide, SLS, artificial colors or flavors. Cruelty-free and safe for all teeth, including sensitive and veneers.
A COMPLETE SMILE CARE SYSTEM – Designed to work as part of your daily routine with complementary Lumineux toothpastes and mouthwashes, for a beautiful smile that's built to last.

reviews.title: Highly recommend this purchase
reviews.body: I have notoriously sensitive teeth and have always avoided whitening strips due to the painful zings they cause. After a month of using Lumineux (three times a week, nine total treatments), I am genuinely impressed. The lack of peroxide is the standout feature--my teeth whitened gradually without any sensitivity whatsoever. After the first week, I noticed a subtle difference; by the end of the month, my teeth were two shades lighter, with no enamel damage or gum irritation. Pros: Completely pain-free application. The strips adhere well and don't slip during the 30-minute wear time. The formula is gentle enough for daily coffee drinkers like me, and the results look natural, not unnaturally white. The dentist-formulated aspect gave me confidence in using it long-term. Cons: The whitening process is slower than peroxide-based strips, so patience is required. You must stick to the schedule to see results. Also, the strips can feel slightly slick if not pressed firmly on the teeth at first. Recommendation: Absolutely. If you have sensitive teeth or want a gentle, enamel-safe whitening option that works gradually, this is a solid choice. For those needing instant, dramatic results, peroxide strips may be faster, but Lumineux offers a kinder, sustainable alternative. I will repurchase.

reviews.title: Whiter teeth are psychologically better than yellow stained teeth.
reviews.body: Lumineux whitening strips do work!! You need to follow the protocol to have the treatment last. And I'm sometimes in a hurry. But, I read 15 minutes is even ok for a quick touch up. That's a very good touch up. I know I get better results if I make the strip go into my cracks and crevices on some of my crooked teeth. My family had 5 children. My mom took us to the dentist but actually braces back then were for the affluent people. I am old now and thank goodness I've never had a cavity. Neither did 2 of my brothers. But a sister and another brother had cavities and problems with their teeth. My sister got married and didn't need braces but her teeth due to genetics turned yellow with age. She used Zoom because she could afford it, and it looked nice, but it didn't last. Nothing can last forever. But, using this product, even though, if you stop, it won't last either, will make you (and don't worry about other people seeing your teeth) very happy! Because you look in the mirror at yourself maybe 100 times a day and seeing your white teeth is a feeling that boosts self-confidence, thus self-esteem, and your mood will be more positive, true, and you'll feel more outgoing. There are actually too many, attributes to list. But this important point, no doubt, has made its mark. The most important point is how you see yourself and more importantly, feel about yourself. White teeth is only a " fix it" solution. Inside your head you need all of these affirmations about yourself. You need to start at beating depression down. Even if it is mild, this kind of depression, the kind inside your head that looks for all your faults, and you look at all of them excessively. Bad "self talk" will ruin so much of the good talk that you can't stand up to it and take charge of all your good God given traits that will move you forward in improving your self-esteem. I found that to help my self-esteem was to say "Yes, my teeth are crooked and yellow. I'm embarrassed by how I look. It really makes me feel bad!" So, being much older gives me wisdom on how best to strengthen my self-esteem concerning my teeth, and do something about it. Money plays a part here, too. Therefore, I saw the commercial on TV and looked it up. And I read about it. Then I bought the kit. Money was no problem for this. There can be hundreds of products out there that claim the same things. I received my package and immediately used it. Haha. It did work!! I was very impressed!! Lumineux DOES work!! Once, I was in a hurry and in as little as 15 minutes I was stunned to see actually whiter teeth. Man, next time I used it close to 30 minutes and was thrilled at white teeth! Once I just did the top teeth very quickly. And later I used the left over bottom strip on my top teeth. I made that thing fit and work. And it did. I don't want to waste anything. If I forget or can't use it as I like, I know I can catch up. What I want is to have very white teeth when I'm talking or smiling or laughing. And I know I can achieve that with my whitening strips. I wish I could afford the clear braces. But, they cost at the start, at least $5,000.00. I wish I could afford that. But, I know I would be on a payment plan for the rest of my life. (I'm exaggerating.) Yet, if my teeth look good and white I'll be happy. I have to decide on financial priorities; and, it will be my Lumineux white strips that take the top of the list. It's better to have the white teeth (albeit some bottom teeth are crooked) than to have yellowish teeth. And yes, to never have had a cavity up to age 60 is good, but nobody looks inside my mouth for dental work unless it's the hygienist or dentist. Yes, and that's a plus for me healthwise. However, and I stress this; Having Lumineux Whitening Strips make my teeth whiter is going to win, for me, every time. And that's even if I wore clear braces. Braces DO NOT whiten teeth. So, I've already bought another box of my whitening strips. I don't want to take pictures of my teeth or give my name. I'm telling the truth. And It has to be on trust that what I'm saying IS the truth. And I'm happy about this. Now wouldn't it be wonderful if they made good, Clear Braces infused with Lumineux whitening?? And while you wear them for the duration, your teeth become straight and white together in a happy relationship!! How wonderful. Someone will think of that someday and bring the cost of those braces way down. And a scientist will find a way to infuse Lumineux into the clear braces. So, I am hoping people all ages buy Lumineux to try and boost their self-confidence and be happier than before. I am happier about these ridiculous teeth than ever before just due to Lumineux. And I wrote about it because it is true. Thank you

reviews.title: Day 1
reviews.body: 3:13 June 5 , 2024 I applied the initial application . I brushed with sensodine tooth paste & dried my teeth prior to the application . After fighting & getting the top film off the backing I easily applied it however the bottom film is a little trickier to apply correctly . I jumped into the shower whe while washing my face I could feel both films sliding on my teeth while salivating more than normal . The top stayed close to the applied site but the bottom wrapped around the back of the bottom teeth . Plus I'm thinking the front of the bottom teeth are uncovered . Almost 30 minutes in & I can feel a peroxide like unwanted sensation in a couple of my 71 year old back teeth . 32 minutes later the top film was pretty much where I put it however the bottom film was indeed covering the back of the bottom teeth . The remaining residue which some discribed as snot & the taste wasn't all that bad . After rinsing I brushed again with Sensodine & baking soda which removed said snot . While it's the initial /test run I highly doubt any change in color but the teeth that were treated feel extremely clean . I'm doubting this product will have the anticipated results , so that's why I gave 3 stars . Day 2 results to follow . Again with the 30 minute procedure & again with what I would say is better results . My teeth do infact look & feel brighter & cleaner . Days 4 , 5 & 6 were pretty much the same results except the time of application changed . reviews.title: So disappointing!
reviews.body: I bought these after hearing multiple social media influencers rave about them for months. Finally caved! I subscribed to these strips because it was cheaper. But I was a little lazy lol and didn’t even start trying them out until after I already had FOUR BOXES of them…ok so I was super lazy. I just don’t love the experience of using white strips so I put it off. But after I had 4 boxes I figured I better start using them. I was so certain they’d be great because these influencers rave so much! But there’s so much they don’t tell you. I have only used these, and different types of the Crest white strips in the past, so I only have the Crest to compare them to. First, sensitivity: this is the one area that I would say is purely a pro. These don’t make my teeth cold sensitive at all after use. If your teeth have a really hard time maaaaybe it would be worth all the cons to use these. Whitening: my teeth are getting whiter, 3 boxes in. It’s taking much much longer than the crest white strips took. I always brush my teeth before applying the strips and wear them for 30 min as directed - I use a timer. So I’m using them correctly but the whitening effect is sooooo slow. Not impressed at all. My teeth would get to a nice white after less than 1 box of crest strips. I’ve used 3 boxes of these already and still my teeth are not as white as they should be (and they weren’t horribly stained to begin with). Application: it’s weird I even have to mention this! With the crest strips you just put them on. With these, you dab your teeth super dry, carefully position them, try to put them on, but they flop and slide around, so you have to try to glue them down with pressure but be careful or they’ll slide…it’s annoying. They’re needlessly difficult to get to stick to your teeth. Plus - often during the whitening process the corners will come loose and be annoying sticking out and poking your tongue. The WORST PART: when you take them off. I was expecting a little residue because the strips I’ve used in the past left a little residue. With these basically all the gel stays behind stuck stubbornly on your teeth. Don’t spit in the sink - you will spit out chunks of gel and it feels so disgusting it’s nauseating. The gel thickly coats every tooth and if you have any crooked teeth it will be worse. What I do is use my wet toothbrush (which I don’t like doing since you’re not supposed to get your mouth wet after these strips but nothing else works) to scrub the gel off my teeth. I have to rinse my toothbrush several times because it gets totally gunked up with gel. Then I spit the remaining bits of gel out. It is extremely unpleasant. The first few strips I used, I thought something was wrong with my box but lucky for me I had other boxes, and none of them were old. but just in case, I tried the newest box. No, they’re all like this. All of the strips leave such a thick layer of goo on your teeth I can’t even imagine why the influencers rave over this product. To me, this is something you should use as a last resort lol if you can’t use anything else, ok try this. If you can handle sensitivity or have money for other means of whitening, avoid these!!!! They are so disgusting. I can’t believe people recommend them without even mentioning the mess of goo at the end and the slowwww whitening! These are so not worth the price. I still have some strips to use up, they were too expensive to throw away, but man do I regret buying them. Yuck!

reviews.title: A Smile Brighter Than My Future: Lumineux Teeth Whitening Strips Review
reviews.body: Attention, fellow coffee addicts, red wine enthusiasts, and anyone else who has ever looked in the mirror and thought, "Are my teeth supposed to be that color?" Have I got a tale for you! Enter Lumineux Teeth Whitening Strips, the little heroes in a box that promised to turn my smile from "library paste" to "Hollywood dazzle." Let's rewind. There I was, browsing Amazon with my usual morning cup of joe (cup number...let's not talk about it), when I stumbled upon Lumineux. "Clinically proven!" it boasted. "No sensitivity!" it declared. "Natural ingredients!" it purred. My stained teeth and I were intrigued. Could this be the answer to years of dental despair? Order placed, I awaited their arrival like a child on Christmas Eve. And lo, they came, these saviors of enamel. The strips themselves were so easy to apply, I thought I'd done it wrong. "Where's the catch?" I wondered. "Where's the pain? The tears? The existential dread?" But no, folks – just slap 'em on, wait a magic 30 minutes (perfect time to ponder life choices or scroll through dog memes), and voila! The deed was done. Now, I won't lie to you, dear readers. The first reveal was no miracle. "Patience," whispered the Lumineux box, possibly in my caffeine-induced hallucinations. And so, I persisted. Each day, a little strip, a little wait, a little more hope. It was around day five that I saw it – the transformation. My teeth, once the color of a well-loved antique, were becoming...what's the word? Bright. No, radiant. I was astounded. My mouth was aglow. I could signal ships at sea. Guide planes to safe landing. Illuminate dark alleyways. You get the picture. But the true test came at the family dinner. "What's different about you?" they pondered. "New hair? Lost weight? Finally got that tattoo removed?" Nope, just my Lumineux smile, blinding all who dared gaze upon it. In summary, these Lumineux Teeth Whitening Strips delivered more than just results – they delivered a new era of confidence, a beacon of light in a world of dental darkness. They're like little magic bands of joy, minus the usual terror of teeth sensitivity that comes with other whitening products. Five stars for the product, and another unofficial star for making me smile at my reflection instead of wondering if I've been unknowingly consuming chalk. Would I recommend them? In a heartbeat. Will I repurchase? Faster than you can say "pearly whites." Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some smiling to practice. My future's so bright, I gotta wear shades.

reviews.title: I hated soft toothbrushes until these
reviews.body: I’ve bought these several times over the last couple of years... usually in packs of four or more. At this point I know exactly what they’re like and I always come back to them to restock. I was always a medium bristle guy. ALWAYS. I used to hate the idea of soft toothbrushes because I assumed they would feel useless, like they’re just moving around without really cleaning anything. These changed my mind. They’re soft, but not weak, and that’s the whole difference. The bristles are the reason I like them so much. When I slow down and focus on one area, I can feel them going between the teeth, especially near the gumline and those really tight cracks between one tooth and the next. I don’t have gaps between my teeth, so I don’t mean actual spaces. I mean the tiny narrow places where you normally feel like only floss can reach. With these, I can push the bristles in gently and get that same kind of deep clean feeling. Honestly, they make me feel less guilty about never wanting to floss. I’m not pretending it’s the same thing, but the feeling is close enough that I trust this brush more than any regular medium toothbrush I used before. The brush itself feels right in the hand. The head size is normal, easy to move around, the grip is comfortable, and it feels well made without feeling bulky or flimsy. Saying a toothbrush is “easy to use” sounds a little ridiculous because it’s a toothbrush, not some complicated tool, but the proportions are good and nothing about it feels awkward. No strange taste either, which I appreciate. The colors are all nice too. None of them are too feminine or too masculine, so the whole pack is usable. Although I somehow always end up keeping the orange and red ones for my wife. They last well. I usually change mine after around six months, not because they stop working, but because I like the bristles to still look straight and fresh. Even near the end, they don’t really lose that floss-like feeling. I just change them once the tips start looking a little too spread out. I wouldn’t mind if they were cheaper, but I keep buying them anyway at the current price. To me they're worth it and the value is good when you buy them in a pack of 4 or more... Hands down these are the best toothbrushes I’ve used.

reviews.title: Best toothbrush ever used
reviews.body: It’s crazy how good these are at leaving my teeth feeling clean and smooth. I was using an electric Sonicare toothbrush every night before bed, followed by flossing. My teeth just wouldn’t feel that clean and it bothered me (and I know how “clean” can feel because I used to brush and floss religiously after every meal while using Invisalign). When I flossed after Sonicare, I could usually still scrape a lot of food or whatever off my teeth using the floss. Now I do a routine where I use CloSys mouth rinse for 1 minute, followed by this toothbrush and then floss. My teeth feel so good afterward, and when I floss, almost nothing comes off my teeth except this one space where food like spinach always gets stuck! I’m a fan of this brush for life.

reviews.title: Durable, Compact, and Ideal for Work or Travel
reviews.body: I picked up this toothbrush as a dedicated travel and work option, and after using it for a few months, I’m very pleased with it. The packaging was solid, the materials feel durable, and the included storage case is excellent. Nothing about it feels cheap or fragile, which is more than I can say for many compact toothbrushes I’ve used in the past. In actual use, the toothbrush performs very well. The vibration is effective without being harsh, and the built-in timing interval is a nice touch that helps guide a thorough cleaning. It’s easy to use and does a good job overall. The only functional limitation I’ve noticed is that the short, straight brush head makes it a little difficult to clean my back molars. A longer neck or slight angle would help, but this is a minor issue and probably part of what keeps the toothbrush compact enough for travel. As a portable toothbrush, this one stands out. It’s lightweight, appropriately sized, and the storage case is one of its best features. The noise level is reasonable, and everything packs neatly away. After a few months of use at work it is still running on the original battery and the head is holding up well. Battery life and build quality are both impressive. Compared to other travel toothbrushes I’ve used, this is far superior. The build quality alone puts it ahead of most options, and the cleaning performance is solid for a compact device. I also feel that the price is appropriate for what you get. If you’re considering a toothbrush specifically for work, travel, camping, or general on-the-go use, this is a great overall choice. It does exactly what it should do, and it does it well. reviews.title: Great deal for great products!
reviews.body: I was in need of a new electric toothbrush, and as someone who has had braces for nearly 3 years (2nd round of braces as well), a water flosser is a helpful luxury. The toothbrush itself has good vibration, with different strength levels and modes, so I think it definitely gets the job done. The color is very pretty (I got pink), and it comes with 4 brush heads total. The water floss machine is very portable. It is easy to hold in your hand without being too bulky, and the water tank holds a sufficient amount. If you're still figuring out the water flossing technique like me, you may have to refill the tank once during use, but once I get the hang of it I'm sure I can stretch one tank for a single session. The water flosser comes with 4 heads total, one of them being a tongue scraper. Aside from the products and their attachments, they do not come with any sort of travel accessories. The toothbrush has a little cap that covers the end of it when there is no brush head attached, and the water flosser has space in the tank to attach 2 (i think?) heads to carry. Otherwise, there is no brush head covers that came with mine, nor is there a travel case or bag. This isn't an issue for me, as I can just buy a cheap travel case. The products themselves are great, and both the toothbrush and the water flosser come with charging cords. I haven't had any issues attaching or removing the accessories, and using the toothbrush and flosser is pretty easy and straightforward. All around, these products are pretty solid for such a good price and convenient combo!

reviews.title: Set 2 en 1 con cepillo e irrigador recargables por USB C.
reviews.body: Llevo varios meses tusando este combo de cepillo eléctrico e irrigador dental y os lo recomiendo no solo por el precio sino porque no está nada mal. Es bastante práctico que sea un sistema 2 en 1 porque en un solo dispositivo tienes el cepillo eléctrico para la limpieza diaria y el irrigador dental para limpiar entre los dientes, algo que normalmente solo se logra bien con hilo dental o aparatos aparte. El irrigador tiene 3 modos de limpieza y 6 niveles de intensidad, lo cual se agradece bastante. Si tienes encías sensibles puedes empezar con una presión baja e ir subiendo poco a poco hasta encontrar el nivel más cómodo. Además, el depósito de agua de 300 ml es bastante práctico porque permite hacer toda la limpieza sin tener que rellenarlo a mitad del proceso. El cepillo eléctrico sónico también funciona muy bien; tiene alrededor de 42.000 vibraciones por minuto, así que deja los dientes con esa sensación de limpieza profunda que normalmente se siente después de una limpieza profesional. También incluye boquillas y cabezales intercambiables, lo que lo hace útil para diferentes necesidades, como encías sensibles o personas con ortodoncia. Otro punto positivo es la batería recargable por USB, que dura bastante. Con un uso normal puede durar alrededor de 25 días en el irrigador y hasta 35 días en el cepillo, por lo que no hay que estar cargándolo constantemente. Este uso dependerá del uso que se le de por día, así como la potencia o modo seleccionado. En general, es un dispositivo bastante completo para mejorar la higiene bucal diaria a un precio realmente bajo, especialmente si quieres añadir irrigación dental a tu rutina sin comprar varios aparatos por separado y con precios mucho mayores. Este producto está fabricado en China.
reviews.body_en: I have been using this electric toothbrush and dental irrigator combo for several months and I recommend it to you not only because of the price but because it is not bad at all. It is quite practical that it is a 2-in-1 system because in a single device you have the electric brush for daily cleaning and the dental irrigator to clean between the teeth, something that is normally only achieved well with dental floss or separate devices. The irrigator has 3 cleaning modes and 6 intensity levels, which is very appreciated. If you have sensitive gums you can start with a low pressure and gradually increase it until you find the most comfortable level. In addition, the 300 ml water tank is quite practical because it allows you to do all the cleaning without having to refill it halfway through the process. The sonic electric toothbrush also works great; It has around 42,000 vibrations per minute, so it leaves your teeth with that deep clean feeling you normally get after a professional cleaning. It also includes interchangeable nozzles and heads, making it useful for different needs, such as sensitive gums or people with orthodontics. Another positive point is the USB rechargeable battery, which lasts a long time. With normal use it can last around 25 days in the irrigator and up to 35 days in the brush, so you don't have to constantly charge it. This use will depend on the use given per day, as well as the power or mode selected. Overall, this kit offers excellent value for money and is highly recommended for those looking to improve their oral hygiene with a practical and effective product. reviews.title: Simple, effective, and reliable sonic cleaning without the extra frills!
reviews.body: As an Amazon Vine Voice, I tested the PHILIPS Sonicare 1100 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush over a two-week period, using it for twice-daily brushing routines to evaluate its cleaning power, battery life, and overall usability. If you want to step up from a manual toothbrush without paying for expensive, feature-heavy models you'll never use, this stripped-down sonic brush is a compelling option. Here is my honest breakdown of how it performs: ⭐ Cleaning Performance & Power Sonic Technology: Delivering solid vibration action, it drives fluid deep between teeth and along the gumline. It leaves your mouth feeling remarkably fresh—way cleaner than any standard manual brush. Single-Mode Simplicity: It features just one cleaning speed and one button. While it lacks multiple intensity settings or fancy pulse cycles, it focuses entirely on doing the core job exceptionally well. Easy-Start Feature: If you are new to electric toothbrushes, it includes a built-in feature that gently ramps up the power gradually over your first 14 brushing sessions to prevent gum sensitivity. 🛠️ Design & Usability Slim & Lightweight: The handle has a sleek, ergonomic profile that feels comfortable and lightweight in the hand without taking up unnecessary counter space. Smart Timers: The integrated SmarTimer automatically shuts the brush off after the dentist-recommended 2 minutes, while the QuadPacer pulses every 30 seconds to signal when you should switch quadrants of your mouth. 🔋 Battery Life & Charging Dependable Endurance: The internal rechargeable battery easily lasts up to 2 weeks (around 14 days) on a single charge under normal use. Convenient Indicator: A subtle battery level LED indicator alerts you when it's time to drop it back on its USB charging base. 🛑 Minor Cons to Consider No Pressure Sensor: Because this is a budget-friendly model, it lacks a pressure sensor warning light. If you have a heavy hand, you'll need to mind how hard you press manually. Basic Accessories: The kit keeps things minimal with just the handle, one brush head, and a USB charging stand (wall adapter block not always included). The Verdict The PHILIPS Sonicare 1100 proves you don’t need to spend a fortune to get a dentist-clean mouth. It cuts out the complicated modes in favor of reliable timers, great battery life, and powerful sonic action. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a straightforward, high-value electric toothbrush!

reviews.title: Good for sensitive teeth
reviews.body: I have been told by dentists for years that I should be using an electric toothbrush, but I have VERY sensitive teeth, and every time I used one it sent me through the roof! Well, a couple tooth cracks later and I decided to suck it up and try again. I bought this one because it has a lot of settings, including one for very sensitive teeth. Out of the box it was sleek and solid, and the display was easy to use and intuitive. It did take some getting used to, and I used it with warm water, but it did not hurt, which was thrilling for me! Now, several months later, I can say that I love this toothbrush and that it genuinely cleans my teeth really well! I am not one for pairing things with apps or my phone, so I can't comment on that side of the toothbrush, but it does have a pressure sensor that lights up red or green to let you know if you are bruising too hard or too lightly as you go. The battery lasts a long time, as do the heads, and it comes with a travel case as a bonus. Two thumbs up!

reviews.title: Works Great but App is Okay
reviews.body: I had the old style Oral-B before and was ready for a new toothbrush. The IO5 was on sale so I bought it. I didn't think I'd use the app at all but it turns out that the gamification of my oral hygiene is a positive for me. I brush longer and use the guided brushing to make sure I'm getting full coverage. The only thing is that the zone identification is sketchy. On almost every brushing, it indicates the wrong active area of my teeth. I've tried Oral-B's recommendations- stand straight, do each tooth one at a time, move to different segments, repeat on inside and bite surfaces- but it still misdetects zones. What that does is make me brush even longer, so not terrible, but better accuracy would be much better and, frankly, I expected much better. Occasional it totally glitches and I need to restart the app and the brush. I also thought the battery would lastonger but it's about the same as my OG Oral-B electric that was around $40. Note that I am probably brushing longer, so maybe the battery is a little better but I hoped for 3 weeks and I'm getting less than 2 between charges. I still like the brush, but just know the app guidance doesn't work as well as you'd think. I do like that it reminds you to floss, brush your tongue, and use a mouth rinse. It also gives you a score for each session and a running score, which I like even though I thought I'd never use that. In summary, it works well and my dentist noticed a difference and told me to keep it up. It is a bit expensive for an electric toothbrush, so I hope it lasts a long time.

reviews.title: Lasted 12 years before I had to buy it again! Superior clean without the hefty price.
reviews.body: After an incredible 12-year run with my first Oral-B Pro 1000, I finally bought it again! The battery on my original brush finally bit the dust, and toward the end, it would only stay charged enough to get me through 24 hours of teeth brushing (if I was lucky) before dying. However, I loved the performance so much over the last decade that replacing it with the exact same model was an absolute no-brainer. Here is why this brush is a classic: Hygienist Approved: My dental hygienist once told me that it really doesn't matter how fancy or expensive an electric toothbrush is—any solid electric toothbrush is far superior to a manual brush. This model gives you that elite, professional clean without making you pay for unnecessary, over-hyped tech features. The One Minor Con: If I have to name one downside, it is the noise. Even brand new out of the box, it does sound a bit like it might be powered by hamsters while it is working. But just because it doesn't sound whisper-quiet doesn't negate the fact that it is a remarkably solid, heavy-duty toothbrush. A Note on the Color: The color is fun, but the listing is a bit misleading. I thought I would be getting a mint green, but instead, it is definitely a powder blue. I much prefer green to blue, but eh, whatever—it still cleans my teeth perfectly! If you want a proven, durable electric toothbrush that will last you for years to come without draining your wallet, this is the one to get. Highly recommended!
