reviews.title: Crooked, Overcrowded, Yellow Teeth
reviews.body: Let me start this review by saying that when I was younger, much to my parent's dismay, I neglected to brush my teeth. I would brush them but not as often and as thoroughly as a child should. This was partly due to my very bad gag reflex and partly due to the fact that it felt painful (?). Anyway, I've had yellow teeth my whole life (I'm 29) because of it. I never got braces (thanks again gag reflex) but my parents tried everything to get me to have better oral hygiene and to have a more aesthetically pleasing smile. Now that I'm well into adulthood, my smile being so yellow, and also very crowded, was starting to bother me. I knew I had to give in and fix one or the other. (To be clear if you have crooked teeth don't feel like you have to change yourself just for society - after 29 years, I can say that I truly wanted to change the yellowness purely for myself). I've gotten healthier in almost all other aspects of my life. I decided to make the plunge and buy this in hopes it would help get my teeth cleaner and help reduce plaque buildup. Not just for aesthetics, but for actual oral hygiene. So, I've used it twice a day for 3 days so far and my brother commented on how "white" my teeth look yesterday evening. That felt very good to hear, not gonna lie. I think this toothbrush is amazing for the price. I love how tiny the head of the brush is. It fits into my small, overcrowded mouth perfectly. I was worried that it would take forever to brush my teeth since I wasn't doing the work, the toothbrush was. However, it takes about 2 minutes and 30 seconds or 3 minutes if you're extra thorough. It allots 30 seconds to each section of your mouth, it will do a variation in the vibration to let you know when the 30 seconds is up and to move to the next portion of your mouth. It doesn't automatically shut off after 3 minutes (that I know of) if you want to go back and do another section of your mouth, which is nice. As for the pressure sensor on the toothbrush, mine does not work. It doesn't indicate any color or anything. It just appears to be a normal electric toothbrush. I may have gotten a "bad" toothbrush since it's not working, but to be honest, I truly just wanted something that would do a deep clean and this toothbrush does that. However, all the other reviews mention the sensor working so if that's something you're looking for, I would still highly recommend this toothbrush. I think mine might just be a dud in that department. The charging took several hours to be full on the first day. I keep it on the charger to ensure that it is always fully charged. If you don't have your charger with you and you need to rely on it without it, I'm told the battery lasts up to a week. Which, is very impressive for a $50 toothbrush. Amazon says that it has Bluetooth connectivity but I do not see any indication of that on the boxes or in the manual. My parents bought me an electric toothbrush when I was little, but I was too young to appreciate it. Now that I'm older, I think this is a great option for any person of any age. I do recommend it!

reviews.title: A great value that comes with power
reviews.body: This is the most powerful electric toothbrush I have ever used! I ordered this toothbrush to replace a manual one that I had. My dentist recommended an electric one so I picked this one up. This is amazing! My teeth have never felt so clean When you first get it, it will come with no charge, so make sure you charge it. In the box, it includes the toothbrush and a charger. You don’t get any extra heads so make sure that you order some. When you do use it though, you will love how clean your teeth get! My teeth have never felt so clean! I use it every day. It is waterproof, so you can take it in the shower, which is perfect for me since my mornings are rushed. It is enjoyable to use and to hold, it’s terrific! One thing I really enjoy about it is the two minute timer. It keeps me accountable to actually brush my teeth for a long enough time, and it doesn’t allow me to brush for a longer time than I have to. It pauses every thirty seconds, so you can brush each quadrant of your teeth for thirty seconds, so you can give one section of your teeth the attention it deserves. With the pros out of the way, I do want to talk about a few cons. There are way too many settings to use. I know that it’s nice to have many options to choose from so we can pick what we want, but you don’t need three different ways to brush your teeth. Most of the time I just click the on button and don’t bother with the other settings and turn it off when I’m done. The other settings aren’t even that different. You can see that in my included video The battery life is also not the best. Some people have reported getting a week or two’s worth of battery, but I’m finding I have to charge mine every five days, which isn’t a dealbreaker, but I travel a lot, so it’s not ideal. Speaking of not ideal, they use a proprietary charger which really makes this toothbrush not travel friendly. You need to take so many chargers with you for your phone and laptop. Those might have the same charger, like USB-C, but this doesn’t. So, you need to take this charger separately. Another thing is that you need to really keep the toothbrush, charger, and any surface it touches, clean and dry. Otherwise, wherever you put this, bacteria will start to build up. If you don’t clean your charger every other day, bacteria will start to build up and it’s gross. The included picture doesn’t do it justice, and that’s just on my sink. Despite my complaints, I really enjoy this toothbrush. It’s relatively inexpensive compared to other electric toothbrushes, it has lasted me a long time, and it’s powerful. I do recommend it!

reviews.title: Don’t be frightened when your teeth feels clean for the first time!
reviews.body: Absolutely phenomenal. People weren’t lying when they said it feels like you just came from the dentist. I don’t know how it does it, but if you brush the same way you brush with a manual toothbrush, alongside the intense vibration, it feels like it removes 100% of plaque, especially the plaque that’s hard to get behind each tooth. Also, at first, the vibration may feel a little intense, but you’ll get used to it. But if it’s too strong, just press the button and it will go to a slower mode. I highly recommend the strongest mode for the most effectiveness. But hands down, this is the best toothbrush I’ve ever got in my life. I will say, because the brush is small, I usually apply the toothpaste on my finger and place it in my mouth manually, then brush. But that’s my personal preference. I just prefer more toothpaste. And it sits well on the charging pad. I honestly have no complaints.

reviews.title: Great cleaning, versatile options for brush heads, charge lasts, but only 1 speed setting
reviews.body: One of my best purchases. I used to clean my teeth with a manual toothbrush, thinking that if I spent enough time and diligence, it would provide the same level of cleaning as an electric toothbrush. I was wrong. After my very first cleaning with this device, I felt a level of clean teeth only experienced when I leave the dentist's office after a cleaning. And it wasn't just a subjective feeling. When I returned for my 6 month cleaning the next time, there was barely any tartar or plaque build up - all had been removed by this toothbrush. I also noticed that my level of bad breath and tonsil rocks declined significantly. Turns out a manual cleaning is nowhere near as good as this machine. I have purchased this toothbrush for familty and friends, telling them it has changed my life. I wish I had this device as a child! The toothbrush comes with interchangebale heads, so that you can pick the one that works best for you - sensitive teeth, hard brush, whatever. Oral-B makes these products available, but you can also purchase no-name brands as well. It does create quite a bit of vibration in your head that I found a little scary at first. However, despite having sensitive teeth and gums, the toothbrush never harmed them. The toothbrush ahs a pressure sensor that stops once you put it too tightly against your teeth to prevent this. There is supposed to be 3 levels of speed for the brush. Mine doesn't seem to have them - has shown in the video. It's not that I don't know how to operate it - the toothbrush I purchased for my family (in white instead of pink) had those features, as advertized. In the end, I don't feel that having those 3 levels are important, except perhaps to get used to the sensation of vibration in the initial phases of use. The toothbrush comes with a plug and charger. It seems t o keep its charge for 4-5 days (I only use this toothbrush once a day for 4 min). Then the little light at the bottom of the toothbrush turns from green to red, alerting me that it is time to charge it (so I can usually travel without the toothbrush charge if it is for a trip that is less than a week). The charge itself happens very quickly - it seems to be charged within 20 min. I highly recommend this spinning toothbrush. It has changed my mouth's health!

reviews.title: Different!
reviews.body: This toothbrush is definitely different! I purchased them after watching a couple of YouTube videos of Dr. Ellie Phillips who highly recommended these brushes. They are gentle on the gums and I can tell that they are effectively removing food particles from between the teeth without the use of floss. I have always been a die hard fan of flossing because I believed that it was the only way to remove food debris from in between the teeth. However, after following Dr. Ellie Philips routine, my mind has changed. If you don't know who she is, she is a retired dentist who came up with a simple and effective program to help reverse gum disease, remove plaque and bacteria and help heal cavities among other things. Flossing can be kind of irritating to gums as I was having this problem. This toothbrush not only cleans the teeth better than ordinary toothbrushes but cleans below the gum line without causing any extra irritation. I noticed that my mouth is actually cleaner using this toothbrush and moving forward, I don't think that I will go back to regular toothbrushes. If you are dead set on flossing, I think that a water pik would be the safest choice which I may invest in the future but so far I don't think it will be necessary. I can't say enough good things about these brushes. Order them try them, If you don't like them you are only out of about 10 bucks. Not a deal breaker. I highly suggest you check out Dr. Ellies videos and then make an informed decision. Otherwise, I'm sold!!

reviews.title: I've been converted!
reviews.body: I've been a Sonicare user for over fifteen years now, but my dentist said it was likely making my gum recession worse. It doesn't help that I'm heavy handed. I took the plunge on these manual brushes not expecting anything special but boy, was I in for a surprise. The bristles feel like a gentle massage on the gums, and they get in-between areas that the thick Sonicare bristles could not (I know, the sonic action is supposed to create cavitation that replaces the need for actual bristle contact, but still...) These toothbrushes feel so good, and my mouth somehow feels cleaner than it did with my electric toothbrush. I now look forward to brushing and have to remind myself to limit to twice per day, because in my situation brushing too much causes more gum issues. 10/10 highly recommended!

reviews.title: A simple but highly effective electric toothbrush
reviews.body: This toothbrush functions excellently. I don't need anything fancier - it has three different speed/pressure modes and recharges on it's base. I have a bar covering my lower teeth that is hard to clean, but this brush and it's heads do it well. This is my first electric toothbrush and I will be sticking with it as long as I can. ONLY con is that grime buildup from the brushing process can build up in both the head and the stem of the brush unit. To keep them both clean, I remove the head, rinse both parts and tap them a few times on the counter to get the debris out. I let them both dry separately, and just reconnect it when I'm ready to use it again. It may seem tedious, but it keeps everything clean in the long run.

reviews.title: Big Performance Without the Big Price Tag: A Total Game Changer
reviews.body: I used to rely strictly on an Oral-B rotary toothbrush, but after picking up a cheap vibrating brush on a whim, I realized how much I preferred sonic vibration. Deciding it was time to step up to a proper rechargeable unit, I chose this one, and it has been an absolute game changer. In fact, I loved my first one so much that I ended up buying a couple more for family members. Real-World Details & Performance The feature that immediately stands out is the variety of oscillating patterns. Each setting delivers a distinctly different vibration feel, making it easy to switch up depending on what feels best for a deep clean. The shape of the brush head is exceptionally comfortable in the mouth, and the cleaning power easily outperforms my old Oral-B—I honestly don't see myself ever going back to a rotating head. While I haven't tried ultra-premium brands like Sonicare, I can't imagine they offer much more than what this unit delivers. Another massive plus is the value packed into the box: it comes with enough replacement heads to last a full year, making it effortless to swap in a fresh head every few months for that brand-new, fresh-from-the-dentist feeling. Pros & Cons Pros: Multiple Effective Modes: Distinct oscillating patterns that allow you to customize your clean. Superior Clean & Ergonomics: Head shape fits comfortably and cleans noticeably better than traditional rotary brushes. Outstanding Value: Includes a full year’s supply of replacement heads right out of the box. High Satisfaction: Fantastic overall performance that prompted me to buy additional units for family. Cons: Sonic Transition: If you are strictly used to rotating/rotary brush heads, the intense sonic vibration takes a couple of days to get used to. Final Verdict I highly recommend this toothbrush to anyone looking to upgrade to a high-performing sonic toothbrush without paying the inflated price tag of big-name brands. It delivers fantastic performance, incredible value, and a top-notch clean.

reviews.title: An absolute game-changer for kids with braces!
reviews.body: I originally purchased two of these electric toothbrushes for my kids after our orthodontist highly recommended switching from manual brushing to help keep their braces clean. Anyone with kids in braces knows exactly how difficult it is to get them to brush effectively around all those brackets and wires! These toothbrushes have been an absolute lifesaver. First off, my kids actually love using them. The brushing modes are incredibly effective at sweeping away food and plaque, but gentle enough that they don't irritate their gums. They find the handles easy to maneuver, and the built-in timer keeps them brushing for the right amount of time without me having to stand there and nag. It has taken the daily battle completely out of our morning and bedtime routines. The absolute best part, however, has been the results. At our last checkup, our dentist specifically went out of their way to comment on how incredibly clean their teeth are now. They noted a massive improvement in plaque removal around the orthodontic hardware compared to when we were using standard manual brushes. If you are a parent on the fence about upgrading to an electric toothbrush, especially if you are dealing with braces, this is 100% worth the investment. The quality is fantastic, the kids are happy, and the dentist is thrilled. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Makes my teeth feel as clean as coming from the dentist
reviews.body: So far, I am pleased with this electric toothbrush. I don’t think I’ve even explored the different modes yet (like the gum care mode), but I really just need it to perform its basic function of brushing my teeth. I haven’t updated my electric toothbrush in many years. I had an older model of the same brand, and it just seemed like the motor/batter had gotten weak and it wasn’t functioning that well anymore. I was definitely correct because this new Philips Sonicare packs much more of a punch compared to my old one. It was almost a little too much at first but I just needed a couple of days to adjust and now it’s great. I’ve noticed my teeth feel incredibly smooth all day long, like they do immediately after I go for a cleaning at the dentist. Now I regret not updating sooner because I think this will be great for my dental hygiene. I got this on a prime day sale so it is absolutely worth the money, however having used it now I would have been happy paying full price for the update in quality compared to my old brush. I haven’t been able to test the battery life yet, but we have travel coming up so I am happy that it comes with a travel case. Personally I love the modern look of the black brush, but it was hard to choose a color. It actually does feel nice to hold as well, when comparing it to my old one. It is slightly smaller and sleeker and slightly lighter weight. But not so light that it feels cheap, it still seems solid. Obviously I haven’t had it long enough to know how long it will last. But the old one (which again was the same brand) was still going after almost a decade. So if I get that long out of it, I will be very happy.

reviews.title: Fantastic clean, superb build quality, and great battery life
reviews.body: As an Amazon Vine Voice reviewer, I have tested my fair share of personal care devices, and the Philips Sonicare 5950 Rechargeable Electric Toothbrush immediately sets a high bar. Out of the box, you can tell this is a top tier, premium product with a lot of thought put into the engineering and design. The matte black finish looks sleek on the bathroom counter, but more importantly, the build quality feels incredibly solid. The handle has a nice weight to it, offering a comfortable, ergonomic grip that does not feel slippery when wet. The buttons have a satisfying click with zero play, and the brush heads snap on with a tight, precise fit. It feels durable and well sealed against water, which is essential for long term use. When it comes to performance, it leaves your teeth with that fresh, dentist clean feel every single time. The sonic vibration power is strong and consistent without feeling harsh on your gums, and the pressure sensor works like a charm to let you know if you are pressing too hard. Having the two brush heads included in the box is a great touch, making it ready for months of use right away. The battery life is equally impressive. A single full charge easily lasts for weeks of twice daily brushing, making it super convenient for travel without having to haul extra cords around. If you are looking for a high quality, reliable electric toothbrush that looks modern and delivers serious cleaning power, this one is worth every penny. Extremely well made and easily recommended.

reviews.title: Better than Phillips Sonicare. App is actually useful and not just a gimmick.
reviews.body: So, I'm a long-time user of Sonicare, which means I've gone through a number of them that always tend to break right at warranty expiry. Though I usually find them on sale, they are not cheap, nor are the brushes, and for the price they are still so prone to breaking down and various issues. So, when my current one started to have an issue (turning on randomly on its own, startling all around), I started shopping for a replacement. This Oral B brush went on sale, so I decided to check it out - maybe return if it wasn't all that great in comparison. At first, I was a little confused, because I thought these brushes mainly worked by rotation, but they are both that and sonication. I don't know if the vibration speed matches to Sonicare, but it doesn't seem critical. One immediate thing I noticed was the light ring which instantly lets you know if you are pressing too hard or not enough. As somebody with gum issues, this is appreciated. Next thing, do set up and try out the app. I was skeptical, but it really does a good job of figuring out what part of your mouth you are brushing, apparently by some kind of bluetooth-based sonar and something in the brush that can tell if it's facing up or down. It's not to the level of knowing which tooth, but it maps the front and two sides of both the top and bottom of your mouth, which is still pretty detailed. Rather than just using some kind of timer, it tracks that you spend the proper amount of time in each of the 6 regions. Your coverage within each region is then up to you. Sure, there are some times when it is a bit off, but I find that that tends to happen if I turn my head. So if you keep your head still, it seems to work more accurately. Not too hard to do. Besides the main brush tracking, you can set specific goals, and it will add recommendations for other steps like tongue brushing and flossing. I started a program for plaque removal. So now, instead of brushing or not kind of mindlessly in the shower one a day, I have started brushing twice a day, with more intention, and it's even slightly fun. And so far, my teeth feel smoother and cleaner. I also get less gum bleed, perhaps due to avoiding pressing too hard. I think this is still a bit pricey at full price, but maybe in this case it could be worth it for the improvement in your teeth and gum health. On sale, I can definitely recommend. Will it last long term? We'll see.

reviews.title: Good: Great cleaning - Bad: MESSY -- a 2 min brushing turns into 4 mins of cleanup
reviews.body: To be clear, the cleaning power gets five stars. However, this is the messiest toothbrush I've ever used. The brush heads have two holes in the back, and you might think you could _hold_ it a certain way to keep toothpaste and spit from getting everywhere. You would be wrong. If you've never had a smart electric toothbrush, the ideas here are very cool and mostly useful, but be prepared to have a LOT more cleanup when done than simply rinsing the head under the sink and wiping your mouth. Pay close attention, or you'll have stains on your shirt. Toothpaste WILL be on your chin, your hand, and dribbling down your arm, unless you keep your elbow raised for the duration! I love the ideas and how well it cleans my teeth, but for the reasons mentioned above, I can't really recommend this to people I actually like.

reviews.title: Incredible clean, with every penny
reviews.body: My roommate was raving about this toothbrush that he bought for himself a month ago. He knows I try to take good care of my teeth, and encouraged me to consider getting one, I’ve been using a manual toothbrush for my entire adult life. I had a ver basic electric toothbrush when I was a teenager, but it was not great, so I was skeptical, as I thought I did a pretty great job caring for my teeth with a manual one, but OH MY GOD was I wrong! I took a leap of faith and bought the io 5 with three different heads. I got it on sale. Well, very first time I used it, I felt like I had gone to the dentist to get my teeth cleaned and polished. My teeth feel sooooo good. I am currently also using the app, which is sorta fun, it maps out and tracks where you have brushed and how long, and the pressure guide is very helpful! It also tracks flossing, tongue cleaning and mouth wash rinsing, and you get trophies for completing a full mouth cleaning routine. It’s really helped me to commit to consistent oral care. If you don’t have benefits to get dental cleanings, I genuinely and honestly strongly suggest that you get this toothbrush. I honestly don’t think I’ll ever need to go get a dental cleaning done now that I have this tooth brush. Also, if you don’t have dental benefits, it is very much in your best interest to get this toothbrush, as dental repair is very expensive and having this brush is likely going to greatly reduce your risk of serious tooth problems. Also, I learned that it has a dual oscillating plus micro vibrations, which is why it cleans so well. I will undoubtedly buy another one of these when the time comes, maybe even level up and get the top of the line. Have only had it for a few days, so I can’t speak for its longevity or durability yet, but if it craps out, I’ll update my review. Seriously, do yourself a favour and get this toothbrush.

reviews.title: Elevate Your Dental Routine with this electric Toothbrush!
reviews.body: As someone who values a sparkling smile, I was eager to try out this cutting-edge device, and let me tell you, it did not disappoint. From the moment I started using it, I could feel the difference. The advanced technology behind this toothbrush delivers results like no other. Within just one week, it's clinically proven to provide 100% cleaner teeth and healthier gums compared to a regular manual toothbrush – an impressive feat by any standard. What sets this toothbrush apart is its Smart Display, which offers real-time personalized coaching. Paired with the accompanying app powered by Artificial Intelligence, it guides you through each brushing session, ensuring every surface of your teeth receives the attention it deserves. It's like having a personal dental assistant right in your bathroom. But the benefits don't stop there. The built-in 2-minute timer with quadrant intervals ensures that you're brushing for the recommended duration and covering all areas of your mouth evenly. Plus, the pressure sensor alerts you if you're applying too much force, safeguarding your gums and enamel from potential damage. In terms of convenience, this toothbrush excels. The rechargeable battery lasts impressively long – I've found myself needing to charge it only once a month, if not less frequently. And with the included travel case, maintaining your oral hygiene routine on the go has never been easier. Whether you're jetting off on a vacation or simply heading to the office, your dental health remains a top priority. Of course, like any product, there are a few areas for improvement. While the toothbrush does alert you when the battery is low with a flashing red light, a battery indication meter would provide even greater peace of mind. Additionally, addressing the maintenance of the brush head to prevent bacteria buildup would be a welcome addition to the product's features. Overall, the Oral-B Power iO Series 5 Limited Electric Toothbrush has exceeded my expectations in every way. It's effective, user-friendly, and backed by the trusted Oral-B brand. If you're ready to take your dental routine to the next level, look no further – this toothbrush is a game-changer.

Within just one week, it's clinically proven to provide 100% cleaner teeth and healthier gums compared to a regular manual toothbrush – an impressive feat by any standard. What sets this toothbrush apart is its Smart Display, which offers real-time personalized coaching. Paired with the accompanying app powered by Artificial Intelligence, it guides you through each brushing session, ensuring every surface of your teeth receives the attention it deserves. It's like having a personal dental assistant right in your bathroom. But the benefits don't stop there. The built-in 2-minute timer with quadrant intervals ensures that you're brushing for the recommended duration and covering all areas of your mouth evenly. Plus, the pressure sensor alerts you if you're applying too much force, safeguarding your gums and enamel from potential damage. In terms of convenience, this toothbrush excels. The rechargeable battery lasts impressively long – I've found myself needing to charge it only once a month, if not less frequently. And with the included travel case, maintaining your oral hygiene routine on the go has never been easier. Whether you're jetting off on a vacation or simply heading to the office, your dental health remains a top priority. Of course, like any product, there are a few areas for improvement. While the toothbrush does alert you when the battery is low with a flashing red light, a battery indication meter would provide even greater peace of mind. Additionally, addressing the maintenance of the brush head to prevent bacteria buildup would be a welcome addition to the product's features. Overall, the Oral-B Power iO Series 5 Limited Electric Toothbrush has exceeded my expectations in every way. It's effective, user-friendly, and backed by the trusted Oral-B brand. If you're ready to take your dental routine to the next level, look no further – this toothbrush is a game-changer.

reviews.title: Torn between this and the other brand
reviews.body: Been a Sonicare user for 10-15 years and decided I wanted to try the Oral B. I didn't want to spend a lot, so I found this one and ordered it. Things I like: Love circular motion of the brush instead of the up an down movement of the Sonicare. Love that it has a sensor to alert you if you are brushing too hard. Such a simple feature and hopefully it shows on my next dental visit. Battery seems to last a long time between charges. I am going on two weeks without charging which is great for travel. Like that the handle stays cleaner compared to my older Sonicare because of how it is designed. Toothpaste and water run down it and does not have a place to collect. Things I don't like: The brush had by design traps water whereas the Sonicare brush design seems to drain water better. I rinse my toothbrush and then lay it brush side down on a towel to let it dry before standing it up on the counter or charger. If not, I worry about it not drying fully and things growing. I hate that it doesn't have an auto shut off. It does vibrate every 30 seconds but it doesn't shut off. First time I used it I probably brushed for 3.5 minutes before I realized it wasn't going to turn off. Overall the quality doesn't seem as nice. Maybe this would be different if I had spent more money on a higher end model, but because this something I was just buying to try, I didn't want to spend a lot. If I was completely sold on this brush, I would upgrade for sure. I really am torn between the two brands of brushes. Now if someone would make one that has the best of both. :)

reviews.title: A brilliant and affordable upgrade!
reviews.body: This Toothbrush is amazing. I've never been able to own a Toothbrush like this one. Coming from a certain OB type one its certainly refreshing to have a toothbrush that works in a completely different way and cleans even better than my old one ever did. It has a 'sonic' vibrating motor inside that is very powerful and moves the brush head considerably more than my old toothbrush so it can reach more area of the teeth and get into places your old one couldn't. The toothbrush has many settings, Clean, Polish, Milder, White and Massage (Each Setting Shown in the video). A con of the device would possibly be that even though it comes with a USB-C charger that it does in fact take 2 hours to fully charge, which if your in a hurry to get somewhere and it has died, you can bet you will be leaving the house without brushed teeth. However the pro fact here majorly outweighs the con, this is because the actual life of the battery is immense. When I purchased this product about a month ago, before writing this review, I have only charged it once and it still seems to have loads of power left. Once! A single charge in an entire month! In certainly did not expect this. This is absolutely amazing given that my last toothbrush had the life expectancy of a few days to a week. Even less as the old toothbrush was very old and I thought it was time for an upgrade, and you can bet, I got one! The actual brush head has lasted the entire month too. Its not warped in any particular way that makes it look old but in fact makes it still look brand new. (As shown in the video). This, coupled with the 8 extra brush heads leads to the conclusion that this toothbrush might last an entire year, or more, without having to pay any extra money for replacement brush heads, something which I found myself constantly doing with my old Toothbrush which in turn cost a lot of money just for the heads themselves. I also noticed that the toothbrush works and cleans your teeth even without Toothpaste, of course I only tried this as a one off experiment to see what all the fuss was about regarding the sonicare technology and to see if it genuinely cleared the plaque off my teeth and to my surprise, it did a good job. (This may not be the same result for everyone as this was only tried once, and not again, so please do not take my word for it.) All in all, I would say that this product is a very good one, its affordable, uses newer sonicare tech instead of a rotating brush head, saves you money in the long term and can last an entire month on a single charge! Id definitely recommend this product to anyone, especially someone like myself who needed an upgrade from an outdated one to a cheap affordable one that gets the job done and done well. Would definitely recommend. Thank you for reading. P.S. I would like to add, at this time of posting this review, I cannot upload any photos or videos due to a problem with my phone, however, I can assure that upon reading this review, you should be able to use the given information (and other information on reviews on this product) to be able to possibly make a good decision to upgrade to a brand new toothbrush that is definitely worth the upgrade. Thank you for reading.

reviews.title: Finally!! This one is perfect!
reviews.body: Take in mind when you read most electric toothbrush reviews, they are coming from manual so OF COURSE YOUR TEETH FEEL AMAZING AND CLEAN, but what about when you’re coming from a really good electric toothbrush (Phillips Sonicare and another cheaper one that both felt like improvements after manual) and there are so many choices without a clear understanding what makes one $79 while another is over $200? I started to go a little crazy trying to figure it out. I asked one dentist to suggest and she said either oral b or sonicare (she doesn’t sell them at the office) while another said oral b (he did sell them) so that was not really helpful. When pressed my dentist who doesn’t sell them prefers oral b and she likes the smaller head. I GET THAT NOW! It’s like I’m polishing each tooth and wrapping the head around the tooth almost and I LOVE THAT! I think the Phillips isn’t getting in between near as well. The thing about either brand is that there is such a wide price range that I couldn’t tell the real $100 difference other than maybe an app and possibly more cleaning modes but that’s about it. I decided to go with oral b to try this round more precise head and went to their website to take the quiz to see what was best for me and this is where I landed. I wanted to stay under $100 (and you can on Black Friday and other big sales but I missed it and paid $119 which isn’t terrible if it’s significantly better than my last electric). I just used it for the first time and MY TEETH FEEL AMAZING , in fact my whole mouth feels so clean. I’m someone who buys a firmer bristle head (NOT HARD but I need to feel scrubbed if makes sense). I think sometimes I may be hard on my gums trying to really scrub my teeth but the happy medium is in this oral b brush head! I’m just not clear which one it is as it came with 2 and says one is ultimate clean and the other is gentle care. I’m assuming it’s ultimate but it’s soft but really dense and just scrubs but it’s gentle on the gums. Love it. Very satisfied. It’s not loud at all and it’s got a great light sensor that indicates when you’re at the perfect pressure. I actually found it quite helpful and it’s clearly visible even if you’re not looking in the mirror. I’m kind of excited about the app because after a long lifetime of heat checkups, something has gone wrong and I’m facing some pretty big restorative dental work so perhaps I’ve been slacking I don’t know But I’m trying to be very diligent and that’s part of the reason for the new purchase. I also felt like my old one wasn’t getting me as clean as it used it so it could be I needed something more aggressive. This is really perfect and considering the price tags you can easily go up to on the big name models, I think this really is the sweet spot for an electric toothbrush ESPECIALLY IF YOU’RE NOT COMING FROM MANUAL. If you’re coming from manual, any real electric toothbrush will be so impressive but I needed to be impressed after exclusively using electric. This is it. I’ve got no doubt about the battery life.. they are all that way.. the travel case is a great touch and it’s nice. Nothing like having your electric toothbrush go off in your closed suitcase when you’re all packed. lol. I was always able to get off brand replacement heads for my sonicare that were great at a fraction of the price. I’ll be interested to see if I can get a real match to this one otherwise it may be worth it to stick brand name. Here’s to your dental health and perfect check ups.

reviews.title: Great toothbush - your dentist will love you again
reviews.body: This is truly an amazing toothbrush. I find this does a much better job of cleaning my teeth and removing plaque. The features are pretty cool-it's the little things, right? You can change the colors of light (where the pressure sensor is) with multiple options. It has a magnetic charger at the base. The case has a charger feature which is a great feature-it comes with a cord and a power adapter-you can't even get that for $1300 cell phones anymore. It even has an interactive display-yes I like the smiley face when I'm done. I haven't tried the app yet, I've been brushing for a long time without one but I'll give it a shot because I do enjoy technology. This is quieter than my first Oral B but still sounds like a small drone in my head, still fairly quiet. The bristles are comfortable. Battery life is pretty good so far. Best part? I got it for a great deal when it was on sale last week. This is light years better than their competitor (rhymes with monic air) which I purchased for a lot more and wish I had returned when I had the chance. I hate it so much I'm willing to give a $200 toothbrush away. It may not be the newest in the iO line but I'm really impressed so far. Time will tell on how durable it is but I'm going to stay with the Oral Be family.

reviews.title: Whiter teeth in a month
reviews.body: I have been using this for a month, I normally only brush once a day because of my rushed schedule. I have noticed a whiter smile and cleaner feeling teeth. My son loves this, every night I brush my teeth with this using the app and at the same time he copies the directions with his normal toothbrush. It takes us 2 min 20 seconds to get a perfect clean score and at 10yrs old he is ok with that. The app shows you when to change sections of your teeth and how much pressure to use with customizable colors. its a little spendy but worth it for the clean feeling . It lasts about 6 brushes per charge and can charge in or out of the case. The app is easy to use and even with out the app the brush communicates to you through color about how much pressure to use.

I spent a lot of time comparing models, reading reviews, and trying to stay within a reasonable price range, and the Oral-B iO Deep Clean with Protect checked all the right boxes. It feels well-designed and comfortable to use, and the clean is noticeably better than a standard electric toothbrush without being harsh on my gums. The brushing experience feels controlled and thorough rather than aggressive, which I really appreciate. Setup was easy, charging is straightforward, and overall it feels like a quality product that delivers exactly what it promises. I’m very happy with this purchase and would recommend it to anyone looking for an effective, reliable electric toothbrush without going overboard on cost.

reviews.title: It's a nice toothbrush - but be watchful of the inside of the brush head, it can become moldy
reviews.body: Wow. This Oral B is a big improvement over the one I replaced. It’s whisper quiet in comparison, and I really like the pressure sensor light (green if good pressure, red if too much pressure, white if too little pressure). I also like that I can set the brush mode (speed) to “sensitive”, which is what I use exclusively with a sensitive brush head. My older Oral B only oscillated. This newer one both oscillates and micro-vibrates. My old Oral B was about 10-12 yrs old. It still worked perfectly. Buying sensitive brushes had become fairly inexpensive. I’m pretty sure it would have kept on working at least another 5 yrs. However, my hygienist repeatedly told me: “You’re not doing this, you’re not doing that, blah blah blah.” Tiresome. Sometimes the brush would strike under the gum line around a crown and cause lingering pain. I learned about the new Oral B with the pressure sensor and decided to buy one. Here was the surprising thing to me: I wasn’t brushing hard enough, at least according to the pressure sensor. The first time I used it, I was repeatedly in the white zone (too little pressure). Also, here’s the thing that really did it for me, I didn’t really know how to brush correctly. I found a video on YouTube (“Tips On How To Brush with an Oral B Electric Toothbrush” by Murmann Dental Health) that explained and demonstrated exactly how to brush using an Oral B with pressure sensor. That was very illuminating. I highly recommend that or a similar video. The thing that stood out from the video was that our teeth are rounded, so we need to wrap the brush around each individual tooth . I’ve been following what I learned in the video. So far, the brush hasn’t caused pain under the gum line. The IO sensitive brush along with the “sensitive” setting on the device have been a more comfortable brushing experience for me. I’m consistently in the green zone. Hopefully, it all makes a difference at my next dental appointment. I was sorry to see my old Oral B go as it was still useful, but sometimes useful doesn’t mean effective or appropriate for teeth & gum challenges. It can still be useful for other purposes. I have never used the app, so no comment there. The travel case is very nice and will come in handy. The only thing I don’t like about it is it doesn’t include storage for what seems to be a proprietary charger. The charger is two-pin, and I guess it’s supposedly safer to use in wet environments; you may need to include it in your travel bag depending on your travel time. 5 stars from me.

reviews.title: Worth upgrading from an older model
reviews.body: I bought my first oral b in 2016, what would be the equivalent of this model back then. I’ve thoroughly enjoyed it, and used it religiously all these years and it’s still going strong but the rubber face is starting to degrade so I figured I’d upgrade. I was NOT expecting the technology to have advanced so much, it is MUCH more powerful than the old style, with much less vibration and noise. It feels like I’m achieving the same clean in half the time with this one, and the new brush head style doesn’t have that stupid hole that dribbles toothpaste slobber all over your face like the old one. The screen is an added “cool factor” but doesn’t really offer a life changing upgrade aside from being able to see the battery percentage. The new charging dock design is nice, makes it easier to wipe clean without the little peg in the middle. All in all, this is a very nice upgrade and well worth the price. Here’s to the next 10 years of compliments from my dentist!

reviews.title: Meilleur brosse à dents avec un suivis avec l’application
reviews.body: Après plusieurs semaines d’utilisation, je peux dire que la brosse à dents électrique Oral-B iO7 a largement dépassé mes attentes. Dès la première utilisation, on ressent une réelle différence au niveau de la propreté des dents. Elles sont lisses, propres et donnent une sensation comparable à celle d’un nettoyage professionnel chez le dentiste. La prise en main est excellente et la brosse est très confortable à utiliser. Les différents modes de brossage permettent d’adapter le nettoyage selon les besoins, que ce soit pour un nettoyage quotidien, en douceur ou plus intensif. Le capteur de pression est un excellent ajout, car il aide à éviter de brosser trop fort et protège les gencives. L’autonomie est très bonne et la recharge est simple grâce à la base magnétique. J’apprécie également l’application Oral-B, qui permet de suivre chaque séance de brossage, de voir si toutes les zones de la bouche ont été correctement nettoyées, d’obtenir des statistiques sur ses habitudes et de recevoir des conseils pour améliorer sa technique. C’est une fonctionnalité très utile qui aide à adopter une meilleure routine d’hygiène bucco-dentaire. Points forts : * Nettoyage exceptionnel et sensation de dents très propres. * Fonctionnement silencieux et très agréable. * Plusieurs modes de brossage adaptés à différents besoins. * Capteur de pression efficace pour protéger les gencives. * Suivi détaillé des brossages avec l’application Oral-B. * Conseils personnalisés et statistiques de progression. * Excellente autonomie de la batterie. * Qualité de fabrication haut de gamme. * Recharge magnétique pratique. En résumé, la Oral-B iO7 est une brosse à dents électrique de très grande qualité qui offre une expérience de brossage nettement supérieure à une brosse manuelle. Les fonctionnalités connectées avec l’application ajoutent une réelle valeur en permettant de suivre et d’améliorer ses habitudes de brossage au fil du temps. Malgré un prix plus élevé, les performances, le confort d’utilisation et les fonctionnalités justifient largement l’investissement. Je la recommande sans hésitation à toute personne souhaitant améliorer son hygiène bucco-dentaire.
reviews.body_en: After several weeks of use, I can say that the Oral-B iO7 electric toothbrush has far exceeded my expectations. From the first use, you feel a real difference in the cleanliness of your teeth. They are smooth, clean and feel like a professional cleaning at the dentist. The grip is excellent and the brush is very comfortable to use. The different brushing modes allow cleaning to be adapted according to needs, whether for daily, gentle or more intensive cleaning. The pressure sensor is a great addition, as it helps avoid brushing too hard and protects the gums. Battery life is very good and recharging is simple thanks to the magnetic base. I also like the Oral-B app, which allows you to track each brushing session, see if all areas of the mouth have been properly cleaned, obtain statistics on your habits and receive advice on improving your technique. This is a very useful feature that helps you adopt a better oral hygiene routine. Strong points: * Exceptional cleaning and feeling of very clean teeth. * Quiet and very pleasant operation. * Multiple brushing modes suitable for different needs. * Effective pressure sensor to protect gums. * Detailed monitoring of brushing with the Oral-B application. * Personalized advice and progress statistics. * Excellent battery life. * Premium build quality. * Convenient magnetic charging. In summary, the Oral-B iO7 is a very high quality electric toothbrush that offers a brushing experience significantly superior to a manual brush. The features connected with the app add real value by allowing you to track and improve your brushing habits over time. Despite a higher price, the performance, comfort of use and features more than justify the investment. I recommend it without hesitation to anyone wishing to improve their oral hygiene.

reviews.title: Buen producto, mal vendedor
reviews.body: El cepillo está bien, se configura fácilmente y en general su uso es muy sencillo y los resultados son bastante buenos una vez que aprendes a usarlo bien. Sin embargo, Recomendaría adquirir este cepillo en otro lado, ya que me enviaron un producto previamente abierto, lo noté porque el empaque venía resellado con cinta de Amazon, y en el producto y sus accesorios se notaba unos rayones, y estaban un poco sucios y todo venía desacomodado. Me dio mucha flojera regresarlo porque fue envío internacional así que me lo quede, lo único que estoy seguro era nueva son los cabezales porque si venían sellados en su empaque original. Le doy dos estrellas porque darle una no le hace justicia al cepillo
reviews.body_en: The brush is good, it is easy to set up and in general it is very simple to use and the results are quite good once you learn how to use it well. However, I would recommend purchasing this brush elsewhere, since they sent me a previously opened product, I noticed this because the packaging came resealed with Amazon tape, and there were some scratches on the product and its accessories, and they were a little dirty and everything came out of order. I was too lazy to return it because it was shipped internationally so I kept it, the only thing I'm sure was new are the heads because they did come sealed in their original packaging. I'm giving it two stars because giving it one doesn't do the brush justice.

reviews.title: A great option over a standard toothbrush
reviews.body: What started as having just one of these in our household has turned into the whole family using these Sonicare toothbrushes. Having considered all the various models this particular one proved perfect for our use case. We have 5 of these in our household. We do have the white and black models and either are based on preference but over time I tend to think that even though the black (this model) might show residue easier that also makes it easier to see and clean and it's possible the white could discolor over time. The travel case is a nice feature to have. Have not traveled with it as of yet to see how functional and how much room it may consume if trying to travel light but it's there. The is not enough room to also store the charger in the case but will hold the handle and the brush (separated from the handle) in the included durable travel case. It does come with two additional brushes which is nice. The charging base is a standard two prong plug. Be cautious as some models seem to have a USB charging base that would require an additional purchase of a charger to charge in a standard outlet. This model has three settings with lighting for each. The bottom of the two buttons easily move through each setting with each press. There is a low battery indicator as well. Brushing with this is amazing. It's much more effective than a standard toothbrush or any standard electric toothbrush used over time. Even the kids notice how much cleaner their teeth seem after a use. Brushing harder is not good on teeth as any dentist has told me over time so this brush helps regulate how you brush. You don't have to brush with the Sonicare. The Sonicare does the brushing. You can simply slowly guide the brush over your teeth and let the Sonicare do its job. If the brush is pressed too hard against the teeth the Sonicare vibrations will halt as a sign you are trying to brush too hard. Overall this device is highly recommended and it's even better if you watch for a good deal that does or had occurred periodically.

reviews.title: I like brushing my teeth with it
reviews.body: I am a lifelong manual medium bristles toothbrush user. Over the years, I have seen electric toothbrushes in my friend's and family's bathrooms and never thought I would ever want to use one. After doing some research, I decided to buy this electric toothbrush. At first, I was not sure if the small brush head would do as good of a job as my standard size manual toothbrush. It took me two days and four brushings to get use to it. The small brush head did a better job at cleaning my teeth. I can not believe how clean my teeth feel after brushing 2 minutes with this toothbrush. Even my gumline has felt cleaner after brushing with this thing multiple times for a week. With my manual toothbrush, there were times I could feel that my gumline was not as clean as it should be. Never once did I irritate my gums while brushing like I did with my manual toothbrush many of times. The electric toothbrush pressure sensor prevented me from doing that to my gums. The 2-minute timer for the clean mode is good for me. After brushing teeth, I switch the intensity to the gum care mode to clean my gums. I like how the brush head replacement reminder and pressure sensor can be deactivated if you do not like those features. My traveling case struggles to stay closed. I may have to buy a different one for traveling with this electric toothbrush. I am impressed with it and wished that I would have bought one of these years ago. 1-24-26 I'm not impressed with the charger. If I use the toothbrush until the battery indicator starts to flash auburn color LED, it takes more than eight hours to fully charge the battery. There is not enough counter space for me to keep the toothbrush docked on the charger. My Philips Norelco All-in-One Series 9000 Trimmer, Wahl Pro Series Detail Trimmer, and Wahl Lithium Ion Pro Rechargeable Cordless Hair Clippers all charge faster than this thing. Heck, a Dewalt 6Ah battery chargers faster than this toothbrush.

reviews.title: My Old Fave Got Replaced, And This Did Even Better
reviews.body: I bought this toothbrush because my old model that’s no longer made had quietly become my go‑to—and I’m thrilled this one kept all the features I loved and then added a few extras. It came highly recommended by my dentist, and I’ve been using it steadily since. It gives that same clean, confident feeling and upgrades things like pressure sensing and smarter modes. Pros: Pressure sensor alerts you if you’re brushing too hard, love this for protecting my gums. Three cleaning modes (Clean / White / Gum Care), gives flexibility depending on what my mouth needs. BrushSync tech: the handle knows when the brush head needs replacing, so you’re not guessing. Travel case included, long battery life, solid extras. Cons: It’s a bit more expensive than my previous toothbrush, but honestly, worth it for the functionality. If you absolutely cannot stand any kind of tech beep or smart reminder, the extra features might feel like “too much.” I’m still waiting to see how long the rechargeable battery lasts compared to the old model. Final Thoughts: If you’re upgrading from a standard electric brush or your model is now discontinued (like mine), this one hits the spot. It keeps the trusted parts I loved and adds smart features I didn’t know I needed. Would absolutely recommend for anyone serious about brushing right.

reviews.title: Great set especially if you have dental implants
reviews.body: I recently picked this up after getting full dental implants and this is a great set. I had ordered black but somehow I received pink? I don't even see a pink set available on Amazon. Regardless I kept it. In all I like it but the charging cables may be an issue somewhere down the line. Here are my pros and cons. Pros: - You can adjust the waterpik settings without needing to have the waterpik on. - You can easily turn the waterpik on/off without fear of hitting one of the setting buttons. - The reservoir is the perfect size for me for one use. - You get a travel case for both the toothbrush and waterpik. - The toothbrush has a very nice "gums" setting - The base charger for the toothbrush has an interesting design which I believe will be easier to clean than my Oral-B. Cons: - You only get one charger cable to share between the waterpik and the toothbrush. - The charger cable is a non-standard barrel charger so good luck on finding a spare online. It should be USB-C or something more universal. - I'm concerned that the toothbrush base charger port may corrode over time due to water ingress. It should not have been removable.

reviews.title: Used it for couple of days and so far excellent product!
reviews.body: If I'm completely honest using floss is not the most practical way for me. I'm closer to 50s than I am to 40s and I still have all my teeth without cavities etc. even if used to eat lots of sweets. I don't go to dentist often (once in 5 years for cleaning) and all I can say is this product makes it easy for me to keep everything much cleaner. Longevity is something I can't confirm but product looks very well manufactured, materials feel solid, tolerances are unnoticeable operation sounds precise and tight. When it comes to options, both devices have various settings and the most powerful settings are not needed, at least not for me. Different adapters for water jet flossing are most likely useful and needed, but so far I'm using ordinary one and it does everything I need. I tend to use lower settings but I tested the most powerful ones too - watchout for those water jets, you could hurt your eyes :) Accessories (also packaging) look like luxury product. Nothing excessive, I know for some luxury is diamonds and gold or at least precious metals, but we are talking sane here - not filling inner voids. It comes with two travel cases, one bag and one nicely designed hard plastic box. Bag is for water jet and a nice box is for tothbrush and two brushes, for you and significant one I guess. You get bunch of other accessories you would expect and besides water and toothpaste you can use them from the moment you unpack it as batteries were near full or full. Still, I would recommend to charge them as soon as possible so the fact that charger is not included should not be an issue today. I have whole bag of them and any will do. Toothbrush charges on a stand and water floss has a rubber covered USB 3.1 connector. I have researched the company, their history and owners and they seem to be invested in developing quality products and uppon arrival it deffinitely looks and feels like one.

reviews.title: Ideal buy
reviews.body: ### Design and Build Quality: The Oral-B Pro 1000 features a simple, ergonomic design that is easy to handle. It has a rubberized grip that ensures a secure hold, even when wet. The toothbrush comes with a single CrossAction brush head, which is angled to effectively reach between teeth and along the gum line. The design is durable, though it lacks some of the premium materials found in higher-end models. The toothbrush is available in a few different color options, typically white with blue or black accents. ### Cleaning Performance: The Pro 1000 is equipped with a 3D cleaning action that oscillates, rotates, and pulsates to break up and remove plaque. This technology, combined with the CrossAction brush head, provides a thorough cleaning experience that is superior to manual brushing. Many users report a noticeable improvement in the cleanliness of their teeth and a reduction in plaque buildup. However, it doesn’t offer the same level of customization or advanced features as more expensive models, such as multiple cleaning modes or pressure sensors. ### Battery Life: The toothbrush operates on a rechargeable battery that lasts about 7-10 days on a full charge, assuming two minutes of brushing twice a day. The battery life is decent, but it falls short of some higher-end models that offer up to two weeks or more. The Pro 1000 does not have a battery level indicator, so users need to be mindful of when it needs to be recharged. ### Features: The Oral-B Pro 1000 is relatively basic in terms of features. It includes a built-in two-minute timer with 30-second intervals, which helps ensure users brush for the recommended amount of time and spend equal time on each quadrant of the mouth. However, it lacks additional features like multiple brushing modes, Bluetooth connectivity, or a travel case. This simplicity might appeal to users who prefer a straightforward brushing experience without the need for extra bells and whistles. ### Value for Money: The Pro 1000 is competitively priced, making it an attractive option for those seeking an effective electric toothbrush without spending a premium. It offers solid performance for the price, providing a significant upgrade over manual toothbrushes and some lower-end electric models. While it lacks some advanced features, it delivers on the essentials of oral hygiene, making it a good value for most users. ### Conclusion: The Oral-B Pro 1000 CrossAction Electric Toothbrush is a great option for those looking for a reliable and effective toothbrush without the complexity or cost of higher-end models. It excels in basic cleaning performance and ease of use, making it suitable for both new and experienced electric toothbrush users. While it doesn’t have many extra features, it covers the essentials well, providing good value for money.

Secondly I feel slightly uncomfortable that the charging port does not have a cap on it, so the toothbrush handle ends with a flat, blunt edge where you use the adapter to charge. And if you're like me, I brush my teeth in the shower in the morning, so I know it's being exposed to water and toothpaste ECT. That is the only reason for the 4 stars and not 5. -No universal charger port, no cover to the charging port and handle is fairly inexpensive feeling, however it is a good toothBRUSH and for the price you pay it is worth the investment. I feel if they fix those few things they'd be right up there with Phillips and other well known toothbrush makers. 4 out of 5 with potential to be a solid 5 with some fine tooning.

reviews.title: Ultrasonic Toothbrush Not True Electric
reviews.body: First, there are two types of electric toothbrushes. True electric and ultrasonic. True electric toothbrushes have heads that spin, etc. They provide spin or rotation to the bristles needed to brush your teeth so all you have to do is move the brush across your teeth. If this is what you want, then skip this set. Then there are ultrasonic toothbrushes, like this one. These toothbrushes have heads that just vibrate. There is no spin or rotation to push the bristles between and around your teeth. You still need to physically run the brush back and forth, in a circular motion, etc, for them to work. With that clarified, this brush works great. The head a nice size - not too big, not too small. The bristles are firm but not scratch off your enamel hard - as long as you don't use too much pressure. The head has longer bristles on either side that reach between your teeth and along your gum lines. The toothbrush stops vibrating for a moment every 30 seconds and then turns off at 2 minutes. This allows you to time your brushing by quadrant (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right). This makes it easy for those non-morning folks who suddenly realize they've been brushing one tooth for 5 minutes (you'll understand if this is you). The vibrations take a bit of getting used to - in some modes they can tickle your gums. Each mode is supposed to be for a specific use: White, Clean, Soft, Polish, Gum Care. The modes appear to simply change the amount of vibration - white being the strongest and gum care being the weakest. I would suggest just finding the mode you are most comfortable with and staying with that. Yes, you DO need to put the brush in your mouth BEFORE you turn it on. Just like you put the lid on the blender before turning it on. If you don't, then there WILL be a mess. This is not a failing of the toothbrush, it is simply the nature of the beast. I like that it comes with 8 heads. I've had other electric toothbrushes only to find after 3-6 months that I couldn't get replacement heads for them anymore. At this price point ($20 as of this review), if I can't get replacement heads after going through the 8 included, then I've still spent less than if I was buying standard toothbrushes. The heads do fit snugly and securely. The more you switch them out, the weaker that connection will be, and a head could come out during brushing due to the vibrations. I recommend you buy separate toothbrushes for each member of the family rather than trying to share and switch heads out daily. The toothbrush holder is simple but effective. It keeps the head protected while allowing it to air dry and it holds the toothbrush for convenient access. I attached the cover to a textured high gloss wall next to the sink and it has stayed in place without issue. The cover opens with just a light pull on the toothbrush so there is no fighting to get your toothbrush out. Overall, I highly recommend this toothbrush if you are looking for an ultrasonic (vibrating not spinning or rotating) toothbrush.

reviews.title: Powerful dual Sonicare set with great features
reviews.body: I purchased the Philips Sonicare DiamondClean 9000 Electric Toothbrush as a 2-pack (black and white) and have been very happy with the overall quality and performance. Having two handles in one package is extremely convenient—for example, one for home and one for travel, or one for myself and one for a partner—without needing to buy a second set separately. The build quality feels solid, and both brushes look sleek and modern, with a premium finish that matches the price point. In terms of brushing performance, the sonic cleaning is excellent. My teeth feel noticeably smoother and cleaner compared to a standard manual toothbrush, and the different modes make it easy to tailor the experience to daily cleaning, gum care, or more intensive polishing. The pressure sensor and timing guidance are genuinely useful; they help prevent brushing too hard and encourage you to cover the full mouth evenly, which is a nice touch for long-term gum and enamel health. The app connectivity is a bonus, especially if you like data and feedback. It can help reinforce better brushing habits and highlight areas you might be missing, though it does add a layer of complexity—Bluetooth pairing and checking the phone during brushing isn’t for everyone. Battery life has been good so far, but you do need to stay on top of charging both handles, especially if you’re traveling frequently or using multiple modes. Overall, this dual-handle DiamondClean 9000 set is a great choice if you want top-tier cleaning performance, smart features, and a premium look, and you value having two brushes in one package. The cost is on the higher side, but if oral health and convenience are priorities, it’s a strong investment.

I really like that new feature. It’s makes it fun to be able to see how long I’ve been brushing my teeth.

reviews.title: Wait until the price is $199!
reviews.body: Okay, if you are reading this and the price is higher than $199, WAIT. It goes down to $199 fairly regularly-- at least it did 2-3 times this year (including prime day), and did last year for Black Friday sales. I LOVE my sonicare. You will have to pry it out of my cold, dead, hands. It makes brushing so much easier, and I like the light when you are brushing too hard, which I've heard dentists say is a pretty bad thing. The battery life is great-- a solid 2-3 weeks out of one charge. I love that I can charge it, go on a week's vacation, and not worry about bringing the charger. I just throw a cover on the brush head and toss in my carry-on (note: since it is a rechargeable battery, please put it in your carry-on). The cover for the brush head is useless, so use something else when putting it in luggage. It has 4-5 different modes-- whitening, gum sensitivity, deep cleaning, etc. I like the whitening one, which is 2 min 40 seconds. It buzzes every 20 seconds to get you to move on to the next section. You can choose from strong, medium, or mild vibration. And the strong one is STRONG. I feel my head buzz when I use it, lol, so I normally stick to the medium. My teeth feel so much cleaner when using this, and I love the discipline it gives me. However, I have seen this vary in price from $199-399. Please don't buy it when it's at its high price. You can get a much better deal!

My teeth feel much cleaner and smoother after every use compared to a manual toothbrush. The only downside is that replacement brush heads are a bit expensive, but overall the performance makes it worth it. Overall, this is a high-quality toothbrush that really improves daily oral care. I would definitely recommend it.

reviews.title: ★★★★★ Great upgrade from a manual toothbrush
reviews.body: I’ve been using the Sonicare 7300 for a few weeks now and it’s made a noticeable difference in how clean my teeth feel. The pressure sensor is genuinely useful — it lights up if I’m brushing too hard, which I didn’t realize I was doing with my old brush. The SmarTimer keeps me honest about brushing the full two minutes, and it pulses every 30 seconds to remind you to switch quadrants. Having 12 different brushing settings might sound like overkill, but I actually use a few of them — the gum care mode is gentler on my gums, and the whitening setting feels more thorough for the odd coffee stain. Battery life is excellent — I’m easily getting close to the advertised 21 days on a single charge, so I’m not scrambling to find the charger during travel. The included travel case is a nice touch and keeps everything protected in my bag. Only minor gripe: it’s a bit pricier than a standard electric toothbrush, and replacement brush heads add up over time. But for the overall brushing experience and results, it’s worth it. Bottom line: A solid, feature-packed electric toothbrush that’s easy to recommend if you want something better than a basic model without going full premium.

reviews.title: A new level in toothbrush performance, but no wall plug and an intrusive app
reviews.body: This toothbrush appears to live up to the extravagant claim on the box. I have no way of knowing if the amount of plaque removed is actually 2000% more than what my previous Sonicare could do, but it is a huge improvement. I used to believe the job of an electric toothbrush was to pound my gums into submission, but this model is far more gentle and does a better job of reaching the tricky trouble spots my dentist never tires of pointing out. So I do recommend this product with almost no reservations. But before you open the box you should know that the power cord is a USB-A plug, wall unit not included. Phillips says this is to cut down on electronic waste, which is such an obvious euphemism for "it saves us money" that you wonder why they even bothered. Also, the Sonicare 7300 has Bluetooth connectivity, and you can download an app and connect to, um, your toothbrush. I said what the heck I'll give it a try. The app says it values your privacy but then it doesn't let you complete setup unless you agree to send all data to Phillips so they can help you with suggestions for improving your dental hygiene. Then the home screen comes up and it's a dental chart, at which point I killed the app and uninstalled it. Perhaps you might find such detailed help useful, but I'm not interested in being an unpaid beta tester or belonging to a floating focus group for future products. I've been using a Sonicare for years and will continue to do so. But the way this product is packaged and presented seems to make it just another way that big business is trying to carve off a big slice of my conscious awareness. And I’m getting tired of that. reviews.body: The Philips Sonicare 7300 doesn’t just clean your teeth — it judges your entire dental existence. In the best way. The first time I turned it on, I swear it sounded like it was saying, “Move aside, amateur, I’ve got this.” And it did. This thing blasts plaque off your teeth like it’s clearing a runway. My mouth hasn’t felt this clean since the day I grew my first tooth. The pressure sensor lights up like a tattletale every time you brush too hard. The timer keeps you honest. The brush heads feel like they were engineered by NASA for enamel. And the clean afterward? Unreal. My teeth are so smooth I’m convinced I could butter toast with them. It’s powerful, it’s smart, it’s slightly condescending — and it’s absolutely fantastic. Five stars. My dentist is going to weep with joy.

reviews.title: Lighter touch than others; higher vibration speed; does a fine job on only one battery.
reviews.body: I have always used the Arm & Hammer Spin-Brush, and now that it is no longer available, had to find a replacement. I specifically wanted one that used batteries, so I don't have to fuss with a charger when on a trip. I was frankly concerned that there were no two-battery units like the Spin Brush, worried that a one-battery unit would not be as aggressive as I would like. And when I first used this one, it seemed less forceful, so my concern remained. Over a few days I realized that this brush vibrates a a much higher rate than the old two-battery Spin Brush, so it seemed to be doing its job just as well as my old device. In fact, it finally occurred to me that the whole idea of an electric toothbrush was to increase the brushing action rate compared to manually brushing; therefore faster is better, offsetting any lack of aggressive power. I have come to believe that this brush is every bit as good as my old one, even with only one battery. One thing I should mention though, is after several weeks I failed to notice it was moving slower. Just as an experiment I put in a new battery and voila! It began spinning at a much higher rate - I hadn't noticed it slowing down, and will now pay attention as it may need a battery every two to three weeks. That's not a problem as my old Spin Brush needed two batteries over 4 to 5 weeks, so it's basically a "break-even" on battery usage. It's been over a month since I got this brush, and in fact ordered several because they are very well priced on Amazon; I waited to review it honestly and can now say I am comfortable with the lighter touch and faster speed as a better solution to power toothbrushing. I hope this doesn't get discontinued in a couple of years now that I find it so useful!

reviews.title: Works well ... but wears out FAST!
reviews.body: Mixed feelings on this one. I've been using it for quite a few years now. I like how it works, when it works. It's just that the brush heads and the brush itself wears out a lot quicker than I like. I generally have to change the heads once a month or so. What happens is while that the bristles themselves aren't really worn down at that point, the head itself loses its back and forth rotation. It might "appear" to be still be turning, but check it in the mirror when there is pressure on it, i.e. against your teeth and gums, or test it against your fingernail, and you'll see when it's no longer effective. At that point, it's just basically vibrating in your mouth without cleaning anything. Folks who use this regularly should check for this. It took me a while to realize that after a month or so, I was merely pretending to brush my teeth but not really cleaning anything. Also, once the head wears, the seam/gap between the main piece and the rotating brush part loosens and widens quite a bit and pinches the insides of your mouth. The brush itself tends to wear out after about 4 to 5 months, where once again it still "appears" to be working, but if you check carefully, you'll find that even if you put a new head in there, the rotating properties diminish greatly. I think the inner mechanism simply wears out by then, and no longer connects and moves the brush head as well. Yes, once again, let's all thank corporate America for "Planned Obsolescence". I used to use Sonic Care. The $125 model I bought was good, but no longer held a charge after 2 years. How convenient for Sonic Care. Then I tried their battery operated $40 model, which worked OK but had a really stupidly designed battery cap which allowed water to flow into the compartment. Wow, that's TITANICALLY STUPID!!! Anyway, found this and works OK ... and have been using it since. However, not without the stated reservations. If one were to change the brush and brush heads as often as necessary (which I do), it's not really all that cheap to use. It's actually pretty expensive to use. About 10 to 12 heads and 2 or 3 brushes a year. Do the math. If I find a better alternative, I'll switch without too much nostalgia, ha ha. Note: I do want to state that my brushing routine is probably a lot more thorough and longer than most (about 5 minutes per session), so others may get a longer "effective life" than I get. But still, can't imagine their recommendation of changing the heads every 3 months being adequate. Folks who use this really should monitor the "TRUE effective life" of their brushes and heads, otherwise you might "think" you're brushing your teeth, but might actually be doing nothing to effectively "clean" them. Hope this is helpful. Cheers

reviews.title: Cheaper than a filling & totally worth the investment after 9 months of use
reviews.body: My dental hygienist recommended this toothbrush about nine months ago. When I mentioned how expensive it was, she said, “It’s still cheaper than getting a filling.” That changed how I looked at the price, so I went for it. The guided brushing app takes the guesswork out of whether I’m actually brushing everywhere. I used it twice a day in the beginning, which really helped me build better brushing habits. Nine months later, I don’t use the app every time anymore, but I still check in here and there to make sure I’m staying on track. The pressure sensor is also super helpful! My dentist mentioned that many people damage their gums and teeth by brushing too hard, and this makes it very obvious when you’re using too much pressure. I’ve had two dental cleanings since switching, and both were probably the quickest I’ve ever had. My dentist and hygienist said everything looked great with very little cleaning needed and mentioned they commonly see this with patients using an Oral-B iO. The brush heads indicate when they need replacing, which for me has been roughly every three months. They’re about $10 per replacement head, so that’s another ~$40 a year to factor into the cost. Not cheap, but reasonable enough for me considering how well the toothbrush has performed. My only complaint is that it’s can be a bit messy. Even after rinsing the head and shaking off excess water, some water/toothpaste tends to run down the handle once it’s on the charger, so I clean the charging base a couple times a week. It’s definitely an investment, but after nine months of daily use and two great dental checkups, I’m very happy I bought it.
