reviews.title: Buy this!
reviews.body: I'm new to electric toothbrush & it took me a minute to get use to this but once I did, I am very, very happy with it! At first it seemed like it wasn't brushing my teeth with much of the toothpaste (it kept slinging it everywhere in my mouth) but to fix that I manually brush the toothpaste on my teeth (just enough to cover my teeth with it) then turn on the brush. That is the freshest my mouth & teeth feel. It's as if I'm coming out of the dentist every time (& that is a great feeling!). My teeth are WAY cleaner & even stains are nearly gone (I drink a lot of dark drinks). It'll stop/vibrate every 30 seconds to let you know to switch to another side of the mouth. I also love how it tells me if I'm pressing the brush to lightly or to hard on my teeth (the colors will tell you, green is good). The spin is powerful & toothpaste will be slinging out. I always turn it off before I take it out of my mouth because it slings so much. I love the multiple settings you can choose but I always choose the sensitive option. It's not as strong as the daily clean option (daily clean was irritating my gums). The charge lasts a good while. I still use manual brush sometimes & I don't use the Bluetooth stuff so my charge lasts longer. I bought this in December & only had to charge it once. So if you use it more than I do you might need to charge it 2 or 3 times a month. Although I don't travel, I like that it came with a travelling charging case. I just see it as an extra charger in case something happens to my regular one. If you decide to buy I recommend looking at every electric toothbrush from this brand & comparing the cleaning options that are available for each one (I love how this one had a lot to choose from). They made it extremely easy on Amazon for me to compare them. The cleaning options you're interested in might result in a cheaper brush, you might not be interested in multiple cleaning options. Also compare the Bluetooth stuff. I don't care about the extra blue tooth stuff so I got this one which is cheaper. Whichever brush you choose, I'm sure you will not be disappointed. This brand is fantastic & I would definitely buy from them again whenever my brush is done for.

reviews.title: Daily Brilliance: Discover the Habit-Forming Magic of the iO 9 Series
reviews.body: Overall Satisfaction: I give the Oral-B iO Series 9 a solid 5. This toothbrush is amazing and well worth the higher cost compared to other series. Main Purpose: I purchased this toothbrush to maintain optimal dental health and minimize the need for extensive dental procedures. Ease of Use: The toothbrush is excellent, and you can even turn on the phone to track your performance. It offers awards for meeting specific goals, some of which can be challenging to achieve. Performance: The Series 9 comes with additional sensors and a flat magnetic mount for convenient charging. While the battery drains quickly, it's not an issue for short 2-3 minute sessions. Features: The ability to visually track cleaning habits is a standout feature. With multiple modes available, I typically use sensitive, whitening, or daily settings. Durability: The toothbrush is very durable, and despite the quick battery drain, it's not problematic for regular use. Value for Money: Although expensive, the toothbrush pays for itself when considering the savings on dental bills, primarily limited to cleanings. Comparisons: Compared to other Oral-B models, the Series 9 is more advanced, with the phone app being the most significant difference. It provides detailed information about brushing habits and areas that need improvement. Pros: Maintain Oral Health: Keep your teeth clean and healthy with advanced features. App Integration: Track your brushing habits and receive feedback on the app. Charging Options: Charge the toothbrush using the magnetic mount or the convenient travel case with an attached cable. Cons: Lack of Apple Watch Compatibility: It would be more convenient if the toothbrush worked with the Apple Watch, eliminating the need to pull out the phone for information. Additional Tips: For a clean toothbrush and to avoid hardened toothpaste, use the travel charger instead of the magnetic mount. Cleaning the head after each use and washing it with water is also recommended. Recommendation: If you're looking for a top-notch toothbrush that not only ensures oral health but also provides insightful data through a dedicated app, the Oral-B iO Series 9 is worth the investment.

reviews.title: A baffling design flaw in a very expensive toothbrush
reviews.body: I bought the Oral-B iO Series 9 expecting a premium product. The toothbrush itself has a lot to recommend it, but the charging base has one of the worst design flaws I have encountered in a consumer product. The iO9 is a relatively tall, expensive electronic device, yet while charging it essentially balances upright on a small, shallow magnetic base. There is no meaningful post, socket, collar, or other mechanical support to keep the handle from tipping sideways. Because the handle is so tall, it takes remarkably little lateral force to knock it off the charger. This isn’t a hypothetical concern. I had a previous Oral-B toothbrush fall from its charger and break. With this one, I eventually stopped keeping it conveniently in the bathroom because I didn’t trust the charger to keep it secure. I actually improvised a second magnetic support against the handle when I kept it elsewhere, which dramatically improved its stability. What makes this especially frustrating is that the problem is neither difficult to foresee nor difficult to solve. Competing electric toothbrushes use charging designs that mechanically locate and support the handle. Even a modest post, recess, collar, or other positive restraint could dramatically reduce the chance of an expensive toothbrush being knocked onto a hard bathroom floor. For a flagship toothbrush at this price, this is particularly difficult to excuse. Oral-B put enormous engineering effort into the iO’s display, sensors, pressure detection, Bluetooth connectivity, brushing modes, and app integration. The company should have put comparable thought into the much simpler requirement that the toothbrush remain standing securely while it charges. Prospective buyers should know about this before purchasing because it isn’t something obvious from the feature list. If you buy one, be very careful where you place the charger

reviews.title: This one is a game changer!
reviews.body: I LOVE this toothbrush!! This is NOT my first electric toothbrush :) I started with a Sonicare -which I really liked. I liked that it told you if you were brushing too hard and the different brushing modes It was about $150 but it only lasted a year or so, so that made me mad! I switched to the Oral-B Pro 1000 which was only about $50 and has lasted a very long time. I have a smaller mouth so the heads on the Oral-B work better for me. I am an aggressive brusher so the simple Oral-B Pro 1000 was really not ideal. It has a timer but nothing more. So I was wearing out the enamel on one side of my mouth. I did all this research on which one to try next and I ended up with the IO 9. I got this for $250 which was LOT, but now that I have been using it - it was totally worth it. I cannot believe how much cleaner my teeth are for the same amount of brushing time. I can feel the difference. Also I love the color to tell me if I am pressing to hard or not enough. I do switch the cleaning mode every day as well. So I do the Daily Clean at night and the Sensitive or Gum Care in the morning. The app is cool too! I love the analysis of my brushing. I heard a dentist say that we should change which hand we brush with to get even cleaning -and he is not wrong! I definitely get one side more than the other. Who knew! I only hope that this one lasts a long time since it was a LOT of money. So far it has been worth it!!

reviews.title: Not as many settings as fancier models, but all the settings I really need
reviews.body: I've long used Sonicare toothbrushes and since I get good reviews from the dentist, I trust them to keep my teeth fresh and clean. I'm replacing a "fancier" model of toothbrush, but this one has all I need as I always used the regular setting and never paid attention to the brush head replacement warning anyway, replacing my brush head when it seemed worn. It has the same quality of buzz I remember from when my old Sonicare was new (it had in the last month or so seemed clunky, that's why I replaced it.) It's actually easier to use since it has fewer buttons, so I'm not accidentally pushing a button and changing a setting as often. The only thing I don't like is the brush head that came with it, but I replaced it with the Diamond Clean head that I'm used to and it's now basically all the same, just a better price. The brush seems well made and the usual quality of Sonicare products, I'll update if it dies sooner than normal. Overall, I like it. I won't discourage you from buying one of the more expensive models if you want the additional settings, but this has all I really need. So I'll stick with it and making sure to floss to keep my dentist happy.

reviews.title: Top tier product without the Top Tier price.
reviews.body: Decided it was time to switch the family back to a electric toothbrush rather then standard brush. With a wife and two kids (12 & 9yrs) the price of the big box brands is hefty. So we decided to try these out because of the value they seemed to bring for the price including so many brush heads. We selected four different colors to be able to distinguish which one as ours. The brushes come with plenty of brush heads, these could last us awhile for sure. After a few weeks of use on the first brush head they seem to be lasting quit well to the daily use. Each brush head came in its own small sealed packing to keep it protected. Only thing I wish was if each bag was labeled with what type of brush head it was, as the product comes with 2 styles. These are rechargeable and they come with their own charging cable (DC style plug not USB) When they arrived I plugged all 4 of the brushes in to fully charge them. After 2 weeks of usage they are still on the original charge and showing no signs of slowing down. I plan to throw all 4 of them back on the charger again this week to keep them all topped of. See if I can get a routine going where I charge the whole families all at once. In regards to the most important part, how does it brush? Fantastic, honestly leaves my mouth feeling way more clean then a standard toothbrush. Allow the brush to do all the work, no need to go back and forth with a scrub. Just slowly work the brush around your mouth works wonders. It has a built in feature where it does a brief pause on the brushing to remind you to rotate to a different part of your mouth. While this feature doesn't really help a adult much because we understand time, for our two pre-teen kids its very helpful. They have mentioned it helps remind them with the foggy morning mind to move onto another area. Overall happy with the product for such a great price, will they last years? That I do not have the answer for, but if I can get 1 year out of them for the price I'll be very happy.

reviews.title: A vibrating, "you-get-what-you-pay-for" electric toothbrush.
reviews.body: I've never bought into the hype of "electric toothbrushes," but I thought I would give this relatively-cheap one I saw discounted on Amazon a shot. Mainly because it came with 10 replacement heads and if the batteries ever went kaput, I could just use it as a normal, albeit bulky, toothbrush. After using it every day over the last month, I have to say that I have rather mixed feelings about this rechargeable toothbrush (words I thought I would never say). First, the positives, and there are some to be found here. The battery life, in my experience, has actually been fairly good. Though, that could likely be attributed to how low-tech this tech toothbrush actually is (we'll get to that later.) The brush is lightweight as well, allowing you to maneuver it easily. The three vibrating modes do work and offer some variation for you to test and see which you like best. The brush also has an internal timer that briefly stops the vibration every 30 seconds, ultimately shutting off after 2 minutes. I personally found this to be annoying at first, but now kind of like knowing how long I've been targeting a specific area for. And finally, yes, you could use this as a "manual" toothbrush if your forgot to charge the battery. Keep in mind that the bristles are incredibly soft, so if you like your normal toothbrushes with some tensile strength, this one might not be for you. Now for the "bad," or mediocre I guess I should say. The Teetheory toothbrush is little more than a vibrating wand with a brush attachment affixed to it. The bristles don't move, sweep, rotate, or oscillate like a more premium electric toothbrush would, so leave that fantasy behind now. Yes, the bristles do technically move, but that's just because of the vibrating motor that your brush head is on. The bristle movements are incredibly fine and gentle, to the point that you question if it's really doing any good at all. In terms of cleaning power, this is probably far from dentist-recommended. Also, if you have sensitive teeth, I wouldn't recommend this toothbrush. The vibration is all along the top portion of the brush, so if you even graze your teeth, you'll get a rather uncomfortable sensation. I personally don't have very sensitive teeth, but every time I've used this brush, I make the mistake of touching my teeth with the plastic, non-brush portion and it doesn't feel pleasant. Now, with a product like this, you have to take into account the price you're paying, which is significantly less than that of a premium electric toothbrush. I'm aware of and totally understand that. But judging this product on merit alone, I can't really say that I would wholeheartedly recommend it. Does it clean your teeth well enough? Yeah. Does it do it so well that I'll never use a normal toothbrush again? Not really. If you're truly gung-ho about dental care, would suggest spending the extra cash for a premium electric toothbrush. Specifically, one of the electric toothbrushes that actually spins. If you absolutely must have an electric toothbrush for cheap and you don't really mind it being low-tech, this will do you just fine, I suppose. As for myself, I will continue to use this brush for the foreseeable future, and hope to see if the reviews others have posted about the brush not working after a few charges are anomalies or something everyone should expect.

reviews.title: Slightly expensive, but a beast all around!
reviews.body: Absolutely love this toothbrush! Our dentist recommended we use Phillips Sonicare brushes and at first I was a bit skeptical. I order this about 1 year ago and waited to see how much I liked it before writing a review. After using it for a year, I'm not sure why I never checked one of these out before. Ergonomically, the base of the unit fits well in my hand and is easy to maneuver. The buttons are placed in great positions so I can change the brushing modes or intensity levels easily on the fly. I keep it on a shelf mounted in the battery charger at home, but I have travelled with it a few times and the battery holds a good charge for more than a few days easily. I've never had a situation where I've taken it with me and had it run out of battery. It cleans very nicely and isn't too bulky to have any issue reaching the back molars and has great maneuverability while brushing. I like the fact that it's not very loud as far as noise, and it has convenient 30 second notifications to let you know how long you've been brushing. I typically do one quadrant for 30 seconds for a total of 2 minutes, so it's nice to have the 30 second 'buzz' go off and let me know it's time to move. Two of the coolest features about this electronic toothbrush: (1) - the pressure sensor that let's you know if you're brushing too hard. It's easy to see the light come on when I tend to put too much pressure on the head. (2) I use it in the shower so it's nice that it's mainly waterproof (even if it's not sold as that in the description) but I have been using it in the shower for a while and it's not had any issues. The travel case is nice to have when you need to pack it up and head out on the road. I stay away from home about 4-5 times a year for work and it packs up really nicely and the case obviously keeps it protected. If I had one complaint it would be the unit cost and the replacement head cost. When I first looked them up, I thought the price was crazy!! But it's held up and continues to be my favorite toothbrush of my life, and I've had many in my 50 years on this planet. If you're thinking about getting an electronic toothbrush, this one definitely delivers.

reviews.title: Well known flaw with gasket causing water to corrode and kill the battery
reviews.body: I really like the toothbrush however they aren’t made to last more then a year or two if your lucky. This is my third purchase of the same item, and has thankfully come down in price. All three times it’s been the same issue that destroys the toothbrush, a white gasket at the top of the toothbrush. I would remove the brush and dry the gasket clean after brushing and remove any toothpaste that surrounds the area. I like the light at the bottom of the brush which activates if I’m pushing too hard. As seen in the pictures, water got in and corroded the battery and the bottom light. This will be my last purchase, the quality build is poor and a well known issue with customer service and countless reviews I’ve read. I have three packs of replacement brushes which are expensive and can’t be returned. I like the features the brush has and cleans my teeth very good and has a great gum care setting. The brush itself is super loud, and annoying, I can tolerate it, but for whatever reason my wife always asks me a question while brushing, and it can be challenging to hear, (note) I’m not hard or hearing, or while trying to listen to a video on my phone. For 200.00 on Amazon, it’s also a high price.

reviews.title: The Rolls Royce of Toothbrushes
reviews.body: Let me start by saying this: if my teeth could throw a party, they’d invite the Philips Sonicare DiamondClean Smart 9500 as the guest of honor. This toothbrush is the Beyoncé of oral care—expensive, yes, but absolutely worth it. Sure, my wallet cried a little, but my teeth have never been happier, so I consider it a fair trade. Durability: This thing is built like a tank. I’ve dropped it more times than I’d like to admit (blame my morning clumsiness), and it still works like a champ. It’s survived my butterfingers and my dog’s attempts to steal it for a chew toy. If this toothbrush were a person, it’d be that friend who always has their life together while the rest of us are just trying to survive. Charging Capability: The charging glass is chef’s kiss. Not only does it look like something Tony Stark would design, but it also charges wirelessly. No fumbling with cords—just plop it on the glass, and it powers up like magic. The battery life is impressive too. I charged it once, forgot about it for weeks, and it was still going strong. It’s like the toothbrush version of a marathon runner. Travel Case: The travel case is a game-changer. It’s sleek, compact, and even has a USB port to charge the brush on the go. I took it on a weekend trip, and my friends were so impressed they thought I was secretly a millionaire. Joke’s on them—I just have impeccable taste in toothbrushes. Value for Money: Yes, it’s pricey. Yes, I had to convince myself I deserved it. But after using it, I can confidently say it’s worth every penny. My dentist even complimented my teeth at my last checkup, and that alone is priceless. Plus, if you divide the cost by the number of times you’ll use it (twice a day, every day), it’s basically a bargain. Math!

reviews.title: I was skeptical, but I really like it!
reviews.body: I was skeptical about these, but with a good deal for Prime Days, I decided to give it a try. I'm glad I did, because my teeth generally feel cleaner and look whiter than they ever have in my life. My wife agrees about whiteness! It's incredibly easy to use and setup, and I only have a couple minor nitpicks that hold it back from 5 stars... 1. The app is a pain, because it crashes a lot. This means having to relaunch it and allowing it to sync a couple extra times to keep my record updated. Not the end of the world but slightly annoying. 2. The accelerometer and gyroscope in it that allow it to detect the angle being held needs to be less rigid... Instead of 45 degrees a range of 30-60 degrees would be better. I wouldn't have to twist it and my head as much to keep it in optimal alignment. I feel like this is probably something that could be solved with a software update. I've submitted feedback on this at least, so here's hoping. Anyway, overall, I really enjoy using it and I have a cleaner mouth to show for it.

reviews.title: Each of these lasts about three to four months! Planned obsolescence.
reviews.body: I thought I'd come by and warn folks about these electric toothbrushes. See, Sonicare is a very famous brand of dental hygiene products, and the technology used here is proven to be very effective. Rapid gentle motion of a set of soft fibers-- you know. We all get it. So I've been using Philips Sonicare for many years, and I'm certain that my oral health has benefitted from that. The trouble is, Philips can't build one of these that lasts more than half a year. I keep having to replace the units because the power switch fails. One after another. The last purchase was 10 April. That's right-- just over three months ago. The rubbery membrane covering the power switch has cracked open and water has leaked into the switch, and the switch has failed. It either won't come on, or if it does finally come on, I can't then turn it off. Can you imagine? In the year 2024? Philips can't design and manufacture a power switch on a toothbrush that lasts more than a few months? Well, of course I know the answer. It's supposed to fail, and I know it. It's planned obsolescence, and I know it. I wanted to let you all know. These are very worthwhile products from the perspective of one's oral health. But the company is ripping you off intentionally. I'm at this moment going to another brand and I will not buy a Philips product of any kind again. It's a matter of principle to me. I won't. I refuse to bow down to these greedy and wasteful and arrogant corporations who try to manipulate me into more sales by intentionally manufacturing failure into their products. They are intentionally trying to arrange for us to develop habitual purchasing of their products, in repetitive cycles, again and again, and they're attempting to teach us to accept miserable quality as inevitable and only customary. I realize that this has become par for the course, and to many people it doesn't matter-- they're not bothered by constantly buying a new item, over and over and over again. I really don't care. I'm a discriminating and conscientious and logical person, and I refuse to participate in this kind of idiocy.

reviews.title: Easy to use, but noticeably weak power
reviews.body: I tried the Oral-B Pro 100 3D White toothbrush, and while it’s simple and easy to use, the overall performance is pretty underwhelming. It runs on regular AA batteries, which makes it convenient, but you can definitely feel the difference compared to rechargeable models. The round brush head is nice and does a decent job cleaning tooth by tooth, and it’s compatible with other Oral-B heads, which is a plus. It also has a built-in timer to help with brushing time, so the basics are there. That said, the power is where it falls short. It feels weak, especially if you’re used to stronger electric toothbrushes. It gets the job done at a basic level, but it doesn’t give that deep clean feeling you might expect. Even reviews describe it as more of a “basic” option rather than a high-performance one. Overall, it’s fine as an entry-level or travel toothbrush, but if you’re looking for something with real power and a stronger clean, this probably won’t be enough.

reviews.title: Fresh from the dentist clean, tiny design flaws.
reviews.body: The positive reviews concerning the distinctive clean feel even after the first use are all true. As a matter of fact, almost all positive reviews on this item are somewhat accurate. I would like to focus on the details that I searched for and couldn’t find on reviews both written or in video format. They may seem like “cons” but I must add that for me they were not deal breakers. Instead I’d like to think of them as constructive criticism, since they are details that I would like to see on later generations of this item. Cable management: It is difficult to tell the power source and cable situation from all the photos and videos online, which are edited for aesthetic purposes. I kind of knew what the set up would be from previous experiences with other electronic devices so I knew what to expect. However, for those who are expecting the same sleek, cable-free look from the photos online please take note that if your bathroom has power outlets above the sink area, like most homes in america, there will be a cable bunch up on your countertop. Even if the cable is wound up and tied together, it may still be an atrocious sight for that OCD gem in your home, who probably spends a lot of time at the sink. Power Adaptor: Once plugged in, the power adaptor sticks out over three and a quarter inches from the power outlet, yet another design flaw. With the amount of compact usb adaptors available this shouldn’t be difficult to correct since the company would only need to replace one part. Power adaptor plug: The placement of the power socket on the base station is a bit awkward and creates a distance of about two and a half inches from the wall or backsplash. I have similar electronics with the power socket located below the item, which makes for a neater appearance and freedom to push the item flush to the wall when necessary. Other small details that the shopper should be aware of is the size of the item and color of the brush handle. Please take a closer look and notice that the brush handle is two toned. I think it looks good but, anyone expecting it to be solid white will be thoroughly disappointed. Also, please double check the dimensions of this item and know that it is not a compact design. Definitely not for a countertop where space is at a premium. With all that being said…or typed; I would like to reiterate that all these may seem like “cons” but they really are small details that everyone should know to ensure that they are completely happy with their purchase upon receipt. So, In conclusion this item would be perfect if it was a bit more compact, and the cable/power adaptor issue was resolved. With the portable power core technology available now a days I don’t see why we shouldn’t expect a wireless base station that could hold a charge for a few days in the near future. If you made it this far, thanks for taking the time to read and I hope this helped out even just a lil bit. Bitty boppity, give me the zoppity!

reviews.title: Cumbersome
reviews.body: I like the way this brush cleans my teeth and I give it 5 stars for that. But, I am having the most difficult time trying to figure out how to hold it properly. I compared it to my old electric toothbrush and it is smaller in diameter. It is also all plastic handle with nothing to really grab onto. It becomes wet and then the trouble starts. It slips and slides. I don’t like the way it is configured. This has nothing to do with the brush itself, but the packaging is the worst packaging I have ever encountered. I absolutely could not get it opened. Trying to open it I tore a piece of skin off the top of my finger. I then got a knife out and cut it open. No instructions in the box. There is a QR code on the inside of the box that you are supposed to be able to slide your phone in and scan the box. That was difficult to do so I again, cut the box into pieces so I could scan. Unbelievable for the amount of money the brush costs the least they could do is give you individual directions. Yes, I like the way it cleans my teeth and I’ll keep the brush, but not happy with anything else.

3 CLEANING MODES: Brush, floss, or both with the touch of a button, for easy and complete oral care with one convenient device. It’s clinically proven up to 2X as effective as traditional brushing and flossing for reducing plaque and improving gum health.

DENTIST RECOMMENDED: Waterpik is the #1 water flosser brand recommended by dental professionals and the first water flosser brand to earn the American Dental Association (ADA) Seal of Acceptance for safety and effectiveness.

reviews.title: Mostly Love
reviews.body: I had an old waterpik which had seen better days. I had a sonic toothbrush which made my teeth feel wonderful but gave me repetitive stress issues. I finally decided to spend the money on this combo unit and it really is better than the the sum of its parts. It finds all the little hidden bits of leaves and such that distress one's teeth while efficiently cleaning that all important gumline. That is, it does exactly what it's supposed to do. And there's no spitting! Bonus! So, only *mostly* love, because it's just a little too smart for its own good. The brush pulses to make four time divisions then turns off. The only way to have enough water to make it to the end is to have it overflow while filling. Filled up to what looks like the same point is not sufficient. I'm big on saving water, but just a tad more generosity in the tank would actually save water. The old hunch is necessary while doing the combination, or else water will run down one's forearm. I'm not sure if there could be any design solution to that, but it's the brushing part that takes that long. Those who can't hunch can use the brushing part and waterpik part separately. It was hard at first to set the toothbrush in the receptacle, but I learned that holding the hose coil in place, against the unit, it's much easier to seat the brush. The only really bad thing about this is the price--and I paid up not to have black. :)

reviews.title: Takes a bit to figure out and adjust to...
reviews.body: One thing to know is that although its advertised that you can brush and floss at the same time, the actual application of this concept leaves something to be desired. When you activate the floss and bruch together feature, the flossing rinses all the toothpaste from you mouth before it can be used. So, I brush, then floss. The deep clean is amazing and this has enough power. The brush is set for two minutes and the it will stop automatically. FLAW: if you pause it briefly while brushing, the two minutes restarts. Unlike my phillips sonic care, which you could pause and restart without resetting the two minute time limit. This comes with two heads, one normal size and one for travel, i found they work equally well until one literally broke off in my mouth. I ordered more from Amazon and they have lasted well, so maybe a fluke. Bottom line: This thing does what it does well, but one must be patient and brush first, then floor. Also, don't forget to fill the water reservoir with warm water prior to using flosser. The flosser is super powerful and will clean the heck out of your teeth. Which, as I think about it, is the entire purpose of this thing: clean teeth. This doesn't disappoint.

reviews.title: Great Customer Service & Tips on Reconnecting the Flosser
reviews.body: TLDR: If somehow the flosser doesn't respond to the toothbrush's signals and the radio and toothbrush resets don’t work, drain the toothbrush's battery completely by setting it idle for a week or so and reconnect the set to power. Make sure you place the toothbrush in the base before reconnecting the set to power. Waterpik offers great customer service and the device works great and does what it's supposed to do most of the time. ----------------------------------------- I bought one 2.5 years ago, and after less than 2 months of using it, the flosser stopped responding to the toothbrush's command. I don't know how it happened but I knew it was a housekeeper who unplugged the device as he had to clean the counter. After a few days of testing the flossing function and trying the troubleshooting techniques without success, I gave up and contacted Waterpik's customer service. They asked for anything, you know, that would allow them to honor the warranty. The process was a bit annoying (just a bit, and is absolutely nothing compared to arguing with insurance about coverage) but Waterpik in the end sent me another set for free which I'm still using today. Being the environmentally conscious and lazy person I am, I kept the first set because it'd be a chore to dispose of it properly, so I just put it into the original packaging and stored it in the vanity cabinet. Last year, I had to move to another state and while I was packing stuff up, I saw the set and decided to give it another try before completely throwing it away. And it xxxxing worked!!!!!! Now that I commute in between cities, I've placed one at the residence close to my workplace!!! Also I've been periodontitis free for the past 2 years! Thanks Waterpik!!

They asked for anything, you know, that would allow them to honor the warranty. Being the environmentally conscious and lazy person I am, I kept the first set because it'd be a chore to dispose of it properly, so I just put it into the original packaging and stored it in the vanity cabinet. Last year, I had to move to another state and while I was packing stuff up, I saw the set and decided to give it another try before completely throwing it away. And it xxxxing worked!!!!!! Now that I commute in between cities, I've placed one at the residence close to my workplace!!! Also I've been periodontitis free for the past 2 years! Thanks Waterpik!!

reviews.title: It was just meh, and then the flosser feature broke
reviews.body: Unfortunately, I don't recommend this product for the following reasons: 1) The button to turn on/off the water flosser is directly below the button to turn on/off the toothbrush. I can't count the number of times that I've inadvertently pressed the flosser button and water sprays everywhere. It's easy to press this button because of its location on the toothbrush, and also because the handle for the toothbrush is small in diameter and slippery when wet...and of course it's going to get wet...so it's tough to avoid pressing buttons while trying to hold onto it. I can disconnect the water flosser to avoid this problem, but that defeats the purpose imho and is a hassle. 2) I seem to spend an inordinate amount of time keeping this unit clean. The toothbrush and base have lots of crevices. 3) At this price, I expected a better product, especially from Waterpik. It’s just meh. Not great, not terrible. I can work around the above annoyances, but wish I hadn’t spent so much money on it. I gave it 3 stars because the water flosser does a good job, and the reservoir holds a sufficient amount of water compared to the "all-in-one" models, where the water reservoir is in the handle. If you have a dental implant, you need a water flosser. Once this toothbrush/flosser needs replacing, I'll look for a different design. Hopefully Waterpik will come up with something better. UPDATE: Not long after giving this product 3 stars and a "Meh" review, the flosser stopped working. Actually, it won't STOP working, and wants to run continuously when the unit is plugged in. Now all I have is an expensive electric toothbrush. It gets one star.

reviews.title: Mismatched items cost time and money!
reviews.body: I had one of these and loved it. I even rave about the product to my friends and bought one for Christmas as a gift for one of my best friends. It ended up being a mistake with plenty of consequences. The unit didn’t work, and after several attempts of investigating it once she turned it over to me, I found that the base unit and the toothbrush don’t match IDs, so the highly touted wireless connection didn’t work and would never work since they are tied to the unit’s ID. This careless mistake on the manufacturer’s side meant I was forced to take back the present and return it. I had to then personally repack it and bring it to the post office and pay $66.60 to ship it back. Amazon is only going to reimburse me for half of that, and only weeks from now. Terrible service on both Amazon’s part (I’ve always been able to get returns picked up but they don’t offer it anymore) as well as Waterpik for screwing up in the first place!

reviews.title: Why have a bright light at night???
reviews.body: The round brush action is great, and the item looks and feels fine (clean lines, elegant). But the bright green pressure light is the worst thing for night brushing because bright light interferes with sleep signals (melatonin), and the light is close to your eyes! I try to cover it up w my hand and a Kleenex, but would much prefer no light. Also re the app, i don’t want to check my phone at night to brush my teeth either. This model does not require that, but I mention because it’s another bell and whistle that makes people look at their phones at night. Think about it: It’s late, people want to get it done - brush, floss and do the mineral mouthwash. I also try to do the WaterPik at night, but all these oral hygiene steps do take time. Oral-B - please make a simple electric toothbrush with no lights or app syncing, and please offer value multi-packs of the Gentle Care and Specialised Tip replacement brushes. These particular brush heads are very good (softer bristles are as important as pressure). Users should replace the brushes regularly but they are not cheap. So make profit from the brush heads (like printers and toner) by encouraging frequent changing of brush heads. Volume packs (not just 2 heads per Pack) would be good because less shipping and packaging waste would be better for the environment.

It's simple and does a good job of removing plaque, and is easy to maneuver in the mouth. I just wish it came with softer brush heads.

reviews.title: Morning One: I'm in Love
reviews.body: 12/15/23 Original Product Review (in case I return for updates). THE BASICS 12/13/23 Found the Bitvae R2 Rotating Electric Toothbrush in Pink on Amazon and Placed Order. 12/14/23 Received the product late this evening, securely packaged and undamaged. The pink hue is true to its image color, and I like it despite not being a "pink person." TLDR This morning, I brushed my teeth for the first time in two years without over- or under-brushing, sensitivity and pain-free, and without feeling like my teeth were shifting. THE FULL STORY Let me explain: In 2021, I got into a major cycling accident that changed a lot of my daily routine I took for granted more difficult. After going over my handlebars, I primarily landed on my mandible with my maxilla taking a hard blow, too. My chin bounced twice on the ground (only for my lower jaw to pop back) before my face (and the rest of me) slid on the concrete to a stop. My top row of teeth, well, the only way I know how to put it is that they immediately felt like they had slumped forward in my face (and they had). After a bit of dampened sound and ear-ringing, bright lights and loud, bothersome noises, not to mention the blood pouring from my nose, face, mouth, and wounds, I was treated (probably insufficiently) at the ER and headed to a local dentist. From the general feeling of skidding my lower teeth and lip on the pavement and having my head jolted enough that each front top tooth looked like someone had crushed ice in a blender and left it sitting in its container, I knew things were going to be bad. THE CONSEQUENCES Not only had the long and painful, but effective process of moving my jaw forward by an orthodontist been completely undermined, but all six top front teeth were, indeed, crushed. The palatine process of my maxilla (soft palate) had a thin, but long crack running back through it, and the other more superficial parts of my maxilla that surrounded my sinuses -- tiny fractures ran throughout. WHY OTHER TOOTHBRUSHES WEREN'T WORKING Since then, tons of anesthesia, twelve surgeries, lots of drilling, filing, and testing, irritating crown fitting, teeth shifting, nerve pain and cold sensitivity...things haven't been the same. Try as I might, what used to be a simple, quick everyday task had become frustrating. I've always believed I shouldn't let the little things get to me. But often, it's exactly the little things that get to you, because they're not just little things. They're habitual. They're routine. Across the span of your life, they're actually really big things. How you approach your health -- including your teeth -- is one of those things. I've tried extra soft and soft manual toothbrushes, different brands, returned to my original Colgate; I tried using the Burst toothbrush and a similar "sonic" variety that my husband uses; different toothpastes; mouthwashes; flossing methods and flossers; coconut oil pulling; everything I knew to do before and that could be done or that recently came out...whatever friends and family recommended. In two years, I've not once felt like my teeth were fully cleaned or, if picked, prodded, and scrubbed well, fully stable. THE BITVAE Nothing has worked like this toothbrush. Today, my teeth feel clean, but my gums aren't sensitive, swollen, or bleeding from my being excessive thoroughness and over-brushing. And I've only tried the "Clean" setting. The timer feature in the Bitvae was a smidge startling because, eager to try it, I overlooked the manual details and was unaware that there was one lol. Let's just say it's obvious. But, if you know to expect it, it's brief and distinct -- a slightly different buzz that cues you to move on and kinda' propels you to, which (having OCD tendencies) I appreciate. And while I wouldn't say the Bitvae is quiet, it's certainly no louder than any of the other battery-operated competitors I've tried. (Because of the accident's damage to my ears, it honestly sounded a little like a quiet light saber at times. Weird, nerdy Star Wars reference, I know, but I'm just calling it like I...heard it.) As un-irritated as my gums feel, they also feel well-massaged. The tissue looks and feels clean and bright, without feeling or showing any signs of inflammation or agitation. From the front of my crowns to the crevices behind my molars and all in between, my enamel is evenly brushed and fresh. The Bitvae's brush head was small enough to clean all around without knocking about or hitting other teeth. Meanwhile its grip, heavy in my hand, was sturdy to hold, but not burdensome in any way. It was very easy to maneuver. My breath smells and tastes better (un-tinged by the last of accidentally brushing something too hard and more so than if I tried "brushing gently"), if that makes sense. And the Bitvae, having come charged, remains charged, worked smoothly -- better than I anticipated. I rarely (IF EVER) give products a five-star rating. I'm a meticulous person who, in herself and the products she purchases, almost always finds room for improvement. But, I'm truly satisfied with this purchase, which cost me less than half of what a similar Oral B would (when the Oral B is on sale for 50%+ off) have. CONCLUSION Buy it. I don't like throwing away money, and I know all of this sounds dramatic, but an accident like the one I had is nothing short of that. Meanwhile, the Bitvae comes with a year's warranty, which is reassuring as a customer and as someone whose dental health has been affected for life. The return of a well-cared-for mouth with the ease I once had of "just brushing my teeth" pre-accident is amazing. To have brushing my teeth -- which had become a process in itself to grapple with every morning -- return to a brief, but effective routine is such a relief. I'm grateful for the bit of time I'll get back every day. I hope you'll take the opportunity to enjoy it, too!

reviews.title: Very nice electrical toothbrush
reviews.body: Came nicely packaged with a sleek travel case and several spare brush heads. It feels a bit bulky in the hand, but it works great. One thing I noticed is that it doesn't have the pressure sensor light like my old Oral-B (which my better half ended up claiming 😅), but to be honest, I don’t really miss it. It has multiple modes: White (which I tried but felt was a bit too intense for my teeth), Clean (my go-to), Sensitive, Gum Care, and Tongue. So there's a good range to choose from depending on your needs. The charger is compact and gets the job done quickly, though I do wish it had a USB-C port. Battery life is solid—I use it once or twice a day and only need to charge it about twice a month. Overall, I’m really happy with it. It performs almost as well as the high-end brushes from bigger brands, but at a much more reasonable price.

reviews.title: Cleans my teeth well and at a fraction of the price of other brands
reviews.body: A great product at a great price and 2 years on it still works like new and cleans my teeth very well each time! I love that it has different settings and that unlike their other model (the one without the spinning circular head), it has a separate power and vibration setting button. I'm so glad that the company made that change because it was so annoying trying to turn off the brush only to accidentally switch settings and have to spend 3 minutes each time trying to reset it. It also comes with a warranty and you can register the product with the company to get discounts and product care from this one purchase, which I found really nice and made me trust them more. The battery lasts about 1.5-2 months before I have to charge it again (I brush 2x daily) so that's also a big plus for me. All in all highly recommend this brush because you really can't beat it for the price and value.

reviews.title: Cleans Teeth Well with Extra Soft Bristles
reviews.body: I have their water flosser and needed a spinning toothbrush to target the brown stains around the teeth near my gum line. I've used manual extra soft tooth brushes and the vibrating tooth brush as well. The extra soft bristles are easy on my teeth and gums especially having gum recession in certain areas. I use the softest spin which still does a great job and can easily reach the rear. 1 downside is that the battery only lasts ~1 week as I'm very thorough with my brushing due to my dental needs brushing ~6 minutes average each time twice daily so you do need to charge it weekly but the benefits outweigh the need for weekly charging. The 8 brush heads are great which means I don't have to buy more brush heads for another 2 years. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Update - R2-Works great at a great price! R1 had a few issues, but were resolved.
reviews.body: I have used this for a few days now and I really like it! It has different settings for different amounts of pressure depending on your sensitivity. I like the timer function and that it lets you know every 30 seconds so that you can change the positioning of the brush. It also came with extra heads that should last me a couple of years. For the price, this is a great toothbrush! I can't comment on battery life yet, as I have not used it for that long. I am considering buying a second one to keep in my travel pack. Update Sep 25, 2024 I still love the R2! It works great and holds a charge well. I recently purchased an R1 just to use as a travel toothbrush. It worked well at first, but after about 6 weeks it would just die during a brushing, even though I had just charged it. The odd thing was, plugging it into the charger for 3-4 seconds would "reset" it and then it worked again. This kept happening though. By then it was past the 30-day return window. I contacted their support and they were VERY helpful! After some troubleshooting that didn't help, they promptly sent me a new one! Time will tell if this one will do the same thing. However, I am very happy with their support! That being said, if I were to buy a new one at some point, I would go with the R2 just because I like its features a little bit better.

reviews.title: So good while it lasted...
reviews.body: I really liked this toothbrush until my second one died after six months... I got my first one in 2023 and it lasted 2.5 yrs B4 it died (turned off during use and no amount of charging could revive it). With the toothbrush being affordable and lasting so long, I got another one in 2025. I've been using the new one just over six months and it has now died as well and won't charge anymore... I'm switching to a new brand because while I may get another one that lasts me years, I don't want to risk getting another one that only lasts 6 months. It did a fantastic job and held a charge well etc for the time that it worked though. 😌 I liked it so much that I also got my husband one in 2024 when he needed a new one. He's been using his for a little over two years now, so I'm interested to see how long his lasts B4 it dies. If you get it, enjoy it while it lasts! May be for years or it may be months, but as long as it works your teeth will be squeaky clean!

reviews.title: Only functional for 2 months!!!
reviews.body: I bought this to replace a Philipps that I had been using for about three years. I didn’t have the money to spend on another Philipps so, I tried this one, after reading all the great reviews. At first, the toothbrush was absolutely amazing, not quite as strong as my old Phillips, but a solid replacement and an excellent price point.. I guess I should have just paid the extra money because now I have to buy a new toothbrush anyway! It started turning off by itself randomly while I was using it, every time after a full charge-up over night! It kept doing this and made the daily task of brushing my teeth, after suffering two strokes this year, even more of a difficult task. I charged it and it turned green, I removed it from the charger and now it won’t even turn on at all! I tried plugging it in again. Nothing. No charge no power nothing. I have only had it for two months! Now I have nothing to use to brush my teeth, as the back and forth manual motion isn’t possible for me right now, due to medical reasons, and I can not afford to purchase another one. It was so affordable, and I was so excited, and it was working so well, and made me teeth so clean, and everything about it was so awesome, until, after 2 months it died… too good to be true. It just makes me very sad.

reviews.title: It should come with a warning label!
reviews.body: ☆Seller kindly gave a retund, but didnt need to! I was so moved that she simply wanted to make things right, that i gladly would have changed my reflection from that message alone! I love a seller that just wants to make their customers happy, and thats what this seller is all about ♡. But this review made her chuckle so I'll keep it up lol. ☆ I don't even know where to begin when it comes to what needs to be said about this mid-sized Sedan- I mean toothbrush. Even on the lowest setting, this thing has enough horsepower to cut clean through your tongue like a scalpel sharpened by Dexter himself. I'm exaggerating but not by much. It does come with a lot of replacement brush heads which is great for the price, so after I gained enough feeling back in my mouth, I popped on a replacment head and asked my parents (with a garbled half-numbed mouth) to try to survive a full tooth cleaning to see if I was just sensitive to vibrations. Neither of them lasted longer than 15 seconds. They both couldn't stop laughing because they found themselves yelling their responses because they still heard and felt the vibrations long after they turned off the device. Listen, if you dont turn on the device, its amazing lol. Its built with good materials, has a lot of replacement heads and the included stand and travel container was so cute! I wanted to love this toothbrush but it is not usable. Im wondering if I got a defective item because there is no way everyone giving positive reviews was using this in their mouths. Maybe to power wash their driveway, remove graffiti from brick, or to lift a few shades from some old dentures, but NOT for teeth cleaning. And im just gonna say what we are all thinking- WHO THE HECK IS SIMEN M. AND WHY SHOULD WE CARE THAT HE RECOMMENDS THIS PRODUCT? (see image) The generic actors in white lab coats cracked me up. I could almost see the Getty images watermark. This product is so insane that I didnt even return it. I keep it in my cabinet as a threat to any of my nieces/nephews who use bad language in this house. We dont need to wash their mouth out with soap when all I have to say is "go brush your teeth" to instill the fear of God in anyone. 😆

reviews.title: Good as new! NOT!
reviews.body: I am very pleased with the condition and function of this lap top. The battery is nearly full strength and there is no visible damage or indication of wear. They put a skin on the outside, I assume to cover any marks or scratches, but this computer is in such good shape, I doubt there could have been much. My only complaint is some bloat wear added for "PC app store" that commandeers the computer at first, literally blocking you from doing almost anything else until you open an account, CC and all. I managed to finally get past it to settings where I could go in and delete that app. It is not the same as the Microsoft app store. Other than that, it is almost undistinguishable from a new laptop. UPDATE: I really liked this laptop, the size was perfect and it seemed to be working like new. A couple of months later, it just stopped working. I don't know what happened, one minute it was working fine, the next it was dead. Black screen. Nothing. I had assure, so I sent it in and they couldn't fix it. If I didn't have assure, I would have been out for the whole thing. I m so glad I back up everything on an external drive. I recommend you do that also, no matter what computer you have!

reviews.title: Dell Latitude - I was expecting better
reviews.body: I actually purchased 2 of these laptops, both advertised to be in excellent condition, which they were. I love the touch screen, size and weight of this laptop, but not so enchanted with the battery life, which on full charge only lasts a max of 2 hours or so. Both laptops have the 43Wh battery which I upgraded to 63Wh thinking my battery life would significantly improve, but that did not happen. That's okay though because I am only on about an hour a day anyway. However, why the 1 start rating is that both these laptops continually freeze up, which is terribly frustrating. And when they freeze, the only resolution is to power the off the laptop and re-boot. I don't like unreliable laptops and unfortunately I have found both of mine are exactly that. Sadly, for medical reasons, I did not start to use these laptops until after the return date expired, otherwise, they would have been returned. I have purchased other refurbished laptops from Amazon and they have all been excellent purchases. I guess I was due to run into a couple of lemons.

I love it's foldable feature to make it a tablet that's not too bad to carry, you can even fold the screen at an angle to use the keyboard as a stand for the tablet function and the keys will automatically disable when folded past 90° (after making sure to update to the latest OS version). It's got good display and quality. One of the best laptops I've ever had. I wish more products were this thoughtful in longevity. I'm honestly amazed with this machine for the price especially. Couldn't be happier.

reviews.title: Good Laptop At A Fair Price
reviews.body: For the price, this laptop gets a 5 star rating. Well, more like 4.5 but I couldn't give it that. It's a good sized laptop with a clear screen. It's pretty darn fast and it looks pretty sharp. Speakers are decent but not mind-blowing and for what it's worth, it has a camera, which is, again, passable, not mind-blowing. The keyboard on the one I got is more of a darker grey (it's advertised as ash grey, which I believe is a lighter color) but I actually like the darker keyboard better. Typing on the keyboard is pretty smooth too. It could use one or two more outlets on the sides though. You only get one USB Type-A port, one USB Type-C port and a headphone jack. Fine if you're more of a minimalist, but not ideal for multi-tasking work. Also, a little tip; When powering on, all you need to do is press the power button, NOT press and hold. I didn't realize that at first and thought initially that their was a problem. Just a piece of advice. Overall, it's a good laptop, at a fair price and should work well for the "Average Joe". I just got it, so the only question I have is, how long will it last? Hopefully it lasts me quite a while. But we'll see. I also got one of the recommended carrying cases for it, but that's another review for another time. Overall Rating: 4.5/5 stars.

reviews.title: Great! Love! Saved my business emergency

This came overnight and was plug and play. This low priced Chromebook synced to my bookmarks and passwords through Chrome, and allowed many individual password protected passwords for separate already existing Chrome accounts. Paired with a cheap HP printer, a cheap wireless mouse, an already owned barcode reader, allowed my business back to production within 18 hours. Only two usb ports, but shifted seamlessly to another when connected. Not lightning fast, but for my need, that did not matter. I am beyond impressed.

reviews.title: Great Buy, was what i expected it to be
reviews.body: Keep in mind that this is more of a rant, and I'm half asleep, but this is what I've gone through so far with the product. Originally came from an hp g62 2010 - 2018, was able to make the laptop last. Finally wanted to upgrade and saw this on sale, so I went for it and it was what I wanted in a laptop for what I do: Music, School, Youtube, Slaughtering Demons. The rant and rave of an individual: The screen is very nice, I can confirm it is an In-plane Switching Monitor or (IPS) as I do not have to center the screen or move my body to get a great view of it, unlike a lot of TN panels that I've used back in the day. The disassembly of the device is very very simple, remove the screws from the bottom of the case and the case pops off, might need a thin tool to pry the case off a bit (only con here) and you'll see the ram and the hard drive and the nvme along with the fans which make it easy for upgrades and cleaning. Also the battery is not soldered into the board and easily comes out for replacement after you remove some screws. All screws I noticed were Phillip's head. (I like to watch disassembly videos in case something happened, that way I can tear into it and hopefully fix the issue.) The ram is decent for 12 gigs, a 4 gig stick and an 8 gig stick, but I plan on upgrading the ram soon. Now after uninstalling a few things and setting windows to use less resources, I idle at about 18-19% which isn't bad at all, depends on what you do though. I do believe the manufacturer specifications have tested up to 16 gigs of 2666 on the board, however; there are cases with other omen laptops, where you can plop in 16 gigs in each dimm slot for a total of 32 gigs, wouldn't recommend it because it's not officially supported, but I will go ahead and try it (making sure i'm at the latest bios update from hp), and will provide an additional review/update. (I like to run a lot of things at once.) The processor is very nice, windows shows that i have 4 physical cpus and 8 logical processors, and I idle at 0% after turning the thing on (which mine booted into windows less than 3 seconds with the nvme 128 gig harddrive). I plan on upgrading the nvme from 128 gigs to 1 terabyte, might clone the drive or just grab a fresh install of windows 10 and slap it on a usb drive and fresh install, go from there. From what I read on the specification sheet for the dc0010nr, I think a cap of 512 Gigs nvme was officially tested and supported, but I'm going another 512 and see how the machine fairs. The 1 terabyte hard drive isn't slow at all, but I have nothing on it but a few games and some music, I constantly keep it defragged. The sound on the laptop is definitely an upgrade from my old hp g62 via software and hardware, but i use headphones into the 3.5mm jacks for mic and playback anyways. when it comes to gaming: Doom 2016 gives about 100 to 130fps on 1080p, ultra + open glide settings.... battlefield 1 on 1080p ultra gives about 45+ on mp and 60+ sp, drop it to high and it gives about 60+ but it depends on what map and what all is going on via gameplay. The heat on the laptop isn't bad, the machine will get warm and the fans will kick into high gear almost like a delay, but there is absolutely no throttling and when i'm finished with my gaming, the fans kick off to silent almost immediately. Also with the gpu, this is a verified gtx 1050 ti with 4096MB of vram in it. Final note: I think it's worth what I payed for: 799.99. If my desktop crashes and burns, it's a great replacement for it. It absolutely destroys solitaire and minesweeper along with other office products like excel spread-sheeting and you're in need for a couple of Pareto diagrams or 3 point beta distributions to resolve employee padding with P.M.O affairs making sure the stakeholders are happy. Alas I digress... I unboxed it, i pressed the power button and it immediately shot into windows and was ready to go. :)

reviews.title: Samsung Galaxy Chromebook Go — Affordable, Lightweight, and Built for Basic Computing
reviews.body: The Galaxy Chromebook Go is exactly what it appears to be: an affordable Chromebook designed for web-based work, education, and everyday tasks. It is not a performance machine, but for the right user it delivers a reliable and straightforward experience. The biggest strengths are portability and simplicity. The laptop is lightweight, easy to carry, and boots quickly. ChromeOS remains one of the easiest operating systems to maintain, making this a good choice for students, casual users, or anyone who primarily works in a browser. Battery life is another positive. In normal use, it easily gets through a day of web browsing, email, document editing, and video streaming without constantly searching for a charger. The 14-inch display provides a comfortable amount of screen space for schoolwork and everyday tasks. While the resolution and color quality won't compete with premium laptops, it is perfectly adequate for browsing, Google Docs, YouTube, and video calls. The integration with Android phones is convenient, particularly for users already invested in the Google ecosystem. File transfers, notifications, and cloud synchronization work smoothly. Performance is where expectations need to be realistic. The Intel Celeron processor and 4GB of RAM handle basic tasks well enough, but heavy multitasking can slow things down. Running numerous browser tabs, streaming video, and using multiple applications simultaneously will push the system to its limits. Storage is limited at 64GB, although ChromeOS relies heavily on cloud services, which helps offset the smaller local storage capacity. For users who primarily work online, this is less of a concern than it would be on a traditional Windows laptop. The build quality is respectable for the price point. It feels durable enough for student use, travel, and everyday carrying. The lightweight design makes it easy to toss into a backpack without much thought. Overall, the Galaxy Chromebook Go is a practical budget laptop that performs well within its intended role. If you need a device for web browsing, email, schoolwork, streaming, and cloud-based productivity, it offers good value. Just don't expect the speed, multitasking ability, or storage capacity of a higher-end laptop.

reviews.title: What a Difference !
reviews.body: I bought a HUGE Fire TV. Perfect for watching movies. Everyone who visited, loved it. “You have yourself a little theater here, “ said my father. However, I felt as if the standard sound coming out of the television, itself, wasn’t enough. That it wasn’t providing the FULL theater effect. I decided to search for a compatible soundbar but they were all well over $100. As if Amazon’s Alexa knew me, I saw this particular sound bar that I liked. It didn’t look too bulky and the reviews said that it was quite easy to install. In days, this soundbar dropped right under $100, to $99.99. SOLD! I LOVE this Fire Soundbar! I love that it is so PERFECTLY compatible with my Fire TV. So much so that I only have to use one, whichever one, to turn the volume up or down. When I turn the television off, using its own remote, the soundbar turns off by itself. So, I never have to worry about it remaining on when it is not in use. I LOVE that it has three settings, one for dialogue, another for music, and another for movies. I LOVE that it was so easy to install! Just TWO cables. One for the power and one to connect the television to the soundbar. The shape at the ends of the cable are the same and you can’t get confused because there is only ONE hole with that shape at the back of the soundbar and at the back of the television. If you were good, as a child, at putting the square peg into the square hole and the round one into the round hole, you will certainly get this. I decided to connect the cable so that I would never have to deal with bluetooth connectivity issues/slowness. Connectivity just seems more secure and direct with the cable. The sound? What a world of difference! Now the package is complete! You get the full theater effect! My family loves to watch movies with me! I love bass. But for those of you who don’t, you are able to make easy adjustments. I LOVE to listen to the introductory sounds right before the movie begins. It makes me feel—-due to the sound—-like I am sitting at the theater. I also LOVE that if I am in the living room and the television is off, and I just want to listen to some music. I can connect my phone via the bluetooth feature, to my soundbar, and use it as a speaker! How cool is that? I HIGHLY recommend this little soundbar, especially for those who already have a Fire Television!

reviews.title: A Solid Entry-Level Option!
reviews.body: The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar offers a decent audio upgrade for those looking to improve their TV's built-in sound without breaking the bank. Dolby Audio, along with the convenience of Fire TV integration. However, it's important to have realistic expectations given its price point. What's Good: Easy Setup: Connecting the soundbar is a breeze, especially if you already have a Fire TV device. The setup process is guided and intuitive. Fire TV Integration: This is a major selling point. Seamlessly controlling the soundbar with your Fire TV remote is incredibly convenient. No juggling multiple remotes! Improved Sound over TV Speakers: The soundbar definitely provides a noticeable improvement in clarity and depth compared to most television speakers. Dialogue is clearer, and the overall soundstage is wider. Compact Size: The soundbar's slim profile fits nicely under most TVs without being intrusive. Affordable Price: This is a budget-friendly option for those wanting better sound without a huge investment. Bluetooth Connectivity: The ability to stream music wirelessly from your phone or other Bluetooth devices is a welcome addition. What's Not So Good: Limited Bass: Being a 2.0 system, the bass response is somewhat lacking. While it adds some low-end presence, it won't satisfy those looking for deep, rumbling bass for action movies or music. Consider a subwoofer if bass is a priority. Virtual Surround Sound: While DTS Virtual:X and Dolby Audio are present, the simulated surround sound effect is subtle. Don't expect a truly immersive experience. It provides a slightly wider soundstage, but it's not a replacement for a dedicated surround sound system. Sound Quality Could Be Better: While better than TV speakers, the overall sound quality is adequate, not exceptional. The mid-range can sometimes sound a bit muddy. Limited Connectivity: The soundbar primarily focuses on Fire TV integration. While it has Bluetooth, it lacks other input options like HDMI ARC, which could limit its versatility. Overall: The Amazon Fire TV Soundbar is a good entry-level soundbar for those primarily focused on improving the audio from their Fire TV and who are on a budget. The seamless Fire TV integration and improved dialogue clarity are its strongest points. However, if you're a serious audiophile or crave powerful bass, you'll likely need to spend more for a higher-end system. This soundbar is best suited for casual viewers who want a simple and affordable upgrade to their TV's built-in speakers.

reviews.title: Happy for now but not impressed
reviews.body: So, I have a insignia fire tv so you would think an Amazon fire soundbar would work perfectly? It was particularly hard to set up, but the issue was that tv speakers wouldn't switch off so I would have an echoing, double effect of audio. The setting said they were off, but they were not. In fact, I couldn't even switch them off normally. Even with nothing connected, I switch them off and still get sound pushed through. I kept trying to fix it. What I had to do was: 1) Settings 2) HDMI-CEC control 3) Switch One Touch Play off 4) Turn off Soundbar 5) Set Volume to 0 6) Turn Soundbar back on That seem to let the soundbar function independently, get rid of the echoing, and get everything to work as described. The downside, the volume will only go up and down at 2 intervals despite what I set it to internally. And, there is no easy way to switch between the TV and sound bar for audio without screwing up the good result I got after working all day on it. Also, make sure you plug into your first HDMI port/Arc port. I had my gaming console set up and didn't realize my intital issue of no sound was the fact that I needed to swap the ports. Frankly, being an Amazon soundbar with and Amazon TV that specifically has a set up for it. I would say the functionality kind of sucks because it it should just work, like it says it should, by following the instructions without having to search up and down for way to keep both audios from playing. Like, the setting say the internal speakers were off despite being a lie and that setting effected nothing. It made it more difficult them it needed to get it to work somewhat normally. I would prefer to set it so volume interval is 1 but I guess to make this usable I am stuck at 2 everytime. And, I better hope that nothing changes and messes it up again in a update to the TV. The sound itself is a improvement, and there is a marked difference between regular and surround sound. It sort of like watching TV versus going to a theater. It terms of the way it fills the room and hits your ear. I can't say that the movie, music, dialogue settings seem to different to me. The size is okay. It just tall enough to not block my screen. The length is just about the size of my dresser. Depth is about 3.5 inches so as long as you have another room in front or to push back your TV, you will be fine. Overall, it is nice but I am not sure if I am total happy I bought it considering it was almost $90 for what I would categorize as works okay. I feel like for that price, and the fact I specifically bought Amazon for the fact I thought it would better with fire tv, that I am not blown away. Happy for now, but not impressed.

reviews.title: Look elsewhere
reviews.body: I would not recommend this soundbar. I give it 2 stars because it does improve the sound of the tv speakers, it is relatively easy to set up with a Fire tv, and the control of the soundbar works seamlessly with the Fire tv remote; but there are so many glitches that make it undesirable. First of all, the sound quality is improved over the tinny tv speakers but nothing to blow you away. I have it in a small bedroom, and the sound quality is merely acceptable. Secondly, the volume control only increases or decreases by 2's. (For example: 20,22,24, etc). This isn't a deal breaker, but it's annoying to not have control over it. Lastly, and most bothersome, whenever there is a power blip, I have to perform what is called an HDMI handshake. I have to unplug the HDMI cable from both the tv and the speaker, turn everything off, wait 30 seconds, and then reconnect and turn the volume extremely high before it kicks back in. I sometimes need to perform this several times before I get any sound from the bar. I have owned numerous other soundbars through the years and have never been this disappointed with the quality and performance.

reviews.title: Excellent “Used - Like New” Condition!
reviews.body: We have two Amazon Alexas in our house, and somehow they’ve both ended up living in my 5-year-old’s room! 😂 He is absolutely obsessed with them. As an only child, he loves to role-play with Alexa, and it’s been wonderful for encouraging his imagination, expanding his vocabulary, reinforcing good manners, and giving him someone besides Mom to talk to throughout the day. Every parent knows the constant “Hey Mom!” moments, so hearing “Hey Alexa!” every now and then gives me a chance to get a few things done around the house. I was able to snag this Echo in Used – Like New condition for more than half off the regular price, and I jumped on it as soon as I saw it. I’m so glad I did! I also purchased the wireless battery base, and now my son carries Alexa around the house like a little friend, making sure it’s included in all of his adventures! Even after buying the battery base, I still spent about what I would have paid for a brand-new Echo Dot, so I feel like I got an incredible deal. The condition truly lived up to the “Like New” description. It arrived in excellent shape with no signs of wear at all. While it didn’t come in the original retail box, it was packaged securely in an Amazon box and worked perfectly right out of the package. My only minor complaint, and this is just me being picky, is that the power cord is white even though I ordered the black Echo. Since we’re using the wireless battery base, it doesn’t affect us right now, but it might bother me a little if I ever decide to plug it directly into the wall. Even so, for the price I paid, it’s a very small issue. I’m a frequent shopper of Amazon’s Used – Like New products because I’ve consistently had great experiences, and this purchase was no exception. If you’re considering buying one in Like New condition, I definitely recommend it!
