reviews.title: Multi-Music Player mystery solved, how to select more than one echo if you cannot
reviews.body: Alexa Echo Speakers Multi-room Music issues I found a solution to not being able to get more than one speaker to work at a time, paired, or set up a “Multi-Room Music” in the Alexa app. This solution also fixed my inability to get Apple enabled devices connected into HomeKit, or even Google Nest Hubs to set up, period. Quick answer: Deselect “Enable Wireless Isolation” when activating your 2.4 Wi-Fi broadcast on your router. I also took all speakers off guest wifi. But I’ll try to put them back to see if that is necessary now. Back story: Months of issues with HomeKit, (only weeks with Echo Multi-Room Music), I gave up trying and decided to try Alexa and Google to replace my Apple smart home efforts. I spent way too much time. After the fix, I’ll live a blended tech life. I’ll give a quick answer, followed by my backstory: Last week I was at my wits end in utter frustration over three major roadblocks. I acquiesced and decided to try Alexa because I couldn’t get almost any of my Apple HomeKit enabled devices into HomeKit, except for new Apple products. I knew it had to be something small I was missing. Alexa was sooooo easy and quick to connect to everything, before I figured out the fix. (I dislike the echo show advertising, their echo speakers are better.) While they seemed a breeze to connect everything, for some reason I couldn’t get more than one echo speaker to work at a time. I was continually blocked from setting up Multi-Room Music or even connect a pair to play together. Hundreds of tries. I deleted, reset, rebooted, spent over 4 hours with Comcast yesterday (thankfully a Boston native who did not put me on hold every minute like certain countries) getting my internet working again. I had rebooted my modem and router so many times, my computer got molasses slow and I feared I went too far In interest I also decided to try a few Google nest hub speakers. Black Friday had great sales on all this stuff. Trying to set up googles hub 7 was impossible. It wouldn’t stay connected to the internet for more than a split second before “Something went wrong” message. Probably over 70 tries. (Google is better than Echo Show. Apple HomePod mini sounds crisper and better than Amazon echo 4 and mini 5’s. But Alexa is way friendlier to interact with verbally, and price point, well...) Frustration. Thursday, I broke down and bought my first Apple Homepod Mini to see if I can get that working and see if it works better than the Apple TV 4k Ethernet connection. The HomePod mini gave me a hint how to solve all these l connection and internet blocks. The HomePod mini kept telling me that I don’t have “peer-to-peer connection” allowed on my network. Now, I’m a little techy, but it took three days (ehem, months) to finally take a chance on a for granted setting I always enable on my netgear router. It’s the blasted first Wireless page when enabling a wifi broadcast. I had to deselect “Enable Wireless Isolation.” That was it. It solved every issue I have come across with smart home tech for the last 4 months, ..year. For the months that I could not solve these problems, Amazons Multi-Player Music issue made me dig deeper. I did not find anyone suggesting this particular router setting, so I thought I’d share with ppl. Tonight, I finally am able to simultaneously play music on all of my Echo speakers, connect my HomeKit enabled and Google nest hubs. I’m not sure what this will do for my/your internet security. But I’m going with it for now. And I’ll try to put all devices back onto guest Wi-Fi. I’ll never really leave Apple, but after interacting with other smart speakers, it’s probably not going to be my main go to for speaker or answers to questions. Or I’ll just get too creeped out by Google and Amazon invasiveness and acquiesce with Apple instead. Echo Dot 5 (this is such a sprite, great speaker!) Echo 4 are my favorite for Amazon Echo Echo Studio seems the least smart, most deaf, quiet, combative, difficult to interact with, of the three speakers. Hopefully the Multi-Room music fix will improve my experience with it Echo Show 8 Meh. Far too much and annoying advertising of non-solicited or wanted advertisements. Least user friendly screen to work with. It sits unplugged for the most part. I mostly got this for a friend who visits who wants a YouTube fireplace playing on the tv. SIDE NOTE on other Smart Home Amazon (online, or physical store) products, related to this topic: I have been pleased with Smartbot plugs, switches and app, the Levoit 600s air purifiers and app (app goes by VeSync), and Lutron Caséta Light Switches and Dimmers, and hub. reviews.body_en: Alexa Echo Speakers Multi-room Music issues I found a solution to not being able to get more than one speaker to work at a time, paired, or set up a “Multi-Room Music” in the Alexa app. This solution also fixed my inability to get Apple enabled devices connected into HomeKit, or even Google Nest Hubs to set up, period. Quick answer: Deselect “Enable Wireless Isolation” when activating your 2.4 Wi-Fi broadcast on your router. I also took all speakers off guest wifi. But I’ll try to put them back to see if that is necessary now. Back story: Months of issues with HomeKit, (only weeks with Echo Multi-Room Music), I gave up trying and decided to try Alexa and Google to replace my Apple smart home efforts. I spent way too much time. After the fix, I’ll live a blended tech life. I’ll give a quick answer, followed by my backstory: Last week I was at my wits end in utter frustration over three major roadblocks. I acquiesced and decided to try Alexa because I couldn’t get almost any of my Apple HomeKit enabled devices into HomeKit, except for new Apple products. I knew it had to be something small I was missing. Alexa was sooooo easy and quick to connect to everything, before I figured out the fix. (I dislike the echo show advertising, their echo speakers are better.) While they seemed a breeze to connect everything, for some reason I couldn’t get more than one echo speaker to work at a time. I was continually blocked from setting up Multi-Room Music or even connect a pair to play together. Hundreds of tries. I deleted, reset, rebooted, spent over 4 hours with Comcast yesterday (thankfully a Boston native who did not put me on hold every minute like certain countries) getting my internet working again. I had rebooted my modem and router so many times, my computer got molasses slow and I feared I went too far In interest I also decided to try a few Google nest hub speakers. Black Friday had great sales on all this stuff. Trying to set up googles hub 7 was impossible. It wouldn’t stay connected to the internet for more than a split second before “Something went wrong” message. Probably over 70 tries. (Google is better than Echo Show. Apple HomePod mini sounds crisper and better than Amazon echo 4 and mini 5’s. But Alexa is way friendlier to interact with verbally, and price point, well...) Frustration. Thursday, I broke down and bought my first Apple Homepod Mini to see if I can get that working and see if it works better than the Apple TV 4k Ethernet connection. The HomePod mini gave me a hint how to solve all these l connection and internet blocks. The HomePod mini kept telling me that I don’t have “peer-to-peer connection” allowed on my network. Now, I’m a little techy, but it took three days (ehem, months) to finally take a chance on a for granted setting I always enable on my netgear router. It’s the blasted first Wireless page when enabling a wifi broadcast. I had to deselect “Enable Wireless Isolation.” That was it. It solved every issue I have come across with smart home tech for the last 4 months, ..year. For the months that I could not solve these problems, Amazons Multi-Player Music issue made me dig deeper. I did not find anyone suggesting this particular router setting, so I thought I’d share with ppl. Tonight, I finally am able to simultaneously play music on all of my Echo speakers, connect my HomeKit enabled and Google nest hubs. I’m not sure what this will do for my/your internet security. But I’m going with it for now. And I’ll try to put all devices back onto guest Wi-Fi. I’ll never really leave Apple, but after interacting with other smart speakers, it’s probably not going to be my main go to for speaker or answers to questions. Or I’ll just get too creeped out by Google and Amazon invasiveness and acquiesce with Apple instead. Echo Dot 5 (this is such a sprite, great speaker!) Echo 4 are my favorite for Amazon Echo Echo Studio seems the least smart, most deaf, quiet, combative, difficult to interact with, of the three speakers. Hopefully the Multi-Room music fix will improve my experience with it Echo Show 8 Meh. Far too much and annoying advertising of non-solicited or wanted advertisements. Least user friendly screen to work with. It sits unplugged for the most part. I mostly got this for a friend who visits who wants a YouTube fireplace playing on the tv. Lutron has the most stable and reliable app out there. I was fine running their apps separately. They are very nice, better than the big 3 apps. reviews.title: Impressive Speaker
reviews.body: I work as a grill cook, which means I’m in a very noisy environment. So I need a speaker that is very loud. And I can say this speaker gets very loud for its size, but is never harsh on the ears, like some other speakers which leave an almost ringing in your ears after a high note. And it does not distort at max volume which is a plus for me. I used to have a 50w Rave Neo from soundcore, until recently when I sold it to a coworker who was in need of a good speaker. I had it for nearly 5 years. When I had it, I was constantly getting compliments on how impressive that speaker sounded. So I decided to buy another speaker from Anker since it’s quality I can trust. Comparing to the 50w Rave Neo, both with bass boost, and boom 2 out of box sound profile. The boom 2 gets louder than the rave Neo, however gets a little “muddier” at high volumes, while the rave Neo keeps a fuller sound. Probably due to the fact the boom 2 is missing a full range driver, and only has tweeters and a racetrack “subwoofer”. However does not matter in my use case. The battery life seems the same, after 3 hours of use at high volumes with bass on, I only used 40% of the battery on the boom 2, while I also used 40% of the rave Neo. Portability goes to the Boom 2. It is only the length of a ruler, height of 3/4 of a ruler, and is fairly slim. so it fits on any standard sized table easily, it also weighs less than half what the rave Neo weighs. The rave Neo felt like a workout carrying it work, while the boom 2 is easily carried by one finger. I also give appearances to the boom 2. The metal grill on the boom 2 feels very rugged and is much superior to the metal grill on the rave Neo. Both plastics feel the same as well, however it does seem the boom 2 is more vulnerable to scuffs and marks as I already have a scuff on the boom 2 with only 3 hours of use, while I have never gotten a scuff on the rave Neo. The LIGHTSHOW. The boom 2 is amazing to watch as it lights up and moves the radiators to the music. Very nice touch since I never really enjoyed the lights on the rave Neo. The rave Neo was also impressive, but the diffusion on the boom 2 looks very premium. Charging. Both charge with an input of usb type c. However, with the rave Neo, you had to use a usb type A charging block, which was super annoying because I have been trying to get away from usb type a, and micro usb. Type c charging blocks and cords are worlds superior. And the boom 2 can charge from any type c charging block. Sound. The boom 2 is loud. It is not audiophile quality. But if you plan on sticking it in the corner of the room or on the outside of a basketball court, you might not feel or hear every instrument or every vocal chord in a singers throat, but I guarantee you will be satisfied with the volume of music you are receiving from this speaker, which does sound very pleasant at least, which is what this speaker is meant to do. Get loud, so you can listen to music while you are doing other activities. I highly recommend higher end soundcore speakers, can’t go wrong.

reviews.title: Big sound from a small box
reviews.body: I’m very happy with the volume and fullness of the sound coming from this little box. I bought this for outside on the patio and around the pool. I had been using a Bose Flex, which was great for indoor near-field listening, but a little weak for outside. This Boom 2 gets plenty loud enough to reach the pool half way across the yard at a comfortable listening level, and it can easily get loud enough to annoy the neighbors. Music is full and clear - the bass won’t rattle the furniture, which I never expected from a box this size, but there’s plenty of it for casual listening and small outdoor gatherings, for which this guy is perfect. Bluetooth connection to my iPhone is flawless; once it’s paired, you just need to turn it on and it automatically connects. The Soundcore app is easy enough to use if you need it, which I usually don’t. I just turn it on and start the music on my phone, and the party is on. USB-C charging is convenient, because almost every gadget I have uses it now, so there are plenty of charging points around the house.

reviews.title: Un son monstrueu pour un petit gabarit !
reviews.body: Les matériaux sont robustes, design très simple et épuré agréables à regarder. Pour la taille le son est vraiment excellent ( véritable stéréo) : des basses bien présentes, mais jamais trop excessives, donnent de la profondeur au son et une belle rondeur. Les médiums sont très agréables, les voix sont très bien reproduites et naturelle. La puissance est importante : certes, nous sommes loin de vrai 80w, mais il y a beaucoup de volume. Peut être utilisé sans problème même à l'extérieur, dans de grands espaces, ainsi qu'à la maison pour écouter de la musique à faible volume, en profitant d'un son agréable et rond. La batterie dure très longtemps, surtout lorsque vous éteignez les lumières, gadget pour faire joli sympa mais pas très utile. Dans l'ensemble : excellent produit, à tel point que je n'ai commandé une deuxième, en jumelant les deux enceintes on atteint une puissance max de 160 w pour une valeur max de 200€ (2 fois 99€) très rentable. Excellent pour regarder un film sur tablette. Enceinte polyvalente qui se prête à tous les usages et à tous les espaces. Bien au-dessus de la marque JBL de même gamme, plus léger, moins cher et meilleur son. Deux petits points négatifs (mais vraiment parce que je suis chiant) il n'y a pas la possibilité de brancher une clé USB, carte micro SD ou prise jack dommage et pas d'encoche pour mettre une sangle. Vous pouvez en faire l'acquisition vous ne serez pas déçu.
reviews.body_en: The materials are robust, very simple and refined design pleasant to look at. For the size, the sound is really excellent (true stereo): very present bass, but never too excessive, giving depth to the sound and a nice roundness. The mids are very pleasant, the voices are very well reproduced and natural. Power is important: certainly, we are far from true 80w, but there is a lot of volume. Can be used without problem even outdoors, in large spaces, as well as at home to listen to music at low volume, enjoying a pleasant and round sound. The battery lasts a very long time, especially when you turn off the lights, a nice gadget but not very useful. Overall: excellent product, so much so that I ordered a second one, by pairing the two speakers we achieve a maximum power of 160 w for a maximum value of 200€ (2 times 99€) very profitable. Excellent for watching a movie on a tablet. Versatile speaker that is suitable for all uses and all spaces. Way above the same range JBL brand, lighter, cheaper and better sound. Two small negative points (but really because I'm annoying) there is no possibility of plugging in a USB key, micro SD card or jack socket, too bad and no notch to put a strap. You can purchase it and you will not be disappointed.

reviews.title: A real powerhouse of a speaker.
reviews.body: I originally got this speaker to play in the shower. I have since moved to playing it in my garage, outside when doing yard work, and in my car when I want to connect to my songs without having to connect to my car audio. It is very loud, the battery last for yours, and it is very easy to carry around. I love this thing. Pros - Sound Quality – is excellent. It is a lot loader than I thought it would be. Can play in your car and it matches the best sound system I have ever heard in a car. Sound is crisp with voice, thumping with bass, treble, tones, and other variables. The lights are neat, but I got if and kept it for the sound output. - Quality – nicely built. Heavy material which adds to the bass. I use it in the shower, so I know condensation is not an issue. Have not taken it in water, you will have to let me know how that goes. - Value for the money – you get a lot of sound for your buck. If all speakers this size plays like this, then you can only get the same, not better. - Connectivity – connected easily to my phone on the first attempt. Now I only have to turn it on and it connects every time. - Portability – Love the cord that comes with it. I am able to hang it in the shower or on a hook in the garage. I also take it outside in the yard and dust and bugs don’t affect it. - Battery life – the battery last a very, very, very, very...did I mention “very” long time? Well it does! I also like that it lets you know when the battery is going low. - Reliability – has been working perfectly since I got it. Never had an issue with it turning on or connecting. - Volume – it is very loud. Cons - None

reviews.title: Was a workhorse, bought another.
reviews.body: I have one I got from someone else. Have been using it for nearly three years. The other day it was turning itself off every few songs even when plugged in like it was powering down and the lights quit working. I looked it up to see if buying a new one was an option. I can’t believe these are only $30. From what I got out of the other one, and how it sounds, I figured it’d be $70-80 for a new one. New purple one came today. Highly recommend at this price point for sure. Always connects right to my phone, always had a long battery life unplugged, great sound for the size, and versatile due to compactness and alleged waterproofing. I dropped it prolly a hundred times, threw it at the wall once or twice. Lasted me three years and wasn’t brand new when I got it. I rarely leave reviews… this one I had to. If you have read this far, I recommend using the eq button on the speaker as well as an eq on whatever app you’re playing music through. No a 30 dollar speaker isn’t going to play standard eq well. You have to cut mids out a few decibels to get clear bass and highs. Simple way to make this speaker sound great instead of good.

Definitely worth the money and apparently worth guarding closely too.

The come with cords to charge and another dual to plug in to a head phone style jack. I used w my Alexa for better sound with no problems. For the size I feel like they exceeded expectations. Says waterproof thats a bonus, but again cant speak on that yet

reviews.title: Sound not as good (lacks bass even on Bass mode) as I'd hope, and some tech issues
reviews.body: Update 3: I am not doing "never ending updates" but just typing this to say that the issue STILL hasn't come back. The one thing I have noticed is that i am getting NO WHERE NEAR the "30 hour playtime" ... even 20 maybe pushing it. I am disappointed in that but overall ... I dont mind the speaker. Something in my reviews I thought of mentioning is that while this speaker doesn't sound as dynamic as others ... a "more even sound ... even if that means it lacks a 'thump' in the bass"... IS NOT always a bad thing ... say my Tribit XSound Surf ... listening to smooth jazz at night at low volumes ... it has "too much" of a thump ... this speaker not having that in my view ... makes this one better in some cases .... same way with my DOSS Soundbox Touch having a similar sound (but better mids/highs i think) Update 2: been a few days and "constant use" since the last update. The issue with no sound has NOT come up again yet ... and while i forgot what i have rated the Oontz Angle 3 Ultra (3.5?) i may have to bump that up to 3.75 (not to get crazy with decimals) when i say this ... but i'd give this a 3.5... yeah with certain genres it seems "flat" and lacking bass i'd like (I like a clean bass at best ... not overly done, so i am no "bass head") but other times my new favorites the Tribit XSound Gos have a "subwoofer like sound" (WHICH IS WHY it is my favorite ... at times) but late at night at low volumes i wish i could turn that extra bass off ... I BRING THAT UP due to the fact that THIS SPEAKER sort of has THAT type of sound. So with say easy listening, instrumental, and some jazz stuff in that exact situation ... i DONT DISLIKE the Tribit ... I just like the "lack of bass" (so to speak) more. I cant remember if i recommended or didn't recommend this in my original review.. to me now i'd say this is "ok" (even if that sound issue comes up where i have to play sound in a different app to get it back again, issue comes up) ... you can do better "bang for buck" but ... this is not terrible either. Update 1: Ok after trying what another reviewer said and trying to reset the speaker (pressing power button and holding for at least 8 seconds) I got things to work again. I also couldn’t get any sound in Kodi with my local media but after opening up another app and playing audio fine in that, (same device), then going back to Kodi sound in there worked again. I cant explain what happened but as I said others are having this issue too, but someone mentioned this and it worked for me. Now I plan on sort of doing part of what I planned to in the original review, I have a few other BT speaker, which include an Oontz Angle 3 Ultra, two Tribit Xsound Surfs, two Tribit Xsound Gos, a DOSS Soundbox Touch and a Braven BRV1BCB BRV-1. Versus the Tribits: - to me while I wish the Xsound Surf had better battery life (ONLY ADVERTISED at 10hr) … I would still say either the Xsound Surf or the XSound GO are the better option. They are my favorites and just overall in the same price range … they are just a better value and MUCH better sound. Versus the DOSS Soundbox Touch: - This is where it is interesting. I have not done an “A-vs-B” comparision head to head but out of all my speakers, this speaker sounds closest to this one. If I remember, the bass on the DOSS seems lower at lower volumes but while not like other speakers I have or a “Sub woofer” type sound. It gets more “present” as the volume goes up. It sounds clear and balanced but not for “bass heads”. I think the DOSS may sound better than this one, however its close … I think this speaker’s tuning in the mids are a little off but like the DOSS I’d say both of these speakers are a more “balanced” sound without a subwoofer like “thump”. Versus the Oontz Angle 3 Ultra: - note: I can only compare this to the Ultra model … I hear that if you go down in Oontz models they don’t sound as good. - This is where I wish I could take the extra bass in the Ultra and put it in the X10. The bass is there in the Ultra but while not muddy in MY VIEW. It CAN “linger” a bit. Where it slightly effects the low mids and mid-mids depending on the track. This I feel is exactly what the X10 here is MISSING, EVEN ON Bass Boost mode in the built in EQ. - Build quality – even if the Ultra is NOT my favorite speaker, I still totally recommend it and like it… the build quality alone (not the only thing) blew me away, for the sub $40 price I paid for it. Versus the Braven: - I admit that I do not use this as much as I should. This was gifted to me by someone who had no use for it and .. .well I love this one. It has a decent thump in the bass but not overdone. From what I remember this sort of reminds me of a Tribit tuning … a Good V-shaped sound but clean and not “forced” or overdone. (sound wise) “Everything is where it should be” Summary: I still cant say I recommend this due to the problems I had BUT if its a “ok this is a dumb fix to a problem that shouldn’t exist in the first place” (almost a James May quote) thing if I have the no sound issue again… Ok … I am ok with keeping this and I am not as “upset” (I don’t want to ham that up) about it. The bottom line is (say the “360 sound” that is just fake marketing … If it was “this looks like a JBL Flip but this is not 360 sound .. it just LOOKS the same” … ok then) … I just cant “trust” this speaker… not until I have more time with it and it behaves fine … I will be GLAD to do a second update to report the good news, if that happens. ---------------------------------------- Original Review I was going to write a more in detail review, comparing this speaker to various others I have but unfortunately things are not looking great. I am not 100% saying I am returning this already, but it looks like it may go in that direction. I will list some Cons but .. .things are not all bad when it was working correctly… Hopefully I can not some things as I go. Cons: - Sound quality – ok this is not all bad … but I knew this would lack bass … I get it but even with a V shaped EQ on top of the speaker (same I have set in the same app for ALL others I have) ..and even in this speaker’s third EQ setting “Bass Boost” there is a lack of bass in most genres, people would typically listen to. HOWEVER one of my use cases is late at night listening to say intrumental, Jazz, or Classical music. The lack of a big “Thump” in the bass (which CAN be overdone in other speakers I have heard) … wasn’t too bad and with those genres at lower volumes … the sound quality wasn’t bad. Really I’d never call it “muddy” but even bass boost (built in EQ) sounded like there was a lack of “average bass”. ALSO THIS IS NOT 360 sound. Sure you hear sounds from all sides but the two speakers are only facing one way (the exact opposite side of where the buttons are) … that is the direction things sound “clearest” … the sound is different on any other side and with the lack of bass … including the “bass” radiators on the side as part of the “360” is laughable in itself. - Voice pompt – this wouldn’t be too bad if it wasn’t SO LOUD … late at night it a bit loud compared to say where the volume is set … “BLUETOOTH MODE” “BLUETOOTH CONNECTED” … again I’d like just a beep or something like a ton but even the voice wouldn’t be that bad IF it was a “few clicks” lower in volume. Unsure (Pro? Con?) - Build quality – I WILL SAY this doesn’t feel super cheap, but others like my Oontz Angle 3 Ultra, or any of my Tribit speakers, just feel better. I also have to say I have never had a JBL Flip or any other speakers with an “all over” grill … and I knew I was getting this so maybe versus other speakers, this “style” makes it feel less solid … I could get a JBL Flip and think “oh … they ‘feel’ the same” build quality wise. ------------------------- My main issue – I was thinking of MAYBE returning this, having my sights on a Tribit speaker I have not experienced yet, but with the other Tribit speakers I DO have, blowing me away overall, I have kept my eye on a sale for that one. Not even a week into owning this speaker, while all devices connect to the speaker, the speaker outputs ZERO audio from any COMFIRMED CONNECTED device in bluetooth mode. I do admit PART (but just half at best) use-case is the microsd card slot and one reason I wanted this speaker. In addition to Rain and Ocean waves (“sound machine style”) I wanted to load a microsd card up with that sort of stuff and say maybe smooth jazz and sort of use it as a “custom” sound machine. Right now the microsd card slot function STILL outputs audio and it doesn’t sound bad … but with no sound no matter what I do (including a speaker reset) working … in under 7 days of having this…. I cant even trust this will last. I do note that many of the negative reviews also mention this exact problem. I can live with the sound quality being “meh” at best for typical genres and this only being a good speaker in specific use-cases but now there is no audio for any bluetooth … that is a deal breaker. I just CANT recommend this speaker. While my Tribit speakers are my favorite, I will say I have an Oontz Angle 3 Ultra and sound wise it has the opposite problem (bass tends to … not make things muddy… but it’s bass “lingers a bit too long” at times) … I still LOVE and recommend that speaker.

reviews.title: Incredible Sound, Long Battery Life & Perfect for Anywhere! 🔊
reviews.body: I’m extremely impressed with this Bluetooth speaker! The sound is loud, clear, and well-balanced, with rich bass that makes music sound amazing indoors and outdoors. Despite its compact size, the audio quality exceeded my expectations. The IPX7 waterproof rating is perfect for using it in the shower, by the pool, at the beach, or while camping without worrying about water. The battery lasts a long time, and Bluetooth 5.3 provides a fast, stable connection with excellent range. I also love the dual pairing feature, which creates an even more immersive listening experience. It’s lightweight, portable, and easy to take anywhere. Overall, this speaker offers outstanding performance and excellent value for the price. Highly recommended!

title: Amazon Echo Dot Max (newest model), Alexa speaker with room-filling sound and nearly 3x bass, Great for living rooms and medium-sized spaces, Designed for Alexa+, Graphite
bullet_points: Meet Echo Dot Max: Experience rich room-filling sound that automatically adapts to your space and fine-tunes playback. Features a built-in smart home hub and Omnisense technology for highly personalized experiences.

Music to your ears: With nearly 3x the bass versus Echo Dot (2022 release), it fits beautifully in any space, delivering your personal sound stage with deep bass and enhanced clarity. Listen to streaming services, such as Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify, and SiriusXM. Encore!

Do more with device pairing: Connect compatible Echo smart speakers and smart displays in different rooms, or pair with a second Echo Dot Max to enjoy even richer sound. Pair your Echo Dot Max with compatible Fire TV devices to create a home theater system that brings scenes to life.

Simple smart home control: Set routines, pair and control lights, locks, and thousands of smart home devices that work with Alexa without needing a separate smart home hub. With Omnisense technology, you can activate routines via temperature or presence detection.
Say goodbye to drop-offs and buffering - With eero Built-in, Echo Dot Max doubles as a mesh wifi extender, adding up to 1,000 sq. ft. of wifi coverage to your existing eero network.
Get things done with Alexa: From weather updates to reminders. Designed to support Alexa+, experience a more natural and conversational Alexa that delivers on tiny tasks to tall orders.

Designed to protect your privacy: Amazon is not in the business of selling your personal information to others. Built with multiple layers of privacy controls, including a microphones enable/disable button.

reviews.title: A major smart-home upgrade, with better sound and one minor design drawback
reviews.body: I bought my first Echo in April 2015, back when it was simply called the “Amazon Echo.” Eleven years later, it’s still running strong. Since then, we’ve accumulated an Echo for nearly every room in our home. My daughter, who was born the same year as that original Echo, had been relegated to using it in her bedroom. We finally decided it was time for an upgrade. I wanted her to have access to Alexa+ so I could teach her how to use AI appropriately, and we also needed another Matter hub, as her room is tucked away in the corner of our apartment, and the smart shades in there weren’t always responding reliably. Since installing the Echo Dot Max, her room (and our entire smart home) has become noticeably smarter. The Matter-compatible shades now maintain a strong connection. We have them programmed to open every morning to help wake her up and close again in the evening for privacy. The built-in temperature sensor has also been surprisingly useful. It allowed me to create a routine that automatically turns on her otherwise “dumb” air conditioner when the room reaches a certain temperature. We’ve also been using Alexa+ for everyday questions, weather, music, and those random things families find themselves noodling over. I can monitor my daughter’s activity and help make sure she’s using it appropriately. Compared with the old Alexa experience, Alexa+ is a huge leap forward. It understands more natural questions, handles follow-ups, remembers some conversational context, and is far less likely to respond with the dreaded, “According to an Alexa Answers contributor…” For casual home use, it can answer many of the same kinds of questions I would normally ask Claude, which I pay for separately for my business. Prime members also receive access to Alexa+, which makes the Dot Max a much more capable device than the older Echo speakers we own. The sound quality is good. I still prefer the speakers in the original full-size Echo, but the Dot Max sounds much better than the various standard Echo Dots and Echo Shows we’ve owned. For a child’s bedroom, it is more than adequate for music, audiobooks, and general Alexa use. Because Wi-Fi can be spotty in that corner of our apartment, I was also interested in the built-in eero extender capability. It only becomes useful if you already have (or later purchase) a compatible eero router, which I don’t currently own. Still, I’ve been considering switching to eero, and it’s nice to know her room is already somewhat future-proofed if I do. I was also happy to see that the Dot Max comes in Amethyst (purple). The color makes it feel unique without resorting to an overtly childlike design. It looks attractive on her desk and, depending on your frame of reference, resembles either the Death Star, Olympic Stadium in Montreal, or Spaceship Earth at EPCOT. I did run into one strange problem while trying to pair an Amazon Mickey Mouse clock. No matter how many times I tried, the Dot Max wouldn’t recognize it as an Amazon gadget. I eventually paired the clock with my original Echo, left it connected for a while, and then tried pairing it with the Dot Max again. Somehow, that worked. I’m not sure whether the clock received a firmware update or whether it was simply dumb luck, but it has remained connected since then. My other complaint is the placement of the indicator light. On several older Echo devices, the light is on top, where it can be seen from almost any angle. Here, it faces forward. Unless Alexa gives an audible response, it can be difficult to tell whether she heard you when you’re standing behind or beside the device. Those are relatively minor inconveniences, though. Overall, we love the Echo Dot Max. It has improved the reliability of our smart-home devices, added useful automation through the temperature sensor, and given my daughter a much better Alexa experience. It has assimilated quite nicely into our growing family of Echo devices. Its great-grandfather, meanwhile, has been reassigned to the bathroom.

Prime members also receive access to Alexa+, which makes the Dot Max a much more capable device than the older Echo speakers we own. The sound quality is good. I still prefer the speakers in the original full-size Echo, but the Dot Max sounds much better than the various standard Echo Dots and Echo Shows we’ve owned. For a child’s bedroom, it is more than adequate for music, audiobooks, and general Alexa use. Because Wi-Fi can be spotty in that corner of our apartment, I was also interested in the built-in eero extender capability. It only becomes useful if you already have (or later purchase) a compatible eero router, which I don’t currently own. Still, I’ve been considering switching to eero, and it’s nice to know her room is already somewhat future-proofed if I do. I was also happy to see that the Dot Max comes in Amethyst (purple). The color makes it feel unique without resorting to an overtly childlike design. It looks attractive on her desk and, depending on your frame of reference, resembles either the Death Star, Olympic Stadium in Montreal, or Spaceship Earth at EPCOT. I did run into one strange problem while trying to pair an Amazon Mickey Mouse clock. No matter how many times I tried, the Dot Max wouldn’t recognize it as an Amazon gadget. I eventually paired the clock with my original Echo, left it connected for a while, and then tried pairing it with the Dot Max again. Somehow, that worked. I’m not sure whether the clock received a firmware update or whether it was simply dumb luck, but it has remained connected since then. My other complaint is the placement of the indicator light. On several older Echo devices, the light is on top, where it can be seen from almost any angle. Here, it faces forward. Unless Alexa gives an audible response, it can be difficult to tell whether she heard you when you’re standing behind or beside the device. Those are relatively minor inconveniences, though. Overall, we love the Echo Dot Max. It has improved the reliability of our smart-home devices, added useful automation through the temperature sensor, and given my daughter a much better Alexa experience. It has assimilated quite nicely into our growing family of Echo devices. Its great-grandfather, meanwhile, has been reassigned to the bathroom.

reviews.title: Thoroughly Impressed
reviews.body: I purchased two Echo Dot Max speakers with stands. One for the upstairs and one for the downstairs. I already installed Amazon Basic Smart LED Light Bulbs in the living room and upstairs bedroom. Having already set up the Alexa App on my phone with WIFI connections, the Echo Dots took less than 3 minutes to set up. The automatically synced with my Alex App, downloaded a firmware update, and were ready to go once I grouped them according to their location in my home; one for the living room and one for the main bedroom. I didn't have to input WIFI names and passwords, the whole set up process was extremely easy and seamless. The Echo Dots once assigned to their group location and their microphones enabled, easily controlled my lights in the upstairs bedroom and downstairs living room just by giving the Echo Dots a command: "Alexa, turn on the lights in the bedroom" or "Alexa turn on the lights in the living room". Any command I would give to the App on my phone the Echo Dots commensurately responded to. I then linked my Pandora account to the Echo Dots which was super easy to do on the App and now the little Echo Dots can play any station or music I chose on Pandora. Have to say I am thoroughly impressed with the technology. Yes they are a bit pricey but well worth it because of all the features they have and they sound fantastic too. They look great on my bed stand and living room end table. I don't know how I got along without them. I will probably buy a third Echo Dot for my other upstairs guest bedroom. No wonder Amazon is as big as they are. It's an incredible company providing goods and services that everyone can thoroughly enjoy. UPDATE: I purchased the third Echo Dot Max for my guest bedroom. One note: I had difficulty connecting the WIFI due to the remoteness of the guest bedroom. The problem I had when setting up in the upstairs bedroom, was that the Alexa App prompted me to input the WIFI password which I did but it wouldn't recognize it and asked for me to input it again. I did this four times when I decided to take the Echo Dot Max and the Lamps downstairs into the same room as the WIFI router and the problem went away. The setup proceeded without any issues bypassing the need to input the WIFI Password. I took the lamps and the Echo Dot Max back upstairs and the system works. The Echo Dot easily recognized three smart bulbs turning them on and off with a spoken Alexa command. Also streams Pandora like the other Echo Dots.

reviews.title: Big Sound, Small Footprint—A Fantastic Smart Speaker Upgrade
reviews.body: If you are looking to upgrade your smart home audio without cluttering your counters, the Amazon Echo Dot Max hits the absolute sweet spot. It takes everything convenient about the compact Dot series and packs in a massive audio punch that completely changes the game for small-to-medium-sized rooms.Why It’s a Great Addition to Your Home:Incredible Sound Upgrade: The "Max" moniker is well-earned here. The audio profile is night and day compared to older Echo models. It delivers surprisingly deep bass, rich mid-tones, and crystal-clear highs. Whether you are listening to a podcast or streaming music, it fills the room effortlessly.Sleek, Modern Design: The compact design looks incredibly sharp on a desk, nightstand, or kitchen counter. It blends right into your decor while still offering a clear, easy-to-read LED display for the time, weather, and song titles.Fast, Responsive Processing: Thanks to the upgraded internal processor, Alexa responds to smart home commands (like turning on lights or adjusting the thermostat) noticeably faster than previous generations.The One Caveat:Microphone Sensitivity Could Be Better: If there is one minor downside to the "Max" hardware, it’s that the microphone array seems a bit weak compared to the booming speakers. If you have music playing at a higher volume or if you are speaking from across a noisy room, you might have to raise your voice or repeat yourself once or twice to get Alexa’s attention.Performance at a Glance:FeatureMy Rating Note Audio Quality⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Deep bass and clear vocals; punches above its weight Smart Home Speed⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Lightning-fast processing for routine commands Design & Display⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Sleek look with a highly useful LED interface Mic Sensitivity⭐⭐⭐☆☆Requires a bit more effort to wake in loud rooms Bottom Line: Despite needing to speak up occasionally when the room gets loud, the Echo Dot Max is a stellar device. The massive upgrade in sound quality more than makes up for the slightly weaker mic. If you want a compact speaker that actually sounds excellent for music, this is a fantastic buy!

reviews.title: Small Size, Big Sound—I’m Extremely Impressed!

My replacement is the new Echo Dot Max, and I couldn’t be happier. It’s surprisingly compact, but don’t let its size fool you. The sound is outstanding! It’s much louder than I expected, the bass is rich and clear, and the overall audio quality is excellent. I use it every day for weather updates, news, reminders, timers, music, and answering quick questions. It’s become one of those devices I didn’t realize I depended on until I had it. For such a small speaker, it delivers an impressive performance and is an excellent value. I’m genuinely impressed with this little Echo Dot Max and would absolutely recommend it to anyone looking for a smart speaker with great sound in a compact package.

reviews.title: Good, but there’s room for improvement
reviews.body: This was my first ever Alexa device, and honestly it’s been somewhat disappointing. The pros: sound quality is good and definitely fills a room, setting up voice command routines is easy and there are a lot of fun options (when they work), it does well with simple voice commands, and it works reliably with my smart lights and other smart devices. An additional pro is the “call for help” feature, which fortunately I haven’t had to test out, but it does give me some peace of mind as someone who lives alone with chronic health issues. The big con: the Alexa-specific features that don’t connect with other smart devices have been unreliable for me. More often than not, it just stops in the middle of a pre-programmed routine. When I try to troubleshoot with the virtual chatbox in the app, it just says “the team is working on it” with no real solution proposed except manually recreating shorter routines… which isn’t really what I wanted to be doing at the price point, as the routines I built initially are not at all complicated. Overall I don’t regret the purchase, but would have opted for a cheaper model if I knew how unreliable some core features could be.

reviews.body: Esta versión ofrece una mejora en conectividad y respuesta con respecto a modelos anteriores. También viene preparada para Alexa+. El audio es bueno dado el tamaño, nada sorprendente pero mejor que cualquier otra versión de Echo Dot. Si lo que buscas es un muy buen sonido es mejor irse a la versión de Studio, la diferencia de precio es considerable pero también lo es la diferencia en audio. Aun no decido si me gusta o no la actualización a Alexa+, le pusieron una voz que pretende ser "mexicana natural", pero a mi me suena rara todavía, aun seleccionando la voz supuestamente original.

The audio is good given the size, nothing surprising but better than any other version of the Echo Dot. If what you are looking for is a very good sound, it is better to go for the Studio version, the price difference is considerable but so is the difference in audio. I still haven't decided if I like the update to Alexa+ or not, they gave it a voice that pretends to be "natural Mexican", but it still sounds strange to me, even selecting the supposedly original voice.

reviews.title: Product Is Excellent — Purchasing Process Was Needlessly Difficult
reviews.body: Product Review: The Echo Dot Max itself is excellent. The sound quality is impressive for its size, functionality is solid, and Alexa performs exactly as expected. Once everything was set up, the device worked great and feels well designed. I genuinely enjoy the product and look forward to continuing to use Alexa devices in the future. PURCHASING & CUSTOMER SERVICE EXPERIENCE (Important Context): I want to provide context around the purchasing process, as it required a significant amount of time, persistence, and unnecessary stress. I originally attempted to purchase two older versions of this product (used). After multiple payment processing issues, I was forced to cancel and attempt to repurchase, at which point the items disappeared entirely and could not be located. After contacting customer service, I was told that no new or used stock of those models remained. After the representative spoke with a supervisor, I was offered a price-match arrangement on the newest model instead. I received an email confirming this offer and was instructed to complete the full-price purchase and then call back to receive reimbursement of the price difference. I followed those instructions exactly. When I called back, I was told by another agent and supervisor that the reimbursement could not be processed until the item was delivered. I waited, received the device, and called again. At that point, despite prior confirmations (now involving multiple frontline agents and supervisors), I encountered repeated resistance to honoring the agreement. The call turned into hours of back-and-forth, during which I was repeatedly told the reimbursement could not be done, despite written confirmation stating otherwise. During this process, I was repeatedly encouraged to end the call without resolution or to be transferred to the Echo/Alexa specialist team, with the suggestion that they had authority over the purchase. This created additional DELAYS & DEFLECTION, even though the issue was not related to product functionality but to a previously confirmed purchase arrangement. The situation became EXTREMELY STRESSFUL, as the purchase required funds I had set aside for essential insurance payments, and an NSF would have resulted in penalties I could not afford. The prolonged uncertainty was disheartening, especially after relying on information that had been repeatedly confirmed. After several hours of persistence and refusing to allow the issue to be dismissed or deferred further, the agreement was finally honored and the matter was resolved. Additional Observation: After everything was resolved, the original models I was told were unavailable suddenly appeared back in stock. I was then able to purchase the two used devices (used) as I originally wanted at the reasonable price they were still listed as. FINAL THOUGHTS: The product itself is outstanding, and I’m very happy with the Echo Dot Max and the additional Echo devices I later purchased. My hope in sharing this experience is simply that internal communication and consistency improve, so customers are not placed under unnecessary financial stress after relying on confirmed information. Despite the ordeal, I remain a satisfied Alexa user and appreciate the final resolution to some respect. But, overall, it does NOT MAKE up for, nor compensate for the Uneeded, undue TIME & STRESS endured, especially after I had mentioned my current Ongoing HEALTH Related Battle. My Opinion: While the product itself is excellent, this experience showed me how difficult it can be for individual customers to resolve issues when information is inconsistent across multiple representatives.

reviews.body: The IPX7 Waterproof Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker has honestly impressed me more than I expected. It was recommended by my brother, and for the price, it performs better than a lot of bigger-name brands I’ve tried. The sound quality is crisp and clear, with no noticeable degradation so far even after regular use. It delivers enough volume and fullness to work well indoors or outdoors without sounding muddy or overly distorted. Connection has also been straightforward. Devices pair quickly, and the USB-C support is a welcome feature compared to older connection types. Having both USB and Type-C compatibility adds a bit of convenience and flexibility depending on your setup. Battery life is another strong point. It holds a charge for a long time, which makes it reliable for extended use or outdoor settings. The tradeoff is that it’s not a particularly fast recharge, so you’ll want to plan ahead rather than expect a quick top-off before heading out. The waterproofing is another plus, especially for outdoor use or keeping around a work area where accidents happen. Combined with the long battery life, it feels like a speaker designed more for actual use than just shelf appeal. Now comes the real test: durability. In this era of planned obsolescence, the question is how well it will hold up after a year or more of regular use. That’s ultimately what separates decent electronics from genuinely reliable gear. Still, first impressions are strong. The overall design feels practical and time-tested, with a bit of an old-school sensibility that focuses more on utility than gimmicks. Overall, this speaker punches above its price point. It’s practical, sounds good, connects quickly, and avoids a lot of the overhyped branding that bigger companies rely on. For the money, it’s been a solid buy.

reviews.title: Unbelievably good at the price point.
reviews.body: This is one very impressive Bluetooth Speaker. So good in fact that within a hour of the delivery of the first one I bought another one. I can't wait to hear how 2 sound connected with the way the first one sounds. Im not easily impressed when it comes to music and sounds being a bit of a audiophile. But I am completely and totally impressed with this speaker. It's just that good. The bass is even better than I expected. The clarity and volume are equally impressive. It connected to my phone and my tablet without a second wasted. It looks good, sounds amazing and is going to be difficult to beat . It's fairly heavy for it's size which surprised me. It's really that good. You won't be disappointed if you buy one . It's versatility and functionality are as impressive as it's sound quality. I went for a ride in my hot rod Jeep CJ5 and had no problem hearing the speaker loud and clear. And my jeep isn't exactly quiet but I heard every note and verse without any problems. Can't wait until I get the 2nd one I just ordered. Im not exaggerating, it really is that good ! Update... I received the 2nd speaker and it is just as I expected as far as sound quality and performance. They sound fantastic and the difference between having a single speaker and having a 2nd speaker is significant but not as significant as I expected it to be. I thought that the bass and mid range sounds would increase and that would improve the only thing I think needs improvement with these speakers. That's the Bass and Midrange sound quality. They have Bass and Midrange sound but I think it could be or should have been much better with 2 speakers. There was a improvement but not as much as I expected There would be. There aren't 2 passive radiators on the rear that I can see. There's a long oval shaped thing that I guess is what they are calling w passive radiator. Even using my Dolby Sound app on my phone and the different sound levels and music type preset equalizer settings still produces little or no noticeable Bass or Midrange improvements in reality. 1 speaker sounds good and 2 sound much better than 1. But 2 don't improve the sound quality and range of performance the way I expected it to. The speakers are really good considering the price. They could even be described as Great. But they certainly could be better than they are . But at the current price point they are a fantastic bargain and are impressive without question. In a bedroom or small house they are undoubtedly going to be loud and sound great. But outside even having 2 of them turned up and separated by about 15 feet. They weren't as impressive or good as the 1st speaker led me to believe 2 of them would be. Definitely not bad , and a improvement over just 1 speaker. But definitely not the improvement as far as sound quality and overall volume one might anticipate. The stereo sound improved as it should have. But improvement in Bass or midrange sounds that I expected with the addition of another speaker just weren't what I expected or have experienced with other speakers in the past . Still a Great buy . But the addition of a second speaker linked to the first didn't provide the sound quality or volume I expected them to. They sound good but I expected there would be a more noticeable improvement in sound quality and volume with the 2nd speaker than I've observed.

SOUND THAT TAKES YOU PLACES: Take advantage of the surprisingly powerful performance of this Bose wireless speaker with its clear, balanced, high-fidelity audio and deep bass that is easy to take with you

PERFECTLY PORTABLE, WITH BATTERY LIFE TO MATCH: This Bluetooth speaker is small enough to fit in your hand or clip onto a bag using the utility loop, plus it has up to 12 hours of battery life* so you can focus on the fun at the beach, hikes, or pool
TOSS IT, DROP IT, IT’S ALL GOOD: This IP67 rated Bose portable Bluetooth speaker is waterproof and dustproof and is wrapped in a durable, silicone-wrapped body to withstand drops, shocks, and rust
STEREO ON THE GO: Amp up the adventure with more sound when you link two compatible Bose speakers, choose Stereo Mode for left and right channels, or go for Party Mode for even bigger, bolder sound

STAY CONNECTED WITH ADVANCED BLUETOOTH 5.3: This outdoor speaker uses Bluetooth 5.3 to ensure a continuous connection to your device from up to 30 feet away and can pair to multiple devices at once using multipoint technology

reviews.title: Sounds good, great size.
reviews.body: Bought this Bose speaker to use in the bathroom while showering. Sounds pretty good, even over the sound of the water running. Doesn't crackle or sound frizzy and is really clear. Connects to Bluetooth devices seamlessly. Its a great size for a small bathroom because it's not big or bulky. Really appreciate the small, slim design. The battery lasts for a decent amount of time, considering it's size. On a full charge and being used daily for about 2 hours, we charge it once - MAYBE twice - a week. It will drain about 10% daily. We don't leave it on the charger when it's not in use. Charge it only when the battery is low. It won't take long to charge either. The volume is good for what we use it for. We don't try to blast it for the neighborhood to hear it but sounds good outdoors around a group of friends by the fire or for background tunes while having a card night with buddies. Even works well and sounds good in the garage while working with power tools. Would probably even be great on a river float. Very happy and satisfied with this little speaker.

reviews.title: Powerful, Personal, Portable Flex Speaker
reviews.body: The Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen speaker is hands down my favorite bluetooth speaker, though I do own the latest Beats Pill and love it for its capabilities. At present, I own eight of these 2nd Gen Flex speakers, one in each color variant. I do find that audiobooks, podcasts and spoken content sound best on the 2nd Gen Flex. Most Music does as well. Some reviewers report sound differences between the color variants. After initially suspecting this and repeatedly comparing the identical audio on each speaker, I found that the most likely explanation is how one is holding the speaker when audio is playing, as the audio does change based on the position of the speaker. Features I would like to see in the 3rd Gen model include: Much longer battery life. The technology and capabilities exist. The speaker is so excellent that paying a little more for much longer battery life, perhaps double, would be worth it. Lossless ability. When connecting the latest Bose Ultra headphones and even the Beats Pill to my iPhone with the Usb C to Usb C cables, each offer lossless streaming. The ability to connect the Flex to a CD player or some other audio device via the cable. There are Usb C to 3.5mm male and female cables on the market and this would be nice as I still have a small Bose CD player and plenty of CDs. While there are bluetooth transmitters such as the AirFly which make connectivity possible, direct wired connectivity is still nice for some of us. A detachable strap. The Beats Pill and the most excellent Bose SoundLink Micro 2nd Gen both offer a detachable strap. This would be a nice option for the Flex in the future. Pairing four Flex speakers in surround sound mode. While two Flex speakers are great in stereo, pairing four for surround sound would be next level great. The ability to change the volume of the obnoxious sounds the Flex puts out. I do like these sounds, particularly when the speaker connects to bluetooth. However, these are way too loud. The Beats Pill has the option of controlling the volume of its sounds. The same is true for the voice prompts. While some of the voice prompts can be disabled in the app, the volume cannot be changed. Even without these potential additions to a 3rd Gen Flex, this existing 2nd Gen Flex is a phenomenal bluetooth speaker that serves many purposes. The Alpine Sage color variant has been discontinued, as it was limited. However, the existing color options are excellent, particularly the Twilight Blue. Although the Flex and Beats Pill are both excellent and come down to personal preference when selecting one or the other, I would also go with the Flex if I did not have the luxury of owning both. In fact, I would go with the Flex over any other, even if it has yet to fulfill all its potential, which with the suggestions I mentioned for the 3rd Gen Flex, it would be an untouchable speaker. Highly recommend the 2nd Gen Flex to all reading this.

reviews.body: Ich habe mir den Bose SoundLink Flex für unterwegs und den Garten geholt – und bin absolut begeistert! Der Lautsprecher überzeugt mit kraftvollem, glasklarem Sound und einem überraschend tiefen Bass für diese kompakte Größe. reviews.title: Powerful, Personal, Portable Flex Speaker
reviews.body: The Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen speaker is hands down my favorite bluetooth speaker, though I do own the latest Beats Pill and love it for its capabilities. At present, I own eight of these 2nd Gen Flex speakers, one in each color variant. I do find that audiobooks, podcasts and spoken content sound best on the 2nd Gen Flex. Most Music does as well. Some reviewers report sound differences between the color variants. After initially suspecting this and repeatedly comparing the identical audio on each speaker, I found that the most likely explanation is how one is holding the speaker when audio is playing, as the audio does change based on the position of the speaker. Features I would like to see in the 3rd Gen model include: Much longer battery life. The technology and capabilities exist. The speaker is so excellent that paying a little more for much longer battery life, perhaps double, would be worth it. Lossless ability. When connecting the latest Bose Ultra headphones and even the Beats Pill to my iPhone with the Usb C to Usb C cables, each offer lossless streaming. The ability to connect the Flex to a CD player or some other audio device via the cable. There are Usb C to 3.5mm male and female cables on the market and this would be nice as I still have a small Bose CD player and plenty of CDs. While there are bluetooth transmitters such as the AirFly which make connectivity possible, direct wired connectivity is still nice for some of us. A detachable strap. The Beats Pill and the most excellent Bose SoundLink Micro 2nd Gen both offer a detachable strap. This would be a nice option for the Flex in the future. Pairing four Flex speakers in surround sound mode. While two Flex speakers are great in stereo, pairing four for surround sound would be next level great. The ability to change the volume of the obnoxious sounds the Flex puts out. I do like these sounds, particularly when the speaker connects to bluetooth. However, these are way too loud. The Beats Pill has the option of controlling the volume of its sounds. The same is true for the voice prompts. While some of the voice prompts can be disabled in the app, the volume cannot be changed. Even without these potential additions to a 3rd Gen Flex, this existing 2nd Gen Flex is a phenomenal bluetooth speaker that serves many purposes. The Alpine Sage color variant has been discontinued, as it was limited. However, the existing color options are excellent, particularly the Twilight Blue. Although the Flex and Beats Pill are both excellent and come down to personal preference when selecting one or the other, I would also go with the Flex if I did not have the luxury of owning both. In fact, I would go with the Flex over any other, even if it has yet to fulfill all its potential, which with the suggestions I mentioned for the 3rd Gen Flex, it would be an untouchable speaker. Highly recommend the 2nd Gen Flex to all reading this.

reviews.title: Cute little owl
reviews.body: I got this for my 2-year-old, and the design alone was a huge win. The little owl look is really cute, and I paired it with the stand so it sits on a tree-style bookshelf in his room. It actually blends in like decor, which I love. So far, he hasn’t tried to grab or play with it much because he thinks it “belongs” on the shelf, which is honestly a plus. It feels like a kid-friendly device without being distracting or constantly handled. Where it’s been most useful is during our nighttime routine. We use it to play music and control other Alexa devices, which makes winding down a lot smoother. It’s been reliable for that and easy to use hands-free when my hands are full. Now I have my music waking me up and it continues to play more of the same until I say, from my bed, to stop. While I'm getting dressed I ask what's the weather and if there's any news I should know. I have it figure out the calories of the breakfast I'm going to make. We talk about things I'm interested in and it says goodnight and that's nice when you're alone living above a family that reminds me of the joy I had. I ordered the kids owl. title: Bose TV Speaker - Soundbar for TV with Bluetooth and HDMI-ARC Connectivity, All-in-One Compact Soundbar, Includes Remote Control, Black
bullet_points: HEAR YOUR TV BETTER: Designed with simplicity in mind, the Bose TV Speaker is an all-in-one soundbar that clarifies speech and is a simple fix for better TV sound
WIDE, NATURAL SOUND: 2 angled full-range drivers deliver a more realistic, spatial audio experience for overall better TV sound from a small soundbar
ENHANCED DIALOGUE: This sound bar for smart tv is designed to specifically focus on clarifying and elevating vocals and pronunciation

BLUETOOTH TV SPEAKER: Pair your device to this Bluetooth soundbar to wirelessly stream your favorite music and podcasts. Connect up to 3 devices through the inputs (HDMI, Optical in, and AUX in); the first powered on device will automatically connect
SIMPLE SETUP: A single connection from this compact soundbar to the TV via an optical audio cable (included) or an HDMI cable (sold separately) has you up and running in minutes

COMPACT SOUNDBAR: This small soundbar is just over 2" tall for easy placement in front of your TV or mounted to a wall (wall brackets sold separately). Overall TV speaker dimensions are 2.21" H x 23.38" W x 4.02" D; Remote Control: 4.1" H x 1.6" W x 0.5" D (0.07 lb)
REMOTE CONTROL INCLUDED: Compact TV speaker comes with a remote control that enables a dialogue mode to further enhance speech or add a bass boost for more depth

reviews.title: Bose Compact TV Subwoofer is a Great Value!
reviews.body: I recently bought this compact Bose soundbar on Amazon for $199.00. I can honestly say that it exceeds my expectations! Right out of the box you get the sense it’s a high quality product! The construction is solid and robust. My Bose soundbar is connected a recent model Samsung 32” QLED television via the HDMI Arc terminal. The audio quality is quite good IMO. Blindfolded you would swear the speaker was much larger. It’s got great high frequency response and the middle frequencies are crisp, balanced, possessing outside speech clarity. The bass is somewhat attenuated but given the compact size of the speaker it’s still very respectable. If you’re so inclined you can connect compatible Bose subwoofer to supplement the bass frequencies. I believe the Bose subwoofer represents a terrific value in the crowded home speaker market. I’m giving it 5 Stars since it exceeds my expectations!

reviews.title: INSANELY good for a small office/bedroom
reviews.body: I was looking for a small home office set up (10 X 12 room) and wanted something that was uncomplicated but also sounded really good given the room size. It's used primarily for music, but I'm often in meetings with up to 20 other people, so I wanted something with a voice clarity option. I figured I was going to have to sacrifice one for the other, but the speaker really delivers! What was most amazing to me was the level and quality of bass, which I didn't think was possible with a standalone sound bar, and a small sound bar at that. When I bought this, I also bought the bass module 500 which I've since returned, as it was completely unnecessary. The speaker produces a very balanced soundstage. I placed the soundbar across two studio monitor speaker stands with a 15 degree tilt, super highly recommended if you're planning to use this for a home office solution. This is absolutely not a speaker as a standalone in a larger room, but it's perfect for a small space. No subwoofer needed. You can literally feel the bass.

reviews.title: Excellent audio with consistent levels
reviews.body: This is my third and hopefully final soundbar in my hunt for something that just works. I did a bit of research that landed me on the Bose TV Speaker. This is for a living room with a 20' ceiling and a TV mounted above the fireplace. With young kids, the TV is usually on their shows during the day or mom and dad trying to watch something in the evening. We aren't looking to be fully immersed in booming action movies, dialogue is the focus. The last one I had would drown out dialogue with background music and I was always trying to adjust the levels. This is perfect, I don't have to fiddle with it and it does a great job of staying consistent and I never have an issue hearing dialogue. It connected easily to my Roku TV and even supports Roku TV integration, allowing me to adjust things through the TV interface. I like that it's relatively small while packing powerful audio. The only problem I had may have been due to my TV - when I connected to the Bose over Bluetooth it messed up the hdmi-arc connection and my TV was no longer powering the Bose on and off, I had to factory reset the TV to resolve this and I haven't tried the Bluetooth connection since. Bottom line is that I didn't want to spend more than $200 and I just wanted something that would just work - apparently that is a unicorn in today's age of soundbars - and the Bose TV Speaker is that unicorn

reviews.title: Finally, a simple solution to the madhouse of audio alternatives for television
reviews.body: I had a Bose one piece sound system many years ago. Really enjoyed it. It eventually gave up so I started down the dark hole of soundbars. In about 10 years I've had 3 and with each one there was always something that wouldn't sound right, mainly when someone talks and there's music in the background, only the music that's supposed to hang back instead blares like a foghorn and drowns out the dialogue. I have to admit the last one, a Vizio, soundbar only, no subwoofer or surround speakers, did it's best to keep the dialogue to within reach. It's main issue was it wouldn't cooperate with a Vizio TV, wouldn't maintain a setting if you had the ability to pay it. So, I'm back to the simple Bose TV Speaker. Ya got two settings, bass and dialogue. There are others but they don't involve audio. It plugs into my Vizio TV via HDMI eARC (cable not included), but it does come with an optical cable and I plugged it in but isn't required. ARC allows my TV remote and Fire Stick remote to control the soundbar volume which is the only thing you really need to control once you set the soundbar with it's own remote to be controlled by other devices and the sound setting you like (your choice of two or both at the same time, why not go for it). I can hear music, I can hear voices, I can hear them both at the same time and anyone who says you need a small room to use it in is probably wanting more than the bar can deliver regarding audio. It's plenty loud. Where I sit fairly far from the TV and the room is kind of open concept leading to not open concept, like rooms elsewhere. I can hear it through out the house. Good bass too. Okay I said two settings but the bass actually has 3 levels. The longest portion of the entire setup from unpacking to connection and listening was the unpacking. It's packed pretty well. Good things come in small packages they say, this is one of them. I recommend this to anyone who doesn't require sound bouncing from the holes in their shoes and from the coffee mug sitting beside them. It's a great sounding speaker that removes the requirement of having to take a course or two in sound engineering and makes listening to TV simple and comfortable and enjoyable again, you don't have to constantly change the audio settings to work with the video. It just works.

reviews.title: Big beautiful Bose sound
reviews.body: This is a truly excellent product that fully lives up to expectations. The sound is big and the complexity of setup is small, although to make it work with my older Sharp Aquos TV, which lacks HDMI ARC, I had to buy a dongle — an HDMI audio extractor that pulls the sound out of the main source HDMI and shunts it to an optical jack that can communicate properly with the Bose device using the supplied optical cable. More modern TVs won’t need that. For those whose TV had great video but the audio sucks, this is the cure. It would be worth it for full price but it was nice to get this one as a Prime Day door-buster sale item. I know the days of Bose products being made in Framingham are long gone but this particular item is built in Thailand, which is an ally or something like one. As an ABC shopper I’ll settle for that.

reviews.body: Buena opcion, la calidad claro se siente diferente a una barra comecial, de inicio pense no sonaba bien y le faltaba potencia pero es que hay que saberla configurar, la puse cob hdmi y se configuro al control remoto de izzi para se prenda y apague con la tv, al cambiar el volumen de la tv sale el modo de amplificador y la pongo al 40 y se escucha bastante fuerte sin modo de amplificacion de voz (que parece un extra bastante fuerte) a vexes le quito esta funcion ya al dormir porque se escucha muy potente, en realidad la barra es bastante buena pense que necesitaria a fuerza el modulo de bajos pero bajea bien para una barra al nivel de una barra 2.1 creative que tenia antes (60/80rms aprox) la verdad solo hay que moverle, jugarle a configurarla y listo, el volumen sin este modo que sale en la tv el nivel es dificil de subir y piensas no sube, la calidad es muy buena y escucho muy diferente a la barra anterior aunque fuera 2.1, si muy contento y la calidad es demaciado bueno, por el precio es una super compra, no duden en pedirla.
reviews.body_en: Good option, the quality of course feels different from a commercial bar, at first I thought it didn't sound good and it lacked power but you have to know how to configure it, I put it with HDMI and it was configured with the izzi remote control to turn it on and off with the TV, when I change the volume of the TV the amplifier mode comes out and I put it at 40 and it sounds quite loud without voice amplification mode (which seems like a pretty loud extra) I'll sometimes remove this function now when sleeping because it sounds very powerful, in reality the bar is quite good I thought I would need the bass module by force but it lowers well for a bar to the level of a 2.1 creative bar that I had before (60/80rms approx) the truth is you just have to move it, play with configuring it and that's it, the volume without this mode that appears on the TV the level is difficult to raise and you think it doesn't go up, the quality is very good and I hear very different from the previous bar even if it were 2.1, if you are very happy and the quality is too good, for the price it is a great purchase, do not hesitate to order it.

reviews.title: Great sound for the room — simple, reliable upgrade
reviews.body: I picked up the Bose TV Speaker to replace my old CineMate Bose system that finally died, and so far it’s been an excellent, hassle-free replacement. Setup was plug-and-play with my existing Bose TV’s optical out and it started working immediately. I haven’t used the Dialogue Enhancer feature, but even without it the speaker delivers clear, natural-sounding audio that suits my room very well. The unit is compact but sounds bigger than it looks. The bass has respectable weight for such a small speaker — not a home-theatre rumble, but enough to give action scenes and music some presence. The included remote is simple and intuitive, and overall build quality feels solid and understated like other Bose products. Pros: - Smooth setup — truly plug-and-play - Clear, balanced sound that fits the room nicely - Compact footprint; good for smaller living areas or bedrooms - Solid build and easy-to-use remote Cons: - Not a substitute for a full surround system if you want immersive multi-channel audio - Won’t match a dedicated subwoofer for deep bass Would recommend if you want an easy, reliable upgrade from an older compact Bose unit — great for improving everyday TV sound without fuss.

reviews.title: The Perfect Speaker
reviews.body: This is essentially the perfect bluetooth speaker. The sound quality, especially after dialing the EQ, is as good as it gets. Clear bass, sparkling highs, powerful mids. I just don't see how you could get better in this form factor. Speaking of which, this thing is small, about the size of a hiking boot. Coupled with the excellent handle you have an extremely convenient package for carrying with you around the house. You could even travel with it if you don't mind the significant weight. It's built very solidly, the quality is satisfyingly obvious. The bluetooth functionality is flawless. Just turn it on and it syncs to your phone within 5 seconds EVERY SINGLE TIME. Not sure why it's taken so long to get this tech reliable. The app is great also. Yes, it's expensive, but it is absolutely worth the price, considering it enhances my life pretty much all day long.

reviews.title: Durable, Great Sound Quality - Worth It
reviews.body: Fantastic speaker—well‑built, durable, and quick to charge. The size is perfect for pool days, parties, or tossing in a bag for travel. I bring it on trips for hotel‑room music, and around the house it never loses connection, even when I’m in another room or out in the backyard. It’s waterproof, so shower use is fair game. It charges via USB‑C, and that same port can top off your phone in a pinch. There’s also an AUX input if you ever need it. Multiple devices can connect via Bluetooth (though that can get chaotic), and it can pair with other Bose speakers. Once you’ve paired your device the first time, it reconnects automatically every time you power it on. Sound Quality: The sound is excellent. You can tweak the EQ in the app, the bass is strong and clean, and this thing gets loud without losing clarity. Treble stays crisp, and overall it’s one of the best‑sounding speakers in its size class. Is it worth the price? I’d say yes. Plenty of speakers check the same boxes, but if you want a bougie speaker that performs - this one is for you.
