reviews.title: It brings the bass
reviews.body: As a long-time owner of the first-generation Bose SoundLink Mini, I had high expectations for the Bose SoundLink Max, and it did not disappoint. This review covers various aspects of the speaker, including sound quality, durability, ease of use, compatibility, setup, and design. The SoundLink Max lives up to the Bose name. After testing it with a myriad of musical genres, I was blown away by the fullness of the sound. The bass is so powerful that you can feel it, yet it does not drown out the mid and treble frequencies. It is worth noting that the initial EQ settings are flat, which might be why some users have complained about the lack of fullness. This could be addressed by repurposing the shortcut button for quick EQ adjustment. The SoundLink Max meets the IP67 standards, making it rugged, dustproof, and waterproof. Weighing nearly five pounds, it is heavy, but this is an acceptable trade-off for the durability it offers. In a pinch, you could even use it as a brick or a weapon for defending yourself from zombies! Using the SoundLink Max is straightforward. Press the power button, then play to start enjoying your music. When it’s time to change settings, the buttons are clearly labeled. The Max charges via a supplied USB-C cord and power block and can also serve as a portable power device. This is my main point of contention and it is not specifically with the Max, but with Bose as a whole. They have partnered with Qualcomm/Snapdragon for their HD Audio, which is currently confined to the Android ecosystem. As an iPhone user, I felt a little left out in the cold. Straight out-of-the-box, the Max was nearly ready to go. It took two seconds to pair and less than that to start charging, thanks to the included USB-C cable and power brick. The Bose app was easy to find and quick to install. I was able to set up an account and start using the app right away. While the setup was easy, more emphasis should be placed on the necessity of using the app to achieve the best sound, as the default EQ settings are a bit flat. The SoundLink Max boasts a sleek and simple design. There are no unnecessary lights or reminiscent designs to distract you—just a rugged exterior that protects the speakers while delivering excellent sound quality. The rope handle is a nice feature that accentuates the rugged yet simple design. They are easily changeable for other colored handles and shoulder straps, which are available at a steep premium on the Bose website. The Bose SoundLink Max is a phenomenal portable speaker that lives up to the high standards we expect from Bose. After several days of testing in various locations and with different music genres, I have not been disappointed. While there have been some reports of less-than-fantastic sound quality, this issue is easily resolved by adjusting the EQ settings in the Bose app. The final question is, is the SoundLink Max worth the $400 price tag? The simple answer is yes, it is worth every penny.

reviews.title: Sounds like a box of farts, and not in a good way. Maybe it is broken?
reviews.body: When I first unpacked this product and listened to it, I was completely won over. What an amazing first impression. Excellent soundstage. Wide, detailed, clear, everything you could want. Unfortunately, once you take the volume to even close to 50%, which you'd want to do in many situations and certainly outside, and it all falls apart. Hero to zero in the blink of an eye. The bass has a fart-like quality to it which ruins everything. The only way to make this sound acceptable is to use the EQ to take the bass pretty much to nothing or even a negative setting. In which case, you could buy almost any other Bluetooth speaker for less than half the price that is going to sound just as good. Many of the reviews talk about bass and presence, but that's only true at really low levels. At least assuming the unit I was sent is working to factory spec. And don't get me wrong, I'm not listening to music at window rattling levels designed to annoy the neighbors. I'm not even listening to tracks that I think are especially bass heavy. As an example I listened to Clocks by Coldplay. Hardly a hardcore bass fest. The opening bars sounded amazing. But as soon as the gentle bass chords joined the music, the speaker lost itself. I tried the product on a hard wooden stool. A hard wooden deck. A patio table. A different patio table. A few feet away. A few meters away. It really didn't matter. I played with numerous EQ settings. But the bottom line is that it just can't put out bass in any real capacity unless you are willing to lower the sound to a background volume. In which case, it's amazing. To me, the bass being available in such a quiet and tiny sweet spot, makes it kind of worthless to include it at all. I have a pair of B&O Explore speakers, that sound amazing and can be set as a stereo pair. If you buy them well you can have two of them for $100 less than this Bose. What they lack in bass, they more than make up for in incredible sound stage, stereo separation and can go toe to toe in terms of detail. The thing is, they also KNOW they can't do much bass, so they don't even try. Bose, is trying too hard to make bass happen that apparently isn't possible in this system. Just like I don't drive my car at 100 mph ever, I want it to be capable of that. I want it to accelerate from zero to sixty in under seven seconds, even though it's not how I drive. And when it comes to speakers, I want to know that if I want to turn up the volume a little, it isn't going to sound like a box of farts. I tried to give it every opportunity to impress, but it failed at everything except very quiet listening levels. I was mainly streaming from Apple Music, and I even looked for songs offered at their highest bitrate or including spacial audio technology. For the price they are charging, there is no way I keep this item. It is already in the box ready to go to UPS. Maybe it would be different if you have a different sound source, are using a different streaming service, are using AUX or Android. My tests were iOS based, and bluetooth streaming. Tracks that I have previously tested on my Marshall Woburn II speaker as an example, with the same source equipment.

reviews.title: Great Sounding Speaker ... If You Are Patient
reviews.body: *FIRST IMPRESSIONS: Listening to music as it comes out of the box, I had two impressions,something is missing from the music and what is that painful squeael in the treble area. while they may sound bad out of the box, the hardware is capable of greatness with the right tweaks. The rest of this review provides information about the basic setup and configuration of these speakers and what needs to be done to improve the sound. * PROS: Sound great; full spectrum with clear highs and lows, but takes work to bring it out. In fact, for the best sound, you'll need an equalizer. Once equalization has been applied, they can have the clarity found in a pair of much higher priced speakers; they have great lows, but can't match the 28Hz lows of the Cerwin Vega D-9s but the highs are reasonably close. Fairly easy to pair with another speaker but see below. * CONS: All detailed below with solutions: 1. Out of the box, it sounds much worse than it actually is. The default equalization was for marketing. The bass is pushed up 4 dB, the midrange down 2 dB and the highs up 5 dB. This may be impressive for a short time, but you may eventually be dissatisfied as the center has been cut out of the music and you'll cringe at the outlandish scream at 6.3 kHz. 2. Connecting to the Bose app involves an overlooked step, Bose should fix this. 3. Interconnecting speakers as a stereo pair is a bit tricky. 4. Serious power management problem which Bose should also fix. 5. Most buttons lack tactile icons for the visually impaired, but they are easy to find and count. For this device, there are six buttons arranged in a single horizontal row on the top front from left to right as follows: (1) power, (2) Bluetooth, (3) link, (4) Volume down, (5) Play/Pause, and (6) Volume up. Note that the function of the Play/Pause button may be affected by your music player and bluetooth configuration. Now for the details: * SETUP: - Connecting To The Bose App: It is hard to get The Bose app connected so you can take advantage of built-in features. This complaint appears often on the Google Playstore. - Getting Into The Configuration App: Download and install the Bose app from the web; it is in android and Apple download sites as well as the Bose web site. For best results, connect your phone to the speaker via bluetooth. Open the app and follow instructions until you get to a page that ought to be showing your device name and which contains the "Add Device" link. * NOTE: Before clicking this link be certain that notifications are enabled on your phone and that you will be alerted when a new notification arrives. Note to Bose, this ought to be stated on that page as a reminder to users. Assuming it has the right device, click the "Add Device" link. You will almost instantaneously get a notification. Open it and click the "Pair" link in that notification. If you are too late or something else happens, go back to that add device link and try again. * CONFIGURING THE SPEAKER: There are two areas of interest in the Bose app, one allows you to make some adjustments to the equalization for the speaker. The other allows you to control automatic power down parameters. - The Built In Equalizer: The built in equalizer has only three frequency bands for you to deal with, the bass, midrange and the treble. By default, these bands are set for marketing impact, to impress casual shoppers with the amazing highs and lows this speaker can produce, but you may find music reproduction very disappointing. If you want this primarily as a portable speaker, use the equalizer controls to produce a sound more to your liking. However, this won't clean up the sharp power spike at 6.3kHz., for that, an external equalizer is required. - Correcting The Frequency Response: If you have an Equalizer on your phone or computer, that equalizer will be far better than the one built into the speaker. Suggested Equalizations are given below. * POWER MANAGEMENT SETTING: Disguised as a profile area is the settings area (top right corner of the apps home page. The primary area of concern is the power setting. By default it is set to automatic. That means the speaker will turn off after 12 hours, even if plugged in. This is a battery safety feature. However, if you're using the speaker at home and have it always plugged in, you can set it to "Never," but be aware that this could be a problem if your power fails for you take it with you and fail to power it down first, the result could be a drained and if it goes long enough, damaged battery. The risk is yours, balance that risk against your convenience. Note to Bose, you should disregard the power down parameter if the speaker is plugged in. I consider not doing so a major engineering defect on your part especially as it could lead to battery problems. NOTE: Keep in mind Listening at high volumes or with very heavy bass will eventually cause the unit to shut down, even while plugged in. Also, under those conditions, the discharge time on full batteries without being plugged in is only three hours. To completely recharge the batteries after a shutdown will take about 5 hours. Recharge time from shutdown can take far longer if you try to turn it on again after a shutdown. * Personalizing The Sound: First, be aware that we all have different preferences in how music sounds, but here is what I did. I am using Equalizer APO on windows, but there are several similar apps for Android phones - Wavelet, Poweramp Equalizer, Echo Equalizer). For Mac users, you can achieve these same results using SoundSource (with an AU plugin) or the 'Expert' mode in eqMac. It generally acts like the loudness contour in older amplifiers. It greatly increases the bass at low volumes and reduces the bass amplification as volume increases. It is also intended to produce the "Bose Sound" that is "full, meaning exagerated lows and highs." The response curves and filter/equalization settings below assume moderate volume. They work against the built in DSP settings to extend the frequency range where the response is considered "flat," that is, the range in which the volume stays between + or - 3dB. That is the normal standard for top grade amplifiers and speakers to ensure that you hear the music as intended by the artists who produced it. The following is the list of frequency and power level, in dB that I'm using to correct the factory tuning and achieve a more balanced, high-fidelity sound. I found the following frequency adjustments to be effective. These values help neutralize the sharp spikes and restore the midrange that is missing out of the box. NOTE: These values assume the default Bose equalization has not been changed. They are the settings recommended on the internet, I found them to give a booming bass, so I substituted the lines that are not commented out. Make your own choice. Preamp: -6.5 dB #Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -1.5 dB Q 1.0 #Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -2.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 1: ON PK Fc 100 Hz Gain -3.5 dB Q 1.0 Filter 2: ON PK Fc 250 Hz Gain -4.5 dB Q 1.5 Filter 3: ON PK Fc 1000 Hz Gain 2.0 dB Q 1.0 Filter 4: ON PK Fc 2500 Hz Gain 1.5 dB Q 2.0 Filter 5: ON PK Fc 4000 Hz Gain -3.0 dB Q 1.5 Filter 6: ON PK Fc 6300 Hz Gain -6.0 dB Q 3.0 Filter 7: ON PK Fc 10000 Hz Gain -4.0 dB Q 2.0 Filter 8: ON HS Fc 13000 Hz Gain 4.5 dB * A comparison of frequency response curves: Bose out of the box: Effective Range +/- 6dB; 60 Hertz to 14,000 Hertz • Using the Equalizer settings: Effective range +/- 3dB;110 Hertz to 5,000 Hertz., limited by that massive cut at 6.3 kHz. Using the first Filter settings: Effective range +/- 2.5dB; 55 Hertz to 15,500 Hertz. Using Filter settings #2: Effective range +/- 3dB; 52 Hz to 16,500 Hz Clearly, the filter settings are the winner. feel free to adjust the equalization values to your own satisfaction, and if you feel the need, you can supply intermediate values. If you increase the power too much, and get distortion from clipping, reduce the preamp value. * Making A Stereo Pair: This area is considered to be a bit flakey, perhaps because people forget critical details or their timing is a bit off. so be prepared to repeat if required. To make a stereo pair. On the speaker you want as the left speaker, do a long press and then a quick second press of the third button from the left (the Shortcut/Link button). After the speaker tells you to do so, do a single quick press of the third button from the left on the second speaker, this will be the right speaker. Be patient, the speakers takes longer than one would expect to respond to the button presses on each speaker; allow 30 to 45 seconds for each speaker. reviews.body_en: *FIRST IMPRESSIONS: Listening to music as it comes out of the box, I had two impressions,something is missing from the music and what is that painful squeael in the treble area. while they may sound bad out of the box, the hardware is capable of greatness with the right tweaks. This may be impressive for a short time, but you may eventually be dissatisfied as the center has been cut out of the music and you'll cringe at the outlandish scream at 6.3 kHz. 2. For best results, connect your phone to the speaker via bluetooth. Open it and click the "Pair" link in that notification. By default, these bands are set for marketing impact, to impress casual shoppers with the amazing highs and lows this speaker can produce, but you may find music reproduction very disappointing. If you want this primarily as a portable speaker, use the equalizer controls to produce a sound more to your liking. reviews.title: La calidad de los materiales es muy buena, el sonido es muy completo.
reviews.body: Me gustó mucho la calidad del sonido y la de los materiales, realmente se siente una bocina de buena calidad; ya tengo otras bocinas de la marca me sorprendió el bajo que puede llegar a tener esta, la compatibilidad con otras bocinas es limitada me hubiera gustado que tuviera compatibilidad con más bocinas anteriores, el volumen es bueno al 70 o 75 % pero pasando pierde algo de nitidez no solo en el bajo en el cuerpo completo, no suena mal pero no ideal.
reviews.body_en: I really liked the quality of the sound and the materials, it really feels like a good quality speaker; I already have other speakers from the brand, I was surprised by the bass that this one can have, the compatibility with other speakers is limited, I would have liked it to have compatibility with more previous speakers, the volume is good at 70 or 75% but going past it loses some clarity not only in the bass in the full body, it doesn't sound bad but not ideal.

reviews.title: Outstanding Sound
reviews.body: If there were two ratings, one for the speaker and one for the Seller (Amazon), Speaker gets 5 Stars and Amazon gets 2 Stars. The speaker doesn't deserve a low rating due to Amazon. I watched a lot of reviews and had a hard time to decide between JBL or Bose, only because of the Bose price. I already have 2 Bose Soundtouch 300s and 1 Bose Wave Sountouch, so I already knew the rich sound Bose puts out. Because of the sound quality of my previous Bose I figured I would take a chance on the Pricey Bose Soundlink Max. Before I go any further, I do need to say first, Amazon should be ashamed of themselves, selling OPEN BOX for BRAND NEW. I don't believe this is the fault of Bose, it is Amazon Re-Selling their returns, as I bought 2 Bose Soundlink Max's "Shipped by Amazon" and both were OPEN BOX which was not stated in the selling add. They were at a good sale price, but i dislike not being told they were OPEN BOX, especially when paying close to $400 CAD for 1 speaker. Even though the speakers are outstanding I am thinking of returning both speakers due to this unless Amazon can do something about it. 90% of my purchases are through Amazon, and having this done disgusts me. Back to the Bose Soundlink Max. This review is based on only one evening of trial. For starters I had no issues with the bluetooth, it was very easy to connect both my Samsung phone and Samsung tablet, and that was without the Bose App installed. Once I was linked, I started playing all types of music. Pop, Dance, Rock etc, and with a bit of bit of fine tuning with the built in EQ on Samsung, this little speaker fills the room with such amazing rich sound. I read a review once where it said this speaker sounds great out of the box. It sounds ok, but tune an EQ on it and it is amazing. I would shut the EQ off and On while playing and listening to this speaker through an EQ makes a world of difference, which BTW would be the same with any speaker. The build of the speaker is very nice. Does not have a cheap plastic feel. A good portion of the speaker has a grippy silicone feel. The weight of the speaker alone tells a lot about the build Quality, Not too heavy, but also not too light, its very solid. The carry handle is very sturdy and well connected as well. I still need to try the linking feature between the two speakers. Will update soon

reviews.title: Buen producto
reviews.body: Soy amante de las bocinas y me la compré para ver que tan potente era. No está mal, se oye fuerte, calidad de bajos está mejor que revolve y todas las bocinas por debajo. Yo realmente la uso para mi cuarto y se oye súper bien. Algo volumen si usa Spotify se escucha feo, con Apple Music tiene mejor calidad y se escucha mucho mejor. Si le vas a dar uso rudo recomienda la negra.
reviews.body_en: I am a speaker lover and I bought it to see how powerful it was. It's not bad, it sounds loud, the bass quality is better than Revolve and all the speakers below it. I actually use it for my room and it sounds great. Some volume if you use Spotify it sounds ugly, with Apple Music it has better quality and it sounds much better. But the high quality is strong, bass at high volume is not heard too. I bought it on sale and for traveling, hiking, or going out it is perfect. It scratches easily, and gets dirty. If you are going to use it harshly, recommend the black one.

reviews.title: Great Sound, Premium Build, and Perfect for My Desktop Setup
reviews.body: I picked up the Marshall Emberton III during Amazon Prime Day for just $99, and it has been one of my favorite purchases this year. I was looking for a single speaker to sit in front of my computer monitor instead of using traditional left-and-right desktop speakers. The rectangular shape fits perfectly on my desk and gives me the clean, soundbar-like setup I wanted. On top of that, the retro Marshall design looks fantastic and feels very premium. I also own a JBL Flip 6, and both speakers sound great. However, the Emberton III fits my desktop needs much better. I really like that all the controls—power, Bluetooth pairing, and volume—are conveniently located on the top, making them easy to access without reaching around the speaker. The sound quality is excellent, with impressive volume, clear audio, and surprisingly punchy bass for its size. Whether I’m listening to music, watching YouTube, or using it as my everyday computer speaker, it performs beautifully. Overall, I’m extremely satisfied with this purchase. If you’re looking for a stylish, well-built Bluetooth speaker that doubles as an excellent desktop speaker, especially at the Prime Day price, I highly recommend it.

Would be cool if you could toggle lights auto on on and off, but for the price I can't complain 😎 Hope this helped someone 🙂

reviews.title: Looks Great and Sounds Very Good
reviews.body: It's a solid speaker that is plenty loud and appears to be a Sony knockoff. It looks almost like a previous generation Sony and has similar lighting. The Sony definitely sounds better with more bass and refined audio quality, but the Sony was also 3x the price. You get what you pay for. It was important for me to buy this for my wife to replace her broken 4 year old Sony without confusing her or spending a lot of money. The controls are on this Beat Boom unit are easier to see and use and it uses a USB-C to charge. The Beat Boom is also more attractive, but larger than my own Anker speaker. Again the controls are easier to use, however the Anker has superior audio quality at a similar price. Had no problem connecting the Bluetooth to phones either. If you want a mid-priced range BT speaker < $50 that is plenty loud with colorful lights and is not a toy, then consider this unit. Head-to-head I prefer the sound on the Anker and as long as there is a little bit of room light I can work its controls just fine. The Beat Boom has much better lighting and it ultimately the easiest to use and very loud. The sound is good at this price point, but not the best. To get the best for the same price you would need to give up other features.

reviews.title: Great speaker! But don't make the mistake I did.
reviews.body: Purchased in February 2024. Great audio quality and high volume. If anything, I'd say the battery life isn't quite as long as the similar name brand products. My mistake: I was using a wall charger with a USB A to C adapter at the end of the charging cable. Bad mistake, because USB A doesn't carry enough power to charge this speaker properly. As a result, even though is appeared it was charging, my speaker started malfunctioning, and I eventually thought it was defective. As a last ditch effort, I found a high wattage Samsung USB C only charger and connected it to USB C only cable. Like magic, my speaker started charging, again. Problem solved. Works great now!

reviews.title: Under $80 Juggernaut (3 speaker battle)
reviews.body: was having a hard time choosing between this, and Oontz angle 3 Pro, and a Doss Soundbox Pro. Im looking for something primarily for the house to be used in a bedroom/office. EVERY SINGLE ONE WAS A WINNER and I wouldnt hesitate to choose any of the 3. Sound quality was very very....VERY comparable with each one and pretty much a wash (explained below). I dont like letting my batteries drain so I cant vouch for battery life on each one, but im not worried. Below is why I would choose each model, hopefully it helps you. Also if it matters, I listened to Radiohead-The National Anthem and Skrillex-Rumble to test the speakers. --Why I chose the Doss Soundbox Pro: I hate to admit it but the price....and I actually chose this one over the Tribit and Oontz after my sound tests. The sound was on par with the other 2 (similar wattage to the Oontz) and I liked this one just a hair more than the Oontz because it was a little crisper sounding where the Oontz was a little fuller...if that makes sense. So with the sound being the same, the fact that I could ALSO pair multiple Doss speakers for a multi speaker set up just like the Oontz (this is a great feature for when entertaining guests/having a small party/get-together), and considering I'd primarily be using this in a bedroom (where the powerbank wouldnt come in as handy like the Oontz has).....I had to choose this one. I didnt realize it was the cheapest until I had finished testing all 3 and went back to the invoice. This is the best bang for your buck speaker of the 3 and im big on value....but dont mind spending either if the value is there. --Why I would choose this speaker (Tribit Stormbox Micro 2): This one is the most travel friendly. Its the smallest and has a strap across the backside of it so you can easily attach it to a backpack, bike, UTV/ATV or any type of bar....the straps so tight to the body of the speaker that you can even put it on something as small as a car antenna and itd hold securely. Since the strap is snug to the body it stays secured. They dont list the wattage and this had the lowest wattage of the bunch at 10w compared to the other 2 at 20w/21w each.....but it was without a doubt equally as loud as the other two with trebles and bass being on par with the other two. Id really like to see how loud and clean a tribit with higher wattage sounds if this 10w speaker matched the higher wattage speakers I compared it to in my test. --Why I would choose the Oontz Angle 3 Pro instead: This one was the biggest and beefiest which I am a fan off....but I dont want you to think its a brick. its still plenty light where it wont feel like a burden lugging it around. This one also has a ocean/boat theme color pattern which is sweet and almost swayed me since i will be using this on my boat too. The other thing that almost swayed me was that the speaker can be used as a powerbank!!! So this ones sound is just as good as the other but the standout features are the looks, and the fact that it can be used as a powerbank which can come in very handy. Its not included but they have a bracket mount that clamps on to stuff.......not sure how it would hold up to movement and things like that but there is that option out there. These can also be paired with other Oontz speakers for a multi speaker set up. --Why I would choose the Doss Soundbox Pro: I hate to admit it but the price....and I actually chose this one over the Tribit and Oontz after my sound tests. I didnt realize it was the cheapest until I had finished testing all 3 and went back to the invoice. This is the best bang for your buck speaker of the 3 and im big on value....but dont mind spending either if the value is there.

reviews.title: A good unit with many features, and perhaps a tad pricey because of those features
reviews.body: In the world of Bluetooth speakers, this one struck me as a tad pricey, but not overly so. I am hoping for quality of build to let this thing last many years, and we'll see how that works. Meantime, the sound is nice. I use it mostly to listen to podcasts (including podcasts with music) and to stream stuff from Amazon music and Pandora, and the sound quality is OK for me for those purposes. I haven't used the bass emphasis button, finding I don't need that for what I listen to. The lighting feature is amusing, but I keep it off to lengthen battery life. The speakers provide a stereo sound, but I can't really discern a stereo result. Which is OK, I wasn't really expecting much in those regards, considering the speakers are so close to one another. The unit pairs with my iPhone extremely quickly. Haven't had it long enough to assess battery life (which can be a function of volume, use of lighting effects, use of the bass effect, and perhaps the phase of the moon). Overall, it meets my expectations fully and feels like it is well made.

reviews.title: Great little speaker!
reviews.body: This speaker is great. So far the battery life is superb and it gets very loud! I use this speaker in conjunction with a NUX Mighty Plug for guitar on the go. As expected with such a small speaker box the bass isn't extremely powerful but it sounds very crisp and full range if placed in the corner of a room with solid walls. I had a problem with the unit powering itself off at first until I realized it wasn't a low battery but an 'auto-off' feature when not playing anything. Searching this on the web, I didn't find anything on either their website or manual regarding an 'auto-off' feature for this model. Some suggested that DOSS has a firmware update available that disabled it. I spoke through email with a very nice person named Lizzie with their Customer Care team. Lizzie explained that units with the Version ID of VS3582 do not require any firmware updates to enable or disable this feature. If yours is a VS3582 then all you need to do in order to enable/disable the 'auto-off' feature is a button combo of Mode+Power and you'll see if flash red twice for off, green twice for on. Hold the bass button to cycle through lighting options (low, high, off). So far this little speaker has impressed me with what I intended to do with it and all my expectations are met. I am considering a 2nd one for stereo play! Hopefully Lizzie gets a raise soon

reviews.title: Stereopairing, Musik und Licht
reviews.body: VERPACKUNG: Nicht nur durch eine einfache Tüte wird die SoundBox Pro von DOSS geschützt, auch eine auf den Lautsprecher abgestimmte Kunststoffform ist im Karton. Ansonsten noch eine sehr gute Gebrauchsanweisung (auch Deutsch) ein USB A auf Micro USB Kabel und ein 3,5mm Klinke - Klinke Verbindungskabel. DESIGN: Der Lautsprecher ist umlaufend gummiert, an den kurzen Seiten könnte man Leder vermuten, es ist jedoch die Gummierung mit Ledermuster. Die Tasten sind gut erreichbar und haben einen gut spürbaren Druckpunkt. Kleine LEDs geben zusätzliche Info. Auf der Rückseite hinter der Gummideckung befinden sich Micro USB, 3,5mm Klinke und ein Micro SD Karten Anschluss. Vorn schützt ein Gitter die beiden aktiven und passiven Lautsprecher. Umlaufend befindet sich ein Kunststoffrahmen der von LEDs beleuchtet wird, sehr schick. FUNKTION: Vom Klang her ist die SoundBox Pro nicht zu unterschätzen. Die Lautstärke ist ordentlich und der Klang verzerrt minimal bei max Einstellung. Der Bass kommt gut rüber für so eine kleine Box, er ist eher mit einem Kickbass also knackig zu vergleichen. Langes gedröhne bekommt man wenn der Lautsprecher auf einer Unterlage platziert wird die etwas mitschwingen kann, z.B. Holztisch. Durch Equalizer Einstellungen am Handy kann man da aber noch einiges verändern. Das Stereopairing ist eine tolle Funktion die bei mir anstandslos funktioniert hat. Ich konnte keine Verzögerungen erkennen, es tritt auch kein Echo Effekt auf. Die Lichteffekte sind schön vor allem bei einer Gartenparty. Nachts kommen diese am besten zur Geltung. Für mich eine Funktion die sicherlich in einigen Situationen einen tollen Effekt hat (z.B. ruhige Musik abends auf dem Sofa mit pulsierenden LEDs). FAZIT: Ich möchte die Boxen nicht missen bei Kauf von zweien gab es einen Rabatt im Aktionszeitraum. Es macht auf jeden Fall Sinn hier zuzuschlagen und durch das Stereopairing eine tolle Klangkulisse zu schaffen. Sollte Bluetooth Mal nicht die richtige Wahl sein, kann man auch mit 3,5mm Klinge direkt verbinden (für Stereopairing immer mit dem master verbinden) oder alternativ Lieder auf Micro SD.
reviews.body_en: PACKAGING: The SoundBox Pro from DOSS is not only protected by a simple bag, there is also a plastic mold tailored to the speaker in the box. Otherwise there are very good instructions for use (also in German) a USB A to micro USB cable and a 3.5mm jack - jack connection cable. DESIGN: The speaker is rubberized all around, on the short sides you might suspect leather, but it is the rubber coating with a leather pattern. The keys are easy to reach and have a clearly noticeable pressure point. Small LEDs provide additional information. On the back behind the rubber cover there are Micro USB, 3.5mm jack and a Micro SD card port. At the front, a grille protects the two active and passive speakers. There is a plastic frame all around that is illuminated by LEDs, very stylish. FUNCTION: In terms of sound, the SoundBox Pro should not be underestimated. The volume is decent and the sound distorts minimally at max setting. The bass comes across well for such a small box, it can be compared to a kick bass so it's crisp. You get a long rumble if the speaker is placed on a surface that can vibrate a little, e.g. a wooden table. However, you can still change a lot using the equalizer settings on your cell phone. Stereo pairing is a great function that worked flawlessly for me. I couldn't detect any delays and there is no echo effect. The lighting effects are beautiful, especially at a garden party. These are best seen at night. For me, this is a function that certainly has a great effect in some situations (e.g. calm music in the evening on the sofa with pulsating LEDs). CONCLUSION: I don't want to miss the boxes. If I bought two, there was a discount during the promotional period. It definitely makes sense to go for it here and create a great soundscape through stereo pairing. If Bluetooth isn't the right choice, you can also connect directly to a 3.5mm blade (always connect to the master for stereo pairing) or alternatively songs on Micro SD.

reviews.title: Powerful, Personal, Portable Flex Speaker
reviews.body: The Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen speaker is hands down my favorite bluetooth speaker, though I do own the latest Beats Pill and love it for its capabilities. At present, I own eight of these 2nd Gen Flex speakers, one in each color variant. I do find that audiobooks, podcasts and spoken content sound best on the 2nd Gen Flex. Most Music does as well. Some reviewers report sound differences between the color variants. After initially suspecting this and repeatedly comparing the identical audio on each speaker, I found that the most likely explanation is how one is holding the speaker when audio is playing, as the audio does change based on the position of the speaker. Features I would like to see in the 3rd Gen model include: Much longer battery life. The technology and capabilities exist. The speaker is so excellent that paying a little more for much longer battery life, perhaps double, would be worth it. Lossless ability. When connecting the latest Bose Ultra headphones and even the Beats Pill to my iPhone with the Usb C to Usb C cables, each offer lossless streaming. The ability to connect the Flex to a CD player or some other audio device via the cable. There are Usb C to 3.5mm male and female cables on the market and this would be nice as I still have a small Bose CD player and plenty of CDs. While there are bluetooth transmitters such as the AirFly which make connectivity possible, direct wired connectivity is still nice for some of us. A detachable strap. The Beats Pill and the most excellent Bose SoundLink Micro 2nd Gen both offer a detachable strap. This would be a nice option for the Flex in the future. Pairing four Flex speakers in surround sound mode. While two Flex speakers are great in stereo, pairing four for surround sound would be next level great. The ability to change the volume of the obnoxious sounds the Flex puts out. I do like these sounds, particularly when the speaker connects to bluetooth. However, these are way too loud. The Beats Pill has the option of controlling the volume of its sounds. The same is true for the voice prompts. While some of the voice prompts can be disabled in the app, the volume cannot be changed. Even without these potential additions to a 3rd Gen Flex, this existing 2nd Gen Flex is a phenomenal bluetooth speaker that serves many purposes. The Alpine Sage color variant has been discontinued, as it was limited. However, the existing color options are excellent, particularly the Twilight Blue. Although the Flex and Beats Pill are both excellent and come down to personal preference when selecting one or the other, I would also go with the Flex if I did not have the luxury of owning both. In fact, I would go with the Flex over any other, even if it has yet to fulfill all its potential, which with the suggestions I mentioned for the 3rd Gen Flex, it would be an untouchable speaker. Highly recommend the 2nd Gen Flex to all reading this.

SIMPLIFY YOUR SETUP EVEN MORE. Integrated 3-channel mixer features two channels for microphones and instruments and one dedicated to music playback.

LEAVE THE CABLES BEHIND. Optional mic/line and instrument wireless RF transmitters pair effortlessly with the system’s integrated wireless RF receivers, and can be stored neatly in the speaker and charge (sold separately).

The Bose S1 Pro plus wireless PA system was rigorously tested and verified to provide up to 11 hours of battery life while playing music at room temperature from Spotify’s Global Top 50 at a comfortable volume that you can talk over while listening indoors. A singer/songwriter performing indoors for up to 100 people can expect to get 5 hours or more of battery life at performance-volume levels.

reviews.title: I FINALLY GOT THIS SPEAK AND LOVE IT!!!
reviews.body: The Bose S1 Pro+ Wireless Speaker is a masterful blend of portability, power, and premium sound quality, making it an excellent choice for musicians, DJs, and music enthusiasts alike. Bose has set a new standard with this portable PA system, offering unmatched versatility and audio excellence. Design & Portability The S1 Pro+ boasts a sleek, modern design that’s both professional and stylish. Its compact form factor and lightweight build make it incredibly easy to transport, while the integrated handle ensures a firm grip. Despite its portability, the speaker exudes durability and feels solid, a testament to Bose’s commitment to quality. Sound Quality True to the Bose name, the sound is where the S1 Pro+ truly shines. Crisp Highs, Full Mids, and Rich Lows: Whether you’re playing soft acoustic tracks or pumping out bass-heavy dance music, the speaker delivers with remarkable clarity and balance. 360° Sound Coverage: The unique design ensures even distribution, making it perfect for both intimate gatherings and larger events. Automatic EQ: The speaker adjusts itself to the environment and placement, ensuring optimal sound whether it’s on the ground, elevated, or tilted. Features & Functionality Wireless Connectivity: The S1 Pro+ comes with seamless Bluetooth pairing, making it easy to stream music from any device. Built-in Mixer: The integrated three-channel mixer with reverb and tone controls allows for quick adjustments, ideal for performers and presenters. Battery Performance: With a rechargeable battery offering up to 11 hours of playtime, this speaker ensures the music keeps going all day (or night). Expandable Options: Pairing with other Bose speakers is effortless, allowing for an even more immersive experience. Use Cases The Bose S1 Pro+ is incredibly versatile, excelling in: Live music performances. Outdoor parties and events. Corporate presentations. Small to medium-sized DJ gigs. Personal use for those who value top-tier sound. Pros Exceptional sound quality with Bose’s signature audio precision. Portable yet robust design. Easy-to-use controls and a built-in mixer for versatile applications. Long battery life for uninterrupted playtime. Cons Premium pricing might be a consideration for budget-conscious buyers. No dedicated app for advanced customization. Final Verdict The Bose S1 Pro+ is a game-changer in the portable speaker market. It combines professional-grade sound, user-friendly features, and unmatched portability, making it an excellent investment for performers, event organizers, and audiophiles. Its premium price is justified by its quality and versatility, ensuring it remains a favorite in any setting. Rating: 5/5 If you’re looking for a portable speaker that delivers uncompromising sound quality and functionality, the Bose S1 Pro+ is in a league of its own.

Crisp Highs, Full Mids, and Rich Lows: Whether you’re playing soft acoustic tracks or pumping out bass-heavy dance music, the speaker delivers with remarkable clarity and balance. 360° Sound Coverage: The unique design ensures even distribution, making it perfect for both intimate gatherings and larger events. Automatic EQ: The speaker adjusts itself to the environment and placement, ensuring optimal sound whether it’s on the ground, elevated, or tilted. Features & Functionality Wireless Connectivity: The S1 Pro+ comes with seamless Bluetooth pairing, making it easy to stream music from any device. Built-in Mixer: The integrated three-channel mixer with reverb and tone controls allows for quick adjustments, ideal for performers and presenters. Battery Performance: With a rechargeable battery offering up to 11 hours of playtime, this speaker ensures the music keeps going all day (or night). Expandable Options: Pairing with other Bose speakers is effortless, allowing for an even more immersive experience. Use Cases The Bose S1 Pro+ is incredibly versatile, excelling in: Live music performances. Outdoor parties and events. Corporate presentations. Small to medium-sized DJ gigs. Personal use for those who value top-tier sound. Pros Exceptional sound quality with Bose’s signature audio precision. Portable yet robust design. Easy-to-use controls and a built-in mixer for versatile applications. Long battery life for uninterrupted playtime. Cons Premium pricing might be a consideration for budget-conscious buyers. No dedicated app for advanced customization. Final Verdict The Bose S1 Pro+ is a game-changer in the portable speaker market. It combines professional-grade sound, user-friendly features, and unmatched portability, making it an excellent investment for performers, event organizers, and audiophiles. Its premium price is justified by its quality and versatility, ensuring it remains a favorite in any setting. Rating: 5/5 If you’re looking for a portable speaker that delivers uncompromising sound quality and functionality, the Bose S1 Pro+ is in a league of its own.

title: JBL Charge 6 - Portable Waterproof & Drop-Proof Bluetooth Speaker, Bold JBL Pro Sound & AI Sound Boost, 28Hrs Playtime, Built-in powerbank & Comes with a Sturdy/Removable Carrying Strap (Black/Teal)
bullet_points: Surprisingly rich, powerful bass & crisp higher frequencies give the Charge 6 a whole new reason to humble brag. New proprietary tech, AI Sound Boost, which analyzes your music in realtime to deliver maximum acoustic performance with less distortion.

Up to 28 hours of playtime: Keep the mood alive for 24 hours on a single charge - and when we really need to squeeze some extra juice out of our jubilee, or another dance with our darling, we can get an extra 4 hours with JBL Playtime Boost.

Wouldn't it be great to share the vibes with our tribe? Now we can. With Auracast, we can effortlessly stereo pair two Charge 6 speakers for a wider sound stage & connect multiple Auracast-enabled JBL speakers to cover more ground with the same playlist.
On top of our legendary water-proof and dust-proof design (an industry-leading IP68, BTW), we've also made sure that if you drop it from 1-meter onto your concrete floor, it'll keep kicking.

Why is there no USB-C charging cable included with my product? To minimize e-waste, we consciously choose not to include a charging cable in our packaging. However, you can use any standard USB-C cable to charge your JBL product.

reviews.title: Reliable Performance with Refined Improvements
reviews.body: Overall Impression This is my second speaker from the JBL Charge line, and once again, I’m impressed. The Charge 6 builds on what already worked well in previous models while delivering dependable performance, strong sound quality, and easy usability. Design & Build Quality The speaker feels sturdy and well-constructed without being overly bulky. It’s portable, easy to move around, and sits securely on a variety of surfaces. Whether placed on a kitchen counter, coffee table, or taken outdoors, it feels durable enough for everyday use. Setup & Connectivity Setup is quick and straightforward. I’ve had no issues pairing the Charge 6 with any of my devices. Bluetooth connection is stable and reliable, something I really value, as I’ve owned other speakers that occasionally failed to appear or dropped connection. In this area, the Charge 6 performs consistently well. Sound Quality For a speaker in this price range, the sound quality is impressive. Volume: Gets surprisingly loud for its size. Clarity: Remains stable and clear even at higher volumes, with minimal distortion. Bass: Punchy and full without overpowering the mids and highs. Vocals: Crisp and easy to distinguish. The overall sound profile feels balanced and energetic, making it versatile for different genres of music. Compared to the JBL Charge 5 I upgraded from the Charge 5, which already delivered excellent sound. The difference here isn’t dramatic, but the Charge 6 feels slightly louder and punchier, with a bit more fullness at higher volumes. It’s more of a refinement than a complete redesign, but a noticeable and appreciated one. Ideal Use Cases This speaker is well-suited for small to medium-sized rooms and performs great for small outdoor gatherings or backyard settings. I liked it enough to purchase a second unit and place one in each corner of my living space for a more balanced, room-filling setup. The stereo pairing through the JBL Portable app is simple and works seamlessly. Whenever I have friends over, the sound quality consistently gets compliments. Battery Life JBL advertises up to 24 hours of playback (tested at 50% volume). In my experience, listening at around 60% volume yields approximately 17–19 hours on a single charge, which has been more than sufficient for daily use. If I had one minor critique, it would be that battery life drops more noticeably at very high volumes. For example, during an all-day beach trip or extended outdoor event where the speaker is running near maximum volume, you may need to recharge sooner than expected. That said, for normal day-to-day listening and typical gatherings, battery performance has been dependable and not a deal breaker for me. Final Verdict The JBL Charge 6 delivers strong, punchy sound, reliable connectivity, and solid battery performance in a durable, portable design. While the upgrade from the Charge 5 isn’t dramatic, it’s a meaningful refinement. Overall, it’s a great value for the performance it provides and an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a versatile Bluetooth speaker.

reviews.title: The Ultimate Audio Wingman: Why the JBL Charge 6 Brings the Boom Without the Bulk!
reviews.body: We all know that feeling of finding the perfect piece of gear that just clicks with our lifestyle, and that is exactly what happened when I got my hands on the JBL Charge 6. In a sea of portable speakers that overpromise and underdeliver, this crisp, white beauty stands out as a true heavyweight in a surprisingly compact package. I am always on the move, whether I am out working in the garage, heading to the beach, or just kicking back by the backyard fire pit, and I need a device that can keep up. What struck me immediately about this particular model is how it completely redefines what a mid-sized portable speaker should be capable of handling. It is not just about making noise; it is about delivering a premium experience that seamlessly integrates into whatever crazy adventure my weekend throws at me. ​Let us talk about the absolute core of this device: the sound. The Bold JBL Pro Sound alone is phenomenal, but the real magic here is the AI Sound Boost technology. I have listened to countless audio setups, and I can confidently say that this proprietary audio processing algorithm fundamentally changes the game. It actively analyzes the music in real-time, pulling maximum acoustic performance out of the drivers while keeping distortion virtually non-existent, even when you crank the volume all the way up. The low-end bass kicks with a satisfying, punchy depth that you can feel in your chest, while the mids and highs remain exceptionally crisp and clear. Whether I am blasting classic rock anthems or heavy hip-hop tracks, the soundstage feels massive, filling up the entire patio or living room with rich, immersive audio that makes you forget you are listening to a portable unit. ​Now, an incredible-sounding speaker is useless to me if I have to baby it, which is why the rugged build of the Charge 6 is such a massive win. This thing is built like an absolute tank. It boasts serious waterproof and drop-proof credentials, meaning I never sweat it when a sudden rainstorm rolls in or when someone inevitably knocks it off the picnic table. I have watched it take a tumble directly onto hard concrete and brush it off like it was nothing, keeping the tunes rolling without a single hiccup. Adding to its utilitarian charm is the newly integrated, sturdy removable carrying strap. It sounds like a minor detail, but having that secure strap makes hauling it around infinitely easier. I can sling it over a bag, hang it from a hook in the workshop, or just keep a solid grip on it while hiking, all without compromising its sleek, streamlined white aesthetic. ​Perhaps the most crucial factor for a device that travels this much is endurance, and the battery life on the Charge 6 is nothing short of legendary. JBL packed this beast with up to 28 hours of playtime, and it absolutely delivers on that promise. I have taken it on multi-day camping trips and never once had to reach for a wall charger. But the absolute lifesaver is the built-in powerbank feature. We all know how fast smartphones drain when streaming high-quality music outdoors, so having the ability to plug my phone directly into the speaker to juice it back up while the playlist keeps pumping is incredibly practical. It is the ultimate two-in-one companion that ensures neither the party nor my phone dies prematurely. This speaker does not just meet my high standards for portable audio; it utterly shatters them.

reviews.title: Honest review of the JBL Charge 6 portable bluetooth speaker
reviews.body: At almost 60 years old, I’ve experienced just about every kind of audio system imaginable — component stereo systems, high-end car audio setups, premium headphones, earbuds, home theater systems, and portable speakers from many of the biggest brands. Because of that, it takes quite a bit to genuinely impress me when it comes to sound quality. The JBL Charge 6 absolutely impressed me. What JBL accomplished with this speaker is remarkable. The sound is incredibly powerful considering such a small footprint. This thing is compact enough to fit easily into almost any backpack, yet it produces bold, room-filling sound that feels much larger than the speaker itself. The audio quality is excellent. The highs are crystal clear, vocals sound clean and detailed, and the bass is deep, punchy, and robust without sounding muddy or distorted. Even at higher volumes, the sound remains balanced and enjoyable. The volume range is outstanding — this speaker gets surprisingly loud while still maintaining clarity. I’ve owned expensive audio equipment over the years, and honestly, the sound coming from this little speaker is shocking for its size. Whether indoors, outdoors, traveling, relaxing at home, or using it near water, the JBL Charge 6 consistently delivers an impressive listening experience. Bluetooth connectivity is fast and simple, and the portability is one of its biggest strengths. JBL also did a great job with durability. The waterproof and drop-proof design makes it ideal for everyday life, travel, and outdoor use without constantly worrying about damaging it. Battery life and durability seem to vary somewhat based on user experiences. Many people report excellent battery life that lasts all day, while others feel it could be better depending on usage and volume levels. Most users praise the rugged build quality, though a few have experienced durability concerns after heavy use. Overall, this speaker exceeded my expectations. After decades of owning and listening to high-end audio equipment, I can honestly say the JBL Charge 6 delivers an incredible amount of performance, clarity, and power for such a compact portable speaker. Small speaker. Massive sound. Very impressive product from JBL.

reviews.title: Fun, safe smart speaker for my little one – the Anthro Pup design is a hit!
reviews.body: Got the Echo Pop Kids in the Anthro Pup design (that cool dog with headphones and shades) for my 6-year-old, and it’s been a game-changer for bedtime and playtime. Setup was straightforward through the Alexa app—created a child profile, set parental controls (time limits, content filters, activity monitoring), and the included 6 months of Amazon Kids+ kicked in right away. Sound is surprisingly good for such a compact, rounded speaker—clear vocals for stories, music from kid-safe playlists, and Alexa answers questions appropriately without adult content. The silicone sleeve feels durable and kid-proof, plus there’s a physical mic-off button for extra privacy peace of mind. My son loves asking for bedtime stories, animal facts, jokes, or playing songs—he’s obsessed with the pup look and calls it his “DJ buddy.” We’ve used it daily for routines like morning alarms or homework help skills. No issues with connectivity or quality after a couple months. At $49.99 with the free Kids+ trial (worth about $30), it’s a great value compared to bigger Echo Dot Kids models. Highly recommend for ages 3-10ish—perfect balance of fun and parent-approved safety

reviews.title: A Perfect Kids' Companion: Amazon Echo Pop Kids (Newest Gen)
reviews.body: I recently got the Amazon Echo Pop Kids (newest gen) for my child, and it's been a fantastic addition to our home. This smart speaker is specifically designed for kids, and it offers a great blend of fun, functionality, and parental control. First off, the design is really appealing for children. It comes in a range of vibrant colors and has a fun, kid-friendly aesthetic that fits well in any child's room. The compact size is perfect for smaller spaces, and it doesn’t take up much room on a shelf or bedside table. The sound quality is impressive for its size. The Echo Pop Kids delivers clear and crisp audio, making it great for playing music, audiobooks, and interactive stories. The speaker also handles voice commands well, allowing kids to easily ask for their favorite songs or information. One of the standout features is the robust parental controls. The Alexa Kids interface offers a range of safety settings, including content filters and time limits, which give parents peace of mind. You can manage what content your child has access to and ensure they’re using the device in a safe and controlled manner. Additionally, the Echo Pop Kids includes fun, educational content and skills tailored for children. It provides access to interactive games, quizzes, and stories that can keep kids entertained and engaged. The speaker also supports routines, which can help with setting up bedtime reminders or daily routines in a fun way. Overall, the Amazon Echo Pop Kids (newest gen) is a fantastic choice for families with young children. It combines engaging features with strong parental controls, making it a practical and enjoyable device for kids. Highly recommend for a fun and educational addition to your child’s tech collection!

reviews.title: Where have you been since I started cooking (age 15 now 52)? Thank YOU Dalstrong for caring!

reviews.title: Amazing set for the price
reviews.body: Since you're looking at this particular set, I'm going to guess you've probably set a limit to how much you want to spend on what's likely going to be your every day set of knives. You might own more expensive (and arguably better) knives, but you’d rather not see them used by anyone who is not as concerned as you are with their integrity and longevity. You’ve also seen first hand the difference between the Wusthof Gourmet series and the classic Wusthof, and you also know Henkel doesn’t quite cut it. If I guessed right and you’re considering buying this set for these or similar reasons, do not hesitate: buy it right now! These knives are a cut above your usual value knife sets. Cool, sexy looks, sharp blades that stay sharp, full tang, well balanced overall, sturdy but ergonomic handles with no sharp lines. They even sound great - you know, that tuning fork ring they make if you just give them a gentle tap - so it’s really easy to pick up the right knife with eyes closed if you have perfect pitch! :P Everything most knives in this price range aren’t. I actually ended up liking these knives so much I now use them more often than my Global set. This is not to say the Globals are not the superior knives, it’s just that these Dalstrong knives are *perfectly fine* for most things someone who cooks for pleasure and not for a living will find themselves using them for. I will say that one of the knives I received had a small flaw - a crack in the side of the handle that looks like it occurred on riveting. I contacted Dalstrong support. Three days later I had the replacement. No runaround, no BS. They looked at the pictures I sent and just replied asking for my shipping address. Honestly, how often does that happen? (Thanks Rachelle for the terrific customer support experience!) You may rest assured that whatever issue you have with the product, they’ll make it right. I believe other reviews mentioned the awesome customer support as well, and I can confirm these guys really stand by their product. After the very positive experience with this set, I do think I’ll try some of their more premium knives soon (they’re still not even close to premium-priced). In short: These are value-priced knives that have none (or close to none) of the shortcomings you’d expect for the price, while blowing some of the established choices out of the water in some regards. Certainly the modern, streamlined looks will strike some conversations (yes, I know, that’s highly subjective).

reviews.title: High quality knife set
reviews.body: I received the Dalstrong Gladiator knife set a couple of weeks ago and I am very pleased with this purchase. I am not a professional chef, nor do I play one on TV, but I do enjoy cooking and good tools make the process that much more enjoyable. Whenever I see an item on line that interests me, I always read the reviews starting with the worst ratings first. There aren’t many for this product, which was a good sign, and those that were there didn’t appear to be major issues. The 85% of 5 star reviews should give a good indication of the level of customer satisfaction. I’ve used various knives from the set (not all yet) every day since getting them. My observations are they are very well designed with a pleasing appearance, they are well crafted and well balanced, they feel good in the hand and are easy to handle, and they are sharp. With the quality steel used in the design I imagine these knives should last a very long time with minimal maintenance. Some comments spoke of shoddy workmanship on the wood handles or fittings. I did not find this to be the case as all the handles match up to the metal tang of the blade perfectly. The mounting block is a fine piece of woodwork and I can see no issues with it. It is big and heavy, but I’ve received compliments on it from friends. I agree with one other post that recommended not using a green pad to clean the knives, or any knives for that matter. I also never put knives through the dishwasher and occasionally wipe them down with cooking oil to maintain the surface. But that’s me. I did not comment on durability as I have had this set for a minimal amount of time. I would be surprised if they failed to deliver over the long haul and will comment further should they not. Overall, this set is aesthetically pleasing and does very well what it is supposed to do. I highly recommend this Dalstrong set.

reviews.title: What a Huge Difference
reviews.body: First, we could not be more pleased with this 18 piece "Gladiator" set of knifes; across the board the appearance, craftsmanship, weight/balance, sharpness, and block (which is huge BTW) are all top shelf! Further, I can honestly tell you all that I have never written a product review before so that should tell you that I am really impressed. Disclaimer/Quality: I must admit I have never owned a high quality set of knives before (thought a Faberware Set in a block was high quality--NOT!), but I cannot imagine a better set of knives for the novice/wannabe Chef's like my Fiance' and I. Until we got this set, we never really thought about using different types of knives for the various areas of cooking/prepping in the kitchen. Our AHA moment came when we discovered/realized that using the right type of knife for the job, and the reasons why, make all the difference--I assure you it does! So much so, that we now have the picture and description that Dalstrong provided taped up over the block and give each other a hard time if either of us use the wrong knife for the task. :o) Price/Value: In my opinion, even at $399.00, it truly is an amazing price for a potentially lifetime set of knives. So you know, we also ordered the Gladiator series Meat Cleaver with the set. All I can say about this meat cleaver is Holy $#!%! I took one look at this thing and immediately thought it should be registered as a lethal weapon! Not only is it extremely well crafted and gorgeous, this thing is very big, razor sharp and weighs a ton--I told my Fiance' that I needed to start working out just to be able to wield it properly. Bottom Line: Great job Dalstrong--Keep up the great work and reasonable price points--I am already looking for more Gladiator Series knives.

reviews.title: We’ll see.
reviews.body: Received the set today. With that in mind, I’m writing the review about the individual set that I got, not the Dalstrong product line. Delivery: The knives came individually wrapped and tip-protected. The set split between 3 boxes, the block and 2 boxes packed with knives. All neatly packed. Each knife, as I said, with a plastic tip protector, sheathed in cardboard and wrapped in bubble wrap. In my case, observing the packaging that I received, it’s beyond me how could anyone cut their fingers to the bone unwrapping, as some reviewers said they did. Construction: Superb. Simply superb. No lose parts, no unfinished surfaces. I’m not sure where other reviewers found “sharp edges”, in mynindividual case - superb construction. Block: again, having read other reviews I was expecting sloppy glue job, cracks in the block etc. What I received is far from that - a superb block. Yes, the logo is plastic. I don’t care. The block is hard wood. Nicely finished. Period. The socket for the sharpening iron is a bit through - that’s what gives you the clue, it’s wood. Not plastic glued witn veneer. It is solid wood. Balance. I’m not a professional, rather an amateur chef, but I cook for the family of 5 a lot. And I mean it - a LOT. I love it and yo me working with a good tool in the kitchen is as important as cooking a lamb kabob to juiciest perfection. These knives are very well balanced. The 8” chef just asks to put it in action right away - the weight of the knife is right there, comfortably fit in your hand. I chopped up 3 onions with it just for the pleasure of the experience. Bagged the onion - will put it to a good use tomorrow. Again, right out of the box, the knives that matter are reasonably sharp (and not excessively), offer good balance and are nice looking tools all around. Bottom lime: great delivery. Great packaging. Awesome set. I cannot speak for the long term performance just yet. Having read some other reviews that claim that the blades developed rust, I resolved to hard washing and wiping the blades with a lightly oiled paper towel. Something I do anyway. Will update if detwct any issues going forward. That’s why I keep the “durability” section vacant our now.

reviews.title: 9 years later - still slicing
reviews.body: I bought this set 9 years ago. After using them thrice daily cooking for a family of five they're still great! I have obviously sharpened them, several times, over the years, but the handles and block still look good. The honing tool also works well between sharpening sessions. The knives are well balanced and the grips are a comfortable shape and size. No rust has ever occurred on the knives, but I always clean and dry them quickly after use. I wish this set came with a carving fork, but I didn't know that it I wanted that 9 years ago.

reviews.title: Best knives I have purchased to this day
reviews.body: OK guys hello! And welcome to my review! I will inform you that I purchased a white set 18 piece block and upon arrival it was like any other Amazon package. I read the reviews and was quite amazed at some reactions. I have only owned them for 3 weeks so far, no I have not ridden over them, jumped on them or thrown them off the roof and had them break..... I unpacked them and the block from the boxes and the knives were sharp enough to cut my arm hair with just grazing them. That was a pretty good start. The block itself is very smooth, nice wood cuts. Love the finish on it and fits on the counter with finesse. Once I set the block up I was eager to try out the knives. The ergonomics of the these knives are great, they fit well. Smooth, not bulky, and easy to adhere to. Tried the 🍅 test with the chef knife and it passed, the paper test needed some more testing but they are great. I have used the slicing knife for chicken and brisket, I have used the chef knife for all my general slicing, steak knives for steak and they are all.performing above the expectation for the price!. This set is a must have for your kitchen, seriously authentically pleasing, comfortable, and great to use. One con is they shouldn't go into the dishwasher and that they have to be cleaned and dried. They shouldn't be left in the sink for too long. So overall I would recommend these knives to intermediate/ expert level cooks just for daily house hold cooking and outings. Though you do need to sharpen them after a week of use. Easy to sharpen though. They recommend a whet stone from their shop, but the rod works fine.

reviews.title: Un magnifique produit et des couteaux de qualité.
reviews.body: J'ai acheté ce produit (en promotion )et la qualité des couteaux Gladiator est élevée avec un tranchant et une dureté exceptionnelle. je n'aurai jamais mis la somme de 1000 € demandée au départ... Le lot de couteaux est homogène avec 3 rivets sur les manches et une magnifique finition. Le maintien des couteaux et la qualité des manche est du haut de gamme avec une garantie à vie. Le Bloc en noyer est lui aussi magnifique mais nous avons dû retourner l'ensemble car le bloc bois était fendu. C'est hélas ne soucis récurrent de ce type de bloc. Nous avons retourné le produit et pris un ensemble Dalstrong avec 6 couteaux pour un rangement bois magnétique de 12 couteaux moins imposant. D'ailleurs on voit les couteaux en permanence ce qui est plus pratique et plus sympa. Les couteaux sont encore d'une gamme plus élevée (Phantom). Dommage pour le bloc bois, bien fini avec tampon en dessous. Le retour s'est fait sans soucis. On est vraiment sur de vrais couteaux durables loin de ce qui peut être proposé dans des ensembles bien "jolie" mais à la durabilité faible.
reviews.body_en: I bought this product (on promotion) and the quality of Gladiator knives is high with exceptional sharpness and hardness. I would never have spent the sum of €1000 requested at the start... The set of knives is uniform with 3 rivets on the handles and a magnificent finish. The maintenance of the knives and the quality of the handles is top of the range with a lifetime guarantee. The walnut block is also magnificent but we had to return the whole thing because the wooden block was split. Unfortunately, this is a recurring problem with this type of block. We returned the product and took a Dalstrong set with 6 knives for a less imposing magnetic wooden storage of 12 knives. Besides, we see the knives all the time, which is more practical and nicer. The knives are of an even higher range (Phantom). Too bad for the wooden block, well finished with stamp underneath. The return was hassle-free. We are really looking at real durable knives, far from what can be offered in very “pretty” sets but with poor durability.

reviews.title: Outstanding product, even better customer service.
reviews.body: The first set that arrived had a minor (and I mean minor) finishing flaw which niggled at me enough to make mention of it to the seller, wow! This seller goes above and beyond in satisfying their customers, this is the sort of customer service that major companies only dream about, they are truly top tier! The knives themselves I have been using for a couple of weeks or so and they are showing no signs of wear and tear, keeping a sharp edge and haven’t even needed to see a steel let alone a sharpener yet. On top of that the block looks great on the worktop, even the wife was impressed after whinging about the cost lol. I would highly recommend this product and I will purchase from this company for the rest of my life so long as they keep up their standards as I was so highly impressed with the care they gave me as a customer. In fact I have already lined up my next purchase ‘the Obliterator’ cleaver which is part of this range. Honestly I am so happy...of course if the knives start showing signs of rust or ruin within an unreasonable time frame I will update this review.

reviews.title: Sehr schöne wertige Messer
reviews.body: Es gibt nicht viel zu erzählen, Sehr scharfe Messer mit tollen Design. Schöne Verarbeitung ohne optische Fehler. Messer liegen sehr gut in der Hand. Dazu ein schöner Messerblock der das Gesamtbild aufwertet. Preisleistung für mich als Hobbykoch top. Über die Haltbarkeit kann ich noch nicht viel sagen. Habe die Messer ja gerade erst neu. Nur eine Anmerkung an den Hersteller/Versender: Es sollte nicht so offensichtlich sein was im Karton versendet wird. Meine Karton wurde geöffnet und wieder schlampig verklebt. Es wurde wahrscheinlich nur nichts gestohlen weil die Verpackung der Messer noch in Folie verschweißt waren.
reviews.body_en: There's not much to say, very sharp knives with a great design. Nice workmanship with no optical defects. Knives feel very comfortable in the hand. There is also a beautiful knife block that enhances the overall picture. Great value for money for me as a hobby chef. I can't say much about durability yet. I just got the knives new. Just a note to the manufacturer/shipper: It shouldn't be so obvious what is being shipped in the box. My box was opened and sloppily taped again. It's probably just that nothing was stolen because the knife packaging was still sealed in foil.

The knives themselves are gorgeous looking with beautiful wooden handles which are obviously ergonomic. They definitely add to the richness of the kitchen and the knives themselves ooze quality. They can give a run to my branded knife sets any time as the three knives amongst themselves can take care of all my kitchen needs from cutting meats (chicken and fish), vegetables and fruits or breads and cakes you name it. The blades are very sharp and one has to be quite careful but the grip is amazing and that give you the sense of safety that you need when handling these. Once I am done my job with these, I wash them in warm water with soap, rinse and wipe them off. I do have several knife sharpeners so once the blade gets dull I can always polish them. I do recommend as the price is almost one third of my branded set but does the same job.

reviews.title: Great value, nice edge
reviews.body: I recently received the Shinobi Chef Knife Set by Cutluxe, and I am very impressed with their performance and craftsmanship. This 3-piece set includes a chef knife, a santoku knife, and a paring knife, all designed with Japanese-inspired aesthetics and razor-sharp blades. The first thing I noticed was how incredibly sharp they are, they literally glides through vegetables, meats, and fish without any resistance. The high-carbon stainless steel used in the blades makes them durable, and I can already tell they’ll last me a long time. The ergonomic Pakkawood handles not only look great, they are comfortable to hold, giving me great control while chopping or slicing. I also appreciate the full tang design, which ensures the knives feel solid and well-balanced in my hands, even when performing more delicate tasks. The knives feel and look professional at a great price point. Cleaning them is a breeze, and they maintain their sharpness after several uses. Honestly, I was skeptical, but after using them, I can confidently say these are great knives. If you’re looking for knives that combine beauty with performance at a reasonable price, this set is definitely a solid choice.

reviews.title: Fantastic quality for such a low price !!
reviews.body: Now, to be quite frank, I don’t treat my kitchen knives very well. I do tend to throw them in the dishwasher, not store them properly and forget to sharpen the blade most of the time, so I cannot be trusted with fancy expensive knives. I did need to get some new ones, and I decided to give this set of 3 a try, and i am NOT disappointed. I didn’t expect much from these when I ordered because of the low price, but i am so so pleasantly surprised by the quality of the knives ! They come in a nice sturdy box ( great for a gift ! ), and I was just baffled by the knives themselves. They have good weight to them, and the blades are well made, sharp, and not too thick. With the 3 knifes, you can literally cut anything in the kitchen. The handles aren’t the best, but that’s to be expected because of the low price, but they are still so easy to handle and manipulate. Overall, if you are looking for a great set of knives for a low price, this is absolutely it.

All over the listing it says Japanese and has a Japanese name on it, but it's really just made in China with unknown steel source. Easy to wash with warm soapy water. Should last a decent bit but definitely not the sharpest or highest quality knives you can get.

reviews.title: Great set, review after a year of use
reviews.body: I've had this knife set for over a year now. I have no cons to it at all. I use the honing rod probably every other time I use the big chef knives, and they're still as sharp and beautiful as the first day I got them. Every single knife is sturdy and feels solid. I hand wash all the sharp blades, but I do run the serrated ones through my dishwasher sometimes because I'm lazy 😅. I like that the prep knives lay on their sides in the block, I think that protects the blades better. The steak knives fit in vertically, but I just put them in upside down so they don't rest on the cutting edge. I don't like how close the honing rod is to the bread knife right below it, but that's not too big of a deal. The knives and block look beautiful on my counter, and everything seems to be great quality. I am glad I bought this and am considering buying one for my daughter.

reviews.title: Decent quality blades that are easy to keep sharp
reviews.body: The steel is arguably soft, but that is typical of european (particularly german) blades. The iron content of this stainless steel is high and the nickel content may be low. If left wet for long, it may develop rust spots. However, you should always clean and dry a knife after using it anyway. If taken care of, these blades will last many years. They will cut what you want and retain a nice shape. The chef's knife is great. It is the primary knife used in my kitchen. It is comfortable to use, slices through most anything with relative ease. After about ten to fifteen diced onions I like to hone the blade again to keep work quick and easy. A dull knife is much more dangerous than a sharp one they say. Despite frequent maintenance, it does an excellent job and doesn't fatigue me. The santokus are of decent quality, and feel excellent for everyday tasks. The larger one has a good weight and feeling allowing for prolonged veggie extermination, and the smaller one is light and maneuverable to really slice and shape whatever you need. The paring knife is a razor blade with a handle basically. If the chef knife is too big or unwieldy for a task, the lil guy will step up with no issue. The bread knife is sharp. It WILL cut bread. Cake too, I bet. There is another smaller serrated knife but I have yet to use it. The scissors are nothing special but provide you something to open any package of food. The steak knives are beautiful but have lesser quality steel than the bigger knives. These will straight up form rust spots if left in the sink overnight, esp along the handle and spine of the blade. Just clean them after use and they should stay pretty and sharp for ya. The included file is useful to keep my blades honed. I'd say this set is a pretty solid value for your money if you are looking for a good set of knives for the kitchen. If you don't sharpen your knives or prefer a cheap kitchenaid knife, this isn't for you. For the home cook who uses their knives for everything and appreciates them, I recommend them.

reviews.title: 200 reasons to skip washing the butter knife.
reviews.body: These are good quality for disposable knives. They’re sturdy, heavy duty, BPA-free, and heat resistant, so they can handle both hot and cold foods without feeling flimsy. They’re definitely nice enough for parties, cookouts, and other events, but honestly, that’s not why I got them. In my house, apparently nobody wants to wash the butter knives after using them, so I decided to solve the problem! Now here’s 200 reasons why nobody (ME!) has to for the moment lol! For everyday home use, having a big supply of sturdy disposable knives is just convenient. For 200 in the pack, I think they’re a decent bulk value and exactly what the main in the house dishwasher (Me again!) calls for. One buying note: the presentation you receive is much more basic than what’s pictured online. I received them in plain brown cardboard with no identifying graphics, just a small sticker and barcode on the side indicating what the item is. So if you’re expecting the presentation shown in the listing, just be aware that what you receive may look quite different.
