reviews.title: Perfect for Camping and Gatherings
reviews.body: These knives are a great value. They aren't quite as heavy-duty as some of the more expensive name-brand disposable options, but they are noticeably better than many similarly priced plastic knives I've tried in the past. Those tended to be flimsy, undersized, and prone to bending, while these feel sturdy enough for everyday use. I brought some along on a recent camping trip and was pleasantly surprised that they had no trouble cutting through steak. (Although, to be fair, I deserve some credit for cooking a pretty good steak.) It was convenient not having to dig out my metal knives and then deal with cleaning them afterward. My only minor complaint is that the clear plastic on the business end has a slightly wavy appearance. It doesn't affect performance at all, but it is noticeable if you look closely. Then again, if your guests are closely inspecting the appearance of your disposable knives at a gathering, you probably should have used the metal ones in the first place. Overall, these are a solid choice for parties, camping, picnics, or any situation where you want a durable disposable knife without paying a premium.

reviews.title: High quality steel. Holds an edge.
reviews.body: Meet cleavers are not just for cutting meat. I have had this knif for around a year. This is the best knife I have ever used for cutting ALL my food, not just meat. All the reviews that wrote that they can't get a sharp edge on it, don't know how to sharpen a knife! This is one of the easiest knives I've ever sharpened. I use a chefs rod sharpener and it come out very sharp EVERY time. If you don't know how to sharpen a knife, that is one thing. But don't write that it is a cheap knife that won't get a sharp edge just because you don't know how to sharpen a high quility carbon steel cleaver. And the review that said that it is to heavy, that he will be using it instead to chop wood, doesn't realize that all good quality cleavers are heavy like this. News flash. This is a meat cleaver. If you want a ax, go buy an ax. I have used it at least sixty times to cut food for dinner. This knife is made of fantastic high carbon stainless steel. It should be at least three times the price. That's how good this knife is. It also comes with a thick, good quality leather sheath. It is relitvly easy to sharpen. It really holds an edge incredably, once sharpened. The steel is not to hard where it becomes brittle. It's also not to soft where it won't hold an edge. The hardness is just the correct balance. It holds an edge better than my $150 great brand camping knife. Once the food is cut on my chopping block, I can easily scrap up the food onto the side of the knife, having the blade go under the side of my hand and pushing it onto the knife then picking up the food and putting it into a bowl, frying pan ect., just the way the chefs do in Chinese restaurants. It is much more efficient that way. That is what makes this a much better option for cutting ALL my food, rather than using a regular chefs knife. I know. I used to be a chef in a five star restaurant in CT. This knife is just as good as the expensive $140 knives that were bought from a restayrant supply company for the restaurant I worked at . So, buy it. You won't be disappointed with it!!!

reviews.title: A perfect addition to my kitchen
reviews.body: While visiting my sister, I used her set of Cuisinart knifes. She place the time of purchase somewhere between 5 and 7 years, and they were wonderful. Easy to handle, not to heavy, and a great variety of knives for cutting different types of foods. The steak knives are the best I have ever used, the Santoku (the blade is wide in height and snub nosed) cut a left over roast into very, very thin slices for hot roast beef sandwiches. In early July, I purchased the Classic Forged Triple Riveted set of 15 knives and the block, because the set held most of the knives I was looking for and they fit right into my kitchen décor. And, my struggle of 59 years in my kitchen, trying to cut vegetables, fruits, meats and breads and struggling with knives has come to an end. It is such a mental and physical relieve to start a meal knowing that cutting "whatever" will no longer be a struggle. My new knives are the best I have ever purchased and I have purchased a lot of knives. Wish I had know a long time ago about Cuisinart knives, didn't know that they made anything but electric appliances for the kitchen. A little bit of a down side, be prepared for a larger than normal knife holding block, and it is heavy, but again the length of the knives make it necessary and are worth the block size and weight. Would I recommend them to my best friend.....in a heart beat! But...would I purchase this set again, no, but I would purchase the solid metal handle set, as the paring knife handle has cracked from the rivet to the edge of the handle. I care for my knives, I hand wash and dry them and put them away, I am concerned that if one handle cracks after a month and a half of use, how long before another on cracks. Overall, I would have given this set of knives a 5 star except for the cracked handle.

reviews.title: Beautiful set.
reviews.body: This is a very nice mid-range kitchen knife set. The steel used is actually named and is a good solid stainless steel that's a good balance for a set like this. The handles are beautiful and look high-end. The only thing I find a little odd is the scissors. The little swivel lock fell out and the spring disappeared somewhere in the kitchen within the first week of use. They still work OK but seem a bit over-complicated for kitchen scissors. They blades are very sharp out of box - so be careful. A little warning for you all if you get these - and I'm embarrassed to even discuss this: When you fill the knife block with the knives - make sure the sharp side of the big knives are all turned to the middle of the block. Otherwise - the sharp end hangs out over the edge of the block and is a significant danger. I loaded the knives without thinking about that and reached around the block at one point and got the top of my right thumb with the heal of one of the big knives that I loaded backwards. It got me good. I'll always have a scar there now. It was stupid and completely my mistake - so don't do the same thing. Be careful. the only blades that shouldn't have the sharp end pointing to the middle of the block would be the steak knives at the bottom. Those can be loaded with the sharp end down. The block will cover the apex just fine when loaded that way. Anyhow - I would recommend this set. Check the price history because the price does seem to bounce around a bit. It's a great deal when the price is down.

reviews.title: Sharp knives with a unique heel design
reviews.body: The knife set by PAUDIN includes 5 popular styles used in today’s kitchens. The set includes an 8” Chef, 8” Bread, 7” Nakiri, 5” Santoku and a 5” Utility knife. According to the product listing, the knives are constructed with CJ14C28N steel that undergoes Vacuum Nitriding and Deep Cryogenic Treatment to enhance toughness, reduce edge chipping risk, and improved corrosion resistance. The edge angle of the blade is listed as 13° and has a hardness rating of 63HRC. The full tang handle is covered with G10 high pressure fiberglass laminate. The included product guide states to use a wood or bamboo cutting board and to hand wash and dry immediately after use. I could not find any mention of “dishwasher safe” in the product guide. I tested all 5 knives and they are all incredibly sharp. In fact, the bread knife is the sharpest bread knife I have ever had and cleanly cuts through hard crust without crushing the bread. The Nakiri, Chef’s and Santoku knives easily cut through a variety of vegetables with very little effort. While the Nakiri knife may look like a mini-cleaver, it is typically intended for cutting soft foods or vegetables. The G10 handles are comfortable to hold, grippy and are thicker in the middle. The heel of the knife has a curved cutout for the index finger, but creates a sharp point where the curve meets the edge of the knife. While this sharp point is easy to avoid on the larger knives, it is not the case for the 5” Utility knife because of the lower blade height. If you typically hold the knife with a thumb and index finger, it is easy to poke yourself because there is less physical space. I’m thinking of dulling the point with a stone to prevent skin punctures. Even though I’m on the fence with the heel design of the blade, this set contains a nice variety of very sharp knives that would be great in any kitchen.

reviews.title: Sharp Today, But Ask Me Again in Six Months
reviews.body: New knives are fun. Very fun. There is nothing like a fresh blade. I opened the box like a kid on Christmas. Five knives. All shiny. All new. All grinning at me in a menacing, helpful way. And they cut. Oh, they cut. Ultra sharp, just like the box said. I sliced a tomato and it barely noticed. Thin slices. Clean slices. Slices you could read a newspaper through. I chopped an onion. No sawing. No crushing. Just a smooth glide. The onion did not stand a chance. The onion did not even see it coming. Let me talk handles. Full tang. That is the good stuff. The metal runs all the way through the handle. No cheap little stub hiding in there. It feels solid. It feels balanced. It feels like it means business. That full tang is a good sign. It usually means quality. It usually means the knife will not snap when you get bold with a squash. So far, so good. But here is my big question. The only question that matters. How long will they stay this sharp? That is the real test. Anything is sharp on day one. Day one is easy. Day one is a honeymoon. The blade is fresh. The angle is perfect. The romance is real. Day two hundred is the truth. Will they still glide? Or will I be sawing at a tomato like a caveman with a butter knife? I do not know yet. I cannot know yet. Sharpness fades slow. It sneaks up on you. One day you are slicing like a pro. The next day you are pressing hard and hoping. So I am watching. I am cutting. I am keeping notes like a suspicious scientist. Right now they are wonderful. The full tang gives me hope. The build feels honest. But the jury is out. Way out. The jury went home for the weekend. Let me talk value. Five knives for a fair price. Good so far. If the edge holds, this is a steal. If it dulls fast, this is a lesson. So here is where I land. Great out of the box. Scary sharp. Solid handles. But durability is the whole game, and I have not played enough of it yet.

reviews.title: Arrives nicely packaged and sharpened
reviews.body: These knives arrive sharpened and ready to use immediately, and have been a great addition to our kitchen. These knives are light, but they have just the right amount of small weight so that it can cut through thick meats and fruits easily. The Santoku Knife was probably the most unexpectedly impressive out of all of the knives. At first glance, it seems that the knife is too small to handle for everyday use. However, it is in fact this size, and how well it cuts is what makes it all-rounded. The knife is light, which makes it easier to cut faster whilst having control over it. Until I started using the Santoku knife, I did not realize how unnecessarily big other knives were. The Chef Knife is an average sized chef knife. I mainly use this to cut thicker, harder things. Although slightly heavier than the Santoku knife, it is still light which gives me a lot of control. With how well it is sharpened, it can cut through hard fruits like melon/watermelon like butter. The other knives are also nice and sharpened, and is high-quality overall. The price is quite high, and for this price it would have been nice if it came with a knife holder. However I can certainly say that these are one of the best kitchen knives I've used. I am hoping that the knives will retain its sharpness for quite a while before it will need sharpening.

reviews.body: I’ve been very impressed with Paudin knives in general, and this 5 piece set certainly continues that. The knives are extremely sharp, and the handles are comfortable for my hands. With plastic handles and stainless steel blades, they are easy to keep clean and should last a very long time. It’s a little hard to judge the price; currently they are listed at one price but have a coupon for 40% off…at the list price I would say they are a decent value but that you might find other sets to be a better value; at the coupon price, they are a great value. I didn’t have any particular intention when I ordered this set, but now that I have them, this is going to be my traveling knife set. I’ve gotten used to taking at least one or two knives with me when I rent a summer vacation house, since they never seem to have decent or sharp knives. With the padded carrying case these come in, I can now take a very nice selection of sharp and high-quality knives with me. That’s a win. My final comment, and it doesn’t detract from my rating, is that I’d love this set even more if the santoku and small utility knife were just a little bigger. My favorite overall knife is a 6” chef’s knife, and this one is a little smaller than the ones I prefer. But overall, if these knives fill your need, it’s a great product.

reviews.title: Catch them on sale for $20 and it's a fair deal.

They are fairly sharp when new but lose the edge quickly. "Razor" sharp? NO WAY! The cheap steel has a limit on how sharp they can be sharpened, and they don't hold the edge very long, before needing resharpened. The scissors are pretty cheap. The handles are hollow, so they have to be dried almost vertically, or you'll get water dripping when you put them in the block. A couple handles have dents, possibly from dishes being set on them in the sink? I have only recently started trying them in the dishwasher, so far, no issues. They're holding up ok, with no sign of rust or spotting. I gave my daughter my much old, much larger set of "decent" Farberwear knives when I ordered these. Wish I'd waited til they arrived, she would've gotten this new set. The block is solid and heavy.

reviews.title: I received a damaged, recirculated returned item :(
reviews.body: I must’ve received the same set that’s been returned over and over again. Rather than continuing to recirculate a clearly defective return, why not send out a new, quality item? I purchased the green set, and as several other reviewers have mentioned, the color is not really Sage green—it’s much closer to avocado, although not quite that bright. More importantly, the oxidation and chipping on the gold metallic parts are very noticeable and simply shouldn’t be present on an item being sold as “new.” At a discounted price, this might be a reasonable thrift-store purchase. The actual steel quality seemed decent for a Chinese-made set, although the handles felt somewhat plasticky. That said, these obviously aren’t top-of-the-line pieces, so I wasn’t expecting premium construction. Ultimately, my main issue isn’t necessarily with the Martha Stewart brand itself, but with this particular vendor.

reviews.title: I LOVE THESE KNIVES!! **UPDATE**
reviews.body: **it has been 3 wonderful years with these knives and they're still as sharp as the day they arrived! I have had no need to have them sharpened, and honestly, I still have no complaints. They. Are. AMAZING. I can't say enough good things about these knives. I recently moved into a new house and of course needed to upgrade some items. First on my list was a good knife set since I'm a avid cooker. Despite some bad reviews, I went ahead and ordered these. First things first; they are SHARP. I can only cut with one hand and these bad boys slice through tomatoes like nobody's business. One handed cutters dream!! Second, they are GORGEOUS. I have had several knife sets, but these are my absolute favourite!! Some people were complaining about them rusting, and fair, that COULD happen. But if treated right, they wont do that. My number one rule is these do NOT go in the dishwasher. In certain circumstances, they don't even see soap. They are washed immediately after use, thoroughly dried, and returned to the block. Should spots appear, I use stainless steel cleaner. They are still as beautiful as the day I took them out of the box. They also have required no sharpening since I got them. If stored and taken care of PROPERLY, these knives will never need replaced. They are every bit what I had hoped for and worth every penny spent. I highly recommend them to anyone who asks and even to those who don't!!! If you want knives you don't care about or you'll throw in the dishwasher, these are not for you. Take care of your knives, love them, respect them, and they will deliver excellent performance time and time again.

reviews.title: Excellent All‑Steel Knives That Perform Better Than Expected!!
reviews.body: I’ve owned several Cuisinart knives over the years, and this all–stainless steel set is definitely one of their winners. Each knife is forged from a single piece of steel, giving them a sleek, modern look and a sturdy feel. I’ll admit when I first saw the stainless steel handles, I assumed they would be slippery, especially when chopping veggies. Luckily, that wasn’t the case at all. They’re surprisingly comfortable, well‑balanced, and offer a secure grip even during longer prep sessions. The standout for me is the 7” Santoku knife (C77SS-7SAN-25K). It’s a Japanese style incredibly sharp, solidly built, and the longer blade length gives you great control. If you’re used to a 5" Santoku, it may feel a bit heavier and may take a little bit of getting used to, but once you do, it’s hard to go back. Like the rest of the knives in the set, this one arrives razor‑sharp and stays that way as long as you care for it properly. My next best favorite is the western style Chef's knife (C77SS-CF-25K) which is what most folks like including the chefs as it allows to cut a wide variety of vegetables and fruits. It has a curved edge("belly") with a pointed tip. My Third favorite cutting knife is the Slicing Knife (C77SS-SL-25K) which is specifically useful for slicing large cuts of either cooked meat or fish. It has a long, narrow blade with a pointed tip. I found this to be useful for cutting larger fruits like Watermelon, Melons or gourds etc. as the longer blade allows you to cut/slice them their vertical length. To keep these knives in top shape, here are a few care tips I personally follow: Use the right cutting surface: Stick to wood or plastic cutting boards. Harder surfaces like glass, stone, or metal will dull the blade quickly. Hand‑wash only: Clean with warm, soapy water and dry immediately with a soft cloth. Make sure the knife is completely dry before storing it. Avoid scraping with the sharp edge: If you need to move chopped ingredients, flip the knife over and use the back of the blade or a scraper. Store properly: Always use the included sheath. Storing knives loose in a drawer can damage the edge and create a safety hazard. If you follow these simple steps, these knives will stay sharp and serve you well for a long time. Overall, this is a great quality set that delivers excellent value and performance. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: If you cook a lot, you need knives from these folks. They're amazing!!

I caught them on sale and honestly couldn't be happier. The set was packaged in foam cut so nothing shifts during transport, they really took the time to pack them well. reviews.title: Absolutely beautiful!

That way you will always know which knife goes into which slot, also, the font on the wooden block is very stylish. The blades are made of High German Carbon Stainless Steel 'Made in China' 😂.The other thing I love about it is that it matches the wooden handle of my coffee pot perfectly. Be careful, they (at least the one I tried) are as sharp as a razor, if not sharper. I Love It!!!

reviews.title: High quality steel. Holds an edge.
reviews.body: Meet cleavers are not just for cutting meat. I have had this knif for around a year. This is the best knife I have ever used for cutting ALL my food, not just meat. All the reviews that wrote that they can't get a sharp edge on it, don't know how to sharpen a knife! This is one of the easiest knives I've ever sharpened. I use a chefs rod sharpener and it come out very sharp EVERY time. If you don't know how to sharpen a knife, that is one thing. But don't write that it is a cheap knife that won't get a sharp edge just because you don't know how to sharpen a high quility carbon steel cleaver. And the review that said that it is to heavy, that he will be using it instead to chop wood, doesn't realize that all good quality cleavers are heavy like this. News flash. This is a meat cleaver. If you want a ax, go buy an ax. I have used it at least sixty times to cut food for dinner. This knife is made of fantastic high carbon stainless steel. It should be at least three times the price. That's how good this knife is. It also comes with a thick, good quality leather sheath. It is relitvly easy to sharpen. It really holds an edge incredably, once sharpened. The steel is not to hard where it becomes brittle. It's also not to soft where it won't hold an edge. The hardness is just the correct balance. It holds an edge better than my $150 great brand camping knife. Once the food is cut on my chopping block, I can easily scrap up the food onto the side of the knife, having the blade go under the side of my hand and pushing it onto the knife then picking up the food and putting it into a bowl, frying pan ect., just the way the chefs do in Chinese restaurants. It is much more efficient that way. That is what makes this a much better option for cutting ALL my food, rather than using a regular chefs knife. I know. I used to be a chef in a five star restaurant in CT. This knife is just as good as the expensive $140 knives that were bought from a restayrant supply company for the restaurant I worked at . So, buy it. You won't be disappointed with it!!!

reviews.title: High quality steel. Holds an edge.
reviews.body: Meet cleavers are not just for cutting meat. I have had this knif for around a year. This is the best knife I have ever used for cutting ALL my food, not just meat. All the reviews that wrote that they can't get a sharp edge on it, don't know how to sharpen a knife! This is one of the easiest knives I've ever sharpened. I use a chefs rod sharpener and it come out very sharp EVERY time. If you don't know how to sharpen a knife, that is one thing. But don't write that it is a cheap knife that won't get a sharp edge just because you don't know how to sharpen a high quility carbon steel cleaver. And the review that said that it is to heavy, that he will be using it instead to chop wood, doesn't realize that all good quality cleavers are heavy like this. News flash. This is a meat cleaver. If you want a ax, go buy an ax. I have used it at least sixty times to cut food for dinner. This knife is made of fantastic high carbon stainless steel. It should be at least three times the price. That's how good this knife is. It also comes with a thick, good quality leather sheath. It is relitvly easy to sharpen. It really holds an edge incredably, once sharpened. The steel is not to hard where it becomes brittle. It's also not to soft where it won't hold an edge. The hardness is just the correct balance. It holds an edge better than my $150 great brand camping knife. Once the food is cut on my chopping block, I can easily scrap up the food onto the side of the knife, having the blade go under the side of my hand and pushing it onto the knife then picking up the food and putting it into a bowl, frying pan ect., just the way the chefs do in Chinese restaurants. It is much more efficient that way. That is what makes this a much better option for cutting ALL my food, rather than using a regular chefs knife. I know. I used to be a chef in a five star restaurant in CT. This knife is just as good as the expensive $140 knives that were bought from a restayrant supply company for the restaurant I worked at . So, buy it. You won't be disappointed with it!!!

reviews.title: Gorgeous but can be dangerous
reviews.body: Knife sharpness: 10/10 Beauty: 10/10 Block folded in a drawer: 8/10 Block easeled on the counter: 2/10 The foldable block is a nightmare on the counter. It has an easel so it can stand on the counter which looks stunning and high end, but the magnets aren’t strong and the weight distribution was made to be easy to pull up from a drawer, so one knock of the handle when it’s upright and that sharp end flies up. If you have it facing the direction of easily using the handle on the counter, it’s backwards and doesn’t look as nice from the back. However, the knives are INCREDIBLY sharp. I accidentally ran my finger over an edge unwrapping them and the cut was so clean it didn’t bleed for like a minute. I thought I cut myself, looked at my finger and saw there was a white line, but it wasn’t painful so I thought it was just an impression, but as I finished unwrapping I noticed I was bleeding everywhere. It was so clean my body didn’t even realize it was cut. I don’t cook much so it doesn’t bother me much, but if you plan on using knives every day and want them on display, the round one is probably a safer option.

reviews.title: Excellent Knife Set!
reviews.body: Wow, my husband and I absolutely love this knife set! We are both retired, both cook often, and was looking for a good knife set with good gripping handles, self-sharpening, and had good-sized steak knives. And boy, did we find it with this product! We have only had this set a week, but so far, we love it! (I will update my review, if anything changes.) We have been hand-washing them and then drying with a cloth and leaving them on our drying mat overnight to air dry thoroughly, before placing them back in the knife block. We purchased the 14-piece set and it fits very nicely on our counter, without taking up much room. I really wanted the 20-piece set so that we would have 8 steak knives, instead of just the 6. However, after reading the reviews of how big the block was on the larger set, and me not being able to find the dimensions of the block anywhere, I opted for the smaller 14-piece set. All the knives state they were made in India, and the shears and black wood block was made in China. This is truly a beautiful set. We have been delighted at how sharp these knives are and highly recommend this set! (Just a side note, the box states there is a “prep knife,” but on the wood block it states it as a “utility” knife.)

reviews.title: Finally a quality knife set
reviews.body: I was first drawn to these because the steak knives have a smooth blade. So many cheap, and even many more expensive knife sets have serrated steak knives which I can't stand. A steak knife should slice your food, not tear it. These slice with ease. I've been using the knives for a little over a month and haven't had a need to sharpen them yet, so I can't speak to the built-in sharpening tool, but they are holding an edge well. And that's with cleaning them in the dishwasher. Yes, I know hand washing is better, but in my household that's simply not happening much of the time, and these knives haven't punished us for it. The handles are very comfortable, and full tang, 3-rivot design makes them very sturdy. I'm expecting they'll last for decades. My one complaint is that when all the knives are in the block they all look so similar that you might end up grabbing 2 or 3 different knives trying to find the one you want. I'm not actually sure I'd want anything changed to 'fix' that though... I think any sort of labeling would detract from the design, and the issue is just too minor.

I’ll update further on its performance if needed!

reviews.title: Beginner-Friendly, Pro-Ready — The Perfect Launchpad into DSLR Photography
reviews.body: As someone who wanted to level up from phone photography but wasn’t quite ready to dive into $2,000 camera bodies, the Canon EOS Rebel T7 was the perfect bridge — and it has exceeded expectations. ⸻ Image Quality The 24.1 MP sensor captures crisp, clean images in both daylight and low light. You’ll instantly notice the difference in depth, clarity, and color accuracy compared to any smartphone. The controls are intuitive, even for someone brand new to DSLRs. The built-in Feature Guide explains settings in real-time, helping you learn as you shoot. It’s like a camera and teacher in one. ⸻ Connectivity Built-in Wi-Fi is a huge plus. I can snap a photo and send it to my phone instantly for social media or editing. It’s a fantastic intro into the world of serious photography, and once you start using it, you’ll wonder why you waited. Sharp photos, simple learning curve, and real Canon reliability.

Battery life is commendable, allowing for extended shooting sessions without constant recharging. In conclusion, the Canon Rebel T7 is an excellent choice for entry-level photographers seeking a reliable and user-friendly DSLR camera with solid image quality and performance.

reviews.title: Great Entry-Level DSLR with Solid Image Quality
reviews.body: Great Entry-Level DSLR with Solid Image Quality I purchased the Canon EOS Rebel T7 as my first DSLR, and it’s been a great experience so far. This camera is perfect for beginners who want to learn photography without getting overwhelmed by too many features. Pros: • Image Quality: The 24.1MP sensor delivers crisp and vibrant photos, especially in good lighting. I’ve taken some fantastic landscape and portrait shots. • User-Friendly: The interface is intuitive, and the built-in guide mode helps explain settings and functions. Great for those new to DSLR photography. • Wi-Fi and NFC: Easy to transfer photos to your phone or tablet using Canon’s app. A big plus for quick sharing on social media. • Battery Life: It lasts a full day of shooting if you’re not constantly using Live View or flash. Cons: • No 4K Video: It records 1080p, which is okay, but if you’re looking to shoot high-quality video, this might be a limitation. • No Touchscreen or Articulating LCD: The screen is fixed and not touch-sensitive, which can make navigating menus slower compared to more modern cameras. • Autofocus in Live View: Slower and less reliable, especially when shooting video or using the screen instead of the viewfinder. Bottom Line: If you’re just starting out and want a reliable DSLR without breaking the bank, the Canon T7 is a solid choice. It’s not packed with advanced features, but it gets the job done and does it well. Ideal for hobbyists, students, or anyone learning the ropes of manual photography.

reviews.title: Excellent beginner camera!
reviews.body: The Canon EOS Rebel T7 is an excellent entry-level DSLR camera that offers great value, especially with the included EF 18-55mm and EF 75-300mm lenses. Whether you’re a beginner learning the basics of photography or someone looking for an affordable camera with solid image quality, this kit delivers. Pros: ✅ Image Quality – The 24.1 MP APS-C sensor captures sharp and vibrant images with great detail, even in low-light situations. ✅ Dual Lens Kit – The 18-55mm lens is great for everyday shots, while the 75-300mm lens offers solid zoom capabilities for wildlife, sports, and portrait photography. ✅ Built-in Wi-Fi & NFC – Easily transfer images to your phone or tablet for quick sharing. ✅ Simple to Use – The camera is beginner-friendly, with automatic shooting modes and an easy-to-navigate menu. ✅ Full HD 1080p Video – Decent video recording quality for casual videographers. Cons: ❌ No 4K Video – Video recording is limited to 1080p, which may not be ideal for serious videographers. ❌ Fixed LCD Screen – The display does not tilt or swivel, making it less versatile for vlogging or tricky angles. ❌ No Image Stabilization in the Lenses – Handheld shots, especially at higher zooms, may require a tripod for steady images. ❌ Slower Autofocus – Compared to higher-end DSLRs or mirrorless cameras, the autofocus speed is moderate, especially in live view mode. Who Should Buy This? ✔️ Beginners & Hobbyists – If you’re just starting with DSLR photography, this kit is an excellent choice with everything you need to learn. ✔️ Casual Photographers – Great for family, travel, and portrait photography. ✔️ Budget-Conscious Buyers – You get a lot of value with two lenses included. Final Verdict: For the price, the Canon EOS Rebel T7 offers solid performance, good image quality, and an easy-to-use interface. While it lacks some advanced features found in more expensive cameras, it remains one of the best budget DSLR kits on the market. If you’re looking for an affordable way to step into DSLR photography, this kit is a great choice!

Whether you’re a beginner learning the basics of photography or someone looking for an affordable camera with solid image quality, this kit delivers. Pros: ✅ Image Quality – The 24.1 MP APS-C sensor captures sharp and vibrant images with great detail, even in low-light situations. ✅ Dual Lens Kit – The 18-55mm lens is great for everyday shots, while the 75-300mm lens offers solid zoom capabilities for wildlife, sports, and portrait photography. ✅ Built-in Wi-Fi & NFC – Easily transfer images to your phone or tablet for quick sharing. ✅ Simple to Use – The camera is beginner-friendly, with automatic shooting modes and an easy-to-navigate menu. ✅ Full HD 1080p Video – Decent video recording quality for casual videographers. Cons: ❌ No 4K Video – Video recording is limited to 1080p, which may not be ideal for serious videographers. ❌ Fixed LCD Screen – The display does not tilt or swivel, making it less versatile for vlogging or tricky angles. ❌ No Image Stabilization in the Lenses – Handheld shots, especially at higher zooms, may require a tripod for steady images. ❌ Slower Autofocus – Compared to higher-end DSLRs or mirrorless cameras, the autofocus speed is moderate, especially in live view mode. Who Should Buy This? ✔️ Beginners & Hobbyists – If you’re just starting with DSLR photography, this kit is an excellent choice with everything you need to learn. ✔️ Casual Photographers – Great for family, travel, and portrait photography. ✔️ Budget-Conscious Buyers – You get a lot of value with two lenses included. Final Verdict: For the price, the Canon EOS Rebel T7 offers solid performance, good image quality, and an easy-to-use interface. While it lacks some advanced features found in more expensive cameras, it remains one of the best budget DSLR kits on the market. If you’re looking for an affordable way to step into DSLR photography, this kit is a great choice!

reviews.title: Great camera even though model is 8 years old
reviews.body: The D7500 came out in 2017, is one of Nikons higher quality models from that time. Does not have latest tech compared to latest cameras or even phones. But for my needs, its almost perfect. Excellent viewfinder, awesome battery life (typical of dslr's, and one of the advantages over mirrorless cameras). So easy to get a great image. Fast accurate auto-focus. I prefer Program mode, but when in Auto mode, you can still get amazing, dependably sharp lower noise photos. The lens (18-140mm) it comes with is awesome, great image quality at all focal lengths. I bought an older model, because it was new (hard to find this model new anymore), on deep discount (at least compared to price when released in 2017), and was the higher quality model I was looking for. Lens and camera body are weather resistant. Great movie quality, too. I almost always use 4k, I'm ok with 30 fps., (though many newer models have 4K 60fps) movie image quality is clear, sharp, pleasing. It is certainly larger than a compact camera, but I can't afford one of the better compact models out now, and even many full frame cameras are now smaller than the D7500. What with Tariffs and general inflation, good cameras are VERY expensive now. I must admit I am partial to Nikon, and I wanted a camera with a decent range telephoto lens. This camera tiks all the boxes important to me, I extremely happy with it. The lens is fairly compact for an 18-140mm configuration, is just an outstanding lens.

reviews.title: Excellent camera!
reviews.body: This camera, although it would be considered “dated” by younger generations of photographers, is still very much a powerhouse and a must have for anyone wanting to take photos in a variety of situations! This is a step up from the previous DSLR I owned so there is a small learning curve for me as far as the features. I also consider it a step up from the z50 mirrorless I own. While mirrorless is lighter weight, there are situations where it just isn’t capable of doing what I need. The real test for this D7500 will be marching season during halftime shows, but as of so far, I’m impressed! The 18-140 lens is truly an excellent lens! It is able to zoom in and out as I need in all situations I’ve used it so far. Very fast auto focus and I love that I can easily switch to manual on the lens itself without fiddling with settings on the camera. This significantly lowers the risk of me missing a photo opportunity because I’m looking for a setting in the camera menu. Sturdy body. This does add weight to the camera but honestly I feel like that isn’t a bad thing. I started my photography journey with an SLR with no auto focus and black & white film in HS. I learned to develop the film and photos myself. The features and options on this camera are truly amazing and I still have a lot to learn about it, but so far I’m impressed! I’ve always been a Nikon girl and they continue to provide excellent photography cameras and lenses! *photo taken at my local Memorial Day ceremony. This pup was super fast and I took several photos in quick succession to get the one shown on the review here. The D7500 didn’t hesitate, focused quickly and I was able to take this picture. The owners were thrilled when I posted it on the local page as they had yet to get a good pic of their new pup :)

reviews.title: First time DSLR owner - great choice
reviews.body: 3 week update: Have used this camera daily. It is simple to learn, simple to use, a real joy for wildlife. After 3 week the menus and controls are becoming more 2nd nature. Because of all the features I expected that it would take longer to start feeling familiar. Occasionally I have to go back to a reference to find what I am looking for, but really, this camera is an amazingly intuitive piece of technology even for a beginner. Your camera takes good pictures goes the joke. It is no joke with the D7500. I have used the Coolpx P900 for ~two years. I have never used a DSLR. The D7500 is my first. The pix with this review were taken on the first two days I owned it. These pix were shot on shutter preferred and manual. I had no idea a DSLR camera could be so amazing and forgiving. If I can do this, imagine what you can do if you have knowledge and experience. I carefully researched DSLRs before making this purchase. You will find that if you do this camera is highly rated. Let those reviews will guide your decision. I got this camera because I wanted a camera I could grow into, a camera that would work for wildlife and action, and a camera that was considered an excellent buy in professional reviews. I also chose Nikon because I was familiar with the layout and language because of my P900. For me it was a spectacular choice. I highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Customer service failure
reviews.body: If I could give this 0 stars, I absolutely would. I purchased this camera listed as new, not refurbished. When it arrived, I was initially very pleased. I’ve used Canon cameras most of my adult life, and this one seemed no different—great picture quality, easy to use, and the included accessories made it feel like a solid value. However, that positive impression didn’t last. After just three uses, the camera completely failed on the fourth shoot. I took one picture and the camera stopped functioning entirely. At first, I assumed it was a dead battery. After recharging, I tried again—nothing worked. The flash would fire, but the menu wouldn’t even come up. At that point, it was clear this was not user error—it was a defective unit. Then things became even more concerning. When I attempted to register the camera with Canon, the system indicated that the camera and one of the lenses had already been registered. That should never happen with a product sold as “new.” It strongly suggests this item may have been previously used or resold. About a week later, when we tried again, that warning mysteriously disappeared—which only adds to the suspicion. At this point, we contacted Amazon, since we were still within the return window. I simply wanted a replacement or refund for a clearly defective product. Because we no longer had the original packaging, we were told we had to deal directly with the third-party seller, Beach Camera. This is where the experience completely broke down. Despite receiving a defective camera that failed almost immediately, Beach Camera: Refused a straightforward exchange or refund Opened a vague “investigation” instead of resolving the issue Attempted to offer only $88 compensation for an $800+ broken camera Required me to pay return shipping Charged a 20% restocking fee—even though the product was defective Charging a restocking fee on a defective item is unacceptable. Passing the cost of their failure onto the customer is worse. Thankfully, Amazon ultimately stepped in to make things right, although I now have to cover costs upfront and wait for reimbursement. Without that support, this would have been a complete loss. Bottom line: Most vendors—and Amazon—stand behind what they sell. Beach Camera does not. They failed at every stage: selling a questionable “new” product, refusing to take responsibility for a defect, and attempting to penalize the customer for their own failure. I strongly recommend avoiding this vendor.

reviews.body: TL;DR: If you're looking into photography as a hobbyist/beginner this is an amazingly compact powerhouse. It doesn't break the bank AND allows you to save your money for lenses. This camera is addicting. It's my gateway to beginner photography and I want to take pictures of everything. I took it to my local Renaissance Faire, take daily pictures of my sister's cats, candid photos of my friends and family, flowers and shops during my wife and I's daily walks, etc. It's so light and compact that the thought of getting larger and longer lenses on this would make it look really silly. Its Continuous shooting mode is fast enough to capture some horse back riding during the Ren Faire and I captured my wife's arrow mid-flight (although blurry) at 1/4000 when we participated in archery. The GUI is so beginner friendly and explains what each mode does (Manual/Aperture Priority/etc.). It actually helped me understand what each is used for so my wife took plenty of pictures with the right settings quickly. If you dig deeper into the menus there's more granular options like Manual Focusing, Viewfinder/Display brightness, Display options, etc. There's a ton and it's a hassle to navigate through them all... Until you find out you can create your own custom quick access menus. These quickly allows me to navigate to my favorite menu options that I frequently tinker with without moving through all of the other options one by one. The body is so small that I was afraid it would easily slip out of my hands. That was not the case as the grips on the right-hand side is grippy enough that it feels like it you can hold it with a light squeeze while adjusting focus with your left hand on the lens. This kit also provides a strap that allows the camera to be hung around your body for quick access. The performance on the batteries lasts for at least a day with heavy usage so I recommend another battery just in case. Unfortunately, it does not come with a charger and the manual's "Charging the Battery" section talks about charging the battery with a charger. So buy a charger that's compatible with LP-E17 batteries. The autofocus' performance is so impressive that it's enticing my wife to get one for herself. Disclaimer: These photos are taken with the Canon RF50mm F1.8 STM Lens, Fixed Focal Length Prime Lens and NOT the lens included with this kit (Canon RF-S18-45mm F4.5-6.3 IS STM Lens).

Six Frames Per Second Burst Mode to Capture the Decisive Moment: Never miss peak action with six frames per second burst shooting that captures rapid sequences of wildlife movement, sports action, and fast-paced events; review each burst on the three inch LCD and select the sharpest frame for consistently better keepers when subjects are unpredictable, moving quickly, or the moment happens in a fraction of a second

Sixteen Megapixel BSI CMOS Sensor with Optical Image Stabilization at Every Zoom Level: Backside-illuminated sensor technology delivers sharp, detailed images with better low-light performance, while built-in OIS actively compensates for hand movement even at maximum fifty two times zoom reach—so handheld telephoto shots come out crisp and clear without requiring a tripod in the field

Built-in Wi-Fi for Wireless Control and Instant Social Sharing Straight from the Field: Connect the AZ528 to your smartphone or tablet to wirelessly transfer photos and post to social media immediately after every great shot; use your phone as a live remote viewfinder for hands-free shooting from a distance; full one thousand eighty p HD video records smooth wildlife sequences, travel adventures, and event coverage

Rechargeable Li-Ion Battery and Generous Memory Support for Full-Day Shooting Sessions: A rechargeable lithium-ion battery powers extended shooting sessions in the field, and the camera accepts Class ten SD, SDHC, or SDXC memory cards up to five hundred twelve GB—enough storage for thousands of high-resolution photos and hours of Full HD video from a full day of wildlife photography, travel, or sports

reviews.title: Nice camera, great price
reviews.body: I like this camera a lot. I bought it for optical zoom, and I'm very pleased with the shots I'm able to get, which is mostly wildlife and waterfowl. I take all of these types of shots using the SCN>Pet Mode. I learned that little trick many years ago on a Panasonic camera I had. So for my uses, this is a pretty good camera, particularly for the reasonable price. Pay attention to instructions to achieve focus by first pushing the button down halfway. You'll hear a tone and see a green bordered rectangle when the camera feels it has focus. It doesn't always, but you'll get the hang of it to achieve a pretty decent level of what you expect. I used to have an old Easyshare years ago, and operationally, the PixPro is very similar, though far superior. So this was an easy camera to learn for me. Once you've familiarized yourself with its operation, I think most people will find it fairly simple to use. It is also comfortable in your hand. With the kind of shots I'm taking, I'm usually using a tripod. Keep that in mind. I've included 4 photos, which you probably won't be able to see that well, but all were taken on near max zoom except the deer, which I was very close to. The encasement of the camera is a little strange and super easy to mar or scuff. When I tried to clean it with a cloth, I then had scuffs and lint. I found the best thing to clean the encasement with is the red antibacterial Wet Ones wipes. I would not say the battery life is long. But the batteries are cheap. And I bought two of them in a package deal with a double charger. It connects by USB C to my OnePlus car charger, so I'm getting supervooc charging. Very fast! No need to charge slow by connecting to the micro USB! Easy battery in and out of the camera. I rotate 5 batteries including the one that came with the camera. I have no complaints about the regular photos I've taken of landscapes, sunsets, people, etc., but I usually use my phone for things like that. Also, it's super easy connecting my devices, both tablet and phone, to the camera's WiFi. Additionally, the PixPro app works extremely well with both devices, which are OnePlus, but I haven't updated that app on either device. I'm a little afraid it won't work right if I do. If there's ever a need, I'll update it 😉

reviews.body: This is an amazing camera. In a world of technical terms, it does take some time to learn how to use it. Things to do (or) know. This camera does use an (LB-060) reactangular shaped (lithium rechargable battery) which is included but I recommend buying a second battery. It does not come with a memory card. You will need to purchase a minimum of (32gb) memory card. Do yourself a favor, download the user's manual .pdf file from the internet. Just type in the full name of the camera followed by "users manual" and you will have what you need to set up your camera correctly. It has a lot of features that work great, probably more than you need if you are not a professional. After having to purchase multiple cameras, this one is by far the best value for the price. It does take some patients and tweeking but when you are done I found this camera much better than my GoPro 12, in my opinion. Although I wouldn't classify it as an action camera, it does take great stills as well as videos. This is a great value all in one camera! 1080p is so close to 4k it's very hard to tell the difference. That's what this camera is a 1080p but the small difference is worth avoiding all of the 4k headaches.

It's been fun trying to learn to use it and we've gotten some great shots of wildlife--mostly ducks and birds. It's relatively easy to use for a "beginner," and has some nice features--like charging the battery without removing it from the camera. However, I'm not impressed either with panoramic shots or the color. In fact, we are quite disappointed with colors that seem muted. I know we can brighten shots with a phot editor, but it would be nice to get that true color from the camera itself. I know the reviews aren't great for this product so we were warned. I'm not really sorry I bought the camera, just a little disappointed in the color quality. But if you mostly want it for the zoom capability, this is definitely a choice in the lower budget range.

reviews.title: It's Guess and Hope
reviews.body: Ordered this for my wife to take pictures of birds in our yard using a lens hood and UV filter (both must be purchased separately). It has not been used indoors. The major problem with this camera is the lack of a viewfinder. Pictures must be set up using the small LCD screen on the back of the camera. Unfortunately, when you use the camera outside, the screen shows your own reflection looking back at you and you can't see what you are aiming at. I contacted Kodak customer service to see if anything could be done about this: perhaps a non-reflective coating that could be applied to the screen. This was their reply: "...when hit with sunlight the screen will look black and the only thing you can do is hover your hand over the top of the camera to keep the sun from hitting the LCD screen before pressing the shutter button." Unless you have 3 hands or are using a tripod this is an unworkable solution. The shutter and zoom controls are on the right side of the camera so you hold the camera on the right. You need to steady the camera with your left hand when the zoom is extended because the camera becomes front heavy. Using this camera is like standing in a crowd and holding your cell phone over your head to try to take a picture of something you can't really see. Sometimes you get a good picture, most times you don't. It's not point and shoot - it's guess and hope.

reviews.title: Pro level at an accessible price
reviews.body: Compared to the 2 Canon DSLRs I have owned in the past, it blows them out of the water in terms of auto focus speed and accuracy. For low light, I've never seen anything like it in the consumer market, not counting the A7s ii which I haven't tried yet. The version that I bought came with the kit lens and it's performance is fine. It's not the best to use for the ultimate low light capabilities, but it's reliable enough. Interestingly enough, the kit lens even has firmware that you can update. I have successfully used my Canon glass with it using a Simga MC-11 adapter. The Canon 17-40mm f4L and Canon 70-200 f2.8L focused quickly. My Sigma 8-16mm lens focused well, though it's meant for APS-C sensors. Oddly enough my Canon 50mm 1.4 paired with the A7iii and Sigma MC-11 takes about a minute or two before the aperature control is functional but once it kicks in, this combo turns night into day. I also use a 35mm 1.8 OSS Sony lens that I used with my a5100 and even though it puts it into APS-C mode which sacrifices quality, it's still good enough. I can even use my Canon 580ex ii successfully with this (manual mode/no HSS) with a Fomex flash trigger. The reason I bought this however was for video. 4k is stunning, though I have to say, plan for paying a but extra for a UHS-II card to get it to work. The S&Q setting is nice for switching over to slow-mo very quickly. The menu system is a bit much but at least it includes a lot of features that are missing with Canon. Battery performance is quite incredible. Overall, I can't see why this camera wouldn't satisfy most pros unless they work in a harsh environment in which case, the weather sealing probably won't be enough. The compact size of it though is nice when you don't want to draw attention.

reviews.title: Literally Makes Me Hate Photography
reviews.body: I've had this camera for about 10 months now and it is probably the worst photographic decision I have ever made. I only wish I could have returned it while I had the chance. Let me start of by saying I've been a professional photographer for 15 years and mostly photograph models in a studio setting or outdoors. I use natural light and also strobes. I started with Nikon, went to a Canon 5dmkii, have had other canons and also 3 fuji x series cameras Firstly, what kind of company ships a $2000 camera without a battery charger? I get it, it can plug into your computer to charge or car adapter via USB-C. But that means more wear and tear on the USB port which will eventually be loose and then have issues. When I get home I prefer to take my battery out and put it on the charger which will tell me when its charged. Second. I read all the reviews who talked about the poor color science and then all the videos who said all the things you had to do to fix it. I never realized how bad it actually is. When I would view my photos from my canon in camera raw or capture one I was only one click away from getting an accurate representation of what I had originally seen. Sony has its own version of Capture One (I also use the pro version) and the images look like garbage from the moment they appear on the screen. they even look worse then what you get in Lightroom. The next issue is the awful menus. Do I need to be the next person to complain about the menus? ISO is on page 9 of the menu. White Balance on page 12. Sure, you can set a custom quick menu, but I would have expected updates to make it better. Another thing I was kind of surprised about were the files sizes. I guess I kind of thought they would be like my Canon where a 24 megapixel image had a raw file of 24 megabytes. I did not expect the raw files to be double that. a typical raw file on the Sony is about 48 megabytes, and the matching jpeg is 12 MB. I just can't stand shooting with this camera and the struggle of working on the images. Luckily I'm not too heavily invested in the Sony ecosystem so I can change back to Canon or even Fuji

reviews.title: A Smooth Transition from Fujifilm X-T3
reviews.body: The Sony A7III with the 28-70mm f/3.5-5.6 kit lens has been a great transition for me from the Fujifilm X-T3. The first thing I noticed was how much simpler and more intuitive the menus and button layout are—getting used to it was effortless. While I do miss the X-T3’s 10-bit video capabilities, the full-frame experience is on another level in terms of depth and low-light performance. One of the most surprising aspects has been the battery life—it’s incredibly good. I initially thought about getting a spare battery, but for someone like me who isn’t doing heavy professional work, it doesn’t feel essential. The kit lens is decent for a beginner setup, offering good sharpness and versatility, but I can already tell it will be my first upgrade. I find myself needing a lens with a wider aperture for better low-light performance. So, the A7III feels like a solid upgrade.

title: KODAK PIXPRO AZ405 20MP Digital Camera, 40x Optical Zoom, AA, OIS, Black
bullet_points: Forty Times Optical Zoom for Close-Up Clarity from Any Distance: Bring distant subjects into sharp focus with forty times optical zoom and a twenty four mm wide angle lens that covers everything from sweeping group portraits to tight close-ups of birds in flight, athletes in action, and performers on stage—with genuine optical sharpness that no smartphone or lower-zoom camera can match

Twenty Megapixel Sensor for High-Resolution Photos Worth Keeping: A twenty MP CMOS sensor captures rich, detailed images with vibrant color across a range of shooting environments, producing photos sharp enough to print large, enlarge, and share from birthdays and vacations to wildlife outings and sports events with consistent, reliable results

Optical Image Stabilization Keeps Every Frame Sharp: Built-in OIS actively reduces the effect of involuntary hand movement at every zoom level, ensuring crisp, clear results even at full forty times reach without requiring a tripod; this makes a significant difference at sporting events, concerts, and any outdoor situation where you cannot physically move closer to your subject

Intuitive Controls with Automatic Scene Detection for Effortless Results: Multiple automatic shooting modes and smart scene detection handle the technical decisions so you can focus on composing the shot; full one thousand eighty p HD video records smooth travel clips and family moments, and the camera pairs with Class ten SD, SDHC, or SDXC memory cards up to five hundred twelve GB for a full day of shooting

AA Battery Convenience and Trusted KODAK Performance Built for Travelers: Power this bridge camera with standard AA batteries available at any store worldwide—no proprietary charger required, no worrying about outlet availability on a safari or cross-country road trip; backed by over a century of KODAK imaging heritage, the AZ405 is the dependable travel companion serious photographers trust to deliver every time

This is a great camera and you can download a much more detailed user manual than the one that came with the camera. I highly recommend this camera.

reviews.title: Stunning, feature packed digital camera, in a light, relatively small package
reviews.body: This camera is a Kodak, so I already had some pre-conceived ideas about what it should be able to do. It not only does everything I wanted it to do, but it does lots more. It is easy enough to use that an absolute beginner can use it right out of the box (almost - you need an SD card), but it is also complex enough to satisfy the needs of a seasoned pro photographer. The zoom is an incredible 40X, and is almost too much - at the max zoom, it is like holding a telescope in your hands and trying to keep it still enough to see - it is truly amazing and fun to play with. The image quality is right up there with much more expensive units. I would give this little camera more stars if I could. All these quality features at this price point? It's a no-brainer - if you need a camera, get this one! You won't be sorry.

reviews.title: DON'T BUY THIS CAMERA!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.body: This camera is terrible in every aspect and design, to get the SD card out you have to open the battery compartment, which when doing so you loose all the settings as in date and time on the camera and you have to completely reset everything. If you use the cord to download the pictures to your computer instead of taking out the card it drains the batteries very quickly. Even when not using the cord to download, the batteries drain very quickly, it's such an issue that it's one of the trouble shooting things that they have listed with this camera. There solution is to shut off any apps or things on the camera you're not using, tells you to turn down the brightness of the screen. Really your solution to this problem is to disable features that are on this camera, what's the point of having those features if when using them they drain the batteries very quickly. Let me explain what I use this camera for, to take pictures of items I sell on line. I put in a new set of energizer batteries, tested them with my ohm/volt tester, they tested 1.58 volts. I took 17 pictures downloaded them by using the cord and then I took 10 more pictures and the camera shut off and right before it did it said batteries expired. So I took the batteries out and tested them and they tested 1.28 volts, which will make most things still run, like my game cameras. There's definitely an issue with these cameras and the power they use and how fast they drain batteries. I've also have had it lock up and stop working several times and it wouldn't shut off or do anything, had to open up the battery compartment which takes all the power from the camera so it will reset and then close it and then turn it back on. I had a Sony Cyber shot which they don't make anymore, for over 10 years and I took literally thousands of pictures with it and it cost half as much and the pictures were clearer and of higher quality than what this camera is capable of taking. I would still be using the Sony, but some how it developed a gray spot that was showing up in all of my pictures and it was causing potential buyers to ask what that spot was on the item. So I had to stop using it and bought this camera thinking it would work great for what I was doing and also work great for taking pictures of nature and wildlife. I wish I would have sent it back right away, but I figured I would give it a chance to get better, because they said it would if I did the update. Well it's only gotten worse with time instead of better.

I tried to give this camera the benefit of the doubt and see if the video setting was any better than the photo. I admit this camera has decent quality, video recording but, after trying to view that same video on a computer(Lenovo- chrome book) I was unable to see the file or video. Which again became a big disappointment. Although I read the reviews before purchasing this camera I still had to give it a try for myself! After trying this camera out I would not primarily recommend this camera to any friends! I can say that you get what you paid for. This is a nice cheap camera which has potential if you’re invested in learning how to use it or invested in purchasing camera accessories to make your photos pop. 2/5 Stars.

reviews.title: A fantastic way to get into Full Frame without breaking the bank!
reviews.body: Finally, after waiting almost 20 years to jump into Full Frame, I elected to pull the trigger on the Canon RP. I've been shooting with various Micro 4/3, Fujifilm, and Canon EOS gear - love them all. But as I mentioned, I was always intrigued by Full Frame, but due top the high costs and size involved with that system, I deferred. After seeing the great deal for the RP and the 24-105 kit lens, I knew that this was the time. OK - right off the bat, the RP is a wonderful camera - well-built, yet very light and smallish. It's a delight to hold in the hand, and you have a variety of options. Now keep in mind, my style of photography involves scenic, architectural, portraits, and landscapes - all of which this RP handles quite well. If you're a fast moving sports enthusiast, or a birds-in-flight aficionado, then forget about this camera. I ordered mine with the RF 24-105 kit lens (not the L version) as part of a package deal and considering the cost vs performance ratio, this is a superb package price for the kit. The kit lens is fairly good, but like most kit lenses (but not all), the edges are a bit soft and fuzzy. You can get around some of that by setting the camera to an aperture of 8 and above. The center areas are quite sharp. The 24-105 MM range is superb and should endear itself to most photographers. I'd like to start saving for the F4L version of this lens to provide greater clarity across the frame - but in the meantime, this kit lens is really ideal. So overall, considering the price of this kid, the fact that it's full frame, includes a nice kit lens that would cost $400 separately, you can't go wrong here.

reviews.title: The perfect balance of beautiful video and beautiful photos
reviews.body: I previously had a Canon T3i and I absolutely loved that thing. It was amazing the results that camera could do for its time and I will always think it's one of the best budget cameras ever made. However, I've recently gotten more into video and that is one thing the T3i wasn't meeting my needs for. It was missing so many features like autofocus and modern video resolutions and frame rates. Therefore, my search for a new camera began. I seriously debated nearly every camera in this price range from every manufacturer. Sony, Fujifilm, Panasonic, you name it. However, it seemed like they all had one fatal flaw to them. Sony with their weird coloring, Fujifilm with the overheating issues, Panasonic with the awful autofocus. Some were better at photos, some were better at video. However, I needed something that would do great with both, as I wanted this to be something I could shoot professional portraits with but also shoot vlogs. At the end of the day, all signs pointed to this camera, and I'm so glad this is the one I chose. I'm not a super-advanced user, however, I do think I've moved past the beginner stage of photography and videography. I think this camera really fits me perfectly as I'm not incredibly overwhelmed with options and features that I don't know how to use, but it still has a ton of capability that allows me to learn more about photography and videography. I've also just been using the 24-105 kit lens that comes with this bundle on Amazon. The video on this is amazing. HUGE step up from the T3i. The face detecting autofocus works great and nearly all of my shots are perfectly in focus unless it's super dark which it has a little more of a struggle with but obviously any camera would. I was a little hesitant about the fairly disabled 4k capability with this camera due (disabled dual pixel AF, crop factor, 30 min time limit, 24 fps max) especially since other cameras in the price range have a more robust 4k capability. However, I've found that 1080p meets my needs just fine and looks absolutely gorgeous. It's also much more friendly on the file size and processing in video editing. The photo capability has shocked me even more than the video. I knew this would obviously be a great camera for photos, but I didn't realize what a step up from my T3i it would be. I honestly thought my T3i photos would look just about as good as this camera since the T3i does admittedly take amazing photos. However, this blows it out of the water. The autofocus on this is SO much better. With the T3i, fast moving subjects were nearly impossible to get in focus. This does so much better. The full-frame sensor on this camera makes a huge difference too. The low light performance is so much better and the size of these photos is insane. You can zoom in to the photos so much and it's still amazingly clear. As for the body of the camera itself, it feels incredibly well made. Grabbing my T3i now feels like a cheap plastic toy compared to this thing. It feels very solid and durable. The grip on the camera is incredibly easy and comfortable to hold. The only negative thing I've encountered so far is the kit lens that comes with this bundle doesn't have a physical switch between autofocus and manual focus. You have to go into the camera settings to switch between them. I don't find myself doing this very often as the autofocus is amazing but when I do need manual focus it's a little bit of an inconvenience. Overall, it's an amazing camera and I'm very happy that I went with this one.

reviews.title: Beautiful camera for beginners and intermediate
reviews.body: I have been thinking of replacing my t4i for a few years and I'm glad I did. Most of the negative reviews must be from serious/pro photographers who would be better served with the higher end R camera ($$$). However, I mostly take pictures of my family, vacations, and maybe the occasional scenery shot. The auto focus is very fast and it can continuously autofocus for example when your kid charges at you to see what picture you just took, you can just keep clicking. Our first trip was to the beach and I was blown away by the pictures. My T4i is a bit old at this point, but I didn't realize how old it was until i upgraded to the RP. Beaches have a lot of backlight reflected from the sand and water which causes people to appear as shadows. But even on auto, people's faces are bright, easy to see, and in focus and the background behind them isn't washed out. I had a much higher percentage of in focus, well balanced images to choose from than my old camera. I ended up getting the lens with the RP as well and even though my old lens had slightly better specs, I had no problems with the new lens (maybe because the body is so much better than my old camera). I would definitely buy this again given the choice.

reviews.title: Cumple con lo especificado y detalles extras.
reviews.body: Compre esta cámara buscando mejores imágenes y cumple con el objetivo. De pasar a una cámara APS a una Full Frame fue un salto considerable, por el precio esta bastante bien, puede tomar ráfagas de 43 fotografías seguidas en archivos RAWs, tiene intervalometro con programación incorporado para hacer timelaps, fotografía HDR, video en RAW. Eso sí, se ocupa una memoria de alta velocidad para absorber los datos tan pesados, pero con memorias más económicas se puede grabar a 1080p 60fps y tomar las fotografías RAWs sin problemas. Otra cosa, es muy ligera comparadas con cámaras 5D, 6D, etc. Hasta las cámaras 70D, 80D son más pesadas comparadas con la RP, cosa que me asustó un poco cuando llegó un paquete muy grande y no pesaba casi nada. Nota: Compren baterías extras, porque son muy pequeñas y no duran tanto como los de los modelos anteriores. 10/10 Recomendada para quienes quieran empezar con cámaras Full Frame.
reviews.body_en: I bought this camera looking for better images and it meets the objective. Going from an APS camera to a Full Frame camera was a considerable leap, for the price it is quite good, it can take bursts of 43 consecutive photographs in RAW files, it has an Intervalometer with built-in programming to make timelapses, HDR photography, RAW video. Of course, high-speed memory is required to absorb such heavy data, but with cheaper memories you can record at 1080p 60fps and take RAW photographs without problems. Another thing, it is very light compared to 5D, 6D, etc. cameras. Even the 70D, 80D cameras are heavier compared to the RP, which scared me a little when a very large package arrived and it weighed almost nothing. Note: Buy extra batteries, because they are very small and do not last as long as the previous models. 10/10 Recommended for those who want to start with Full Frame cameras.

reviews.title: Best and still the cheapest full-frame camera out there
reviews.body: Been using the RP for more than a year now. What made me go for the RP is its affordability, i can still say now in 2025 that the RP is still the cheapest full-frame camera in the market. It's worth every money spent! Pros: -Cheapest FF -Decent Sensor Size -Its a canon -face detection -focus is fast but this will only be noticeable on RF lenses. -perfect option for still shots. -very light compared to other full-frame mirrorless cameras out there. Cons: -Its a canon RF mount, this means very limited lens option as of now unless you get an EF adapter. -no IBIS -no animal eye detection -no mechanical shutter, closing the shutters while changing lenses wont be an option. -battery can be an issue if shooting video (very limited video capabilities for 2025). Final thoughts: Though there are some limitations on the RP, it is okay so as this is marketed as an entry camera to full-frame. I would definitely not buy another one, as there is no point. I would invest on the higher tier canon bodies. But i definitely not regret getting the RF as this has been fantastic starter even with the limitations.
reviews.body_en: Been using the RP for more than a year now. What made me go for the RP is its affordability, i can still say now in 2025 that the RP is still the cheapest full-frame camera in the market. It's worth every money spent! Pros: -Cheapest FF -Decent Sensor Size -Its a canon -face detection -focus is fast but this will only be noticeable on RF lenses. -perfect option for still shots. -very light compared to other full-frame mirrorless cameras out there. Cons: -Its a canon RF mount, this means very limited lens option as of now unless you get an EF adapter. -no IBIS -no animal eye detection -no mechanical shutter, closing the shutters while changing lenses wont be an option. -battery can be an issue if shooting video (very limited video capabilities for 2025). Final thoughts: Though there are some limitations on the RP, it is okay so as this is marketed as an entry camera to full-frame. I would definitely not buy another one, as there is no point. I would invest on the higher tier canon bodies. But i definitely not regret getting the RF as this has been fantastic starter even with the limitations.
