reviews.title: I love this French Press!
reviews.body: I have been using this French Press daily for over a month and love it. The 18oz size is perfect for one generous cup of coffee. Once you've experienced a well made French Press cup of coffee you will never go back to your old method. The duel basket allows for using beans ground for drip coffee, which is incredibly convenient. The novelty of grinding your own beans wears off quickly, at least it did for me when I ventured into French Press years ago. Traditionally, French Press calls for a course ground, not the grind you find in prepackaged grounds, that being the main reason I went back to drip. An added bonus is the ability to use a paper filter. Not only does it ensure no grounds end up in your cup, it also traps the coffee oils which can contribute to increasing cholesterol levels, in the event that is a concern. Granted, a cup a day is no big deal, but if you indulge throughout the day it may be. You can purchase the pre-cut filters made to size, however I found could purchasing generic filters at the store and cut several at a time to size for a fraction of the cost of the pre-cut ones. The Press comes with a few pre-cut filters, I just saved one to use as a guide. I saw some reviews stating that the carafe was hard to clean. I simply scoop out the grounds with a rubber spatula into the trash, pretty simple. If you have a garbage disposal keep in mind that coffee grounds are not it's friend. Yor plumber may not thank you for putting most of the grounds in the trash, but your pocketbook will!

reviews.title: Quirky little guy
reviews.body: It has its quirks for sure, but I'm happy with the performance at the price point. The first quirk is that it will always overheat if you use the steamer first, so you need to run a single shot somehow. I like to make a double, so it's annoying to have to run a single first and then do the double. This would work out though if you prefer to do a single--you can just press single twice and have your single made. It's the only way to clear the overheat warning though. Second quirk is that while the touch screen is nice in theory, the buttons are hard to press and hard to line up with. I usually end up unplugging it and starting over just to press the buttons. Classic buttons would work best here in my opinion. Otherwise, I am pleased with the level of foam in my drinks and the steamer does work very nicely after it spits out the residual water. For this issue , I just set a mug under it and let it spit out the water for the first 2 to 3 seconds and then put milk/cream under there so it's not watered down. It is very light and airy and a very nice thing to have at home. There was a comment about the clearance under the portafilter, but my favorite mug fits under there nicely, so no complaints on that end.

reviews.title: Incredible value! Makes café-quality espresso right on my counter.

I was looking for something that could make a genuine, bold espresso without costing a fortune, and this machine delivers on every level. It is sleek, compact, and fits perfectly on my counter without taking up too much space. The best part is the quality of the shots—it pulls a rich, dark espresso with a beautiful layer of crema every single time. I use it with fine-ground espresso (Cafe La Llave is my favorite), and the flavor is consistently bold and smooth, never burnt. The steam wand is also a huge plus; it froths milk quickly for lattes and cappuccinos that taste just like the ones from a coffee shop. For the price, you honestly cannot beat the performance. If you are on the fence, just buy it. It has completely upgraded my morning routine!

reviews.title: The double filters on this mean you don't need as good a grinder
reviews.body: I bought this along with a super high-quality grinder, and discovered that I kinda only needed one or the other. The mesh filters are fine enough on this that you can get away with a relatively crappy grinder. You can even use regular pre-ground coffee, and it'll come out okay. With a normal glass/single layer mesh press, using regular grounds will result in actual sludge in the bottom of your cup. With this unit, the Costco bulk ground coffee will leave some fines in your cup, but will work fine otherwise; the second layer of screening is good enough to keep the sludge at bay. If, on the other hand, you have a high quality, consistent grinder, you can buy a less expensive press and do fine. That said, pairing this with a good grinder makes absolutely *splendid* coffee. You don't necessarily need both, but I doubt you'll regret the purchase. The double filters can also help you calibrate your grinder; if the inner filter is getting many grounds on it, you probably want a slightly coarser grind. This unit is tall and skinny, and does better with a tall sink for cleaning. If you're trying to rinse it out upstairs in a standard bathroom sink, you should be able to do it, but it'll take a little maneuvering. The actual cleaning process is very easy, although you do have to clean two little baskets instead of one. It takes a wee bit longer than cleaning a standard press. The build quality seems good. Oh, one other note: because of the filter design, you end up with some coffee left in the bottom that you can't drink. You're using a more water than normal, so it takes more grounds than you're probably expecting. Further, French presses need more grounds for the same amount of coffee, because they're ground coarse and use a shorter brewing time. (normally 4 minutes.) I use six tablespoons of coffee per batch, and I get two 16-ounce cups out of it. With my older drip brewer, it took only four tablespoons. In exchange, the quality is *vastly* better, you can use almost any grounds, and after you've plunged it, the coffee stays excellent for at least an hour. Seems well worth it to me, but if your coffee budget is small, the higher consumption might be something to consider.

reviews.title: White Espro7 18oz: a great upgrade with some trade offs
reviews.body: TLDR: hotter longer, much less grit, harder to clean, high minimum brew requirements, poor powder coat finish, great customer service. I bought this as an upgrade to my body glass French press. Overall it is a much better press. It’s hotter longer and the dual filters do a fantastic job. Before, at the end of my coffee, it was almost unbearable. It was like gritty sludge. It was like drinking dirt. Now with the espro 7, it’s much less, and what does get through is so fine, that I can drink the last drop. It’s hotter longer, but it’s not vacuum insulated. It stays hot for 1 hour, warm after another 30 minutes. After that its Luke warm. It’s harder to clean but not by much. With glass, I can just rinse and dump it out, set it to dry and it’s good to go. By comparison, the espro filters clean very easily. In fact, the long term maintenance is probably easier. But the stainless steel press doesn’t rinse as easily. It might still have some residue and require a brush on daily use. My biggest gripe about this is the high minimum requirements. I usually just brew enough to make one cup, but this requires 2 tablespoons of grounds and enough for 1 and a half cups of coffee. The way the filter is, it seems like more water gets trapped in the bottom, and that’s why it needs more water. It’s not a big deal, but I grind my beans each use, so it doubles my grinding time and consumes my beans faster. These are bigger and heavier than a glass press. My powder coat was chipped under the handle and even had some rust built up on it. I contacted the company directly and they’re sending me a new one free of charge. And I get to keep the old one! (which still works just fine) Also the lid is painted white, but it’s plastic and not a sturdy powder coat. It scuffs easily after just a couple days of use. I believe the stainless steel (no powder coat) option has a stainless steel lid. The video attached shows what very little grit does make it into the cup. The picture shows the grit stuck between the two filters. The second picture shows the chipped paint.

reviews.title: Aero Press vs Espro P7
reviews.body: Aero Press vs Espro P7. So I bought both products but at different times. Aero Press I have been using for about 3 years or so. It’s great. Very easy to use, you buy these paper filters that fit easily at the bottom. Then put the container over a cup and push the plunger down. Can’t get much easier and as important the coffee is good to very good. Also, I would give the ease of cleaning up a Solid 10 !!! Why because you just unscrew the bottom piece counter clock wise and then put the coffee plunger over your garbage can and push the plunger all the way down. The coffee grounds and paper filter just drop out. Rinse the plunger and container and you are ready for another smooth cup of Joe. So Espro P7 is better at the amount of coffee pressed since it is 18 oz. The coffee is also good to very good. It’s easy to make also. But the clean up….. wow this is a sloppy cleanup. The plunger comes out but what is left behind is a wet, wet mess. No way does it come out easily in the garbage can. You have to either use multiple paper towels or rinse the container under the kitchen sink without getting the left over coffee grinds down the drain. No way Ray is that going to work. Bottom line buy the extra large Aero Press and enjoy a good to better cup of coffee with awesome clean up no fuss, no mess, no clogged drains. Just my opinion.

reviews.title: Looks Great, Works Great, Tastes Great
reviews.body: I got this coffee maker a little over 2 years ago, mainly because of its aesthetics, specifically the design and layout were visually pleasing to me compared to other coffee makers. Also all my appliances are black and stainless. On the two cup setting, it takes about 6 minutes to brew. When it's done the coffee is really hot, and I have to wait about 5 minutes before drinking it, or drop in an ice cube and I can start drinking in about 30 seconds to a minute. I found a combination of things with this coffee maker that turns a good cup of coffee into a great one. The ninja branded measuring spoon that comes with it is more important than you might think. They've literally hit the nail on the head regarding the exact amount of coffee grounds that should be used. It's very simple, one flat scoop for every standard size cup of coffee you want, and remember the word flat. Also there's markers on the water tank so scoops and water match up. I personally found if I use a flat scoop of coffee grounds, not letting the coffee grounds be higher than that, it tastes perfect every time for me. So I would say that's a huge key to a great cup of coffee on this device. Next up, paper filters improved the taste significantly! The goldish mesh metal filter that comes in the box does not filter out all the coffee grounds. I even tried other brands of metal filters to see if they improved that, but it didn't. You will likely have some coffee grounds in the bottom of your coffee cup if you stick with the included metal reusable filter. At first I didn't think it was very many coffee grounds, but then one day I immediately poured the coffee into a glass after brewing it. Then I held the glass above my head and shined a flashlight at the bottom, and there were a lot more grounds that I saw that way, than when I was getting close to finishing a cup of coffee. Meaning, I was likely swallowing a lot of grounds and would have never known that. So I stopped using the Ninja metal filter and started buying and trying #4 cone paper filters and that did 4 things. 1. No more coffee grounds in my coffee cup. 2. No more upset stomach after drinking coffee. 3. The oily stuff that kind of floated to the top of the coffee was gone. 4. The taste of the coffee significantly improved. I would strongly suggest trying a box of paper filters to see if it improves the taste for you. Do not attempt to use a paper filter and the mesh filter at the same time. I tried that once and it significantly reduces the flow of the coffee out of the filter area. This causes the water to build up in that filter area and overflow from there on to your countertop. In closing, this is a good coffee maker, but if you use flat scoops, a good brand of paper filters, and purified water, I think those might be the keys to turning a good cup of coffee into a great one.

reviews.title: Clear, detachable reservoir separates this coffee maker from the masses.
reviews.body: I've owned this coffee maker over a month now and love it. Intuitive-to-operate controls and a very attractive appearance are among its virtues. Of course, hot water dripping over coffee grinds isn't rocket science and is something most coffee makers do comparably well, and the Ninja likewise makes excellent-tasting coffee. Other reviews were mildly critical of the "sneak a cup" functionality, but I've found it on par with that of my last two coffee makers (Krups and Cuisinart). Yes, a couple of drops of coffee will still splash on the hot plate while you pull the carafe out, but I've never used or seen a pot yet that didn't do that, and the spring mechanism on this carafe is at least as robust as any I've seen on other coffee makers. Where this pot really shines is in the clear, detachable water reservoir. That obviously offers you the (completely?) unique option of detaching the tank to fill it over the sink before brewing, which I've done a few times and anticipated doing regularly. Frankly, however, I find it unnecessary because the reservoir itself provides an unusually large opening/target for pouring directly from my filtered water pitcher. But there are other benefits to the reservoir design, including the fact that it allows you to easily monitor the conditions inside . . . i.e., when the moist environment inevitably leads to mildew, you will know it (and, because the reservoir is transparent to any ambient sunlight, mold/mildew should theoretically take longer to manifest in many kitchens.) More importantly, you'll be able to easily clean the reservoir in a sink of hot soapy water (with a little bleach) without repeated electric cleaning and rinse cycles for the whole brewer, followed by awkward attempts to wipe the nooks and crannies of the integral, typically black reservoir with a white paper towel to see if any undesirable residues remain. But perhaps the greatest advantage of this design is in what it will save you if you should *ahem* forget to put your carafe in place before you hit "brew." I've only done this twice in my life but, ironically, both times occurred within the last six weeks: once with my last Krups pot and once with this new Ninja. (Put aside for the moment what such forgetfulness might be saying about me.:-) At the very least, I gained valuable, first-hand experience in how the Ninja's design saved my a$$ while the typical integral design on the Krups resulted in a ruined coffee maker, which prompted my purchase of the Ninja in the first place.) When you fail to put the carafe under the filter spout on a coffee maker that offers the increasingly ubiquitous "sneak a cup" feature, the spring mechanism on the filter holder is never engaged and the water that's dripping down over your grinds to make coffee is never given proper egress below. So your mistake may go unnoticed for quite some time since you won't hear the kind of gushing and sizzling sound that an older model without the sneak a cup feature would produce when dripping coffee is merrily dispensing and burning on the naked hotplate below. Instead, the water stays in the filter holder, eventually having nowhere to go but over the sides, which, on the vast majority of drip coffee makers, means that the brewed coffee--complete with floating grinds--will spill over and back into the reservoir itself. That is exactly what happened to my Krups, and, despite hours of repeated cleaning cycles and an aborted effort to dismantle the innards, I realized the pot was shot (no pun intended) and would never process water properly through its (clogged) pump pathway again. Enter the Ninja. After making delicious coffee for a week or so, I, once again, got distracted by something (probably my Yorkie yapping to get out for a morning pee) and neglected to actually seat the carafe on the coffee maker before hitting brew. When I got back in, I noticed the problem just before the brewing coffee was about to overflow the filter holder. The difference was, even had I been a bit later, I would have only had to deal with a messy countertop and not a ruined $80+ coffee maker. In other words, if the Ninja coffee filter overflows, the brewed coffee will NOT go back into the reservoir because the latter is physically higher and isolated from the former in a way that would not permit that. So, should you repeat my negligence, you will hear coffee suddenly dripping on your hotplate and counter top, but you won't have to buy a new coffee maker. The only "negative" to the pot is that the carafe lid does not flip up via the common thumb depression above the handle. You have to slide/turn it to remove, which is more easily done with two hands. But this is a very, very minor ding in my view and not worth deducting a star for an otherwise very well-designed, highly practical, and elegant-looking appliance.

reviews.body: I've been using this coffee maker every day for over a month, and I have zero complaints. The coffee comes out consistently great, and since I usually brew 4 cups, the Small Batch setting has been perfect. I use disposable paper filters instead of the included reusable one because it's more convenient for me to just throw them away after brewing. Cleanup is quick and easy. reviews.title: Actually does improve the flavor of coffee compared to others. Capable, but not super well designed
reviews.body: UPDATE: For our second brew, I ran it on "Classic" instead of "Rich". I really was a significantly superior brew. It tasted good with the old machine, but really fine with this one. Now after over a week of use- it's a consistent result every day, and a cup of coffee is, indeed, superior with this machine and all else being equal. I found another issue, though. There's a gap between the back of the carafe lid and the handle. Steam escapes there, and it gets very hot. I have fairly large hands and I tend to put my thumb there. I have gotten burned a couple of times. It's painful but not long lasting. It's not the steam alone, but the fact that the little bit of steam heats the material for the entire brew time plus serving time. Cleaning is getting burdensome. The carafe needs a re-design. I got this to replace (?) a very basic Mr. Coffee that is about 5 years old, that is one of my favorite examples of design. It's as simple as can be: an on/off switch and a carafe that is capacious and very easy and fast to clean. It has very few right angle areas that would make it hard to clean. (They have changed the design since we bought it, and not for the better.) It still works. This Ninja is nice, and the filter basket will barely sit on the scale while I weigh the grounds into it, but it's going to tip over, and often. Once the coffee is made, you can't pour all of it from the carafe, because the plastic rim extends around the edge and into the lip, and it has a square edge. The lid of the carafe, has a strange pipe that extends to near the bottom of the pot. Why? You'd have to use a round brush to clean it well. I've made one pot of coffee so far. I used the rich setting. My wife liked it, but I thought it was much more bitter than yesterday's coffee. It was visibly darker (remember, I weigh the grounds, so that's constant). I found the liquid measure to be the same as the coffee make we've been using. Tomorrow I will try the "classic" setting. I don't really need another clock to set, or a timer, or really any of the features this sports beyond "on/off". I will also mention that the reservoir works well. But it's clear plastic. So with our regular water, it will get mineral spots (and it's virtually impossible to clean with all the strange grooves and right angles). So we have to use distilled water. I like a spotless kitchen. (The reservoir in the old one doesn't need hand cleaning because it's mostly black plastic with a frosted window to gauge water level. It much much easier to see the water level with this Ninja, though.)

reviews.body: I've had the 12 cup model for about 1.5 years now and have been happy with it. It brews good coffee, is easy to use and easy to clean. My only complaints are the buttons are somewhat "stiff" to press compared to my old Cuisinart and the printing is rather small for older eyes but not an issue on a daily basis. I broke the carafe about a year ago and it was pricey to replace but at least it was available. My favorite feature is the removable reservoir which makes it simple to keep clean. I like to get it ready to brew the night before and my old Cuisinart would get microbial gunk growing in the reservoir which was extremely difficult clean out and probably not healthy. No such issue with the Ninja. I just leave the lid off the reservoir after brewing and it drys out very quickly. Plus it is easy to clean out if needed.

reviews.title: Compact, Quiet, and Still Going Strong After a Year
reviews.body: This Keurig single-serve coffee maker has been great for everyday use, especially if you don’t want a large machine taking up counter space. I’ve had mine for over a year, use it every day, and it still works just as reliably as it did when I first got it. It brews incredibly quickly, usually in around 30 seconds or less, and it’s surprisingly quiet while running. I also love how small and lightweight it is. It’s easy to move around, pack up, or take somewhere else when needed, so portability is definitely one of its strongest features. I’ve had no issues using different pod options with it. It works with the regular coffee pods I buy, including Starbucks, as well as the reusable pod options I’ve tried. I like having the flexibility to use either prefilled pods or my own coffee without needing separate equipment. Pros: * Excellent space-saving design * Very quiet * Brews in around 30 seconds * Small and lightweight * Extremely portable * Works with multiple pod options * Compatible with reusable pods * Easy to use * Reliable for daily use * Still working great after more than a year Overall: This has proven to be a really dependable little coffee maker. I use it every single day, it takes up barely any room, and I can have coffee ready incredibly quickly. reviews.title: Very disappointed.
reviews.body: First, an introduction, this will take some going through, bear with me. First, I had refused for years to get a Keurig, as I did not feel the quality and richness of a good strong cup of coffee was possible. But I finally got tired of trying other methods of brewing, from using a regular single cup espresso maker, moka pot, pour over, French press... I finally opted for the ease of a Keurig mini-plus. Coffee was ...eh... I switched coffee brands, to what I feel has to be the best commercial brand. And the coffee was EXcellenT! About a year later, despite regular cleaning cycles, the thing just stopped working. I tried to take it apart, watched some youtube videos which just solidified the fact that the company made these non-serviceable. P.O.'d at this obvious tactic to sell more, I waited a few weeks, but went and got another one. Same deal a year later. Another one. This last one gave me signs before ending it's own life. I would have to run several cycles where nothing would come out... till finally something... drip... by drip... several hours later, the thing would start running again, only to stop again the next day or two. Finally, it just died. So I REFUSED to get another. These things are ridiculous, right? So I got a new French press. Coffee is great!! But... omg... what a pain cleaning that thing every.... single... time... I mean, really, it's no big deal. But, it CAn be. So I saw this thing on sale, I thought, well, it's HAlf the price of the other ones... and I def want something different this time. Cut to now.... This thing has SEVERAL issues that I don't like. First of all, it is a thinner cheaper plastic, and has a cheap looking shine to it. Ok, I'm over it. The plastic... I mean, can't they make these things with glass reservoirs.... the plastic reservoir has screws on the inside of it. I don't care if they say it is food safe... Plastic is also considered food safe... but that doesn't mean it is.. those are just bureaucratic rhetoric lies. But I digress,...So this coffee maker has an adjustment for high altitude... is THAT what ruined my previous Keurigs? High altitude? Hmmm. Ok, so maybe that's a plus. It also has different sizes that you can choose -8,10, & 12 oz. With the mini-plus, you choose the size by the amount of water you pour in. That means that this one measures what it sucks in. Hmmm. The mini-plus had the controls on the top. Easy peasy. This one has the controls on the side. It also doesn't have rubber feet on the bottom. So when you try to push the buttons, the thing slides away from you. Impossible to push any buttons with one hand, you have to use two. Even with rubber feet, you have to use two hands. I'm not a paraplegic, but it's rather stupid to have to hold the thing to press a button or two, or three. Which is what you have to do. It's just really awkward because you really have to hold it in the back to keep it from moving when you press the button in front. And you have to do that without touching the reservoir, which will pop out if you tried that. But let's get to the coffee. So with the mini-plus, the first liquid out of the machine, was dark coffee. As it was finishing, the coffee would be a little more clear, but not pure water. With this machine, for the first few seconds, it is spewing out crystal clear WATER. I don't even know how that is possible. But this, it does. It also claims to be faster than the mini-cup. I hestitate to say "brews faster", because it doesn't brew, Keurigs simply spew water into and through the k-cup, it's a pressurized system, not a true brewing system. And it definitely IS faster. And that's a problem, as evidenced by the watery coffee that it spews out. Sure enough, the "coffee" tastes like water. This is the 8 oz brew, mind you, with the machine set to "strong". I first tried the 12oz, and ended up pouring it down the sink. The 8 oz wasn't much better. My next step is to switch out cups while it's pouring out the water at the beginning of the cycle and see if I can get a stronger "brew". All in all, it's convenient enough. But it will sit on my counter, mostly unused, for when I have those really lazy, sleepy, or sick days, when all I want to do is pop in a capsule, and deal with the rest of it... Very disappointed. Perhaps if you live in a low altitude area, the mini-plus would work for you. I really do recommend that one above this.

reviews.title: Most excellent
reviews.body: I got this to replace my original Keurig. The old k50 or whatever it was. This thing takes up less space, looks more sleek, and works better than the original. It's faster, the coffee tastes better, it has the strong button. Also, I keep my coffee maker in my bedroom, and with the old one if you wanted it to be ready to make a quick cup of coffee it had to be turned on which meant that it had lights illuminated. I had to cover them with tape. This new one can go from being turned off to making a quick cup of coffee immediately. And after 5 minutes it automatically turns any illumination off. That means it doesn't make light in my bedroom at night. It's just a way way better version. It's quieter. I love it I'm so glad I got it. I will say that I got this brand new, and it was a really good deal, and I can see why because the manual includes an offer for discounted coffee that expired over two years ago. I'm guessing Keurig punched out a few too many of these models and they've been sitting in a warehouse for too many years. My advice is buy it now before it goes out of stock. It is an excellent coffee maker.

reviews.title: Practical, economical, and quite good at what it does!
reviews.body: Neither my husband nor I are coffee drinkers, but we have many family members who are. We had an old Mr. Coffee who should have been called, "Mr. Reliable." Since he was getting on in years, we felt it wise to invest in an economical, low-tech, potential work-horse of a coffee maker primarily for guests and entertaining. Enter Amazon, research, and reviews finally deciding on this model. Now please do not mourn for Mr. Coffee, he is still with us residing in the pantry for emergency service when needed. This particular Hamilton Beach model fit the bill of reasonably priced, low-tech, easy to use and clean, and hardworking from a well established and reliable company. Mr. Hamilton Beach has been in our employ for almost 3 years now, and what an outstanding employee he has been. He has served at multiple parties and family gatherings; he has hosted many, many house guests, and has reliably made coffee when asked to do so. We have no complaints about this faithful servant. The programmable feature, the Select-a-Brew component, the attractive look, and certainly not least of all the delicious coffee others always comment upon when served have all contributed to the enjoyment and functionality of this attractive, unobtrusive coffee maker. The 24 hour preprogramming coupled with the 2 hour shut off give peace of mind whenever it is in use. The swing out basket makes cleaning simple and easy. There have been no malfunctions, leaks, discolorations, or chips or cracks in the carafe. All in all, Mr. Hamilton Beach Programmable Coffee has been a great addition to our kitchen staff! reviews.title: Don't be afraid to buy this coffee maker. :)
reviews.body: I regularly read all the negative reviews first to see what the complaints actually are. In many cases, that has kept us from purchasing something of inferior quality. And, of course, sometimes a product is a lemon, so the negative reviews are justified. BUT, many complaints are often very subjective for whatever reason and have little to do with the product's quality or ability to perform properly (i.e., cord is shorter than they like, a button isn't in the right place, it doesn't have this bell or this whistle, etc.). And to be blunt, some folks either don't read and/or understand the product's directions and end up using it improperly, which can damage or shorten it's life-expectancy. Anyway, we ordered this Hamilton Beach coffee maker after reading a boatload of negative AND positive reviews. It worked perfectly out of the box, and, using the SAME coffee we always use, it made a better-tasting brew than the one it replaced (Black and Decker). We just read directions carefully, set it up properly, and made sure we put the carafe where it is supposed to be on the plate so the spring-loaded nozzle actually lines up with the hole in the carafe lid (so there would be no leaks or drips --about which some people complained). No problems. SO...don't be afraid to order this product. It's fine. :)

reviews.title: short lifespan, bottom-of-the-line features, and -extremely- prone to spilling while brewing
reviews.body: I used this machine daily for 17 months. Then, quite suddenly, it died: it wouldn't pump water or heat coffee. 17 months is a very short lifespan for a coffee machine. (Another of my Hamilton Beach machines also lasted a little less than 18 months. Perhaps the entire brand suffers from durability issues.) This machine's coffee is as good as the coffee I've had from $50 Hamilton Beach machines. But I regret buying this machine, and indeed, I am never going to buy another Hamilton Beach product. In so many ways, this machine's features are limited or poorly implemented: 1) Extremely prone to spilling coffee all over your countertop. This is not a problem with the carafe; instead, it's a problem with the spring-loaded nozzle that transmits coffee from the machine to the carafe. About once every three months, this Hamilton Beach machine (and others that I've had) floods my countertop. Many other reviewers have detailed this problem: see "Hamilton Beach strikes out again" (which has the best detail), "flow cutoff sucks, leaks", "Coffee Goes All Over the Counter", and more. See also the picture at the bottom of this review. A recommended solution is to use a little less ground coffee than you normally would, and then to use the machine's "bold" setting. But this hasn't stopped my machine from flooding on occasion. This alone is a fatal or near-fatal flaw. But there is more... 2) Water reservoir: not removable (and thus difficult to wash). Also, the water gauge, which lets you see how much water is in the reservoir, appears on only one side of the reservoir -- rather than both sides, as with many other machines. Depending on how you position this machine on your countertop, you may need to bend at an odd angle to see the gauge. 3) Carafe: before making coffee, you push it into the machine so that it sits atop the holder, just as with most other coffee machines. But if you push it in as far as it can go, you have gone too far; the carafe won't be well positioned, and your coffee will spill outside the carafe. (But the carafe itself is better than the carafes from Hamilton Beach machines of a few years ago, because it's less likely to spill when pouring.) 4) LED indicator lights: they're white, which makes it a little more difficult to see whether they're on during the daytime. Any other color would have been better. 5) Power cord: not retractable, as it is on other low-cost coffee machines. As a result, the power cord will spill out over your countertop at least a little. 6) Buttons: they are very shallow and stiff; they require too much force to press. Again, it's not a huge problem. But to press the power button or any other button when the carafe is less than half-full, you need to firmly hold the machine itself with one hand, while pressing the button with a finger of your other hand. If you just attempt to press a button without holding the machine in place or otherwise anchoring it, you'll simply tip the machine over onto its side. 7) Battery backup: there is none. If you lose power for a second, or unplug your machine just for a moment, you will need to reset the current time, the time at which you want coffee-making to start (if you use that feature), and any special settings that you have. This isn't easy, as Hamilton Beach doesn't make it simple for you to set the time or, especially, the time at which you want coffee-making to start. This machine is worse than you would hope, even given the low price. And the flooding problem, while it happens to me only once every three months or so, is terrible when it does happen. Avoid Hamilton Beach.

reviews.title: AMAZING PRODUCT & CUSTOMER SERVICE TEAM! (What more could you ask for?)
reviews.body: Let me tell you about how AMAZING not only their products are but, also how AMAZING they are as a company! I bought my duo March 28, 2025. This past Saturday we woke up to our coffee pot no longer working && giving us an error code. My spouse && I done all sorts of trouble shooting for HOURS working on this coffee maker. I finally gave up! I was shocked because I had owned Keurig before && they ALWAYS held up. I caved && called customer service. They was SHOCKED to hear that this coffee pot was only a few months old! They tried to help me troubleshoot it as well. Just a few steps && they couldn’t get it either. The customer service guy sent me a link to send my proof of purchase && I had to wait for them to look it all over. Within 24 hours I was approved for my warranty && of course the next day was Sunday. It’s now TUESDAY && my coffee pot is here! I’ve never seen a name brand company ship a product so fast! THANK YOU KEURIG && THANK YOUR CUSTOMER SERVICE TEAM! I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THEIR PRODUCTS! They stand behind them 100%! I got this coffee pot when my k-cup coffee maker I had bought a year ago went out. (That’s a different story.) I got this specific maker because my spouse loves a pot every morning before before he goes to work && I like to use the single side occasionally for my drinks! I have SPOILED him with this Keurig && I absolutely BABY this coffee pot! He tells me all the time every cup is just as good as the very first. (If you keep it very clean && well maintained yours will do the same!) When this went out you would have thought he lost his best friend! Needless to say he was ecstatic when I told him the new coffee pot come in today! I will always buy Keurig from here on out! You couldn’t ask for a better product. (My was obviously a flunk. That happens occasionally with ANY product.) You also couldn’t ask for a better customer service!

reviews.title: MORE AND MORE, Continuous issues, only 30 days old, DO NOT BUY THIS MACHINE!!
reviews.body: I bought this on Jan 2 and have been using it for only 24 days. Today I continued to get a "add water" message (with a full tank) and "error 8" message followed by "dry". I cleaned the tank and re-filled several times and unplugged the machine to re-set it as online has indicated. I was finally able to get the machine to brew. Mind you this is a brand new machine and after 24 days has issues. I use filtered water so this should not be an issue. I have notified Keurig to see if there are solutions to fix these issues. I will keep this rating updated, but use caution when purchasing this machine. EDIT: So I have been able to get the coffee machine to work once again. After getting errors, I unplugged the machine for a period of time, flushed out the water tank, and plugged it back in with fresh water. I was able to get it to function normally for the past several days. I use the timer and it have brewed coffee without issue for a few days. The single use side is functioning normally. Don't know if unplugging it reset whatever chip is inside but it works for now. If it continues to function normally over the next few months I will change my star rating. For now, I am skeptical of long term use. 02/08/25 UPDATE: DO NOT BUY THIS MACHINE!!!!!!!! I experienced same issues as listed about. Tried to repeat the "fix" three times without success. Contacted Keurig, but I am not optimistic I will receive a full refund. Amazon also closed my ability for a return on 02/01/2025, so I now can ONLY DEAL WITH KEURIG. If I could give zero stars I would. 02/28/25 ANOTHER UPDATE: Was able to finally get Keurig to send me another machine on 02/16/25. On 02/28/25, I received the new machine. Unpacked and carefully followed the directions to the "T". Plugged in the machine as directed and it failed to turn on. Tried a different outlet, nothing. Tried another machine and it powered up without issues. Not an outlet problem. It was clearly a machine problem walked around the house trying the machine on various outlets, nothing. Called Keurig and they ran through troubleshooting, nothing. Machine DEAD ON ARRIVAL. They tried to tell me since this was a warranty replacement machine, it no longer was subject to warranty. EVEN THOUGH THIS MACHINE WAS DEAD ON ARRIVAL. I was able maintain my composure and convince Keurig to send me another machine, which will be here in 7-14 days. Stay tuned folks! BTW way, my first machine still has the above issues and continues to periodically stop working, then work, then not work... I would love to have my money back, but Keuring rather spend more money on shipping and returns than refund my purchase price. Come on Keurig, you can do better. EDIT: 04/20/25, ANOTHER UPDATE. Since my last update on 02/28/25, I received a third replacement machine from Keurig to replace the dead one. Got #3 all set up on 03/03/25 and ready to go and it worked until 03/28/25, exactly 25 days, then I got the dreaded "add water" and "error 8" message. Called Keuring and asked for a refund, but they still refuse since I bought it from Amazon. Asked to get another comparable machine, which they didn't have in stock (UGH). Ordered #4 replacement. On April 3, 2025, #4 replacement machine arrived. Got #4 all set up and on 04/20/25, it stopped working like the others. This one only lasted 17 days. EDIT: Keurig has started ignoring my calls. I was referred to a "specialist" who told me I needed to send my #4 machine in first BEFORE I could get sent a replacement. As I did not want to send them my machine without a replacement first, they started ignoring my emails and are now refusing to correspond with me at all. #4 machine continues to brew 2 cups then shut off reporting it is dry when there is a full water tank. I will never purchase another Keurig product and you should seriously consider doing the same. Four unusable machines in 8 months is ridiculous!

reviews.title: Keurig has changed the game again!
reviews.body: The Keurig K-Duo Single Serve & Carafe Coffee Maker is an absolute game-changer for households that want both quick morning speed and full-pot brewing capability. By seamlessly combining single-serve K-Cup convenience with a classic 12-cup glass carafe, it replaces two separate appliances with one sleek, space-saving countertop setup. Brew speeds are impressive on both ends. Single-serve pods deliver a rich, flavorful cup in under a minute, while a full 12-cup pot brews in just a few minutes without over-extraction or bitterness. The control panel is intuitive, with clearly labeled buttons for cup size and carafe settings. Maintenance is equally straightforward, featuring accessible filter baskets and clear fill indicators. The Keurig K-Duo hits the sweet spot between weeknight simplicity and weekend batch brewing. For anyone seeking speed, versatility, and dependability without cluttering their kitchen counters, this coffee maker is an exceptional choice.

reviews.title: Why Pay More For A Coffee Machine?

They're also durable and don't have the malfunctioning problems like these "fancy" coffee machines that are over-designed with technological components that fail far too soon. I've seen these simple coffee machines last longer than the Keurig's and Cusinart machines in office spaces where multiple people have to operate the machine to make their coffee. The price is dirt cheap but you get an old school reliable coffee making machine that not only does the job perfectly every time, but is simple to operate and lasts. I not only highly recommend this product but also the Black+Decker coffee grinder as well. Imagine spending $200 on a Cuisinart coffee machine that doesn't even burr your coffee beans, but then you could buy this coffee machine and their coffee grinder and pay less than half the price and less hassle. I swear by this coffee machine and highly recommend it.

title: MEGAWISE Espresso Machine with 20Bar High-Pressure Extraction
bullet_points: 20-bar High-Pressure Pump For Rich Flavor: This Expresso Coffee Machines equipped with a professional-grade 20-bar pressure pump and a high-performance 1450W motor, this machine extracts coffee at optimal pressure to fully release its deep aroma and signature golden crema, resulting in exceptional Italian-style coffee. The powerful pressure system ensures that every sip is full-bodied, rich, and flavorful—on par with the offerings at your favorite specialty coffee shops.

Precise NTC Temperature Control System: Cafetera equipped with an advanced NTC temperature sensor, the machine maintains a stable water temperature between 90–95°C—the ideal range for Italian-style extraction. The 30-second quick-heat-up function gets the machine ready in no time; the stainless steel steam wand features an insulated sleeve at the top to prevent burns while ensuring your coffee cup remains at the ideal drinking temperature.

Effortlessly Create Silky-Smooth Milk Foam: This adjustable milk frother produces velvety-smooth foam with a fine, airy texture—an essential tool for latte art or rich milk-based beverages. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced barista, you can easily froth milk to perfection, adding a professional touch to every cup of coffee. Experiment with different frothing techniques to find your own unique style.

All-In-One, Easy To Use: Combines Italian-style espresso extraction, steam-powered milk frothing, and cappuccino and latte preparation in a single machine; intuitive operation with one-touch single-cup or double-cup extraction buttons; semi-automatic design with indicator lights showing the status of each step—temperature control, extraction timing, and pressure management are all handled by the machine, ensuring consistent results even for beginners.

Compact Design, Great Value: This coffee maker features a compact stainless steel body measuring 12.6 x 12.4 x 6.38 inches that takes up minimal counter space. It comes with coffee bar accessories and is suitable for a variety of settings, including homes, dorm rooms, and offices; A large, removable 40.6-ounce water tank allows for continuous brewing with a single fill; non-slip silicone feet on the bottom ensure stability and prevent slipping during extraction or frothing.

Professional-Grade Sealing: Align the handle with the slot opening on the brew head at a 45° angle to the left, then push it in; next, rotate the handle to the right until it aligns with espresso coffee machine centerline (or slightly to the right). You may feel slight resistance when locking—this is proof that zero-pressure-drop extraction is achieved, ensuring that the high-pressure water flow penetrates the coffee puck 100% to fully extract the coffee oils and flavors.

reviews.title: Great Espresso Quality, but the Portafilter Is Very Hard to Lock In
reviews.body: I’ve been using this 20-bar espresso machine regularly, and the espresso itself comes out very well. The shots are hot, rich, and flavorful with a nice crema, and the stainless steel body looks great on the countertop. Setup was easy, and the removable water tank makes refilling and cleaning convenient. For its compact size, it does a solid job producing café-style espresso at home. That said, the portafilter is extremely hard to lock into place. It often takes several tries of unscrewing, realigning, and pushing very hard before it finally locks in. At times, I honestly feel like I might break the machine just trying to secure it properly. This is easily the most frustrating part of using the espresso maker and something that definitely needs improvement. The steam milk frother works, but making good frothy milk takes some getting used to. With practice, I’ve been able to get decent foam for lattes and cappuccinos, but it’s not effortless and requires patience to dial in the right technique. Once you get the hang of it, the results are good, just not instant. Overall, this machine makes excellent espresso for the price, and I enjoy using it despite the learning curve. If the portafilter locking mechanism were smoother, this would be an even better experience. Still, for home espresso lovers willing to work through a few quirks, it delivers solid performance.

reviews.title: Design Flaws, Difficult Filter Holder
reviews.body: I was really looking forward to making a cappuccino with this espresso machine. However, as I unpacked it and set it up I noticed a few things. First, before even removing the water tank I saw some large scratches along one side of the tank. The tank was really hard to pull up and out of the back of the machine, so I assumed a prior user might have made the scratches trying to force it out. Then I noticed the 'MAX' waterline label was not visible when the tank is set in the machine; the top of the machine wraps around the tank top so you can't see the waterline label if you're filling the tank that way. Nothing seriously wrong, just annoying. Next, started checking out the milk frother feature. The round knob that adjusts the steam pressure was not great. The movement was not smooth and easy, but got stuck a little bit halfway through turning it. Someone, somewhere decided little rubber suction cups on the bottom was a good idea. I don't think so. Every time you need to move the espresso machine, you get to play tug-of-war with those suction cups. Just plain solid rubber protectors would work better. I put the espresso grounds in the filter, tamped them down and can't wait for my cappuccino. Oh no! I can't push the filter holder (portafilter) into the correct position. I'm pushing really hard now, afraid I might break the machine. After several attempts I gave up. Also, the end of the filter handle was not smooth, it had some jagged edges that inflicted some painful nicks to my fingers. So I never got to try this espresso machine completely. Maybe it would work for you and actually make good espresso. Maybe the design flaws I noticed don't bother you. But from my experience I think I'll pass on this one.

reviews.title: It takes some muscle to lock in the filter. That's for sure.
reviews.body: In the box you get the machine, a portafilter handle, a single-shot basket, a double-shot basket, a plastic tamper/scoop, and a small removable drip tray with a splash guard. It has three buttons: single espresso, double espresso, and steam/hot water. The indicator lights stay solid when it’s ready (takes about 45-60 seconds to heat up). There’s also a separate knob on the side to switch between brewing and steaming. First-time setup is straightforward: fill the tank with cool filtered water (I use filtered to slow down scale buildup), run an empty cycle with the portafilter locked in, then run some water through the steam wand to prime the pump. The initial water that comes out is clean, no weird plastic taste. The portafilter locks in from about a 45-degree angle and needs to be pushed in firmly and perfectly straight (or slightly to the right) for the brew to start properly; it can take a little force and fiddling at first. Tamping matters; grounds need to be as level as possible and the rim kept clean, otherwise it won’t seal well. Once it’s locked in, the single and double buttons dispense a fixed volume that produces a decent espresso with visible crema. For milk, the steam wand works fine. You turn the side knob to steam mode, wait for the light, submerge the tip about 1 cm into the milk, and it froths quickly. The wand itself is a simple panarello style. Cleaning it properly is important: the outer plastic sleeve twists off counterclockwise (it’s stiff on purpose), and you really need to remove and rinse both the sleeve and the metal tube underneath after every use, otherwise dried milk builds up inside and affects taste. Overall, it’s a very basic but functional 20-bar pump machine. It makes real espresso and steamed milk in a tiny footprint, requires a bit of care with assembly and cleaning, and definitely rewards a level tamp and a firm hand when locking the portafilter. Nothing fancy, but it does what it’s supposed to do. This review is based on a video transcript. The video can be found on my Amazon storefront/profile.

reviews.title: Great Features, but Frustrating to Use
reviews.body: I was excited to try the MEGAWISE 20-Bar Espresso Machine because I love offering guests a barista-style coffee after a meal. The machine is surprisingly lightweight, which made it easy to lift and set up on my counter. However, I found the filter holder extremely difficult to align and twist into place. Despite following instructions, it kept slipping out until I finally dumped the grinds and started over. I eventually figured it out, but it was not an experience I’d want to repeat with guests waiting for coffee. On paper, this espresso machine offers impressive features — a strong 20-bar pump, temperature control, and a milk frother for cappuccinos and lattes. In practice, though, the challenging design detracts from the overall usability. It’s a sleek, compact unit with potential, but it requires patience and precision to operate smoothly.

reviews.body: This is a very nice espresso machine however it’s a very basic machine and small. It is stainless steel and in the color silver. I recommend this though for beginners and people that want to save money and nice to have at home. On the downside I feel like I have a lot of fingerprints on this so I'm constantly wiping it because I feel like also guest are curious and always want to look at it.

reviews.body: UPDATE - the Customer service team has gone out of their way to try to resolve the issue. For that they get 2 stars added. Most companies do not care enough to bother. reviews.body: Definitely not worth $50+. Maybe $25-30?? I'm sure we've all seen the reviews of people who say they received a used item. I didn't and that's not what this review is about. But, if you buy this, buy the paper filters and use those instead of the reusable one until you decide that you're going to keep it. I would return this but the reusable basket is stained and I feel bad returning it used because they would probably just send it to someone else. Some say who cares, but overall the machine is not THAT bad. It has annoying features that are written about in MANY reviews: It's hard to fill up, it leaks out the bottom if you so much as put one, JUST ONE, more drop than the max level, and it super slow on the strongest setting. It's also hard to fill. So I use a 24 oz water bottle. The medium setting isn't too slow. It gives me time to take the dogs out and feed them. So I've learned to use 7 scoops to get the strength I want. But I really wish I had listened to the reviews and bought something else. However, if you're willing to take the chance because you like the way it looks, use the paper filters just in case you decide to return it. It's perfect for me as I'm the only one that drinks coffee in my house. It makes 2 nice 12oz cups. If you don't care returning it used, then it doesn't matter what filter you use. I just don't feel right returning it used and stained...

It's also hard to fill. So I use a 24 oz water bottle. The medium setting isn't too slow. It gives me time to take the dogs out and feed them. So I've learned to use 7 scoops to get the strength I want. But I really wish I had listened to the reviews and bought something else. However, if you're willing to take the chance because you like the way it looks, use the paper filters just in case you decide to return it. It's perfect for me as I'm the only one that drinks coffee in my house. It makes 2 nice 12oz cups. If you don't care returning it used, then it doesn't matter what filter you use. I just don't feel right returning it used and stained...

reviews.title: Nearly Eight Years of Service—Good Enough to Buy Again
reviews.body: I originally purchased the Cuisinart DCC-3200 PerfectTemp 14-Cup Programmable Coffeemaker on October 31, 2018, for $75.92. Nearly eight years later, it still makes excellent, hot coffee. It recently began making a slight squeaking noise during the brewing cycle, so I decided to play it safe and purchase the same model again on August 2, 2026. That should say plenty about how much I like this coffee maker. It is dependable, easy to operate, makes a full 14-cup pot, and has served me well for almost eight years. I would not have bought the exact same model again if the first one had not performed so well. My only complaint is the price increase. The original cost $75.92, while the replacement cost $107.43 before tax—an increase of $31.51, or about 41%. Even with the higher price, its performance and longevity made it worth buying again. Five stars.

reviews.title: Good durable coffee maker.
reviews.body: One of the best and cheapest, good looking coffee makers out there. I have one at home and one at the office for years and it works everyday. The coffee is hot, it keeps it fairly hot not burned, easy to fill, easy to add coffee. I have bought many coffee makers and some are much much more expensive. But just for a good consistent pot of coffee once you get the correct measurements of coffee and water I think there is none better. It came with the gold filter which is good since I never use paper, it has a few brew temp and carafe temps and you can set the timer to brew automatically. It does not take up much space is fairly easy to keep clean. The water tank though does take a bit of work to get clean and keep clean though. Over time it gets pretty rank and I cleaned mine by spraying soap and Clorox in it and using a dishrag to clean it out. I then rinsed it out in the sink all the time being upside down so as this would not enter the brew track. Once cleaned and rinsed then filled with water and ran a couple of pots of water through it and its as good as new. Now unless your a professional, I don't recommend doing this LOL but it never stopped working and never stopped brewing a good cup of coffee. Looks and works as good as the day it was purchased. I did buy another one and had a funeral for the old one after many years. It still worked, so it was hard to part with but the wife said we had to get a new one. Sheesh, Why? O well you know how that goes.

reviews.title: Revised My Rating
reviews.body: I ordered this coffee maker after researching it as thoroughly as possible. Much to my disappointment, the initial batches of coffee tasted like plastic. I ran carafes of filtered water through the device several times, but the taste of plastic persisted. Then I used ChatGPT to see what information was available and sure enough, this is a common problem. It would have been nice if Cuisinart had addressed this issue in the manual. This is why I am giving a 3 star rating. My next step was to use coffee cleaner, followed by 2 more carafes of filtered water. I could still smell the plastic in the filter basket, so I washed it with a strong mixture of Dawn detergent. Then I ran another carafe of water through it. That finally seems to have gotten rid of the plastic taste in brewed coffee. The entire process probably used several gallons of filtered water and took several days to complete. Otherwise, this coffee maker is well designed and of good quality. The plastic components are thick, unlike the current Moccamaster plastic parts which are thin and flimsy by comparison. (The Moccamaster also has a tube attached to the carafe lid that’s unnecessary, cumbersome and hard to wash. Their old models have a separate tube which isn’t used for the same reason.) I desperately needed a replacement coffee maker and I’m glad I persisted in my efforts to get rid of the plastic taste instead of returning it. This makes good coffee as other reviews have stated. Just be prepared to get rid of the plastic taste. UPDATE As of February 7th, I need to revise my rating to 4 stars. Except for the problem with the plastic taste I explained above, this is a high-quality product that makes good coffee. I love the 1 - 4 cup feature which is what I use to make 24 ounces of coffee. If you drink coffee black and enjoy the flavor of good coffee, you will love this feature. This makes the best coffee I've ever tasted. That said, the initial plastic taste with no mention of it in the manual is a major problem that has to be overcome.

reviews.title: Initial Setup and Usage Review
reviews.body: UPDATE AFTER USING FOR 6 WEEKS: I've been using this new Cuisinart almost every day for 6 weeks, and have NEVER had any issues with the carafe leaking/spilling OR the condensation on the maker lid leaking water onto my countertop when I open it up to add coffee grounds and pour water into the reservoir. Not even once. The only thing I can think of to explain SOME of those carafe complaints is that they are trying to pour from the carafe TOO fast. I must admit 10 years ago when I FIRST got my old Cuisinart2800, I tried pouring from the carafe and poured too fast and spilled. But just a slight slow down fixed it and no issues since. But other than that pour speed issue, I have no idea what those reviewers were doing to cause the maker or the carafe to leak water as they described. Everything else I wrote in my initial review still stands too! ============================================================= I read thru a LOT of reviews on this Cuisinart DCC3200NAS (this is the SS and Black). I JUST set it up on my countertop last night and ran a pot of plain hot water thru it as suggested. This morning I made my first pot of coffee in it!! 9 cups. Very tasty coffee! BUT this review is NOT about how good the coffee is. Nearly all the reviews have established that its great. This review addresses a few of the most common complaints about this coffee maker. FYI: This new 3200 replaced a refurbed Cuisinart DCC2800WFR I had for 10 years that recently started leaking water. The MOST common complaint is the carafe. I am honestly NOT sure why. The new carafe seems IDENTICAL (except black plastic vs white) to the carafe that was on my 2800 that I used for 10 years with no issues. Spout dripping: The easiest way to MAKE the spout drip is pouring too fast. Just slow your pour down a TICH. I put water for 9 cups in my carafe and poured it into my water reservoir in about 10 seconds without spilling a drop. It works exactly the same way AND as well as my 2800 carafe did for 10 years. No spills. No issues. HELPFUL HINT: Make SURE the 3200 lid is FULLY opened (past 90 degrees) before you try to fill the reservoir. Then just rest the carafe spout on the SIDE of the reservoir with the water level indicator. Pour. Done. Carafe Lid not hinged and/or too tough to take off and/or put back on properly: Not hinged is true! But why is that bad? I don't know. It snaps off and on easily for me. Has for 10 years. And I don't even bother taking the lid off to fill the carafe with water. Just fill it thru the spout hole! The new carafe lid DOES require a SLIGHTLY firmer push to pop it off and back on than my old carafe, but I'm guessing in 12 months this one will pop off and on a little easier than it does now too. HELPFUL HINT: Pop the carafe lid off by LIFTING the tab that your thumb sits on when holding the carafe. Pop it back on in reverse: Insert spout side first, then pop the thumb side down. Done. Easy peasy. The 3200 control panel is significantly different from my old 2800. I read a couple reviews that suggested the 3200 control panel was difficult to understand and use properly!?! I found the exact opposite to be true. Once you know exactly what option each button controls (button labels seem clear & obvious to me), setting the options properly is completely simple. As you press each button, it cycles thru the available settings for that option. Stop pressing that button when that option is set to your liking. If you miss it, cycle around again. Done. The basket the filter sits in DOES need to be PUSHED fully back down such that it "pops" down into the maker after being removed (in my 2800, it just dropped in loosely). BUT that is obvious to the careful user since it requires that same "pop" to remove that basket in the first place. If that basket is NOT popped down into place, the carafe lid won't reach (much less push up on) the spring loaded valve on the underside of that basket, so that valve would stay closed, and as your maker dumps more water into your filter, coffee grounds will overflow your filter and go everywhere including the bottom of the water reservoir. PS: Same thing happens if you put a LIDLESS carafe in the coffee maker! Lid isn't there to push up on the valve, so the valve stays closed. I found the 5 "Coffee is Done" beeps and the 2 "Heating Pad Off" beeps to be the right volume for my house. Not loud, BUT loud enough that on a normal (ie: semi-quiet) morning, I can hear it from the next room easy. AND it is super fast and easy to turn the beeping off and back on with the "Tone" option button if you need to. Bottom Line for me: I am boggled by all the carafe and reservoir filling issues so many reviewers have! I have NO dripping issues or lid issues with my carafe, NO reservoir filling issues, and NO setup or control panel issues. All 5 stars. Now lets just see if it stands the test of time like my 2800 did!

reviews.title: BKSP1 Model Clock Runs FAST
reviews.body: This BKSP1 (black stainless appearance) 14-cup coffeemaker replaced a 12+ year old Cuisinart 12-cup unit we used until it finally quit working. Great coffeemaker and it produced great coffee. My research to replace the old unit settled on the BKSP1 model and Amazon delivered straight-a-way. I got it all cleansed out, programmed and set up for begin brewing at 4:45 the next morning. It brewed a great pot of coffee and all worked wonderfully ... EXCEPT that the clock on the BKSP1 was running FAST. It had "gained" almost an hour since I had set it up the day before. Thus the coffee was actually brewed at ~3:45AM. I reset the clock and kept watching it as I would walk by the coffeemaker and noted that it was gaining time or running FAST. I went through this for several days and finally sent a message to Amazon C.S. and they immediately replaced with another BKSP1 and I returned the original unit. I went through the setup process with the #2 BKSP1 and was hopeful that the clock would keep proper time ... however it did not. The clock on the #2 BKSP1 also ran FAST. The coffeemaker worked just fine in all regards ... save for the clock running FAST. So, I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. with this "fast clock" issue and they replaced the #2 BKSP1 with the #3 BKSP1. I did all the setup with #3 and lo & behold ... the clock on the #3 BKSP1 also runs FAST. All other elements work just fine, brews great coffee, but the clock just has a mind of it's own. So (you can guess what is next), I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (again) with the fast clock issue noted in graf above. A ticket was established and I was shipped a #4 BKSP1 to replace the #3 unit. Can you see where this is going? The #4 BKSP1 unit was set up and put into service and the clock on #4 also runs FAST. So ... it appears that there is something common going on with the BKSP1 model units. This time I called Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (I had been establishing all other tickets via the inter-web and e-mail). The lady with C.S. was simply excellent and she noted my BKSP1 ticket history and said she would have another unit shipped out straight-a-way. She asked if I still wanted the same BKSP1 model or would I want to get the SP1 model (SP1 is the brushed stainless appearance). I figured what the heck ... I would get the SP1 this time. In a couple days I received the #5 SP1, got it all set up and ready to brew coffee the next morning at 4:45. I would glance at the clock on the #5 SP1 as I walked by the unit and the clock was ACCURATE. I was again hopeful that the clock would hold and keep proper time. At 4:45AM the brew cycle started and it actually was at 4:45AM. The clock held it's accuracy for one day at that point. It has now been 3-days and the clock on the #5 SP1 is "spot on". So (there is the 'so' word again) I noted on the boxes the coffeemakers were shipped in had the countries of manufacture stamped on them. The BKSP1 units were all manufactured in China. The SP1 unit was manufactured in Indonesia. AHA - I said. There is a manufacturing plant issue going on. I did an extensive observation letter to Cuisinart/Conair about my situation and thoughts of what is going on. BTW - In addition the BKSP1 units all dripped extensive moisture droplets down the back side of the unit when the top lid was opened to removed the coffee grounds. This had me wondering if there was a leak as there was water all over the counter under the BKSP1 units. Turns out the drip lip on the upper back of the BKSP1 appears to be 'flat' without adequate slope to have the water droplets flow back into the reservoir. Also the drip lip is not as deep as what I noticed on the SP1 units. I also observed (on both the BKSP1 and SP1 models) that there is a lot of moisture condensation that collects on the upper front panel where the control buttons are located. To me this could affect the electronics that I'm guessing is located near or behind this panel. Ergo couple items of note for Cuisinart/Conair: 1) Production molds for the BKSP1 and SP1 are NOT the same between the China and Indonesia manufacturing plants. Thus the drip lip issue noted above. 2) The chips/electronics being used in the China plant for the BKSP1 are defective and can't keep proper time. All-in-all ... The Cuisinart 14-cup coffeemaker is an excellent product and works very well and produces great coffee. Save for the units (in my case) that are manufactured in China where the chips/electronics they are using just don't work. Adding to that the manufacturing mold difference that slightly changes the size of the drip lip on the upper back. I would suggest getting the the SP1 model and keep your fingers crossed that it is also manufactured in Indonesia as opposed to China. At least until such time as changes are made in the manufacturing facility in China to correct the noted issues. Cheers, Nolan K.
reviews.body_en: This BKSP1 (black stainless appearance) 14-cup coffeemaker replaced a 12+ year old Cuisinart 12-cup unit we used until it finally quit working. Great coffeemaker and it produced great coffee. My research to replace the old unit settled on the BKSP1 model and Amazon delivered straight-a-way. I got it all cleansed out, programmed and set up for begin brewing at 4:45 the next morning. It brewed a great pot of coffee and all worked wonderfully ... EXCEPT that the clock on the BKSP1 was running FAST. It had "gained" almost an hour since I had set it up the day before. Thus the coffee was actually brewed at ~3:45AM. I reset the clock and kept watching it as I would walk by the coffeemaker and noted that it was gaining time or running FAST. I went through this for several days and finally sent a message to Amazon C.S. and they immediately replaced with another BKSP1 and I returned the original unit. I went through the setup process with the #2 BKSP1 and was hopeful that the clock would keep proper time ... however it did not. The clock on the #2 BKSP1 also ran FAST. The coffeemaker worked just fine in all regards ... save for the clock running FAST. So, I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. with this "fast clock" issue and they replaced the #2 BKSP1 with the #3 BKSP1. I did all the setup with #3 and lo & behold ... the clock on the #3 BKSP1 also runs FAST. All other elements work just fine, brews great coffee, but the clock just has a mind of it's own. So (you can guess what is next), I reached out to Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (again) with the fast clock issue noted in graf above. A ticket was established and I was shipped a #4 BKSP1 to replace the #3 unit. Can you see where this is going? The #4 BKSP1 unit was set up and put into service and the clock on #4 also runs FAST. So ... it appears that there is something common going on with the BKSP1 model units. This time I called Cuisinart/Conair C.S. (I had been establishing all other tickets via the inter-web and e-mail). The lady with C.S. was simply excellent and she noted my BKSP1 ticket history and said she would have another unit shipped out straight-a-way. She asked if I still wanted the same BKSP1 model or would I want to get the SP1 model (SP1 is the brushed stainless appearance). I figured what the heck ... I would get the SP1 this time. In a couple days I received the #5 SP1, got it all set up and ready to brew coffee the next morning at 4:45. I would glance at the clock on the #5 SP1 as I walked by the unit and the clock was ACCURATE. I was again hopeful that the clock would hold and keep proper time. At 4:45AM the brew cycle started and it actually was at 4:45AM. The clock held it's accuracy for one day at that point. It has now been 3-days and the clock on the #5 SP1 is "spot on". So (there is the 'so' word again) I noted on the boxes the coffeemakers were shipped in had the countries of manufacture stamped on them. The BKSP1 units were all manufactured in China. The SP1 unit was manufactured in Indonesia. AHA - I said. There is a manufacturing plant issue going on. I did an extensive observation letter to Cuisinart/Conair about my situation and thoughts of what is going on. BTW - In addition the BKSP1 units all dripped extensive moisture droplets down the back side of the unit when the top lid was opened to removed the coffee grounds. This had me wondering if there was a leak as there was water all over the counter under the BKSP1 units. Turns out the drip lip on the upper back of the BKSP1 appears to be 'flat' without adequate slope to have the water droplets flow back into the reservoir. Also the drip lip is not as deep as what I noticed on the SP1 units. I also observed (on both the BKSP1 and SP1 models) that there is a lot of moisture condensation that collects on the upper front panel where the control buttons are located. To me this could affect the electronics that I'm guessing is located near or behind this panel. Ergo couple items of note for Cuisinart/Conair: 1) Production molds for the BKSP1 and SP1 are NOT the same between the China and Indonesia manufacturing plants. Thus the drip lip issue noted above. 2) The chips/electronics being used in the China plant for the BKSP1 are defective and can't keep proper time. All-in-all ... The Cuisinart 14-cup coffeemaker is an excellent product and works very well and produces great coffee. Save for the units (in my case) that are manufactured in China where the chips/electronics they are using just don't work. Adding to that the manufacturing mold difference that slightly changes the size of the drip lip on the upper back. I would suggest getting the the SP1 model and keep your fingers crossed that it is also manufactured in Indonesia as opposed to China. At least until such time as changes are made in the manufacturing facility in China to correct the noted issues. Cheers, Nolan K.

reviews.title: Finally—One Coffee Maker That Does It ALL: Full Pot, Single Cup, Hot or Iced! & No K-cups needed!!
reviews.body: I really like the versatility of this Coffee Maker. Some mornings I want to brew a full pot, while other times I only need one cup, so having both options in one machine is extremely convenient. It also saves me from having two different coffee makers taking up counter space. The 12-cup glass carafe is a great size when making coffee for more than one or when I know I’ll want a second cup. For those times when I just want something quick, the single-serve side is exactly what I need. I also appreciate being able to make either hot or iced coffee depending on what I’m in the mood for. The coffee comes out nicely brewed and flavorful. The Auto Pause & Pour feature is another small convenience that I use more than I expected—it’s nice to be able to grab a cup before the entire pot has finished brewing. The controls are straightforward, and I like the clean black finish. Even though it offers two brewing options, the overall design is practical and doesn’t feel unnecessarily complicated. For me, the biggest selling point is simply choice: a full 12-cup pot when I need it, a single cup when I don’t, and the option for hot or iced coffee. ALSO - NO K-CUPS needed! Just use your favorite coffee for a single cup. It’s a very practical everyday coffee maker and a good option for a household where everyone doesn’t necessarily drink coffee at the same time. The only thing I do wish this machine had was the ability to use a K-cup instead of ground coffee for the single-serve. But, this is not a deal-breaker since this machine offers so much more.

reviews.title: It’s not flashy—it’s just nearly perfect!!
reviews.body: Our Ninja coffee maker was great but dying. Really tired of spending $125+ for this small appliance that only lasts two years or so….we’ve replaced a lot of coffee makers! I’d been looking at this unit but when the price notably dropped during Prime Days, that was it! Still, I didn’t have high hopes for this inexpensive unit. No clue about its lifespan (yet), but so far I LOVE IT! There are two downsides: it brews slooooooow on both sides, pot or cup. The other is a common issue—aiming water in the lid opening is rough if there are cabinets overhead. Even without cabinets the fill area is rather small and awkward (coming from a Ninja with a separate water tank). Upside is everything else is awesome! Brews VERY hot….like a $600 coffee maker a coffee master would buy. Coffee tastes excellent from extruding at 200+ degrees using the “bold” setting, and the warming pad keeps it very hot! Ninja didn’t come close. Controls are super easy to use, looks beautiful and more expensive than it is, carafe pours beautifully without the drips at the end, delay timer and “stop dispensing to grab a cup” features are perfect. If you’re in the market for a coffee maker and you don’t require flashy manufacturing labels or endless brewing options—this is the unit!! Buy it!!!

reviews.body: I don't love this coffee maker. The burner is way too hot so if coffee is brewed and in the pot on the burner for longer than 15-20 minutes, it's so hot it will burn me. I have to leave for work and take the lid off my coffee in the car before I can even drink it. Not ideal obviously. And when there's a cup or two left on the burner, it burns in the pot and smells and tastes like nasty gas station coffee, so it's undrinkable and wasted. Also, when you pour water in using the caraffe, it doesn't just drip, it gushes out no matter how slow/fast or what the pouring angle is. I have to pour it into the machine with a towel on the counter. The single cup brewing is the part I like. I haven't tried iced coffee yet, but the instructions basically have you brewing normal coffee into a cup or the caraffe with ice in it. I guess the burner turns off for that part. It would be a really great machine without the overheating and dripping issues and now I've spend $100 buck on it and can't justify getting a new one so here we are.
