reviews.title: Really decent coffee maker that could use a few quality of life upgrades
reviews.body: Overall, I really like this coffee maker. It does have a couple of quirks though. One thing I didn't see talked about in any of the reviews I read before buying was that this has two separate water reservoirs. If you fill water from the opening at the front of the maker, you're filling the single cup portion first, and then the excess goes into the main tank for brewing a pot. I find this to be the easier place to fill it using, but that also means that you always have water in the reservoir for the single cup. I'm not a huge fan of that. It also means that if you decide you want a smaller single cup later, there's no way to remove any of the water that you've already put in. So, you're always going to get a full sized cup. The single cup function is great and really convenient though, and I find myself using it more often than I expected. The mesh filter is really handy but you will always end up with some really fine grinds on the bottom of the cup. This isn't a problem for me, but some people may feel sick if they drink this portion of the coffee. The iced coffee function is nice to have, but makes really weak coffee. Typically, to make iced coffee, you would leave the grinds soaking in cold water for several hours. So, this is a quick way to get room temperature coffee, but it's not great and melting ice will only further weaken it. Also, if the machine drips at all after you've taken the cup off, it falls into a small pool under the cup holder. It's nice that it's there, but would have been better if there was something you could remove to rinse out instead of just being part of the unit itself. I also wish that it was possible to adjust how long the hot plate stays on for. It doesn't go off for four hours, and that's just way too long to leave coffee sitting. The carafe is pretty decent. It doesn't stain easily, which is always nice. But it isn't great at getting all of the water out when pouring, even if turned completely upside down. Not a huge deal, but it's not what I'm used to. There also seems to be something about the way the brewer and carafe line up that always causes a few drops of coffee to fall from the machine after you've taken the carafe off, falling onto the hot plate. I find myself having to clean it off way more often than I should. Overall though, it's a very solid machine that does a good job making coffee. It's easy to use and although I have mixed feelings about all of the additional functions, they're nice to have in something around this price point. I'm happy with the purchase overall.

This optimal pressure unlocks deep, layered flavor and a smooth, full-bodied mouthfeel. Every shot tastes rich, aromatic, and cafe-worthy — no watery output, just real espresso you'll want to savor

Fast Extraction: 800W heating system and 6 bar pressure extract rich, bold espresso in just 2 minutes. Pre-infusion soaks grounds evenly for a smooth, balanced shot — no bitter aftertaste. Ideal for your morning rush or quick office break

Effortless Toggle Control: One flick of the toggle — you're in Brew, Steam, or Off mode. No long presses, no digital settings. A tactile, responsive control that makes every coffee routine fast and intuitive

Creamy Milk Frothing: Powerful steam wand with steam-water separation technology prevents milk from being diluted. Produces creamy, micro-foam texture for lattes, cappuccinos and flat whites. Bimetal thermostat keeps extraction temperature steady, unlocking coffee’s full aroma

Compact & Portable: Measuring just 12.99”×9.06”×6.69”, it fits tiny kitchen counters, RVs, or office desks. Stainless steel cup warming tray preheats your cup, keeps every sip hotter and flavor intact longer

Auto Relief & Safety: Once brewing is done, simply toggle to OFF — the machine auto-releases leftover pressure instantly. No sudden steam bursts when you open the brew head for refilling or cleaning. Built-in high-temp fuse, boil-dry auto shut-off, and overflow drainage provide multi-layer protection. The detachable drip tray and wand head rinse clean in seconds

reviews.title: Great Basic Espresso Machine
reviews.body: We drink a lot of coffee around here, but we never had an espresso machine till now. It was something we talked about getting "some day", so we were really excited to have a chance to try this one out and see what we think! The size is nice for our smaller kitchen and doesn't take up too much additional counter space. Since we use it daily (or near daily) it definitely earns it's spot to be kept out. It only brews 2 cups worth at a time, so if you're really heavy coffee drinkers like we are you'll have to do a couple brews in a row to get enough, but we knew that would be the case when we got it so not a problem. It's super easy to use, and just as easy to clean which I very much appreciate. It brews in just a couple of minutes, so even in hectic mornings coffee is not a hassle. It isn't too noisy when brewing, but it does get pretty loud when steaming/frothing milk. Loud enough that the first time I used it my husband came wandering down from the opposite side of the house to investigate because he thought something was wrong. The cat was also not a fan lol. The one thing most lacking, for me, was the fact this didn't include a steaming pitcher. We don't have one, so we are just using a tall mug instead. I know not everyone may need one but it would be nice if one were included, at least optionally, for those who need it. Overall this has been a solid appliance for us so far. It doesn't have any fancy features or custom adjustments like higher end machines do - and it's definitely not super high quality in terms of the materials it is made from and the overall look and feel of the machine itself. But its super easy to use, easy to clean, and efficiently keeps our coffee flowing every day. Definite win for us!

reviews.title: Great espresso maker for a beginner or any coffee lover
reviews.body: Solid 5 stars for a beginner, learning how to make espresso. This machine is by no means a professional level machine. Nonetheless, it's built with good quality parts and feels durable. The carafe is made of thick glass and the portafiler is made of a thick, heavy metal the seals tightly. This espresso maker is an excellent choice for a beginner who is learning how to make espresso and espresso based drinks. I am a coffee lover. Yet, I've never owned an espresso maker, but this machine is a game changer for me. It has 2 functions: make 1 or 2 shots of espresso at a time AND steam/froth milk. The espresso maker comes with an instruction manual that walks you through the steps of making an espresso shot. It also has instructions on how to steam milk. The instructions are very easy to understand. Making the espresso shot was easy. There are two lines on the side of the carafe. The first line is the fill line for steaming and the second line for the espresso shot. I filled the carafe for the espresso shot. Filled the reservoir and turned the dial for espresso. The shot took about a minute and a half to complete. I poured that into my glass then filled the water for the steam. I then turned the dial the opposite way to steam and the steam started bubbling the milk. I frothed the milk and poured that into my glass. I cleaned the parts of the machine and enjoyed my very first latte !!! As I mentioned before, the machine only performs those two basic functions of making an espresso shot and frothing milk. However, that's all I need. It's a really good deal for the price! This machine is about the size of a Keurig single serve. The parts are easy to clean and easy to assemble and disassemble when needed. This makes a great gift for a coffee lover OR a great gift to yourself, because you deserve it! Honestly, a great find!

reviews.title: VERY Impressive espresso maker - perfect ‘starter’ set up and more!
reviews.body: This amazingly compact and light weight (thus easily portable) espresso maker is fabulous! A GREAT gift for any college student - or espresso lover of any age! Also perfect for those who love espresso now and then but don’t want to spend hundreds for a model that gathers dust much of the time. Lets break it down.. First of all - though my husband and i love espresso drinks of all kinds - this is my first personal espresso maker. So i was uneducated in the ‘how to’. The instruction booklet is TERRIFIC. The first thing it says is to read all instructions first - and i highly recommend doing so. I learned numerous tips and tricks along the way. This is one of those times reading all the instructions in the book really make a difference. Then, I simply went back to page 1, followed the process - and had no problems at all. The instructions begin by having you run through full operation for espresso and steamer 2-3 times to clean the machine. I did so and became very familiar with the simple process and how things work, along the way. Next, i grabbed some coffee beans from a bag we’d been gifted months ago, ground them to a fine grind, and made my first cup. It was so-so. Maybe not even that good. I quickly realized i needed to adjust the grind. Then, though improved, i realized my beans were older than wise - so i acquired freshly ground coffee from the local coffee shop for testing purposes - BIG improvement! I also played around - making a total of 3 cups with the ‘good’ grinds - and indeed found the espresso improved with each cup. As for the milk steamer. Having followed the cleaning process earlier, i was now familiar with how the steamer/frother works. Its actually trickier than making the espresso! First, be aware that the machine makes a good 3-4 minutes of steam per instruction - so you aren’t in any hurry or fear of running out of steam. After pouring water into the machine as instructed, You put the empty pitcher under the steamer to catch the condensation that will come out first - then you replace that pitcher with YOUR pitcher of cold milk or cream. I used a tiny cream pitcher because its pretty. Bad idea. The frother REALLLLY works - the milk froths and puffs up. A cute little pitcher does NOT work well. You need something like a measuring cup or something the size of what the baristas use in shops. Then if you want you can pour your warm cream directly into your espresso or even into your cute little pitcher. Lol. The one thing i did notice in frothing milk is that i ended up with a bit of a mess under the steamer nozzle. (see photos). If the milk sputters over as you froth, and definitely as steam continues after you remove your pitcher and thus sprays both steam and milk from around the nozzle - it makes a mess (see photo). Thus i recommend using a rubber ‘bar’ coaster as i did - or at the least a folded paper towel under your pitcher. Also. Do not forget to remove and clean both the outer and inner nozzles on the steamer. Let to sit, milk will dry on both, become harder to remove, and build up over time. Clean off the residue while its warm and “soft”. My last bit of advice is to practice before you plan to impress your spouse or guests. Great espresso making is a but of a skill! All that said - i ended up producing espressos every bit as good as any restaurant or coffee shop with this little guy. So you BET i love it!

reviews.title: Made a really good cappuccino!
reviews.body: Don't be intimidated if you've never made espresso or cappuccino before. It's not as hard as you think. I'm no bistro, so if you are, you might have some notes for me but I was quite happy with the results of my first couple drinks I made with this. The first use is in the instruction book. Pretty easy to follow. Just run though 2-3 brew cycles and 2-3 steam cycles and you're ready to go! When you go to make your coffee, if you're going to steam, I do recommend you premeasure your steam water so you don't have to clean your espresso cup between brewing and steaming. This eliminates a little extra cleaning work for you and keeps you from contaminating your water tank. Other than than, make sure you have milled beans (not ground) super fine. Espresso relies on resistance and uses pressure to brew so get it fine and pack it tight! Let the machine take it from there! Only take a couple of minutes to get your espresso so it brews pretty fast. When you're done with that, steam your cream / milk and serve! Everything comes apart so it seems pretty easy to clean. This was a really tasty cappuccino! Part of that might be the beans. My dad brings be beans from all over the world, I can't remember where these came from but it was darn good! This is small enough to accompany your other machines, it doesn't take up a huge amount of space which is nice! I can leave this out and not have to take it out and put it up every time I want to use it. Nice product for the price! Inpress your guests next time they're over! This has now earned a permanent space in my pantry!

reviews.title: A MUSA type espresso maker—how does it compare?
reviews.body: MUSA style espresso makers like the XIXUBX are one of the most inexpensive—and popular—machines for making espresso worldwide, including in Italy, the land of the most drinkable espresso. We tested this machine against the other most inexpensive and popular way of making espresso—a moka pot. So which one made better-tasting coffee? The XIXUBX beat out the moka pot in terms of coffee taste and also outperforms other MUSA type espresso machines we’ve used in terms of temperature control. Moka pot coffee, even when made by someone with skill, inevitably has a slightly bitter flavor because the coffee is extracted at too high a temperature WHICH IS UNAVOIDABLE BECAUSE MOKA POTS ONLY WORK WHEN WATER IS BOILING. And boiling water yields bitter coffee. The espresso extracted from the XIXUBX machine, in comparison is extracted at slightly lower than boiling temperatures, was rich tasting and NOT bitter at all. The XIXUBX also produced crema during the extraction, whereas moka pots do not. Between these two inexpensive ways to make espresso, the XIXUBX clearly produced more flavorful and overall better coffee. The steam wand also outputs sufficient steam. So what’s not to like? This machine uses an aluminum portafilter and an aluminum boiling tank. It also is produced mainly out of plastic. If you are against plastic and aluminum being in contact with anything that you imbibe this machine isn’t for you. However, if you’re ok with the materials, want better tasting coffee than what you’d get from a comparably-priced moka pot, and are on a budget, this machine may appeal to you. It is more attractive than many other MUSA type coffee machines with stainless steel exterior panels and a simple Euro aesthetic. The design is time-honored, intuitive and very easy to use. It comes well-packaged and with an easy to understand user manual.

reviews.title: EXCELLENT ESPRESSO MACHINE. RIVALS VERY EXPENSIVE ONES.
reviews.body: This Espresso brewer is outstanding and rivals the more expensive models by other companies. It offers so many espresso recipes at the touch of an icon. It is easy to clean and brews excellent coffee delights. The loud sounding solenoids gave me some misgivings in the beginning but now I am comfortable with this entire unit. I believe the quality of construction to be very good, however, time will tell. I did purchase an extended warranty. It is manufactured by a minority owned company which I believe to be a good thing. If you love various coffee drinks custom made to your taste this is an espresso machine for you. UPDATED ONE MONTH LATER. I have owned the Espresso brewer now for about a month and have used it extensively. It is an outstanding brewer that I highly recommend if you love coffee. My advice is to clean the milk frothing unit every time you make one of the coffee drinks otherwise the tube or the actual frother has a tenacity to clog up. It is exceptionally easy to clean which is another plus. THIS IS A TWO MONTH UPDATE: I have been successfully using this espresso machine for exactly 2 months and still delighted with it. However, in these 2 month the coffee dustpan has collected about 3 ounces of ground coffee that seems to be discarded into the pan after every use. This is somewhat of a waste so I collect it and seal it in an airtight container to use later. Granted it won't be as fresh as I would like but it also won't be wasted. I still highly recommend this unit. CUSTOMER SERVICE UPDATE:: Don't rely on the Magia customer service. The plastic plug that covers the ground coffee chute broke quite easily and this company will not even answer my request for a new one. I finally went to Ace Hardware and purchased a metal cap that works better than the original.

reviews.title: Beautiful machine, works wellseemed like a
reviews.body: First impressions are awesome. The thing is beautiful on my new countertop. Touch screen is cool and works well. I haven't yet dived into special programming, so I'll hold comment on any special operations. As sent, it makes a decent cup. I do have some down side comments, though the coolness of the machine makes them tolerable. All down side concerns are in machine design. The water tank is way too small. It needs to be refilled quite often. This may say more about my somewhat unhealthy consumption of coffee and less about the tank. I'm currently designing a float valve so I can hook up a water line and never have to refill myself. The bean hopper is also small, though easily accessible to add more without a problem. The main issue in the hopper is that it lays pretty flat and does not feed the beans into the grinder very efficiently. I find myself having to own the top and push the beans around in order to make it feed. My final concern, and probably most concerning, is the way it wastes dry grounds inside the side door. I'm not sure if it's malfunctioning or is really bad design. When I empty the spent puck container (which is a really cool feature, by the way) I find several shots worth of dry, unused ground coffee in the compartment. Enough that it requires brushing out before the puck container can be replaced in its slot. Not only is it messy, it's sure its spending a lot on coffee to be simply be swept away. All in all, so far, I like this machine a lot. It's functional and pretty. I've been using a high end single group brewer and am enjoying the simplicity of a super auto. reviews.title: Honest review and it’s very disappointing to write.
reviews.body: I’ll start by saying that I am a coffee addict. I have entirely to many appliances and manual devises for making coffee and espresso drinks. This machine was appealing due to variety and price point. There are far more negatives than positives in this review. I used for more than a week before leaving this review. Cons: - This machines self cleans and it does it constantly. If you’re wanting to make more than a couple beverages before filling the small water reservoir then look elsewhere. It cleans itself when it starts up, while it’s sitting idle, and when it goes to sleep. I have made all the cleaning intervals as long as possible and it still cleans over and over. - The water reservoir is 3 times smaller than it should be for the level of self cleaning. - I went through 5-7 espresso pours to see if the quality would increase as the manual says. I changed the grind setting during and after and the espresso is still very weak. The pucks are not pucks when discharged, they are just balls of grind goo. It doesn’t press hard enough. - The milk system requires you to have a cup and a clean cup of water nearby at all times. It constantly runs a clean cycle on the milk so you can’t just leave it out for a few hours between cups on a weekend morning. - The touchscreen isn’t very responsive. Hit it 4-5 times and it might stop or go backward in options. - The settings are all in ML so have a conversion chart handy for our US cup measurements. - The waste water reservoir needs to emptied multiple times a day just like the water needs filled multiple times a day. - If you enter a descale phase while making an espresso separately to add to a latte, it will just start to descale and ruin your drink. You then have to go through the whole descale process before you get your next drink. This is very unfortunate when you’re in a morning rush to get to work. Pros: The drinks are hot. I was super excited for this machine and the reviews, while limited on Amazon were pretty good. I was left very disappointed and returning the unit because it doesn’t function properly as it should and the quality of drinks is very low compared to others I have and use frequently.

reviews.title: HIGHLY RECOMMEND IT!
reviews.body: To start out, I was exited to receive it. Item was packaged well. It was easy to unpack and a few steps was to setup the machine. This coffee machine is absolutely unique, there isn't anything else out there. I did my research. When you turn it on, put water in, it does a self cleaning. Then you have the selections for many different type of coffees. Latte, cappuccino, regular, espresso, and on. You can have different users and have different types of coffee on each user. Each coffee is adjustable in the setting, such as temperature of the water, milk, how much coffee do you want in volume, how strong you want to coffee to be and so on. It's fantastic. It grinds up the coffee beans, sucks up the milk from a cup you place next to it to make the latte, it steams the coffee. It makes the layers like the real cappuccino as it shows in the pictures. Fully automated. It will tell you when you have to empty the ground coffee trash bin. When you turn it off, it does an automatic cleaning. Not to mention, this machine looks high tech, elegant and it will definitely bring the attention to your guests and everyone in the house. This coffee maker is smart and had a lot of attention to every detail put in. I hardly ever leave a review, but this, I highly recommend this product even it is high priced.

reviews.title: Very easy to use, small water tank, multiple issues - 2 month update
reviews.body: Zulay Magia Super Automatic Coffee Espresso Machine **Update 9/20/2023** I've been using the machine now for about 2 months and wanted to provide an update. First, you can edit your custom drink after you set it, so I wanted to correct that. The constant auto cleaning is still annoying. There is a lot of coffee waste. In 2 months, I was able to fill up a standard size ziplock of unused coffee grinds. This is caused by several reason. 1. Coffee grinds get in and all over the brewing unit inside. Guessing when it's grinding, there isn't a good seal between grinder and brewing unit. So make sure you pull it out about once a week to shake it out. 2. There is a small tray below brewing unit that catches grounds from some part of the process. This doesn't do a good job at catching the grounds as it builds up behind the tray. 3. The unit will randomly stop making coffee right after it grinds the beans and presses the coffee. No errors, no reason, you hear it go through it's process of pressing the coffee, then it just stops and dumps the grounds in to the coffee ground box. This has happened several times in the last two months. **Original review** It works great and is simple to use. The espresso taste just as good when I manually make it on a standard espresso machine. It's menu has multiple coffee types which are all one press and it's all handled for you. From grinding the beans, pressing the coffee, and adding the milk/foam all in one unit. There is also another menu to make more premium drinks like White Chocolate mocha. It will list the ingredients you need and the amounts and after you add the extra ingredients it will start making the drink. There are multiple profiles you can choose to setup up different custom coffee setups per user. You can't rename the profiles, they are just user1, user2, etc... You also can't customize a coffee type more than once. So if you wanted to created different sizes of a drink, you have to use different user profiles. You also cannot edit your custom drink after you set it. You have to delete and recreate it. Cleaning the machine is pretty simple and straight forward. It does an automatic flush of the funnel and frother unit on startup and shutdown. However, I feel that's too much and just waste the limited water in your bin. I get running the cleaning on shutdown, but I don't see the need for it to also run on startup. While there is a cleaning setting, there is no setting that lets you turn off automatic cleaning. It also alerts you when to clean the internal components, like empty the coffee grind bin. Everything about the unit is easy to clean and maintain. The water tank is placed on the back of the unit. This will cause problems for those with counters that are not deep. The unit itself already will take up most of the counter depth because its so big. So you may have to keep pulling your unit out just to get the water tank off and out to fill up. This will be frequent unless you only drink the 2oz /4oz espresso drinks only. But even then, with all the cleaning it does, you'll still find yourself filling the tank frequently. Personally, I think they should have just made it wider than deeper. A side water tank would have held more volume and would have been more convenient to refill. The quality of the build of the machine is nothing to be excited about. It's made of all plastic and kind of makes it look cheap. Internal components are mostly plastic as well. However, it's all pretty sturdy. For roughly $800 out the door, it's just lacking. It's like they've done just enough but didn't polish it out. I would peg this more in the $500 line just due to its automation as I'm sure there is complexity there. But outside of that, it's disappointing for having paid this much.

reviews.title: Multi-user Customization and Good/Bad points..
reviews.body: Since I struggled with individual customization for a while (till I figured it out) - I thought I should do a step by step on how to customize coffee for each user in the family. You can follow it through with pictures added to review. 1) On the main screen - touch the "User" icon on the top left (Picture 1) 2) You will see a 10 user screen (BTW - You can edit names of each user by selecting that user and touching the name "user1" on the top center) - Here you touch "+" sign at the bottom left to pick the coffee style you want to customize for this user (Picture 2) 3) Select the coffee you want to customize - using "Latte" as an example here (Picture 3) 4) On return - you will see "Latte" added to "user1" (Picture 4) 5) Now is when it gets strange - when you touch "Latte" icon - it will start making "Latte" with default recipe (have a cup under drip ready before touching "Latte" icon!!) 6) WHILE it is brewing Latte for you - it will display the "Brewing" screen - bottom left of that screen you see three bars (Picture 5) - touch on it and the customization screen pops up (Picture 6) 7) Adjust your recipe to what you desire and touch "return". Now your recipe is stored in your user profile for FUTURE brews when brewed from your user profile. The strange/weird thing is that it starts brewing coffee before you can customize - so you are technically customizing FUTURE brews... Now some pros/cons: Pros: 1) The machine looks beautiful 2) A large number of recipes 3) Automatic functionality is super impressive 4) Customization ability is amazing - one can adjust coffee, temperature, time (assume that translates to volume) of hot milk, time for foam, and liquid volume for coffee. 5) User profile storing is even more impressive for a machine in this price-range (it was frustrating while I was trying to figure it out though!) 6) Quality of coffee produced is excellent (See picture 7) - foam quality is good, temperature is good (and can be adjusted). 7) Support is VERY responsive to email contact. Couple of my questions were answered in matter of hours. (Edit: sorry - pictures seem to be in some random order on posting) Cons: 1) Screen stays on as long as machine is plugged into the wall (it does go into a "screensaver" display) - no switch to turn it off. I worry about screen burn-in and also light pollution at night. Power usage is less than 10 watts while machine is off but screen is on. (I put it on a smart plug and I turn it off after making coffee via Alexa/Google). 2) Water container is in the back and needs to be lifted "up" - which means this unit can NOT be under a cabinet. You would need approximately the height of the machine clear above it to take out and refill container. 3) The dispensed coffee puck container is on the side - so again - you need to keep the right side of the machine clear. Only drip tray can be removed from the front. My DeLonghi machine prior to this had everything removable from the front. 4) Everything is through the screen - that could end up being a single point of failure - not quite like mostly mechanical coffee maker I had before. 5) In my case - dispensed pucks are non-existent (it looks like a slushy liquid) - See picture 8 - I am going to reach out to them to find out if this is something that will be fixed over time or if I need to change some settings (will update review when resolved). Taking 1 point away for above items. For now - I am happy with it (24 hours so far). Only unknown is how robust it is and how long it would last. I will come back and update review periodically. Warranty is for 1 year - I am thinking I will get extended warranty from Asurion on Amazon (can buy it within 30 days after purchase).

title: HIBREW H10B Programmable Espresso Machine with LED Display & Pressure Gauge
bullet_points: 【Stable Uniform Extraction with Pressure Gauge】Upgraded 20-bar pump paired with an NTC temperature sensor maintains stable extraction pressure to fully draw out coffee’s rich aroma. The adjustable pre-infusion soaks grounds evenly to avoid channeling for balanced, smooth flavor. A built-in real-time pressure gauge lets beginners and home baristas monitor the whole brewing process for consistent results every shot.

【Space-Saving Stainless Steel Body】Made of food-grade brushed stainless steel, this machine is scratch-resistant, durable and super easy to wipe clean. Its compact footprint occupies little counter space, ideal for small kitchens, apartments, office pantries and home coffee nooks while retaining full professional espresso performance.

【Clear LED Digital Control Panel】User-friendly LED display keeps brewing fully visible: it shows preset temperature on standby and switches to a real-time extraction timer mid-brew. Simple visual feedback delivers straightforward, error-free operation for daily use.

【Fully Customizable Brewing Parameters】Adjust extraction temperature (194°F–204°F), single/double shot volume and pre-infusion duration to match your coffee bean roast and personal taste. Quick one-touch toggle between Celsius and Fahrenheit for customized, repeatable espresso.

【Powerful Steam Wand for Latte Art】Equipped with a stainless steel adjustable steam wand (257°F–302°F steam temp) that outputs steady, strong steam. It whips smooth velvety microfoam effortlessly, great for crafting cappuccinos, lattes and fancy homemade coffee art.

【Beginner Friendly, Works With All Ground Coffee】No professional skills required. The included pressurized filter basket fits any regular pre-ground coffee, generating thick golden crema without expensive specialty beans, lowering the barrier for new home coffee lovers.

reviews.title: Amazing Quality Espresso / Cappuccino Machine!
reviews.body: This HiBREW H10B Espresso maker is an excellent choice for beginners or as an affordable alternative to more expensive brands. I am not the type that likes to overspend on machinery and equipment if I am not sure I want to fully invest in a hobby. One would think this would mean a budget friendly machine like this would be lacking in quality. Not so, and could not be further from the truth. The build quality is superb for the price point and has a small footprint for countertops. This espresso machine allows inexperienced individuals like myself learn the espresso / cappuccino workflow with ease. I started with the pressurized 2 shot basket first with preground coffee. This still made what I thought were very decent cappuccinos which is what I primarily bought this machine for. It was easy to learn the milk frothing technique and dilute the coffee down a bit without needing creamer. The adjustable heat settings are great and allow for tweaking of different styles of coffee. A cold brew function is also possible at 25 degrees Celsius. There are no leaks, and the steam wand works great for milk frothing. The simple design of the machine keeps itself very clean as long as you purge it after every use and take care to clean it and not abuse it. I advanced later after buying a grinder for "true" espresso shots with Kona Hawaii coffee whole beans and it is simply amazing. The learning curve was not bad as it functions very similar to the preground basket, you just have to change to the bottomless basket for espresso grind and carefully tamp, and monitor the process. All the portafilters for this machine are for 51mm size and it seems only hold about 14 grams of espresso ground coffee. Any more than 14 grams will overfill it and it won't want to seal. The pressure gage is fantastic for diagnosing what grind setting and other variables for making your espresso better and learning the process. This is a fantastic value espresso maker for the money! I wanted to get into homemade espresso making to reduce the amount of overly sugary and expensive coffee drinks bought at coffee shops. If you follow the math of buying coffee at shops, this machine pays for itself after a few short months and even sooner if you buy multiple coffee drinks a day! At this price point, it allows one to enter the espresso making process at a reasonable price point with amazing quality and features. Plus, for the money, you wind up making better tasting coffee at home. Finally, the Hibrew company reaches out to you directly after purchase and seems to have great customer support! That is very rare nowadays, and is very comforting to know a company doesn't leave you high and dry after purchase! Keep it up!

reviews.title: So good I bought 2!
reviews.body: I have waited one year before writing this review so that the performance and reliability over time is accurately described. in a word, it is fantastic! Absolutely no issues and the consistency of its temperature and shot volumes are amazing! I have come to admire just how well this machine is built. this machine has everything you need in terms of adjustability to make perfect shots. The ability to set the volume of water for the espresso shot is the best feature. It is amazingly consistent. The variable temperature settings are equally outstanding in accuracy and consistency. The pressure gauge has proven extremely useful in helping me dial in the best grind size and I'm glued to it like a television set every time I pull a shot to see how the extraction is going, you can tell instantly if the needle starts dropping suddenly or bouncing around too much that something went wrong with your puck, like a bad tamp or a clump or something that started channeling. Don't be alarmed if your pressure indication goes into the red zone for extractions, it's perfectly fine , this is a relative indicator, you'll get used to it. And you will become addicted to it! You would be crazy to spend $500-$1000 or more for machines that do less or have unnecessary complications like Bluetooth to your phone. I am a coffee fanatic and for about 50 years now have been roasting my own beans for the ultimate in flavor. This machine gives me everything I want and has proven more reliable than anything from Breville or others and I used to have a Breville. Because of my experience with Breville's , when I first bought this machine I contacted their customer service through email to ask if replacement gaskets would be available since these were a common failure on my Breville machines. Their customer service responded immediately letting me know that if I ever needed one they would be happy to send it to me. I also complimented them on how happy I was with the purchase and what a great machine they had. I also let them know how I removed the insert in their porter filter handle in order to be able to use a non-pressurized basket of my favorite size. they were amused by my ingenuity, so much so that they sent me a porta filter handle that is open at the bottom so that it will take baskets of any size and type. They sent it to me for free! I guess because I was so enthusiastic about their machine. I looked on their website and it's worth around 50 bucks! They were really nice, real people who care. So I decided to do some research and found a YouTube video that shows the operation of the company and the CEO and was blown away at what a great operation and how charismatic the CEO is and how everybody is happy working there. I highly recommend that you look on YouTube for the video titled: HiBREW BRAND STORY. You'll appreciate your machine even more when you see the people and how it designed and manufactured! This is a great company! They design and build these products and they have the pride that these are their babies! Buy this unit, you will be happy! I guarantee it! and don't think that you need a larger diameter filter basket like 58mm, 50 mm has been my preference for decades because for my 18 g shots it's perfect and resists channeling better than the larger diameter baskets I think. Shortly after I bought my first one, I was so impressed that I bought another one just in case they ever stop making them!

reviews.title: Silly how good this is for the price
reviews.body: First off, I am NOT a coffee beginner. I roasted my coffee for a decade, I helped to develop a very advanced espresso machine and have tried novel espresso preparation methods and techniques over the years. That said, I kind of got burnt out on it and a year ago, sold off my very expensive machine and grinder and have just been doing drip or pourover. However, I got the bug again recently just watching some reviews of cheaper machines like the Hibrew H10A and decided to grab this one seeing it has the same internals at an even lower price. I am shocked at how capable this tiny little thing is. And it is tiny. Feels like a toy. It's light, the portafilter is small and light. The steam wand is baby. It feels miniature. But it also feels solid enough. It hardly takes up any space and I think it looks pretty good! It's got the capability to do adjustable preinfusion as well as adjustable brew and steam temps (They probably aren't super accurate, but as long as it is consistent, it is a win) - It even has 'stop at volume'. The water tank is of reasonable size and comes off for refill in a snap. Essentially unheard of stuff at this price point. The machine came with a couple pressurized baskets and one single wall - which I determined can hold 15g of coffee. The supplied scoop/tamp is awful, but they all are. I have a 51mm tamper which is much better as well as a dosing funnel which makes getting the coffee in the tiny portafilter without making a big mess a whole lot easier. My workflow looks like this - I'm grinding for espresso with my very capable 1zpresso k plus hand grinder. Takes about 20 seconds to grind 15g which isn't much less than it takes this machine to heat up. I generally pull a blank shot to get things warmed up while I'm grinding. Pulling the shot itself is simply pushing a button. Love that there's a timer built in - I'm aiming for about 35 seconds total with the 10s preinfusion I've got set. My pressure gauge is off on my unit - I need to see if I can fix it as it doesn't reset to zero, but I don't really find myself looking at it anyway. Once I hit about 35g of coffee in the cup, I stop the shot. There's no 3-way solenoid valve here, so coffee continues to drip for a bit - That's part of it being very inexpensive. I then hit the steam button to have the machine warm up to my 150C setting (the hottest). This takes about 10-15 seconds, which allows me to knock the coffee puck out and give it a wipe. Once steam is ready, I purge the water from the wand into the drip tray, and then restart in my milk pitcher. Steaming 200ml takes about 1 minute. It's a bit long, but hey, tiny machine. It's got just enough power to make decent microfoam and I can pour art with it without trouble. I then purge the wand again after switching back to coffee and wipe it down. I can go from cold machine to latte in about 5 or 6 minutes, though results do benefit from the machine being on for 10 or 15 minutes before starting. All in all, with good coffee and a good grinder, the results you can achieve from this machine are pretty astounding. It costs 40x less than my last machine and I'm probably 90% of the results. Negatives are really down to the size and mass. None of the materials hold heat well, so temps will vary. The 51mm filter is a bit of a limitation, but the H10A has a 58mm portafilter if you'd like something more traditional in size for a bit more money. The steam wand is also teeny tiny, but once you get used to it, it is workable. So long as you can deal with the diminutive sizes of things here, I can highly recommend it. It's perfect to scratch the itch of wanting a latte once in awhile for me without going all in on really expensive gear, and with the current price of one at your local cafe, it pays for itself in like a week!

reviews.title: Mighty little machine for a good price!
reviews.body: This mighty little machine makes really good espresso. My husband was disenchanted with our Keurig saying it doesn't make his coffee strong enough. We already have a frother and burr grinder so we just needed a good espresso machine. Right out of the box we got an E-2 error but I searched reviews for "E-2" and found a customer who fiddled with the steam button and voila, success. Wish it produced crema on top of the espresso but it's not necessary the way my husband mixes it with steamed chocolate almond milk. Did lots of research and purchased a 51mm bottomless Portafilter as well as Hugh basket but they did not fit this machine so I returned them. Also based on previous reviews, I run a short cup cycle without the portafilter after brewing and it removes excess grounds left behind. I wish the clearance below the portafilter once inserted was a tad higher. I have to untwist the portafilter then remove it together with my short espresso pitcher or I end up spilling espresso into the tray below by tilting the little metal pitcher to remove after brewing. It heats up quickly, easy to use, stays put with suction feet, and has a small footprint on my counter next to the Keurig I still use most mornings.

reviews.title: Excellent little espresso engine that could!
reviews.body: I've been using the H10B for a couple months now on a daily basis and I am thoroughly impressed with the quality of shots I've been able to get from this machine! This is my first espresso machine upgrade from my thrift store Delonghi machine, although the Delonghi was pretty good, it was a combo machine with a drop side and I needed a smaller unit to fit on my coffee station. I was drawn to the H10B for a few standout reasons. It is 51mm, so I could keep my accessories from my Delonghi, it has temperature and pre infusion control, and it includes pressure gauge so at under $150! All these controls on an entry level machine have been a huge game changer. I can better dial in my shots and make tasty drinks. Because of these features and resulting quality shots, I've been able to transition to drinking my coffee black. My Americano drinks have been so delicious. It's also small enough to be semi-portable. I've taken it to my partner's house for a weekend hangout and made affogatos for everyone. It streams milk pretty well, I'm just not that great at it. I can't say too much about it since I don't drink milk drinks often, but it does the job. I've been able to make some great shots with my Oxo burr grinder, but I recently upgraded to the Kingrinder K6 and the quality of my espresso has dramatically improved! I don't see myself needing to upgrade this machine anytime soon. The fact that I've been able to pull such great tasting shots with this little machine as beginner says a lot about it. With the money you save with the H11B, you can invest your money in great quality beans, filtered water, a high quality burr grinder, and other stuff after. After using this multiple times daily for the past couple months, I highly recommend it. 👍

reviews.title: Great value…love this machine
reviews.body: I purchased the H10B several days ago after reviewing YouTube videos. I'm a coffee rookie. This is my first 'expresso' machine and I love it. I have successfully used it each morning since it arrived. The instructions read easily and it is simple to use and makes an outstanding expresso and the frother adds to my morning cappuccino. First thing I noticed is that the machine comes extremely well packaged and the construction appears to be very good. I'm impressed with all of the features (PID), temperature selection for coffee and cold brew, and the ease to select the steam selection for frothing. This machine reaches temperature quite quickly both for coffee and steam. Another nice detail, the suction cups on the bottom are a nice addition and really do work quite well. Overall, I am very impressed with the quality and really look forward to having that first burst of caffeine in the morning. The H10B is well worth the money. This is a 6 week update. I REALLY REALLY enjoy this espresso coffee maker. I look forward to going through my morning ritual to make my cappuccino. The H10B makes it easy to get the right temp and the perfect taste every time. As I stated right after my first use of the machine the temp rises to 95 (my selected temp setting) quickly (<25 secs) and the steamer hits 130 in under 30 seconds after brewing as well. I received a bottomless portafilter from the manufacturer 2 weeks ago and enjoy using it for a bit of variety. Don’t laugh but those little rubber feet on the bottom of the machine really do help hold the machine in position. I’d buy this again in a heartbeat if I was just starting out. Based on what I’ve experienced with this machine I’ll definitely try one of their high end machines when the time is right (and my wife wants a gift idea from me). August ’25 After 6 months this machine is still going strong. It is used every day that I’m home and it never disappoints. January ’26. I still love it. It has been almost a year since I purchased this machine. It is still going strong and making a great espresso/cappuccino most every morning. I find it interesting that numerous people on line want to sell their more expensive (complicated?) high end machines and are searching for an easy to use machine. This HiBrew would be an obvious choice.

reviews.title: You get what you pay for!
reviews.body: Bought the Hibrew H10B as a back up in case our other espresso machine fails. Tried it out for 2 weeks to test it out since Amazon only give you 30 days to return it and it worked fairly well so we decided to keep it. I could tell that the steamer wasn’t as strong as our other machine but it still got the job done. So we decided to pack it back up and save it for an emergency when our other machine eventually dies. But before we packed it up, even though I didn’t think it needed it (we have soft water), I descaled it anyways just to make sure no build up happened and could ruin the machine and not work when we needed it. Well, it finally came time to pull her out a year later to save the day. Wrong! It would make the espresso fine, but the steamer barely worked and for only about 20 seconds and would stop working. Tried this several times and it kept doing the same thing. What a piece of junk. Don’t buy. You know the old saying, “You get what you pay for”. Save yourself the trouble and buy the real deal. You’ll be glad you did. I'll be amazed if the company reaches out and tries to make this right.

reviews.title: Reliable and dependable beginner machine
reviews.body: I’ve had this machine for over a year. I use it three times a day, both pressurized and unpressurized, and I steam milk for lattes. reviews.title: Una increíble máquina de espresso a un precio sumamente razonable y repleta de funciones
reviews.body: Una increíble máquina de espresso a un precio sumamente razonable y repleta de funciones. Si te tomas el tiempo de investigar, leer y experimentar, esta pequeña máquina puede producir un espresso asombroso. Lo digo como dueño de un restaurante y como alguien que ha sido capacitado por mis baristas, quienes se han posicionado entre el 1% superior en competencias a nivel nacional. La capacidad de preinfusión, el ajuste de temperatura y el manómetro para monitorear la presión de extracción son características que normalmente se encuentran en máquinas de gama alta. Su construcción totalmente de acero la convierte en un dispositivo elegante y compacto. Además, cuenta con ventosas en la base para brindarle estabilidad al insertar el portafiltro. Mi única recomendación es que adquieras un portafiltro sin fondo (hay varios disponibles en Amazon) y un filtro adicional para colocar sobre el café molido. Estos dos accesorios elevan esta máquina a otro nivel. Esta empresa fue fundada por un ingeniero con más de 20 años de experiencia en el sector del café, y eso se nota. China está demostrando su capacidad para producir artículos de alta calidad que ahora están disponibles en el extranjero. Uno de los aspectos que se deben tener en cuenta es... La disponibilidad de productos chinos de alta calidad para la exportación se ha visto limitada en el pasado. Esto se debe principalmente a que los importadores de diversas empresas buscan el producto más barato posible para obtener el mayor beneficio, lo que ha generado una mala reputación en China, asociándola únicamente con la fabricación de productos baratos, lo cual no es cierto. Al igual que en cualquier otro país, China puede fabricar productos que van desde muy económicos hasta de muy alta calidad y precio elevado (como el iPhone). Todo depende de cuánto esté dispuesto a pagar el cliente y de la oferta de los importadores. Es positivo ver que el mercado global ahora puede acceder a algunos de los productos chinos de mayor calidad a precios razonables.
reviews.body_en: An incredible espresso machine at an extremely reasonable price and packed with features. If you take the time to research, read, and experiment, this little machine can produce amazing espresso. I say this as a restaurant owner and as someone who has been trained by my baristas, who have placed in the top 1% in national competitions. Pre-infusion capability, temperature adjustment, and pressure gauge to monitor draw pressure are features typically found on high-end machines. Its all-steel construction makes it a sleek and compact device. In addition, it has suction cups on the base to provide stability when inserting the filter holder. My only recommendation is that you purchase a bottomless portafilter (there are several available on Amazon) and an additional filter to place over the ground coffee. These two accessories take this machine to another level. This company was founded by an engineer with more than 20 years of experience in the coffee sector, and it shows. China is demonstrating its ability to produce high-quality items that are now available abroad. One of the things to keep in mind is... The availability of high-quality Chinese products for export has been limited in the past. This is mainly because importers from various companies look for the cheapest possible product to obtain the greatest profit, which has generated a bad reputation in China, associating it only with the manufacture of cheap products, which is not true. Just like any other country, China can make products ranging from very cheap to very high quality and high priced (like the iPhone). It all depends on how much the client is willing to pay and the importers' offer. It is positive to see that the global market can now access some of the highest quality Chinese products at reasonable prices.

reviews.title: Buyer beware - don't make the mistake of buying this product
reviews.body: I wanted to love this coffee maker so much, I really did. It's definitely a fun design and looks great, and it worked like a charm for a couple of months, but then I started having the same issue that so many others started having when their pot wasn't very old. It started steaming up a storm (literally making the machine soaking wet with steam sweat as it tried to brew) and brewing very, very little coffee... and having a burnt taste to what actually did end up in the pot. On top of that, the carafe is incredibly thin and fragile. My first one cracked by the handle within weeks, and after some teeth pulling I managed to get a replacement from the company... but then, a little over a month later, the brewer itself stopped working. I know I've read about a 1-year warranty, but I honestly don't even think it's worth the hassle trying to get a replacement for a crappy coffee brewer that's just going to crap out on me again after a few months. For example, when I tried to get a replacement carafe... I first contacted Amazon and was told I had to go directly to Nostalgia, so I did. I emailed them first, but after many days did not hear back. I then found a phone number and called. After a looooooong hold time I finally spoke to someone and she was very nice and said she was sending me a new pot (despite their website saying they were out of stock). A day after I spoke to this lady on the phone someone else replied to my email and said they couldn't send me a new carafe. I told her that I spoke to someone who said they would send me a new carafe to which this person basically replied, "so she did." It sounded like the person on the email didn't want to send me a replacement at all despite them actually having them in stock. I'm glad I got someone on the phone, because they did come through... but that's still a bit shady - hence why I don't even feel like dealing with trying to replace the whole crappy unit now that it's crapped out on me. I'm sadly tossing this in the trash and putting money towards a top rated and top notch coffee brewer. No fun nostalgia in my kitchen, design wise, but I'd rather have functionality any day of the week.

reviews.title: Very disappointed.
reviews.body: First, an introduction, this will take some going through, bear with me. First, I had refused for years to get a Keurig, as I did not feel the quality and richness of a good strong cup of coffee was possible. But I finally got tired of trying other methods of brewing, from using a regular single cup espresso maker, moka pot, pour over, French press... I finally opted for the ease of a Keurig mini-plus. Coffee was ...eh... I switched coffee brands, to what I feel has to be the best commercial brand. And the coffee was EXcellenT! About a year later, despite regular cleaning cycles, the thing just stopped working. I tried to take it apart, watched some youtube videos which just solidified the fact that the company made these non-serviceable. P.O.'d at this obvious tactic to sell more, I waited a few weeks, but went and got another one. Same deal a year later. Another one. This last one gave me signs before ending it's own life. I would have to run several cycles where nothing would come out... till finally something... drip... by drip... several hours later, the thing would start running again, only to stop again the next day or two. Finally, it just died. So I REFUSED to get another. These things are ridiculous, right? So I got a new French press. Coffee is great!! But... omg... what a pain cleaning that thing every.... single... time... I mean, really, it's no big deal. But, it CAn be. So I saw this thing on sale, I thought, well, it's HAlf the price of the other ones... and I def want something different this time. Cut to now.... This thing has SEVERAL issues that I don't like. First of all, it is a thinner cheaper plastic, and has a cheap looking shine to it. Ok, I'm over it. The plastic... I mean, can't they make these things with glass reservoirs.... the plastic reservoir has screws on the inside of it. I don't care if they say it is food safe... Plastic is also considered food safe... but that doesn't mean it is.. those are just bureaucratic rhetoric lies. But I digress,...So this coffee maker has an adjustment for high altitude... is THAT what ruined my previous Keurigs? High altitude? Hmmm. Ok, so maybe that's a plus. It also has different sizes that you can choose -8,10, & 12 oz. With the mini-plus, you choose the size by the amount of water you pour in. That means that this one measures what it sucks in. Hmmm. The mini-plus had the controls on the top. Easy peasy. This one has the controls on the side. It also doesn't have rubber feet on the bottom. So when you try to push the buttons, the thing slides away from you. Impossible to push any buttons with one hand, you have to use two. Even with rubber feet, you have to use two hands. I'm not a paraplegic, but it's rather stupid to have to hold the thing to press a button or two, or three. Which is what you have to do. It's just really awkward because you really have to hold it in the back to keep it from moving when you press the button in front. And you have to do that without touching the reservoir, which will pop out if you tried that. But let's get to the coffee. So with the mini-plus, the first liquid out of the machine, was dark coffee. As it was finishing, the coffee would be a little more clear, but not pure water. With this machine, for the first few seconds, it is spewing out crystal clear WATER. I don't even know how that is possible. But this, it does. It also claims to be faster than the mini-cup. I hestitate to say "brews faster", because it doesn't brew, Keurigs simply spew water into and through the k-cup, it's a pressurized system, not a true brewing system. And it definitely IS faster. And that's a problem, as evidenced by the watery coffee that it spews out. Sure enough, the "coffee" tastes like water. This is the 8 oz brew, mind you, with the machine set to "strong". I first tried the 12oz, and ended up pouring it down the sink. The 8 oz wasn't much better. My next step is to switch out cups while it's pouring out the water at the beginning of the cycle and see if I can get a stronger "brew". All in all, it's convenient enough. But it will sit on my counter, mostly unused, for when I have those really lazy, sleepy, or sick days, when all I want to do is pop in a capsule, and deal with the rest of it... Very disappointed. Perhaps if you live in a low altitude area, the mini-plus would work for you. I really do recommend that one above this.

First, I had refused for years to get a Keurig, as I did not feel the quality and richness of a good strong cup of coffee was possible. But I finally got tired of trying other methods of brewing, from using a regular single cup espresso maker, moka pot, pour over, French press... I finally opted for the ease of a Keurig mini-plus. Coffee was ...eh... I switched coffee brands, to what I feel has to be the best commercial brand. And the coffee was EXcellenT! About a year later, despite regular cleaning cycles, the thing just stopped working. I tried to take it apart, watched some youtube videos which just solidified the fact that the company made these non-serviceable. P.O.'d at this obvious tactic to sell more, I waited a few weeks, but went and got another one. Same deal a year later. Another one. This last one gave me signs before ending it's own life. I would have to run several cycles where nothing would come out... till finally something... drip... by drip... several hours later, the thing would start running again, only to stop again the next day or two. Finally, it just died. So I REFUSED to get another. These things are ridiculous, right? So I got a new French press. Coffee is great!! But... omg... what a pain cleaning that thing every.... single... time... I mean, really, it's no big deal. But, it CAn be. So I saw this thing on sale, I thought, well, it's HAlf the price of the other ones... and I def want something different this time. Cut to now.... This thing has SEVERAL issues that I don't like. First of all, it is a thinner cheaper plastic, and has a cheap looking shine to it. Ok, I'm over it. The plastic... I mean, can't they make these things with glass reservoirs.... the plastic reservoir has screws on the inside of it. I don't care if they say it is food safe... Plastic is also considered food safe... but that doesn't mean it is.. those are just bureaucratic rhetoric lies. But I digress,...So this coffee maker has an adjustment for high altitude... is THAT what ruined my previous Keurigs? High altitude? Hmmm. Ok, so maybe that's a plus. It also has different sizes that you can choose -8,10, & 12 oz. With the mini-plus, you choose the size by the amount of water you pour in. That means that this one measures what it sucks in. Hmmm. The mini-plus had the controls on the top. Easy peasy. This one has the controls on the side. It also doesn't have rubber feet on the bottom. So when you try to push the buttons, the thing slides away from you. Impossible to push any buttons with one hand, you have to use two. Even with rubber feet, you have to use two hands. I'm not a paraplegic, but it's rather stupid to have to hold the thing to press a button or two, or three. Which is what you have to do. It's just really awkward because you really have to hold it in the back to keep it from moving when you press the button in front. And you have to do that without touching the reservoir, which will pop out if you tried that. But let's get to the coffee. So with the mini-plus, the first liquid out of the machine, was dark coffee. As it was finishing, the coffee would be a little more clear, but not pure water. With this machine, for the first few seconds, it is spewing out crystal clear WATER. I don't even know how that is possible. But this, it does. It also claims to be faster than the mini-cup. I hestitate to say "brews faster", because it doesn't brew, Keurigs simply spew water into and through the k-cup, it's a pressurized system, not a true brewing system. And it definitely IS faster. And that's a problem, as evidenced by the watery coffee that it spews out. Sure enough, the "coffee" tastes like water. This is the 8 oz brew, mind you, with the machine set to "strong". I first tried the 12oz, and ended up pouring it down the sink. The 8 oz wasn't much better. My next step is to switch out cups while it's pouring out the water at the beginning of the cycle and see if I can get a stronger "brew". All in all, it's convenient enough. But it will sit on my counter, mostly unused, for when I have those really lazy, sleepy, or sick days, when all I want to do is pop in a capsule, and deal with the rest of it... Very disappointed. Perhaps if you live in a low altitude area, the mini-plus would work for you. I really do recommend that one above this.

reviews.title: Most excellent
reviews.body: I got this to replace my original Keurig. The old k50 or whatever it was. This thing takes up less space, looks more sleek, and works better than the original. It's faster, the coffee tastes better, it has the strong button. Also, I keep my coffee maker in my bedroom, and with the old one if you wanted it to be ready to make a quick cup of coffee it had to be turned on which meant that it had lights illuminated. I had to cover them with tape. This new one can go from being turned off to making a quick cup of coffee immediately. And after 5 minutes it automatically turns any illumination off. That means it doesn't make light in my bedroom at night. It's just a way way better version. It's quieter. I love it I'm so glad I got it. I will say that I got this brand new, and it was a really good deal, and I can see why because the manual includes an offer for discounted coffee that expired over two years ago. I'm guessing Keurig punched out a few too many of these models and they've been sitting in a warehouse for too many years. My advice is buy it now before it goes out of stock. It is an excellent coffee maker.

reviews.title: Wonderful machine
reviews.body: Okay, so this review is long overdue. I bought this beautiful machine in December of 24 as a Christmas for myself from my husband and I actually had surgery on Tuesday and that may seem irrelevant but stay with me. On Tuesday of this week 07/14/26 is when my baby decided to start smelling like something was burning and would not turn on. I was devastated 💔. So we pulled out our old single cup, wait a half hour to heat up water, back up and used it until Thursday. Went looking for a replacement, this machine had went up in price by over 50 bucks so I'm not liking the situation already. I found a video on how to fix the problem. The thermostat overheated due to the water tank being off kilter. So the warranty is void anyway, I popped the case off and reset the thermostat with a paper clip, and the machine works perfectly. This is a common issue with this machine apparently. So if this happens don't throw your treasure away, please find the video and try to save your beloved machine.

reviews.title: Great product but it stopped working after 8 months. The warrantee was honored.
reviews.body: I've used Keurig coffee makers for many years. I really like the K-Supreme. It's compact, brews a cup of coffee quickly, has a strong brew option and I like having the serving size options (4, 8, 10 and 12oz). The problem I had is it stopped working after 8 months - it would not power on. Granted I used the coffee maker a lot - 5 to 6 cups a day - but it should last longer than 8 months. My guess, and it's just a guess, is the thermal fuse went - there was a slight "burnt electronics" smell when it stopped working. Keurig did honor the 1 year warrantee and shipped me a brand new replacement unit at no cost and I did not have to return the defective unit. A word of warning, I had to prove the unit was purchased on Amazon and shipped directly by Amazon. Apparently, Keurig may not honor the warrantee if the unit was purchased from a third party seller. The warrantee claim process was challenging at best. The call center is most likely overseas. Information like your email address is repeated back to you in a Alpha Charlie Bravo manner. Even with that, the Agent got it wrong and I waited about a week for an email to start the claims process. A call back confirmand they had my email address wrong. I submitted the required proof of purchased information and my claim was denied. Another call resolved that when I pointed out the receipt showed I purchased the item on Amazon and I told the Agent I had additional proof the unit was shipped directly by Amazon. My claim was then approved and I received a brand new replacement with all accessories in about one week.

reviews.title: Great coffee maker so far upgrade over previous generations
reviews.body: OK so this review is an overall review of not just the product but Amazon as well. I have had this machine around 3 months now. The machine itself is amazing. The ease of use from the previous generation one is night and day. Things i like: The handle on the water reservoir.. finally.. LoL. The reservoir plastic is also thicker and more durable. My previous model reservoir was thinner plastic and cracked and it was also curved. This machine's water container is rectangular so more solid. That in itself makes this machine worth it. This machine makes hotter coffee and the over ice feature is nice. I love the grey color. What i dont like: Lid will not close all the way with reusable K-cups. Will not close even with the Keurig branded ones. This is only cosmetic it seems though. Functionality seems unchanged. When i use this coffee maker the LED lights in the kitchen will flicker. The previous model did NOT do this and had similar wattage rating and a grounded plug. The wattage is listed on this newer machine is 1520W. the only other thing on the same circuit is the LED lights. This coffee maker does NOT have a grounded plug. Maybe this is why the lights flicker? I got a great price on this for Black Friday time. The first one i got was DoA and would not turn on. It had very obviously been repackaged and retaped. Getting an Amazon chat associate is not as easy as it should be. The AI questions absolutely suck! I was able to finally get a rep on chat and they did make it right. Had UPS come and pick it up at my home which saved me a trip to the UPS store that has lines out the door. The new machine I received is working great so far!

reviews.title: Best Cup of Coffee
reviews.body: I upgraded my previous Keurig coffee maker that I bought in 2013. It was worth the upgrade. I like how easy this machine is to use. Easy setup: Right out of the box there was little that needed to be done. Just remove factory tape, plug it in and run a single water only cycle and good to go. Taste: I use a quality coffee. I played with the "strong" button and that was one of the best cups of coffee I've had. Speed: Hot water on demand. This machine heats the water right before it hits the pod. There is no internal reservoir the water is first pumped into to heat first. This means the speed of use is much faster. My previous unit had this and it took a bit longer to get that first cup. Because there is no internal reservoir there is less places for scaling to take place. Using filtered water also reduces this buildup. Extraction: This unit is cooler than some other units and extracts at 192 with a final cup temp of about 165. This is less than coffee enthusiasts recommend. I taste no difference as my coffee still had a rich and bold flavor. For someone who enjoys coffee without all the fine tuning this works great. Ascetically pleasing: I love how small this unit is and how it looks on the counter. It doesn't have a LCD readout with the time or a way to auto set for an automatic cup. The hot water on demand eliminates this need. Just turn it on and you have a cup in maybe a minute. Also, without an LCD display, less to break. Clean up: The area that the pod is inserted in is not concave as my previous unit was. It can be easily wiped clean. My previous unit could get a buildup of crud around the pod area. That can't happen with this unit. Descaling setting: While I've not used it yet, I like that it has a descaling setting when I do clean out my machine. My previous didn't have this and it took longer to run cycles. Cons: Factory taste!! My first two cups of coffee tasted like crap. I assumed this was because it was still getting the factory taste out of the unit. On the 3rd attempt I used the "strong" button and wow I tasted a difference. I'm also using zero water for my coffee. Overall if you want a "no thrills" machine that makes coffee fast and very well then I recommend this product.

reviews.title: Loyal Keurig User
reviews.body: Perfect for individuals or couples who don't drink enough coffee to make a full pot and waste the rest. My wife and I typically only drink about 3 cups each morning. We used to brew coffee by the pot, but even limiting the brew to four cups, we still ended up wasting a cup. Our previous Keurig K-Supreme stopped working, so we tried another brand that offered both K-Cup and coffee pot capabilities. We were expecting company for Christmas, and this seemed to be a good idea at the time. The Keurig K-Supreme provides a much more robust flavor and gives a comparable amount of coffee in about half the time of the other brand. We purchased the other brand about a month before Christmas, so we could try to adapt to it. After a week, I ordered the K-Supreme and stored it until after the company left at the end of the holidays. The K-Supreme is easy to use, fits on the coffee station counter, and under the cabinet with no problem. If there is any fault with the K-Supreme, it is the tendency to fail after several de-scaling periods. I think the solution would be to de-scale the unit more regularly and not wait until the warning light goes off. It may be the mineral content of our water, but we do use and replace the water filter in the tank regularly. I have seen cleaning tablets offered on Amazon. I plan on giving those a try. The only other nit to pick, and it is probably the result of using fine-ground coffee in the mesh pod that comes with the brewer. We had purchased ground coffee for use in the brewer from the other company. It works just fine and does not pass the fine grounds through the mesh, but the grounds get so tightly packed during brewing that it is difficult to clear the grounds from the mesh cup. After the ground coffee is gone, we will switch to medium grind.

reviews.title: Filter traps air bubbles & machine needs to be burped occasionally.
reviews.body: UPDATE: We did buy a new one, but it's in the box until needed. Wife noticed there were air bubbles under the reservoir filter & wondered if that was causing the problems. She removed the filter (we have whole house filtration anyway) & burped the machine by shaking it upside down, Solved the problem & has been making great coffee ever since! Love the slimness. Made great coffee, until it didn't. Followed all instructions & descaling schedule. Started having issues 3 months after purchase. Would only make half a cup of 12oz coffee. Then it didn't recognize that it was full of water & we had to jiggle the reservoir. Sometimes it would make noise without brewing at all. Ordering another one since we purchased a bunch of the stainless K-cups with the 5 holes specifically for this machine.

title: Ninja Luxe Café Premier 3-in-1 Espresso Machine, Drip Coffee, & Cold Brew
bullet_points: BE YOUR OWN BARISTA: Café-quality espresso shouldn't require a PhD. The Ninja Luxe Cafe Premier is a 3-in-1 machine designed to take the guesswork out of every latte, cappuccino, cold brew, and cup of coffee. Perfect for beginning espresso enthusiasts and anyone looking for a great, dialed-in cup of coffee with practically zero effort.

3 MACHINES IN 1: Includes 2 Espresso Styles — double shot or quad shot, 3 Drip Coffee Styles—classic, rich or over ice, and 2 Cold Brew styles— cold pressed espresso or cold brew coffee (drip coffee and cold brew available in 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 oz. sizes)..

HANDS-FREE FROTHING: Dual Froth System combines a spinning whisk with automatic steamer to produce perfect, silky-smooth microfaom every time. Simply pour the milk, select style, and walk away. 4 preset programs including steamed milk, thin froth, thick froth and cold foam or the option to manually froth..

COFFEE MAKER WITH GRINDER: A built-in conical burr grinder features 25 settings for precise, versatile grinding based on your specific drink. Brew your classic morning cup of coffee or create a summer afternoon cold brew with the exact grind and dosage you need.

SMART TECHNOLOGY: This coffee and espresso combo machine features Barista Assist Technology that guides you every step of the way, from automatic precision grinding to weight-based dosing, assisted tamping for the perfectly pressed puck, and active real-time temperature and pressure adjustments based on your selected drink.

FLAVORFUL COLD-PRESSED DRINKS: Create decadent espresso martinis or iced lattes using the cold pressed espresso function, which brews at a lower temperature, pressure, and pace to extract a more flavorful, smooth brew. If drip is more your style, enjoy rapid cold brew coffee without the wait.

CONVENIENTLY DESIGNED: Bult-in accessory storage saves precious countertop space. This coffee and espresso maker comes with Portafilter, Milk Jug, Double Basket, Luxe Basket, Assisted Tamper, Cleaning Brush, Cleaning Disc, Funnel, Descaling Powder, Cleaning tablets, Hard Water Testing Kit, Instructions & Inspiration Guide.

reviews.title: "This One Earned Its Spot."
reviews.body: My wife had always wanted an espresso machine without spending a fortune. The night she ordered this one, she could barely sleep. When it finally arrived, her excitement was through the roof. We've been using it regularly since it was delivered on May 29, and it has exceeded our expectations. The reality is that this is an excellent product at a reasonable price. There isn't a single part that feels cheap or flimsy. The machine feels sturdy, well-built, and refined, and it looks great sitting on our coffee bar. I think the stainless-steel finish is a great neutral color that fits into almost any kitchen. If you're looking for something a little different, Ninja offers other color options on their website. You can certainly spend more on a higher-end model, but for our family, this machine has everything we need. If you're looking for Starbucks-level speed every morning, it's capable of delivering that. However, I'd encourage you to slow down and enjoy the process. There's something incredibly satisfying about crafting your own coffee and producing a drink that feels café quality from the comfort of your home. The instructions and videos are so well done that they leave you feeling confident from day one. After a little practice, you'll feel like you could walk into a coffee shop and tell the barista, "Thanks, but I'll make my own coffee today." To wrap up this admittedly long review—because Ninja deserves it—they absolutely knocked it out of the park. Between the build quality, ease of use, and quality of the drinks it produces, this machine has earned a permanent place in our kitchen. As an Air Force veteran, I appreciate products that do what they promise, and this one delivers. I'm extremely happy with this purchase and would recommend it without hesitation.
