reviews.title: Nice chair, easy to put together, nice style, limited arm movement priced quite high at 370
reviews.body: Quick important tip: DO NOT TOSS THE BOX WHEN YOU UNPACK IT! The directions explain to prop the pieces onto the outer box to build the chair and it was a GENIUS idea! Pay attention to the sticker on the seat that says FRONT of chair and aim the arms that way. Also the metal back piece needs to aim so the overhang part is at the back of the seat so the back piece can attach to it. I sometimes sit a work for 4-5 hours straight w/o a break so I need a good chair. The chair that I had was an expensive chair from a good brand, but, the seat cushion just didn’t give me the support and comfort that I was looking for and need. I also really wanted a white chair to go with my white office furniture. This chair hit all of the marks. This was a heavy box so be prepared to maybe have some help getting it in the house. I did it ok by myself, but my awesome Amazon driver left it on my top stop for me. This was very straight forward to put together, but I am also ok with putting things together in general. I do not think there will be many issues putting this together with one person. The directions are a little clunky. The chair is comfortbale and supportive. I did 3 hours straight of deep focus work and I was very comfortable. I also really like the color of grey and white. I was looking at $1100 Henry miller chairs because I really need a good chair- I’m glad I went with this chair- it’s good quality. It’s priced a bit high at $370. On the positive side, the chair was fairly easy to assemble, and the instructions were straightforward. Unfortunately, ease of assembly wasn’t enough to make up for the overall experience. For the amount this chair costs, I expected better comfort and quality. I wouldn’t purchase it again.

reviews.title: Feels Premium
reviews.body: I recently grabbed this Nouhaus Strato Ergonomic Chair because since I mostly work from home, I spend a lot of time in the same chair for work and gaming. The first thing I looked at was the build quality. The construction looks and feels both premium and sturdy at the same time. Installation was a snap following the detailed step by step instructions. All the materials feel durable enough to last for years and the stitching feels flawless without any loose threads found. One of the strengths of this chair is just how customizable the chair really is. The height-adjustable backrest and headrest allowed me to fine-tune the fit to match my posture perfectly, providing excellent support throughout the entire day. The ergonomic design of this chair promotes proper sitting posture and significantly reduced the fatigue and stiffness I previously experienced after hours at my desk. The lumbar support feels well-positioned and supportive without being overly firm. I found the adjustment mechanisms to be smooth, which makes it easy to find my ideal seating position for my body. I find the seat cushion is comfortable without feeling too soft, offering me the right balance of support and comfort. The back mesh design and materials promote air circulation to prevent unnecessary back sweat and the feeling that you are "sticking to the chair". The caster wheels feel rugged and glide easily across a low nap carpet. I have probably sat in this chair close to 30 hours so far and I have zero regrets picking it up. I haven't experienced any discomfort or body fatigue while using this chair. Overall, this Nouhaus Strato chair combines comfort, adjustability, and premium build quality into a stylish office chair that I would highly recommend to anyone working from home or in an office.

reviews.title: Comfortable Ergonomic Chair That Provides Excellent All-Day Support
reviews.body: This ergonomic office chair is thoughtfully designed for people who spend long hours at a desk. With multiple adjustment options and full-back support, it offers the flexibility needed to stay comfortable throughout the workday. One of the standout features is the height-adjustable backrest. Rather than relying on a fixed lumbar cushion, the back adjusts to better follow the natural curve of your spine, providing support across a wider range of sitting positions. The reclining backrest is another highlight. Multiple recline angles make it easy to switch between focused work, reading, or taking a quick break without sacrificing support. Combined with the adjustable headrest, it helps reduce strain on the neck and shoulders during extended use. I also appreciate the 3D armrests. Being able to adjust their height, depth, and angle makes it much easier to find a comfortable position whether you're typing, using a mouse, or simply relaxing between tasks. The breathable mesh back promotes good airflow, helping keep you cool during long work sessions, while the cushioned seat provides comfortable support without feeling overly soft or sinking over time. The sturdy base and smooth-rolling casters give the chair a stable feel while allowing easy movement around the workspace. Its clean, modern appearance also fits nicely into both home offices and professional environments. Assembly is straightforward, and the wide adjustment range makes it suitable for a variety of users and desk setups. Overall, this is a well-designed ergonomic chair that combines excellent adjustability, breathable comfort, and reliable support. It's a great investment for anyone looking to improve posture and stay comfortable during long hours of work, studying, or gaming.

reviews.title: Best Out of Three
reviews.body: This is my third gaming chair in the past few years and is my favorite of the three. It looks fantastic and sleek in my office space. I was drawn to the creme color and couldn't be happier with it in person. In fact, it matches even better than I anticipated. I have a smokey grey desk and shelf system which it fits well with and also looks good with my hard wood floor. Before I jump to more pros, I will point out the cons first that caused me to knock a star off of my review. The condition was not perfect. The flange was cracked as you can see from the picture and on one side of the seat there was a little dimple and the other side kind of wrinkled, but very minimal and not a deal breaker. The cracked flange is not a big deal because they usually end up cracking anyways and it doesn't have any effect on the mechanics of the chair. Now onto some more pros. *Comfortable! It is a good size, big enough for a big 245ln 6'0" guy like myself but somehow manages to stay slim in your space as well. *High Quality material - even when I was putting it together it was evident that every piece was solid and good quality. This contributes to the comfortability of the chair. *Easy to set up - if you have put any chair together in the past it does nothing unique to complicate it, but I found the tools to be well built and organized. *Footrest - much better than the last chair that I bought. The last one tended to swivel to the left when I tried to kick my feet up. This one feels much more stable so far. *Speaker system - I saved the best for last. I am pleasantly surprised at the quality of the blue tooth speakers. It wasn't difficult to set up, but you do have to download the app to initiate it. I like to listen to YouTube or podcasts while I am playing certain games, such as Microsoft Flight Simulator or City Skylines. I love how I have the sound of the game in front of me, while having the sound of my videos behind me. It balances the sound between the two sources very well so that they do not conflict with each other too much. I would usually have to turn my game down in order to hear my podcasts. I haven't figured out if I can pair with my PC though. I don't think that I can. I have only had it for a couple of days, so longevity is still a question. But it was well packaged with clear instructions and the packet is actually quite sleek.

reviews.title: The reviews were right!
reviews.body: There were plenty of reviews before mine that reported the same issues that this chair we got has. It came in with stains already on it, that formed splatter patterns once assembled. Some looked like black ink on the arm of the chair. Some looked like droplets of dried blood splattered on the left side along the seat and the back. God, I hope it’s not! I sanitized the chair, but none of the stains even lightened no matter what I tried. Even with careful, meticulous assembly, the left side and arm are drooping lower to the front of the chair. The chair looks even from the back. You might as well toss out the footrest. It was a nice idea, just not a sturdy one. The color of the chair is darker and drabber than depicted here. Other than those issues, my son is happy with the chair, and can use it for hours at a time doing homework and also gaming. Hindsight, I should have gotten a black chair so that any and all stains would not be so visible, but I probably would not have spent any more for a different chair because a gaming chair isn’t a real necessity, and it’s not going to be loved like a Lazy Boy anyway. Unless you are considering this for your husband or 40 yr old son, consider that a (hopefully NEW) chair like this will probably last as long as this phase that it is wanted for.

reviews.title: High quality gaming chair
reviews.body: This chair is a replacement for another gaming chair I had for a number of years that had the fake leather on it and tore off over time, so I decided to get one with a cloth cover instead. I'm happy with the quality of the chair and it looks like it will hold up well over time. It also looks really good. One thing to be aware of is that the chair seat is very firm. If you want a chair that is softer, this is probably not the best option for you. It is still comfortable and I'd still recommend it for anyone who doesn't mind a more firm seat. Another thing to be aware of is that the width of the back between the raised sides is rather narrow. If you have broad shoulders or are a bigger person, you may not be able to lean back comfortably in the chair. The chair can be put together pretty easily by one person and the only issue I had was the picture for attaching the seat back to the seat... the bar that attaches is shown in the picture backwards from what it is supposed to be. If you watch the video that they provide, it's clear how to attach it, but if you're following the instruction images, it may be confusing. The reclining lever is the type that you can push or pull and let go while adjusting the back rather than the spring ones where you have to hold it while adjusting the back. Either option is fine, but I find this style to be slightly more convenient.

reviews.title: Great chair, unbelievable price

Easy to assemble, looks pretty good, easy to operate, cushion, lumbar, and neck support are all really good and better than I was expecting. I love the foot rest and the ability to set the exact recline with ease. I’m 5’10” 170 lbs and this chair is very comfortable and foot rest is perfect. For larger people this chair may not be perfect, but it would likely get the job done. If you want something that looks fancy, this isn’t your chair. It looks nice and it’s sturdy, but not fancy. All parts are heavy black plastic. Are there better chairs out there. Yep. Do they cost 3x to 10x more? Yep. I’d say you get 90% of the chair for half the price of name brand “budget” gaming chair options. I’d be surprised if anyone who bought this chair didn’t rate it 8 out of 10 or higher.

reviews.title: Absolutely worth it! A great deal!
reviews.body: This chair has been a fantastic purchase! I thought I would have to get a super expensive chair to get the comfort and support I wanted but this one was very reasonably priced and I got it on sale too. It's extremely versatile and very comfortable even for all day gaming. The lumbar pillow is the perfect firmness. The seat width is such a breath of fresh air. I can change how I'm sitting regularly and comfortably with plenty of room. All of its movement is smooth, i.e hinges, support column, wheels. My favourite feature so far is locking the recline in the exact angle I want with a quick push of a lever. It was easy to put together (though it took a bit of hand strength for some spots, like the last screws on the sides, so it may not be very easy for anyone with dexterity concerns.) It's almost completely noise-free and what noises it does make are quiet. The fabric is holding up well so far (2 months at the time of review). As a seamstress, I had concerns since the faux suede types usually aren't, but it's doing well. And the temperature regulates great. No overheating or sweating. The only thing struggling occasionally are the zippers on the neck and lumbar pillows. Sometimes they slip open since the fabric is so tight over the inserts, but they can be closed again and the zippers aren't technically broken yet. The footrest is a nice addition but doesn't extend far enough out to fully stretch my legs out. An extender that collapses into the main bars for the footrest would be needed since the bars are exactly the depth of the seat when put away. It they were longer they would stick out the back underneath the seat. All-in-all, a fantastic purchase that my weary body is appreciating when I'm at my computer. I'll try to remember to update this on the durability in a few months!

There wasn't really a clear manual included with the chair, so figuring out exactly how everything was supposed to go together was a little confusing. I had to rely on YouTube videos to figure out some of the assembly, and finding a useful video was a bit of a hassle. Once I figured everything out though, the chair went together fine. Overall, I am very happy with the chair. It has been a major comfort upgrade from my previous chair and after a little over two weeks of use, it still feels just as good as when I first put it together.

reviews.title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
reviews.body: This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor) I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them. Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis. As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable. Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

(e.g., the floor) I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them. Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis. As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable. Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

reviews.title: Sehr guter Stuhl (Lest mein Fazit durch)
reviews.body: Super gemütlich, allerdings muss man sich erst eine Woche an den Stuhl gewöhnen, um ihn gemütlich zu finden. Dies liegt an den Kissen. Am Anfang denk man „wie ungemütlich sind die Kissen“, aber der Körper muss sich erst eine Zeit an die neue Sitzhaltung gewöhnen und dann sagt man nur „BABA!“. Der Gaming Stuhl bietet ziemlich viele kleine Extras z.B. Die verstellbaren Lehnen oder auch die vordere Fußbank ,die man ausfahren kann. ZUSAMMENBAU: Bei mir hat das ganze fast eine Stunde gebraucht, dabei muss man beachten das ich davor noch nie irgendeinen Stuhl aufgebaut habe und erstmal einbisschen von der Anleitung geschockt war,allerdings stellte sich heraus das die Anleitung schnell zu kapieren ist. Man kann sie mit einen Ikea Aufbauplan vergleichen. FAZIT: Mein Fazit ist das ich diesen Stuhl auf jedenfall empfehlen kann, denn er bietet viele Extras ist gemütlich (wenn man sich an die Form eines Gaming Stuhls gewöhnt hat). Trotzdem ist er Preis von diesen Stuhl natürlich ein Batzen Geld, aber ich würde sagen es lohnt sich, denn diesen Stuhl behält man auf jedenfall einpaar Jahre und die Firma ist weltbekannt für ihre guten Gaming Stühle.
reviews.body_en: Super comfortable, but you have to get used to the chair for a week to find it comfortable. This is because of the pillows. At the beginning you think “how uncomfortable are the cushions”, but your body first has to get used to the new sitting position and then you just say “BABA!”. The gaming chair offers a lot of little extras, e.g. the adjustable backrests or the front footrest, which can be extended. ASSEMBLY: The whole thing took me almost an hour, but you have to keep in mind that I had never assembled any chair before and was a bit shocked by the instructions at first, but it turned out that the instructions were easy to understand. You can compare it with an Ikea assembly plan. CONCLUSION: My conclusion is that I can definitely recommend this chair because it offers many extras and is comfortable (once you get used to the shape of a gaming chair). Nevertheless, the price of this chair is of course a lot of money, but I would say it's worth it, because you'll definitely keep this chair for a few years and the company is world-famous for its good gaming chairs.

reviews.title: Calidad-precio insuperables
reviews.body: Lo primero, un 10 a la entrega, me ha llegado 1 semana antes de lo inicialmente previsto. La calidad de los materiales es muy alta, destaca el tacto y la precisión de las piezas. El montaje es muy sencillo, siguiendo las instrucciones no cabe lugar a dudas (recomiendo un atornillador eléctrico para apretar los tornillos o es muy tedioso estar dándole vueltas a la llavecita). El funcionamiento, la comodidad, el que tenga de todo (bluetooth, altavoces, los reposabrazos ajustables (rotatoriamente también un poco) y el reposapiés la hace genial para sesiones intensas de ordenador, sea por trabajo, ocio o gaming. Incluso es cómoda para echar una siesta si se quiere. La única pega, y espero que el vendedor o fabricante me resuelva esta duda, es que el altavoz izquierdo no suena. Entiendo que estos altavoces son para una experiencia envolvente y por ende no tienen mucho volumen, ya que se escucha muy tenuemente. Pero el altavoz izquierdo no me suena. Mirando el receptor bluetooth, parece que cada altavoz debería tener un cable jack independiente, y conectar ambos cables al receptor. Yo sólo encontre uno, y antes de abrir la funda (que implica desmontarlo) quiero asegurarme de que sí que tiene que haber un cable, y que éste se encontrará dentro de la funda por haberse colado por el agujero de salida. Sin duda, al precio que está, la recomiendo encarecidamente.
reviews.body_en: First of all, a 10 for delivery, it arrived 1 week earlier than initially expected. The quality of the materials is very high, the touch and precision of the pieces stands out. Assembly is very simple, following the instructions without a doubt (I recommend an electric screwdriver to tighten the screws or it is very tedious to keep turning the wrench). The operation, the comfort, the fact that it has everything (Bluetooth, speakers, the adjustable armrests (also rotating a little) and the footrest makes it great for intense computer sessions, whether for work, leisure or gaming. It is even comfortable for taking a nap if you want. The only drawback, and I hope that the seller or manufacturer resolves this doubt, is that the left speaker does not sound. I understand that these speakers are for an immersive experience and therefore do not have much volume, since It sounds very faint. But the left speaker doesn't sound to me. Looking at the Bluetooth receiver, it seems that each speaker should have a separate jack cable, and I only found one, and before opening the case (which involves disassembling it) I want to make sure that there must be a cable, and that it will be inside the case because it has slipped through the exit hole.

reviews.title: Reasonable for the price point
reviews.body: We bought this chair for our 13-year-old son to use at his desk. On unboxing day, he was able to assemble it with minimal help, which was a nice bonus. The chair was true to the advertised color and overall build. My thoughts: In general, I find most gaming chairs to be on the rigid side, and this one is no exception. It doesn’t offer as much support for the back and neck as I’d prefer, even with the included pillow accessories. Compared to other chairs I’ve owned—like my previous Secretlab, which was much heavier and more substantial—this one feels lighter and a bit less sturdy. That said, the material is soft to the touch. I can’t fully speak to how breathable it is yet. Overall, it seems like a decent option for someone looking for a budget-friendly chair while saving up for a higher-end model. Longevity will really depend on how it holds up over time. My son’s thoughts: (I’ll update with more detail later.) He enjoys the added features, especially the leg rest, reclining function, and the included cooling mat. He finds it comfortable and has no issue sitting in it for extended periods. With summer coming up, we’ll see how well it stays cool in hotter conditions. I’ll update this review over time with how it holds up to regular use.

Chair sits pretty firm, and I was using a very old office chair before hand and was just looking to purchase something for my desk. For the price point the quality is good, but for the price point I had expected more for the comfort aspect, and there are more affordable comfortable chairs than what this chair can offer you.

reviews.title: Chair is for little people, but it’s still nice
reviews.body: I guess I misread the size this chair is intended for (description says 54”-62” - but I saw it as 5 foot 4 to 6 foot 2 because of the 300 lbs weight limit) - I mean, I guess that’s really my fault.. but seriously, WHO IS 300lbs and 4 foot 6? So needless to say the lumbar support is in the totally wrong place for me being 6 ft - but I’m sure it’s well placed if you’re a petite person for which it was intended. Anyway, I’m keeping it because it works for my daughter that is 5’ 6” (she says it’s “super comfy”) and the chair design looks really sharp and modern (we got the Gray on White frame). The reason I’m not giving it 5 stars is because there’s no way the seat cushion can handle 300lbs, I’m only 210 and my butt fell asleep after 2 hours of sitting in it.. also, the arms flex so much using them to get up out of the seat I’m afraid they will snap under my weight (again, I’m not even close to the 300lb weight limit it’s intended for). While the lumbar adjustment goes in and out towards or away from your back, it’s good to note that it does NOT adjust up or down. Props to the mfr for keeping the parts to a minimal and reusing the same screw sizes for most of the build, that was helpful so I didn’t have to worry if I was using the correct screw lengths or washers.. they also include a really nice T Allen wrench instead of the standard L style (which is a super nice touch) - so all this kept the assembly simple and I was done in less than 20 minutes. Putting my misunderstanding to the side, the reason this gets dinged a star is due to the seat having weak arms, thinner than expected seat padding, and the inability to adjust the lumbar support up/down.. other than that it’s actually a good solid and stylish chair for somebody in the 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 foot, sub 200lb demographic.

reviews.title: Decent chair but not for us taller people
reviews.body: I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with. For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive. After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected. The good: 1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal. 2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems. 3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me. 4. Appearance. Very nice. 5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy. The not so good. 1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well. 2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case. 3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable. 4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward. 5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me. Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier. My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well. 2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case. 3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable. 4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward. 5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me. Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier. My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

reviews.title: Good chair, comfortable for work day use, a little creaky.
reviews.body: I've had the chair for 7 months, and it is a good pick overall with no buyer's remorse. I am 6'2 and 180lbs and sit in the chair for ~7 hours a day. The support is okay, as they are just adjustable lumbar/neck pillows and nothing rigid. I have a 30" waist, and I would say a 34" or 36" is around the max to fit within the seat bolster. The arms do not adjust out, only up and down, which is not an issue for me. If you are larger, that is something to consider. The recline feature works hilariously well as you can recline nearly flat and not fall over. The leather is still in great shape with hardly any creasing and no damage or wear to the material. It's comfortable to sit in for the whole day. The chair was very simple to assemble in ~5 minutes and comes together like every standard office chair with 4 bolts for the base, and 6 for each arm. This chair has started to creak which can't be helped. I would give it a 3.5-4 rating due to this alone. The creak comes from the pressed steel pin the chair tilts on at the top of the post, so it can't be tightened or adjusted in any way. It is a little obnoxious, but my only real issue with the chair. To compare, I have a $1,500 Humanscale Freedom Task Chair with Headrest at home, and I feel no real difference in the chair's comfort or overall quality. The Humanscale does have better built-in ergonomic adjustments like the arms, seat pan depth, and lumbar position versus the Corsair, which only includes a couple pillows for lumbar and neck support. The Humanscale is really underwhelming for the price, very loud with the smallest movements, and not that comfortable. Do not feel compelled to spend more expecting better quality. Overall, I would probably purchase the Corsair TC500 Luxe for a little more next time for more adjustability, and the built in lumbar system.

reviews.title: Looks good in pictures and description. Return before 30 day window ends.
reviews.body: Looks good in pictures but shows it flaws quickly. I love the Corsair brand and took a chance on this chair because it looks great. Some issues I found include: lumbar cushion is too large and impractical/uncomfortable; unusable. Head cushion is fine, but taller people will have to slouch for it to fit your neck and cause lower back pain; remove it and there is no neck support at all. back cushion material is very thin and will quickly give way to the lumbar frame, which is not comfortable at all. The entire chair mechanism and controls are cheap quality. Even in the locked position the chair still rocks back and forth to a small degree. You are constantly flexing your muscles just to stay in one because of the sway. The bolt holes are flimsy and even when tightened beyond capacity, the entire chair still rocks and flexes. No stability at all. Arm rests are completely fixed in place and can only go up and down. Arm rest surface is hard and uncomfortable. Arm rests stay in place when leaning back causing your arms to completely come off the arm rest or having to stretch both arms just to stay on the armrest, another huge inconvenience and ergonomic issue. Seat cushion is just thin as the back support. Thin cheap poly stuffing across metal frames. Get ready for serious lower back issues. Unless you are a small child, this chair is not for you. Now I know why they only give you 30 days to return the item. The chair shows its issues after that window closes.

reviews.title: Glad I bought it…Well not for long
reviews.body: I was hesitant to buy this chair. Every review I read was an emotional rollercoaster. One minute it’s great, one minute it’s trash, I wasn’t sure what to believe. I decided to just commit to it and order since I’ve always wanted this chair, and it matches my Corsair peripherals. I ordered it Monday, it came Wednesday, which is pretty awesome. Everything was well packaged. Branded bags, a lot of protection surrounding the products, I was impressed. It does NOT come with physical instructions, but you can just find them online. Super straight forward install which took me a solid half an hour at most. Now, the final verdict. First sit down and I was really impressed. The bottom cushion is honestly nice, and the two back pillows work well and fit my body like a glove. I’ve already used this for a consecutive couple of hours and I’m happier than I was in my other chair. I was rocking a Respawn 110 Pro, which is very large and plush but is very cheap feeling in comparison. For those looking to get this chair, every single one of the complaints I’ve seen did NOT fit my experience. Whether it be the parts, the bolts, the cushion, whatever. But I do understand where some of these may come from. Let me advise that this chair is absolutely perfect for me. Im 5’11 and 145 so I’m not your average bodybuilder. It still has some room but just be mindful of that since it does seem like it’s meant for the “smaller” peeps. Besides that, everything feels great and is premium. It left me surprised, and I will continue to not trust reviews and just get the dang thing myself. Glad I made the decision. EDIT: LMAO I sold it less than a year later because it started hurting to sit for long periods of time. The chair formed to my seating position but it never felt soft/comfortable enough. Sadly my 5 star didn’t last that long. Recently got a GT Player suede chair for half the price and it’s 10 times better. It’s ight you live and you learn. Just get an ergonomic chair if you want comfort

Such a let down sitting on this thing for the first time. It’s very firm and in no way comfortable. There is a lever to that locks the chair from leaning back and the opposite direction lets it free. I own many Corsair products, and i find them all high quality, well made. 10 minutes I gave this chair before requesting a refund.

For long gaming sessions or Zoom marathons, this chair delivers. Worth every penny.

reviews.title: El ryzen 5 de las sillas.
reviews.body: Sólida pero no es hecha para maltratarse. Una de las cosas más shockeantes a la hora de recibir este producto es su packaging. Uno cree que compró algo barato cuando la realidad es que todo está optimizado para que recibas el mejor producto posible por el precio que pagaste. Esta silla no es para nada frágil. La mayor parte de la construcción es de metal y de plástico de buen material, además de contar con un diseño ingenioso para ajustar los tornillos para tener el mejor ensamblaje con relación de dificultad. Los tornillos están posicionados de tal manera que aunque simple, permite garantizar una presión y sostenibilidad superior a lo que te esperas por este rango de precio. Eso si, esto no esta hecho para armarse a la rapidez y con mucha fuerza. Requiere paciencia y "maña" a la hora de insertar los tornillos de las patas, la espalda de la silla y sobre todo los brazos. Le doy un 7/10 de dificultad de armando que aunque es sencillo requiere que prestes atención. ¿Recomendaría este producto a los más "exigentes"? La respuesta es compleja, pero en mi experiencia. Un si, si deseas tratar tu silla con debido cuidado de no agitarte demasiado o no tener malas posturas que el mismo instructivo te dice que debes evitar para un uso óptimo de la silla. Un no, si lo que buscas es una silla ergonómica que aguante el uso más rudo de lo rudo. En resumen, gran silla, packaging que da algo de miedo pero es una experiencia satisfactoria al final. Altamente recomendable si estás en un apuro económico o si es tu primera silla de escritorio.
reviews.body_en: Solid but not made to be abused. One of the most shocking things when receiving this product is its packaging. You think you bought something cheap when the reality is that everything is optimized so that you receive the best possible product for the price you paid. This chair is not fragile at all. Most of the construction is made of metal and plastic of good material, in addition to having an ingenious design to adjust the screws to have the best assembly with difficulty ratio. The screws are positioned in such a way that, although simple, it guarantees pressure and sustainability higher than what you would expect for this price range. Of course, this is not made to be assembled quickly and with great force. It requires patience and "craft" when inserting the screws on the legs, the back of the chair and especially the arms. I give it a 7/10 for difficulty assembling which, although it is simple, requires you to pay attention. Would you recommend this product to the most "demanding" ones? The answer is complex, but in my experience. Yes, if you want to treat your chair with due care so as not to shake yourself too much or have bad postures that the same instructions tell you to avoid for optimal use of the chair. A no, if what you are looking for is an ergonomic chair that can withstand the roughest of rough use. In short, great chair, packaging that is a bit scary but it is a satisfying experience in the end. Highly recommended if you are in a financial pinch or if it is your first desk chair.

reviews.title: High-End Quality Without the High-End Price Tag
reviews.body: This is an impressively high-quality chair at a very competitive price point. While there are a few minor details that could be improved, the overall craftsmanship and thoughtful design make it a standout choice for a home office. One of the most impressive aspects was the packaging. The box was meticulously taped on all sides, preventing any dust or particles from entering; a level of care I wish was standard for all furniture companies. Inside, rather than using messy styrofoam that breaks apart and litters the floor, the company used neat bubble-style wraps for each part. This attention to detail ensured that even though the chair is heavy, every piece arrived clean and in perfect condition. The build quality is excellent, starting with the solid metal base that gives the chair a reassuring heaviness and stability. Assembly was relatively straightforward for someone used to DIY projects, though a second person might be helpful if you aren't familiar with fixing things. The headrest is particularly noteworthy; unlike more expensive chairs I’ve owned where the headrest constantly slips, this one is very sturdy. The lumbar support is also highly effective, allowing you to adjust both the height and the support strength. The 3D armrests are another highlight, moving back and forth, twisting, and flipping up 90 degrees so you can either use them for support or move them out of the way to push the chair fully under the desk. The seat cushion is equally impressive, with 3.14-inch thick foam that feels deep and resilient, giving me confidence that it won't flatten out or lose its shape with regular use. There are a few areas where the product could be refined. The armrests are made from a PU-padded material, which I find to be a negative as it is prone to friction damage over time; I would have preferred a simple high-quality plastic or a full mesh/cloth finish. Additionally, the assembly gloves included were far too small for an average adult. I also have a suggestion for the company regarding the extra hardware provided: since these chairs often come with spare screws or tools, it would be a fantastic and unique innovation to build a small, dedicated compartment into the frame of the chair to store these extra materials. I haven't seen this feature on other chairs, but it would be a very pragmatic way to ensure the spare parts aren't lost over the years. Despite these small points, this remains a five-star quality chair in my opinion.

reviews.title: A review after a year of owning this chair
reviews.body: It’s been over a year since I bought this and have decided to write my review. My experience with this chair during this time- since I bought it and up till now is overall good experience. It’s not the greatest chair out there available on the market, but especially for the price and usability, I would say it was worth it. A few Pros worth mentioning: • adjustability • comfortable cushion • lightweight and easy to move around A few cons worth mentioning: • No reclining- just a “rocking back and fourth” which you have to twist below the seat to adjust the sensitivity- which I find very tedious, tiring, and long. • Headrest is honestly not the best and kind of protrudes your head forward a bit- although adjustable, still not as comfortable as I would like. • Cushion will eventually wear out- BUT not too much and still lowkey comfortable, but I started to felt the need to change my sitting position more overtime. As stated before the chair is decent- especially for the price. For me personally, I love that the seat encourages you to sit up straight and nicely, but naturally, it does get “tiring” after a bit of time. Even then, not sitting the way it intended to- is ironically the most comfortable way to sit on it. The seat does not get too hot which is also nice. If the chair had actual reclining, this chair would be perfect. Also, the chair has some decent height adjustability aswell. The building process was easy and didn’t take that long to do. Overall, if you needed something that was comfortable enough, cheap, and reclining is not a need, I would recommend this chair.

reviews.title: 45 minutes assembly -- piece of cake. Nice chair.
reviews.body: Before I finally landed on this chair I read about a million articles with buying advice for ergonomic desk chairs, looked for second hand expensive chairs, read so many Amazon reviews. Obviously you can spend a whole lot of money on an ergonomic desk chair (even used ones), but I really didn't want to. I just bought this today, so the jury is out on long term wear, ,but I can say that the components feel solid, assembly was easy, it is *very* comfortable so far, and -- even more to the point -- VERY adjustable in so many different ways that physical therapists etc recommended in the articles I read. I am 5 foot 5; in order to put the chair at the right ergonomic height for my particular desk and keyboard, I need a footrest so my feet aren't dangling. But that would be the case with any chair in my setup. The headrest is great, the arms are soft and comfortable, the back support piece is perfect, and everything can be adjusted as you sit in it. Rollers are quiet and stable on laminate floor. The box was a good size and heavy enough (~32 lbs) to be awkward for an unfit middle aged lady to wrangle down apartment steps; however, the Amazon driver brought it straight to my door. The chair was carefully packed. Whoever wrote the assembly instructions (which are in English and Spanish) for this chair is some kind of technical writing genius -- I have never seen clearer or more easy-to-follow instructions. From slicing open the tape on the box to finished chair was 45 minutes for me. All you need for assembly is included -- also fabric gloves (for protecting your manicure? I guess?) and extra bolts and washers. Super buy. If I'd known I could get such an affordable and massive upgrade from my previous garbage chair I would have done it long ago. Great value for the money. I rarely write reviews but all the reviews I read helped me make a great decision, so here ya go.

reviews.title: Received a returned item
reviews.body: I was so excited to finally get a new chair for my desk at home. When it arrived, the delivery driver even walked it down the hall to my apartment for me. Once I brought it inside, I saw that the box was kind of badly taped up, but I didn't think much of it at first. Once I opened it, the items inside were haphazardly wrapped in plastic and bubble wrap, but again, it's a cheap chair from Amazon, so not too worried yet. Then I pulled out the little plastic envelope with the toolkit and gloves and that's when I realized that this was not a new chair. The gloves were dirty and had clearly been used before and the toolkit was open in several places. Ugh! All of the pieces were included and I didn't see any obvious damage on any of the parts. Plus, the thought of trying to send it back was too much, so I decided to move forward. The first step was attaching the legs which went fine. Then I needed to insert the wheels. Four of the wheels snapped in very easily. The 5th wheel, however, would not budge. I tried it several times and on different legs and it wouldn't move. I noticed the other wheels have a little groove on them and the stubborn one does not. It looks like someone might have tried to create a groove, but gave up. Needless to say, I was disappointed and frustrated. I reached out to Amazon through their chat feature. (I should note hear that the person I dealt with was extremely kind and efficient). After explaining the issue (and pointing out that the chair was an obvious prior return), I was offered the chance to return the item. I didn't really want to do that; I just wanted the wheel I needed. I was then offered a refund of $19.45 and provided a link to purchase new wheels which would cost $11.99 (before taxes and shipping). I explained that wasn't sufficient since after repurchasing the wheels, my actual refund would be about $7.00! reviews.title: Great Instructions, Straightforward Assembly
reviews.body: I just received this chair today, so my product review is mostly on the packaging, instructions, and assembly. The product was well-packaged, and it was obvious when I unboxed it that a lot of care and thought went into packing it in the most efficient way that would also protect the parts. I was positively impressed with the packaging. I was also incredibly impressed with the instructions and assembly process. I am used to cheaper products where the parts only half fit or important components are missing, or where the instructions were confusing and unclear. This chair's instruction manual was very clear and concise. The diagrams were easy to understand and neat. The screws came labeled and separated and also included the scew types and sizes/lengths, which is handy in case you need to pick up extras at a store somewhere. But they also included one extra of each type of screw, washer, and cover, which I appreciated during assembly. (I didn't find myself worrying what would happen if I dropped a screw, which is something I would normally be distsracted by while working.) The only things I would take points off for were these: 1. The instructions said the chair came with gloves for assembly, but no gloves were included. That was fine with me, but why mention them if you won't include them? The instructions even later say not to use the chair if not all components were present...but all the important ones were, so I assembled it without gloves (as I probably would have done anyway, since it was for me and not another person). 2. It matters which side of the seat is the front, but the sticker was confusing. The instructions show a sticker placed on the side that is the front, and that is where my sticker was placed. However, the sticker says "FRONT" and has an arrow pointing somewhere. In the instructions this arrow pointed to the front. On my seat, however, the arrow pointed to the back. So am I supposed to believe the sticker placement (it was diagonal, so it looked haphazardly slapped on) or the arrow? On that particular step the piece you are screwing into the seat can fit both ways, but thankfully there is a later step where it becomes obvious which side is the front vs. the back. (The arm rests can only be attached to the back.) So I wish that had been clearer up front, but otherwise it was okay. Recommendations for assembly: - To attach the wheels, apply firm, direct, straight-down pressure. I tried screwing them on at first but you just push. Make sure they go in the whole way like the picture shows. - When they say to tighten the screws to only 60%, it's a helpful tip, because you can't fit the armrests on both the seat and chairback at the same time with the screws completely tightened. Just tighten them enough to fit the pieces on, then later you can tighten up the screws. So far I find the chair to be very comfortable and I'm exceedingly happy with it. The lumbar support seems like it could potentially be a little chafy or scratchy, but I'll give the chair a chance before deciding if it's problematic or not. Like I said, I only got the chair today, so I can't speak much to its long-term comfort, durability, or longevity. But I was so impressed with how easy and straightforward they made the assembly that I had to write a review to show my appreciation.

reviews.title: Comfortable and Stylish Chair with Just a Minor Assembly Issue

The assembly process wasn’t too difficult, though I did encounter a bit of trouble when it came to attaching the headrest. It may have been something I was doing wrong, but that part of the assembly felt trickier than it needed to be. I think it could be designed in a way that makes attaching the headrest a bit easier. Aside from that, the rest of the assembly went smoothly and didn’t take too much time. In terms of comfort, the chair definitely meets my expectations. The seat is comfortable, and the support it provides is just right for long hours at the desk. This is my first time using a mesh chair, and I have to say, I’m impressed with how well it breathes. The mesh design keeps me cool and comfortable throughout the day, even during extended use. It’s a significant upgrade from the traditional padded chairs I’ve used in the past. The lumbar support is also a nice touch, and it helps me maintain good posture, which is important for me since I spend a lot of time working at my desk. The chair also looks great! The modern, sleek design fits well with my home office setup, and I love how it adds a touch of sophistication to the space. It’s not just functional but also stylish, which is a bonus. The neutral color and clean lines make it versatile, so it can fit into a variety of different spaces, whether at home or in a professional office setting. While I’m optimistic about the durability of the chair, especially with the mesh construction, only time will tell how long it lasts. I’m hopeful that it will hold up well over time, but as this is my first mesh chair, I’ll be keeping an eye on how it performs with daily use. So far, everything feels sturdy and well-built, and I don’t foresee any issues, but it’s always something to consider with a new type of chair. All in all, I’m really pleased with this chair. It’s comfortable, stylish, and relatively easy to assemble, with just a minor hiccup when it came to the headrest. If you’re in the market for a mesh office chair that offers good comfort and looks sharp, I would definitely recommend this one. It’s been a great addition to my workspace, and I’m looking forward to using it for years to come.

reviews.title: Not a great seat, but the back support is good and the build quality seems quite good honestly.
reviews.body: Disclaimer - this is an initial review - only had this chair a few days Size: 6'4" ~280lbs The good: the materials and build quality overall is pretty good, not sure what more you could want for a <$500 chair. The only thing that worries me is how long the mesh will last. I'd be happy with 3 years to be honest for the price ($180 at time of purchase). The lumbar/cervical neck support is very good. This is pretty much why I bought it. It will help me force myself into a good posture since my neck is such a mess, both lumbar and cervical. The head rest is actually quite good. It could be slightly stiffer to stay in place maybe, but it's pretty nice. The smell - call me weird but the smell of new plastic in a room for a day or two is a pro not a con for me. It honestly looks pretty nice, not a huge plus for me but it does look sleek. The bad: The reviews saying the seat is uncomfortable are right....at least so far as it is a very narrow seat. If it was ~3-4 inches wider, it would be a 10/10 chair for me at least on initial use. The edges are a bit harsh on your hips if you are north of a 38" pants size. If you're sitting pretty straight, not really a problem. The mesh feels fine, it's not as good as a cushion but the tradeoff of breathability is worth it I would say. What I did right off the bat to help with comfort a bit was get some pipe insulation foam I had laying around in the garage, cut it in half, and lined the front half of the seat underneath with it. Just kinda stuffed it in there up against the edges as much as I could. Does it help? Actually....kinda, ya. I'd say it makes it a good 15-20% more comfortable at the edges. Picture attached (you can kinda see through and see what I did). Edit: I used the other half of the foam for the back half. So I completely lined the edge underneath with pipe insulation. It does actually help. I also figure this will keep the edges of the mesh from fatiguing as quick since it shouldn't pull down on it as harshly over time. The casters it comes with are pretty bad. If you buy a chair for <$500 though, you should be buying a ~$15-20 set of roller blade casters to swap in. I ran the stock casters for a day as the roller blade ones I got here on Amazon for $16 didn't come until the next day. The stock ones work, but they're quite slow. In my opinion, any reviews saying that the caster input area welds failing were partly due to the stock casters being slow in the first place. This makes you need to push more, and puts more pressure on these spots - making it more prone to failure. The welds to me don't look bad to be honest, and it doesn't worry me - if they failed I'd just reweld them myself. The arm rests are way too adjustable. They are honestly not bad, but they don't need any more adjustment than literally just going up and down. THIS WAS THE #1 REASON FOR NARROWING MY SEARCH DOWN TO THIS CHAIR - for playing guitar flip-up armrests are a must for me, which narrows down the search dramatically, as anyone reading this knows. But the arm rests aren't bad. Conclusion: As a big guy, this is a good chair that will help with posture. The seat is too narrow if you are size 38 or greater pants - it's undeniable. Hopefully the mesh holds up - if that is the case I'll be plenty happy for the price. If this chair gets a better version in the future with literally just a wider seat, I will absolutely buy it when this thing is worn out in (hopefully) like 3 years. NOTE: THE TOP LUMBAR SETTING ISN’T A SETTING IT IS THE RESET. So many people in reviews, including myself thought the lumbar didn’t stay set - it does, just the top most spot is NOT a setting it is meant to unlock it and reset to the bottom.

reviews.title: It’s not comfortable. Id like to return it.
reviews.body: To be honest. I had high hopes for this chair. Now. I hate it, I don’t know who is sitting on this for extended time. I can’t. Its supposed to be for bigger people. Im not huge. Its not wide enough with the arms down. I changed the wheels because it didn’t roll correctly. I added a pad because its too firm. The mesh is supposed to be more comfortable. The support is more stiff than relaxed. The design of the head rest is awkward. You’re supposed to be able to adjust it. It got locked into place. Now the height of it is too low. I misplaced the directions. I know there is a way to re-adjust it. Its just not clearly noticeable; such as a knob or button. As far as quality, its well made, as far as sturdiness goes. The thing is that when i go to sit down, there is that lip in front. I have to have an arm down on the chair, hold onto it, then sit down, otherwise the chair rolls away and I would fall on my butt. So, in that way- its not really safe. Even though I have this cushion on it, its still hard and my back hurts all the time Im sitting there. Not immediately, but soon afterwards. If I could return it, I would. That’s the thing about furniture, tho, isn’t it? Once its together, you can’t really take it apart and rebox it and send it back. It takes a week or so to figure it. Then the box is gone. Maybe if it were a little higher. I don’t know. Im fairly sure its all the way up. So yeah. Make sure your surface is really flat. Even changing the wheels doesn’t help. It moves well enough when you’re not in it. But trying to get in it and moving around in it is a different story. Also. I always feel like I’m leaning forward unless I intentionally sit back against against the back of the chair. Then it feels awkward where the headrest is and the back support. I don’t know. Im not a happy camper. Its the second mesh chair. Neither are actually comfortable. There really isn’t enough padding if you’re a bigger guy. This is supposed to support up to 400lb. Well its not breaking, but it’s also not comfortable.

reviews.title: Supportive, Customizable, and Surprisingly Comfortable for Long Hours
reviews.body: After spending 8+ hours a day at my desk, I finally upgraded to the CAPOT ergonomic mesh chair—and the difference is night and day. It’s not just a chair, it’s an adjustable support system designed for serious desk work. ✅ Pros Comfort: The seat cushion is firm yet breathable, and the mesh back keeps me cool even during long sessions. Lumbar support is adjustable and actually targets the lower back instead of just being decorative. Durability: Frame and components feel solid—no wobble or flex after assembly. Rated for 400 lbs, and it absolutely feels like it could handle that without strain. Weight: Despite its heavy-duty rating, it’s surprisingly lightweight when rolling or repositioning thanks to the smooth PU wheels. Custom Fit: Between the 3D headrest, 4D flip-up armrests, and 3-level tilt lock, I was able to dial in the perfect seated position. Great for switching between typing, video calls, and relaxed browsing. Color: The matte black finish with subtle texture gives it a professional and understated look—perfect for a clean setup. Ear/Head Support: The headrest cradles comfortably behind the neck and base of the head, reducing fatigue without forcing posture. Low noise level. ❌ Cons Armrest Adjustments Take Getting Used To: Lots of movement axes, which is great—just not intuitive at first. Assembly Takes Time: While everything is labeled and packed well, it took me a solid 40 minutes with careful attention. 📝 Final Thoughts The CAPOT chair nails what most office chairs miss: true adjustability without feeling gimmicky. If you’re someone who switches between focused work and laid-back browsing, this chair adapts right along with you. It’s now a core part of my productivity setup, and I’d confidently try other CAPOT ergonomic products moving forward.

reviews.title: Replacement Chair Base Recommended
reviews.body: I would love to give this product 5 stars, as the chair itself is WONDERFUL. Very comfortable, great for back support, and the ability to make micro-adjustments for lumbar support are game changing. After just over 1 year of daily usage for work, the material is still in great shape, very breathable, and comfortable. Unfortunately, the portion of the chair legs where the wheels attach have broken twice within the past 5 months. I reached out to the seller initially, and they graciously provided a replacement leg the first time free of charge, but now the leg has broken a second time in the 2 months since the initial replacement (I did not reach out for a second leg replacement). For context, the chair is rated up to 400 lbs and I am ~250 lbs, so my weight being that far below the limit could be a contributing factor? Either way, I do not think that metal chair legs should not be breaking at the welding point when the user is well under the max weight limit. I have opted to purchase a replacement chair base from another seller as well as a floor mat in hopes that this will remedy the issue. The chair itself is 11/10. The base is 3/10 with regular usage, at least in my experience.

reviews.title: Great chair, unbelievable price
reviews.body: I’m not sure what more you can ask for out of a chair at this price. Easy to assemble, looks pretty good, easy to operate, cushion, lumbar, and neck support are all really good and better than I was expecting. I love the foot rest and the ability to set the exact recline with ease. I’m 5’10” 170 lbs and this chair is very comfortable and foot rest is perfect. For larger people this chair may not be perfect, but it would likely get the job done. If you want something that looks fancy, this isn’t your chair. It looks nice and it’s sturdy, but not fancy. All parts are heavy black plastic. Are there better chairs out there. Yep. Do they cost 3x to 10x more? Yep. I’d say you get 90% of the chair for half the price of name brand “budget” gaming chair options. I’d be surprised if anyone who bought this chair didn’t rate it 8 out of 10 or higher.

reviews.title: Absolutely worth it! A great deal!
reviews.body: This chair has been a fantastic purchase! I thought I would have to get a super expensive chair to get the comfort and support I wanted but this one was very reasonably priced and I got it on sale too. It's extremely versatile and very comfortable even for all day gaming. The lumbar pillow is the perfect firmness. The seat width is such a breath of fresh air. I can change how I'm sitting regularly and comfortably with plenty of room. All of its movement is smooth, i.e hinges, support column, wheels. My favourite feature so far is locking the recline in the exact angle I want with a quick push of a lever. It was easy to put together (though it took a bit of hand strength for some spots, like the last screws on the sides, so it may not be very easy for anyone with dexterity concerns.) It's almost completely noise-free and what noises it does make are quiet. The fabric is holding up well so far (2 months at the time of review). As a seamstress, I had concerns since the faux suede types usually aren't, but it's doing well. And the temperature regulates great. No overheating or sweating. The only thing struggling occasionally are the zippers on the neck and lumbar pillows. Sometimes they slip open since the fabric is so tight over the inserts, but they can be closed again and the zippers aren't technically broken yet. The footrest is a nice addition but doesn't extend far enough out to fully stretch my legs out. An extender that collapses into the main bars for the footrest would be needed since the bars are exactly the depth of the seat when put away. It they were longer they would stick out the back underneath the seat. All-in-all, a fantastic purchase that my weary body is appreciating when I'm at my computer. I'll try to remember to update this on the durability in a few months!

reviews.title: Very Comfy and Holding Up Great
reviews.body: I ordered this chair on August 6th, and after a little over two weeks of regular use, I absolutely love it. It is much more comfortable than my previous chair, which I had been using for years, and I can sit in it for long periods without feeling uncomfortable. I also haven't noticed any degradation in the cushioning, materials, or overall comfort so far, which is a great sign. The only downside I had was the assembly. There wasn't really a clear manual included with the chair, so figuring out exactly how everything was supposed to go together was a little confusing. I had to rely on YouTube videos to figure out some of the assembly, and finding a useful video was a bit of a hassle. Once I figured everything out though, the chair went together fine. Overall, I am very happy with the chair. It has been a major comfort upgrade from my previous chair and after a little over two weeks of use, it still feels just as good as when I first put it together.

reviews.title: Bad, bad, and also not good.
reviews.body: This chair looks great. I bought it because it had pocket spring construction and the seat wasn't your typical "chunk of foam on a piece of plywood"...and it was red. I hate it. It creaks and wobbles every time you move in it. It took me a solid hour to get one of the arm rest bolts threaded, then the next day, the arm fell off. It's back on, but I have no faith that it will not say goodbye again. The fabric is so slippery that after you sit in it for 15 or 20 minutes, you start to slide forward, out of the chair. Microfiber. Yuck. Warning: Do *not* try to lean back when the chair is in the upright position or you'll end up sitting on the floor (after the seat scrapes your back on the way down.) The headrest is in the right position and is quite comfortable. The lumbar cushion is uncomfortable and, if you do give it a try, it helps in pushing you out of the chair. Sitting on it doesn't help. If you decide to recline, make sure you have a friend there to take a video...so you can post it in the 'funny videos' area of YouTube. It reclines, but the spring isn't adjustable and has so little tension on it that you may end up somewhere you don't want to be. (e.g., the floor) I don't know who this chair was made for but it certainly wasn't me. Maybe it was you. I'm not a gamer. I just wanted a decent (and fairly comfortable) chair for my desk. Maybe if I was a 16 year old gamer I'd be ecstatic. But I'm not. While I'm at it, how does that tubby guy in the picture get his hugeness on that seat and cross his legs? I'm probably half his size and fairly flexible and I can't do that. I tried. Didn't work. I can easily get one leg up on the foot rest though - two if you cross them. Finally, on top of all of this, the pneumatic cylinder seems to lose air on a random basis. As much as I thought I would like this chair I do not. In fact, as much as I hate to say it, this is probably one of the worst chairs that has ever been introduced to my rear end...and back...and arms. I have been in old, wooden office chairs devoid of all padding and/or adjustment that were more comfortable. Even though it says "FREE RETURNS", I would return this chair in a heartbeat - except that I'd have to disassemble it and get it back in the box in a satisfactory manner. You should buy this chair, but only if you want a nice-looking, fabric covered chair that you will never enjoy sitting in. For me, it's just money wasted.

reviews.title: Sehr guter Stuhl (Lest mein Fazit durch)
reviews.body: Super gemütlich, allerdings muss man sich erst eine Woche an den Stuhl gewöhnen, um ihn gemütlich zu finden. Dies liegt an den Kissen. Am Anfang denk man „wie ungemütlich sind die Kissen“, aber der Körper muss sich erst eine Zeit an die neue Sitzhaltung gewöhnen und dann sagt man nur „BABA!“. Der Gaming Stuhl bietet ziemlich viele kleine Extras z.B. Die verstellbaren Lehnen oder auch die vordere Fußbank ,die man ausfahren kann. ZUSAMMENBAU: Bei mir hat das ganze fast eine Stunde gebraucht, dabei muss man beachten das ich davor noch nie irgendeinen Stuhl aufgebaut habe und erstmal einbisschen von der Anleitung geschockt war,allerdings stellte sich heraus das die Anleitung schnell zu kapieren ist. Man kann sie mit einen Ikea Aufbauplan vergleichen. FAZIT: Mein Fazit ist das ich diesen Stuhl auf jedenfall empfehlen kann, denn er bietet viele Extras ist gemütlich (wenn man sich an die Form eines Gaming Stuhls gewöhnt hat). Trotzdem ist er Preis von diesen Stuhl natürlich ein Batzen Geld, aber ich würde sagen es lohnt sich, denn diesen Stuhl behält man auf jedenfall einpaar Jahre und die Firma ist weltbekannt für ihre guten Gaming Stühle.
reviews.body_en: Super comfortable, but you have to get used to the chair for a week to find it comfortable. This is because of the pillows. At the beginning you think “how uncomfortable are the cushions”, but your body first has to get used to the new sitting position and then you just say “BABA!”. The gaming chair offers a lot of little extras, e.g. the adjustable backrests or the front footrest, which can be extended. ASSEMBLY: The whole thing took me almost an hour, but you have to keep in mind that I had never assembled any chair before and was a bit shocked by the instructions at first, but it turned out that the instructions were easy to understand. You can compare it with an Ikea assembly plan. CONCLUSION: My conclusion is that I can definitely recommend this chair because it offers many extras and is comfortable (once you get used to the shape of a gaming chair). Nevertheless, the price of this chair is of course a lot of money, but I would say it's worth it, because you'll definitely keep this chair for a few years and the company is world-famous for its good gaming chairs.

reviews.title: Calidad-precio insuperables
reviews.body: Lo primero, un 10 a la entrega, me ha llegado 1 semana antes de lo inicialmente previsto. La calidad de los materiales es muy alta, destaca el tacto y la precisión de las piezas. El montaje es muy sencillo, siguiendo las instrucciones no cabe lugar a dudas (recomiendo un atornillador eléctrico para apretar los tornillos o es muy tedioso estar dándole vueltas a la llavecita). El funcionamiento, la comodidad, el que tenga de todo (bluetooth, altavoces, los reposabrazos ajustables (rotatoriamente también un poco) y el reposapiés la hace genial para sesiones intensas de ordenador, sea por trabajo, ocio o gaming. Incluso es cómoda para echar una siesta si se quiere. La única pega, y espero que el vendedor o fabricante me resuelva esta duda, es que el altavoz izquierdo no suena. Entiendo que estos altavoces son para una experiencia envolvente y por ende no tienen mucho volumen, ya que se escucha muy tenuemente. Pero el altavoz izquierdo no me suena. Mirando el receptor bluetooth, parece que cada altavoz debería tener un cable jack independiente, y conectar ambos cables al receptor. Yo sólo encontre uno, y antes de abrir la funda (que implica desmontarlo) quiero asegurarme de que sí que tiene que haber un cable, y que éste se encontrará dentro de la funda por haberse colado por el agujero de salida. Sin duda, al precio que está, la recomiendo encarecidamente.
reviews.body_en: First of all, a 10 for delivery, it arrived 1 week earlier than initially expected. The quality of the materials is very high, the touch and precision of the pieces stands out. Assembly is very simple, following the instructions without a doubt (I recommend an electric screwdriver to tighten the screws or it is very tedious to keep turning the wrench). The operation, the comfort, the fact that it has everything (Bluetooth, speakers, the adjustable armrests (also rotating a little) and the footrest makes it great for intense computer sessions, whether for work, leisure or gaming. It is even comfortable for taking a nap if you want. The only drawback, and I hope that the seller or manufacturer resolves this doubt, is that the left speaker does not sound. I understand that these speakers are for an immersive experience and therefore do not have much volume, since It sounds very faint. But the left speaker doesn't sound to me. Looking at the Bluetooth receiver, it seems that each speaker should have a separate jack cable, and I only found one, and before opening the case (which involves disassembling it) I want to make sure that there must be a cable, and that it will be inside the case because it has slipped through the exit hole.

reviews.title: Chair is for little people, but it’s still nice
reviews.body: I guess I misread the size this chair is intended for (description says 54”-62” - but I saw it as 5 foot 4 to 6 foot 2 because of the 300 lbs weight limit) - I mean, I guess that’s really my fault.. but seriously, WHO IS 300lbs and 4 foot 6? So needless to say the lumbar support is in the totally wrong place for me being 6 ft - but I’m sure it’s well placed if you’re a petite person for which it was intended. Anyway, I’m keeping it because it works for my daughter that is 5’ 6” (she says it’s “super comfy”) and the chair design looks really sharp and modern (we got the Gray on White frame). The reason I’m not giving it 5 stars is because there’s no way the seat cushion can handle 300lbs, I’m only 210 and my butt fell asleep after 2 hours of sitting in it.. also, the arms flex so much using them to get up out of the seat I’m afraid they will snap under my weight (again, I’m not even close to the 300lb weight limit it’s intended for). While the lumbar adjustment goes in and out towards or away from your back, it’s good to note that it does NOT adjust up or down. Props to the mfr for keeping the parts to a minimal and reusing the same screw sizes for most of the build, that was helpful so I didn’t have to worry if I was using the correct screw lengths or washers.. they also include a really nice T Allen wrench instead of the standard L style (which is a super nice touch) - so all this kept the assembly simple and I was done in less than 20 minutes. Putting my misunderstanding to the side, the reason this gets dinged a star is due to the seat having weak arms, thinner than expected seat padding, and the inability to adjust the lumbar support up/down.. other than that it’s actually a good solid and stylish chair for somebody in the 4 1/2 to 5 1/2 foot, sub 200lb demographic.
