reviews.title: Decent chair but not for us taller people
reviews.body: I really wanted to like this chair but, while there are things I do like about it, there are too many things I find fault with. For context, I am 73 years old, am 6’3” and weigh in around 265lbs. My last chair was designed for big and tall people and it fit me to a tee. I worked from home for two years during the apocalypse and that chair was super comfortable and I could spend over 8 hours a day in it with no problems. Unfortunately the faux leather wore off so I needed a replacement. I retired a couple of years ago and now only spend a few hours a week in front of the computer so I really don’t need anything too fancy or expensive. After researching a bunch of chairs, I settled on the Tralt Mesh Back Ergonomic Computer / Gamer Chair. I’ve never had a mesh chair before so I expected it to feel a lot different from my old all faux leather chair and it does feel a lot different but it’s what I expected. The good: 1. Price. For $130.00, I think this is a pretty good deal. 2. Assembly. Fairly quick. It took me about 30 minutes to unbox and assemble but I took my time so you could probably do it in 15-20 minutes easy. All parts lined up correctly and all bolts screwed in without any problems. 3. Weight. This chair is at least 50% lighter than my old chair so carrying it fully assembled upstairs was easy for me. 4. Appearance. Very nice. 5. Adjustments. Raising and lowering the chair is smooth and easy. Control lever and hydraulic piston work well. Tilting mechanism is also smooth and easy. The not so good. 1. IMO, this chair is NOT for anyone over 6’ if you are going to spend any time in it. The Amazon description says this will fit people who are 5’2” - 6’4”. Nope. The measurements shown in the description PHOTOS says 5’3” - 6’2”. Also nope. The front of the seat cushion hits my legs about half way up the thigh. It should hit closer to the knees. This makes me feel like I’m sitting on the edge of the chair. If the seat cushion was 24” in depth instead of 19-1/2” this would solve that problem. Also, if the lumbar support was positioned correctly, it might fit and feel better as well. 2. Lumbar support. As other reviewers have stated, the lumbar is too low and hits your tailbone, not the lumbar area of your back. This setup might be acceptable for someone shorter but for anyone 6’ or taller this is a problem. The lumbar is adjustable but it’s kind of a moot point in my case. 3. Arm rests. They are adjustable and slide forward but for taller people, even if fully adjusted forward, the arm rests still sit too far back and are not comfortable. 4. Stability. When I sit in the chair it doesn’t feel super solid. I don’t know how to explain it but I feel like I am going to tilt off to the side. It’s just a weird feeling. The chair doesn’t actually tip side to side but it’s just this odd feeling I get when I sit and even when rolling forward. 5. Weight capacity. The description says the chair has a weight capacity of 330lbs. This is probably true but, after using the chair for a while, I wonder about the longevity of the chair for someone heavier like me. Look, as I said earlier, for the price this is a good deal. I only use the chair once or twice a week so decided to keep it as returning it was more of a problem than I wanted to deal with. If the seat cushion was 3-4” longer, it would fit my legs much better and I would be a lot happier. My advise: if you are big and tall like me, pass on this chair. Spend a little more money and get something that fits you.

reviews.title: Great option for a great price
reviews.body: I REALLY like this chair. Originally it arrived without wheels but quick contact with the sellers customer service and they sent me wheels right away. Customer service was friendly and easy to work with. Sometimes you never know and I was pleasantly surprised. I love that the arms of the chair can flip up so I can choose to use them if I feel like it. I typically don’t use chair arms and have to remove them, but having the option is even better. The seat area is very large, which I like since I’m someone who usually has a leg up on my chair and I still have plenty of space for my booty. I’m short (5’3”) and this chair works well for me. I prefer to rest my feet on the tops of the wheels & chair legs since I’m used to not touching the floor. Just the same, the height adjustment is helpful if I didn’t prefer to float a little higher off the ground. The seat is nicely padded and comfortable. It’s lasted perfectly for the last 7 months. It’s lighter in color and could stain easily if you’re not careful with your morning coffee. I’m very happy with my purchase.

reviews.body: Just got this today, but my first impression is that it’s exactly what I needed! Is this a gaming chair? Yes. Did I buy it to use in my work office at 41yrs old? Also yes. My nephew got this over xmas and when he showed it to me, he made me try it. It was love at first sit. I’m pretty small, 4’11 and 95lbs, so all of my work chairs are very uncomfortable for me. My feet never touch the floor, the chairs didn’t recline and my head was too short to have it hit the actual headrest. After I saw my nephews, I knew I had to get this. It’s everything I need. My feet hit the floor, it has a pillow that sits under my neck, back support and even the foot rest. I love that it reclines as well and impressed with how well it came together. I’m very excited to bring to work and finally be comfortable! Price: I got this on sale for 109$. It’s normally 129$ but 20$ shipping. I wish it would stay at 99$ all around since the shipping isn’t free. It was a super heavy package though so I get it. Style: I got all black so it blends in at work and it’s as pictured. I wish the logo wasn’t so big and bright for those who don’t use this as a gaming chair but I may use a black sharpie & color it to make this more discreet. Size: If you are on the shorter side, this is a great chair. Great for kids obviously and tinier adults. Not sure this is a heavy duty chair for the regular sized adult so keep in mind. Delivery: said it would take a week but came next day which was impressive and I was very happy with that. Arrives in great condition. Setup: the directions are so so. My husband put this together and it took wayyyyy longer than it should have because some of the directions were mislabeled. Screws numbers were added that weren’t needed for this chair and some of the images were so tiny you couldn’t see much. For some reason we had the biggest issue with the footrest. We had to do it like 3xs b/c we couldn’t tell from the image how it actually sat. Got it done none the less and worth the struggle. Bottom line: worth the buy and seems good quality for the price but I’ll see how it hold up when I bring it to the office for actual use.

reviews.title: Sturdy, very cute, easy to put together!
reviews.body: I didn't expect much for how much it cost. I thought it would be okay, but knew I couldn't afford a super fancy chair, so didn't my hopes up. It's actually a fantastic chair! I'll start with the TINIEST gripe. It was filthy. GROSS. I had to get a magic eraser to get the grime off of it, grease and stuff from the factory. But it's a gorgeous pink and white chair, feels so sturdy and comfortable. Great support for your back, and that's even without the lumbar pillow that comes with it. I will say, the instructions were clearly written by ChatGPT. Awful. But the pictures were just fine, so it was actually easy to put together, haha. So don't fret if you read it and it's confusing. The diagrams are accurate and easy to read. It also didn't take long at all to put together. OH! I personally didn't want rollers, as I have a pup and didn't want to squish toes. So if you're like me and wanted to change them, they're compatible. But the wheels are super cute. :) Honestly so pleased with this chair. I am very happy with it, and look forward to using it while I work and draw and game for a long time to come.

I guess you have to decide before assembly if it will fit or be comfortable. I should have ordered a workable crystal ball. You have to buy a big box to ship it back in and you have to pay shipping. I may not get my money back, but I hope this will save others from buying this falsely advertised item.

reviews.title: Quality and comfort
reviews.body: This office chair looked nice in the listing photos, but it’s even better in person. I ordered this for my home office space which previously had an armchair that my kids broke by tipping in it. I love the light gray color of this one, since my desk is gray wood, and I love that it is a leather-type material that can be wiped down, since I have messy kids. It has a nice, stylish sleek look to it that elevates my office space. The chair was easy to assemble, but it does come with some assembly needed. It took about a half hour to get it assembled. My twelve year old did it though, so it might take an experienced adult less time. The chair is just as comfortable as you would hope for it to be. It has decent cushioning, and the lumbar pump works impressively well. The material is soft and doesn’t stick to your skin or make noise when you move. This chair is adjustable in height. For reference, I am 5’6”, and at max height my heels are about 3” off the ground. In the middle setting, my heels just touch the ground, with a couple more inches to drop. As far as width, I would say it’s standard for a full-sized office chair. I am about average in size, but I do think it’s more accommodating for larger adults than many others, due to the fact that the sides are mostly open, and the arms easily lift up. It’s also a pretty deep seat bottom and tall seat back. The build is also very sturdy. I couldn’t ask for a better office chair. I’m super happy with the overall quality, features, and design of this chair. I can’t imagine that it would disappoint anyone who bought it.

reviews.title: Comfortable adjustable-lumbar chair, kind of annoying to assemble
reviews.body: I don't have much experience putting furniture together. This was probably the most challenging piece I've assembled so far. The two armrests were by far the hardest part. Start to finish, it took me about an hour to put the thing together. First, the instruction manual also has a typo worth knowing about. One step lists screw (11) as M6 x 25 mm, while the parts legend and the screw bag both show M6 x 30 mm. This happened right in the middle of the hardest part. I spent a while convinced I had the wrong screws before realizing it was just an error in the booklet. At least the parts are labeled, with FRONT printed on the seat plate, so orientation wasn't a guess. Still, the typo cost me a lot of wasted time. Not worth deducting a star in the review, but a real annoyance. Once it's together, though, the chair is really comfortable. I like office chairs with soft arm support. These armrests stay comfortable through long stretches of sitting. The headrest pillow is a nice touch and gives good support when I lean back. My favorite feature is the inflatable lumbar support. With a pronounced lower back curve, I find pumping up the lumbar makes a real difference. A separate back cushion isn't something I've needed. The faux leather feels pleasant to the touch. There wasn't any chemical smell when I started using it. Because it's a leather-style surface, it breathes less than a mesh chair. Where I live it gets hot and humid, so that's definitely a tradeoff. Anyone who sweats a lot might want a different material. The wheels roll smoothly across wood floors without sticking or catching. Moving it around my workspace is pretty easy. Overall, the assembly could be smoother or better documented, but the comfort, the adjustable lumbar, and how easily it rolls make this a solid office chair... once it's put together.

reviews.title: Mr. Picky loves the chair
reviews.body: The Mr. Picky I live with is loving this chair after rejecting many others. It is super comfortable and looks and feels like quality furniture. It is high enough to support his frame of six feet and support his neck which was a problem with other chairs we tried. It was very easy to put together and only took me 40 minutes. I just have a few notes to make it easier for you. There is a QR code to scan for a video or the chair comes with an instruction booklet in the bag with the seat of the chair. I showed in a picture that you may have to move the arm piece a little to see all four holes that will attach the arm to the back and seat cushions. The instructions talk about 25 and 30 mm screws in the instructions book where you attach the arm but there are only 30 mm screws included and only these are needed. One tip not mentioned is you need to lean the back piece on something like the box to make it easy to attach the arm and then the seat cushion also to the arm. These are all minor and I hope will save you time when you put together this chair. I think it is well worth the cost (and even more) and it is so comfortable to sit on. The wheels were able to easily glide on my low pile carpet. It is an added bonus that the arms lift up to push the chair closer to your desk if needed. It looks good in any office or even a living room.

reviews.title: Comfortable
reviews.body: I like this chair. Size and style match the product description/images. Assembly really went pretty well. Everything lined up well and screws went in without too much trouble. It's a little bit of a hassle to put the seat cushion on, but there's enough slack in the assembly (before snuggling it down) to let you get both sides lined up. Size feels good to me, and I like the adjustability of the product. You do have a overall height adjuatment for the seat to the ground. The lumbar support can also be adjusted up and down a bit. At first I thought it looked really odd - like it stuck out way too far - but after sitting in it for quite a while I really think it is comfortable. You can also move the headrest up and down to position it right where you want. One potential downside is that the armrests are at a fixed height - which happens to be just right for myself - but that can be lifted up and out of the way if they interfere with your desk. There's also a locking mechanism to keep the chair fixed upright or allow it to tilt. The force needed to tilt can be adjusted via a large tension handle underneath, but I found it just right out of the box. As far as comfort - the material is made of a mesh like fabric, which breaths really well, but it that material on the armrests does feel a little rough on the forearms near my elbows, but only just barely. The seat cushion is very comfortable, and overall, I think the chair is really very comfortable to sit in for long periods of time.

reviews.title: Ok quality- small, almost child sized
reviews.body: This is the only all white gaming chair that I could find that was actually pretty much allllll white. I didn’t realize how small this one was until it was fully assembled- which was quite easy and not very time consuming. My last one had a much wider seat cushion which I loved and this one doesn’t. Now, I am 5’1 and a smaller built person (not to be a pick me, this is just for the sake of the review) but I would’ve been a little more let down if I was any taller or had a wider bottom and would probably return it. The quality of this is okay but has good attributes like the leg rest and the reclining feature. I wouldn’t call the pull out part under the chair a foot rest by any means bc I would have to fold up my legs a little to get my feet on there. I know that gaming chairs get a little pricey but I would’ve at least liked a bigger chair for the cost. If you’re someone who is taller or is looking for good support or a sturdy chair I probably wouldn’t pick this one with longevity and comfortableness in mind. The arm rests are a little loose, even with a good tightening. I wouldn’t trust this chair when it’s reclined if I was heavier. The back rest is also not very tall and the overall height of the chair itself is shorter than most run of the mill gaming chairs. I tried to include as many measurements as possible. I’m going to be spending a lot of time in this chair so if anything goes awry or I think something is worth mentioning I will update with review (if I can figure out how). This is good for kids or small-statured people in general. The value for the coin is ehh. For the average adult… probably not… spend your money on something better.

Or if I flip it all the way out, I sit my feet on it with my knees up, but theres still room to fit under my desk like this. I dont like to sit with my feet on the floor, and this chair meets my requirements while gaming in that aspect. I dont sit longer than 2 hours at a time for anything, so that isnt a concern i can address, anyone looking for an all day kind of review. But I dont get uncomfortable at all for the couple hours i use it at a time. The speakers face more outwards, so the sound goes out instead of in and at you. Which works great for music while doing things around the room but not so much for doing things at the computer. The volume is reasonable but not real loud. As a casual gamer though with an enjoyment for music while working around the home, this chair has been fantastic.

reviews.title: DO NOT BUY, NOT WORTH $140!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.body: Honestly I hate to write this review, one because I hate complaining and two I was super excited for a new gaming chair…… BUT after paying $160 for a chair that I would probably still be upset paying $50-80(but would expect for going the cheapest route) , the chair is super flimsy and POOR quality materials. All screws are super tight and the chair is still flimsy and moves around too much and also creaks. The back support is leaning to the side even after trying to adjust the T-bar support bracket, it’s the tilt mechanism that is causing it to lean, even after trying to reposition and tighten everything possible and the knob that the backrest T-bar slides into the tilt mechanism, it has too much play due to parts not fitting properly causing it to much free play to move around……. Also wouldn’t call this a massage chair with this super cheap non adjustable vibrating block (which you barely feel) that someone clearly ripped the backrest foam out with their fingers and it’s super uneven and crooked.(see attached images) Lastly, chair is on the smaller side! I’m 5’ 7” about 185lbs and the cushions are not too comfortable. I can feel the hard support under the seat cushion luckily the backrest and neck support pillows allow some sort of comfort for the backrest. I’ve sat in cheap $70-80 chairs that were 10x more comfortable and better quality, wish I knew the names and would have definitely purchased one of those instead, I figured spending double I would get a decent chair that I would enjoy ……. Lessened learnt, don’t expect a better quality because it cost more, and don’t purchase a gaming chair without actually sitting in it or at bare minimum having a 1st hand recommendation from a trusted source! Clearly the 4.1 stars, that magically dropped to 3.9 from purchase date to delivery date 🤬 wasn’t reliable Definitely returning,

reviews.title: A bit of style over comfort.
reviews.body: I'll start off by addressing the title. It's not the most comfortable chair. If you sit and play games for 10 hours a day, you might as well go a little higher and get something with a bit more cushion. I personally loved the style of this chair, and it was quite a bit off the standard price. So for me, I think it was worth a shot. I really like it. As a larger person 6'5" 240lbs it holds my frame and weight well. The footrest however, feels a little flimsy, and is also fairly small. I probably won't be using it. It DOES tuck completely away under the seat when not in use. The chair is SILENT so far, and rolls well. All the parts work, reclining is easy and smooth. I love the mesh back, as it has some softness, give, and breathability. The head and back support are a little hard, but they probably need a bit of wear to break in well. The chair was easy to put together. With an allen ratchet it took me about 25 minutes. This is not my first chair to assemble, so a first timer with the tools provided might take an hour or so. If you want a little style, and need that gaming look, this is a solid chair. Maybe a BIT higher than some other chairs, but I think the quality is worth it. My chair DID say GTRacing not Player but it is not a knockoff. Other than that stitching, it is exactly like the description and image. They make chairs that say both. Not an issue for me, but that is a possibility I guess. Recommended if you want the gaming chair look and can spend a bit more than a budget chair.

reviews.title: Exceptional all-day comfort and premium build quality at an affordable price
reviews.body: After more than 45 years of purchasing office chairs and office furniture, I can confidently say this is one of the finest office chairs I've ever owned. It delivers exceptional comfort, outstanding build quality, and remarkable value for the price. The chair is solidly constructed and feels extremely durable. The lumbar support is excellent, providing the right amount of support without feeling intrusive. The seat cushion strikes an ideal balance between firmness and softness, using a high-quality, resilient foam that remains supportive even after extended use. I spend between 8 and 12 hours a day in this chair, and it remains consistently comfortable from morning to evening. One feature I particularly appreciate is that the backrest stays exactly where I set it and doesn't gradually recline or rock. The height adjustable armrests are another standout feature. From opening the box to sitting in the finished chair, the entire process took approximately 38 minutes. Overall, this chair has exceeded my expectations in every respect. It's comfortable enough for all-day use, exceptionally well built, and offers features and quality typically found in much more expensive office chairs. I would not hesitate to recommend it to anyone looking for a premium office chair at an excellent value.

reviews.title: Great chair; very comfortable and worth the purchase.
reviews.body: What I have learned from many years of purchasing and putting together chairs like this is it's always best to buy a chair upon which the arms are separate from the body of the chair. There are many chairs on the market that are put together such that the entire support of the chair rests on the arms connecting the bottom of the chair to the body of the chair. That is way too much pressure on the screws that hold the arms on. This chair is not like that. You can actually put this chair together WITHOUT the arms and the chair will function properly. First, the parts of the chair were packaged very nicely. Everything was wrapped separately inside the box to protect against damaging the soft fabric of the two parts of the chair (back and bottom). Very easy to put together - intuitive and the directions were better than many I've seen. When you apply the arms, there is "give" in the application point of about an inch where you can tighten the arms closer to the body or farther away from the body giving yourself more space. I chose to tighten the screws farther away from the body so I can sit cross legged. When you apply the back of the chair to the bottom, there is the same "give" in the application point of about an inch where you can give yourself a "deeper" seat or a "shallower" seat. I chose to tighten the screws farther away from the seat so I can sit cross legged. The arms of the chair will adjust higher - which I use while I am on conference calls to appear more "relaxed". When I want to pull my chair closer to the desk, I can adjust the arms down and they slide under the desk perfectly. The leg rest slides out pretty far - I'm surprised how far this goes - and you can slide further away or closer to you depending upon if you want to extend your legs straight out or cross them. When not in use, it slides neatly back under the seat. I do not personally like to use a recline feature on an office chair. To me, it's asking too much of a moderately priced chair to perform that function (even if advertised as a main feature). That is not what an office chair is for - and I feel it's just going to wear certain points out faster than necessary. If I want to recline or relax, I go the couch or bed. Instructions for the recline feature on this chair is included but I did not try it. I believe there is also a "rock" feature. Again, I'm not going to use my office chair as a rocker. I am pleasantly surprised the back of the chair is just higher than the top of my head. I'm tall (5'9") and I am usually disappointed in the height of chairs. This chair does not have an adjustable head rest but it's just the perfect height for me. From the looks of the chair in the pictures, it really looked like it would be "huge" and just a bit "too much" and I would be swallowed up by it. It's just the perfect size. Not too big that it takes up too much space around my desk but big enough that I feel the chair hugging around me. I think this is going to really help my posture too because my old chair was so uncomfortable that I found myself always sitting on the edge of it like I was trying to get away from it (LOL) and this chair encourages me to actually sit back and relax into it. I purchased the beige chair because it was one of the three colors that was going to arrive quickly. I didn't want black again and I'm not brave enough for white. The beige is a beautiful color. Very calming. I am very pleased with my purchase and hope the seat holds up. Obviously the seat is the first thing to wear out on a chair no matter the size of the person using it. The back of this chair is so comfy though I hope if the seat does wear out quickly, a cushion will help because this chair is a dream.

reviews.title: Excellent and Comfortable (and BIG) Office Chair
reviews.body: A very large and very comfortable office chair. This is a review for the EXCEBET Big and Tall Office Chair in light grey color. I am 5'10" and 215 lb., and I would not want an office chair that is any bigger than this one. It is super easy to put together, and there are videos to show you how. The material is PU leather which is a kind of faux leather - but it's very soft, and pleasing to the touch. See pictures. I included a picture of the EXCEBET chair along side a normal sized office chair so you can clearly see the difference in form factor. Side-by-side, the regular office chair looks kind of puny. I think even Bigfoot would be pleased to sit all day in this EXCEBET chair. The reclining option is also very nice, but I should mention that it is not the same experience as a recliner sofa. The footrest is somewhat narrow, so you have to keep your legs together when reclining. Overall, I highly recommend this chair. It's not really expensive for all the value that is provided. I hope it lasts at least 5 years, which is the typical service life for an everyday-use office chair.

reviews.title: Good Price Good Comfort
reviews.body: For reference I'm 6'2 and 275lbs (~125kg). I work in an office 5 days a week, 9am to 5pm so I needed something that would at least let me be comfortable while I type my life away. Assembly was fairly easy, just make sure that when you get to the part where you have to put the back rest and the seat together that you actually keep the 4 screws that attach to the back rest loose so that it will fit into the slot of the seat. In terms of cushion I'd give it a solid 7.5 maybe 8 out of ten. It's not a recliner couch you have at home, but for an office chair at this price it's pretty dang close. It's definitely enough to make you start dozing off if you're not too careful. The main reason why I went for this one though was for the leg rest. Kinda have to get used to it to find the sweet spot because if you're fully upright and you try to use the leg rest the chair will lean forward a lot due to how it's built, it's not the most sturdy thing in the world so you gotta balance it out by reclining a bit. For a big and tall chair the leg rest isn't as big or wide as I would hope for it to be, I find myself really squeezing myself to try and fit both of them on and end up just crossing my legs most of the time, but it's still comfortable. I'd give it a 7/10. In terms of back support and the firmness of it, I haven't had issues with it or my posture, but for those that slouch, do be careful as it's not built fix or support poor posture. I'd give it a 6/10, but in my opinion this shouldn't take away from the overall score since that's not really what these are for, if you want ergonomics and good lumbar support you go for chairs designed for that. If you want casual comfort at the workplace and you're able to get up and walk around a lot then this is fine as it's not killing your spine as long as you're not fully set into it all day without breaks. Overall for the price I would highly recommend it. There are a few other chairs I'm looking at that's more expensive than this that'll surely beat it, but for fast delivery and pretty dang good comfort for a big fella, would definitely recommend.

reviews.title: Doesn't Have Advertised Features (ex. Rocking) & Support Doesn't Honor Free Replacements Advertised
reviews.body: UPDATE 5: The seller responded and AGAIN refused to honor their advertised free gas cylinder replacement, even though the original they provided failed within 3 months. Their excuse was that we were past the return window. The problem with that excuse is that we contacted them well within that window with a replacement request, and they repeatedly pretended not to understand the request, then to reject it. So they're stalling customers until they can say you aren't eligible for anything anymore. Also, if you read reviews, you'll notice a "warranty department" is mentioned, and that's who supposedly sends out the replacement parts they advertised. This apparently doesn't exist. Strongly suspect there might be some fake reviews in here given the way the company uses false advertisements and a complete lack of support. Will be reporting them to Amazon today. You should note, they seem to have removed the image that offered the free wheel replacements (though I believe I still have a screenshot for that report I'll file). But they do still mention free gas cylinder replacements in the original is too high (which is what I originally requested). I've now had to spend more money on replacement wheels because the seller lied about offering free replacements (the rubber ones safe for hardwood floors). And now I'll have to buy another cylinder for it. 100% not letting this go. I'm so tired of companies selling furniture items here with false advertising, knowing it's too difficult for most customers to return those items. UPDATE 4: Exactly 3 months from the day we ordered this chair, and after refusing to honor their advertised offer for a lower replacement cylinder, the original gas cylinder for this chair failed. No one using it uses it roughly. No one using it even comes close to the advertised weight limit. It was just being used in a stable position and suddenly failed. We reset it, and it failed again within minutes, making the chair unusable for us. I'm going to contact the seller one more time and insist on a replacement cylinder given they outright advertise they provide one, but if they refuse again, I'll be taking it up with Amazon, because this combination of quality issues and poor support is not acceptable. UPDATE 3: I definitely cannot recommend this chair. After weeks of use (with the wrong wheels and gas cylinder size because the company refused to honor their offer to send replacements), this chair causes a lot of pain. Lower back pain in particular is really bad. I suspect it's due to the combination of the very hard seat (disappointing given I looked for a spring-based seat intentionally -- if they're there, they're too small to be of any use as you still feel like you're sitting on a hard board) and the lack of lumbar support. Despite their description, there is basically NO lumbar support with this chair. It's incredibly painful even after minor use. I may even have to go back to the old chair this was replacing as the entire point was to reduce pain and increase comfort, of which this chair does neither. It's poorly made. It feels very unbalanced if you lean at all (especially with the lack of proper tension to prevent you falling backwards all the way). Way too many cracking and creaking sounds for a chair this new being used well below its advertised weight limit. Not supported at all by the seller (other than offering minor refunds to keep the junk and figure out how to dispose of it yourself at a loss). Just overall feels unsafe, uncomfortable, and I can't trust either the chair or the seller. UPDATE 2: After several back-and-forth messages with the seller here on Amazon, they've repeatedly ignored requests for the free replacement wheels (needed if you use it on hardwood floors) and the free replacement gas cylinder (if the original is too high) that are advertised on this page in the product images. After ignoring the request repeatedly, along with any tips on getting the tension to actually provide... tension... they flat out refused to honor their advertised offer for those replacement parts. All they did was offer a very small refund if we're willing to keep the chair... without the wheels needed for our floors... without the appropriately-sized canister... and without any reasonable tension function to lean back safely (forget "rocking" as noted in the description because this chair can't do that). It would cost us more to buy our own wheels and canister than what they offered, and that still doesn't address the false advertising of this being a rocking office chair or the unsafe lack of tension for the recline function. I would absolutely never do business with this company again, and we'll be contacting Amazon to see what can be done about them refusing to honor what they advertised. Extremely disappointed after a very long search for a replacement chair. UPDATE: This page, in the images, says the company will provide free replacement rubber casters / wheels if needed (which you need for hard floors), and a free lower replacement gas cylinder if the chair is too high (which it is for my wife). After asking them to send these multiple times via Amazon's messaging system, they've so far refused to do so (will update if they sort this out soon). They've also responded to questions about fixing the lack of tension and the misrepresentation about this being a "rocking" chair (it's definitely not; just reclining), and all we ever seem to get is a copy/paste response offering a small partial refund if we agree to keep the chair. We keep trying to tell them we're hoping to keep the chair, but we needed info on getting the tension to increase and we need the replacement parts they offered to make it work. But they've mostly ignored specific questions and just keep saying the same things. Until the last message where they said they couldn't send replacements for the "missing parts," even though we never said anything was missing. We're just requesting the parts they offer to send right in their Amazon description. Not happy with support at all so far. -- ORIGINAL REVIEW I have mixed feelings on this chair. First, it feels like a sturdy build. And if you're on the larger side, the cushion offers plenty of support -- firm, but mostly comfortable. The exception to the seat's comfort is that the front edge is very firm, and it can cut into the back of your thighs, negatively impacting circulation. This was the problem with my old chair and why I was replacing it. Normally I prefer a higher chair, but this is causing issues even at its lowest setting. The seller does mention in the images they'll send a lower cylinder if necessary, so if I keep the chair and receive that, I'll update on how that affects the pain at the front of the seat. The seller also offers to send replacement wheels if you need the rollerblade-style kind for hard floors. The plastic ones are extremely loud and totally inappropriate for hard floors and their protective mats, so it's nice they provide this option. But if you know you'll need them, I'd request them early. Otherwise you won't be able to fully assemble things until they arrive, or you'll have to risk damage to your floors using the defaults until the replacements can be swapped in. While I like the sturdy sense I get from the chair, there are two big problems for me. I've contacted the seller hoping I'm just not figuring out the settings properly, but I'll update if appropriate later. 1. The description advertises this as a "rocking" office chair. With office chairs, that means something very specific -- the back and seat move in unison in a true rocking action. This looks like the seat can angle back a bit based on the video, but it doesn't seem to do that when "rocking." All it does is lean the top back. That's not a rocking office chair, which was an absolute requirement in me choosing this as a replacement for my old chair. Again, I'm hoping I just missed a control or something and that this will work as-advertised. Oddly though, when the foot rest is out, the seat itself does seem to recline back, so it clearly *can.* It just won't rock otherwise? And if you have heavier legs, or longer ones like I do, the leg rest isn't really usable because your center of gravity will get thrown off (and that's the one thing that doesn't seem sturdy in general). So, for a chair advertised for bigger users, are we simply not "allowed" to use the rocking function because it's tied to the leg rest?? 2. I'm also having issues with the tension knob. All the way in one direction and the back of the chair practically falls backwards the moment you touch it. All the way in the other direction and there's barely any more tension that that. It leads to a very insecure feeling unless you lock the "rocking" function, which again was a major deciding factor in choosing this chair. I'm hoping I'm missing something here too because I've never seen an office chair with this lack of tension. Other than that, the back is comfortable, and I like that the arms are adjustable (width during installation, and height while in-use). Aside from the rocking and tension, two things would make this chair near-perfect though: 1. Adjustable lumbar support. Fixed lumbar support is all but useless in an executive chair because if you're sitting properly you're not going to be leaning back all the time. Proper lumbar support doesn't require you to recline back. It should help you stay upright and maintain your posture. 2. I agree with another reviewer who was disappointed in the lack of head rest. For all the padding on the back of this chair (which is soft, yet dense enough it feels like it will hold up for quite a while), there's no real head rest. The head area is relatively flat and sits too far back, so your head won't even touch it unless you're lying back in more of a reclined position. The only other comment I'll make for now is that any reclining is pretty loud. There's a surprising amount of squeaking and creaking for a new chair. If I keep it, I might see if something needs to be greased. But if not, just know that could be an issue if that sort of noise bothers you. Oh, and like another reviewer, my box also arrived quite damaged. The entire bottom was split open. At first we were afraid we received a used chair after ordering a new one, but the internal pieces seemed OK and everything was there. But if multiple people are receiving damaged, open boxes, I'd make sure you have somewhere sheltered for this to be delivered. Had this been left by our garage in the rain (as many larger packages are here), the chair would have been ruined before we even opened it.

I'm going to contact the seller one more time and insist on a replacement cylinder given they outright advertise they provide one, but if they refuse again, I'll be taking it up with Amazon, because this combination of quality issues and poor support is not acceptable. UPDATE 3: I definitely cannot recommend this chair. After weeks of use (with the wrong wheels and gas cylinder size because the company refused to honor their offer to send replacements), this chair causes a lot of pain. Lower back pain in particular is really bad. I suspect it's due to the combination of the very hard seat (disappointing given I looked for a spring-based seat intentionally -- if they're there, they're too small to be of any use as you still feel like you're sitting on a hard board) and the lack of lumbar support. Despite their description, there is basically NO lumbar support with this chair. It's incredibly painful even after minor use. I may even have to go back to the old chair this was replacing as the entire point was to reduce pain and increase comfort, of which this chair does neither. It's poorly made. It feels very unbalanced if you lean at all (especially with the lack of proper tension to prevent you falling backwards all the way). Way too many cracking and creaking sounds for a chair this new being used well below its advertised weight limit. Not supported at all by the seller (other than offering minor refunds to keep the junk and figure out how to dispose of it yourself at a loss). Just overall feels unsafe, uncomfortable, and I can't trust either the chair or the seller. UPDATE 2: After several back-and-forth messages with the seller here on Amazon, they've repeatedly ignored requests for the free replacement wheels (needed if you use it on hardwood floors) and the free replacement gas cylinder (if the original is too high) that are advertised on this page in the product images. After ignoring the request repeatedly, along with any tips on getting the tension to actually provide... tension... they flat out refused to honor their advertised offer for those replacement parts. All they did was offer a very small refund if we're willing to keep the chair... without the wheels needed for our floors... without the appropriately-sized canister... and without any reasonable tension function to lean back safely (forget "rocking" as noted in the description because this chair can't do that). It would cost us more to buy our own wheels and canister than what they offered, and that still doesn't address the false advertising of this being a rocking office chair or the unsafe lack of tension for the recline function. I would absolutely never do business with this company again, and we'll be contacting Amazon to see what can be done about them refusing to honor what they advertised. Extremely disappointed after a very long search for a replacement chair. UPDATE: This page, in the images, says the company will provide free replacement rubber casters / wheels if needed (which you need for hard floors), and a free lower replacement gas cylinder if the chair is too high (which it is for my wife). After asking them to send these multiple times via Amazon's messaging system, they've so far refused to do so (will update if they sort this out soon). They've also responded to questions about fixing the lack of tension and the misrepresentation about this being a "rocking" chair (it's definitely not; just reclining), and all we ever seem to get is a copy/paste response offering a small partial refund if we agree to keep the chair. We keep trying to tell them we're hoping to keep the chair, but we needed info on getting the tension to increase and we need the replacement parts they offered to make it work. But they've mostly ignored specific questions and just keep saying the same things. Until the last message where they said they couldn't send replacements for the "missing parts," even though we never said anything was missing. We're just requesting the parts they offer to send right in their Amazon description. Not happy with support at all so far. -- ORIGINAL REVIEW I have mixed feelings on this chair. First, it feels like a sturdy build. And if you're on the larger side, the cushion offers plenty of support -- firm, but mostly comfortable. The exception to the seat's comfort is that the front edge is very firm, and it can cut into the back of your thighs, negatively impacting circulation. This was the problem with my old chair and why I was replacing it. Normally I prefer a higher chair, but this is causing issues even at its lowest setting. The seller does mention in the images they'll send a lower cylinder if necessary, so if I keep the chair and receive that, I'll update on how that affects the pain at the front of the seat. The seller also offers to send replacement wheels if you need the rollerblade-style kind for hard floors. The plastic ones are extremely loud and totally inappropriate for hard floors and their protective mats, so it's nice they provide this option. But if you know you'll need them, I'd request them early. Otherwise you won't be able to fully assemble things until they arrive, or you'll have to risk damage to your floors using the defaults until the replacements can be swapped in. While I like the sturdy sense I get from the chair, there are two big problems for me. I've contacted the seller hoping I'm just not figuring out the settings properly, but I'll update if appropriate later. 1. The description advertises this as a "rocking" office chair. With office chairs, that means something very specific -- the back and seat move in unison in a true rocking action. This looks like the seat can angle back a bit based on the video, but it doesn't seem to do that when "rocking." All it does is lean the top back. That's not a rocking office chair, which was an absolute requirement in me choosing this as a replacement for my old chair. Again, I'm hoping I just missed a control or something and that this will work as-advertised. Oddly though, when the foot rest is out, the seat itself does seem to recline back, so it clearly *can.* It just won't rock otherwise? And if you have heavier legs, or longer ones like I do, the leg rest isn't really usable because your center of gravity will get thrown off (and that's the one thing that doesn't seem sturdy in general). So, for a chair advertised for bigger users, are we simply not "allowed" to use the rocking function because it's tied to the leg rest?? 2. I'm also having issues with the tension knob. All the way in one direction and the back of the chair practically falls backwards the moment you touch it. All the way in the other direction and there's barely any more tension that that. It leads to a very insecure feeling unless you lock the "rocking" function, which again was a major deciding factor in choosing this chair. I'm hoping I'm missing something here too because I've never seen an office chair with this lack of tension. Other than that, the back is comfortable, and I like that the arms are adjustable (width during installation, and height while in-use). Aside from the rocking and tension, two things would make this chair near-perfect though: 1. Adjustable lumbar support. Fixed lumbar support is all but useless in an executive chair because if you're sitting properly you're not going to be leaning back all the time. Proper lumbar support doesn't require you to recline back. It should help you stay upright and maintain your posture. 2. I agree with another reviewer who was disappointed in the lack of head rest. For all the padding on the back of this chair (which is soft, yet dense enough it feels like it will hold up for quite a while), there's no real head rest. The head area is relatively flat and sits too far back, so your head won't even touch it unless you're lying back in more of a reclined position. The only other comment I'll make for now is that any reclining is pretty loud. There's a surprising amount of squeaking and creaking for a new chair. If I keep it, I might see if something needs to be greased. But if not, just know that could be an issue if that sort of noise bothers you. Oh, and like another reviewer, my box also arrived quite damaged. The entire bottom was split open. At first we were afraid we received a used chair after ordering a new one, but the internal pieces seemed OK and everything was there. But if multiple people are receiving damaged, open boxes, I'd make sure you have somewhere sheltered for this to be delivered. Had this been left by our garage in the rain (as many larger packages are here), the chair would have been ruined before we even opened it.

reviews.title: Great Chair...bit of a read, but good info maybe...
reviews.body: This is a bit long, but maybe will help someone. The chair is great. I have been looking for a chair for several months, and finally settled on this one. My only hang-up was that I really wanted genuine leather, which this chair is not. The chairs with genuine leather are either (a) priced well over $1k, or (b) are cheap junk. This chair replaces my old, genuine leather chair, that was less than 3 years old. Unfortunately, it fell into the "cheap junk" category, as I came to find out. I had ordered that chair, just based on the leather...and in fact that is the ONLY part of the chair that held up. I replaced the base when it broke, replaced the hydraulic lift when it broke, and had to re-work the arm rests so they would stop falling off. The sides and back were also deteriorating...so quite literally, the ONLY "good" part of that chair was the actual leather itself. So, apologies for the back story, but that leads me into the review of this chair. In putting it together, I could easily see that this chair is hands down much more well-made than my old one. The base of the old one appeared to be a cast metal or some kind. Problem with cast metals are that they tend to be brittle...which is exactly what happened to me…one of the legs broke off with no warning. This chair's base is welded steel...I'm pretty confident it's not going anywhere. Second is the comfort. Lesson learned from the old chair is that if it appears to be thin padding, it definitely is. After a year or so, I had to add more fill to the old chair to keep it from being so "flat.” It was filled with some sort of cubed foam. This chair has the spring-cushion seat, and bolstered back with lumbar support. It is very comfortable, and the padding is 2, maybe 3 times thicker than the old chair. While the covering of this chair is not genuine leather, it does have a very good feel, looks to be of high quality, and is breathable - which would have been my biggest complaint had it not been. The arm rests are generous in size, and fit comfortably under the desk without hitting. I probably could have done without the footrest, but suppose it may be nice to have at some point. The tilt features work very well...plenty of firm resistance, but not so much to force you up straight, or be horizontal with a simple lean back...the tension is just right. Putting the chair together was easy...took me maybe 30 minutes, and half of that was easily spent just unpacking all the parts, as they were well protected in the box. I would agree with what some others have said about needing a second set of hands with getting the back on. I managed okay, just me, but probably should have had my wife come help...but you know, men can do it all on their own... So, all in all, I'm very happy with this chair, thus far. Hopefully it will withstand the test of time...if I can even get three years out of it, that's okay...I feel a lot better about getting a $2-300 chair every 3 years, than I do about spending $700+ each time. Some photos for reference...you can see how thick the padding is, compared to the other chair.

reviews.title: My Goldilocks Chair
reviews.body: I wish I could fully express how long and hard I was searching for what I'd begun to call my "Goldilocks chair." I had incredibly specific things I was looking for: - a padded seat (I work and game at the same desk, so I spend the majority of my day in my chair) that was wide enough for me (a 5'7", plus-sized woman) to sit cross-legged - padded armrests (surprisingly difficult to find) that wouldn't get in the way - or could be moved out of the way - if I did sit cross-legged - a back that would recline (not rock, which was sometimes hard to differentiate in product descriptions) - my white whale: a footrest to prop my legs up on for crochet and reading I ordered a possibly insane number of chairs only to return them (and for some of them, eat the cost in my depseration); I tried finding search points I could compromise on (especially that footrest - I'd all but resigned to get a tiny ottomon for my itty-bitty space under the desk); I took to Reddit forums and talked to friends, family, coworkers, family's coworkers; I gave up and continued on sitting in my old gaming chair that was quite literally falling apart several times, only to resume the search when I had the emotional fortitude to do so. This chair was like a God-send. It fulfills *every* *single* *one* of my criteria. The back, seat, and arms are plush, but supportive and (after wearing it in a little) incredibly soft and comfortable without feeling like it's going to go flat on you. After lifting the armrests high enough I'm able to cross my legs without pressing against them at all. The reclining feature is exactly what I needed (though for my purposes, I mostly just need the recliner to lock at a preferred angle for day-to-day use; the seat does tilt back some when you recline, which can be annoying, but *how* annoying depends primarily on *why* you're reclining, and whether or not you have room under your desk for your footrest to be a little higher than usual.) The back is tall enough for me to rest my head against with no issues. The footrest can be fully extended or pressed against the seat as an extra cushion for when my legs don't want to cross quite as tightly as usual (or it can be used as a tiny platform for my yarn ball!) And the pale purple and design on the cushion are pretty! At the time it felt like a gamble; I'd been burned so many times. But when this came in and my husband put it together it fit me like a glove. Everyone has different needs, so I don't know if this will meet yours or not, but I couldn't be happier.

title: BestOffice Ergonomic Gaming Chair for Adults, Video Game Chair, Blue
bullet_points: COMFORT FOR LONG GAMING SESSIONS – Stay supported through gaming, streaming and desk time with a high back, thick cushioning, lumbar support and headrest pillow designed to reduce pressure during extended sitting.

ROCK BACK AND RELAX – Take a break between matches or work sessions with the rocking function (90-125°). Lean back and gently rock when you want to relax, then return to an upright position when it is time to focus.

RACING STYLE BUILT FOR YOUR SETUP – Blue PU leather, a high-back racing profile and padded seating give this gaming chair the look of a dedicated gaming setup while keeping the surface easy to wipe clean.

STABLE SUPPORT, SMOOTH MOVEMENT – A heavy-duty metal base supports up to 250 lb, while the 360° swivel and smooth-rolling nylon casters make it easy to move between your monitor, desk and gaming setup.
SET UP AND START GAMING FAST – Everything needed for assembly is included, with step-by-step instructions and required tools. Most setups can be completed in approximately 10–15 minutes.

reviews.title: Comfortable, stylish, and great value for the price!
reviews.body: I’ve had this chair for a few days now, and I’m really impressed with how much comfort and quality you get for the price. The setup was easily understood based on the instructions & it took me about 20–30 minutes. Once assembled, it looks sleek and felt sturdy. The functionality is great for a basic gaming / office chair & it is very easy to move around unlike others that you have to drag with you. The lumbar support & adjustable recline are perfect for long work or gaming sessions. The padding is firm but not too stiff, and the armrests sit at a good height. I use it daily in my office for video editing & gaming, and it’s made a big difference in my posture & comfort. Overall, this is a solid, budget-friendly chair that doesn’t feel cheap. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a stylish, ergonomic upgrade without breaking the bank.

reviews.title: Its much better than nothing and much cheaper than higher quality chairs
reviews.body: I'm a big believer in "you get what you pay for" and I usually advise to save up, make one purchase, make one investment and don't worry about it for a few years. But something about this chair's value really scales, especially if you can grab it on sale. I got mine in white for $75 including tax and shipping. Many quality gaming chairs cost hundreds of dollars. There a handful of cheap office chairs you can snag for $60. This chair compared to one of those generic office chair is worth the extra $15. If you're looking at this chair for $90 or higher, then the former statement is true (save up). Anyway. I've had this chair for a day now and it isn't perfect. I'll go over what I like and what I don't like. Appearance: It looks nice. Doesn't look or feel too cheap. The base is metal with plastic feet. Many chairs have plastic base with plastic feet.+1pt Functionality: This chair has a handful of features-- You can adjust the height. +1pt But it only has about a 3in range -1pt It has a lock to let you remain upright and can be unlocked so you can recline back. +1pt It does NOT have a way to lock in the reclined position. -1pt Comfort: This chair is pretty comfy. It has a removable/adjustable head pillow and a removable/adjustable lumbar pillow as well. +1pt It is a little stiff. Some people may like that. It also may break it after a while. I've only had it one day so I will update if something new develops. The chair has a *mostly* comfortable width to me. It measures 19" for arm to arm. But it has this little "cushion" that tries to contour your legs that makes it a little uncomfortable to sit with my legs spread even a little. I have to keep my knees closer together than I normally would to keep the "cushion" from digging into the side of my legs. Because of this, there is really only about 16" of room for your butt or the sides of your thighs. I'm about 5'10" Male 215lbs size 38 pants XL shirt. I think I am at the cusp of being able to comfortably sit in this. It was not made with larger people in mind. It does state a 250lb weight limit while we're on the topic. -1pt Assembly: I've assembled several office chairs before and this process was similar and just as easy. +1pt If you aren't experienced or if you struggle with Ikea stuff, you may find it difficult. The hardware that they include is kinda junk. If you have the luxury of using your own hardware (or hand tools at least), I would highly recommend it. I had one bolt that had really junky threads from the factory and I couldn't do much about it, just had to cross thread it and tighten it the best I could. I had another bolt that stripped and the thread never would grab. Luckily there was one extra included in the packaging and I ended up being able to tighten it without cross threading. I think I got lucky. 90% of the assembly was smooth sailing and the few snags that arose, I knew exactly what to do. Again, if you aren't experienced with this, it could easily turn into a headache and a return to amazon over poor quality hardware

I think I got lucky. 90% of the assembly was smooth sailing and the few snags that arose, I knew exactly what to do. Again, if you aren't experienced with this, it could easily turn into a headache and a return to amazon over poor quality hardware

reviews.title: Not bad, not great
reviews.body: At roughly a year-ish of ownership. It became my main office/computer chair, replacing a pretty standard office chair originally bought at staples/office depot. Work from home so in this chair a pretty consistent amount of time, beyond leisure time/work outside of this. Pro's - pretty durable. I'd say its gotten its fair share of wear and tear and it's still holding pretty well. No rips that I see, arm supports still holding strong, can lean back and shift the chair up/down with no issues. Head rest isn't half bad, same with the included lower lumbar support. (Sort of) Con's - It's a little smaller width wise than I'd realize. The previous staples office chair wasn't that expensive, but it had a few extra inches in the seat so it felt a bit more leisurely than this. It's not terrible, but check the width dimensions just to be sure. The seat cushion you sit on isn't much of a 'cushion' in the sense that it's soft or has any 'give' when you sit, its pretty solid. The good of this means it kept its form over time - the bad is it isn't very comfortable after extended periods; depends what you're expecting. This sturdiness also translates to the occasional bit of not so comfortable sitting with the family jewels. I bought it the intent to see if this style of chair is worth it, considering some of the competitors want $500 for these. It's good for the price point, but with some shortcomings so to me, it was worth it over spending $500 and having the same complaints.

title: Corsair TC500 Luxe Gaming Chair – Premium Breathable Fabric – Wide Seat – Five-Way Adjustable Armrests – Adjustable Built-in Lumbar Support – 90-135 Degree Recline – Sherwood
bullet_points: Discover True Comfort: The TC500 LUXE is built from the ground up for premium, plush comfort, combining premium breathable fabric with a quilted seat and backrest that look as good as they feel, all atop a sturdy steel frame.

Get Settled In: Relax into a seat that’s wider and flatter than the typical gaming chair to fit many body types and seating positions, with contoured foam and subtle bolstering to support you for long hours of lounging as well as intense work and play.
Omniflex Adjustable Armrests: CORSAIR’s Omniflex armrests are adjustable in five directions so you can find the sweet spot for your arms.
Adjustable Built-in Lumbar Support: Feel the comfort with the TC500 LUXE's easy four-way lumbar support – perfect posture, less back strain, more luxury.
Detachable Magnetic Neck Pillow: Offers additional support for your head and neck, with fast magnetic attachment and height adjustment.

reviews.title: This review is all over the place but informative!
reviews.body: Initially worried about the reviews I've read about the arm rests and some other things, and the price almost pushing me away from buying this chair. Finally pulling the trigger I can say with confidence they either fixed what people were talking about with the arm rests (made them closer to the chair and more adjustable) or people just expect a love seat or couch. The chair is perfect, not a single problem putting it together, I had it together in 20 mins. The chair is extremely solid and doesn't squeak at all. not only does the back of the chair recline super far like most gaming chairs, it has a separate paddle to set how far the base (place you're butt goes) reclines back to avoid having to sit back against the chair using you're weight to recline which is a massive bonus for me. some chairs require weight to recline but without being locked this chair reclines with ease. The adjustability of this chair is everything you would need. I work from home and this chair keeps me comfortable all day and all night for gaming sessions. Its a stiff chair but not too stiff, Stiff in the best way. when I first sat in it I was concerned it was going to be too stiff but after pulling 6-8 shifts for 2 weeks without standing up during, it has kept me comfortable and with 0 pain compared to my last gtp office gaming chair. after returning my Secret labs titan due to discomfort, I went from a 300$ gtp office chair to this. It has all the features you could need whether you are strict about posture, or you just wanna sit back drink a beer and watch movies or even console game its perfect. I wanted to stick to a gaming chair style but have that lumbar support and some other stuff. and I found it all in this chair. I'm 6,2 at 215-225 pounds. chair fits me perfect. I would 100% recommend trying it out if you want all the features in a gaming chair, while still keeping as much of that ergo you can with the style of chair. the pillow is actually super soft and squishy too. Its actually comfortable to use compared to other brands with really stiff pillows more for look. The chair looks leather in the mock ups, but its far from, its hard to explain, it's sort of a matte leather underarmor t shirt material. smooth and grippy but not sticky like leather. that may sound weird but in my opinion its the perfect material for a computer chair. its almost like a smoother suede material. Only negative I guess I would give them which wont effect anyone using this chair on carpet, is the wheels are pretty stiff if you dont have the weight of the chair on them. they wont freely spin if you flick the wheel with you're hand but they spin just fine. definitely not a hard floor friendly wheel, which I don't know of much other then buying roller blade computer chair wheels for commercial office spaces. all in all doesnt effect me all and the chair moves just as easily as any other on carpet. TO ANSWER SOME QUESTIONS IVE SEEN PEOPLE ASK ONLINE... 1. you cannot feel the diamond stitching at all on your back even after long sitting sessions. 2. the arm rests are more adjustable then secret labs and the gtp office chairs and not too far away from the chair (anymore?). 3. the price is steep until you feel the quality and durability of the materials they use, the weight and thickness of all the bolts, plastics, metals and fabrics show the quality. 4. how does it compare to secret labs? in my opinion the secret labs are super over hyped and over priced, yes they last a long time. but in my opinion they are super uncomfortable. for 150$ less then the titan, this chair takes the cake. All in all this chair is a 10/10 FOR ME. I know chairs fit everyone differently but I found the only chair I'm going to be sitting in until the tc600 or up comes out! sorry for the all over review if you made it this far, I just had all these questions when I was buying and I think this wraps up most of them. 500$ is alot for a chair but this is 500$ well spent in my book. I posted pictures I thought would best explain the chair. there is simply not enough reviews or info on this chair online yet with this model being less then a year old and being expensive I hope this helps you! cheers and good luck on you're chair hunt. p.s I am not sponsored by corsair although I wish I was, I just really like the chair :)

reviews.title: Great chair
reviews.body: This is is such an upgrade from my last sub $100 chair. The adjustable back support is worth the cost alone. I was hunching over in my last chair and now my posture is correct. These chairs are made of soft fabric. I am 5’4 and it adjusts to my height. There is a qr code for build instructions on the top of box when you open it. The arm rests can be adjusted multiple ways. There is a tab on each arm that lets you move them up and down. I didn't notice this at first, so I couldn't reach the arm rests till I moved them up. The box is very heavy and very large. You will need 2 people to pick it up or you can turn it on its side and roll it like i did if you don't have help. Cons: The fabric has a break-in period and might feel stiff at first, but it will adjust the more you use it. I recommend getting a memory foam cushion if this bothers you. There is a primer-like new smell but will go away in a few days. You might want to open a window during this period if it bothers you. Since the arm rests move if you pull on them, I recommend grabbing the wings near the top of the chair to move it.

reviews.title: A Great Chair…. Almost
reviews.body: First I want to start off by saying I really wanted to love this chair so badly! I was so excited to buy this and get it into my office setup, but it really fell short of expectations. The 3 star rating is for the $550 price point - I was able to get it on a considerable sale, so for the price of about $300 it’s more worth it and would give it 4 stars but I cannot recommend this chair at full price. Cons: - My office does get warm with my gaming computer and this chair absolutely gets hot after sitting for a couple hours compared to my old mesh one, not sweaty but uncomfortable. - The back has awful padding. The lower portion with the adjustable lumbar feels like a rock pushing into your back if you actually use it so I have to keep it almost all the way depressed. Then right where it transitions from the diamond stitching to the flat part where the wings are, it’s like there’s a metal rod going across (likely the top of the adjustable lumbar thing) but man it’s really not comfortable to lean back into or use that fully reclined position. So overall the lower back is really hard, then there’s this middle that’s extremely plush, and then at the top middle back below your shoulder blades it’s hard as a rock so it’s unfortunate. Not as comfy as most good reviews make it out to be but it’s also not unbearable just being picky due to price point. - It squeaks!!! I was hoping a few of these reviews were just a couple bad batches but nope. Same thing others have said, right where the metal hinge is on the left side, if your sitting and using the rocking feature it creaks and squeaks every time you rock. Thats something that was just fully unacceptable for a chair at this price. - The hip bolstering really digs into the sides of my legs if man spreading and hurts after a while. - Overall the chair just doesn’t seem too sturdy/stable on the base. It has a fair amount of play when moving around but again not the end of the world it’s still fairly solid. Pros: - The bottom cushion is actually really comfortable for me sitting in it all day long even though it’s more on the firm side. It’s also big so even at 6’2 with all height in my legs I can kick a leg up. - While the backing is annoyingly uneven, I think it promotes much better posture than my other chair. - It looks just so good!! and it is definitely made out of good premium materials, I do see this chair lasting a long time! - Building it took maybe 15 minutes and you really don’t need any instruction, it’s common sense for anyone who’s ever put something together. - The pillow is so comfy! - While the wheels are stiff, and the chair is heavy I was worried about how it rolled on carpet but man it’s a breeze! It rolls really well around the room on carpet. - For the most part it’s a chair that I can sit in all day and it’s comfortable. The backing is borderline making me want to return it, but I got a great discount so I’m sticking with it. - Oh and the arm rests! At 6’2 I have longer arms but what… they are perfect for me. They aren’t too far forward or too far back at all. That’s why they have the 180 design if you want to get closer to your desk just flip them around and scoot up! Overall, again don’t buy this chair at full price you’ll likely be disappointed as the creaking and the back padding are my biggest complaints. If you can get 40%+ off it’s more worth it but be warned if you’re looking into something that’s plushy. It’s very firm. But it’s really pretty to look at!

reviews.title: Great chair for a killer price.
reviews.body: I have had a Secret Lab chair that I have been using for work for the past 6 years and have had my share of issues with it (their warranty is a joke). When I had to return to the office and took my Secret Lab back, I needed a chair for home. I refused to pay over $500 for a new chair. I looked into this one and got it around Christmas time for $250. At that price, this chair is a phenomenal value. It is a little smaller than my Titan XL but accommodates my 6-ft 280 Lb frame without complaining. It looks awesome. The green that I have really feels like a master chief OD green. (I'd love to embroider a Chief helmet on the back). The adjustment of the lumbar is great and I was able to make it more comfortable and supportive than my Secret Lab. My only gripe is the armrests don't lock into place. While they are great for their adjustability and range of motion, they can easily move when you are adjusting or really "in the zone." That's really the reason for 4 stars because the armrests are what you interact with the most after the seat itself.

reviews.title: Well Made but Stiff
reviews.body: Had this thing almost a year now with about daily use. People are right saying it's stiff. It's well made with nice materials but really lacking in cushioning. The recline and rotating/extending arm rests are nice but it doesn't make up for the low comfort overall. For the price you can definitely find something more comfortable, but if you need something presentable and you're not sitting in it for 8hrs a day it's decent.

reviews.title: Very LUXE(urious).
reviews.body: Chair was easy to setup. Heads up, there are no instructions in the box, but a QR code to scan to get both a written and video manual. All parts are very sturdy and you can tell that the quality is top notch. Chair is relatively firm, looks amazing, and has great lumbar support. Wheels seem a little tight, but I'm sure it will break in over time. Many people ask if you feel the "diamond" pattern stitching, I do not notice at all. A nice bonus is the magnetic head pillow! It is very soft. I debated between this and the Secret Labs Titan Evo, and tried both out before I bought. The Titan is a bit more firm, this is a bit more cushy. I think for the value (before the occasional discounts), this chair is a better value.

I know a lot of people complain They’re too far forward but that is easily fixed by switching them around, the problem is they’re still not that great even after doing so. The main issue with this chair is the absolute window, licking engineering that went into the back rest. I don’t think these companies genuinely test their products before they release them, but you can 100% feel the support bar that holds the lumbar system at the top of the back rest. It is immediate as soon as you sit in the chair no it is not the lumbar itself it is a brace that holds the mechanism. Also, I am 5 foot 10 and the side bolsters of the back rest make contact with my arms in certain positions and is far from comfortable. Do not let this chair deceive you it does not hold your upper back. You get an uncomfortable bar at the middle of your back and the only other point of contact is the head pillow. Yeah let’s talk about the head pillow you could sneeze in this thing falls off. They use the weakest magnet imaginable, and the pillow feels infinitely cheaper than other companies. Please stop making chairs corsair.

reviews.title: でかいが質感よし座り心地よし
reviews.body: AK●cingからの乗り換え勢です。 エンジニアのためずっと座っていますが現状イイ感じ、満足してます。 ただでかい、低身長はフットレスト必須（ないと太股の裏圧迫されそう）。 ●良い点 組み立て ★：ありえん簡単 質感 ◎：布製なのにスベスベ。PUレザーは耐久性が嫌だけど、ファブリックも質感がなぁという場合の最適解。 ランバーサポート 〇：内蔵型にしては結構わかるくらいせり出てくれる。 アームレスト ◎：しっかりした感じ。上はちゃんともっちり。 座面・背面 〇：AKのふかふかタイプに慣れていた人間からすると結構ハードタイプ。よくあるゲーミングチェアみたいなセミバケタイプの立ち上がりがないのであぐらをかきやすい。 ロッキング ◎：沈み込んでゆったりできる、イイ感じ（語彙力の喪失）。 ピロー ◎：座面などに対してこっちはソフト、後頭部が辛くない。 ●悪い点（元々調べてわかっていたので許容済） サイズ感 △：シリンダーが高い、身長165cmには大きすぎる、流石外国モン。175-180cmの人とかだと丁度よさそう。 ※別でフットレスト用意したのでこれは問題なし。 キャスター △：オフィスのマットみたいな地面で使っているが、あんまり転がらないのでちょびっと動かす時に力がいる。逆に考えればどっしりして安定感はある。
reviews.body_en: I am a transfer from AK●cing. I'm an engineer so I'm sitting there all the time, but the current situation is good and I'm satisfied. However, if you are big and short, you will need a footrest (otherwise it will put pressure on the backs of your thighs). ●Good points Assembly ★: Impossibly easy Texture ◎: Smooth even though it's made of cloth. This is the perfect solution if you don't like the durability of PU leather, but you also like the texture of fabric. Lumbar support 〇: For a built-in type, it protrudes quite a bit. Armrest ◎: Feels solid. The top is really chewy. Seat/Back 〇: For someone who is used to the fluffy type of AK, this is quite a hard type. It doesn't have a semi-bucket type rise like common gaming chairs, so it's easy to sit cross-legged. Rocking ◎: A nice feeling where you can sink in and relax (loss of vocabulary). Pillow ◎: This pillow is soft against the seat surface and does not hurt the back of your head. ●Bad points (I knew this from research, so it's acceptable) Size: △: The cylinder is tall, too big for someone 165cm tall, and it's definitely a foreign product. It seems to be perfect for people of 175-180cm. *This is not a problem because I prepared a separate footrest. Caster △: I use it on the ground like an office mat, but it doesn't roll around much so it takes a lot of force to move it a little. On the other hand, it feels solid and stable.
