reviews.title: Es war ein Versuch mit dem Stuhl der sich als wirklich gut herausstellt
reviews.body: Mein alter Bürosessel hat es nach 30 Jahren nicht mehr gemacht aber was will man nach dieser Zeit auch verlangen. Ich hab kaputte Bandscheiben und war auf der Suche nach einem Stuhl in dem ich wenigstens eine halbe Stunde oder Stunde verbringen kann und hatte auch schon einen Fehlkauf hinter mir. Selbst wenn einem versprochen wird dass ein Stuhl extra toll ist für die Wirbelsäule bedeutet das nicht gleich automatisch dass ich da noch sitzen kann. Geld war natürlich auch begrenzt zur verfügung also dachte ich mir, dann versuchst mal was, was für einen Bürostuhl nicht so üblich ist und siehe da, ich sitze in diesem Gamerstuhl sehr angenehm. Ich kann ihn fast in eine Liegeposition bringen was mir sehr hilfreich ist und habe auf der Sitzfläche genügend Platz um hin und her zu rutschen. Die Armlehnen sind in verschiedenen Achsen verstellbar was für mich neu war und gleich als positiv zu bewerten war. Die Kippfunktion ist für mich sehr wichtig da sie mir Druck von der Wirbelsäule nimmt. Eigentlich kann ich nach 6 Wochen der Nutzung nichts wirklich negatives finden jedoch möchte ich nur 4 Sterne vergeben weil in der Kippfunktion in der Beweglichen Achse etwas Spiel ist und man das beim Kippen merkt und die Nähte sind an meinem Stuhl an den Rundungen nicht ganz rund genäht. Ich hoffe das der Stuhl sehr lange hält da die unterkonstruktion doch sehr massiv gebaut ist. Der Fuß ist aus Alu-Druckguss und macht wirklich was her. Das Nackenpolster ist klasse und wird von mir gern benutzt. Auf das Polster im Lendenbereich muss ich verzichten, das drückt mir mit meinem Problem zu sehr.
reviews.body_en: My old office chair no longer worked after 30 years, but what else could you ask for after that time? I have broken discs and was looking for a chair in which I could spend at least half an hour or an hour and I had already made a bad purchase. Even if you are promised that a chair is great for your spine, that doesn't automatically mean that I can still sit there. Of course, money was limited so I thought to myself, then try something that is not so common for an office chair and lo and behold, I sit very comfortably in this gamer chair. I can almost put it in a lying position which is very helpful and I have enough space on the seat to slide back and forth. The armrests can be adjusted in different axes, which was new for me and was immediately rated as positive. The tilt function is very important for me because it takes pressure off my spine. Actually, after 6 weeks of use, I can't find anything really negative, but I would only like to give it 4 stars because there is some play in the movable axis in the tilting function and you notice it when tilting and the seams on my chair are not sewn completely round on the curves. I hope that the chair lasts a very long time because the substructure is very solid. The base is made of die-cast aluminum and really looks great. The neck cushion is great and I enjoy using it. I have to do without the padding in the lumbar area; it puts too much pressure on me with my problem.

reviews.title: Comfortable, multi-adjustable and durable desk chair
reviews.body: This is an excellent desk chair, especially for long hours at the computer, but i have to confess that it's taken a little time to get used to it only because this chair and my old faux leather desk chair (also sold on amazon and pictured below for reference) are at totally different ends of the spectrum. The new VIOLET mesh computer chair is extremely comfortable even after spending most of my days and nights sitting in it since i spend many, many hours daily working, communicating and gaming on my desktop computer. the chair may appear to be lightweight; however, it's got a decent amount of weight to it because of the high quality materials used to make it, especially the solid metal parts that make up the strong and stable base. In my opinion, the ability to adjust the arm rests, seat height and lumbar support proved to be a godsend, which i was not expecting, because it all enhances the versatility and functionality of the chair. Being able to change the chair to recline a bit is probably very useful for many, but I prefer a sturdy, stiff, upright chair back, so i adjusted it accordingly at a set in place 90-degree angle. The lumbar support is especially helpful to maintain proper posture and spinal alignment, yet again there was a small issue in that i generally sit with a slight forward lean or, as stated earlier, with my shoulders directly over my hips. in order to have full back support, you must lean back slightly, and that's an awkward position for me in any chair. the arm rests can be moved down at your sides or in an upright position as if there were no arm rests at all. and i have found myself switching back and forth between the two depending on what i am doing and how much movement i require in the chair. they can also be moved forward and backward a short distance, which i did find a little bothersome when the arm rests were down and i bumped them when i happened to move my arm(s) a little. they do not lock in place, but i'm positive that this is just another little concern that i can easily get used to since the old chair's arm rests were not adjustable at all. did i mention that it's PURPLE!?! not the only reason, but definitely one of the main reasons, that i purchased this chair over every other chair i looked at. and there were a lot of them under consideration. it comes in several different colors, including the traditional, brown, white and black, among others, which i really liked a lot since my room of course has a purple theme going on, and this fashionably attractive and functional chair fits in perfectly with the decor and further brightens up the space! i am so happy with this purchase even though it took me 3 hours and not 15-20 minutes to assemble. and that was all on me because (1) i am really slow and methodical when i'm doing new things, taking care with every step to do it right, and (2) i am not handy in the least and can barely hammer in a nail these days. as advertised, all tools, primarily the allen wrench, are included. no parts were missing, and nothing was damaged upon delivery. and, best of all, i can say that i assembled it all by myself perfectly on the first try, so it was well worth the time and effort spent.

reviews.title: Good chair that's pretty easy to put together with 5 year warranty
reviews.body: Here are my comments and concerns with model YX001 only. The instructions have a few issues imho: black letters/words printed on a dark/darker background, I literally could not read them at times and had to go to another room with a spotlight to make sure I followed directions. A box around the words are fine, but not a colored box. The 6 star gear shims (piece I) on the arms really needs a better way to identify instead of “placed in the direction of the instructions”. I am not having any issues with the arms so I assume I may have gotten it right. There aren't any instructions when to tighten all the screws that you were told to leave untightened, that could lead to an issue if when you finally get the chair finished and see step 8 saying Done and try to sit in it. Not impossible use the included Allen wrench (great it is included!) to tighten the screws from step 4 to Done because the T-handle will not fit in the now put together space. We have a bunch of regular Allen wrenches so I was able to complete the tightening required. Overall assembly was not that difficult and the time to accomplish it was not longer than expected. While the above caused some delay, the chair is still fine after 4 weeks of continuous use. The chair itself: the lumbar support is very nice and easy to adjust. The arms are attached to the back and the seat seemingly to give more support for them when getting in and out of the chair. The arms lifting up and away is nice. Would recommend if you want something durable that doesn’t feel like a chore to wear daily.

reviews.title: I packed a whole city and almost got arrested!
reviews.body: I packed a whole city and almost got arrested ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ I am a traveller with a problem: too much stuff. I had already checked two suitcases and still had luggage that could fill a small village. So I bought this SHRRADOO Extra Large Travel Laptop Backpack because I needed something that could swallow my belongings without looking suspicious. When it arrived, I was honestly disappointed. It looked small. I thought, “This thing can barely fit a rat, let alone my entire life.” But then I started packing. And packing. And packing. Different compartments, hidden pockets, secret zip zones, nice color combinations, travel friendly, this bag is like a magician’s hat. I fit clothes, shoes, gadgets, snacks, and maybe a small city and the entire Amazon. I am pretty sure I probably packed a house and a car too. The zippers are strong. The fabric is tough. And when I put it on my shoulders, the straps were so soft and comfortable I almost cried. I thought I had won. I walked past the airline ground support with confidence, they didn’t suspect a thing. But then came TSA. The scanner lit up like Christmas. They saw the entire city inside my bag. I was flagged. They searched it and found the Mayor tucked in one pocket. Everyone was shocked. How did I pack so much? Lesson learned: the bag is amazing, but it will make you look like a suspect when you packed a city! Now for the aftermath. When I arrived home, my shoulders and back were screaming for mercy for three days. I could barely lift my arms as they ache from the weight. But you know what? It was worth it. I carried my whole world on my back and survived to tell the tale. If you need a backpack that can hold everything and make you feel like a superhero (with back pain), buy this bag. It is a beast. 10/10. Would pack a city again 😂🎒🌆💀

reviews.body: 2024 update 4yrs in this bag is STILL going strong. I’m starting to see others rocking this brand on their commutes. This bag has traveled no less than 30k miles by car, train and planes. It’s my go to travel bag. The absolute best. (2021) I wanted to write this review after 1yr of use. This bag has held up extremely well! On par with LL Bean for quality and durability but with thicker material. The reason I picked this up is because I needed something bigger than my deluxe LLB to fit my 17” laptop in that would also accommodate the laptops protective zip case. I looked at several different brands and ultimately landed with this one because of the great reviews and the warranty. What sold me was the law student review with all her textbooks. Yup if it can carry all those around for 1yr of law school this bag has the durability I need. If you want to save money on a weight fitness vest you can easily throw a couple 20lb weights in this thing and run up and down flights of stairs for a fraction of the cost and plenty of weight scalability. For normal users this bag is amazing. There are plenty of storage pockets and device protection within those pockets. This bag can carry anything. And in my case it has. From overnight bag to technology bag and everything in between. I’ve packed 17” laptop (in case) with iPad chargers cables and VR headset along with water bottle and snacks to bring to a friends. I’ve carried board games and clothes. Hiking gear etc. everything has fit and stored very well The straps and top handle are sturdy the zippers remain resilient. They do not catch and seal and track seamlessly no hiccups or jerks along the way. Sometimes it’s tight around the 17” laptop in its protective case and the zippers still work well and seal tightly despite the stress out on them. I’ve loaded this thing up with easily 50lbs of gear and hauled it on my back and it has stood the test of time There are no rips or tears in the materials, handles, straps or zippers. The water bottle netting is holding strong, too. I love all the pockets for organization purposes. I love how deep and wide this pack is. Deep enough to hold the big laptop. Wide enough to accommodate an oculus headset alongside in the middle pocket. Enough protection that I feel comfortable carrying these gadgets in the bag. This has become my go to bag for everything. Several times I have thought to buy another one. I don’t have a use for 2 but I enjoy it so much because of its versatility and durable reliability that it might be nice to have a backup. Friends and family are amazed but how much I fit in this bag. They go to lift it and I say don’t pick it up that’s heavy, I’ve got it. They laugh and go to pick it up and pause to gather their strength and lift and are impressed that I carry it around and then the fact that it holds so much. This bag keeps me strong and in shape for sure. It is also strong. Outdoor enthusiasts will love this bag. It can carry ski boots, hiking gear, gym gear, sports or sparring gear, picnic supplies, weekend away bag, tailgating gear, you name it. This bag carries it all. At this point I see it lasting many years to come. If anyone needs a backpack I will buy/recommend this. For the price ($25-30) and durability (1+yr) it’s unbeatable.

reviews.title: Best Traveling Backpack!
reviews.body: I'm a 48-year-old teacher, so my back has been through a lot. But this SHRRADOO backpack? It's genuinely great. I originally bought two for myself and for my wife. I'm the kind of person who carries a gaming laptop, three textbooks, a tablet, a jumble of cords, my lunch, a spare sweater, and a random stapler that's been living in there for weeks. This bag handled all of it without any trouble. The shoulder pads are thick and breathable, I honestly forgot how much I was carrying. And the combination lock is nice. I mostly use it to keep my students out of my snack stash. (I'm only half joking.) Then I saw it was on sale, and I went a little overboard. I bought four more as gifts for: 1. My nephew in college (he uses it for classes and weekend camping) 2. My friend who travels for work (it's airline approved and fits under the seat) 3. My neighbor who hikes 4. And my own teenager, who kept "borrowing" mine anyway The quality is really top tier. I've stuffed this thing under airplane seats, strapped it to a camping chair, dropped it in a puddle, and used it as a pillow on a delayed flight. Still looks brand new. The 20+ pockets mean I don't lose my keys or charger anymore. If you're a teacher, a gamer, a parent, a hiker, or just someone tired of carrying multiple bags, buy this. Especially if it's on sale. Your back will thank you. And your friends will thank you when you inevitably buy them one as a gift too. Pros: Huge capacity, durable, comfortable, lockable, great price Cons: None that I've found. I fit my gaming laptop, books, tablet, cords, water bottle, jacket, and random classroom supplies with room to spare. – A very happy teacher who is now also a very popular gift-giver

reviews.title: Fantastic travel / work backpack at a great price!
reviews.body: I bought this backpack in early August and used it daily as a teacher. Ten months later and at the end of the school year, this backpack is still going strong with little to no signs of wear. Style: This backpack looks sleek with a touch of vintage appeal. The color is great, which helps if you want to maintain a low profile while using it. There's a small pocket up front, a medium pocket behind that (with a separate zipper pocket inside for safekeeping valuables; and slots to hold several pens), and the main storage area has a separate laptop sleeve. One of the photos has my school-issued 13-inch laptop. It easily fits in the slot with plenty of room to spare. The sides of the backpack have two mesh-like pockets that can hold small items. Comfort: The handle on top along with the two straps have thick padding. It's comfortable carrying the backpack whether you use one strap or two. Durability: My backpack is still in great condition after heavy use for the past ten months. This includes tossing it on the rear seat of my car, placing it in my trunk, and having it rest many times on the carpeted classroom floor. The back and bottom of the backpack still look great. I will easily be able to continue using this backpack for at least another full school year. Cargo capacity: My everyday carry included our school-issued laptops, plus a power cord, an iPad (with protective case), an external hard drive, about half a dozen pens, a pad or two of paper, and other assorted items. Even with all that stuff I can fit more in there if needed. Overall value: Excellent. This is such a great backpack that I bought one for my wife, and she uses it at her school. If you're looking to save some money but still want a durable and useful backpack, do not hesitate. Buy this backpack with confidence.

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.body: I'm absolutely loving this backpack! I used to use a Nordace backpack that was supposed to have 2 laptop pockets, but one of them was very much not meant for laptops, and was disappointed so I looked elsewhere. I am so glad I found this one. It is far more lightweight than my Nordace one, plenty of pockets and zippers for organization, inner pockets and a back pocket for security (I personally keep my wallet in an inner zipper pocket since the back pocket is a wee bit small). It also looks exactly like the picture (which is very exciting to me). Here's a bit of a breakdown: Pros: - Large laptop pocket (fits my 16" laptop) - Lots of pockets - Against-the-back security pocket - Very breathable - Very light - Feels high quality and durable - 3 bottle-holder pockets (2 outside, 1 inside) - USB charging for portable batteries - Strap for attaching to luggage - Waterproof Cons: - Likely won't hold larger items like textbooks (at least, it doesn't hold my large ones) - Security pocket is small - Doesn't have 2 laptop pockets - VERY tight outer bottle holder pockets I, personally, got this for both work and school so I can carry both laptops together. It doesn't have 2 laptop pockets, but the one that it does is MASSIVE. The strap is actually loose even after putting both laptops into it so it can easily fit larger laptops. I went on a work trip and it was perfect. Half the time, I forget how much stuff I have in my backpack because of how light it is and how well it disperses the weight. I also appreciate that it's slim. My previous backpacks have always been bulky and I always felt awkward while trying to squeeze down the aisles of a plane to get to my seat, but it wasn't a problem this time. I do wish the outer bottle holder pockets were a little looser and larger so that I can fit my larger water bottle into them, but it isn't too big of a deal for me since I like to carry my bottle for the most part. Overall, this backpack is AMAZING for the price that it's set at and I hope more people find this. This has honestly been life-changing after having so many poor backpacks. My back thanks you for your product, Volher. Keep making these backpacks to perfection.

reviews.title: You won’t regret this purchase!

I wanted it all - ample room for the work I bring home, safe spot for my laptops, and the one bougie request - a slot to fit my 40oz travel mug!! I wanted it to be cute, too. I’ve searched high and low - and guys - I’ve found it all and more in this bag! First, the bag is so functional!! I can’t believe the storage it has. It looks pretty, and the straps have cushioning and are very comfortable. There are two side pockets that easily hold a 40oz Stanley or Brumate. It has a special strap that keeps it from tipping over and I absolutely love that! I got tired of shoving cups into my other bags, just to have them spill or have to carry them in my hand. The one zippered bag slot has 2 places for laptops, which is outstanding because I have my personal laptop and my work laptop. I no longer hand to pick and choose which one to bring home with me. There are two other zippered compartments for additional storage. I’m so excited to use this bag! The material seems really durable and hasn’t gotten dirty yet. Seems like you could easily wipe off any dirt or spills. I think it was a great value for the money! I’ll probably order another one to have as a hockey mom travel bag! It would be a perfect weekend bag. And - it has the awesome pocket on the back of the bag that allows you to slip it on top of the handle of a suitcase! That’s a sweet bonus feature that I have to mention! Overall - I adore this bag. It took 18 years, but I finally found THE perfect teacher bag. Click add to cart now. You will not regret it!

reviews.title: Perfect backpack!!
reviews.body: Okay, I have been searching for the right bag for SO long, and I finally found my favorite!! I have been using this bag every single day for months and it is perfect. I carry a LOT of stuff in my bag on a daily basis. Don’t ask me why, for some reason I think I will need everything at all times throughout the day: laptop, notebooks, a Bible, sometimes books, medicine, feminine products, pens/pencils, etc. This is the ONLY bag I have found that carries whatever I want comfortably, has enough pockets, and looks super cute. It has tons of pockets, enough to effectively organize anything you want. If you’re a normal person using it for regular daily use, you may not even use all the pockets. I love the material. It doesn’t look cheap, it’s very cute, and I haven’t washed it yet (clearly, don’t judge how dirty it is I’ve used it every day for months) but it looks like it would be easy to wash. Everything is like a canvas-type material except for the brown, which is like a leather. It has adjustable straps, 2 pockets for water bottles, and it is really comfortable to wear. Unless this thing breaks, which it hasn’t after months of daily use and hauling around lots of weight, I don’t ever want another bag!

reviews.title: Perfect Travel Backpack with Plenty of Storage
reviews.body: I bought this backpack for my mom, who takes long international flights every other month. She wanted something comfortable to carry on her back with plenty of storage and compartments to keep everything organized. I spent quite a bit of time comparing different brands and styles before choosing this one. There are travel backpacks that cost a couple hundred dollars, but after comparing features, I realized many of them offer the same functionality. This backpack stood out because of its excellent reviews and unbeatable price, and I'm so glad I chose it. My mom absolutely loves it. The backpack has so many compartments that it's easy to organize travel essentials, electronics, documents, snacks, and personal items without everything getting mixed together. It also holds much more than it looks like it can. She packed it with everything she needed for her trip, and it handled it all with ease. The backpack is comfortable to carry, feels well-made, and has held up very well through multiple trips. It's practical, lightweight, and perfect as a carry-on for long flights. One thing to keep in mind is the design. It's simple, practical, and more functional than fashionable. If you're buying it for a younger or teenage daughter who prefers trendy or stylish backpacks, this may not be the most appealing option. However, for anyone who values organization, comfort, and functionality over looks, it's an excellent choice. Overall, this has been an outstanding purchase. In my opinion, there's no need to spend two or three times more on a travel backpack when this one delivers everything you need at such an affordable price. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for great quality and exceptional value.

reviews.title: Best Travel Personal Item
reviews.body: This may be one of the best travel purchases I've made in years. I bought it to use as my airline personal item for a business trip, and it made traveling incredibly easy. The bag fit perfectly under the airplane seat while holding my leather work backpack, a small purse, my medications, TSA liquids bag, and both my work and personal laptops. The padded laptop compartment kept my electronics secure, and I appreciated having a dedicated protected area instead of everything shifting around inside the bag. This bag really shines for airport travel. Going through TSA was quick and stress-free because my liquids and electronics were easy to access without unpacking the entire bag. The pocket layout is extremely well thought out. Once I arrived at my destination, I simply removed my work backpack and left this bag in the hotel. It was the perfect travel organizer and protected my nicer leather backpack during the trip. It's lightweight, comfortable to carry, surprisingly spacious, and exceptionally functional. For the price, I honestly couldn't believe how well it performed. I would absolutely buy it again and highly recommend it to anyone looking for an affordable, well-designed travel bag.

reviews.title: The carry-on personal backpack/item that almost made me enjoy flying!!
reviews.body: I absolutely LOVE this backpack! After taking it on my trip, I can confidently say it earned a permanent spot in my travel lineup. The number of pockets is fantastic. I had a place for everything without digging around like I was on an archaeological expedition. The top handles made it easy to grab, and I especially loved that I could wear it as a backpack while navigating the airport. My shoulders were very thankful. I flew American Airlines, and it fit perfectly under the seat in front of me. The photos are from Main Cabin (not First Class), where I had just a little extra legroom. On my return flight, I was in standard coach, and it still fit under the seat just fine. The only difference was that, when I had the bag packed to the brim, it was a little harder to slide out and access things during the flight. My only tip: Pack anything you’ll want during the flight (headphones, snacks, charger, Kindle, etc.) right at the very top of the bag. Once it’s tucked under the seat and fully loaded, you probably won’t want to go spelunking for that granola bar hiding at the bottom. Overall, this backpack exceeded my expectations. It’s roomy, comfortable, TSA-friendly, and fit exactly as advertised. If you’re looking for a personal item that maximizes space without looking enormous, this one is a winner. I would absolutely recommend buying! ✈️🎒

reviews.title: Quality made, plenty of room, easy to carry travel backpack. Durable. Classy looking.
reviews.body: UPDATE: 7/26 I just received a second bag that I ordered after traveling with the black one. I bought the cream with tan accents. Looks high end. It’s amazing that this isn’t priced higher. I’ve put the black one through three trips with zero issues, tons of storage, and still easy to carry as a back pack with the convenience of the handle for lifting and the sleeve for sliding onto luggage handle. I see buying these for Xmas gifts. I’ve waited to review until actually traveling with it. The material is a good heavy nylon blend. Keeps the bag lightweight before filling it up. Good 4” depth in the packing compartment. Comes with waterproof shoe bag. Lid side has two zipper permed compartments that are a perfect size each for holding make up etc, and anything that might leak or is wet. External pocket is generous. I put my ipad, kindle and a journal in there with other misc items with plenty of room. Also helped to ‘square out’ the bag. The cinching clips on the side are basically useless, they don’t tighten down the bag. Packed full of women’s 4 days worth of clothing and accessories and it still fit under the airplane’s seat. Got a bit heavy to carry, but that was to be expected. Shoulders are comfortable padded. Only negative is the lack of a chest strap with clip. With the length of the bag, it would have been appreciated on my 5 foot frame. Straps were also a bit long even adjusting to the shortest point. Again I’m 5 foot, but could have use another 2” of shortening area. Packed enough in this backpack to replace my carry on hard case bag. 10 0f 10.

reviews.title: Mochila cool 🥳
reviews.body: Perfecta. Llevo 3 meses usando la mochila y hasta ahora ha sido mi mejor compra. Es bastante espaciosa, ideal si llevas muchos libros y mucho más si eres de llevar artículos extra para cualquier emergencia, como yo, ya que los bolsillos también cuentan con bastante espacio. Le cabe perfectamente una laptop de 16 pulgadas (quizá hasta un poquito más, como 16.7), yo le meto mi laptop de 16" y una tableta grandota en el compartimento para laptop, ambas caben perfecto. No se ensucia fácilmente (pedí el color negro, los otros colores no sé), y si sabes acomodar tus cosas no te verás como repartidor de rappi, jajaja. Cabe aclarar que se siente que es de material de buena calidad, la he llenado entera de cosas y es bastante resistente, no se siente como si la correa se fuera a romper en cualquier momento por el peso. No cuento con fotos de la mochila, pero se ve exactamente igual a la foto. 🙃 Espero te sirva mi reseña, tuve mis dudas al comprar la mochila ya que en Amazon no suelen haber buenas reseñas, pero hasta ahora todo perfecto. Gracias por leer hasta aquí.👍
reviews.body_en: Perfect. I have been using the backpack for 3 months and it has been my best purchase so far. It is quite spacious, ideal if you carry a lot of books and much more if you like to carry extra items for any emergency, like me, since the pockets also have plenty of space. It fits a 16-inch laptop perfectly (maybe even a little more, like 16.7), I put my 16" laptop and a large tablet in the laptop compartment, both fit perfectly. It doesn't get dirty easily (I ordered the black color, I don't know about the other colors), and if you know how to organize your things you won't look like a rappi deliveryman, hahaha. It should be noted that it feels like it is made of good quality material, I have filled it completely with things and it is quite sturdy, it doesn't feel like the strap is going to break at any moment due to the weight. I don't have photos of the backpack, but it looks exactly the same as the photo. I hope my review helps you, I had my doubts when buying the backpack since there aren't usually good reviews on Amazon, but so far so good. Thank you for reading this far.

reviews.title: Great slim bag with a weird laptop holder
reviews.body: I spent more time than I would care to admit looking for a solid backpack, but good ones are expensive and I didn't feel like buying a few to try then return. I wanted a backpack for my office job to carry my tablet, laptop, work binders/folders, blender shaker bottles, and small knick-knacks to and from work and between different offices. These were my requirements: - Holds my laptop in a sleeve (preferably padded/protected) - Tablet sleeve big enough to hold my Kindle Scribe Colorsoft - Stylish and slim with plenty of room - Good quality without breaking the bank - Side water bottle cup holders with straps to hold down my insulated blender bottle shakers - Plenty of pockets for smaller items (gum, chargers, charging blocks, pens, etc.) - Something I could use for an overnight or couple day trip I hated it for the first 20 minutes I owned it because I thought it did not have a general large interior compartment area with folder dividers as shown in the product images. However, I quickly realized the zipper track blended in too well with the bag and I simply missed it (it's right in front of the larger top handle). This backpack nailed it. Even the tablet compartment hold my kindle scribe securely, though I'll likely only use that when traveling as it's a tad too snug. The only thing I don't care for is how the laptop compartment is only a side entrance zip and the "sleeve" is a plush arm that secures the laptop in place with velcro that you have to remove and reattach every time you move your laptop in it. That seems a bit odd and is slightly tedious to do, but I assume it's for easy access; they should really include that in the pictures of the product. Also, I understand that the backpack essentially zips in half to open up 180 degrees for quick airport security laptop checks, but I almost never fly, so that may be useless to me. I've read other reviews that claim the bag opens up on its own because of this feature. I've only had it a week so far but that hasn't happened to me yet and I don't see how it would unless the bag was packed full and only partially zipped shut. Overall I love this bag, it meets all of my requirements and then some. It also redistributes the weight well due to its longer size, so more weight in the bag somewhat feels like less. Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Excellent bag for daily coummute and, likely, travel if you need
reviews.body: My work laptop was upgraded from a 15" to a 17" model which just wouldn't fit in my current SwissGear pack which I've had for over a decade. The brand is high quality, well produced, and durable. Never had an issue with my current one that I've used both for my work commute and travel, so when it came time to look for something that could carry the new laptop, I looked to SwissGear. The only real issue I had was the pocket arragnement having an exclusive laptop carry section to make travel through TSA checkpoints easier, but as I don't intend to take my worklaptop on trips (vacation) I didn't need that - but all their existing bags are designed this way it seems. No biggie as there's ample room in the bag for the stuff I noramally carry to/from work and added side pockets are nice as are the very well padded straps and back. Highly recommennd the brand as a whole.

reviews.title: Great bag! Great value! But not water proof if that’s important to you
reviews.body: It’s exactly what’s advertised. Great bag, holds more than you think it should, sturdy, comfy, can be a professional work laptop bag or a day hikers bag at the same time. Why only 4 stars? It’s not particularly water proof. Got caught in the rain walking to my car and even with an umbrella, the bag got a little damp. When I got home, the insides weren’t soaking wet or anything, but the inside fabric was damp and in contact with my stuff. To be fair, this bag was not advertised as water proof… there is no deception here. And for the price, it’s still a great buy… but the speed at which water got in the bag is a big negative.

reviews.title: What is your backpack purpose? Repeat customer for Swissgear products
reviews.body: This is my favorite brand of computer backpack. My household has been using this brand for over 20 years. For many years they were used daily. The inner liner on the tiny pocket of my previous 20 year old backpack finally tore so I purchase this one as a replacement. Mainly used for travel and anyplace I have to tote a laptop too. So far, things are going well. I will update if that changes. Material and workmanship: Sturdy and quality. I understand sometimes there can be defects and I would hope they stand by their warranty. So far all is good. Size: This is a good size. Small enough to fit under an airline seat, big enough to hold the essentials. I use mainly for all types of travel. I can fit a change of clothes, medications, umbrella, bose headphones, airpods, water bottle, snacks, wipes, tissues, etc. I travel with a macbook air always and sometimes a heavy lenovo laptop. It holds both. Pockets and design: This is a slightly different design than my last one. I went with this one because it was on sale. For the overall purpose ( to haul all my stuff around,) it serves the purpose. I kinda wish I spent a little more and got the similar model I had before. -The laptop compartment has a padded velcro adjustable strap. I do not know if this is necessary but it is there. It is removable. Compartment is roomy enough to hold 2 laptops. This compartment only has a "one side" zipper. It does not zip all the way around. I found this a little annoying since my last one had a zip around. I am sure I will adjust to it but I prefer to pull my laptop out of the top instead of out the side. The downfall of one zipper, you can not zip tie or put a lock on the zippers. Depending on where we were traveling, we would zip tie the zippers. It does have a tiny pocket on the top. Not quite sure what I would use that for. - Next compartment for a tablet. It is padded around the sides and has mesh in the middle. This one unzips all the way around. TSA friendly design. Have not tried this out with two laptops yet so I don't know how that will go with tsa. The tablet pocket is small so maybe ipad mini size? The ipad pro would not fit. They could have designed this to be bigger. I was thinking of getting a laptop sleeve and using this compartment for my macbook air when I travel with 2 laptops. - main compartment: has a mini pocket for phone but I use for my airpods. Has a divider for books, papers or whatever. I actually use it for wipes. Can fit a change of clothes in a packing cube, medications, headphones, snacks and everything I need. There is a mesh zipper pouch on the top. This is great for cords or whatever. - top front pocket- I have a love hate relationship with this one. Easy to empty your pockets and phone into when going through tsa but a pain to get stuff back out. You have to dig around a little. I will probably need to separate things in little bags to make this pocket work for my needs. I miss having a small top pocket for things like chapstick and eye drops. Making two pockets, iphone sized and a small one for little things, would have been my ideal solution. - bottom front pocket: this one is fine. Big enough for epipen, inhaler, key hook, hand sanitizer, tissues, gum, some toiletries, misc stuff. Also has some loops on outer part of pocket. - side zipper pockets: there are small size zipper pockets on each side that are deep. These are ok. Weird shape. Can fit a small umbrella or a standard plastic water bottle. Space for other things but I don't have that many skinny long things going in a backpack. Pocket is deep so if you wanted to put money or something way down at the bottom of this pocket, this would be hard for anyone to just grab out of your bag. You can not fit a water bottle or similar item in the mesh pockets on the outside of these ones if there is stuff in the pockets. - mesh stretchy water bottle pockets: The pockets are a little small. These can hold a smaller sized water bottle. There is a strap to help secure. It would be better if there was a loop at the top to hook a carabiner on it, to secure a water bottle. I have lost a water bottle before out of this pocket. Sometimes I use the strap to tie a sweatshirt or raincoat to it. Backpack Straps: padded, thick work well. Have a few loops for whatever. Back is padded enough. Comfortable enough to carry around for a few hours. Overall, a good backpack. When shopping for a backpack, think of your purpose and what you want to put in it. Does it have the right sized pockets for your needs? The price was right for this one and I will use it until it breaks.

reviews.body_en: I came across this SwissGear backpack at De Gaulle Airport and this is my fourth one. My first impression was that I could easily fit a 17" Mac bag on my back. I also bought some more expensive bags along the way, but I ended up hating them as soon as I carried them on my back. This manufacturer's bag is by far the most comfortable to carry on my back. When I carry it on my back, this is the only one that fits comfortably on my back. This is due to the Shoulder strap system and Airflow back system. I was convinced that this manufacturer was the only one that would suit me.However, I don't like that it's too big and falls forward when I put it on the floor.Well, I guess it can't be helped.

The main compartment is spacious enough for books, folders, and everyday essentials, while the dedicated laptop compartment is padded and keeps the laptop secure and separate from other items, which gives extra peace of mind when carrying it around. The ergonomic shoulder straps are cushioned and comfortable even after wearing the bag for extended periods, and the weight is distributed well so it doesn't dig into the shoulders. Overall, this is a well-made, functional, and good-looking backpack that combines style with practicality. It's great for school, work, or travel, and I'd definitely recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable bag with good organization and a nice aesthetic.

reviews.title: Big and spacious
reviews.body: If you’re looking for a backpack that can handle everything, this JanSport Big Laptop Backpack is definitely worth checking out. What I love most is the amount of space. It has two large main compartments, a dedicated padded sleeve that fits up to a 15-inch laptop, plus multiple front pockets to keep all of your smaller essentials organized. There’s even a side pocket for your water bottle, so everything has its place. The quality is good, and it’s made with durable recycled materials that feel sturdy for everyday use, whether you’re heading to school, college, work, or traveling. The ergonomic S-curve shoulder straps and fully padded back panel also make it comfortable to wear, even when it’s packed full. One thing I am a little concerned about is the weight limit. Since this isn’t made from the thick, heavy-duty material of the original classic JanSport backpacks, I’m not sure how well it would hold up if you constantly overload it with very heavy books or gear. For everyday essentials like a laptop, notebooks, and personal items, it should be perfectly fine, but I probably wouldn’t recommend stuffing it with excessive weight on a regular basis. Overall, if you need a spacious, comfortable, and well-organized backpack for everyday use, I think this is a great option. And with over 35 colors and patterns available, there’s a style for just about everyone. You can find it linked right here on my Amazon storefront.

reviews.title: Excellent quality stitching and materials
reviews.body: I've been using this backpack for months now and it is very sturdy & well-made, and has very high quality stitching and materials. The shoulder padding works nicely. The side pouches for holding water bottles are perfect for traditional single serve bottles of water. It is not big enough for a large thermos-type water containers. I bet I could slide my little umbrella in it as well. It's very handy. The exterior pouch is large and very utilitarian. It doesn't have a bunch of smaller dividers and zippers, which I like. I just dump my small stuff in there. I cannot comment on the laptop sleeve part of the interior as I have not used it for that purpose. But I do find the pocket useful for other things. I can easily fit a two inch binder into the main compartment sideways. (Two inch is pretty large, not your standard size binder.) I've never tried putting two in there, but I bet it they would fit. All in all, a very good backpack. There are no cons to this backpack.

reviews.title: Great productivity monitors with fantastic value
reviews.body: Never heard of the brand, price too good to be true, so risked buying one, then bought another one. These replaced my dual Samsung 27 inch Viewfinity S80D 4K IPS. My review is from my experience after a few weeks using these as external monitors for my macbook pro. First, the cons: 1. Noticeable IPS glow, poor viewing angle, bad HDR compared to S8 (although S8 wasn't stellar with its HDR). 2. Poor out of the box colors for both monitors, need calibration. 3. Subpar build quality, not robust, cheap feeling plastic indentations for monitor settings located on the back, screen can bend so must handle with care even when taking it out of the box, whereas S8 was a tank. 4. Basic monitor stand, only horizontal orientation, whereas S8s monitor stand was robust and could rotate to vertical. 5. As other reviewers mentioned, VESA 75 mount is not located in the center of the monitor, but at the lower half, making vertical orientation tricky, but more on that below. 6. S8 brightness could be controlled by macOS keyboard's brightness keys, these cannot. With those issues you might wonder why I am giving this 5 stars. That will depend on what you are looking for in a monitor. I use these for work, and these are the pros that made me get two and replace my S8s: 1. Increased vertical size due to 3:2 aspect ratio feels significant for me. One in horizontal orientation, the other vertical, feels extremely spacious for reading and coding. 2. Very light weight and very thin, which means easily supported by my VESA monitor arms, and I'm able to adjust these to the back edge of my desk without any fear of it falling or tipping over my monitor arms set up, increasing distance to the screen, significantly reducing eye strain. The default monitor stand, although basic, does not take up any room, has very little depth compared to the S8, so even without monitor arms, you can push these to the very edge of your desk, way further than my S8 with its large monitor stand. 3. Guessing due to its light weight, these do not shake at all when I'm typing. Zero shake with the stand or attached to monitor arms, whereas my S8s shook all the time when I typed on my keyboard with their default robust monitor stands. This is by far the most important factor for me, since I'm typing the whole day. 4. The text is very sharp and crisp, which reduces eye strain for those working with text a lot like I do. 5. I appreciate the minimal, light weight, slim, and bezel-less design. You are just paying for two large and crisp panels, nothing more (just pretend the speakers aren't there). I was eyeing BenQ's 28 inch "programming" monitor before, but didn't buy it because it was too thick, comes loaded with unnecessary software and a ring light, weighs 3x more, and costs 4x more. Neither pro or con, just notes having used these for two weeks: 1. Factory colors leaning towards red with too much glow, turn black boost in setting to zero, set to RGB, and use software calibration. With macOS screen calibration I got these pretty close to my S8, and fairly close to my macbook pro's screen. It doesn't hold up to a LG OLED for movies, but these beats the LG OLED for work. 2. My initial concern with poor viewing angle becomes almost a non issue as I pushed these to the back edge of my desk with my monitor arms. 3. The matte coating is above average, not as good as my S8, but I work in very bright room and these are perfectly fine for both light and dark modes. 4. Despite the fact that the VESA mount is way off center, these are so lightweight, you won't find any issues rotating these to vertical and keeping it that way provided you have a solid VESA monitor arm. A VESA monitor desk stand probably won't work without an bracket extension. 5. I'm assuming these are not thunderbolt, because I could not enable daisy chaining with my macbook pro despite having 2x DP ports per monitor. I ended up using a DP for one, and HDMI for the other. The DP enables 60hz, HDMI is only 50hz, but I can't tell the difference when I'm working. No noticeable latency. For the price and my use case, this is a 5/5.

reviews.title: Fantastic productivity monitor for the money. One downside: max brightness
reviews.body: This is for the 28-inch 4K+ 3840x2560p monitor. Raw score: 4 stars Value for money: 5 stars Rounding up to 5 stars overall Setup hint: there is a stupid gamer-oriented setting called "black boost", and by default it is set to 5/10. TURN IT OFF. When on, the colors all look washed out and low contrast. This is NOT a gaming monitor. When "black boost" is turned off (set to zero), contrast is just fine. Not earth-shattering, but perfectly adequate for productivity (I do coding and research on mine). Note: screen sizes are misleading! This is a 28" 3:2 aspect ratio monitor. It has 18% more area than a conventional 27" 16:9 monitor - same width, 2.4" taller! The display area is even 1/4" taller than a typical 32" monitor (which is usually actually 31.5" diagonally), but 4" narrower. For productivity, I prefer the layout of two of these over two 27" or 32" 16:9 monitors. I am using a pair of these with a docking station for a MacBook Pro. They don't have USB-C input, don't charge your notebook, and don't daisy chain like $1000+ displays. But they cost a SMALL fraction of the cost too. I actually replaced my mid-grade LG 4K 27" display with these. The image quality is roughly on par, and the anti-reflective surface is better in my visually noisy environment. I'm actually perfectly happy to use these instead of my 5K LG monitors attached to my other desktop Mac. There is effectively only one significant downside. They have only a maximum brightness of 270 nits (aka cd/mm^2 or candela per square millimeter). Typical high-quality monitors have maximum brightness of 400-500 nits or more. In practice, 270 nits is enough. In my brightly-lit room, I keep these at 100% brightness. However, in a few years, as the backlight wears, these will definitely get dimmer. Even LED backlights fade over time. Keep that in mind. Still, for the next few years, I expect to be extremely happy with the quality of these. They will become my roughly 50% daily drivers (my LG 5K the other 50%). Other minor nits: The build quality is meh. They have small bezels (about 1/4" top and sides, 5/8" bottom). They have an odd 75mm VESA pattern and it's at the bottom, so they fit oddly on monitor arms. The inputs point down and are so close to the bottom that you essentially can't avoid seeing the cables stick out the bottom of the monitor. They have cheap wall-wart power supplies. The logo on the bezel and during power-up is ugly and looks cheap. But, well, it IS cheap, in a good way. The stand is pretty pathetic, and if you tip it at all, it will scratch your desk. These advertise HDR capability, but ignore it... it's worse than useless on these monitors. They are physically incapable of emitting enough brightness for HDR.

reviews.title: For the money, I don't know how I could be any happier.
reviews.body: 28 Inch 3840x2560p display. I replaced a 32" 4k monitor with this. It doesn't sound like the extra vertical resolution is all that much, but it's VERY noticeable in real life. I feel like I can get so much more "stuff" on screen at once, or I can view long chunks of text without scrolling. Plus, the slightly smaller screen fits my desk better, and means I can see everything at a glance instead of feeling like I have to "look around" to see the whole screen. It really seems like this must be using the exact same panel as the "BenQ RD280U 28.2” 4K 3840x2560 3:2 Programming Monitor" that sells for $600! I have no dead or stuck pixels, the backlighting is reasonably bright, and text looks great on either light or dark backgrounds. Really, this monitor gives you such a great display for such a small amount of money I feel like I stole it! Of course the rest of the package is the cheapest possible plastic and pot metal. Nothing about it feels premium, and apparently there is a speaker, but I don't know why they bothered as it's completely useless. Just like with the 3:2 BENQ monitor, you have to use DisplayPort (not HDMI) to get 60hz at full resolution, but it has two, separate DisplayPort connections (along with 2 more HDMI ports), so I had no problem hooking it up. It works fine with an M1 Pro Mac, a Dell laptop using a Dell dock, and a desktop PC, all using DisplayPort. For this price, the only complaint I have is that my desk isn't big enough for me to buy another one! I'd been complaining that there aren't enough 3:2 monitor options. I guess you really don't need a lot of options when you can get one this good for this cheap!

reviews.title: Not as good as the BenQ
reviews.body: I own the BenQ version of this and I was hoping this would be close enough that I could replace all of my monitors with it. It most likely is the same LCD panel as the BenQ, but the backlight is nowhere near as good. The monitor's hue is very warm and it's hard to find a setting that doesn't look muddy. It is much less bright which limits how much you can change the other settings because you don't have much headroom. The matte coating is also much less effective. The BenQ softens reflections and diffuses background light. This is a matte screen too but bright lights are much easier to see and the background light causes a general haze on it that the BenQ doesn't have. That said, the resolution is great. 4K+ at 60hz works fine on display port. The sound is bad, but that's not critical. The build quality is low, I see foam padding sticking out between the bezel and the panel. The input placement is horrible and you'd need to use right angle adapters to not have visible cables since the put the connectors so close to the bottom edge. The VESA mount is also really low, but these are resolvable issues. Every corner was cut to bring this screen down to this price point. I'm unsure who this is targeted at. The BenQ is 5x the price, Gawfolk should have made this a bit nicer than this but still cheaper than the BenQ. They could have sold this for twice the price if it was a real alternative to the BenQ. This screen aspect ratio and resolution is premium, so I don't know why they decided to make a low end budget monitor out of it. If you plan to use this in a bright room I'd skip it. If you plan on coding with this 10 hours a day, I would skip it. If you want to have the color and brightness match your other monitors, I would skip it. If you have a creative need for this aspect ratio and resolution, its a dope monitor at a rock bottom price with no reasonable priced alternative and I would recommend it. But I'm returning it and buying another BenQ, which I consider the best productivity monitor on the market.

The BenQ is 5x the price, Gawfolk should have made this a bit nicer than this but still cheaper than the BenQ. They could have sold this for twice the price if it was a real alternative to the BenQ. This screen aspect ratio and resolution is premium, so I don't know why they decided to make a low end budget monitor out of it. If you plan to use this in a bright room I'd skip it. If you plan on coding with this 10 hours a day, I would skip it. If you want to have the color and brightness match your other monitors, I would skip it. If you have a creative need for this aspect ratio and resolution, its a dope monitor at a rock bottom price with no reasonable priced alternative and I would recommend it. But I'm returning it and buying another BenQ, which I consider the best productivity monitor on the market.

reviews.title: Crystal Clear Display
reviews.body: I am very pleased with this monitor, it has a beautiful crystal clear display. I'm using 4k wallpaper and it is really beautiful and detailed on this screen. The screen size is something I like too. I chose the 28" monitor which gives me plenty of viewing area without occupying my entire desk. The height of the screen is another feature I personally like. It is a taller screen rather than one that is short and long. You get a couple of inches in height that most screens don't offer. I'm talking about the screen itself, not a taller stand. It was easy to put together and took less than 5 minutes. The stand is metal not plastic, which I really like. It attaches on the back, then slides in place. One screw is all it takes to add the feet to the stand. The tilt feature doesn't work so great. It seems tight and I don't want to apply force for fear of breaking the screen. Even though I wish the tilt feature worked better, it isn't enough for me to knock off a star. I'm satisfied with it's position and will leave that as is. There is not much of a frame, it's mostly screen rather than large strips of plastic running around the outside. The only drawback is not having much area for safely carrying or moving the thing. Your gripping area is carefully holding the bottom of the screen. It's lightweight so it isn't too awkward. Another thing worth mentioning is that the price is extremely reasonable for such a nice picture. So far, I'm glad I went for this one, it's a pleasure to look at every time I'm at my desk .

reviews.title: Great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160)
reviews.body: Bought two of them. They arrived last night. Spent far too much time testing them. Summary: great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra width. Huge pro: the resolution. Those extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160) are incredible for usability, either in portrait mode or landscape. Even at 200% scaling (to avoid blurry text caused by the rendering that Windows 10/11 has at anything other than 100%/200%/300% because DPI scaling in Windows 10/11 is atrocious. So in landscape mode, I can see two pages, even at 200%. The portrait mode allows me to have very usable, larger text, fitting a page & the header of the next page. Very clear text. Ahhhh..... Huge Pro: has DC dimming, not PWM. That's critical for my eye strain. I cannot use PWM because my eyes tire quickly. I don't have a physical device, but the app that I use says that the flickering is very low (below 5%). I don't notice anything, in any event. Pro: supports FreeSync, which means G-Sync worked for me on my ancient 1060 card. YMMV, I guess. Pro: slightly above average contrast ratio (for an IPS) of 1,200 to 1. Pro: supports DCR. Probably not a higher end implementation, of course. Pro: has a blue light mode. I don't use that, because I prefer using software for that. Con: the stand is perfunctory. I put it on a $30 stand that I previously bought for another monitor. The 75x75 VESA mounting holes are at the bottom of the panel, which means it works well for landscape but do not work for portrait without significant effort (the monitor in portrait mode is also on a custom stand and to offset the sag caused by the mounting hole placement, I have a small shipping box propped under the sagging side, with more cardboard as spacers to level the monitor. Update: I fixed the sagging by buying two VESA adapters (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0741CFJVW), which allows the monitor to be very close to the center of the monitor stand. Con: although the display is IPS, the panel's viewing angle is not that great. Even looking at it straight on, the right side of the landscape and the right side of the portrait mode monitor are washed out. Think of this as poor man's BenQ RD280U. I don't know if it's the same panel, btw, just the same resolution, contrast ratio, and both have a matte finish. This has 120% sRGB; the BenQ has 100% sRGB. Perhaps this is a prior iteration of the panel used in the BenQ (the BOE MV282CVB-N11). Perhaps it is uses the BOE MV282CVB-N10. I don't know, though as software does not show the panel manufacturer (other than the Gawfolk model, GF005. Small Con: HDMI does not run at 60 hz. But the two DP ports are 1.4 and can easily handle 60 hz. I'm now very tempted to buy another set for my office at work.

reviews.title: Monitor's great! Maybe some of the accessories could use some work.
reviews.body: I really like this monitor. I've been using 1080p as my native resolution since college (back in 2008 at least) so going to 1440p is the first resolution upgrade I've done in over 15 years. I originally had ordered a pair of 1440s from LG but after reading some remarks about the dynamic contrast being locked I bailed on those and ordered these, despite never having ever bought anything from KTC before. This monitor seems to satisfy everything I wanted to accomplish the jump (a larger screen space over 27" to accommodate the increase in pixels while also supporting the higher refresh rate and VESA AdaptiveSync features of my 27" gaming monitors). The monitor is also brighter than I was expecting. 1440p at 32" has a denser PPI than 1080p at 27", meaning text looks cleaner on this monitor than the 27" displays I was using (I've been told that at 32", 1440p is more comparable to using 1080p on a 24" canvas in terms of PPI). The default color temp is maybe a bit on the cool side but it can be adjusted (the default for "User" seems to suit me). I ordered two of these, one for each of my gaming setups, and neither of them have any dead pixels. The description says "165 Hz" but in actuality I managed to run this thing at 180 Hz (which means it's a 165 Hz panel overclocked). I notice the thumbnail for the product says "180 Hz" so go by that. If I had to complain about anything I'd say the accessories leave a little more to be desired. The base is one of those three-point things that looks cool but creates some awkward situations with your keyboard if you have to put the monitor directly onto the desk where your keyboard lives. It takes up less space than I was expecting but I still think I might go for a flatter base. However more importantly the base isn't height-adjustable, which can create issues if you have to set your monitor on a surface where you might want it lower or higher to meet your eye level (it is tilt-adjustable at least, which helps with the desk where I had to put it on a higher ledge). More than the flat base I think this is what would motivate me to get an aftermarket stand solution. Furthermore the complaints about the short DisplayPort cable in the box are indeed correct. For my setups this isn't an issue, they can reach the port without difficulty, but you definitely may need to consider buying longer cables to handle that if your PC isn't directly below your monitor like mine is. Additionally I'd like to say the cable connecting the power brick to the monitor is also really short. There's a decent chance yours could end up dangling if it can't reach the floor from your desk, even if the cable you run from the plug to the brick isn't short.

reviews.title: a good budget-friendly monitor
reviews.body: I bought this during a pre-Black Friday sale: an Amazon "Lightening Deal" combined with a KTC coupon that dropped the price well below $200. So, my positive response to the H32S17 is partly based on the big discount I got for my purchase. The monitor is the advertised 32 inch width. The bezels are very small, about 2 mm; however, the panel has a small, black border, which is never utilized. So the border around the display area extends another 5 mm around the left, right, and top. So, the max viewing area, measured by the diagonal corners is 31.5 inches. The build quality is solid plastic for the monitor, and the monitor base does use metal. I can't speak to the amount of adjustment the monitor has on its base since I have mine on a 3rd-party VESA mount. The 1500R curvature is very gentle. I use the monitor up close and viewing content from a distance up to 10 feet away, and the curvature isn't annoying. Be aware, since the panel is a VA, the viewing angles aren't as wide as with an IPS or OLED panel. But there is some viewing angle, especially if you are viewing content from a bigger distance. You don't need to be directly dead center in front of the monitor to get a good viewing experience. The out-of-the-box calibration of H32S17 is not good. You will have to adjust such things like the color hue, saturation, gamma, brightness, and contrast to fit your environment. Some have complained that VA panels aren't very bright. I'm happy with the brightness of this monitor. I never have the brightness maxed out, and I often lower it to 85 - 75% depending on what I'm watching and how dark my office is at any given time. When I finally got it adjusted, the display is vibrant with good color saturation and deep blacks. This wasn't clear when I researched the monitor, so I will confirm that the H32S17 has an overdrive mode that has 4 different speeds. I currently have it on the highest speed, but all the levels do influence the gray-to-gray response times differently. So, this monitor, like any VA, will have some black smearing, but the overdrive, plus the high refresh rate, will mitigate it some. I'm satisfied with the low level of smearing, but I don't play high-level FPS games where smearing would cause problems. I do use the monitor for productivity. Text clarity is very good, whether reading black text on white backgrounds or white text on black backgrounds. I was a little concerned about that when I bought the monitor, but it has exceeded my expectations in this aspect. If you have a decent PC and GPU that can push high frame rates, I recommend connecting the monitor to your GPU with the display port. With a DP connection, the monitor provides a stable 180 frames, which is even higher than the advertised 165-170 hz. I'm extremely happy with that. Overall, this is a budget-friendly monitor that is good for multiple purposes (viewing content, casual gaming, and productivity). It won't compare to the best IPS and OLED monitors, but, for what I paid, I believe I got a quality product.

reviews.title: Moderately good monitor
reviews.body: The overall design is standard plastic with a fairly thin bevel along the top and sides. It's actually nearly identical to a flat 34" monitor I have from 7 years ago. But it's lightweight. I hardly notice the light from the LED ring on the back of the monitor - it's pretty dim. There seem to be no settings to control the LED light, other than turning it on/off. When waking up from sleep, the monitor takes a full 3-5 seconds to turn on after my laptop is awake. A few times, the KTC monitor did not turn on at all. I had to manually turn the monitor off, then back on. So that's not so great. This was not an issue with the last 34" UHD wide monitor that is about 7 years old (which I still use), so it's not the laptop causing the long lag time in waking up. Stand The stand is sturdy enough to prevent the monitor from being knocked over by accident; however, if the desk shakes, the monitor shakes slightly more than my other 34" that is connected to a desk mount. My main issue with the stand is that it does not lift the monitor very high, only about 6.5 inches between the surface of my desk and the bottom of the stand. So the top 3.5 inches of my laptop obscures the bottom of the KTC monitor. And the laptop covers about half of the length of the monitor. That's quite a lot of monitor being blocked from view, a very annoying situation when working with programs that place controls along the bottom of the screen. Screen / Image Quality I did have to adjust the color, brightness and contrast to get a closer match my laptop, which has a very bright, high-end display. Out of the box, the color and contrast of the KTC monitor appear washed out and too gray to me. After increasing brightness, saturation and contrast, I had to bring the black point down quite a lot to get something that does not appear to have a wash of light gray over the colors. As a result, I find my "Custom" color setting way better than any of the pre-installed color modes offered in the settings menu. Gaming I don't game off this monitor; however, with a Thunderbolt 4 to DisplayPort cable, I'm getting full resolution at full refresh rates. I don't need the high refresh rate, but the monitor deliveries in these aspects. Overall Rating I've had the monitor for less than 2 weeks from the time of writing this review, so perhaps my opinions will change over time. I think this monitor is fairly good for its price range, so I'm giving it 4 out of 5 Stars. If compared to higher end monitors, this would probably be 3 out of 5 for image quality. Also, I purchased during a sale of over 30% off. That put it at about half the price of many other monitors at this level, which is pretty good. Knowing the image quality now, I don't think I would buy this monitor at full price. At a discount, totally worth it. I do a lot of 3D and video editing work, so color and clarity are important, but not essential. This monitor is in no way a monitor that should be used for exact color correcting or color matching. But, for doing things like creating textures for 3D assets, game engine editors, and video editing where perfect color is not so important, then this monitor works well.

So the top 3.5 inches of my laptop obscures the bottom of the KTC monitor. And the laptop covers about half of the length of the monitor. That's quite a lot of monitor being blocked from view, a very annoying situation when working with programs that place controls along the bottom of the screen. Screen / Image Quality I did have to adjust the color, brightness and contrast to get a closer match my laptop, which has a very bright, high-end display. Out of the box, the color and contrast of the KTC monitor appear washed out and too gray to me. After increasing brightness, saturation and contrast, I had to bring the black point down quite a lot to get something that does not appear to have a wash of light gray over the colors. As a result, I find my "Custom" color setting way better than any of the pre-installed color modes offered in the settings menu. Gaming I don't game off this monitor; however, with a Thunderbolt 4 to DisplayPort cable, I'm getting full resolution at full refresh rates. I don't need the high refresh rate, but the monitor deliveries in these aspects. Overall Rating I've had the monitor for less than 2 weeks from the time of writing this review, so perhaps my opinions will change over time. I think this monitor is fairly good for its price range, so I'm giving it 4 out of 5 Stars. If compared to higher end monitors, this would probably be 3 out of 5 for image quality. Also, I purchased during a sale of over 30% off. That put it at about half the price of many other monitors at this level, which is pretty good. Knowing the image quality now, I don't think I would buy this monitor at full price. At a discount, totally worth it. I do a lot of 3D and video editing work, so color and clarity are important, but not essential. This monitor is in no way a monitor that should be used for exact color correcting or color matching. But, for doing things like creating textures for 3D assets, game engine editors, and video editing where perfect color is not so important, then this monitor works well.

reviews.title: Great for the price
reviews.body: I saw a video about this monitor being available for $70 on black Friday pricing. By the time I got around to buying it, it was $85. I bought two of them, and I'm very happy, but there's some caveats I think you should know. This monitor does exactly what it says on the tin... and no more. It has one HDMI and one VGA input (why?) and that's it. It takes in audio via HDMI and has a headphone out jack, and even has volume control on the control nub, but no speakers. It takes 19v power from a barrel jack, but you can swap that for a 20v supply from a USB-C brick with the right adapter (you want the 6.0x4.4mm barrel). The HDR is rubbish, the VRR works fine. The picture quality is plenty good but not remarkable. The settings are pretty minimal and sane out of the box, you'll tweak one or two of them and then never touch them again. The stand is a joke. Of the two of these I bought, one of them was missing the 2 required screws to mount the display to the stand. Fortunately, it has a 100x100mm vesa mount on the back, though it doesn't come with screws for that either. I put mine on monitor arms, and threw out the stands. Basically, if you need a 24" 1080p 120Hz display, and nothing else, of good quality, for as cheap as possible, this is it. For everything else, you'll have to pay more.

reviews.title: Great inexpensive 1080p monitor
reviews.body: There's not much bad to be said about this monitor. It's got great colors with three color adjustment AND six color hue and saturation adjustment. That's crazy to me at this price point. I was able to dial in the colors to where I like them without a problem. I can't get them dead on, but it's very close. It's very green-tinted and over-saturated out of the box, so be prepared for some adjusting. Viewing angles are also good, and it works fine at 120 Hz without any issues on Windows 11. For build quality and other bits, the whole thing feels solid. The stand is made of metal and requires four screws to assemble, but there's almost no wobble. There's also no height adjustment, but it has a 100x100 VESA mount if you want to get a better stand. Audio output for my external speakers is good too, with no audible noise and plenty of volume. The single knob for menu navigation is the one point I'll put against this monitor, as multiple buttons are always better. Knobs are just finicky and annoying to use. If you want a large 1080p monitor with good colors and a higher-than-60 Hz refresh rate, you can't go wrong here.

This is especially useful for photography and content creation, where color matters. 🔹 HDR10 Support While not true high-end HDR, it still enhances brightness and contrast enough to make media look better than standard displays. 🔹 Reader Mode (Eye Comfort) Reader Mode reduces blue light, making it easier on your eyes during long sessions—perfect for work, studying, or late-night editing. 🔹 Clean, Minimal Design Slim bezels and a modern look make it a great fit for multi-monitor setups or a clean desk aesthetic. ⚠️ Things to Consider 🔸 Full HD (1080p) Only At 24 inches, 1080p is decent—but if you're doing heavy photo/video editing, you might eventually want a 1440p or 4K upgrade. 🔸 HDR is Basic HDR10 is nice, but don’t expect premium HDR performance—it’s more of a bonus than a standout feature. 🔸 Built-in Speakers (if included) are average Fine for casual use, but for better sound, external speakers or headphones are recommended. 🎯 Best For Students & teachers (like your setup 👀) Work-from-home setups Dual monitor setups Casual gamers Beginner photographers/editors 💡 Final Verdict If you’re looking for a smooth, reliable, and affordable monitor, the LG 24U411A-B delivers great value. The 120Hz refresh rate and IPS panel really stand out at this price point. 👉 Great entry-level or secondary monitor—especially for productivity and light creative work.

reviews.title: Works fine but ghosting really holds it back
reviews.body: I bought this monitor as a secondary display for my setup, and overall the installation was pretty easy. Everything worked right out of the box, and for general use like YouTube, Discord, or multitasking, it does the job without any major issues. The size is good, and for the price it’s definitely usable if you just need an extra screen. But... there are a few drawbacks I noticed right away. The BIGGEST one is the ghosting. Whenever I drag windows like Discord or scroll through darker content, there’s a visible trail behind moving objects. In games, the motion clarity isn’t very ideal compared to an IPS monitor and darker scenes smear more than I expected. The stand also doesn’t offer much adjustment. The 100Hz refresh rate is nice to have and better than 60Hz and the overall image quality looks okay but just a bit brighter compared to my ASUS monitor. My recommendation for this monitor: use DP and tweak the monitor settings to reduce ghosting. Just keep in mind that because this is a VA panel and some ghosting will always be there it’s part of the panel technology and can’t be fully fixed This monitor is fine as a budget secondary screen but if you’re sensitive to motion blur or want better motion clarity you’ll definitely notice the limitations. It works, but it comes with compromises. If you want completely clean motion with no ghosting Id suggest going with an IPS monitor instead.

reviews.title: equal price to quality but lifespan is < 3 years.
reviews.body: i do not know why there are so many 1 star reviews but here's my take. i had this monitor since november of 2023 and there was nothing really wrong with it, i quite enjoyed it once i adjusted the colors to closely match my oled phone. the colors were imo above average for this price point although i prefer dark rooms and only struggled with glare in the mornings when the sun was low and peeping through windows. however suddenly today in august of 2026 the monitor has stopped functioning suddenly giving it slightly less than a 3 year lifespan in ideal conditions, i even use a special swivel mount to prevent cable damage and the power brick shows that power is being administered correctly meaning the monitor itself has short curcuited. So is it worth it? i don't recall what i paid at the time but at $200 it is not bad price for 3 years, but its also not ecomical and i would recommend it ONLY if you ONLY have $200 and no more at present and really want a 1440p monitor immediately.
