reviews.title: Budget gaming monitor with a high end feel.
reviews.body: Typically, i like to wait a bit before reviewing anything i buy online. But honestly, this KTC monitor impressed me for being a budget option at this price point so I’m going to go ahead and five my thoughts on it. packinng was what you would expect, nothing too fancy. Included was the mount and and stand for the monitor as well as the power cord, an HDMI cable and a DisplayPort cable. The Good: - Picture quality on this monitor is really good. 1440p looks crisp and clear and even downscaling to 1080p, while degrading the image a bit, still doesn’t look overly fuzzy. So if you really wanted to play or use this monitor at 1080p you could. (But being a 1440p monitor, don’t know why you would want to) - there is very very little ghosting with this monitor at stock settings, i found that setting overdrive to low makes the ghosting pretty much go away without reducing image quality at all so that what I’ve kept mine on. I’ve attached a video to try and show an example of what it looks like. - Freesync/ G-Sync works well without issues, there was no flickering at all during gaming at 165hz. Gaming felt smooth and i had no issues with stuttering or response time. Just note, 165hz only works with the DP cable. If you decide to use HDMI, you’ll only be able to go up to 144hz. - Talking about the picture quality, the colors are vibrant without looking overly saturated, the blacks, while not being as dark as you’d see on a VA monitor, are still pretty good. Out of the box, you probably wont need to adjust the settings at all, unless you want really want to. - Speaking of settings, i thought that using one button to essentially control everything would be annoying, but it’s actually pretty easy. Just press the button once to access the menu, and then move it in the direction you want to change whatever settings you want and then press the button again to turn off the menu. The Bad: - the monitor did arrive with some stuck pixels at the bottom right corner of the screen , just above the power button. It wasn’t enough to make me want to return it, as it isn’t noticeable when using the monitor for gaming or when using it for day to day tasks. This is more a QC issue more than anything, so your mileage may vary. I’ve attached a picture of it so you can see it for yourself. - although it doesn’t affect performance at all, the RGB lights on the back of the monitor only have the option to turn it on or off and no setting to change the color to whatever you want. Out of the box, it just changes colors in this slow wave like effect. But this is just me being nit-picky. - HDR on thins monitor is pretty bad, it does increase the brightness a bit if that’s what you’re looking for, but it washes out the colors too much and overall just looks too bright imo without manually changing settings in both the monitor and windows. If you’re looking for a monitor for primarily game in HDR, you might want to look at other options. - this one is me being nit picky again, but the USB port on the back of the monitor doesn’t seem to have functionality, seems its just there to use a USB stick to update firmware or something. I plugged a mouse in there and a USB light strip, the mouse didn’t work at all and only half of the light strip lit up. So while a cool feature, doesn’t seem all that useful. I don’t know, maybe it’s in a firmware update that I haven’t done yet? Ill update this if i’m able to figure out more. UPDATE: the USB port on the back works, i ended up swapping out old parts for new ones and it suddenly started working. I tried a LED strip and a mouse and both worked fine. I don’t know why or how this would interfere with the monitor, but it is what it is. Overall, this monitor is really solid for the price, it comes with decent enough features to make it comparable with other options, but keep in mind it is a budget monitor so you won’t get some of the features here like you’d see with higher end models. But if you’re looking to get a gaming monitor with good image quality, good colors, high refresh rate, a 1ms response time and no ghosting, you’d be hard pressed to find a better monitor at this price point.

reviews.title: Incredible - especially for the price. I took a gamble and hit the jackpot.
reviews.body: This review is for the KTC Gaming Monitor, 27 Inch 1440p 165Hz 144hz Monitor, 2K QHD 1ms GTG Fast IPS Computer Monitor, HDR, HDMI/USB C/DP Vertical Monitor, FreeSync & G-Sync, Swivel Tilt Height Pivot Adjustable, H27T22. First off, several reviewers left inaccurate reviews based on some misunderstandings of this specific monitor, monitors in general, operating system settings, GPU control panel settings, or game settings. I want to correct these inaccuracies so shoppers can make a more informed purchase: 1. The monitor is 27 inches - NOT 24 inches. Monitors are measured diagonally, NOT horizontally. This monitor measures 27 inches diagonally (while it measures 24 inches horizontally). 2. The monitor does have true HDR (not fake HDR), and it has very strong effects, especially when properly configured. Needing to configure HDR is not a limitation of this monitor. It is a fact of life as it relates to HDR. It needs to be configured in the monitor, AND in the Windows operating system (search "Windows HD Color Settings" and turn on "Use HDR" - presumably, if you're using MacOS, it likely also has something similar to this), AND in each specific game which you want to use HDR in. 3. When using HDR, you want to adjust your color, brightness, contrast, black level, gamma, etc. in the GPU control panel (e.g. NVIDIA Control Panel), the Windows OS, search "Color Management" > then click the "Advanced" tab where you'll find a lot of options; and similar in each specific game. I believe a similar function may exist within modern consoles as it relates to turning on HDR, brightness, gamma, etc. in the consoles themselves. This can be adjusted to be easy on the eyes, and even goes far beyond what is needed (i.e. the limitations far exceed the need and therefore do not restrict your ability to adjust it to your liking). Pros: 1. If IPS panels are supposed to have poor black levels, this monitor completely changes this rule. The blacks are pitch black; like a black hole, they are so black. Again, you have to know what you're doing to properly configure things. So if your blacks don't look black, it is a problem with your configuration, NOT the monitor - unless perhaps you got a lemon, but that isn't likely as this company, while new to consumers, has been producing monitor hardware for decades and isn't as new as they seem. 2. The brightness and contrast are extremely well defined. No complaints whatsoever. 3. The HDR truly puts this monitor in an entirely new class of it's own. The level of detail, the dark blacks, the bright whites (to whatever level you adjust them), the contrast, the color vibrancy/saturation - it all looks so amazing, and it is extremely broad in how it can display images, video, and games. The colors are amazing, and can go far beyond what you need, or dialed back if you prefer. 3. The 1 ms response time, the 165Hz refresh rate, the 1440p (2K) resolution, the G-Sync & FreeSync, the incredible viewing angles of 178° both horizontal AND vertical, and fully adjustable height, swivel, tilt, and pivot, all add up to a monitor without any significant weakness compared to other monitors, and many very solid strengths. Con: Only con for me is the bezel is slightly larger than it appears in the pictures, but for a single monitor setup it isn't too noticable. Summary: Overall, just as the title says, after a LOT of research into monitors, I still felt like I was taking a gamble buying this one, yet it truly feels like I hit the jackpot. I HIGHLY recommend this monitor, so get it while it's hot.

reviews.title: Great monitor
reviews.body: Was debating between this and something pricier for a while and honestly really glad I went with this one. 1440p at 200Hz on a 27 inch IPS panel just looks clean. Like genuinely sharp — games look way better than on my old 1080p setup and I noticed the difference immediately out of the box. The 1ms response time is real, no ghosting issues at all even in fast paced games. Motion feels smooth and tight. FreeSync works great too, zero screen tearing which was a problem I dealt with constantly before this. Colors are vibrant without being oversaturated and the IPS panel means the viewing angles are solid. The stand is better than I expected too — height, tilt, swivel, all adjustable which a lot of monitors at this price skip out on. If I had to nitpick, the HDR is decent but nothing crazy, don’t buy this expecting OLED level contrast. And the built in speakers are pretty much nonexistent so use headphones or external audio. But for gaming those aren’t dealbreakers at all. For the price this thing punches way above its weight. QHD and 200Hz for under 250 bucks is hard to argue with. Setup was painless and it’s been running flawless since day one.

reviews.title: This is a nice monitor
reviews.body: Honestly, wasn’t expecting it to be this good. I figured when I started it up that it would be broken considering the horrible packing job that was done. Monitor was just floating in a box four times the size with no packing or anything. The tape was there for decoration essentially. Anyways, it’s so thin and light I was really surprised it’s a really good monitor and for the price it’s great. Better than some monitors I’ve gotten for three times the price. It has basic monitor setting capabilities via the side buttons. Can we talk about the fact it has dedicated buttons and not just that weird stick a lot of companies are switching to? Loved this. It has basic customizable settings for gaming, movies, etc so nothing crazy. Played various games with it and no tracking or anything and THAT was the biggest shocker. It’s a real ips and not a va. I know that shouldn’t be a surprise but you’d be shocked how often some sellers on Amazon do the switch up. One complaint is the fact the company shipped it with a display cable and not an hdmi. Everything is hdmi now. I dont have a port for anything other than an hdmi and if you use an adapter, there’ goes the whole quality standard and reason for using the display cable in the first place. So I had to go out to find an hdmi to even just test the screen which was more of a hassle than I wanted. The cable it came with is going in a drawer to be forgotten forever. Oh and it has built in speakers. They aren’t the best but considering, I was impressed with how big of a performer it is. My last note is the c type port in the monitor is so close to the edge that it’s very hard to find a cable that is thin enough to connect. Picture is included for reference. A lot of the cables I get are chinky c types for durability reasons and none of then were thin enough to connect. I use a docking system for my computing needs which happens to directly use the usb c specifically. So overall, it’s a great monitor. Like really good overall capabilities.

reviews.title: Nice monitor especially for price but imput ports on the bottom, hard to reach from the front
reviews.body: This is a nice monitor. Worked out of the box on FreeBSD (2 machines with a KVM switch). However, if it's on a desk and you can only approach it from the front, it's difficult to connect cables (in my case, HDMI and power cable). I had limited space and have it on a stand on my desk. The desk is against a wall so the only way to reach it is the front. My case may be somewhat of an outlier. My other complaint was the base. They provide screws as well as a magnetic screwdriver, but, in part due to my clumsiness, it was difficult attaching the screws properly and the monitor twice came off the base. This is almost certainly more my fault than Sceptre's, but it seems to me that ever other monitor I've set up was much easier to attach to the base. All of my earlier monitors were smaller though, the largest 32" and that may be a factor. Though I was getting so annoyed I was thinking of a 3 star rating, between the hard to reach ports and the stand, but realized much of that is Just Me(TM). I am not a gamer so I can't speak about that, but it seems good video quality, and on FreeBSD it goes to its default resolution of 3440x1440 @100 with no configuration on my part. This is using a KVM for 2 machines, one with an Nvidia Geoforce GT 1030 and one a Beelink with Cezanne Radeon Vega series VGA) I also didn't use the built in speakers so I can't speak of those, either.

reviews.title: Excellent Budget Monitor for Dedicated Business Use — Know Its Limits
reviews.body: I run multiple monitor setups across my office for different purposes — including writing, business operations, and video production. Not every machine needs a high-end display, and that’s exactly why I picked up this KOORUI 22” monitor. This one is dedicated strictly to my business correspondence system — email, documents, and general communication tasks — running off an Apple M1 Mini. For that purpose, I wanted something affordable, clean, and easy on the eyes for long sessions. This monitor fits that role very well. Text is sharp and easy to read, which is the most important factor for how I’m using it. It’s excellent for writing, reading, and basic graphic placement — but not for critical viewing of those graphics. Color is where you start to see the difference between this and higher-end monitors. It’s a bit washed out and lacks the vibrancy and precision you’ll get from more premium displays. Brightness is moderate, but in this case, that actually works in its favor — it’s very comfortable for extended use without eye fatigue. PROS: * Very affordable for what it delivers * Sharp, clean text — excellent for email and document work * Easy on the eyes for long sessions * Lightweight and simple setup * HDMI and legacy VGA connectivity * VESA compatible for flexible mounting LIMITATIONS: * Colors are somewhat muted — not ideal for photo or video work * Brightness is moderate, not high-impact * Lacks DisplayPort and USB-C connectivity REAL-WORLD USE: As a dedicated communication monitor, this is exactly what I wanted. It does its job without distraction and without the need for expensive features that wouldn’t add any value in this role. However, if your work involves photography, video editing, or anything requiring accurate color and high visual fidelity, this is NOT the monitor for that. BOTTOM LINE: For business use, writing, and communication-focused tasks, this is a strong performer at a very attractive price point. For color-critical work… look elsewhere. This earns a solid FOUR-STAR rating from me — and would have pushed into five stars with more modern connectivity options like DisplayPort or USB-C. Recommended for the right use case. reviews.title: I'm impressed!
reviews.body: I have been using an old Sony 27” non-smart TV as third monitor for my workstation setup. I recently upgraded my CPU by purchasing a Minisforum NAB6 mini PC (highly recommended and better than buying a laptop and a hub to support all your devices), I figured it's time to buy a real monitor. Since I am on a budget, I scoured Amazon reviews for a good monitor and found this Koorui brand. Given the price point ($129.99 on Boxing Day 2023), I am impressed by this monitor. I am not a gamer nor a content creator, but I use this monitor for work applications, streaming, surfing, and some video/photo editing. I like the following: 1) I am satisfied with the brightness and colors of Koorui (rightmost monitor in the attached picture). The larger monitor on the left is 43-inch 4K LG monitor 60Hz with all its fancy features. Koorui held its own against a monitor about 6 times the price when it comes to video streaming. 2) I have been using this monitor for almost a month now and so far, have not encountered any problem at all – no flickering, no dead pixels, no problem with latency, and no dreaded blue screen. 3) Because of the plastic components, it is so lightweight it is almost like a toy, and I mean it in a good way. This means that when I travel and stay in a hotel, instead of bringing my laptop, I could just bring my Minisforum mini PC and Koorui. 4) With my current workstation requiring attention on 3 monitors, Koorui’s viewing angle is ideally suited to my work needs. Adjusting buttons was a pain in the beginning but I got the hang of it, if ever I do need to make re-adjustment, it’s now a piece of cake. The seller was also quick to respond to my inquiry. I thought the unit I purchased came with built-in speaker. The reviews are for different models so make sure the review you read applies to the right size and model of monitor that you are about to purchase. Sure, I can always return the unit to Amazon and have it replaced with the model with built-in speaker. I did not do so because I find it unfair to the seller and Amazon to return something based on the specs that I completely overlooked. Whether it’s for extra or main monitor use, given this price point against branded competitions, this 27-inch 75Hz IPS monitor is a real steal. You won’t regret the purchase – 5 stars.

reviews.title: Más pros que contras
reviews.body: El **KOORUI Gaming Monitor de 24 pulgadas** es una excelente opción para jugadores y usuarios que buscan un monitor asequible pero con características sólidas. Con una resolución Full HD de 1920x1080p y una frecuencia de actualización de 100 Hz, este monitor ofrece una experiencia visual fluida y nítida, ideal para juegos, trabajo o entretenimiento. A continuación, detallo los pros y contras basados en mi experiencia: ### **Pros:** 1. **Calidad de imagen**: La resolución Full HD proporciona colores vibrantes y detalles claros, perfectos para juegos y películas. Además, el modo Eye-Saver reduce la fatiga visual durante largas sesiones de uso. 2. **Frecuencia de actualización de 100 Hz**: Aunque no es tan alta como otros monitores gaming, los 100 Hz ofrecen una experiencia más fluida que los 60 Hz estándar, especialmente en juegos rápidos. 3. **Adaptive Sync**: Esta tecnología ayuda a reducir el tearing y los stutters, lo que mejora la experiencia de juego al sincronizar la tasa de refresco del monitor con la tarjeta gráfica. 4. **Diseño ergonómico**: El soporte ajustable permite inclinar el monitor para encontrar el ángulo perfecto, lo que es ideal para largas sesiones de trabajo o gaming. 5. **Altavoces incorporados**: Aunque no son de alta fidelidad, los altavoces integrados son útiles para quienes no quieren invertir en parlantes externos. 6. **Montaje VESA**: El soporte VESA de 75x75 mm permite montar el monitor en pared o en un brazo articulado, lo que añade versatilidad a su colocación. ### **Contras:** 1. **Frecuencia de actualización limitada**: Aunque 100 Hz es una mejora respecto a los 60 Hz, los jugadores más exigentes podrían preferir monitores con 144 Hz o más. 2. **Altavoces básicos**: Los altavoces integrados son funcionales, pero no ofrecen un sonido de alta calidad. Para una experiencia auditiva óptima, se recomienda usar auriculares o parlantes externos. 3. **Ajustes limitados**: Aunque incluye inclinación, no tiene ajuste de altura, giro o pivot, lo que podría ser una limitación para algunos usuarios. 4. **Brillo máximo**: El brillo podría ser un poco bajo en ambientes muy iluminados, lo que afecta la visibilidad en ciertas condiciones. ### **Conclusión:** El **KOORUI Gaming Monitor de 24 pulgadas** es una excelente opción para quienes buscan un monitor económico pero con características gaming. Su resolución Full HD, frecuencia de actualización de 100 Hz y tecnología Adaptive Sync lo hacen ideal para jugadores casuales. Sin embargo, los usuarios más exigentes podrían echar de menos una mayor frecuencia de actualización y ajustes ergonómicos adicionales. En general, es una gran compra por su relación calidad-precio. ¡Recomendado para quienes buscan un monitor versátil y funcional!
reviews.body_en: The **KOORUI 24-inch Gaming Monitor** is a great option for gamers and users looking for an affordable monitor but with solid features. With a Full HD resolution of 1920x1080p and a refresh rate of 100 Hz, this monitor offers a smooth and sharp visual experience, ideal for gaming, work or entertainment. Below I detail the pros and cons based on my experience: ### **Pros:** 1. **Image Quality**: Full HD resolution provides vibrant colors and clear details, perfect for games and movies. Additionally, Eye-Saver mode reduces eye strain during long usage sessions. 2. **100 Hz refresh rate**: Although not as high as other gaming monitors, 100 Hz offers a smoother experience than the standard 60 Hz, especially in fast games. 3. **Adaptive Sync**: This technology helps reduce tearing and stuttering, which improves the gaming experience by synchronizing the refresh rate of the monitor with the graphics card. 4. **Ergonomic design**: The adjustable stand allows you to tilt the monitor to find the perfect angle, which is ideal for long work or gaming sessions. 5. **Built-in speakers**: Although not high-fidelity, built-in speakers are useful for those who do not want to invest in external speakers. 6. **VESA mounting**: The 75x75 mm VESA mount allows the monitor to be mounted on a wall or on an articulated arm, adding versatility to its placement. ### **Cons:** 1. **Limited refresh rate**: Although 100Hz is an improvement over 60Hz, more demanding gamers might prefer monitors with 144Hz or higher. 2. **Basic Speakers**: The built-in speakers are functional, but do not offer high-quality sound. For an optimal listening experience, it is recommended to use headphones or external speakers. 3. **Limited adjustments**: Although it includes tilt, it does not have height, swivel or pivot adjustment, which could be a limitation for some users. 4. **Maximum Brightness**: The brightness might be a little low in brightly lit environments, which affects visibility in certain conditions. ### **Conclusion:** The **KOORUI 24-inch Gaming Monitor** is an excellent option for those looking for an affordable monitor but with gaming features. Its Full HD resolution, 100Hz refresh rate, and Adaptive Sync technology make it ideal for casual gamers. However, more demanding users might miss a higher refresh rate and additional ergonomic adjustments. Overall, it is a great purchase for its value for money. Recommended for those looking for a versatile and functional monitor!

reviews.title: A 6-Month Review from a Casual Gamer
reviews.body: Let's get straight to business with this review. This monitor has been with me since July of last year, and it's safe to say it's held up amazingly. I upgraded from a basic 1080p monitor from Sceptre (that I still use as a secondary monitor to this day), and while the color profile is different (until making adjustments on the monitor itself), the high refresh rate makes it a super smooth experience, especially for gaming. Not to mention, with a powerful enough graphics card (I rock a 4080 Super), the high refresh rate paired with high fidelity makes all aspects of gaming gorgeous, to the point where I'm considering getting a second one to have a triple monitor setup. One thing I should mention is the weight. It isn't heavy per se, but I would be cautious depending on what mounting bracket you plan to use with it, and the size paired alongside the weight makes it a bit cumbersome when mounting to a bracket/stand. Besides that, if you need a relatively affordable, high refresh rate monitor, this Nitro 27in model will do its job and more. Highly recommend.

All of the display settings are easily adjustable through the analog button on the rear of the monitor. Also the monitor has settings that can actively adjust your picture for different situations in games (I currently cannot recall the term for it). You can adjust the brightness, saturation, and more. One of my favorite features is the different display presets such as low blue light that can help when working late on the monitor. My only demerit of the monitor is the stand itself is kind of flimsy and is not adjustable. I would advise getting a mount for your monitor of some sort if you are to purchase this monitor. Otherwise this is an amazing monitor I got for an amazing price during Prime Day Deals.

I use it for a mix of office work, video, and gaming, and it handles all three without compromise. For the price point, it's hard to beat. Highly recommend if you want a do-it-all monitor that punches above its weight.

reviews.title: for a budget monitor I couldnt be happier with it
reviews.body: I snagged one of these along with one of the flat monitors for a new system recently. The flat model was $149, while this one was $119, and yet this one is worlds nicer than the flat model. The colors are more even, the blacks are darker, the menu has more options, and as someone that has never had a curved model before I think it looks amazing. If it weren't such a pain to return the flat model and get a second one of these, I would do it in a heartbeat. The only thing I could see might be an issue for some people, is the stand on this model isn't adjustable almost at all. It is very stable, and if you plan to put it on a mounting arm it wont matter, but if you need to constantly adjust the angle of the monitor you might have an issue on some desks with this stand. However everything else is fantastic. If you are looking for a good budget monitor I can't recommend this one enough, even over other models in the same product line. If you are looking at the flat models, save yourself the disappointment and the $30 and go for this one instead.

reviews.title: Please read Specs: A decent value curved monitor with some drawbacks.
reviews.body: OVERALL: This is a decent curved monitor, screen looks nice, easy to assemble, some minor drawbacks. Good Value. Background: I am using this monitor to hook up to my mini computer and my Nintendo Switch. This is my second curved monitor that I have owned. Both have been Samsung monitors as my first one was wonderful but got damaged in a flood. So when I was going to set up a new workstation I default went to Samsung to replace my old Samsung. I found this monitor and ordered it quickly. Shipping was fast and it came in undamaged. The Good: Monitor was easy to set up. It is a good size. Screen looks good. The Neutral/Bad: Monitor boasts a 100 hrtz refresh rate. While this is fine for my needs (switch and basic computing) this is probably not good enough for a heavy gamer or someone dealing with advanced graphics. The monitor only has 01 HDMI input. I find this annoying and I have to buy a HDMI switch in order to switch between my nintendo and my computer. The Monitor does not have built in speakers. My last one had built in speakers and I was spoiled with that simple feature. Overall if you are looking for a basic curved monitor with decent specs, I believe this is a good candidate. However if you are looking for something with the most advanced refresh rates and multiple HDMI inputs, you may want to look a tier or two up. I have included pictures of monitor front and the back (so you can see the inputs).

reviews.title: I'm Not A Gamer And I'll NEVER Spend A Lot Of Money On A Monitor (With Update)
reviews.body: UPDATE: I have had this thing for almost 2 and a half years now. I am happier with it every day! Two things to note are: 1) I have never seen anything like somebody welding something in a Youtube video!! It's so absolutely bright, it lights up the room a little and I reflexively squint until I have time to realize that it can't hurt my eyes because it's not real life. 2) Much of the time, it has better flesh tones than my big screen Hisense TV out in the living room! I can't recommend it enough. It's not even really a budget monitor; it's just not a gaming monitor! It sure is good for everything else!! I've been using this Viewsonic VX2778-SMHD 27 inch monitor since Jan, 2017, Very nice monitor! But, then I built a dream machine. i7-14700K on an ASRock Z790 Riptide motherboard with lots of SSD's and NVME drives. 48 gigs of very fast RAM and two DVDRW's. I'm pretty good at this and I did my very best not to allow any bottlenecks and not spend money on silly things. It absolutely screams; it gets stuff done fast! I also have an older Intel computer, an AMD computer, and a Raspberry Pi in here. So I have an HDMI KVM switcher and an HDMI audio extractor (audio goes straight to a competent home stereo). So, I don't play any games anymore, but I do want to get stuff done! There came a point where I wanted to make use of this somewhat better video card that's better than anything I've ever used. (Still not for gaming, tho.) I scoured Amazon. I ended up getting an NVidia GeForce GTX 1660 used, that was DIRT cheap! I chewed my nails wondering if it was going to work, but it did and it does! From the first momen, for about 9 or 10 months! I forget how much memory it's got, but it's up there. So, now, I had this video card mostly going to waste (Except for hardware acceleration; that's really nice!) So, I measured how much room I have. If I looked at monitors with really thin frames around the screen and measured and did the math... I decided on 32 inches. I scoured Amazon again and got to this monitor: (KTC H32T13 32 Inch) I had a little trouble. First of all, I'm lazy. I was still building that i7 and I set the monitor aside after unpacking it and went through all my other stuff I had to do first. (The other 2 computers mentioned above both needed some help.) (And the computer room needed some rearranging.) There's also that fact that there was absolutely nothing wrong with the old Viewsoni; there was no pressure... Anyway! From March 22nd until just now - two days ago - it just sat there. I don't even know where the quick start guide or whatever it is, went to, and I didn't want to conduct a lengthy search. Someone wrote that the power button is in a bad place. It's not that bad at all. I spent a little while finding it; reach your hand around the monitor's right side, near the bottom and feel for it. It sticks way out. The only time I have to reach for it is when I'm leaving the computer room to watch TV or go out or whatever. I can't reach it sitting down, but I'm getting up anyway at that point. Then I was totally puzzled, trying to figure out how to set the settings on the monitor. It wasn't bad, but I wanted to tweak the brightness, contrast, hue, gamma, etc. It took me quite a while to figure out that that power button, which is also a menu button (if you just touch it instead of holding it for three seconds) IS ALSO A JOYSTICK! Remember that! You can move it left, right, up, and down. Once I figured that out, it has a VERY logical, easy to use menu, unlike the Viewsonic mentioned about. The next problem I had was that a lot of things were ghosted in the menu and couldn't be selected. Scratching my head, I theorized that probably the video card was running the monitor and I turned to the NVidia Control Panel on the computer. There are at least three different places to set all that on that i7 machine, but it ended up being the screen display settings that did it. I love this monitor now! Plenty bright, fast, 2K, really great picture!! If the power button in the back is even a negative, I don't mind a bit. Everything else about it is outstanding! In about a minute, I had all those settings set. Beautiful bright, colorful screen! Perfect! I also have an older Silicon Dust HDHomeRun dual tuner. I encountered something that's never happened before! Watched "The Rifleman" in black and white. NEVER BEFORE have I had perfect black and white! Always some kind of tinge, usually in the dark places. I mean PERFECT black and white! Then I watched some stuff on Charge! (Streaming) and I adjusted color saturation and hue and got the skin tones right. Absolutely perfect picture, no matter what I do, now!! This is not a cheap budget monitor; this is an inexpensive performance monitor that works extremely well! I completely recommend it and I think it's a super nice deal for the money!!

reviews.title: 24 inch 1440p 100hz Monitor
reviews.body: I have been pleasantly surprised with this monitor. It was listed for only $110 and I got it $10 off so paid only $100 + tax. To get a 1440p monitor for so cheap is really incredible. The monitor does kind of have a cheaper feel/weight to it but it preforms well and that's what counts as far as I'm concerned. It came with an HDMI cable which is adequate for a monitor that only does 100hz. If you prefer Display Port than it has an input for that but you will have to provide your own cable. As someone who pretty much exclusively plays single player games 100hz is plenty for me. When I decided to buy the monitor I couldn't find any reviews for this specific version (24" 1440p 100hz). There were plenty of good reviews for other versions but not for this one. I am glad I decided to go ahead and buy it anyway. It really is a nice step up from my previous 1080p 27" 75hz LG monitor which I think was probably meant more for an office than a gamer. I was not sure how noticeable the jump up in resolution would be but it is noticeable and quite nice. The games look better, text is clearer and easier to read, and I noticed that even the UI for Windows and programs I use like Shotcut just look better and seem to be made with higher resolutions (QHD and above) in mind. The jump from 75hz to 100hz has been less noticeable but again I play single player games, also I prefer to play with a controller, and I come from decades of playing on consoles where a solid 30fps is considered pretty good and 60hz a bit of an anomaly. This monitor does accept an HDR signal but I have not been able to test that out much yet. Also I don't believe it has the HDR 400 certification but at this price this is not surprising and from what I hear HDR 400 monitors aren't really all that great for HDR. The cheapest HDR monitor I've scene recommended costs $280, which is quite a jump up from the price of this monitor. Also Windows reports it as a 10 bit monitor. I'm not sure if that was mentioned in the specs but that is nice to see on a budget monitor (instead of only 8 bit). One thing some people might not like about this monitor is it does not have much customization in terms of brightness and colors and things like that. If you are the type of person who really likes to tinker with those kinds of sliders and settings than this is not the monitor for you. It has 7 different presets that you can choose from but that's just about it as far as the choices go. For me there are a few that I like so I have no complaints and if you like to keep things simple than this could be a positive but if you need to tinker than find a different monitor. It does have crosshair and FPS counter choices in the settings but I have not tried them as I do not have a need for them. Before finding this monitor I had never seen a 1440p monitor at 24". They were always 27" and above when I looked. I have to say that initially I kind of missed the extra screen space with the 27 incher but after a couple weeks I got used to it and honestly do think it is a great size. It allows me to be closer to the screen and actually sit at my desk whereas before with the 27" monitor I had to sit a bit back to be able to comfortably take in all the screen real estate. If you are coming from a smaller size monitor than I think this will be a nice upgrade. If your previous monitor was bigger just know that it might take a week or 2 to get used to the smaller size but I think that once you do, you will not miss the bigger screen. Also the pixel density is pretty high at 1440p 24" as most monitors this size are only 1080p. So in conclusion if you are like me and just want an inexpensive but well made 1440p monitor, than I think you will be happy if you choose this one. This KTC H24T27 is very nice for single player gamers like myself or anyone looking for a 24" 1440p monitor. If you are the type of gamer that plays multiplayer games and needs high refresh rates than obviously this is not the monitor for you, I would suggest something with at least 160-180hz.

reviews.title: Great lightweight monitor
reviews.body: Great monitor for the price. I love the combination of 24" with 1440p for the high pixel density, but it is hard to find. I live in Paraguay at the moment and it is impossible to get 1440p monitors under 27" here. And even those are really expensive compared to the US. So I had to import them from the US. The freight forwarder is payed by weight and it is pretty expensive, so I tried to find lightweight options. This monitor was a perfect fit for this requirement. The stand is almost all plastic and therefore a bit flimsy but light weight. The monitor itself is also pretty light. The overall build quality is still pretty decent and more importantly the screen itself is pretty good. Definitely good enough for office work or light color work like web design. I don't have a color calibrator or a really accurate screen to compare, but on it's own they look good. I got three and they all match pretty closely too. The three monitors with an outer Amazon box weight 13.6kg. With the extra shipping I payed around 230$ per monitor. Compared to the alternatives here I'm happy with the purchase. At only 120$ if you are in America they are an absolute steal.

reviews.title: Excellent Value and great performance for a flat 27" 1440p monitor
reviews.body: This KTC 27" QHD monitor is a fantastic value with excellent features. Very good blacks with 4000:1 contrast and the 144hz is a legit gaming entry point. The 129% sRGB was a bit concerning to me as it suggested the color accuracy may not be that good, but the monitor has an "sRGB" mode in the menu that is useful for ensuring color accurate work and was the reason why I gave this monitor a chance. Glad I did. Speaking of which, the menu is accessible by a single joystick type button behind the monitor which takes a little bit of contorting to access from below it but its operation is very easy to use and allows for quick navigation within the menu. Would have been better if that joystick was positioned an inch or more closer to the bottom of the monitor. The standard color profile is the 129% sRGB which gives you slightly more of an extended color palette reminiscent of "HDR". No built in speakers, but that wasn't a deal breaker. Now that its on the desk and I'm using it daily, I can see that for me a 27" monitor like this is probably the practical limit for a "flat" configuration vs curved. On a white background, the bottom edges take on a slightly pink hue when you are positioned in the middle of the monitor but its subtle. That is probably reduced with curved monitors. Despite that I prefer it flat. The brightness of the monitor is very good, and almost too much for my eyes. Since I'm working all day in front of the monitor, i need the ability to lower the brightness to comfortable levels. The lowest brightness level is just about where it becomes comfortable for me so it would be better if it had more range for dimming further. It is HDR capable technically and I believe it but have no intention of testing or using that mode sitting at normal distances from it, with the high brightness and 4000:1 contrast, it would work really well if you're eyes can handle the brightness and color intensity. I have it positioned as the main monitor flanked by two 1080p 22" monitors which are slightly angled inward. As a triple monitor setup it works quite well and I plan to find a game where I can span across all three monitors on my desk.
reviews.body_en: This KTC 27" QHD monitor is a fantastic value with excellent features. Very good blacks with 4000:1 contrast and the 144hz is a legit gaming entry point. The 129% sRGB was a bit concerning to me as it suggested the color accuracy may not be that good, but the monitor has an "sRGB" mode in the menu that is useful for ensuring color accurate work and was the reason why I gave this monitor a chance. Glad I did. Speaking of which, the menu is accessible by a single joystick type button behind the monitor which takes a little bit of contorting to access from below it but its operation is very easy to use and allows for quick navigation within the menu. Would have been better if that joystick was positioned an inch or more closer to the bottom of the monitor. The standard color profile is the 129% sRGB which gives you slightly more of an extended color palette reminiscent of "HDR". No built in speakers, but that wasn't a deal breaker. Now that its on the desk and I'm using it daily, I can see that for me a 27" monitor like this is probably the practical limit for a "flat" configuration vs curved. On a white background, the bottom edges take on a slightly pink hue when you are positioned in the middle of the monitor but its subtle. That is probably reduced with curved monitors. Despite that I prefer it flat. The brightness of the monitor is very good, and almost too much for my eyes. Since I'm working all day in front of the monitor, i need the ability to lower the brightness to comfortable levels. The lowest brightness level is just about where it becomes comfortable for me so it would be better if it had more range for dimming further. It is HDR capable technically and I believe it but have no intention of testing or using that mode sitting at normal distances from it, with the high brightness and 4000:1 contrast, it would work really well if you're eyes can handle the brightness and color intensity. I have it positioned as the main monitor flanked by two 1080p 22" monitors which are slightly angled inward. As a triple monitor setup it works quite well and I plan to find a game where I can span across all three monitors on my desk.

reviews.title: Isn't LG supposed to be a good brand?
reviews.body: My husband and I both replaced our monitors at the same time and ordered 2 of these LG monitors - as they are side by side in our home office, we wanted them to be the same. We ordered LG because we thought it would be a good brand. A few days after receiving the first set of monitors, my husband's started flickering off and then back on. This would happen inconsistently, but is clearly an issue. We returned the monitor and exchanged it for the same thing. This one so far has been okay, but I don't have high hopes because... Shortly after that, the same thing started happening to mine. We have totally different computers, different brands, etc. so we didn't think it was a compatibility issue. We exchanged mine for the same thing again. A few days after the new one was installed, the color went yellow. This is a huge issue for me, as I work with photos and images a lot and need a consistent color rendition. So we exchanged it once again, reluctantly but I still wanted them to match since they are right next to each other. That was a bad decision and I should have returned it and ordered a different monitor because now it won't even turn on or recognize the computer. It is just 4 months old, but past the return time so now I'm out the money and have to order another monitor that won't match anyway. This is very frustrating all around.

reviews.title: Good monitor, but needs manual adjustment for proper color.
reviews.body: Well constructed and very sharp, but terrible color balance that can be corrected with the included controls. The settings I came up with for natural skin tones and not having your eyes ruined by an extremely bright and blue screen output are these: Set it to theatre mode Cut brightness down to 25 (!). Way, way down. Set red, green, and blue under the 'Color Temperature' to 65, 85, and 77, respectively. Your mileage may vary, but you can use these settings as a starting point and adjust for your personal taste. These settings work best in low to average room lighting; if in a brighter room, you may have to adjust more. I would have given the monitor a 5-star rating, but the default settings are not pleasant at all.

reviews.title: Good monitor with one minor caveat.
reviews.body: I got this monitor when it was $149 and while other options exist for a cheaper price and better refresh rate, this has the color saturation option. Basically, you can make the colors pop much more, which is a huge plus in my book as only a few monitor brands have it. It's a huge requirement for me. The 1440p is also a big upgrade compared to my other 1080p monitor, as games and other content looks way better while not being as resource intensive as 4k. However there are a few downsides to this monitor. First downside was getting the monitor to recognize the 1440p signal. When I first set it up, it only recognized 1080p from my mini pc. When I unplugged and plugged the HDMI cable back in, then the monitor discovered the 1440p. Not a huge deal breaker, as I rarely unplug my computers. Second downside however, is a very annoying one. When auto switching from HDMI to Display Port, the monitor sometimes goes into sleep mode, or just bugs out. This is very frustrating as I constantly go from my mini PC (on HDMI), to my Desktop (on Display Port). It'll sometimes work without issue, and other times I have to power off the monitor via the back button for it to work again. But sometimes when powering back on from this issue, the monitor light will be amber instead of white, even though it's not sleeping and fully on. I have to physically unplug and replug the monitor in to fix this. (See the attached photo). Disappointing that this is an issue, given my other 1080p monitor from ASUS never had this issue. So ya, if you can get this for sale under $130 then sure it's a good monitor. If not, find something else that is less buggy.

Basically, you can make the colors pop much more, which is a huge plus in my book as only a few monitor brands have it. It's a huge requirement for me. The 1440p is also a big upgrade compared to my other 1080p monitor, as games and other content looks way better while not being as resource intensive as 4k. However there are a few downsides to this monitor. First downside was getting the monitor to recognize the 1440p signal. When I first set it up, it only recognized 1080p from my mini pc. When I unplugged and plugged the HDMI cable back in, then the monitor discovered the 1440p. Not a huge deal breaker, as I rarely unplug my computers. Second downside however, is a very annoying one. When auto switching from HDMI to Display Port, the monitor sometimes goes into sleep mode, or just bugs out. This is very frustrating as I constantly go from my mini PC (on HDMI), to my Desktop (on Display Port). It'll sometimes work without issue, and other times I have to power off the monitor via the back button for it to work again. But sometimes when powering back on from this issue, the monitor light will be amber instead of white, even though it's not sleeping and fully on. I have to physically unplug and replug the monitor in to fix this. (See the attached photo). Disappointing that this is an issue, given my other 1080p monitor from ASUS never had this issue. So ya, if you can get this for sale under $130 then sure it's a good monitor. If not, find something else that is less buggy.

I highly recommend it and I will only be purchasing the RAYMYLO brand water bottles in the future!

reviews.title: Good for Price!
reviews.body: Great product. Well insulated. Price is good. Strap and carrying case are great and surprisingly comfortable when adjusted. I bought this in the summer of 2024. The carrying case broke in the summer two years later, but the bottle is still in good condition. I would recommend this for adventures outdoors but expect the straps themselves to be fair to the price. Invest a little more if you want the straps to be more comfortable and durable to carry long distances. The option between a straw and chug cap is brilliant, though keep in mind that the bottle’s large size can make it hard to suck from. I think I got the biggest size at the time because I only wanted to have to fill it up once a day. Turns out that it sometimes can go multiple days without refilling but it is awkward to carry because of its size, so I personally would only usey particular size bottle for hikes with multiple people or long trips in heat (safaris, etc). That being said, I am still using this every day partially filled for work until I get another small bottle. My only suggestion to the manufacturer would be to offer a model with a higher quality strap (fake leather or something of the sort) that will do better in harsh environments.

title: Owala FreeSip Stainless Steel Water Bottle 24 oz Very, Very Dark
bullet_points: 24-ounce insulated stainless-steel water bottle with a FreeSip spout and push-button lid with lock

reviews.title: Best water bottle ever
reviews.body: I purchased this bottle just to try out in the summer of 2023. It is now the summer of 2026 and I still use it multiple times a week (only because I now have multiple Owalas and I have just ordered my third Owala FreeSip). I have used so many cups—Stanleys, Yetis, Hydrojugs, Hydroflask, etc—and the Owala is still my favorite. Here’s my favorite things about it: LEAKPROOF! This is the biggest one. I can throw it my bag and trust that everything will stay dry. THE SPOUT! Hands down the best spout I’ve ever used. I love that I can sip through the straw but then close the lid and keep my straw clean and not have any spills if it tips over. And then it also gives me the option to absolutely inhale water if I’m about to shrivel up from dehydration. I think this alone is why I now own three in different sizes. STAYS COLD! The 32 ounce holds ice for quite a while. It varies depending on how often I refill it but if I’m not constantly refilling it, it will hold ice for about 24 hours. THE SIZES! I love the size options. My original one was a 32 ounce and is a great middle ground for me. It holds enough water that I’m not refilling it every hour but it’s not huge. It’s great for work and this bottle will be going to live at my job. I just ordered the 40 ounce for home because I want a little more volume when I’m outside gardening but I can’t say much about the 40 ounce size yet. I also have a 16 ounce (kids size) that I use when I leave the house. It fits in a lot of my bags and it’s leakproof so I always have cold water with me. It’s perfect especially since I’m on medication that causes dehydration if I’m not careful. DISHWASHER SAFE! This one is self explanatory. It’s amazing and I love it. There are a few cons though. The first one is that the 32 ounce doesn’t fit in my cup holder. Not a huge deal since it’s leakproof—I just keep it on the passenger seat. But Owala does have cup holder friendly options now if that’s something you want. The bottle also does dent and scratch fairly easily. I dropped it getting out my car one day and it’s a little beat up now. Kind ugly, but it’s still my fave. It’s kinda disappointing because I have Yetis and Stanleys that have been through far worse and still look new. Just be mindful of that and baby it a little. Still 100% worth it though. Long story short, it’s a great bottle that will keep your water cold and everything else dry. As someone who has used this bottle regularly for years, I highly recommend!

reviews.title: Hiding that lipstick in style!
reviews.body: I freaking love this thing. I'm not a trend person, I go for function. And when my STB SIL got my fiancé a shiney new Stanley I decided it was time to replace my beat up Rtic with the mismatch lid and straw. I may not follow trends, but I didn't want my fiancé's cup to put mine to absolute shame! First off, can we all agree that the marshmallow is gorgeous? THIS cup is spectacular. Strange to say that about a water bottle, I know. But since I never jumped on that train, I didn't know what I had been missing out on. Let me tell you what! The most important things to me is taking care of my service dog. She keeps me safe so her care is paramount to me. This enables me to pour my water into her bowl on the fly, without having to open my bottle past what I would do to drink from it. Quick and easy. That right there was the selling point for me. But as it turns out, there was even more benefit than that. I don't chug my water but if I did, the chug hole does works fine. The straw portion is ready to sip from, and it doesn't stick up tall like other water bottle straws. It's JUST tall enough to get the job done. No worry of toppling over because the straw got knocked over by the cat. (Because that happens.) The "handle", which is generally the locking feature unless you're using it as a handle, is well placed and comfortable for my sized hands. Not to small and not clunky and large. STB SIL likes to talk about how great the Stanley handle is, which I don't really get. I like that this doesn't have a handle. I have one to carry it if I need it, and not if I don't. The seal is completely water tight. I occasionally put a drink mix in it and shake vigorously. No leaks whatsoever. In fact... It fits in a car cup holder upside down. That's how I transport it in the car. It doesn't fit butt down, so I put it top down. I've been known to do this with various bottles, so I tried it with this one and it fits ok. It's not ideal but it's better than nothing. Try it in yours! Since it's completely leak proof there's are no worries about spilling. (Just be careful when you remove it that it doesn't unlatch.) Another bonus of the covered straw is that germs don't get in the straw. Perfect because people in public often don't cover their sneezes. Ugh. And the coolest part? Lipstick messes are concealed with a flip of the lid! Easy peasy! I have noticed that the inside of the straw stains a little, which was disappointing. I don't like that I look at it and it looks dirty when it isn't. But I guess I shouldn't have used drink enhancers then. Also, my top color is very light. Other colors might not show that. Another thing that want fun was that when it fell, it dented! Oh no! So beware of that. It keeps my water super cold and I don't go anywhere without it. I love it so much that I'm thinking of getting another so I don't have to limit myself by style! Definitely worth the price since I use it constantly, every day. This one is so chill and Zen... The next one shall be colorful and crazy! One for every mood! I simply can't say enough about this darn water bottle... Does that mean I'm on trend now? Who knows! I just love my Owalla! I'm definitely a fan!

reviews.title: Our favorite water bottles
reviews.body: Owala water bottles for the win! These are hands-down our favorite water bottles. We have tried just about every popular brand out there—Yeti, Stanley, Hydro Flask, and others—and the Owala is the one that everyone in our family consistently reaches for. I absolutely love the versatility of the lid. You can use the built-in straw when you want to sip, or easily flip it open and drink straight from the opening. Having both options in one bottle is incredibly convenient, especially when you're on the go. The color combinations are also so fun! There are so many options to choose from, and the colors and designs make the bottles feel a little more personal and fun to use. Durability is another huge selling point. These bottles get used constantly and have been dropped and knocked around, yet they hold up extremely well. They seem much less prone to denting than some of the other brands we've tried, which is especially important when they're being used by kids. And, of course, they keep drinks really cold! We can fill them with ice and water, and they stay cold for hours. The lid also seals extremely well—we have never had an issue with them leaking in a bag. After trying so many different water bottles, Owala is definitely the winner for our family. They're durable, versatile, attractive, keep drinks cold, and don't leak. I honestly can't think of another water bottle brand we've liked as much!

title: Owala FreeSip Stainless Steel Water Bottle 24 oz Denim
bullet_points: 24-ounce insulated stainless-steel water bottle with a FreeSip spout and push-button lid with lock
Patented FreeSip spout designed for either sipping upright through the built-in straw or tilting back to swig from the spout opening
Protective push-to-open lid keeps spout clean; convenient carry loop doubles as a lock
Double-wall insulation keeps drinks cold for up to 24 hours; wide opening for cleaning and adding ice; cup holder-friendly base
This bottle is wider than standard cupholders and may only fit in oversized or specialty cupholders designed for larger containers

reviews.title: Best water bottle ever
reviews.body: I purchased this bottle just to try out in the summer of 2023. It is now the summer of 2026 and I still use it multiple times a week (only because I now have multiple Owalas and I have just ordered my third Owala FreeSip). I have used so many cups—Stanleys, Yetis, Hydrojugs, Hydroflask, etc—and the Owala is still my favorite. Here’s my favorite things about it: LEAKPROOF! This is the biggest one. I can throw it my bag and trust that everything will stay dry. THE SPOUT! Hands down the best spout I’ve ever used. I love that I can sip through the straw but then close the lid and keep my straw clean and not have any spills if it tips over. And then it also gives me the option to absolutely inhale water if I’m about to shrivel up from dehydration. I think this alone is why I now own three in different sizes. STAYS COLD! The 32 ounce holds ice for quite a while. It varies depending on how often I refill it but if I’m not constantly refilling it, it will hold ice for about 24 hours. THE SIZES! I love the size options. My original one was a 32 ounce and is a great middle ground for me. It holds enough water that I’m not refilling it every hour but it’s not huge. It’s great for work and this bottle will be going to live at my job. I just ordered the 40 ounce for home because I want a little more volume when I’m outside gardening but I can’t say much about the 40 ounce size yet. I also have a 16 ounce (kids size) that I use when I leave the house. It fits in a lot of my bags and it’s leakproof so I always have cold water with me. It’s perfect especially since I’m on medication that causes dehydration if I’m not careful. DISHWASHER SAFE! This one is self explanatory. It’s amazing and I love it. There are a few cons though. The first one is that the 32 ounce doesn’t fit in my cup holder. Not a huge deal since it’s leakproof—I just keep it on the passenger seat. But Owala does have cup holder friendly options now if that’s something you want. The bottle also does dent and scratch fairly easily. I dropped it getting out my car one day and it’s a little beat up now. Kind ugly, but it’s still my fave. It’s kinda disappointing because I have Yetis and Stanleys that have been through far worse and still look new. Just be mindful of that and baby it a little. Still 100% worth it though. Long story short, it’s a great bottle that will keep your water cold and everything else dry. As someone who has used this bottle regularly for years, I highly recommend!

reviews.title: Hiding that lipstick in style!
reviews.body: I freaking love this thing. I'm not a trend person, I go for function. And when my STB SIL got my fiancé a shiney new Stanley I decided it was time to replace my beat up Rtic with the mismatch lid and straw. I may not follow trends, but I didn't want my fiancé's cup to put mine to absolute shame! First off, can we all agree that the marshmallow is gorgeous? THIS cup is spectacular. Strange to say that about a water bottle, I know. But since I never jumped on that train, I didn't know what I had been missing out on. Let me tell you what! The most important things to me is taking care of my service dog. She keeps me safe so her care is paramount to me. This enables me to pour my water into her bowl on the fly, without having to open my bottle past what I would do to drink from it. Quick and easy. That right there was the selling point for me. But as it turns out, there was even more benefit than that. I don't chug my water but if I did, the chug hole does works fine. The straw portion is ready to sip from, and it doesn't stick up tall like other water bottle straws. It's JUST tall enough to get the job done. No worry of toppling over because the straw got knocked over by the cat. (Because that happens.) The "handle", which is generally the locking feature unless you're using it as a handle, is well placed and comfortable for my sized hands. Not to small and not clunky and large. STB SIL likes to talk about how great the Stanley handle is, which I don't really get. I like that this doesn't have a handle. I have one to carry it if I need it, and not if I don't. The seal is completely water tight. I occasionally put a drink mix in it and shake vigorously. No leaks whatsoever. In fact... It fits in a car cup holder upside down. That's how I transport it in the car. It doesn't fit butt down, so I put it top down. I've been known to do this with various bottles, so I tried it with this one and it fits ok. It's not ideal but it's better than nothing. Try it in yours! Since it's completely leak proof there's are no worries about spilling. (Just be careful when you remove it that it doesn't unlatch.) Another bonus of the covered straw is that germs don't get in the straw. Perfect because people in public often don't cover their sneezes. Ugh. And the coolest part? Lipstick messes are concealed with a flip of the lid! Easy peasy! I have noticed that the inside of the straw stains a little, which was disappointing. I don't like that I look at it and it looks dirty when it isn't. But I guess I shouldn't have used drink enhancers then. Also, my top color is very light. Other colors might not show that. Another thing that want fun was that when it fell, it dented! Oh no! So beware of that. It keeps my water super cold and I don't go anywhere without it. I love it so much that I'm thinking of getting another so I don't have to limit myself by style! Definitely worth the price since I use it constantly, every day. This one is so chill and Zen... The next one shall be colorful and crazy! One for every mood! I simply can't say enough about this darn water bottle... Does that mean I'm on trend now? Who knows! I just love my Owalla! I'm definitely a fan!

reviews.title: Our favorite water bottles
reviews.body: Owala water bottles for the win! These are hands-down our favorite water bottles. We have tried just about every popular brand out there—Yeti, Stanley, Hydro Flask, and others—and the Owala is the one that everyone in our family consistently reaches for. I absolutely love the versatility of the lid. You can use the built-in straw when you want to sip, or easily flip it open and drink straight from the opening. Having both options in one bottle is incredibly convenient, especially when you're on the go. The color combinations are also so fun! There are so many options to choose from, and the colors and designs make the bottles feel a little more personal and fun to use. Durability is another huge selling point. These bottles get used constantly and have been dropped and knocked around, yet they hold up extremely well. They seem much less prone to denting than some of the other brands we've tried, which is especially important when they're being used by kids. And, of course, they keep drinks really cold! We can fill them with ice and water, and they stay cold for hours. The lid also seals extremely well—we have never had an issue with them leaking in a bag. After trying so many different water bottles, Owala is definitely the winner for our family. They're durable, versatile, attractive, keep drinks cold, and don't leak. I honestly can't think of another water bottle brand we've liked as much!

reviews.title: Perfect Water Bottle for Kids
reviews.body: We love this Owala! The 16 oz size is perfect for kids—big enough to hold plenty of water without being too heavy or bulky for them to carry around. The FreeSip design is probably my favorite part because they can sip through the straw or tilt it back to drink normally. It doesn’t leak all over the place, keeps water cold for a long time, and the covered spout stays cleaner than an exposed straw. The Read My Lips color is super cute, too. It’s held up really well to everyday kid use, which says a lot. Definitely worth the 5 stars!

reviews.title: Love the straw + chug option!
reviews.body: I got this Owala for my son and really like it so far! My favorite feature is that you can drink from either the built-in straw or use the chug opening. It gives him both options without having to switch out lids or pieces, which is really convenient. The bottle itself feels sturdy and good quality, and the lid closes securely and has a handle that makes it easy to carry. The colors are also really fun and vibrant. My only concern is the coating on the outside. It feels like it may be somewhat easy to scratch, especially since this is going to be used by a kid and tossed into bags, taken to school, etc. We’ll see how it holds up over time! Overall, though, I’m really happy with it. I’ll update my review once I find out how sturdy it is.

reviews.body: Love Owala bottles and I have several of the 24 oz. I decided to get a larger size (32 oz.) this time to take to sporting events to hold more water. Water stays cold all day like the others, and it never leaks. The only downside is that it doesn't fit in my car or chair cupholders by just a fraction. I kind of suspected that might be the case going in, so it doesn't bother me too much. At games I just have to set it on the ground instead of my sports chair. It just won't be my everyday bottle - I will continue to use the 24 oz for the car since it fits perfectly in the cupholder. But Owala still gets 5 starts for the great design, easy to carry, and staying cold all day.

reviews.title: You’ll Love It!
reviews.body: I love this water bottle for many reasons. It checks off all of my requirements! My list was particular and I didn’t think I’d find exactly what I wanted. The body is stainless steel and is quite sturdy, it keeps my water cold for about 24 hours and the 30 oz. size is perfect. It’s neither too big nor too small. It’s by far the best water bottle I’ve had because it has so many great features. Since it’s easy to carry around by the handle, I am finding myself taking it wherever I go in the house and I’m actually drinking more water because of it! Try it and you’ll fall in love with it just like I did!

reviews.title: Worth every penny
reviews.body: I didn't get into the Stanley craze-I've had too many accidental spills with the whole cup & straw set up. So when my kids started insisting I get an Owala, I was skeptical. But then I saw the TikTok of that one guy using his Owala as a weapon to fight off the men who attempted to break into his house, and not only did he stop them, his Owala survived with just a dent (and a broken handle, if memory serves me right)! Then Owala does the of the best PR stunt/customer appreciation ever, and not only sends that man a safe, but filled that safe with several Owala bottles! I admire a company that can back their products up; but I will support a business who listens and recognizes their customers too! So I started looking for one; I got to thinking as a woman who often does her errands alone, "you know, I can always use it for defense and I can't be accused of carrying a weapon, because technically it's a water bottle." When Owala came out with this Amazon exclusive color, I knew it was kismet! I put it on my cart, but before I checked out, my kid saw what I was doing and she stopped me. She said, "lady, I already bought that for you. It's coming next week." LOL I guess she got tired of telling me to get one, and just grabbed it for me, knowing that burgundy is one of my favorite colors! I've had it for 5 months now. It's a little dinged up on the bottom-nothing too bad. I just dropped it one or two times (maybe more). I love that the mouthpiece is covered up and can be locked so 1)it will always be clean; and 2)it won't accidentally spill if it tips over, or you know, you accidentally drop it. It keeps me accountable-I fill that 40 oz 2-3 times a day to make sure I stay hydrated. I love that it's insulated so I can keep my drink cold or hot-depending on what I fill it with. I love that it's easy to clean-there are no nook & crannies that can't be cleaned or reached! I just love it. Period.

reviews.title: Convenient Without Being Bulky
reviews.body: I've been really happy with this bottle. The 30 oz size feels like the perfect middle ground—big enough that I'm not constantly refilling it, but not so big that it becomes a pain to carry around. It also fits in a standard cup holder, which was a must for me. It's surprisingly lightweight, and the bucket handle makes it really easy to grab and go. The only downside I've noticed is that ice doesn't last quite as long as some other insulated bottles because the lid isn't fully insulated. That said, it's not a dealbreaker for my use. It still keeps my water plenty cold throughout the day, and the convenience and design more than make up for it. I got the Dreamy Fields color and it looks even better in person. Overall, definitely recommend.

reviews.title: HONESTLY THE ONLY WATER BOTTLE YOU'LL EVER NEED!! BEST EVER!!! SON USES IT FOR SCHOOL EVERYDAY!!
reviews.body: I waited to write this review. My 8 year old son needed a daily water bottle for school & I found this on a really great deal in Sept 2025. I loved that It had a strap for him to carry, especially if we had trips! It is now March 2026 & I am BEYOND impressed with this thing! First off, it came with 2 straps- one hand strap & another for his shoulder! He has currently been into sipping through a straw, but used to prefer pouring... This one comes with BOTH types types you can change by screwing that choice lid on! It had 2 straws (I had never had to replace yet- and he brings it everyday)!! It comes with 2 brushes to clean and 1 for the straw. I have washed it so many times- it's easy! it's still exactly the same now as it was! One of the best things I like about it is how cold it keeps his drink (it like dense metal but also not really heavy) but ALSO- HUGE- the fact that somehow it doesn't seem to create any mild easier like others I've had, even if its kept out. (Once he accidentally left It at school during a week vacation and there was no signs of mold in there- I don't know how! That would have never happened with our old ones!) It slides very easily into a pouch that is the "carry pouch". I have his name tag attached to the clip on it. We have gotten so many compliments on it & asked where it came from. I bought another water bottle so I could interchange them during washes- but honestly, I've rarely ever done that bc this is my son's favorite water bottle & this will be the only one you'll ever need!

reviews.title: Missing item (Solved!)
reviews.body: I love my bottle! The colour and quality is amazing! Seems easy to clean as well. The problem? I'm missing the straws, which is kind of a dealbreaker since I only drink from that type of mouth, the other one is useless to me. It also didn't come with the straw or bottle cleaners, that bothers me less since I have some already. I'd really like to not return this and somehow just get the missing items (Mostly the straws.) --- Review of actual product: Gosh darn is this thing HEAVY! I wasn't expecting it. But the quantity lasts me 12 hours just fine. I'm considering the extra weight an excuse to get a workout for my arms, haha, but if you have any type of disability, you might want to consider a smaller size. My stronger and taller friend uses their gifted bottle just fine, they also say they really like it. This one (128oz) doesn't fit in my backpack, which is a shame, but oh well. It can also be a struggle to fill it all the way, depending on what you get your water from. I can do it to the top, my friend can only get 8/10ths unless he wants to use a separate cup to scoop the rest of the water in. The colour is beautiful, the clips and bands seem sturdy, I got a stain on the sleeve, and it washed out with just a dab of water. The mouth is wide enough to pour ice in, and it keeps the same temperature forever! --- Edit: The seller contacted me quickly and helped me find a solution, they were very concise and answered all of my questions. I will say, there seems to be a problem with quality control, I think sometimes bottles get sent back, and they can miss any damages/missing items because of that. I bought another bottle and this one had a black smudge on the sleeve I couldn't wash out, it's not a dealbreaker for me, but so far 2 of the 3 bottles had some error. The only reason I'm keeping it at five stars despite that is because of their customer service being 10/10 and the quality of the product being the same.

reviews.title: La combinación perfecta entre funcionalidad y diseño para fans de Star Wars
reviews.body: La Owala Star Wars FreeSip es fácilmente una de las mejores botellas reutilizables que he tenido. Desde el primer momento destaca por el diseño: los detalles inspirados en Star Wars están increíblemente bien logrados y hacen que se vea mucho más especial que una botella común. Tanto si eres fan casual como coleccionista, definitivamente llama la atención. Pero lo mejor es que no solo se ve increíble, también funciona excelente. El sistema FreeSip es probablemente lo más cómodo que he probado en una botella de agua. Poder elegir entre beber con popote integrado o tomar directamente inclinando la botella parece algo simple, pero en el uso diario hace muchísima diferencia. Es práctico para el gimnasio, oficina, coche o simplemente para traerla todo el día. La calidad de construcción también es excelente. Se siente resistente, bien sellada y hecha con materiales premium. La tapa cierra perfectamente y hasta ahora no he tenido ninguna fuga, incluso llevándola dentro de mochila. Otro punto impresionante es el aislamiento térmico. Mantiene el agua fría durante muchísimas horas, incluso en días calurosos. De verdad cumple lo que promete y hace que siempre tengas bebidas frías disponibles. Además, el tamaño y el agarre son muy cómodos. No se siente aparatosa y el asa integrada facilita muchísimo transportarla. Son pequeños detalles que terminan haciendo una gran diferencia en el día a día. Algo que me gustó mucho es que logra equilibrar perfectamente lo coleccionable con lo funcional. Muchas veces los productos temáticos sacrifican calidad por diseño, pero aquí ambas cosas están muy bien cuidadas.
reviews.body_en: The Owala Star Wars FreeSip is easily one of the best reusable bottles I've ever owned. From the first moment it stands out for its design: the Star Wars-inspired details are incredibly well done and make it look much more special than a common bottle. Whether you're a casual fan or a collector, it's definitely an eye-catcher. But the best thing is that not only does it look amazing, it also works great. The FreeSip system is probably the most convenient thing I've ever tried in a water bottle. Being able to choose between drinking with an integrated straw or drinking directly by tilting the bottle seems simple, but in daily use it makes a lot of difference. It is practical for the gym, office, car or simply to bring it all day. The build quality is also excellent. It feels sturdy, well-sealed, and made with premium materials. The lid closes perfectly and so far I haven't had any leaks, even carrying it in a backpack. Another impressive point is the thermal insulation. It keeps the water cold for many hours, even on hot days. It really delivers what it promises and ensures that you always have cold drinks available. Plus, the size and grip are very comfortable. It doesn't feel bulky and the integrated handle makes it very easy to transport it. They are small details that end up making a big difference in everyday life. Something that I really liked is that it manages to perfectly balance the collectible with the functional. Many times thematic products sacrifice quality for design, but here both things are very well taken care of.

reviews.title: A surprisingly complete 40 oz bottle kit with tons of carrying options
reviews.body: This is an impressively complete water bottle set. Everything coordinates in a black/deep green color scheme that looks great and works equally well for men, women or kids. More importantly, the accessories aren’t just filler—they actually make a 40 oz bottle much easier to carry and use. The black and green paracord handle is especially helpful when the bottle is completely full. My 9-year-old plans to use this for school, and he was comfortable holding it by the paracord handle even with 40 oz of water inside. (I didn’t tell him about the whistle in case he decides to demonstrate it in class.) The paracord handle attaches to a rubber ring that slips over the neck of the bottle. One thing to know is that you can’t remove just the paracord portion—the entire ring and attached hardware need to come off for washing, which is fairly easy to do. If you decide not to use it, you’ll also lose the attached compass and safety whistle. Fortunately, both included lids have their own built-in handles, so the bottle is still easy to carry without it. The locking chug cap comes preinstalled, and there’s also a straw cap with two straws. You get a straw brush, bottle brush, shoulder strap and neoprene bottle sleeve as well. The sleeve is a particularly nice addition because it cushions the bottom so you don’t get the loud metal clang when setting the bottle down, eliminating the need for a separate silicone boot. It also adds two storage pockets: a mesh pocket in front and a surprisingly roomy zippered pocket in back. The adjustable shoulder strap gives you several carrying options. For reference, I’m 5’6”. At its shortest setting, the top of the bottle sits about two inches below my armpit. Fully extended and worn crossbody, the top sits around my hip. Worn over one shoulder at the longer setting, it hangs a few inches below my hip bone. Between the two lids, paracord handle, shoulder strap, protective storage sleeve, cleaning tools, whistle, compass and carabiner, there’s a lot packed into this kit. If you’re looking for a versatile 40 oz bottle that feels durable and gives you plenty of ways to carry and customize it, this is an excellent option.
