reviews.title: A Wonderful Notebook for Writers—But We Need More Mustaches!
reviews.body: I am a published author who writes poetry, fiction, and creative nonfiction, and I have already filled a good portion of this notebook. I genuinely love it. It feels as though someone actually considered how writers and creative people use a notebook instead of simply binding together a stack of identical pages and calling it a day. One of my favorite features is the table of contents. Do you know how useful it is to have an actual contents section in a notebook? I write many different poems, stories, ideas, and fragments, so having a place where I can record what I wrote and where I placed it is incredibly helpful. It makes the notebook feel organized without taking away from the freedom and spontaneity of writing. I also love the variety in the pages and their layouts. Not everything feels perfectly uniform, and I mean that as a compliment. The variation gives the notebook a creative, authentically human feeling. It invites experimentation instead of making every page feel like it must be used in the same way. The paper quality is lovely, and I appreciate all the additional details: the sticky notes, the included pen, the thoughtful thank-you cards, and especially the clear pocket or folder in the back. That pocket is one of my favorite parts because I can keep loose notes, cards, and writing materials with the notebook instead of inevitably losing them somewhere in my home. I was also happy to discover that the company has a business connection to Puerto Rico. As a Puerto Rican writer, that made the product feel even more special to me. I did have an issue with the included pen. The tip appeared slightly bent when it arrived, and the clip eventually broke off. I have arthritis and pain in my hands, so having to angle the pen a certain way made it difficult for me to use comfortably. I now use a different pen with the notebook. This was disappointing, but it did not diminish how much I enjoy the notebook itself. Now we must discuss the truly serious matter: there were not nearly enough mustache stickers. I loved the little mustaches so much that I began decorating the front of the notebook with them and drawing faces around them. I would happily cover the entire notebook in tiny mustaches if given the opportunity. Mr. Pen, please consider offering additional mustache sticker sheets—especially in different sizes or ridiculous prints. Zebra mustaches. Gold mustaches. Polka-dot mustaches. The world is ready. Overall, this is a thoughtful, well-organized, high-quality notebook that works beautifully for poets, authors, journalers, students, and anyone whose mind produces more ideas than they can reasonably keep track of. The table of contents, varied pages, paper quality, accessories, and back pocket make it especially useful for creative writing. I truly love this notebook and would gladly purchase another—preferably in purple, and preferably accompanied by an unreasonable quantity of mustache stickers.

reviews.title: Just right for the task!
reviews.body: I love using these spiral notebooks. It is easy to flip through the pages. The coil doesn't smash easily, loose bits of paper are easy to remove when you take pages out. I like that the size of the paper is actually letter-size and not some odd size. I also like that you get a variety of colors on the cover. I work in an office where I need to keep track of phone calls, conversations where I have committed to doing something. I also use these for our weekly department meetings. I used to sort my tasks between many notebooks, but there's always that one time where you take down a phone message in the notebook set aside for meetings. I have ADHD and found it too hard to keep everything straight. Now I use these for everything. I put the date on the top of the page, and only write on one side of the paper. I used to use steno pads and would use both sides of the paper. It made for some difficult times retrieving notes when things were scattered. These are great notepads. The paper is nice and thick so you don't have to worry about ink bleeding through or using an eraser and having it tear holes in the paper. I just happened to come across these notepads at work. reviews.title: Love the notebooks

reviews.title: Awesome 6-Pack with amazing prices for the quality! Back-to-school is a breeze!
reviews.body: This 6 Pack of Spiral Notebooks is a steal for back-to-school shopping. I only have one child who's in 7th Grade, so sometimes those school supply lists are a pain because the only way to cheap it reasonable is to buy in bulk. Thankfully, my kid doesn't care about name brands at all, *but thinks it's cool when we buy them*, but this 6 pack is really a much better deal than the other bulk paper deals on Amazon primarily because: *** You get 6 Notebooks that are all awesome colors suitable for boys, girls, women, men, etc and they have double-pockets in both the back and front of the Notebooks for extra storage for students (or yourself) ***They are fully lined, very thick, and the covers are not paper. They are the water-resistant plastic covers and also fit right into 3-Ring binders of any size, easily. ***The price is fantastic for 6 of these. And if you only have one student or two students, there's extra Notebooks left over for us adults (I don't know about you, but I need at least 2 or 3 Notebooks around the house for notes and lists) ***They are good quality and durable and last a long time compared to buying "other" brands or buying them individually. I've seen them as high as $5.50 for one notebook even as an "add on" item (only available if you spend $50 total on your order). I really love these and so does my son. I was able to easily cover all of his teachers' requirements for lined paper Notebooks as well as keeping 2 of them for at home. You can't beat the built in pockets and flexible, plastic covers that are so much better for being beaten up at school or work. And for once, every color in the group is fantastic. I kept the White and Pink for at home and my son has the rest for his classes. Definitely grab this 6-Pack while you can. Cardboard, cheapie Notebooks just don't cut it for lasting in backpacks and binders and these have the extra storage and quality covers, too. One of the best Amazon deals I've found on branded, bulk notebooks (and I spend probably 8 hours shopping for each item on his school list). Snag them while you can!

reviews.title: Leather Bound Writing Journal with Beautiful Embossed Cover
reviews.body: I ordered this leather journal as a gift for my grandson. His father had one very similar & he has been asking for one for himself. While I was somewhat skeptical when I ordered it, I am extremely pleased with this purchase as it far exceeds my expectations. The overall size is 6" W x 8-1/2" H x 1" thick. The front & back covers are hardbound in leather with brown stitching 1/8" from all edges. The front is beautifully embossed with a tree of life in the center & what appears to be small suns in each corner with rays reaching toward the tree. There is an embossed line all around the perimeter 3/8" from the stitching with a double row of tiny circles located between the stitching & the line. The spine is a soft flexible brown leather that allows the journal to open 180° to lay flat on a table making it much easier to write. The first interior page has lines for name, phone & email entries followed by 3 pages of lined columns for content/index entries. The remaining interior has 280 cream colored college ruled pages for journal entries with each page thick enough to prevent ink bleed through. On each page in the upper left corner there are 3 boxes to indicate the weather, either sunny, partly sunny or rainy on the day of that page's journal entry. Directly below those are 7 small boxes to indicate the day of the week of the entry. In the opposite upper right corner is a line for the memo (page) number & below that a space for a date entry. The inside back cover has a pleated pocket 4-1/4" W x 7-7/8" H to store notes, ticket stubs, or other small flat mementos. Two 1/4" W ribbon bookmarks, one dark brown & one silver, are stitched into the spine at the top of the journal allowing you to quickly turn to your next entry or find where you left off reading. A 1/4" W brown elastic band is provided to wrap around the front cover to keep the journal closed. It is imbedded into the back of the journal 3/4" from the top & bottom & 3/4" from the side edges. It can easily be gently pulled over the front cover to keep the book closed & rests against the inside back cover when you're writing in the journal. The quality of this journal is excellent & is a great value for the money. This journal is available in brown or green & I opted for the brown version. It is a very nice, rich looking, medium brown, quality leather which I'm certain will last a lifetime. It would make an excellent gift for anyone that keeps a journal or diary. My only disappointment is that it didn't come in a gift box. Rather it was packaged in a plastic sleeve & then in a thin bubble bag. Overall I would highly recommend this product.

reviews.title: Helpful and Insightful
reviews.body: This book is an amazing DIY guide to understanding yourself and healing some of your past traumas. The insights I gained from reading the text and completing the workbook pages have literally changed my life. While one book can't fix everything, this one provides some deep insights and several tools to work with, and it helped me in a lot of really big ways. This is not seven books in one as it claims (nor did I think it would be when I bought it.) It has seven parts, each around 30 pages. Each part has a different theme, but none of them is what I would call a stand-alone book. In the last third of the book, the editing got lax. There were sentences and entire paragraphs that were repeated, and other paragraphs that were literally cut off in the middle. They would break at the end of a page, but not be continued on the next page. The journal prompt for chapter 26 was also a duplicate of chapter 25 - the journal prompts are specific to the reading in each chapter, so it didn't match up at all. I recommend this book - it's insightful and has the potential to help you change your life and your concept of yourself dramatically for the better. I took off one star for the editing errors. There were enough of them that it distracted from the message sometimes, though it was still worth it.

reviews.body: Love the quality and the colors and the overall feel of the book. I journaled in Moleskine for the last 20 years and due to price, I'm starting to look at other options. Overall, this is a solid journal - paper is thick in a lovely cream, binding and cover are sturdy. My only issue, and it's 100% personal issue, is that the lines are college ruled NOT narrow ruled. After two decades of writing in narrow ruled journals, it's glaringly obvious to me. I had to study customer photos, purchase and open the package and then compare old journals to confirm that information. At the time of purchase, that detail is not listed in any of the descriptions. If you're insane and picky AF like me, just be aware the lines are (ever so slightly) wider than Moleskine journals and the title line is on the stumpy side. If you don't mind and are not crazy, please absolutely buy this journal!

Using Paperage journals to me feels a bit like settling, but it still satisfies my journal needs.

After two decades of writing in narrow ruled journals, it's glaringly obvious to me. I had to study customer photos, purchase and open the package and then compare old journals to confirm that information. At the time of purchase, that detail is not listed in any of the descriptions. If you're insane and picky AF like me, just be aware the lines are (ever so slightly) wider than Moleskine journals and the title line is on the stumpy side. If you don't mind and are not crazy, please absolutely buy this journal!

reviews.title: Great quality price - it does the job!
reviews.body: First of all, the paper quality? Surprisingly good. I went in expecting “standard school notebook energy,” and instead got paper that actually respects your pen. Ink does not bleed through like it is trying to escape, and writing on it feels smooth enough to make you briefly believe you have your life together. Each notebook has 100 sheets, which means you start off thinking, “I will use this responsibly,” and end up halfway through with random lists, doodles, and one page that just says “get it together” written ten times. Plenty of space for both productivity and mild existential spirals. The size is perfect. Not too small where you feel cramped, not too big where it becomes a commitment. It fits in a backpack without drama, which is more than I can say for most things in life. Durability? Solid. These can survive being tossed around, shoved into bags, and opened aggressively when inspiration (or panic) hits. The classic composition cover also gives that timeless “serious note-taker” look, even if what you are actually writing is a grocery list and passive-aggressive reminders to yourself. And getting three in a pack? That is optimism right there. Three chances to start fresh, be organized, and finally become the person who uses notebooks properly.

reviews.title: Cuadernos de muy buena calidad
reviews.body: Reseña detallada: Paquete de 12 cuadernos Mead Square Wide Ruled Cuando se trata de encontrar cuadernos funcionales y accesibles, los Mead Square Wide Ruled en paquete de 12 son una opción confiable para estudiantes, profesionales y cualquier persona que necesite organizar sus apuntes. Con un diseño práctico y un formato cómodo, estos cuadernos ofrecen una solución eficiente para el día a día. Diseño y materiales Los cuadernos Mead Square Wide Ruled tienen un tamaño compacto, lo que los hace ideales para llevar en mochilas, bolsos o incluso carteras sin ocupar demasiado espacio. La portada, aunque sencilla, es lo suficientemente resistente para soportar el uso regular, aunque no es rígida como las versiones de tapa dura. En cuanto a la encuadernación, están engrapados en el lomo, lo que mantiene las hojas seguras, pero no permite abrirlos completamente planos sin riesgo de que se despeguen con el tiempo. Sin embargo, este diseño ayuda a que sean más ligeros y fáciles de manejar. Calidad del papel Uno de los puntos más importantes en cualquier cuaderno es el papel, y en este caso, los Mead cumplen bien su función. El gramaje es adecuado para evitar que la tinta de bolígrafos o lápices se traspase fácilmente a la siguiente hoja. No obstante, si se usan marcadores o plumas de gel muy húmedas, puede haber un leve traspaso. El rayado Wide Ruled (líneas anchas) es perfecto para quienes prefieren un espacio amplio entre renglones, lo que facilita la lectura y la escritura ordenada. Este formato es ideal para estudiantes de primaria, personas que escriben con letra grande o quienes necesitan tomar notas rápidas sin preocuparse por la alineación del texto. Uso y funcionalidad Estos cuadernos son una gran elección para estudiantes de todas las edades, ya que ofrecen suficiente espacio para escribir sin ser voluminosos. También son útiles para oficinas, listas de tareas o incluso llevar un diario personal. Sin embargo, es importante considerar que no tienen perforaciones para carpeta, por lo que si se necesitan hojas sueltas, habrá que desprenderlas manualmente. Ventajas y desventajas ✅ Ventajas: • Excelente relación calidad-precio, especialmente en paquetes grandes. • Tamaño compacto y fácil de transportar. • Papel de buena calidad con líneas anchas para escritura clara. • Diseño ligero y funcional. ❌ Desventajas: • No tienen perforaciones para archivadores. • La portada es flexible y podría desgastarse con el tiempo. • La encuadernación con grapas limita la apertura plana. Conclusión El paquete de 12 cuadernos Mead Square Wide Ruled es una compra inteligente para quienes buscan cuadernos prácticos, asequibles y de buena calidad. Son ideales para uso escolar, universitario o personal, ofreciendo un balance entre durabilidad y comodidad. reviews.body_en: Detailed Review: Mead Square Wide Ruled Notebooks 12-Pack When it comes to finding functional and affordable notebooks, the Mead Square Wide Ruled 12-Pack is a reliable choice for students, professionals, and anyone who needs to organize their notes. With a practical design and a comfortable format, these notebooks offer an efficient solution for everyday life. Design and materials Mead Square Wide Ruled notebooks have a compact size, making them ideal for carrying in backpacks, purses or even purses without taking up too much space. The cover, while simple, is durable enough to withstand regular use, although it is not rigid like the hardcover versions. As for the binding, they are stapled to the spine, which keeps the pages secure, but does not allow them to be opened completely flat without the risk of them coming unstuck over time. However, this design helps make them lighter and easier to handle. Paper quality One of the most important points in any notebook is the paper, and in this case, the Meads fulfill their function well. The weight is adequate to prevent ink from pens or pencils from easily transferring to the next sheet. However, if very wet markers or gel pens are used, slight bleeding may occur. Wide Ruled ruling is perfect for those who prefer wide space between lines, making it easy to read and write neatly. This format is ideal for elementary students, people who write with large handwriting, or those who need to take quick notes without worrying about text alignment. Use and Functionality These notebooks are a great choice for students of all ages, as they offer enough space to write without being bulky. They are also useful for offices, to-do lists or even keeping a personal diary. However, it is important to consider that they do not have perforations for a binder, so if loose sheets are needed, they will have to be detached manually. Advantages and disadvantages ✅ Advantages: • Excellent value for money, especially in large packages. • Compact size and easy to transport. • Good quality paper with wide lines for clear writing. • Light and functional design. ❌ Disadvantages: • They do not have perforations for file cabinets. • The cover is flexible and may wear over time. • Staple binding limits flat opening. Conclusion The Mead Square Wide Ruled Notebooks 12 Pack is a smart purchase for those looking for practical, affordable and good quality notebooks. They are ideal for school, university or personal use, offering a balance between durability and comfort. Although they do not have some extras such as perforations or rigid covers, they fulfill their function effectively and are a reliable option for everyday use.

Would make a nice gift for someone you just met or don’t know well

reviews.title: Fountain Pen Ink Friendly! Highly Recommended for Fountain Pens!
reviews.body: I have been looking for this notebook. I didn't want a full legal pad size, nor did I want a "regular" skinny journal size, so the A5 is just right. I wanted a pen loop, an elastic band to hold it closed, and a small pocket. This fit the bill perfectly. I have tried several that fit the bill but would not hold up to fountain pen ink. So, the first thing I did was to test the paper. This notebook advertises 100gsm. Many of the other notebooks I tried claimed to be 100gsm, but they were not. This notebook feels like 100gsm, and I believe it to be. The pages feel smooth crisp and awesome. I grabbed some ink and pens and tested the notebook with the following nibs: <EF>, <F>, and <M>. and the following inks: Pelikan 4001 Brilliant Black, Ostrich 221 Black, Diamine Writers Blood, and Diamine Green/Black. I made some thick lines with heavy line variation, some scribble swatches, writings, drawings, and feeder stress tests in the notebook. There was not one instance of ghosting, shadowing, bleed through, feathering, or any other issue. The reverse side of the page was as usable as the front. The paper is smooth as silk, and it is an excellent notebook. At a far better price than some of the other offering out there. It has an index, an area to write a page number, a date space at the top, and appears very good quality. I am going to immediately order more before they are gone. Most highly recommended!

reviews.title: Well-Made Notebook: Straightforward and Functional
reviews.body: I spent quite a while looking for a dotted notebook that was simple and well made. This one exceeded my expectations. The cover feels nice and is easy to clean (I purchased the black version). The paper quality is good, with a medium thickness that works well for everyday writing. The dotted grid is subtle without being difficult to see. There are plenty of pages, and the notebook lays flat reasonably well when open. I have not experienced any bleed-through with a regular pen. It also has a nice weight to it—not overly light, but not excessively heavy either. The hardcover feels sturdy and well made. The notebook includes useful features such as: a pen holder attached to the back cover, a ribbon bookmark, and a pocket inside the back cover for loose papers or notes. It also includes a small contents section at the front where you can create your own index and reference page numbers. My only suggestion would be to add faint pre-printed page numbers throughout the notebook. The contents section is a useful feature, but it would be even more practical if the pages were already numbered. Overall, the notebook feels higher quality than many of the other dotted-grid options available on Amazon. If you’re looking for a straightforward notebook with good paper quality and useful features, this is a good option. I would and will definitely buy again.

reviews.title: 📝⭐️The Absolute BEST Journal for Early Writers!⭐️📝
reviews.body: 📝 The Mead Primary Journal (Half Page Ruled, Grades K-2) is hands-down the best on the market. The design and layout is the genius of this journal and the half-page format. The top half is completely blank for drawing, coloring, or pasting pictures, and the bottom half features the primary ruling (skip-a-line, dotted midline). This encourages children to fully illustrate their stories and then write the corresponding text, naturally integrating art and literacy. ⭐️ The primary ruling is essential for this age group (Kindergarten through Grade 2). The clear base line and the dotted midline provide the perfect visual cues to help kids practice forming letters correctly, maintaining consistent size, and placing their letters properly on the line. It drastically reduces frustration and messy handwriting. 📝 The quality and durability of the paper is a nice weight—thick enough that markers and heavier pencils don't bleed through easily. The binding is secure and holds up very well to the frequent opening, closing, and rough handling that younger children tend to give their school supplies. ⭐️ It is definitely of educational value, as it is an incredibly effective tool for fostering creative writing, storytelling, and drawing skills. It’s perfect for everything from daily quick writes to full-blown narrative projects. 📝 Overall, if you are a parent or educator looking for the ideal tool to help a young child transition from drawing to writing, this Mead Primary Journal is a non-negotiable must-have. reviews.title: Value + Nostalgia + Sufficient Quality
reviews.body: History More than 20 years ago, Mead Composition books were everywhere in middle school. These were the laptops of the day and back then I used the first-generation Pilot V5 pen in conjunction with these notebooks. And now, more than 20 years later, I've found the Pilot Precise V5 Stick Rolling Ball Pens, Extra Fine Point, Blue Ink, Dozen Box (35335) and the updated Mead Composition Book, college ruled this time around, to be a perfect match for my use. I needed a notebook for making notes to myself, writing ideas, and taking inventory of life. I only recently found that "disposable writings" such as these are better suited to writing long hand, rather than electronically. And having used more expensive notebooks in the past, I found the current-generation Mead Composition book to work perfectly for me. Compared to the others (Moleskine, Clairefontaine, Rhodia) About a decade ago I started using other brands of notebooks, first it was Moleskine which was decent and had some nice touches. However, I cannot currently recommend the Moleskine Cahier Journal (Set of 3), Pocket, Ruled, Kraft Brown, Soft Cover (3.5 x 5.5): set of 3 Ruled Journals as the paper has become rather cheap and the price does not justify the quality, for my needs at least. The Mead Composition book has thicker pages and more quality feeling pages than the Moleskine notebooks, hands down. The same is true for the Moleskine monthly planner in the large size, it is a huge disappointment because the pages are thin and ink bleeds through. Clairefontaine and Rhodia notebooks are top quality, buttery soft pages, solid bindings, made in France, and I highly recommend these notebooks if money is no object and the notebooks are being used for an important purpose. The quality is the highest I've found in notebooks, however, they are four to five times the price of the Mead Composition book and currently too much for my needs. Best value out I became interested in these Mead Composition books after seeing a crowdfunding campaign to bring back higher quality composition books. I learned about the rich history of the black and white cover of the original composition book decades ago. However, the crowdfunding price was nearly $20 for each notebook, so I found that for my use, the Mead Composition book is perfect. The cover isn't thick and hard like it was years ago, the pages are rather cheap, but they are thick thus preventing bleeding from my Pilot V5 pens. The pages do wrinkle easily, but I did count 100 pages, seeing how some other reviewers didn't have all 100 pages. The binding and durability doesn't seem that great, so I would give the quality of the notebook and pages 3 stars out of five, though it is fine for my needs. tl;dr While the more expensive French competition has much better quality, for a disposable/idea notebook for $1.99, the Mead Composition Book cannot be beat based on price and nostalgia factor. Highly recommended.

These were the laptops of the day and back then I used the first-generation Pilot V5 pen in conjunction with these notebooks. And now, more than 20 years later, I've found the Pilot Precise V5 Stick Rolling Ball Pens, Extra Fine Point, Blue Ink, Dozen Box (35335) and the updated Mead Composition Book, college ruled this time around, to be a perfect match for my use. I needed a notebook for making notes to myself, writing ideas, and taking inventory of life. I only recently found that "disposable writings" such as these are better suited to writing long hand, rather than electronically. And having used more expensive notebooks in the past, I found the current-generation Mead Composition book to work perfectly for me. Compared to the others (Moleskine, Clairefontaine, Rhodia) About a decade ago I started using other brands of notebooks, first it was Moleskine which was decent and had some nice touches. However, I cannot currently recommend the Moleskine Cahier Journal (Set of 3), Pocket, Ruled, Kraft Brown, Soft Cover (3.5 x 5.5): set of 3 Ruled Journals as the paper has become rather cheap and the price does not justify the quality, for my needs at least. The Mead Composition book has thicker pages and more quality feeling pages than the Moleskine notebooks, hands down. The same is true for the Moleskine monthly planner in the large size, it is a huge disappointment because the pages are thin and ink bleeds through. Clairefontaine and Rhodia notebooks are top quality, buttery soft pages, solid bindings, made in France, and I highly recommend these notebooks if money is no object and the notebooks are being used for an important purpose. The quality is the highest I've found in notebooks, however, they are four to five times the price of the Mead Composition book and currently too much for my needs. Best value out I became interested in these Mead Composition books after seeing a crowdfunding campaign to bring back higher quality composition books. I learned about the rich history of the black and white cover of the original composition book decades ago. However, the crowdfunding price was nearly $20 for each notebook, so I found that for my use, the Mead Composition book is perfect. The cover isn't thick and hard like it was years ago, the pages are rather cheap, but they are thick thus preventing bleeding from my Pilot V5 pens. The pages do wrinkle easily, but I did count 100 pages, seeing how some other reviewers didn't have all 100 pages. The binding and durability doesn't seem that great, so I would give the quality of the notebook and pages 3 stars out of five, though it is fine for my needs. tl;dr While the more expensive French competition has much better quality, for a disposable/idea notebook for $1.99, the Mead Composition Book cannot be beat based on price and nostalgia factor. Highly recommended.

While a student, I loved the Five Star brand and binders, but I found that system does not work in professional and adult life. Things are much less structured and I need something more flexible. I love that this notebook is smaller, but strong (hardcover and thick paper and spiral bound), I lovee the tabs (makes it super easy to flip to the right place when taking notes quickly). I like there is a big pocket in the back, but I wish there was one for each divider. I also love that each page has the date of the week, memo and date as a header, but I wish it was much bigger. Finally, because it is quite a thick notebook, writing on the last quarter of the page can be a bit uncomfortable. But overall, highly recommend and definitely plan to repurchase this notebook.

reviews.title: Reliable Everyday Companion — Great Value Wide‑Ruled Notebook
reviews.body: The Emraw Composition Notebook Wide Ruled (2 Pack) offers a solid combination of practical features and budget‑friendly value. With durable hard covers, a sewn binding that helps pages stay put, and 100 wide‑ruled sheets (200 pages) per book, it’s a dependable choice for students, note‑takers, or anyone needing reliable paper. The wide‑ruled layout gives generous line spacing, which is nice for legibility. Hardcover and sewn binding mean it feels sturdier than typical cheap notebooks. The marble‑style cover gives it a classic, school‑friendly look. Some points to watch: Paper quality may be basic; some users report thin sheets or bleed‑through with heavier ink. The binding and cover, while decent for the price, aren’t premium; if you’re very rough on notebooks you might want something more heavy‑duty. If you prefer college‑ruled (narrower spacing) instead of wide‑ruled, this might feel too spacious. Verdict: If you’re looking for an affordable, dependable notebook for everyday use — taking notes, journaling, or school work — this Emraw pack is a strong value. It gives the essentials without frills. If you write a lot with fountain pens or heavy markers, you might want to test the paper first or opt for a higher‑spec notebook.

reviews.title: Affordable cute notebook for journaling!!
reviews.body: I got this small little green notebook because I wanted to start journaling. Something small enough that I could take with me, easy to be portable and put into a backpack or purse, and also big enough to actually write on each page. It does come with 140 pages, which is a good amount, and it has a hard cover. With a little band on the back to use and mark the page, as well as a little clear folder to put any papers/stuff in at the back. Nice and convenient little pouch for that! reviews.title: Great Little Notebook for Work Notes
reviews.body: I bought these for work and they have turned out to be the perfect little notebooks. The elastic band is a surprisingly nice feature because it keeps everything together and prevents pages from getting bent up while commuting around. I also like that there's a date section at the top of each page. It makes organizing meeting notes much easier when you're trying to go back and find something later. I admittedly don't use the first couple pages with the index/table of contents setup and usually skip straight to the regular note pages, but that's more of a personal preference than a complaint. The overall quality feels solid, especially for the price. The faux leather cover maybe feels a tiny bit cheaper up close than I initially expected, but honestly once you're actually using it day to day at work, it still looks sleek and put together. Definitely doesn't feel embarrassing to bring into an office or client meeting. I've tried a lot of random notebooks over the years and this one hits a really nice balance of portability, functionality, and appearance. Would absolutely buy again.

reviews.title: My must-have daily notebook
reviews.body: These are my favorite notebooks. I have repurchased and bought for others probably over a dozen times. They are relatively fountain pen friendly. Depends on the ink and nib size but I use a medium nib with Diamine Writers Blood and only have a tiny bit of bleed through if I write over another spot before it is dry (like correcting a letter or something). It does take a second to absorb so don’t flip your page immediately or your ink with smear. Light colored Tom Bows are ok and dark are fine if you don’t build up more than one layer. (Light is pic 3, minimal multi-colored pattern show through in pic 4) The two ribbon book marks are a game changer for me. Price is amazing for what you are getting. I consider these far superior to moleskin for half the price. Page count is great. I have been using the same one as a commonplace (so writing a blurb or two almost every day, give or take) since January ‘26 and am only a little more than halfway through. Lays flat and is still in like new condition even as I throw it in my bag, bring to the beach, etc. (last two photos) Great color selection that is true to the image provided. I can’t say enough good things. I will probably have at least one of these in rotation at all times.

reviews.title: Sturdy, beautiful, and perfect for heavy use.
reviews.body: I use two of these journals at a time: one to plan my novel, and the other as a diary/braindump combo. I don't decorate the pages or do any impressive bujo designs, so I can't speak to how it would serve as a bullet journal. However, these babies see a lot of heavy writing use from me. I've purchased four of them so far and not a single one has disappointed. Page thickness is great. I accidentally spilled water on a couple pages and it didn't bleed through, which was shocking to me, given how affordable this journal is compared to most others listed. The pages are smooth and easy to write on, so be careful with any pens that might smudge or smear. The paper will certainly make it easier to pick up and spread wet ink on your hands. I'm a ballpoint user and I've noticed that finer tips work best, but even with the standard cheap-o pens, I just give them a minute or two to dry and then I'm highlighting all over them with no problem. It's solidly built. I've never had any issue with pages falling out, or the bookmark ribbons unfurling - and I'm writing in my journal at least 3 or 4 hours a day, constantly flipping back and forth through multiple brain dumps. (If you've got ADHD, you understand what I mean.) The color of the cover and ribbons are absolutely stunning, somehow prettier than the pictures show imo. I personalize the covers of my journals with stickers and writing, and whatever I put on has lasted. Overall, this journal has consistently impressed me by serving me well and I couldn't recommend a better one.

reviews.title: Fully equal to many expensive Japanese notebooks & lightyears better than Moleskin. And the Price!
reviews.body: The paper in these RETTACY Notebooks is absolutely fantastic. Smooth to the touch, easy on the eyes, and takes fountain pens as well as ballpoint, rollerball, and pencil all like a dream. The ghosting/show-through through is really minimal, and bleed through almost nonexistent (a tiny bit with a really wet fountain pen). Also works nice with Ranger ink stamp - still no bleed through although there is ghosting/show-through. The lining/grid/dot grids is clear but very subtle and non-distracting. (Do note that the lined notebooks (as opposed to grid, dot grid, or blank) to come with "Date" printed in the upper corner of each page). I think these are easily the equal in quality of Midori MD, Clairefontaine clothbound and Premium C.D. - now, all those (and these) have their own minor aesthetic differences (the Midori paper is creamier and a bit toothier, the Clairefontaine and C.D. is much "slicker"; cover differences, etc.) so everyone will have their favorites - but you won't be disappointed on quality - and how can you beat the price!!!! A million times better than Moleskin

reviews.title: Best Notebook for Organized and Durable Note-Taking!
reviews.body: I’ve been using the Five Star Spiral Notebook for a while now, and it’s by far one of the best notebooks for anyone who values quality and durability. Whether you're a student, a professional, or someone who just loves staying organized, this notebook checks all the boxes. Graph-Ruled Paper The graph-ruled paper is perfect for more than just math. I use it for note-taking, drawing charts, and even sketching out designs. The lines are subtle but provide the perfect structure for clean and organized notes, making it versatile enough for various subjects and uses. Ink Bleed Resistance One of the standout features of this notebook is its ink bleed resistance. I’ve used gel pens, markers, and highlighters on these pages, and they hold up well without bleeding through. This makes it ideal for colorful note-takers or those who prefer using different types of pens. Water-Resistant Cover The water-resistant cover is another major plus. I’ve accidentally spilled water on it before, and not only did the cover repel the water, but the pages inside were protected too. This feature is especially helpful when you’re on the go and need a notebook that can withstand a little wear and tear. Durable Spiral Binding The spiral binding is incredibly sturdy and allows the pages to lay flat or fold back for easy writing. It’s also strong enough to prevent the pages from tearing out easily, even when flipping back and forth frequently. Study App Integration The bonus feature is the study app integration. You can scan your notes and organize them digitally, which is a great tool for students or professionals who like to keep digital backups or want to study on the go. The app is intuitive and easy to use, adding another layer of convenience to an already fantastic product. Overall Experience In conclusion, this Five Star Spiral Notebook is the ultimate tool for those looking for durability, functionality, and versatility in their note-taking. The quality of the paper, the water-resistant cover, and the added value of the study app make this notebook worth every penny. I highly recommend it to anyone who needs a reliable, high-quality notebook for school, work, or personal use.

reviews.title: Bom custo benefício
reviews.body: Gostei bastante deste caderno. Prefiro capas flexíveis às capas duras, pois acho que são mais confortáveis de manusear e machucam menos durante o uso. Também achei a capa bem fácil de limpar em caso de sujeira, como tinta ou outras manchas. Gostei bastante das divisórias internas, que ajudam bastante na organização. O único ponto que não me agradou foi o fato de as folhas serem bem finas e um pouco mais ásperas do que estou acostumada. Mesmo assim, considero que o caderno oferece um ótimo custo-benefício, principalmente quando comparado aos cadernos universitários vendidos no Brasil. As folhas também são bem largas, o que permite escrever bastante conteúdo em cada página. Outro ponto negativo é que a parte de trás da capa é feita de papelão. Portanto, caso molhe, ela pode estufar e deformar. É preciso ter um pouco de cuidado ao apoiar o caderno em superfícies úmidas.
reviews.body_en: I really liked this notebook. I prefer soft covers to hard covers, as I think they are more comfortable to handle and hurt less during use. I also found the cover very easy to clean in case of dirt, such as paint or other stains. I really liked the internal dividers, which help a lot with organization. The only point that I didn't like was the fact that the sheets are very thin and a little rougher than I'm used to. Even so, I consider that the notebook offers great value for money, especially when compared to university notebooks sold in Brazil. The pages are also very wide, which allows you to write a lot of content on each page. Another negative point is that the back of the cover is made of cardboard. Therefore, if it gets wet, it can swell and deform. You need to be a little careful when placing your notebook on damp surfaces.

reviews.title: Updated: Didn’t work for me.
reviews.body: Updated: A month of break-in efforts with all the tips and tricks to soften and stretch the leather did not make these comfortable enough for me to take on a trip for excessive walking. They rub and blister my ankle too much, and heel inserts help a little but not enough for all-day wear. Ended up with a pair of Kiziks that had a lower heel so it doesn’t hit right on my Achilles and required no break in. Prior: I have been trying upwards of a dozen white leather sneakers for an upcoming trip to find the comfiest option for lots of walking, while still being cute enough to go well with sundresses, etc. (not the big Hoka shoe look that does not favor me). I had bought and returned Dr. Scholl's Time Off sneakers after the sole began to separate from the upper after 5 days of wear, and being shockingly uncomfortable (bruise and blister) after a couple days of long walks. So far the Reeboks are the winner for the cushioning and soft leather that won't require a long break-in period, but they run small - I am always a 7.5 in sneakers and am having to return and size up to an 8. They run short and narrow, but I think they're going to be my pick to keep.

reviews.title: VERY SMALL AND TIGHT FITTED, size up!!
reviews.body: I’m an 18 year old girl who was looking for simple white shoes that wasn’t basic air forces that can easily slip on and slip off and am able to comfortably walk around/go about for an entire day (take the bus and get to school and walk around campus for example) without any problems. These shoes were pretty trendy on Pinterest so I bought them. But I had to buy this pair 3 different times before getting the right fit which was quite frustrating! I am normally a perfect size 6, but when it came it was SO abnormally tight, it felt exactly like a size 5 because I have a size 5 pair of shoes. So I ordered a 6.5 instead. Still very tight, practically no difference. I was irritated at this point, why did these run SO small? So finally I bought another pair size 7 and they fit me perfectly and comfortably, not too big or small. They were also 50% off so I’m really grateful for that. I wore them out later today and they were very comfortable, the inside is nice material as well and I rly like the look and color. I can slip these on and off with ease! I’m sure these will be perfect for every day wear when school starts. I would recommend sizing up with these, I don’t have particularly wide or long feet so idk why I seem to one of the only ppl with this sizing issue. I know I’m not typically a size 7 because my size 7 shoes are too big and not wearable as a result. But other than that I’m very happy with these and for the 50% price it can’t be beat

reviews.title: Very pleasantly surprised
reviews.body: I wasn't sure how these would be for me, but I'm surprised and mostly very happy. Pros: I got the deep pink and it's as gorgeous as I hoped. Bonus: I normally wear an 8.5WW size, but saw the recs to size up so I tried a 9. These aren't shown as wide shoes, but they are only a smidge too narrow to fit perfectly properly, but I"m keeping them because they fit well enough. Cons: these are VERY slippery on my kitchen linoleum floor, so "no slip" is quite a stretch. These are fine on pavement, but I really wouldn't wear these if it was raining or if I was going somewhere with very smooth floors. But mine are also suede-ish, so I wouldn't wear those in the rain anyway. The insole padding is...adequate, but I am not 110lbs, and as they are these are a 3K step/day shoe, not a 10-20K step/day shoe. That is, I wouldn't take them on vacation when I average 15-20K steps per day. I already know that would be a painful world of hurt. Though the insoles do seem to be removable, so replacing them with something more formidable could help a lot. The bump/bone below my big toe, which is at about the second lace hole, that's a bit narrow for my feet and will be a hot spot until I stretch it out, but I also have rather wide feet, so someone with narrower feet shouldn't have that concern. The back of the heel seems soft enough that it won't cause blisters, but that's yet to be seen -- these arrived yesterday and I've been wearing them around the house today. Overall, I really do like these, though I'll probably get better insoles so I can wear them for more than an errand or two. These are a great deal for the $30 I paid for them, even if they just become low-step day shoes.

reviews.title: Great for NYC travel & long walking days
reviews.body: I bought these for a weekend trip to New York City and Philadelphia, where I knew I’d be doing a lot of walking. On the first day alone, I walked over 13 miles (including lots of subway stairs and walking between stops), and these shoes held up great. I did wear them every day for about a week before my trip to break them in, which I think helped. I also used blister prevention bandages just to be safe, and I didn’t get a single blister. Overall, I think these shoes are absolutely worth the money. They’re comfortable enough for long days on your feet and stylish enough to wear with just about anything. I’d definitely recommend them if you’re planning a trip where you’ll be walking a lot. The picture below is AFTER the trip.

reviews.title: Real leather?!
reviews.body: These Project Cloud shoes are cute and super comfortable. I am a true size 8 and I would say these run TTS, maybe slightly large. They are very easy to slip my feet into. In fact I may need to tighten up the stretch laces or wear a thicker sock with these because they are pretty roomy. They feel very soft and cushiony, and they're definitely comfortable to walk in. I am dubious of the claim these are made with 100% genuine leather though. I ordered the dark brown and the "leather" parts have no nap whatsoever. When you look closely at the product photos some of the colors definitely look like suede but the dark brown ones look and feel synthetic to me. There is no leather smell. There is also no labeling on the shoe itself indicating these are made with real leather. Up close they look cheap to me. I ordered these on sale so they were under $35, and they are comfy so I'm keeping them. I think they are worth the price I paid but would not pay any more for these shoes. I saw the next day the price went up to around $50 and that's too much, at least for the dark brown ones.

reviews.title: Ordering Again!
reviews.body: This is my third pair of New Balance 608 V5 trainers, and after trying a different color last time (pink), I'm happy to be back to the blue version. My previous blue pair lasted for two years and was incredibly comfortable. The pink pair wasn't quite the same- the leather felt stiffer and never really broke in as well- so I decided to return to what worked. Based on an Amazon review mentioning that the toe box could run a bit narrow, I again ordered the wide width and I'm glad I did. The fit is excellent and feels almost custom-made for my feet. As a woman in her 60s who is prone to foot pain if I walk too much, comfort and support are everything. These shoes, along with the insoles they come with, allow me to walk, hike, and stay active without the aches and pains I've experienced in other trainers. I've spent considerably more on athletic shoes over the years, but these are the pair I come back to. They're comfortable right out of the box, supportive without feeling heavy, and priced surprisingly well for the quality. If you're looking for a dependable walking or everyday shoe, these have earned my recommendation time and time again.

reviews.title: For Weight Lifting
reviews.body: I purchased the New Balance 608 V5 while it was on sale, mainly for weightlifting. These shoes aren't the cutest, but they perform well where it matters most for strength training. The sole is firm and very stable, keeping my feet flat and securely planted on the floor during barbell squats. Unlike cushioned walking or running shoes that compress under weight, these provide a solid, stable base that makes me feel more secure when lifting. Because of that firm construction, don't expect a soft or plush feel. The cushioning is noticeably less than what you'd find in walking or running shoes. The comfort is okay, but that's because the shoe prioritizes stability over softness. The arch support is also fairly minimal. I personally wouldn't recommend these for running since the shoes are quite rigid. If most of your workouts involve walking, jogging, or other cardio, there are more comfortable options available. However, if your main focus is weightlifting or strength training and you want a stable platform for exercises like squats, these work very well. The shoes fit true to size, and I had no issues with the fit. **Pros** * Good stability for barbell squats and strength training * Firm sole keeps your feet flat and securely planted * True to size * Great value when purchased on sale **Cons** * Design is fairly plain and not particularly stylish * Minimal cushioning compared to walking or running shoes * Fairly minimal arch support * Too rigid for running and may not be the best choice for cardio-focused workouts Overall, I think the New Balance 608 V5 is a good choice for anyone looking for a versatile gym shoe with a stable, supportive base for lifting. Just don't expect the soft cushioning or flexibility of a dedicated walking or running shoe.

reviews.title: Still My Favorite Sneakers After 5 Years — So Comfortable and Built to Last
reviews.body: I bought my first pair of these New Balance 608s about five years ago, and they’re still going strong. I wear them for the gym, long walks, and everyday errands, and they’ve held up beautifully — supportive, cushioned, and never once gave me sore feet or knees. As a grandma who’s always on the move, that comfort really matters. I finally decided to get a new pair to start breaking in, but I’ll be honest — I’m still happily wearing my older pair and probably won’t part with them anytime soon. The new ones feel just as sturdy and well‑made, with that same reliable support and soft cushioning that made me fall in love with them in the first place. If you want a sneaker that’s comfortable right out of the box, holds up for years, and works for both walking and workouts, these are a fantastic choice. I’ve trusted them for half a decade, and they continue to be my go‑to.

reviews.title: Lightweight, comfortable and versatile — perfect travel sneakers
reviews.body: I'm 41 years old, 5'2" and about 120 Ibs. I normally wear a size 6-6.5, and my foot measures approximately 9.2 inches long. I ordered a size 6, B gray Before purchasing these, I owned only three pairs of sneakers: running shoes, black platform Adidas, and white platform Reeboks. Since I'm petite, I generally prefer sneakers with some height when wearing jeans or casual outfits. However, my platform sneakers aren't ideal for long walks or workouts, which creates a problem whenever I travel. I usually end up choosing between bringing comfortable athletic shoes and bringing sneakers that look better with my casual outfits-or packing both, which I really don't want to do because I travel as lightly as possible. I was looking for ONE pair that could handle long days of walking and hotel-gym workouts, while still looking good enough with jeans and casual outfits and giving me a little extra height. Since I'm petite with relatively slim legs, finding athletic shoes that don't look overwhelmingly bulky on me can be difficult. I’m genuinely impressed with these sneakers. I sized down based on other reviews, and that was definitely the right decision. The size 6 fits comfortably. My toes on my left foot do slightly touch the front of the shoe, so I was initially concerned about the fit. However, I wore them for approximately five hours of almost nonstop walking, and my feet never hurt. They remained comfortable the entire time. They’re also extremely lightweight, which is another huge advantage for travel. I tried them with several less-athletic outfits and was pleasantly surprised by how well they worked. They still have an athletic appearance, but not so much that I feel limited to wearing them exclusively with workout clothes. I probably wouldn’t choose these as my primary everyday sneakers for regular casual outfits at home or workouts because I have other sneakers specifically for that purpose. For travel, however, these are exactly what I was looking for: lightweight, comfortable enough for extensive walking and workouts, versatile enough for casual outfits, and with enough height that I don’t feel like I’m wearing completely flat running shoes. So far, I’m extremely happy with my purchase and these will definitely be my designated travel sneakers. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

reviews.title: SIZE UP - DON’T REMOVE ANY TAGS OR STICKERS YET.
reviews.body: DETAILED REVIEW : BUY A SIZE AND A HALF UP, DON’T PEEL OFF ANY LABELS OR TAGS YET UNTIL YOU’RE SURE THEY FIT. [July 31st 2026] I am a solid size 9 wide in women’s shoes, with semi-flat feet. It’s hard to find supportive and affordable sneakers. Never purchased Skechers before but I really needed a comfortable, lightweight, affordable shoe for wide support. Read thoroughly through reviews and determined that I should buy a half size up for breathing room. Purchased a 9.5 wide, (Delivered SO fast by the way, next day immediately, I don’t even have prime. For me they arrived in perfect+new condition.), tried just one on, and the sole+arch+heel support was PERFECT and so cushioned. Loved the look of them, but unfortunately they were just an inch too short for the length of my foot, my big toe was *just* scuffing against the tip of the shoe, even in my thinnest/smallest pair of socks. Truly as advertised, minus the sizing discrepancy - which was user error due to my ignorance of the brand styling and sizing. Honestly if you’re scanning through reviews and at your wits end, just order a single size, or a size and a half up. This is the way of ordering online when you can’t try the product on immediately. The shoe is comfortable and easy to slip on and tie. Laces are a little short but they’re genuinely fine to tie loosely about once, twice if you pull them taut for more length. Easy to replace the laces if you’re particular about that. Such a cute shoe, it was perfect for what I needed - absolutely worth reordering for the correct size, I don’t even mind the return process because I caught a glimpse of a genuinely worthwhile, simple, straightforward shoe that I’ll wear often for walking+working out. Even arrived in an adhesive-lined, resealable, bag for convenient and secure returns if needed be - I got a free return! Just printed the labels and secured them on the bag, and inside. (The default order for me arrived with the resealable adhesive lined bag, and inside of that was the brand’s shoe box, for anyone curious on those details.) Don’t stress! Take the leap of faith on the Skechers D’Lites. Order up a size, and at most a size and a half, so your toes aren’t squished if you need that space. Excited to receive my 10 wides! Edit, Monday August 24th, 2026: 10 Wides came in! Perfect fit with extra breathing room - Got 16,000 steps in already! Will definitely have to use some supportive shoe inserts later on in their lifespan as I can already feel the sole compressing downward, but these shoes are great for my long walks so far.

reviews.title: Surpassed expectations on vacation with zero break-in period
reviews.body: Initially thought they might perform poorly. Was insanely impressed. These shoes came and I almost immediately thought of my 70 year old dad--they are bulky, blinding white, and very "utilitarian", thought grandpa shoes are having a moment and I was also sort of going for that look. I panic-bought these the night before a 10 day Ireland vacation because the options i owned for city and country walking shoes were primarily limited to chacos and some very thin mesh runners. I thought the plastic vinyl on these would perform better than my existing footwear and boy---did they.! They arrived 24 hours before departure so I had zero break in. I wore them to the airport to save space in my luggage and to test them out. Guys--I never took them off. These shoes kept my feet warm and dry in an absolute monsoon hike, handled city streets without causing me any back or leg fatigue, and looked equally stylish with my skirts and dresses as with pants. I had zero blisters or pain. They still look excellent despite being put through the ringer and logging over a hundred miles in 10 days. I cannot recommend these enough and am honestly not sure what I would have worn the entire trip had I not brought them along.

reviews.title: Didn't fit my narrow feet, but still excellent shoes at a great low price
reviews.body: These are some of the lightest shoes I've ever seen, but the build quality appears to be excellent. They're tongue-less, like slip-ons, but unlike some, you can adjust the tightness with the laces. The body of the shoe is a mesh-like fabric, which allows good breathability and overall comfort, and the soles are a molded rubbery material with nice treads for grip. I've been wearing a name-brand shoe made very similarly for a couple of years, and these are a very good likeness of them, at a much lower price. I like them because of the light weight and the fabric, which make them feel almost like you're barefoot. Unfortunately for me, I have narrow feet, and these fit more like a D width shoe, with more room in the toe box than I can handle. I'm returning them for that reason. For people with "normal" feet, these make really nice, stylish and comfortable shoes. I don't know how well they would hold up to sports or running, but for walking and day-to-day wear, they're great. I suppose I could grade them down because they don't fit my feet, but I find lots of shoes don't, and many makers use D width as the default for men's shoes. So I'm still rating them as 5 stars.

reviews.title: Why not 5 stars, you ask???
reviews.body: Because I couldn’t give 3.5. Profession: food server. Time spent on my feet and in these shoes 8 hoursa day, 5 days a week. I have been a food server longer than I’d care to talk about. lol. In reality I think I have tried every non slip shoe that is out there. From $30-300. I do not mind paying for quality. That being said. Let me give you my pros and cons. Pros They are ACTUALLY non-slip! Not slip resistant not skid resistant, but NON-slip. They have a thick cushiony sole that makes you feel like you’re walking in air. For a while…. They are cute enough for work shoes. They are breathable They are affordable. I would call the price. Mid range. They have haven’t ripped torn or fallen apart in anyway. But I would not expect that to happen to 2 month old shoes. Because of the massive amount of steps I take each day just on my shift the crapped out fast. (I walk somewhere between 17,000 and 20,000 steps at work alone. I normally replace all work shoes every 3-4 months. This my normal. I’m older and after that time I can feel every step I take. My feet start hurting. My knees back and even my hips. These only made it 2 months before I HAD to reorder. Started feeling every step all over my whole body! Cons: to me they do not hold up the way I would expect a $60 work shoe to hold up. I normally purchase another brand and my shoe is in the $60 range. And I can sometimes go 6 months until I reorder. So while I feel the initial comfort is there. If you walk a lot. I think it won’t be long before they need replacing. I also wish there was more of a style selection. Recap: other than the fact that I need to replace them too often they’re great! But to me that’s a HUGE issue. Because I’m dependent on them every single day!! As most people in the industry are. Just my two cents.

They are not a "cure" but make me feel much more stable when walking and have less knee pain.

reviews.title: Very comfy and supportive for wide feet.
reviews.body: I wasn’t sure what to expect from a “generic” brand sneaker. I have wide feet, and an ankle that tends to swell due to a previous break. I’ve tried several pairs of the Skechers slip-ins, but found them not wide enough and the ankle and top of my foot was way too tight. So I purchased these as basically a “what have I got to lose?” option, thinking I’d be returning them when I tried them on and they didn’t fit. Imagine my surprise when they fit great! I love that they have workable laces, so I can actually tighten them or loosen if necessary, but I haven’t had to so far. The slip on feature works great; I can slip them on or off easily, but the heel doesn’t collapse and my foot feels quite supported. I walked several miles today wearing low socks, and the shoes didn’t cause the socks to slide down. The sole is very comfy, and I haven’t even had to add my arch supports to them. Time will tell how long they last, but so far I would highly recommend them and I would definitely purchase again.

reviews.title: Great for pregnancy related foot pain
reviews.body: I've been wanting a pair of hokas for the last few years but couldn't justify the price. I'm currently 20 weeks pregnant and starting to experience a lot of foot pain at the end of active days and my other pair of tennis shoes are nearing their end of their life so I decided now is the time. They are definitely worth it. I took my dog for a long walk after work as I sometimes do and usually my feet would be hurting when I get home and need all night to recover, but with these, my feet felt pretty normal. I'm glad I didn't wait. For shoes, I'm usually anywhere between a 7.5-9. My feet are pretty narrow with some bad bunions. For tennis shoes specifically, I usually go for an 8. Since I'm pregnant, I got the 8.5 and they fit well. I have just a little extra room in case of swelling or flattening. I hope they last all of my pregnancy and a few months after postpartum. Then I'll probably considering getting another pair.

reviews.title: Comfortable, Properly Snug And On In Two Seconds.
reviews.body: Although your typical 'foreign-made' shoe (Vietnam this time) the 'Slip-in' feature that I made fun of when 1st appearing on TV, turns out to be the lazy-man's dream. Just when you're wondering how much lazier, and fatter can we become, along comes slip-in shoes that look like a traditional shoe, feel comfortable, and properly 'snug' so you don't have heal-rub or feel like the shoe won't stay on...it will!. Construction is solid and the tread/traction is good. So I assume just like our 1st cars with power windows and locks, after these shoes, there's no going back? I did add 3/4 insoles, and the fit still feels fine...comfortable and snug. I don't think I'll abandon my traditional shoes, but check back this time next year and I may have a different story to tell. Does anyone remember Pixar's movie WALL-E! Well, I feel my new Skechers hands free slip-in sneaker's, and my expanding waistband are aiming me in that direction, and fast. I would buy again.

reviews.title: Good for value, not many complaints!
reviews.body: I'll start by saying these are genuinely good value, based on my experience so far — with the caveat that I'm measuring that relative to other similarly priced running shoes. The cushioning is adequate for anyone who isn't a hardcore runner; I'm not, and found the Surge 4s to be no hindrance whatsoever when running. I went all-black, and they look very sleek with a nice overall silhouette. The arch support is sufficient, though it feels quite neutral. For what you pay, especially if you catch a deal, they perform well. As for fit, I'd recommend sizing up half a size — I found my toes making a lot of contact with the front of the toe box, and going half a size up largely resolved that. No real break-in period required from what I could tell; they're pretty much plug-and-play, or rather, run-and-go.

reviews.title: Love the look, but sizing way off- has pros and cons
reviews.body: I'm female but men's sneakers tend to fit better. I like the way these Under Armour sneakers look. They have good symmetry according to the shape of the human foot. I also really liked the lacing system. It was these thick rounded "protrusions" of material so that the laces could go through, and the way these "eyelets" are shaped (thicker and flat) you would need fewer of them to make the shoe lace stretch out over what would be two eyelets. This is good because on one hand it may be trouble to string a shoe lace over a lot of regular style eyelets (holes on the area which I think may be called an "eyestay") but then if you skip putting the lace into some eyelets then , in my opinion it gives the distribution of of the lace on the sneaker a very awkward look, if you can get what I mean. I really dislike lacing systems in which there are just thin strips of string (or sometimes short strips of "ribbon" ) sticking out of the sides on top of the sneaker where the tongue is. If the string or strip of ribbon breaks then it is not easy to repair or is even impossible to repair. It makes the entire sneaker useless. So the lacing system on the Under Armour Men's Charged Surge 4 Sneaker is overall my favorite kind . I also like that the area of the highest eyelet is not rigid and hard. It is important for the upper-eyelet area of a sneaker or shoe to be properly flexible and /or cushioned (though also not of flimsy material). The area of the upper-most eyelet is the area that will push right into your upper foot as you bend your foot in the process of walking or running. This can hurt or cause friction. However , as with other Under Armour sneakers I find that at least certain styles can have odd sizing. I normally use a Women's size 10 so that translates to Men's 8 to 8.5 (which can depend on the style) but I find that in Under Armour I have to use a complete size up. I ordered these UA's in size 9.5. I tried them on. They fit but I was not sure if they would start to hurt my toes should I start walking long distances in them. I could not risk it. I sent them back. I may re-order them in a larger size even though they would look a bit too big. Another thing I did not like about this sneaker is that the sole at the heel part is designed in a way that when you walk with the sneakers on they make a noise like a shoe with a very hard heel with sharp edges would make, not a softer light noise like a sneaker should make. I do wish that this sneaker came in slightly wider widths. It may feel more comfortable than having a rather pointed type of toe-box area. So there are pros and cons to this sneaker at least in my opinion. I would definitely recommend them though. It can depend on your needs.

reviews.title: Retro Sneakers That Have Become a Favorite Birthday Gift
reviews.body: Finding birthday gifts for teenagers can be surprisingly difficult because they're old enough to know exactly what they like but young enough that trends seem to change every few months. When our daughter spotted these retro sneakers, she immediately loved the classic look, so we decided to surprise her with them for her birthday. The first thing she commented on after opening the box was how comfortable they felt. They didn't require much of a break-in period, which is always a pleasant surprise with new shoes. The cushioned sole provides enough support for walking around all day, whether she's at work, running errands, or spending time with friends. She also really likes the vintage styling. The retro design pairs well with jeans, shorts, and casual dresses, making them much more versatile than some of the trendier shoes that only work with certain outfits. They've quickly become one of the first pairs she reaches for when getting ready in the morning. We've also been impressed with how well they've held up. The stitching looks solid, the sole still feels secure, and they've cleaned up nicely after regular use. Shoes that can survive everyday wear while still looking good are always appreciated. Overall, these turned out to be one of her favorite birthday gifts. They combine comfort, style, and everyday practicality in a way that's hard to beat. If you're looking for casual sneakers with a classic look that can easily become part of someone's regular wardrobe, these are an excellent choice.

reviews.title: Cute sneakers
reviews.body: These shoes are very cute and I love the green color. They are a faux suede material, which is expected at this price, although the materials listing says leather. PU leather is not leather. That's a pet peeve of mine. It's a polyurethane product. There is a moderate amount of cushioning. For me - and I have very sensitive feet - I would not be able to wear these all day; they are not supportive enough. But for a few hours shopping or somewhere where I was sitting a majority of the time, they would be great because they're such a fun design. They hark back to sneakers from the 70's and 80's. I found the size spot on. I wear an 8.5 and they fit perfectly. They did rub a little on one of my heels. The rubber sole is good and I would not expect it to slip. The price is very good for a casual sneaker and having little fun knockabout shoes in a unique color makes them worth the price.

reviews.title: Retro Cool!
reviews.body: I love these sneakers! I have feet that are, unfortunately, very wide- to be quite honest, I look like a duck from the ankle down. Needless to say, that makes it very difficult to find shoes that not only fit but fit comfortably. Adding to the difficulty is the fact that it seems different brands have different ideas of sizes. Certain brands have women's size 10 shoes that fit more like an 8 and others have size 10 that fit like an 11. This makes it almost impossible to buy shoes online. However, that is not the case with these! I ordered a size 10 and they fit like a size 10! They have a toe box that isn't overly narrow so my toes have enough room to feel comfortable and blister-free and the sole has a nice amount of cushioning that makes them extremely comfortable to wear! Another great thing? The style of the shoe itself- it's super versatile! I can wear these shoes just as easily with jeans or sweats as I can with dressier slacks or even a dress if I wanted. Dress them up or dress them down, these are great shoes for the office in my opinion- especially if you are one who takes public transportation to/from work and have a bit of a walk from the bus or train station to the office. All told, I think they're great and seem to be very sturdy in construction and as though they will hold up over time!

I like that they have a fairly simple design without looking boring, and the classic sole adds just enough contrast to make them stand out. They feel comfortable for everyday walking and casual wear, and the padded interior gives them a softer feel than I expected. The sole also feels sturdy and provides a good amount of grip on normal surfaces. They are lightweight enough that they do not feel clunky, but still have enough structure to feel supportive during regular use. The laces make it easy to adjust the fit, and the overall shape is flattering without making the shoe look bulky. My only minor criticism is that they are more of a casual everyday sneaker than something I would choose for serious athletic training, but that is really what I expected from this style. Overall, these are comfortable, good looking sneakers with a versatile retro design that is easy to pair with everyday clothes.

I wanted a nice, casual sneaker that I could wear to work and around town, and I was hoping these would do the trick. These shoes run true to size. I ordered the same size I wear in my running shoes, but I probably should have gone down a half size, like I usually do with sandals and other casual shoes. My initial disappointment was that they have very little built-in support. Fortunately, because they were slightly too large, I had enough room to add my own inserts. reviews.title: Did not live up to hype
reviews.body: I bought this shoe because of so many positive reviews both on line and from people I know. The color was good and the slip on factor was also good and so easy to just slip right into them and kick them off at the end of the day. The size was good too. Many people claimed it doesn’t need to be broken in so I thought great, I could buy them and wear them to Europe for a 10 day tour. However, what I experienced was that they rubbed against the back of my ankle and I had a blister. Maybe they would be good if I was just walking 10k steps. Admittedly, we were doing an average of 20k steps and up cliff-sides. Maybe that’s too much for them. The Sketchers I bought handled the daily grind of this trip much better at a much lower price point. I ended up leaving the Cloud 9 in my bag and wearing them the rest of the trip. Now they sit in my cubby collecting dust because I’m too worried about getting blisters. I guess they’re not for everyone. They are light, they are great slip ons, and they are comfortable when you first put them on. That’s why they still get 3 stars
