title: PUMA Men's Voltaic Evo Cross Trainer Shoes

reviews.title: Wonderful lots of compliments
reviews.body: *PUMA Men's Voltaic Evo Running Shoe*** In the world of athletic footwear, finding the perfect balance between comfort, performance, and style can often feel like an impossible feat. But the *PUMA Men’s Voltaic Evo Running Shoe* rises to the occasion, offering an unparalleled combination of cutting-edge technology, sleek design, and all-day comfort that makes every run feel like a victory lap. Whether you're a seasoned marathoner, a weekend jogger, or someone just starting to get active, these shoes are engineered to take your performance to the next level, without compromising on style or durability. **The Perfect Fusion of Performance and Comfort** From the moment you lace up the *PUMA Voltaic Evo Running Shoe*, you’ll immediately notice the difference. It’s not just a running shoe—it’s a performance-enhancing tool that’s been meticulously designed to provide maximum support, flexibility, and comfort with every stride. At the heart of this shoe is its cutting-edge *IGNITE foam technology*, which offers exceptional energy return, cushioning, and responsiveness. The foam adapts to the unique needs of your foot, offering a soft yet springy feel that propels you forward with each step. Whether you’re running on pavement, trails, or even hopping onto a treadmill, the *Voltaic Evo* makes every footfall feel light and effortless, while still providing the support you need to push through the toughest runs. **Lightweight Yet Durable: Built for Long-Lasting Performance** One of the standout features of the *PUMA Voltaic Evo* is its **lightweight construction**. This shoe won’t weigh you down or slow you up, making it perfect for both long-distance runners and those who want a fast, responsive feel. The lightweight design means you can run longer without experiencing the fatigue that comes with heavier footwear, while the sturdy build ensures that the shoes will hold up even through intense training sessions. Despite being incredibly light, the *Voltaic Evo* doesn’t sacrifice durability. PUMA has designed these shoes with a reinforced **rubber outsole** that provides exceptional traction and grip. Whether you're running on slick surfaces or tackling uneven ground, you can rely on the shoe’s robust traction to keep you steady. The shoe’s outsole is crafted with strategically placed grooves to offer better flexibility, ensuring that your foot moves naturally while still providing grip where you need it most. **Breathable and Supportive: The Ultimate Fit** The *PUMA Voltaic Evo Running Shoe* is all about keeping your feet cool and comfortable, no matter how intense your workout may be. The engineered mesh upper ensures that your feet stay well-ventilated, reducing heat buildup and moisture during long runs. Say goodbye to uncomfortable sweaty feet and hello to a breathable, dry, and comfortable running experience. The shoe also features a **sock-like fit**, which provides a snug yet flexible embrace for your foot, preventing slipping or uncomfortable rubbing. The padded collar and heel counter offer extra support around the ankle, ensuring a secure and customized fit that adapts to the shape of your foot, giving you stability and confidence in every stride. **Sleek Design Meets Bold Innovation** Let’s talk about style. The *PUMA Voltaic Evo* doesn't just perform—it makes a statement. With its sleek, modern design, this shoe is sure to turn heads wherever you go. Available in a variety of colorways, you’ll find a look that suits your personal style—whether you prefer bold, eye-catching hues or more understated, minimalist tones. The distinctive PUMA branding adds a touch of flair, while the streamlined silhouette ensures that this shoe looks as good as it feels. Whether you’re using it as your go-to running shoe or as a stylish everyday sneaker, the *Voltaic Evo* offers a dynamic, athletic aesthetic that fits seamlessly into any wardrobe. Its design is as much about functionality as it is about making a bold statement. **Breath-Taking Comfort: Ideal for All-Day Wear** While the *PUMA Voltaic Evo* is undeniably a performance shoe, it’s also built for comfort throughout the entire day. The shoe’s cushioning system ensures that every step feels plush, while the flexible construction allows for natural movement, whether you're sprinting at full speed or walking casually around town. Its combination of breathability, support, and responsive cushioning means you can wear these shoes for hours on end without experiencing discomfort or fatigue. So whether you’re out on a run or running errands, the *Voltaic Evo* will keep your feet feeling fresh and comfortable all day long. **Perfect for Every Runner** The *PUMA Men’s Voltaic Evo Running Shoe* is engineered to meet the needs of every runner, from the beginner to the seasoned marathoner. Its combination of lightweight comfort, high-performance cushioning, and superior traction makes it an ideal choice for anyone who’s serious about improving their athletic performance. Whether you're hitting the pavement, the track, or your local trails, these shoes provide the right mix of support and flexibility to help you perform at your peak. For those who value a responsive and energetic feel underfoot, the *Voltaic Evo* excels. The shoe’s **IGNITE foam** cushioning system ensures that energy from each stride is returned, propelling you forward without requiring excessive effort. Its **outstanding traction** allows you to take on various surfaces with confidence, and its **sock-like fit** ensures that you’ll have stability without the risk of blisters or discomfort. **Final Verdict: The Running Shoe of the Future** In conclusion, the *PUMA Men’s Voltaic Evo Running Shoe* is a masterpiece of design and performance, blending cutting-edge technology with sleek aesthetics to deliver a shoe that’s not only functional but also a joy to wear. Its lightweight build, superior cushioning, and durable construction make it the perfect companion for runners of all levels, offering both comfort and performance in one dynamic package. The breathable upper, sock-like fit, and exceptional traction all come together to make the *Voltaic Evo* a truly exceptional choice for anyone who’s serious about their athletic endeavors. If you’re in the market for a running shoe that can keep up with your pace while still turning heads, look no further than the *PUMA Voltaic Evo Running Shoe*. Whether you’re racing down the track, running errands, or simply enjoying a leisurely jog, these shoes provide the comfort, support, and style you need to take on the day with confidence. Once you slip your feet into these shoes, you’ll quickly realize that the *Voltaic Evo* isn’t just a running shoe—it’s an experience.

reviews.title: Comfortable, lightweight, and true to size
reviews.body: I work on my feet all day for 10 hour shifts on concrete. I need a shoe that's supportive, comfortable, durable, and lightweight. I've only had these shoes for a day and I can say so far they're comfortable, supportive, and lightweight. The first thing I noticed is they're very true to size. I typically wear a 43 EU wide shoe, so I checked the size chart and ordered the corresponding 11 wide. They fit like a glove right out of the box. I also like the wide variety of colors they come in. It's very hard to find fun, colorful shoes if you have larger feet, much less ones that also come in wide widths. So finding these in my size was a huge plus (I got the raspberry and electric lime on black). I like the thin, stretchy heel cup that hugs my heel rather than the typical thick, plushy heel cups that most shoes have, which is just foam that covers a sharp plastic stabilizer. The first place my shoes always wear out is the heel cup, and I'm being stabbed in the heel with that plastic stabilizer. I'm hoping this shoe won't have that issue due to the different heel cup design. They are definitely supportive and I can feel the arch support on the inside of my feet. I tend to underpronate so arch support is important for me. While they are true to size, there isn't much vertical room in the shoe for any additional insert. I typically put some odor eaters inserts in my shoes (again, 10 hour shifts) and they made the shoe a little snug on top. I'm sure they'll loosen up as they wear in, but it's something to keep in mind if you typically wear an orthotic or use another type of insert. They're also very lightweight. I don't feel like I'm clunking around in a heavy brick of a shoe, like I sometimes get with very cushiony shoes. Shoes that are too heavy tend to fatigue my feet and legs after long shifts. They're not so light that I forget I'm wearing a shoe, but they're also not noticeably heavy either. I wish the toe box was just a little wider, but it's not squishing my toes a noticeable amount. I just tend to prefer a wide, roomy toe box. This one is probably a little wider than a typical athletic shoe, but just not as wide as I wish it was. Overall, so far very happy with the shoe. Will update if I run into any problems, but if they continue to perform excellently I can see myself buying another pair.

reviews.title: Great shoes
reviews.body: These Reebok BB4500 Hi2 high tops are a solid throwback-style sneaker, but they definitely feel more like a lifestyle shoe than anything performance-focused. First impression is good — the design has that classic high-top basketball look and they’re easy to wear with jeans or casual outfits. They look better in person than I expected, especially if you like retro styling. Comfort is decent for everyday use, but not amazing for all-day standing or heavy walking. The cushioning is fairly basic, so after a few hours you can start to feel the lack of support compared to more modern sneakers. Fit runs a bit narrow for me, especially in the toe box, and there’s a short break-in period before they start feeling more comfortable. Once broken in, they’re fine for casual wear, but not something I’d choose for long walks or sports. Build quality feels okay for the price — not premium, but not cheap either. The leather upper holds up well, and the outsole seems durable enough for regular street use. Overall, these are good for style and casual everyday wear, especially if you like the retro basketball look, but they’re not a comfort-heavy or performance shoe.

reviews.title: Secondo me, una gran scarpa da running che sta bene anche con i jeans.
reviews.body: Al di là del fatto che sono uno sportivo da sempre, devo ammettere che ho una passione sfegatata per le scarpe da ginnastica. Ne compro in continuazione, non riesco a smettere. Ne ho circa 30 paia dei miei marchi prediletti, che non son pochi. Naturalmente, Under Armour figura nella lista ed anche fra le prime posizioni per preferenza. Non sono fra le scarpe più "tecniche" ma sono sicuramente fra le più belle e confortevoli che si possano trovare sul mercato. Queste UA Charged Assert 10 sono bellissime e ben studiate. La calzata è ottima, la scarpa fascia bene e la suola, secondo me, ha la giusta consistenza per supportare una buona corsa offrendo ammortizzazione e rimbalzo ma senza cedere sotto il peso del passo. Per intenderci, la suola è in espanso, non tipo memory: non è di quelle che danno la sensazione di camminare sulle uova sode tipo Skechers o come svariate Nike. Quelle ultra-morbide, stile pantofola, van bene per pochi passi, un volo in aereo magari ma non si può andarci a correre o camminarci sopra per turismo un'intera giornata, non senza poi avere male ai piedi. Per correre ci vuole una suola come quella di queste Under Armour: non rigida ma reattiva e sostenuta e, la tomaia, non può essere un calzino. Anche quella deve offrire un po' di struttura su tutti i lati. Questa è una scarpa studiata da corsa e presenta i giusti contenuti tecnici. Se poi non è la prestazione sportiva ad interessarvi e state valutando questa scarpa come sneaker da jeans, beh, secondo me siete comunque nel posto giusto perché a livello estetico, queste scarpe, non hanno nulla da invidiare ad Adidas, Puma, Nike e compagnia bella. Per quanto riguarda i numeri, posso dirvi che io ho generalmente un 42 e, da sempre, su Under Armour acquisto il 42,5 con successo. Ciao!
reviews.body_en: Beyond the fact that I have always been an athlete, I must admit that I have a huge passion for sneakers. I buy them all the time, I can't stop. I have about 30 pairs of my favorite brands, which is quite a few. Naturally, Under Armor is on the list and also among the top positions for preference. They are not among the most "technical" shoes but they are certainly among the most beautiful and comfortable that can be found on the market. These UA Charged Assert 10 are beautiful and well thought out. The fit is excellent, the shoe fits well and the sole, in my opinion, has the right consistency to support a good run, offering cushioning and rebound but without giving in under the weight of the step. To be clear, the sole is made of foam, not the memory type: it is not one of those that give the sensation of walking on hard-boiled eggs like Skechers or like various Nikes. The ultra-soft, slipper-style ones are fine for a few steps, maybe a plane flight but you can't go running or walk on them for tourism for an entire day, not without having pain in your feet. To run you need a sole like the one on these Under Armor ones: not rigid but reactive and supported and the upper cannot be a sock. That also needs to offer some structure on all sides. This is a shoe designed for racing and has the right technical contents. If it is not the sporting performance that interests you and you are considering this shoe as a denim sneaker, well, in my opinion you are still in the right place because on an aesthetic level, these shoes have nothing to envy of Adidas, Puma, Nike and co. As for the numbers, I can tell you that I generally have a 42 and, on Under Armor, I have always purchased the 42.5 with success. HI!

I really wanted to love them, but for the price, I expected them to hold up much longer.

title: Skechers Men's Vigor 2.0 Trait Memory Foam Sneaker

reviews.title: Great sneaker, one of the most comfortable fitting Skechers I own
reviews.body: New Review: For Charcoal Grey with Black Accents - Size 13 XW (my first Skechers XW I have ever tried) This review is based on my initial impressions after wearing them for a bit, though (so they last longer) not wearing them for my usual few mile walk. I bought these in 13-W when my usual Skechers size is 13 M and to be fair I think I can get away with 12.5 M but I have always got 13's "force of habit". I saw the great price on these 13 XW’s and despite never trying the Wide Width Sketchers on until today, to took a chance on these. First .. I have a black and gray pair of the Vigor's and while Memory Foam or non-Memory Foam Skechers ... I have loved the fits of all of them. (There is a reason this is my go-to brand, even if my newer Sketchers do not last as long before needing a repair or two, like Skechers bought a few years back). The Vigors for some reason are THE MOST comfortable "model" of Skechers I have, and I have no complaints about any of them. I am just going to sort of aswer my own pre-buy question about the Wide Widths here. I do realize that every single person's foot is different but I will give a little background. Before Skechers, I was not buying the "top brands" (though i did have two pairs of Reebox that lasted a decent amount of time and felt great).... No matter the brand or size I was at the time (talking back in High School)... the brands I went with seemed so narrow that I always went with wide-width ... ALWAYS. Every since I bought my first pair of Skechers, I never needed to... the M aka normal fit was always great. As I said I bought these XW width, because of the sale (nearly 1/2 of the retail price). My question (pre-purchase) was are they like significantly wider… dare I say “comically” wide. Around the upper is where I notice it most and MAYBE right toward the middle left to right (barely) but .. they ARE wider it seems but nothing that would make me want to return them like “oh that is way too much for me”. I have ONE pair of New Balance and it is XW too and it’s sort of the same thing in a way … I prefer the regular fit (say in Skechers I’d describe the 12/12.5’s that SOMEHOW fit me ok .. as “comfortably snug” … I feel the sneaker all around my foot but even the normal fits are NOT TIGHT), but the XW (maybe just tied a tad tighter to make them feel more like the normal fits) are A-OK for me so far. Maybe when I wear these out for a long walk I may change my mind, but I think they will be ok. Assuming I do not have the issues some others have had with the eye-lits holding the laces tearing (for the record I have seen that in negative reviews but never had a pair of Skechers do that to me BEFORE)... I am happy with these. I would go with regular (M) 13's in the future but if a style I like comes up on a good sale XW width … I’d be ok with them I think. The Memory foam is great and as I said the other Vigors are the most comfortable pair of Skechers I have and I already LOVE the fits of all the other models. I am not sure how long the memory foam will last but some people say that when their's go, the "sneakers are trashed" ...eh ... for me I usual have some extra padded insoles that make sneakers feel like slippers they are so comfortable. Even WHEN (and it will go ... it's just nature) the memory foam goes bad so to speak... I will just slip a pair of those insoles I have anyway in and no big deal. The Fit back to front is great (as always with Skechers from my experience) and as far as a few negative reviews go saying how they are the most uncomfortable sneaker they ever had ... I just question A) if they are getting the correct size ... B) sort of the same thing ... do they need wide width for wide feet and getting regular width, maybe? ... The one thing I CANT comment on with this exact pair though i have to say other Skechers I have gotten recent needed to be repaired sooner than I'd like (the Black Downforce model I have comes to mind)... so longevity I cant comment on, even though I admit (note: I wear mine a lot in the sun in Florida summers so maybe adhesive wise holding the sneakers together, the extreme temps and humidity play a role. With Skechers (unlike my one pair of Filas which ... are ok now i admit) there has NEVER been a "break-in" period for me. Years back even with the Reebox that i liked .. there was at least a few day break-in period before they'd go from "ok/good" to "REALLY comfy". One thing I almost missed before finishing this review is that I have a pair of Pebble(brown)/Black "Afterburn - Strike off" sneakers and while i like them I thought the brown in them was going to at least in part be "Suede like". I just noticed that while not all of the grey/charcoal in this pair is ... some is that suede type material … I really like that sort of look, myself .. not sure how long it will stay looking good in the hot Florida summers though. As if i even have to say it, I am happy with my purchase and would recommend these. I just HOPE they last longer than they did for some other people who had bad luck with them. Update after one, 2-4 mile walk. - I have to say that I still do like the regular 13's better but these ... these aren't bad. If anything, AT TIMES it seemed like they were slightly too big and while in a steady stride (I do a constant walk ... not slow... not a run either) ... these seemed almost normal. I also have to say that while I have tied the tops a little tigher... i have not messed with the way they are somewhat losely laced, out of the box. Really right now the ONLY way I'd return these is for the same price or lower, I could return these for a full refund AND get the same exact style and color for instance in 13 M's (regular fit), but even then I'd say these are not bad at all ... if things change more overtime i cant say but "slightly bigger" than I'd like is not bad at all and I got a GREAT deal on these price wise. -------------------------------------- Original Review for a Black with Grey accent.... Size 13 (My usual size) First (even with that title) I want to preference this by saying I have only worn these around the house a bit .. I want to keep them in good shape, longer and I only bought these because they hit a sale price i couldn't pass up, though I love Skechers, dont get me wrong .... could Skechers (any) last longer than they do (say with or without minor repairs)? ... yes I will be honest, but Skechers is still my go-to brand. Like I said in the title, these MAY BE the more comfortable out of the box pair I own ... and with or without memory foam (These DO HAVE memory foam), I love Skechers anyway ... one reason they are my go-to brand is how A) They are the best price versus some other brands when i can catch them on sale B) They do last longer than SOME other brands ... though I do admit it's been a good number of years since I owned some Reeboxs and I always liked them for longevity. Style wise, I love these too ... When I saw the look, "includes memory foam", and the fact that I got them for nearly 1/2 price (note: if a bit higher in price, I'd still say I think they are worth it) compared to the normal Amazon price ... I didn't even think about, I just placed the order and I dont regret it one bit.

My question (pre-purchase) was are they like significantly wider… dare I say “comically” wide. Around the upper is where I notice it most and MAYBE right toward the middle left to right (barely) but .. they ARE wider it seems but nothing that would make me want to return them like “oh that is way too much for me”. I have ONE pair of New Balance and it is XW too and it’s sort of the same thing in a way … I prefer the regular fit (say in Skechers I’d describe the 12/12.5’s that SOMEHOW fit me ok .. as “comfortably snug” … I feel the sneaker all around my foot but even the normal fits are NOT TIGHT), but the XW (maybe just tied a tad tighter to make them feel more like the normal fits) are A-OK for me so far. Maybe when I wear these out for a long walk I may change my mind, but I think they will be ok. Assuming I do not have the issues some others have had with the eye-lits holding the laces tearing (for the record I have seen that in negative reviews but never had a pair of Skechers do that to me BEFORE)... I am happy with these. I would go with regular (M) 13's in the future but if a style I like comes up on a good sale XW width … I’d be ok with them I think. The Memory foam is great and as I said the other Vigors are the most comfortable pair of Skechers I have and I already LOVE the fits of all the other models. I am not sure how long the memory foam will last but some people say that when their's go, the "sneakers are trashed" ...eh ... for me I usual have some extra padded insoles that make sneakers feel like slippers they are so comfortable. Even WHEN (and it will go ... it's just nature) the memory foam goes bad so to speak... I will just slip a pair of those insoles I have anyway in and no big deal. The Fit back to front is great (as always with Skechers from my experience) and as far as a few negative reviews go saying how they are the most uncomfortable sneaker they ever had ... I just question A) if they are getting the correct size ... B) sort of the same thing ... do they need wide width for wide feet and getting regular width, maybe? ... The one thing I CANT comment on with this exact pair though i have to say other Skechers I have gotten recent needed to be repaired sooner than I'd like (the Black Downforce model I have comes to mind)... so longevity I cant comment on, even though I admit (note: I wear mine a lot in the sun in Florida summers so maybe adhesive wise holding the sneakers together, the extreme temps and humidity play a role. With Skechers (unlike my one pair of Filas which ... are ok now i admit) there has NEVER been a "break-in" period for me. Years back even with the Reebox that i liked .. there was at least a few day break-in period before they'd go from "ok/good" to "REALLY comfy". One thing I almost missed before finishing this review is that I have a pair of Pebble(brown)/Black "Afterburn - Strike off" sneakers and while i like them I thought the brown in them was going to at least in part be "Suede like". I just noticed that while not all of the grey/charcoal in this pair is ... some is that suede type material … I really like that sort of look, myself .. not sure how long it will stay looking good in the hot Florida summers though. As if i even have to say it, I am happy with my purchase and would recommend these. I just HOPE they last longer than they did for some other people who had bad luck with them. Update after one, 2-4 mile walk. - I have to say that I still do like the regular 13's better but these ... these aren't bad. If anything, AT TIMES it seemed like they were slightly too big and while in a steady stride (I do a constant walk ... not slow... not a run either) ... these seemed almost normal. I also have to say that while I have tied the tops a little tigher... i have not messed with the way they are somewhat losely laced, out of the box. Really right now the ONLY way I'd return these is for the same price or lower, I could return these for a full refund AND get the same exact style and color for instance in 13 M's (regular fit), but even then I'd say these are not bad at all ... if things change more overtime i cant say but "slightly bigger" than I'd like is not bad at all and I got a GREAT deal on these price wise. -------------------------------------- Original Review for a Black with Grey accent.... Size 13 (My usual size) First (even with that title) I want to preference this by saying I have only worn these around the house a bit .. I want to keep them in good shape, longer and I only bought these because they hit a sale price i couldn't pass up, though I love Skechers, dont get me wrong .... could Skechers (any) last longer than they do (say with or without minor repairs)? ... yes I will be honest, but Skechers is still my go-to brand. Like I said in the title, these MAY BE the more comfortable out of the box pair I own ... and with or without memory foam (These DO HAVE memory foam), I love Skechers anyway ... one reason they are my go-to brand is how A) They are the best price versus some other brands when i can catch them on sale B) They do last longer than SOME other brands ... though I do admit it's been a good number of years since I owned some Reeboxs and I always liked them for longevity. Style wise, I love these too ... When I saw the look, "includes memory foam", and the fact that I got them for nearly 1/2 price (note: if a bit higher in price, I'd still say I think they are worth it) compared to the normal Amazon price ... I didn't even think about, I just placed the order and I dont regret it one bit.

reviews.title: Great shoes
reviews.body: These Reebok BB4500 Hi2 high tops are a solid throwback-style sneaker, but they definitely feel more like a lifestyle shoe than anything performance-focused. First impression is good — the design has that classic high-top basketball look and they’re easy to wear with jeans or casual outfits. They look better in person than I expected, especially if you like retro styling. Comfort is decent for everyday use, but not amazing for all-day standing or heavy walking. The cushioning is fairly basic, so after a few hours you can start to feel the lack of support compared to more modern sneakers. Fit runs a bit narrow for me, especially in the toe box, and there’s a short break-in period before they start feeling more comfortable. Once broken in, they’re fine for casual wear, but not something I’d choose for long walks or sports. Build quality feels okay for the price — not premium, but not cheap either. The leather upper holds up well, and the outsole seems durable enough for regular street use. Overall, these are good for style and casual everyday wear, especially if you like the retro basketball look, but they’re not a comfort-heavy or performance shoe.

reviews.title: Comfortable, Properly Snug And On In Two Seconds.
reviews.body: Although your typical 'foreign-made' shoe (Vietnam this time) the 'Slip-in' feature that I made fun of when 1st appearing on TV, turns out to be the lazy-man's dream. Just when you're wondering how much lazier, and fatter can we become, along comes slip-in shoes that look like a traditional shoe, feel comfortable, and properly 'snug' so you don't have heal-rub or feel like the shoe won't stay on...it will!. Construction is solid and the tread/traction is good. So I assume just like our 1st cars with power windows and locks, after these shoes, there's no going back? I did add 3/4 insoles, and the fit still feels fine...comfortable and snug. I don't think I'll abandon my traditional shoes, but check back this time next year and I may have a different story to tell. Does anyone remember Pixar's movie WALL-E! Well, I feel my new Skechers hands free slip-in sneaker's, and my expanding waistband are aiming me in that direction, and fast. I would buy again.

reviews.title: Reebok Club C Double Platform Sneaker
reviews.body: Review: Reebok Club C Double Platform Sneakers I’ve been wearing the Reebok Club C Double Platform sneakers for a while now, and they’ve definitely become a go-to in my rotation. If you’re into classic silhouettes with a modern twist, these are a great choice. Style: The platform sole gives the traditional Club C design a fresh, elevated look—literally. It adds just the right amount of height without feeling over-the-top. They pair well with everything from joggers and jeans to dresses and skirts, which makes them super versatile for casual or slightly dressed-up looks. Comfort: Surprisingly comfy for a platform sneaker. The cushioning is solid, and the shoe feels stable and supportive, even after a long day on your feet. I wouldn’t call them ultra-lightweight, but they’re definitely not clunky either. Fit: They run true to size in my experience. The leather upper is snug at first but breaks in nicely after a few wears. If you have wider feet, you might want to consider going half a size up, especially if you wear thick socks. Quality: Reebok did a great job with the materials—good leather, clean stitching, and a durable sole that holds up well. They’re easy to clean too, which is a bonus if you like that fresh-out-the-box look. Final Verdict: If you’re looking for a sneaker that balances retro vibes with a modern edge, the Reebok Club C Double Platform is a solid pick. Stylish, comfortable, and versatile—definitely worth it. ⸻

reviews.title: GREAT SHOE, COMFY FOR LONG TRAVEL DAYS/ WALKING AROUND CITIES
reviews.body: I've been eyeing these shoes for quite a while, and finally caved as I was due for a new casual but smart looking tennis shoe. I love the platform and neutral color way of these, and I wear them confidently with jeans, trousers, and dresses alike. I purchased them in time for a week long trip to London where I wore them every single day. In fact, I didn't wear any of the other shoes I'd brought along with me as these were so versatile and comfortable. I wear a 10.5 so I sized up into an 11 as 10.5 is not offered. I think the 11 is a little too big, and if I don't take the time to lace them well, I notice that my heel will slip out a bit and cause some discomfort in my calf. However, I figured that out quickly and adjusted as necessary. In the end, I walked miles and miles around London and it's surrounding towns/villages and was very comfortable.

reviews.title: Comfy and stylish!
reviews.body: I bought the tan and navy blue leather ones. The leather feels good and the shoes are comfortable. Both pairs do crease but that's normal with leather and it doesn't look unseemly. Some of the other reviews talk about the blue leather ones rubbing off and discoloring. I haven't experienced this after wearing them almost every day in very hot/humid weather as well as rainy northeast autumn. I also have not needed to polish them. What I can say is that the sizing on these shoes is vastly different from the same size tan leather ones. The tan leather ones fit great. I loved them and ordered the navy blue leather. Unfortunately, I just kept them in the box past the return date w/o trying them on because they were the same size as the tan ones. When I finally put them on and went out, I realized that they are much much bigger. I actually have 2 insoles and a heel cup placed in the navy leather 11Ws while the tan 11Ws have no insoles or anything. Other than that, they are great shoes and both the tan and navy have been rugged enough to handle my abusive daily commute. I also have 2 of the woolen pairs. One I haven't worn at all and the navy woolen pair does have a problem being too high and cutting into the back of my ankle causing blisters, as someone else mentioned. They may just require some breaking in but I haven't worn them enough to know for sure. Other than the bleeding foot, the woolen navy pair feels and fits well :-)

reviews.title: Hard to Beat for the Price
reviews.body: I purchased these for a business trip to Italy and wore them daily for the two weeks that I was there, during which I walked extensively. For me, there was a break-in period of a few days; before it loosens up, it will bite your heel, so I recommend wearing bandages or heel pads initially. Following the break-in, it's a very comfortable shoe and has served me well. I purchased a wide, and for this shoe, I found the width agreeable; in my experience, Cole Haan wide widths tend to be hit or miss (i.e., a wide is sometimes not all that wide). In terms of durability, I would not expect these to remain in good condition for more than a year if you wear them daily. The leather is not of high quality, but it's acceptable for the price. Expect them to crease very quickly if not using shoe trees. That doesn't bother me, but I know some find it objectionable. All in all, I like them and would buy them again. It's a comfortable alternative to traditional dress shoes for the office and works equally well for casual wear. Most higher quality options cost at least two or three times as much, and many are unavailable in a wide.

reviews.title: Good shoes, NOT new
reviews.body: To start things off: these appeared as Women’s when I added them to my cart (I think it’s a bug with having W for wide sizes) but I can confirm they showed up as Men’s which is what I ordered. Good: These shoes are really nice and much lighter than I expected, a good budget alternative to Common Projects and substantially more comfortable (what I was looking for). If you’re looking for a classic white leather sneaker without any real branding these are a great option. Bonus points for being available in Wide widths, although the toe box seems to be the only part with any notable width added (midfoot is still a little narrower than I’d like). The leather is extremely soft so they’ll break in and crease quickly, but that’s pretty standard for white leather sneakers. Bad: Mine had DEFINITELY been walked around in before and had a few marks on them (see pics). I don’t mean just little creases from being tried on in a store, these had small scuffs/scratches - even one where somebody tried to fill a pinprick with white out - and some phantom purple stain on the end of a lace (honestly looks like grape jelly). On a positive note the sole and insole themselves are spotless, so either somebody wiped them down very well or just clumsily wore them around indoors before returning them. The heel piece is stiff like others have mentioned and I can see that being uncomfortable during break in. There’s also a slight color variation between the leather and sole, I’d call the leather more ivory and the sole/laces straight white (fine for me but might be a deal breaker if you were looking for perfect white). Ultimately I need these ASAP and I’m not seeing any more left in my size, so I’ll keep them despite showing minor signs of wear. I figure since they’re white sneakers I’ll probably scuff them up after 1-2 wears anyways so it’s not the end of the world. UPDATE: 90 days in, these are great shoes. They’re way more comfortable than my Vans/Converse and have held up pretty well. The sole is soft so it does show wear quickly (although cleanly) but the upper itself feels almost like calfskin once it’s broken in. I’ve also gotten a number of compliments on them which is rare. These have become my go to sneaker and I’ll buy another pair once these wear out - albeit probably not on Amazon because these were clearly worn a number of times before they showed up.

reviews.title: Heavier and sportier than expected
reviews.body: This is a good shoe so it gets 4 stars. Minus a star because it lists upper as canvas, but it's really a mix of canvas and rubber. That combo makes them look sportier than I want, and also makes them stiffer and heavier than than I want. That said it's a well constructed shoe and as such, guessing it will hold up well. I walked out of it a bit like I do Sketcher slip-on shoes (I don't even try them any more). But I was pleasantly surprised to see that each pair came with a pair of full-length laces. Although I didn't unpack the laces, I'm certain they will help keep them on better, and might make them visibly less sporty. But not enough to keep them. The extra stitching meets the canvas upper adds extra seams inside the shoe that rub the sides of my feet. I ordered a 7.5M and 8M. Both felt the same in length on my foot. The 7.5 arch was in a better place, but the toe box was tighter. Considered a 7.5W, but a) about $40 more and they will still be just as heavy with extra seams on the inside. If you don't have "princess and the pea" feet like mine, I still give them 4 stars for good arch support and potential durability. Two more pair will be in stock soon :)

reviews.title: Definitely a win
reviews.body: This is the second time I’ve ordered these shoes. I love the memory foam in the insole and the comfort of the shoe. I have back issues (broken disc and spine alignment issues ) so I have to wear decent shoes. These shoes help reduce the pain in my back and reduce the pain in my feet. I also suffer from fibromyalgia and ehler danlos syndrome so I’m definitely recommend these shoes for anyone who has issues with either of those issues. It allows me to actually walk through the grocery store without agony. I also enjoy how you don’t have to lace the shoes and while these aren’t the slip on version of Skechers these do go on fairly easily. They have a number of different designs and I enjoy that there are different designs in black. It allows me to wear the shoes with my dress pants and most people don’t notice I’m wearing Skechers instead of dress shoes.

I wore them to work at my factory job (i didn't need steel toes for my job) every day for years- I was on my feet all day and they were so comfortable, and cute, too! I'm pretty sure they were leather then, also. They were so durable. These shoes looked the same in the photo, but couldn't be further from the originals. They weigh practically nothing! Super-cheap vinyl. Also- I always order up a half size when getting shoes online, to be sure they fit. I tried one of these on, and immediately I could tell that the size is off by at least one full size! I took the shoe right off without walking so I could return them as unworn. They are also very narrow! Even the rubber soles are cheap! You could easily slip, and the soles are designed with a raised center, which makes no sense and is dangerous. They have a lot of nerve charging $70.00 for these shoes. These belong at the swap meet for $15! They are made in Vietnam, which I'm pretty sure the original Reeboks were not. (I need to investigate, cause Reebox were really popular in the '90s, then kind of disappeared). This whole thing is just insane. Do not buy these!!

The box comes a little 'touched', but in good condition, and the shoes inside are perfect and shiny. 100% recommended to anyone who likes Air Force, has seen Sons of Anarchy or simply likes to dress their feet well.

title: New Balance Men's 608 V5

reviews.title: Support properly, and perform their duty day after day
reviews.body: I wear only New Balance Extra Wide shoes. The explanation is neither mysterious nor flattering: I carry more weight than I ought to, and my feet insist on reminding me. These provide the width I need along with an arch that actually supports rather than merely decorates the insole. In a marketplace increasingly devoted to fashion masquerading as function, that is no small achievement. I generally buy the 608 V5 cross trainers because they consistently have the best availability in Extra Wide. That alone earns them a place near the top of my shopping list. They also come in enough colors to satisfy whatever mood strikes you. I've accumulated black, white, brown, blue, and now gunmetal. Evidently, when I find something that works, I become a predictable voter. The shoes are comfortable from the first day, supportive during long walks, and forgiving during those moments when the bathroom scale reminds me that arithmetic is undefeated. They have become my everyday footwear, accompanying me through errands, appointments, and the ordinary business of retirement. No product is without its legislative amendments. Occasionally the shoelaces seem unnecessarily thick or comically long, as though drafted by a committee unable to agree when to stop. It's hardly a constitutional crisis, but every so often I find myself wondering whether someone at New Balance has a side business selling extra lace. Because these are my primary shoes—and because I place a bit more stress on them than their designers probably envisioned—they're generally ready for retirement after about six months. I don't regard that as a defect so much as the inevitable consequence of constant use and a user who could stand to lose a few pounds. Institutions endure because they reliably perform their intended function. The same may be said of these shoes. They are not flashy, they make no extravagant promises, and they will not transform your life. They simply fit well, support properly, and perform their duty day after day. In an era of exaggerated marketing claims, there is something refreshingly conservative about a product that succeeds by quietly doing exactly what it was designed to do. Five stars.

reviews.title: A solid durable feeling shoe.
reviews.body: Pretty good so far. Key point: Don’t order up. Plenty of size in these shoes, and the X wide is working for My Hawaiian feet. I got these for power walking and compared to walking in slippers ( My usual) they’ve really upped My game, enabling me to do a 10 min 34 sec. Split time on a 2 mile walk yesterday. Not bad at nearly 64 yrs old. I also ordered a couple pair of Sketchers. Here’s how they compare. The NB is way more substantial, with a harder, no doubt more durable rubber sole, while the Sketchers have a much more soft, almost a foam sole. NB has much more support and stabilization, but is not quite as comfortable out of the box as the NB. Some of the new balance shoes have an awkward slip on/lacing system. That is very difficult to get snug.. The NB is lighter due to the flimsier foam soles. Don’t skimp on the width. These tend to run narrow even the extra wide isn’t quite wide enough on one of the models I got. Verdict: if you’re simply doing casual walking, perhaps the new balance might fit your needs, but if you’re going to be putting in the miles, like I do at break next speed, you’d probably do better to stick with the new balance.

Now that I have owned several pairs of NB shoes I am hooked. My sneaker inventory is down to two pairs that I would have trashed long ago if I only had a replacement. I was prepared to spend up to about $150 for shoes if I wanted. As I was looking through NB shoes first I stumbled across this patriotic looking pair and saw the amazing prize. I ordered them and two days later I have them and they are wonderful as usual. Also just in time for the Fourth of July. So happy I may buy a second pair. And with the money I’ve saved buy a different pair as well. The price is too good.

reviews.title: Cute, Comfortable, and Supportive Shoe That Holds Up During 12-Hour Shift
reviews.body: I absolutely love these shoes and find them so cute and comfortable. I bought these shoes for work 3 weeks ago and have worn them every shift since. I am an ER nurse who is constantly on her feet at work for 12 hours. This is actually the second pair of new Balance shoes I have bought. I was so impressed with the first and I wanted a different color. I normally wear about a 6.5 to 7 in women’s depending on the brand. I bought a size 7 in the slate gray metallic silver color. These shoes fit me well and are true to size. The toe area is roomy enough to allow me to spread my toes out some. They also leave enough room to accommodate thicker socks, or foot swelling during shifts. I do have arches in my feet and they feel well supported while wearing them. They feel lightweight on my feet during my entire shift and my feet never feel heavy. When I first wore them they were a little stiff, but they never once hurt my feet. I was surprised because usually new shoes have to be broken in. Of course my feet do get tired since I worked 12 hour shifts, but they have never once hurt like they have with other shoes I have worn in the past. The sole of the shoe is cushioned and has not compressed after use. I have never once slipped while wearing them on polished and tiled flooring, so they provide traction. The mesh on the side is breathable. They are a little harder to keep clean because of the fabric near the lace toe and heel. After three weeks of use, I have not noticed any loose stitching and they have held up very well. Additionally, there isn’t any noticeable wear to the outsole. These shoes are good for casual wear, work, travel, and light exercise.

reviews.title: Buy Them! Very comfortable for pronated flat feet. Arishi V4
reviews.body: First off, these New Balance Arishi V4, running shoes are very comfortable, do not drag when walking. They put a spring in my step. One might say I have too many shoes. Maybe. But I like having variety and I'm always looking for comfort as well I wear a size 12, I am 6 ft 1 250 lb and I frequent the gym 4+ plus days a week. I am lean but do like to do cardio. The feeling, sweating it out. I was looking for a pair of comfortable shoes to walk around in. Just randomly browsing. I was looking for specific shoes to help with my arches, which I barely have. I have flat feet and my left ankle pronates. It's an injury from my skateboarding and boxing probably more than 20 years ago. I am not sure as one day I noticed my ankle was off. Maybe I am just made this way LOL. I wear a special insoles made custom. I have many other decent insoles, full and 3/4 length. It's not as bad as it seems, at least I say that lol. Came across these and the Asics gt-2000. For the price that I paid for these, they were very worth it. They were on sale, I saw my size, and ordered them. The shoes look very good in person, is good as in the item picture. Weight - they are very light, I'm not getting too technical by weighing them, but as light as some of my lightest running shoes are. Material - the material and style of the outside of the shoe is particularly interesting. I like the way it's got a fuzzy kind of soft material. The inside are very comfortable and support and comfort the foot. Ride - The ride is smooth, good for heal strikes. Very good ankle support. These definitely are a 5 star shoe. Some weeks I can do about 20+ miles on the treadmill, mostly walking at an incline. So I need good shoes. I also purchased the Asics GT-2000. The New Balance Arishi V4 and the Asics GT-2000 are similar and different. The GT 2000s are a more of a serious running shoe, hold the heel in place better, are bouncy. They are meant and can't work for longer distances. That isn't to say the Arishi V4 isn't great in their own right. They do it 90% just as well for a fraction of the price. So if you're looking for a running shoe or walking shoe, generally a decent shoe and you have flat or pronated feet, look no further. These are the shoes for you. I noticed they don't have many reviews, so trust me definitely worth trying. For the price I paid, < $30ish, I think they are better than other running shoes I've owned. The tech must be getting better, new innovations. I can go on and on. These are great shoes.

reviews.title: Solid and comfy daily shoe.
reviews.body: I have had a hard time finding shoes I can stand in all day, and though I do not struggle with foot pain, my hips and knees are arthritic. Most shoes to alleviate pain include wide widths (I have narrow feet) and correct pronation (I supinate). These have light to moderate arch support, which doesn't force my foot to the outside, and are roomy without being loose. I was able to slip them on without adjusting the laces. Though the ankle is too low to give support- the inserts are perfect for me. They control my stability in the right places- while still being cushiony and soft. I would not run or do anything high impact in these- but for walking and standing all day- they are efficient. Also- first pair of actually cute skechers I’ve ever owned.

reviews.title: Actual comfy shoes with support, but definitely not good on wet concrete :p
reviews.body: Initially ordered a size 6. I did an exchange for a 6.5Wide as it provides more wiggle room. I do not like very tight shoes. the 6 was way too tight for me. they are easy to slip on/off, the soles are thicker than what i prefer, but they are NOT platform style soles, so they should work fine, it is SUPPORT! (avid 25+ year Converse All Star wearer here). they seem to have excellent traction, i've only worn them out once (after i received my exchanged pair) and it was a comfy walk on dry sidewalk. the shoe quality seems to be good, i have noticed a few frayed threads sticking out, but honestly, i do not care. i dislike wearing shoes inside my home, especially on a top floor apartment (noise to neighbors, yes im nice and do everything to prevent heavy walking), but recently have an issue with tendonitis in one foot. OBVIOUSLY from my chucks and getting older and how i walk around at home lol, but listen, I wore these inside for a hour and hardly any noise, i felt floaty... normally I just slide around in socks. OVERALL: the wearability seems on point, I don't have any complaints yet. they are for work where I will be on concrete all day. I already know these will help. I can't really say HOW to choose your size, just do the research and buy a pair with the idea- you may have to exchange for a different size, and with that said- DO NOT LOSE THE TAGS (i removed mine from shoes but kept in great condition inside box for the return), DO NOT WALK OUTSIDE, KEEP EVERYTHING IN GOOD CONDITION- IN CASE- you have to do an exchange. reviews.title: Comfier than my Converse
reviews.body: I have been wearing Converse for years but lately haven’t been finding them as comfortable as I did in my teen years. I love the style of the shoe but I find the toe box now to be a bit too narrow for comfort and the lack of arch support results in heel and foot pain that I didn’t have before. I didn’t want to give up my beloved Converse and spent a lot of time searching for more supportive shoes but I couldn’t find anything that was satisfying enough to replace my favorite shoes. In a last ditch effort, I bought a pair of Footsouls insoles, which are made specifically for Converse and Vans, and came across these shoes. As a cheaper option, I thought I’d try my luck. Honestly, I was so surprised by how much I liked this shoe. I don’t have the highest expectation they’ll last forever like my 10 year old Converse but they are a great dupe for sure. My favorite part is the wider toe box and not feeling like my toes are all scrunched together. Paired with my insoles, they are now a much more comfortable shoe and my foot and heel pain have significantly improved. I usually wear an 8 but bought an 8.5 for a little more room. My heel does slide a little bit in these but not enough where I feel it compromises my gait and I have plenty of room in the toe box too. I wouldn’t wear these for any long type of walks but they work great for running errands, going out with your friends, or doing some light walking for the day. Overall, I recommend these for anyone searching for a Converse dupe. And I like all the color options too! Check out Footsouls insoles too, they are very comfy and help make these stylish though not supportive shoes more wearable for someone who’s not 17 anymore :)

I supinate (under pronate) and wanted something that would stabilize and be good on my knees. The tongue narrows toward the top and for some reason curls easily on the right foot so extra care must be taken when tying them up to ensure it is lying smoothly. The shoelaces are a bit slick and come untied frequently. Other than that the fabric upper is easy to clean and I like it because it is a more subtle colour. If the sole were not a glaring white but rather tinted to match the fabric they could be used for more than just an athletic shoe.

reviews.title: Good for my needs, with reservations
reviews.body: I find that I need a shoe with straps instead of laces, that feels comfortable, and that looks as much as possible like a black business shoe. Shoes with straps are hard to find where I live. These are all-black, have leather uppers and are fairly soft. I wear them semi-actively all day most days, or until they start feeling uncomfortable. The problem for me is that after 10 or 12 months, they start to show noticeable wear. The joint between the foot pad and the inner wall starts feeling uncomfortable after, say, 8 hours of wearing them. And the edges of the soles start to come apart around that same time. I'm probably unrealistic thinking any shoe in heavy use should last more than a year, but shelling out $80 every 15 to 16 months bothers me. Also, the tread is tight. That helps the business-like appearance, but it's hard to clean. On the whole, I don't think there's anything better for the money, but at the end of a long day it's hard to think they're perfect.

reviews.title: After a LONG search I found just what my Father needed.
reviews.body: My Father has Dementia, Diabetes and Size 9 EEEE bad , hurt all the time hurts when you barely touch them feet and toes. Have been putting Merrell Velcro strap sandals (with socks because his feet look so bad) on him for two + years. Decided to try a shoe again because they are just safer and a more stable walking base for him. His instep is very high - hard to find shoes with a velcro strap closure long enough to accommodate his needs - these barely are long enough to stay connected because I cannot fasten them tightly or he complains of pain. These are all issues relative to his particular needs; however, if you have super wide fat feet, have feet /toe pain related to illness and need a shoe easy to put on and take off this is a great shoe. I searched for months for an X Tra Wide shoe that would work - without having to spend hundreds on a Disbetic shoe. I also love the neutral color I was able to choose. This most likely is his last pair of new shoes. They Are well made leather somwill last and look nice with everything he wears. He complains of pain with every step but he did that wearing sandals as well but keeps on going walking. I feel,he is safer taking those walks now.

reviews.title: Holding up well
reviews.body: For years I used to buy $10 velcro shoes at Walmart. They would start cracking at the base of the toes where they bend after a few months wear, but I would usually get a year's worth of use from them. Granted, they received pretty rough treatment from me, since they doubled as work shoes in the yard and garden, so I would get another pair that I wore in "public" when the first pair started cracking. However, the last three years or so, the thin rubber soles, that were just glued to a sort of stiff foam rubber backing, began to become unglued and flap around after only a few days or weeks of use. Determined to get a year's worth of use, duct tape, done in a certain way, accomplished that. Sort of. After a while it just got to be ridiculous. Thus my search at Amazon to find some velcro shoes of better quality. And these are it. Three months and they haven't even shown signs of cracking. Plus they clean up well. The cheapos at Walmart were made of a sort of imitation brushed leather that showed stains and scuffs easily. With the smooth surface on these, a damp cloth works wonders on heavily dusty shoes. I only have three complaints that keep this product from getting five stars: 1. As others have noted, the straps are a little short. Not really a complaint from me, just a very mild annoyance. The velcro holds much better than the cheapos, so there's that. But that is what makes it annoying since you can't easily get your finger under the strap in order to get the shoes off quickly. 2. I love that there is much more sole to this shoe, it's just that compared to the cheapos, it's like wearing high heels. (And, yes, I did have some platform shoes in the seventies.) Plus they make more noise, especially on laminate flooring. They also aren't the most comfortable shoe in the world, but, hey, I would rather go barefoot anyway. 3. The price. Not a real biggie, but I would rather have paid about $10 less for this pair of shoes. But if they continue to hold up as well as they have so far, I will definitely buy these again.

reviews.title: Read this if you are unsure which size to get!
reviews.body: I was looking for a pair of silver sneakers and found these on sale. They are cute and real leather so I thought that was a huge plus. A lot of reviews are saying that they run big and to order down. I paid attention to that and it was a huge mistake. I'm usually between a 7 and a 7.5 but in sneakers I lean more towards 7.5. I first ordered the 7 and they were way too small. They fit like a 6.5 and I know they are in fact a 6.5 because the box said EU 37 which always fits like a 6.5 (7 would be a 37.5 EU) so I ordered the 7.5 (which the box says 38 which is correct for EU sizing) and they fit perfectly! So If you are a 6.5, then go ahead and order the 7. If you are between a 7 and a 7.5 then order the 7.5 for a perfect fit. They do run a bit narrow so keep that in mind if you have very wide feet they might not work for you.

reviews.title: Good pair of athletic shoes for the price
reviews.body: I will start off by saying that I'm not a runner. I do go to the gym a lot, and one of the things I do there is the step mill machine (stairclimber) and the treadmill. I also do a lot of walking (10k steps) in my neighborhood from time to time. I got these shoes for that purpose. While I don't mind paying good $$$ for a decent pair of shoes, the last pair of shoes I paid good $$$ didn't last all that long. In fact, its outer sole was equally as thin as those on the cheaper shoes. With that said, this time around I was a little more budget conscious, and wanted the best quality shoe for the price. I found these here, and after reading the product description and some online reviews, I decided to try them. The shoe fit is true to size. It wasn't too tight or too loose, even with thick socks on. The insole was comfortable and even after an hour of walking around doing everyday stuff, my feet felt pretty good. The insoles felt good and comfortable, although I have plantar fasciitis so I will wait and see how that goes after a longer period of wearing. The outer sole is rubber and felt firm and grippy. This shoe adds about an inch to inch and a quarter of height to my frame. My other shoes were somewhere in the order of half an inch to three quarters of an inch. The top part of the shoe is a mesh like fabric cloth, and allows for some breathability on a hot day. The overall quality of the shoe is pretty decent, and I detect no flaws in the craftsmanship. I am pleased with the shoe upon my initial experiences. Time will tell how the shoe holds up. But in the meantime, I am happy with it. For what I paid ($42), this is a pretty decent pair of athletic shoes. I can't speak to its performance for running, but for my intended use in the gym, this shoe fits the bill quite well without breaking the bank.

reviews.title: Great Shoes… Just Not the Color I Thought I Ordered
reviews.body: These shoes are comfortable, stylish, and honestly better‑made than I expected — but let’s talk about the color. The listing said dark gray, but when I opened the box, my first thought was, “Ah yes… the rare and majestic Lavender Gray, found only in nature and certain 90s windbreakers.” Don’t get me wrong, they look good. They just look good in a soft‑purple‑ish, lavender‑leaning, gray‑adjacent kind of way. If you’re expecting a storm‑cloud gray, you might be surprised. If you’re cool with a little unexpected flair, these will treat you right. Comfort? Solid. Style? On point. Color accuracy? Let’s just say the shoes and the product description are living in slightly different realities. Still keeping them — because apparently I’m now a lavender‑shoe guy, and honestly, I’m not mad about it.

reviews.title: 318 Days. One Pair. Every Single Day. Here's How They Held Up.
reviews.body: 5 out of 5 stars: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 318 Days Later: Daily Worn as My ONLY Pair of Shoes I wanted to wait before reviewing these because I wanted to see how they'd hold up over time instead of writing a review after only a week. These Skechers became my only pair of shoes. I wore them every single day from September 14, 2025 until July 29, 2026 and beyond. That's: 318 consecutive days, my primary (and only) shoes, everyday walking, no rotation with another pair. I paid just under $50 after tax when I bought them. That works out to roughly 15.7 cents per day (about 16 cents/day) over their lifespan. I've attached a photo collage showing exactly what they look like after those 318 days so people can judge the durability for themselves. Comfort: The Air-Cooled Memory Foam was easily my favorite feature. They were comfortable right out of the box and stayed comfortable for most of their life. The Hands Free Slip-Ins also worked exactly as advertised. Being able to step into them without bending over never got old. Durability: Considering these were my only shoes, I'm impressed. After 318 days, The uppers are still intact: Check No holes in the toe mesh: Check Stitching has held together: Check Soles are still attached: Check They still have usable traction: Check The main wear is exactly where I'd expect it: Heel lining has worn through. The insole covering has rubbed away in the heel area. The cushioning isn't as fresh as when they were new. The outsole has gradually worn from everyday walking. Nothing unexpected happened. They simply aged from daily use. Would I buy them again? Yes. In fact, I'm planning on buying the exact same pair again today. Not because these completely failed, but because I got almost 11 months of everyday use from them for about 16 cents per day, which I think is excellent value. I'll will keep this pair as backup shoes for rainy days, yard work, or quick errands. If you're looking for an everyday walking shoe that's comfortable, convenient, and can hold up to nearly a year of constant use, I think these are a solid choice. Would I recommend them? Absolutely!

reviews.title: Amazing Sketchers
reviews.body: I honestly never leave reviews, but this time I felt like I had to because there may be other people going through the same thing I did. I have very sensitive and delicate feet, so I hope my honest experience can help someone else make the right decision. The price is incredibly affordable, especially for the comfort and quality you get. I was originally planning to buy the Hoka Bondi 9, but they are a little expensive, so I decided to look for something more budget-friendly without sacrificing quality. Before buying these Skechers, I ordered another highly reviewed pair from Amazon that people compared to Hoka. Unfortunately, they were extremely hard, uncomfortable, and honestly one of the worst pairs of shoes I have ever tried. I have owned Skechers before and knew they were a reliable brand, so I decided to give these a chance—and I’m so glad I did! I walk five miles a day, five days a week, and these are some of the most comfortable shoes I have ever worn. My feet have not hurt at all, even after my long walks. These shoes have truly been a lifesaver, not only because of how comfortable they are, but also because of the amazing price. When this pair wears out, I won’t even bother trying another brand. I have definitely found my perfect walking shoes. Don’t even think twice—just buy them! I highly recommend these shoes 100%. You will not regret it! reviews.title: Love the Skechers!!!
reviews.body: For many years I faithfully wore the Nike Air Walk and then, low and behold, they stopped making them! They were one of very few "wide" shoes that Nike made -- plus they were all leather, very light, provided great support and were super comfortable. So, once they were discontinued, I was on the search for a replacement.... I didn't think of Skechers much as a "serious" brand, mostly because I didn't know much about them, but it turns out they do sell some wide fitment shoes, and these, for me, are an absolute great fit! I tried a pair, a few years back, and have faithfully replaced them every time, having once again found a pair of shoes I really love. They are very similar to the Air Walks, in comfort and durability, although, sadly, they don't last as long as the Nike's did. Then again, they are about half the price! So, I don't feel too bad having to replace these more often. I'd say a pair lasts six to eight months, where the Nike's used to last more than a year, but, as I say, these are a lot more affordable to replace, so I guess it kind of works out, cost wise. For me, the most important thing is having a pair of shoes that are comfortable, versatile and look good enough to wear to work with good Levi's and a sport shirt, yet can also be used for walks or even light hikes. Since they are all white I have the same problem I had with the white Air Walks, which is that they tend to get dirty kind of quickly, but, like the Air Walks, they also clean up beautifully with some shoe cleaner and a bit of Sneaker whitener, so they tend to look great until they simply wear out -- in my case it is usually the side that eventually blows out -- which was the same on the Air Walks, but just didn't happen as quickly. Even so, six to eight months of life is pretty good to get out of them, considering I wear these pretty often throughout the average week. So, I'm a fan now, and in fact will be getting a second pair of these to have around, since they also come in blue and white, and that way I don't have to clean these up as often, and that's actually an improvement over the Air Walks, since they only came in the white or solid black. With these, I can now have an all white pair, and now can also have a more "casual" sneaker for other looks or outfits or uses, and, since two pairs is not much more than one pair of what the Air Walks use to cost, I'm actually a bit ahead of the game. I'm very happy with these, and I'd certainly recommend them highly!

reviews.title: Superb quality, but not for my feet
reviews.body: I have been a huge fan of Sketchers for awhile now; their quality and craftsmanship are superb and their shoes are built to last! I am pretty tough on my shoes, and demand a lot from them. I need a shoe that offers sturdy support, as my back is pretty much a wuss, and will freak out about the littlest things, including lack of shoe support. Sketchers has always delivered everything I need in a shoe. I was excited to try this design, because I am on my feet a lot at work (I work 12-hour shifts on concrete floors at a manufacturing plant). From what I've read online, these shoes were ideal for my needs, because they offered the support I need for both my back and my feet. I also like the fact that these shoes have a very aggressive tread, as I do a lot of outdoor activities including hiking and camping, and I expect my everyday shoe to hold up for the task (even though I have dedicated hiking boots, sometimes you want a lighter-weight option, especially when you're carrying 60-80 pounds on your back). When these shoes arrived, I was impressed with the amount of tread and grip they provided. It wasn't like the dinky little tread you see on most shoes, it looked like they took a tire, cut it to shape, and put it on the bottom of the shoe - Sketchers meant business when they designed this shoe! The material is warm, but lets your feet breathe, so your feet stay nice and warm in the winter. I can't say how they are in the summer, as I didn't own them in the summer months. Inside, there is a lot of padding all around, especially in the tongue of the shoe, which is nice - it gives a real nice snug fit to keep the shoe in place without having to really strap down the lacing tight. There is a huge amount of padding in back on the bottom for your heels, which, for me, is where the problem comes in. For most people, this would be a very nice feature, but for some reason, it ended up hurting my heels pretty badly, almost to the point where I didn't want to walk from one end of the house to the other. After wearing them for just one 12-hour shift, my feet were screaming, and all I wanted to do was either sit back in a chair with my feet up or lay in bed, just so I wouldn't be on my feet. I understand that every pair of shoes needs to be broken in, and during that time the shoes can be a bit uncomfortable, but not this much. While I absolutely like these shoes and have absolutely nothing against them (other than the heel issue mentioned above), I am forced to return them to Amazon. Please remember that this is not the case for most people - my feet are extremely picky to begin with, and simply put, these shoes just aren't for me. I really like the quality and materials that Sketchers used to design this shoe, and I can honestly say that I believe they are a shoe that will hold up to use and abuse for quite a long time. Despite them not being the right shoe for my feet, I would still highly recommend them, but be aware that there is a large amount of padding in the heel area, and will lift the heel area of your foot upwards somewhat. I don't hold anything against Sketchers or these shoes. In fact, once my return is processed, I plan on buying a new pair of my go-to shoes, which are the Sketchers Men's Stamina Nuovo sneakers. All around, great shoe, just not for me (unfortunately).

reviews.title: NICE
reviews.body: I purchased this men's shoe after being unable to find a woman's shoe wide enough to accommodate my wide, athletic feet. I bought a 6.5 standard--not wide and it fir me nicely. My toes do not hurt and the balls of my feet do not push the shoe out, decreasing the probability of busting out of them. I am woman's 7.5 wide which is a men's 6 regular. But, they did not come in 6, so I got the 6.5 and although a bit long are great. So I kept them and just wear thick socks with them. I like that these shoes are 100% leather too. They Lace-up, have a Shock-absorbing supportive midsole, a Flexible rubber traction outsole Have a cushioned comfort insole and a 11/2 inch heel. The slight heel makes them better to stand in over long periods of time and for me, are more comfortable to walk and jog in. The shoes are comfortable, a good fit, a good quality (been running in them for 6 weeks). The build and shoe quality are good for todays shoes. Moreover, they look good and the weight is light, but not featherweight. One thing I would like to feel is a more cushioned insole. When running they are fine--not hard, but a thicker dense cushion insole wold be beneficial. The outer sole gives well and I can not feel the sharp rocks I run on. This shoe is a good value for your money and I will buy again. I hope I helped you in making a decision on your next pair of sneakers. Happy running.

I like the color (I got the off white) and I think when my current pair of black tennis shoes bites the dust I'll probably replace them with these in black.

reviews.title: Insole breaking down after 3 months
reviews.body: I love these shoes! They have been comfortable from the first time I wore them. They slip on easily, stay on, and support my feet well for walking without becoming sore. I have washed them a couple of times (about once a month) as directed by manufacturer in cold water & let them air dry; haven't noticed any issues with washing. I've put a lot of miles on them, & the outer sole shows hardly any wear. My only issue is that after 3 months I noticed the interior where my toes rest is starting to break down. I really wanted to wear these without insoles because those interfere with the easy slip on feature, but I finally added insoles to prevent further breakdown. I still love the shoes, but can't give 5 stars because of that. I recommend if you get these shoes that you add insoles from the beginning to get the most life out of them.

reviews.title: Level of fragrance really depends on the type of candle you choose!
reviews.body: Have ordered 2 of these candles - the Peace + Tranquility (white) and the Reflection + Clarity (light blue). Both were excellent, but the Peace + Tranquility definitely had a lighter aroma / more subtle than the Reflection + Clarity. Saw several reviews stating they couldn't smell the candle. There are 2 likely reasons - 1: if you have a large room/house that you want to smell the candle in, I highly recommend the coffee table jar, which has 3 wicks and smells much stronger than the single wick candles. However, since it has three wicks, it does burn through faster. I light mine every night for a couple of hours after dinner while I clean the kitchen and they each lasted about 2-3 weeks with nightly use. Secondly, it definitely seems to vary with the the fragrance type you use. The Peace + Tranquility is very light and fresh smelling, but not at all strong. The Reflection + Clarity is very strong and pleasant, it kind of smells like laundry detergent though (this can be a good or bad thing depending on how you feel about your laundry detergent!). I have a large house with high ceilings and you can smell the Reflection + Clarity everywhere after being lit 30 minutes or so. I like to use the R+C type of I make a very strong-smelling dinner (with lots of garlic or onions) where I want to refresh the house. I use the P+T when I just want a nice calm scent. I will definitely order again, but will probably try another couple of types since they seem to vary quite a bit...

reviews.title: Wenn Bruce Wayne eine Kerze wäre…
reviews.body: Als meine Frau mir diese Kerze mit den Worten in die Hand drückte, ich solle mal aufhören zu riechen wie ein Mix aus Fahrradkeller und Müsliriegel, wusste ich noch nicht, dass ich kurz davor stand, in eine andere Duftliga aufzusteigen. Ich zündete sie an, lehnte mich zurück – und der Raum veränderte sich. Unser Straßenkötermix mit Schäferhundblick und der Libido eines Rammelbocks rollte sich auf einmal seufzend zu meinen Füßen. Selbst die Katze hörte kurz auf, wie ein haariger Gollum durchs Wohnzimmer zu geistern. Der Duft? Absolut männlich, aber ohne mit dem Holzhammer zu kommen. Eher wie jemand, der mit Maßanzug und Geheimnissen in einen Raum tritt, statt mit Achselhaaren und Motorsägen. Die Mischung aus Sandelholz und Oud füllt den Raum auf eine elegante Weise – warm, würzig, fast meditativ. Ich hab mich selbst beim tiefen Durchatmen erwischt, obwohl ich sonst eher Team „Fenster auf, Duft raus“ bin. Das Design der Kerze ist purer Stil. Schwarz, edel, mit einem goldenen Etikett, das nicht schreit, sondern flüstert: „Ich bin hier, weil ich es wert bin.“ Auch das Brennverhalten ist top – sauber, ruhig, kein Gesiffe oder Rußen. Sie steht jetzt auf meinem Schreibtisch, während ich diese Rezension schreibe, und ich fühle mich ein kleines bisschen wie ein Autor, der in einem viktorianischen Herrenclub am Roman seines Lebens schreibt. Das Einzige, was fehlt, ist ein Kamin – aber solange diese Kerze brennt, spielt das keine Rolle. Sie riecht nicht nach Weihnachten, nicht nach Zuckerwatte, sondern nach einem Mann, der weiß, wer er ist. Oder zumindest so tun will, als wüsste er es. Hinweis: Ich habe dieses Produkt im Rahmen des Amazon Vine-Programms kostenlos zu Testzwecken erhalten. Meine Bewertung basiert auf meiner ehrlichen und unabhängigen Erfahrung.
reviews.body_en: When my wife handed me this candle and told me to stop smelling like a mix of bicycle storage and a granola bar, I didn't know that I was about to enter a different fragrance league. I lit it, leaned back - and the room changed. Our street mutt mix with German Shepherd eyes and the libido of a battering ram suddenly rolled up at my feet, sighing. Even the cat briefly stopped haunting the living room like a furry Gollum. The scent? Absolutely manly, but without coming with a mallet. More like someone walking into a room with a tailored suit and secrets rather than armpit hair and chainsaws. The blend of sandalwood and oud fills the room in an elegant way - warm, spicy, almost meditative. I caught myself taking a deep breath, even though I'm usually a team "window open, smell out" team. The design of the candle is pure style. Black, noble, with a gold label that doesn't scream but whispers: "I'm here because I'm worth it." The burning behavior is also great – clean, quiet, no buzzing or soot. It's sitting on my desk now as I write this review and I feel a little bit like an author writing the novel of his life in a Victorian gentlemen's club. The only thing missing is a fireplace - but as long as that candle is burning, that doesn't matter. She doesn't smell like Christmas, or like cotton candy, but like a man who knows who he is. Or at least wants to act like he knows. Note: I received this product for free for review purposes through the Amazon Vine program. My review is based on my honest and independent experience.
