reviews.title: Overall great but will not last for a long period of time
reviews.body: I bought two of these and have had them for about two years. I keep one of them on the desk permanently (the pink version). It's perfect for just chilling there, easy access to the charging port, and is adjustable. I love how you can adjust the height, tilt it forward/back, and turn it side-to-side. It comes in two pieces : the phone holder and the actual stand. It's a simple assembly- just click it into place. After two years of wear and tear, I can say that my pink stand is starting to crack at the point where the phone holder clicks into/on the stand and also upwards and downwards from that point. The two separate pieces have become a place of stress for the stand from general wear and tear. If you try to tilt the phone too flat (straight) and you have a larger phone (iPhone max pro here) it WILL fall out. Imagine being on zoom/FaceTime and tilting it to show something directly in front of you (->) and bam! out it falls. It has happened dozens of time to me. Overall great phone stand but I might try a new stand for my phone next time. The Good: Portable Adjustable Easy set up Looks great access to charging point The Bad: Not adjustable enough Will drop heavier/larger phones if tilted too far Limited durability - point of weakness

reviews.title: Good Phone Stand, but the Build Isn't What I Expected
reviews.body: This stand works well for its intended purpose. It offers a good range of height and angle adjustments, making it comfortable for video calls, reading, or keeping a phone visible while working at a desk. The adjustment mechanism holds its position well, and the silicone pads help keep the phone from slipping. That said, the construction wasn't quite what I expected. The product description mentions "sprayed aluminum," but the stand doesn't feel like a solid aluminum product. The main structure appears to be ABS with a metallic finish, while the base contains a metal plate that adds some stability. It looks nice, but it doesn't have the weight or feel of an all-metal stand. The base is stable enough for a smartphone, which is clearly what this stand is best suited for. However, I wouldn't feel comfortable using it with a larger tablet, especially in portrait orientation, because the base isn't heavy enough to inspire much confidence. Overall, it's a good, functional stand for everyday smartphone use. Just don't expect the premium feel or stability of a solid aluminum stand, particularly if you're planning to use it with heavier devices.

reviews.title: Highly recommended for popsocket users!

This stand is specifically (and solely) designed to hold such a phone by the popsocket itself, allowing you to have the best of both worlds. The stand came in 4 pieces and was easy to assemble (it probably took less than 15 seconds.) There’s a locking knob for the vertical arm, and a locking ring for the ball joint, allowing you to fix it in the perfect viewing position. The base is weighted, and should hold even a heavy phone in place. All in all, if you use a popsocket on your phone, this stand is *highly* recommended!

It feels much sturdier than I expected for the price, and the adjustable height and viewing angle make it easy to get my phone positioned exactly where I want it. The base has a nice wide footprint, so it stays put instead of tipping over when I’m using the phone. I also like that it works with a PopSocket and similar grips, which makes it much more convenient than a standard phone holder. The adjustments are easy to make but still hold their position well. Overall, this is a simple, well made stand that does exactly what I wanted it to do without taking up a ton of desk space. Definitely worth the price.

reviews.title: Detailed review: So far so good!
reviews.body: This is only the second tripod I've ever owned, and so far it's going really well! I was iffy about buying a $20 tripod, as there are so many cheaper options out there, but it's totally worth it! This tripod has a little bit of weight to it, which makes it feel sturdier. I will say it is a bit tall, even in it's compact form, so it's not very "portable". For instance, I put it in my backpack and it sticks out since it doesn't fit all the way into the bag. If you're going to be using this as a portable selfie stick while traveling etc, I think something lighter and more compact would be better for you; however, this works great if you're setting up the tripod for more stationary reasons. Moving on to the things I love about it: The legs on a tripod are arguably one of the most import features, at least for me. It's what's going to be holding the weight up and providing a sturdy base support. I love that the legs on this tripod are very much controllable/customizable. If you look at the main picture of this listing, the legs are not in the down-most open position yet. You can control how much you want the legs to open and "flare" out at the bottom. If you want super sturdy support, you can open them further out to provide a wider base. The locking mechanism is also very helpful as you can control how wide your base goes. I love this level of personalization because sometimes I want my tripod to take the least amount of space as possible. It's also very important for me that the legs open with ease. I broke my first cheap tripod because the legs were hard to control and I was trying to force them shut/open. The legs on this tripod open and close with ease, but a little push needs to be applied. The legs also have rubber bottoms to prevent slipping. I have not used this outdoors, so I cannot speak on its performance while it's windy out. I use this tripod to hold my iPhone 14 Pro and I've never had instability issues where it's tipping over. The phone mount is great as it stretches open on both sides as opposed to just one sliding mechanism- This makes it very easy to insert and remove my phone. Its got 4 flip locks to control the height. I don't typically use it at the tallest height. I'd say I use 2 flip lock's worth of height and that's already tall enough for me. There is no installation required, which is a huge plus. You only have to screw the phone mount, or the other mount if you're using it for another device. Takes seconds to screw in. The only criticism I have (which isn't even a big deal) would be that I wish I could immediately move a phone up or down while it's in the phone mount. For instance, if I have my phone set up in the phone mount, it points directly ahead in a straight line, however, sometimes let's say I want to capture more floor, so I wish I could immediately point the phone a little downwards to see more floor. In order to do this, I have to unscrew the little knob to control the range of the phone mount, move the phone facing more towards the floor, and then screw it back in place again. It doesn't take that much time or anything, but sometimes I want it to be a super quick and easy fix, specially if I just want the view to be a couple Millimeters more towards the floor. I do not use the Bluetooth remote, though it already came with batteries and ready to use. If you're an inexperienced tripod user like me and you plan to be using it in a public space, I recommend you get familiar with the set up at home; that way you can set it up and compact it back down fast and with ease. It only took me one minute to figure out how to use it at home and I could quickly set it up when I was on the go. All in all, I think this tripod is sturdy, easy to use, and it seems like it will last me a long time.

reviews.title: Best. Purchase. EVER. My tripod goes everywhere with me now!
reviews.body: This thang. Fabulous, fabulous, fabulous. Did I mention it's fabulous? This is probably the purchase i will enjoy using the most, second only to my Samsung Note 10 Plus. This tripod is to use with said phone. Hence my excitement. If we ever get paroled from Covid Quarantine, I will be able to take pictures of EVERYONE using this bundle of joy. There will be no more people missing from group and family portraits because one fool always had to be taking a picture. I've never been one prone to the silliness of using a selfie stick. I do, however, LOVE taking pics. Amateur photography is my thing, and this little toy has already brought me so much joy. It's super easy to flip up to whichever height you want it at to quickly set up for the perfect shot. I should mention that my phone is very well protected in a nifty little case which I also got on Amazon. It's therefore even bigger than the phone would be by itself. In it's case, my phone measures 6.75" by almost 3.4". The retractable phone holder opens adequately wide to accommodate and then securely hold my phone in whatever way I set it. I've got an alarming number of friends who drank iKoolaid and are in love with their iPhones. My Samsung though, with it's screen size and resolution, takes far superior pictures. They can snap inferior pictures with their iWatches, BUT I HAVE... THIS! The added beauty that an iWatch can't cover is being able to use the far better rear camera, instead of being confined to selfie mode, as seen on an iWatch. So this wins, every time, hands down. The knobs to adjust the height of the tripod are straightforward. You get increments of height added on for every know you unlock, as shown on the product description pictures. You can also stop it at any interim point you like. So if you need your camera at a very specific height, that is easy to accomplish. It is also super easy to switch your phone back and forth between portrait mode and landscape mode: it's a snap to do. I must confess that I have not bothered to link the remote control that came with this tripod with my phone to use it to take pictures. I can do that with a simple voice command or with my nifty phone stylus. So I may NEVER get around to sampling that aspect of this product. Either way, this has been the best gift to myself ever. Assembly, from pulling it out of its handy carrying case to full set-up with your phone clipped and ready to say cheese could be done in about 10 seconds easily. I can also use this for birdwatching, nature shots, and anything else I want to do. Really easy to carry around and flip out whenever you see a shot you want to line up. I love going out on nature trails to snap pics, so this will be used heavily by me. If I had any suggestion for improvement, it wouldn't actually have anything to do with the tripod: it would be that they probably could have put a light shoulder strap on the carrying case, a bit longer than the cord that is currently on it. So i may run a different cord through the loops, but I'm absolutely thrilled with this baby. Happy happy happy customer!

reviews.title: Sturdy, Easy, and My New Go-To Tripod!

It’s super easy to set up and even easier to use. Honestly, I use it all the time now because it just works. Pros: Great quality build – feels durable and reliable Easy setup & use – no frustration here Holds my phone perfectly – secure fit, even for larger phones Super value for the money – feels like a premium product without the premium price Cons: The remote is okay, but I don’t really use it Like any tripod, you do have to treat it with care (don’t whip it around!) Overall, I love this tripod. It’s sturdy, tall enough for all my needs, and versatile with the adjustable ball head and gooseneck. For anyone looking for a dependable phone tripod, this is the one.

reviews.title: Great tripod with a few minor drawbacks.
reviews.body: I’ve been using this tripod for a couple of weeks now, including taking it on a trip to the ocean, and overall I’m really pleased with its performance. Pros: ✔️ Very sturdy – even in windy conditions by the ocean, it didn’t fall or wobble. ✔️ Height adjustment is excellent – I love how tall it extends, and it’s great for group photos, video calls, or content creation. ✔️ Comes with a wireless remote, which is very convenient for hands-free shooting. Cons: • The Bluetooth remote doesn’t attach to the tripod itself, which makes it easy to lose if you’re on the go. A small clip or holder would be a great improvement. • While it’s fairly lightweight, the tripod is not compact. You’ll likely need a larger bag to carry it around if you’re planning to travel with it. Overall, a solid 4-star product! With just a couple of tweaks, it could be perfect.

reviews.title: Awesome purchase!
reviews.body: Awesome tripod👌🏼. I love that it came with a remote, which has worked really with my android phone. A little blue light turns on when u turn it on, but once its connected to your bluetooth, the light turns off. Wish it would stay on just so I can make sure if I do have remote on or off, but it's not that big of a deal. U can easily just turn remote on and off to make sure. When you click to take a picture or click start and stop for video, the blue light does turn on (when you click only. It doesnt stay on). I love that the height is easily adjustable. Also, that phone can easily be placed vertically and horizontally. It's cool also that it came with a Go Pro adapter. I haven't used it cause I don't have a Go pro or anything like that, but it's cool its included👍🏼😁. I like that it can also be used as a selfie stick. U can easily use the remote to take a selfie. I dont think the tripod is flimsy. I think it's pretty sturdy👍🏼. The price is great too. Plus, I was able to use a $4 coupon on it so it came out even cheaper! My only suggestions to make this item even better are the following: 1) wish backpack bag was just a little taller cause with phone mount it's a little harder to close bag (you can close it but u just have to move the phone mount part to the side). 2) If lanyard or string would come with remote, that would be even more awesome. This is easily solved by putting your own on it (there is a space on remote to insert string/lanyard. I put a string in it), but just saying. 3) it would have been nice if it came with a pouch or if backpack bag came with a pouch to put the remote and other things tripod came with. Again, you can easily get your own pouch and problem is fixed. I used a pouch I already had, but again just saying. Overall, I'm happy with this purchase and the price I paid for it as well😁.

reviews.title: Probably more like 4 or 4.5 stars but 5 for the cost!
reviews.body: Works great! Awesome for getting any angle you need, super portable with how small it folds up and the carrying case. The only little reasons I'd say realistically it's maybe more like 4-4.5 stars is because it's a little unstable/flimsy if you're doing anything where you need to touch the phone. I have to hold the tripod and touch the phone so it won't shake so much. I imagine it may be shaky in the wind too but haven't used it outside yet. It's not a terrible shake though, and I'm sure if you really needed to stabilize it at least better you could, but I don't think it's sturdy enough for true stability. Also, the phone clamp/holder piece I got was a little flaky. Little black specs come off of it, but it looks and works fine otherwise. All of that said, given the low cost, it's 5 stars! Gets the job done without costing an arm and a leg.

reviews.title: とっても丈夫！
reviews.body: 結構大きいけれど、リュックには入りました！一応写真には比較用にiPhone6sを置いておきます！(古い)手持ちで自撮りするのには向いてないですね！しかしそれ目的でなかったので大丈夫でした！ 説明書が英語しかないので、「？」ってなりながら組み立てましたが、脚も丈夫だし、三脚の開き具合？を大きくしたり狭めたり調節出来るのでとても良いです。あらゆる場所にネジがあるので、ちゃんと緩めてから角度を変えてしっかり固定できるのもとても良いなと思いました！ リモコンも最初どうやって接続するのかなと説明書君に｢ what？」と、問いかけたら「ヨコニボタンガアリマス」的な声が聴こえたので、それをカチッと上にやったら、Bluetoothが起動してスマホと繋がったので喜びました。最初から電池が入っているのも高得点ですね！リモコンにキーホルダーがつけられるのも無くさなくていいかもしれません。 たしかに付属の袋が付いてなかったり、説明が簡素すぎる部分はありますが、スマホで撮影するには十分丈夫な三脚だと思いました！ ただいつも思うのはこのスマホを挟む部分が壊れないか心配です。まだ長期間使っている訳では無いのでそこは期待です！ お値段も割とお得だし、オススメですぞ！
reviews.body_en: It's quite big, but it fits in my backpack! I've included an iPhone 6s in the photo for comparison! (Old) Not suitable for hand-held selfies! But that wasn't my purpose, so it was okay! The instructions were only in English, so I was wondering as I assembled it, but the legs are sturdy and the tripod doesn't open properly. It's great because you can adjust it to make it bigger or narrower. There are screws everywhere, so I thought it was great to be able to loosen them properly and then change the angle to secure them firmly! When I first asked the manual about how to connect the remote control, I heard a voice that sounded like "Yokoni Button Gaarimasu", so when I clicked it up, I was happy to hear that Bluetooth started up and connected to my smartphone. The fact that the batteries are included from the beginning is also a big plus! You may not have to lose the ability to attach a key chain to the remote control. It's true that it doesn't come with a bag and the instructions are too simple, but I thought it was a sturdy enough tripod for taking pictures with a smartphone! reviews.body: Great 3-in-1 Charger With a Very Strong Magnetic Connection I’ve been really happy with this 3-in-1 MagSafe charging stand. It’s a convenient way to keep my phone, Apple Watch, and AirPods together in one place instead of having multiple charging cables and devices scattered across my nightstand. One of my favorite features is the blue ambient light. It gives the charger a nice, modern look without being overly distracting. The light adds a little bit of atmosphere to my nightstand, and I really like the way it looks when the room is darker. The magnetic connection is super strong. My phone snaps into place securely and stays where it should, which is especially helpful when using the stand overnight. I don’t have to worry about the phone slipping off the charging position with normal movement. The adjustable stand is another nice feature because it allows you to position your phone at a comfortable viewing angle. I like being able to glance at the screen while it’s charging without having to pick up the phone. Charging performance is my only minor drawback. The charging capability is a little slower than some dedicated wired chargers I’ve used. That said, it works well for overnight charging, which is how I prefer to use a charging station like this anyway. I recommend putting your devices on the stand before bed and letting them charge overnight rather than expecting extremely fast charging during the day. The 3-in-1 design is definitely the biggest convenience. Being able to charge three Apple devices in one compact location helps keep everything organized and makes it a great addition to a nightstand, desk, or office. Overall, I really like this charging stand. The strong magnetic connection, attractive ambient light, and ability to charge three devices in one place make it a very convenient setup. If you’re looking for an organized charging station rather than the absolute fastest charging option, I think this is a great choice.

reviews.title: Work desk phone stand is a must have
reviews.body: I didn’t expect much from a simple cellphone stand, but this 360-degree rotating one ended up being one of those “why didn’t I buy this sooner?” upgrades. The rotation is the standout feature—it’s smooth, solid, and actually holds its position. Whether I’m switching from vertical to horizontal for videos, hopping on a quick FaceTime call, or following along with a tutorial, I can adjust it instantly without fighting the stand or worrying about it flopping over. Stability is surprisingly good. The base has enough weight (and grip) that it doesn’t slide around every time you tap your screen. Even when I’m typing or scrolling aggressively, it stays put. That’s a big deal because a lot of cheaper stands feel like they’re about to tip over if you even look at them wrong. The viewing angles are flexible enough to work at a desk, on a nightstand, or even in the kitchen. I’ve used it for everything from watching videos while eating to keeping my phone at eye level during calls, and it handles all of it without needing constant adjustment. Build quality feels solid for the price—no creaking hinges or loose joints. It doesn’t feel like a throwaway accessory. If I had to nitpick, I’d say the rotation could be a touch tighter out of the box depending on your phone size, but it’s not a dealbreaker and hasn’t caused any real issues. Bottom line: simple, functional, and way more useful than you’d expect. If you use your phone a lot throughout the day, this is one of those small accessories that quietly makes everything easier.

reviews.title: Im kicking myself right now
reviews.body: Why did I wait so long to get this? So Ive been thinking about getting a phone compatible tripod for a while but didnt want to end up with another piece of junk equipment that just sat unused in the corner. After seeing this on sale I decided to go for it. First off it's sturdy, when I pulled this out I was actually surprised how hefty it was. Not necessarily heavy but the majority of it is a lightweight metal when I was expecting it to be mostly plastic. Even then its less than 2lbs with my phone on it so those who need portability, youre good. It comes fully assembled other than choosing which adapter you want to use (phone or go pro) so no annoying instructions and zillion little pieces to deal with before you can use it. The feet are adjustable to fit the footprint of whatever area you have from quite small to fit on a small tabletop to spread out for more stability on the floor, and you can lock them at whatever place you need them. The phone adapter easily fit my iPhone 14ProMax. Height is easily and infinitely adjustable from about 16" tall to 62" tall and feels very stable even at full height (although at full extension I definitely recommend spreading the feet out as far as you have room for) Initially I wasn't even going to use the remote but its as easy to connect as a pair of ear buds, through bluetooth settings, and worked perfectly even with my 3rd party camera app. If youre even considering one of these just get it now while it's on sale. Like I said in the title, Im kicking myself that I didnt do it much earlier. Its a great item at a great price.

reviews.title: My friend uses this tripod and remote control to record himself for social media.
reviews.body: I bought the SENSYNE 62" Phone Tripod & Selfie Stick as a gift for a friend of mine who’s a singer and uses it to record himself for his social media. He’s been really happy with it, and after hearing all the positive feedback from him, I figured I’d share my experience here. First, he loves the height adjustment. At 62 inches, it's the perfect height for him to get a good shot without needing to find a ledge or prop his phone up somewhere awkward. He’s been using it both for singing videos and live sessions, and the adjustable height has given him a lot of flexibility in how he frames his shots. The selfie stick feature is another thing he’s mentioned he really likes. He’s able to easily switch from tripod mode to selfie mode, which is great when he wants to record himself up close, especially for those personal moments with his fans. And he really appreciates the remote shutter. He can start recording or snap pictures without needing to run back and forth to the phone, which saves a lot of time and hassle. My friend also told me he’s been impressed with the stability of the tripod. Even when he's singing or moving a bit while recording, the tripod holds the phone steady, and he hasn’t had any shaky footage. He’s been using it regularly for recording Instagram videos and live performances, and it’s definitely helped with getting more professional-looking content. Portability is another reason he’s happy with it. The tripod is lightweight and compact enough for him to easily carry around, whether he’s heading to a recording session or just moving between rooms at home. He says it fits easily into his bag and doesn’t add too much bulk, which is great for someone who’s always on the go. As for the build quality, he mentioned that it’s solid but not too heavy-duty. It’s more than sturdy enough for regular use, though. The phone mount is adjustable and keeps his phone secure, even when he’s recording for extended periods. All in all, my friend’s been super happy with the SENSYNE 62" Phone Tripod & Selfie Stick. He told me it’s made a big difference in the quality of his recordings, and he finds it super easy to use. Based on his experience, I’d definitely recommend this to anyone who’s looking for an affordable and versatile tripod or selfie stick for social media content creation!

reviews.title: Perfect for family memories—just handle with care!
reviews.body: I absolutely love this cellphone tripod for my family! It has been a complete game-changer for creating and capturing memories together. Before buying this, we always had to awkwardly ask strangers to take our pictures, or one of us would have to be left out of the photo to hold the camera. reviews.title: Holds my phone vertically and w/out tipping over
reviews.body: UGREEN Cell Phone stand: I wanted a phone stand that would hold my phone upright vertically w/out tipping over if I needed to use the screen on my phone. This stand seemed the least less likely to tip over. I’ve had this stand for a few weeks now and my phone has not tipped over when using it. This stand works well for what I needed it to do. My phone w/ its case does not fit into the crevice the phone is supposed to fit into, I have an iPhone XS w/ an Otter Box case. My phone sits on top of the crevice (I would have included a pic but I can’t figure out how to w/out giving Amazon full access to my pics and videos). The phone sitting on top of the crevice actually makes it work out better I think, my phones speakers aren’t muffled by sitting on the bottom of the crevice (which I saw some ppl mention in their reviews). I haven’t tried the stand to make a call or face time, but I’m assuming it would work fine w/ my phones speakers and mic sitting above the crevice. If my phone fit in the crevice like it’s supposed to, I could see that being a problem and muffling sounds both ways, esp the mic part since there is only one mic at the bottom of my phone. It is a little frustrating you can’t charge the phone in the stand, which I knew going in and didn’t think would bother me, but turns out that part is pretty inconvenient. My phone is old and the battery ain’t what it used to be, needs to be charged often. This stand doesn’t work great w/ my IPad 9th gen. It’s not sturdy enough to use the iPad screen while it’s in the stand. My iPad w/case sits nice in the crevice, but when using the touch screen, I have to press super super light or the stand expands fully open tilting my iPad back. I didn’t buy this stand for iPad use but it would have been nice if it was functional w/ my iPad. Overall, this phone stand holds my phone vertically w/out tipping over. Again, my phone doesn’t fit in the crevice so my speakers and mic aren’t muffled. For under $9, I’m overall satisfied w/ the phone stand to hold my phone.

reviews.title: Sturdy, but there are some fine details that deserve consideration
reviews.body: The magnetic Tripod/Selfie stick arrived in the color and as described in the Amazon listing. The package included the selfie stick, a magnetic fill light, a USB charging cord, and a fabric case big enough to carry the stick and the accessories. The selfie-stick felt solid in my hand and appeared to be of premium quality.There is also a traditional tripod mount for a 360 camera or action Camera. The tripod was easy to set up, and extend to its full height. The tripod legs appeared sturdy. The magnetic fill-light easily attached to the back of the magnetic selfie stick. It had a dial that allowed for dimming and variable brightness. The magnet for the selfie stick seemed strong enough… but I did find myself accidently knocking my phone off of the selfie-stick when attempting to remove the magnetic light. Fortunately my phone landed on a plush carpet, but I did wonder about how well the magnetic mount might work in real world conditions, where I am often setting up the selfie stick on concrete, or perhaps in crowded areas. It seems like I will need to be careful to assure I don’t accidently dislodge my camera. I also found that the magnetic tripod mount was not as compact as the phone clamp mount that I have on another similar style selfie stick. The tripod mount is nice… but it doesn’t have a dial on it like other similar tripod mount, that helps fine tune the direction the phone/camera is mounted. At time of review this tripod/selfie stick has a price that is higher than comparable products. Although in theory, I like the idea of a magnetic phone mount, in practice I will likely use a more secure mounting method like a clamp mount, and this tripod/selfie stick will likely not replace a cheaper but similar product already in my camera bag.

reviews.title: Throw away your other selfie sticks and phone tripods, this is IT
reviews.body: I'm not hyping it. I'm not fan boying neither, but THIS HERE??? Everything makes soooo much sense! Theres big brains that came into thinking how to design this tripod. Ok let me explain: at its most compact form, its about a foot long (give or take). Its clean, it doesnt rattle, its sturdy and minds its own business in the bag that came with the package. All good right? But once you're ready to take a photo or a video? Simply flip the mag safe end, pull that end of the tripod up to your desired length, then tap the bottom of the tripod right on the ground! Voila! It opens for a quick stable tripod configuration then snap your magsafe equipped phone to the magnet then you're set! (Btw? The magnet is so strong I feel like it makes a promise to your phone that it will never let go... honestly). Pairing the remote is also a piece of cake. Just hold till it lights up and pair it with your bt. Done. Apart from the magnet, if u much prefer to use something else that requires the common 1/4 tripod screw, this has u covered! Need a light? The light this set comes with, although petite, packs a strong illumination. Dialing it way high just simply is too bright (but thats a good thing right?). And if that was enough , this thing when not in tripod mode (more like a selfie stick), extend beyond what id be comfortable walking around with. The length could simply work as a drone shot almost for 360 cams or something. And at any given length, the selfie stick just simply keeps it in place and doesnt slide down. No fancy locks, no twisting, just pull and leave. Its way too easy. Out of all the selfie sticks ive owned, this here, is BY FAR, the most innovative, convenient and well thought of piece that I simply have no reason to leave it behind with any trips I go to. It simply works as you want it to. Easiest 5 stars ive ever give. I highly highly recommend this supervision version of selfie stick+tripod combo.

title: Yamaha GL1 Guitalele, Natural, Baritone
bullet_points: A unique mini 6-string nylon guitar that is sized like a baritone ukulele (17" scale) and plays like a guitar
The guitalele's tuning is pitched up to "A" (or up to a 4th) at A/D/G/C/E/A.
Nylon Strings
Comes with a soft case bag

reviews.title: Great little guitar that can play your favorite Uke songs too!
reviews.body: I've been playing this little gem for a week now as a replacement for my full size acoustic that is in dire need of a neck reset. It sits next to my office chair where I can pick it up and play any time. So far it has done a pretty good job of staying in tune with only the usual nylon string settling in. Tone is interesting with a neat, plucky sound and, being tuned to A, it shares the same finger positions on the 4 treble strings as a ukulele. In fact, it is a good sounding baritone ukulele but could be a little bit challenging for some due to closer string spacing compared to a uke. Action is fine and I am in no hurry to change the setup. factory strings seem OK and i will play on them until they wear out. Yamaha states that low or standard tension classical strings can be used and Savarez, D'Addario and DR are recommended brands. No need for special guilele strings. The finish is very satin and may not be pleasing for those that enjoy glossy guitars though i think it's OK and seems tough enough. My GL1 came with a small blemish in the wood on the back which is an imperfection in the wood itself and not the finish. I would take 1/2 a star for the blemish but quality control is overall pretty good and the fret ends aren't noticeably sharp. I would not recommend this instrument for beginners due to the short fret spacing and slightly more difficult fingering for some chords. A 1/2 or 3/4 scale classical or steel string guitar will be a better choice for learning the fundamentals and will have more volume for performances later on when the player gains confidence. Who is this instrument for? number one, it's for me. I have been playing guitar for decades and have a soft spot for small bodied instruments and recently started playing my wife's ukulele due to my guitar being down for the count. Ukulele players might enjoy this instrument as a way to cross over to six string though the string spacing will take some getting used to. Guitar players who want a sturdy travel guitar will be well served by this instrument but will have to make peace with transposing everything up a fourth. Some players have used high tension strings to allow for standard guitar tuning. I'm not sure I will do so as I like the sound as it is and also play ukulele music. Overall I think the Yamaha GL-1 is a reasonable value for the money and I'm very happy with it so far.

reviews.title: A quality instrument from Yamaha
reviews.body: 69 year old guitar hack here. Played electric, and some acoustic guitar in three bands way back in the 1970's. Played acoustic at a wedding. My neighbor bought a Yamaha GL-1 "guitalele" A few years ago, and told me recently that he loves it! A GL-1 is basically a very compact 6 string classical guitar, but, instead of being tuned Eadgbe, it is tuned 5 frets up on each string, so the low and high e's become a's. This means that all the chord shapes I know on a regular guitar can be played in the same positions, but the name of the chord will be different. Example, an e major chord shape on a guitar, will really be an a major on the Yamaha. If I am just playing by myself for myself, there is no problem. If I was to play along with a regular guitar, we would have to work out what key to play in. Also, if I sing and play, then depending on what key I play in, I would have to sing in higher notes. This thing came quicky to me in Hawaii, and it is in perfect condition! Since it had nylon/classical type strings, it is going to take much longer for the strings to settle down and stop sretching. Way longer than my steel stringers. So, don't write a review after a few days complaining about this. All classical style nylon string guitars do this! Pick it up,tune it, play it, and keep tuning it. The tuners on mine seem just fine. It is a total blast for me to play. It sounds great, especially for the small body size. It has very good volume and sustain too. A bit stingy on the fret markers, both on the fingerboard and side of the neck. If you have big fingers, some chording might be a bit crowded. It doesn't have a truss rod. But, many classical guitars and many other guitaleles don't have them either. I have yet to read a review, or watch a video review, where the owner had a neck warp. In short, I should have bought one of these long ago. Update after more than a year now. I still love this little 6 stringer! I have been selling some of my amps and ukes etc. I had considered selling my Yamaha, but cannot do it! It is just such a great insrument. Mine is still perfect. Drawbacks? Few. The 17" scale is a bit tight for me. One string started unravelling after not too much playing. I was able to buy the one string and replaced it. I read a review somewhere where the writer returned his due to various flaws. Looking at mine it's hard to believe. I think Yamaha should make an option of the GL-1 that would come with an under saddle pickup with tuner and volume/tone controls. Great price, great instrument, great FUN!! 2/28/2025 update: Just wanted to say my estimation of this instrument has gone up if anything. I am taking super good care of it. It us holding up great. I had one of the wound strings start to unravel early and replaced it. Zero problems. After break in it holds tune as good or better than my other string instruments. That alone is saying a lot. The climate here in the Puna District on the big island plays he'll with stringed instruments. Most go sharp sitting overnight, and flat sitting during the day. This little guy is built very well. I wish it had come with an active pickup with tuned and equalizer, but it's still a keeper!

reviews.title: Perfect little guitar for fun and travel
reviews.body: This little thing is one of my dearest possessions!! I've played guitar as a hobby off and on for about 18 years and have a couple of full-sized acoustics. About a year ago I started researching smaller instruments because I wanted something easy to travel with. I looked into 1/4 size student guitars and I looked into the Little Martin and its Taylor equivalent. While the Little Martin has great reviews and a great sound, it costs 3-4 times more than this little guy does. It's definitely worth that price, but I didn't have that kind of money to spend. For about $100, the Yamaha Guitalele is excellent. It has a beautiful sound and it's very easy to pick up and take it with you on trips! (To keep it safer for long trips I bought a hard shell tenor uke case which works really well for it. I also bought one of those little Snark clip-on tuners and have been very satisfied with that as well.) Two things which take some adjusting to if you are used to playing a full-size guitar: 1) The strings are a lot closer together and your fingers may feel fat and clumsy at first. I got used to this pretty fast though. 2) The guitalele is tuned to A instead of the standard E tuning of a full-sized guitar. Basically this means anything you play on the guitalele is like playing your reg. guitar with a capo on the 5th fret. So when you play a C-shape chord on this guy, you are actually playing a G chord. I was used to playing a lot of songs on my regular guitar and had to figure out how to translate them to continue playing them in the same key. (It's possible to lower the tuning to E if you want, but the strings have a slack, kind of rubbery sound and they don't stay in tune as long.) I'd recommend checking out the YouTube video reviews for this instrument before you buy it if you have any more questions. You can hear what it sounds like and get some expert input! It really is great. I love mine to the moon and back and have had a blast playing it!

reviews.title: Fun instrument for the price, but don't expect perfection.
reviews.body: This guitalele has opened up a bit since I got it. I started playing ukulele 2 years ago, and started learning guitar almost a year ago. After having Amazon cancel an order I placed on an acoustic guitar from the Amazon Warehouse. (Grr! Btw on that! I feel really cheated considering the same guitar turned up with a seller who refabs and resells damaged instruments, and I was extremely excited about it, until I got the message "they couldn't find it," last minute on delivery day!!! 😠 That's so wrong imo.) I chose this guitalele in it's stead however. It has issues with frets not being cut long enough in spots but nothing that makes it unplayable. It's cosmetic for the most part. There's a few other purely cosmetic issues. Mine has a couple spots the factory missed applying the wood filler to, on the body to make it smooth. Theres a small spot on the bottom of the neck where the wood chipped before assembly and it wasn't filled with filler or even glue to fill the gap. It's a mass produced instrument at an affordable price. I was expecting small imperfections. The sloppy fret cutting job is the only kind-of annoying one to me. The one I have is actually a replacement for one I exchanged which had a mfg. defect which made it unplayable. The first one wasn't inspected properly and shouldn't have left the factory in the dangerous condition it was in. Amazon took care of me immediately and the exchange was smooth and painless. Hopefully yamaha corrects the quality control issues in their factory. For my own play style I had the nut filed down so my hand could glide over the nut. The stock nut height stopped my hand down there like a brick wall, and having the nut done cost as much as the guitalele. This probably won't bother most people. I'm just throwing it out there, that the nut sticks up above the string height, and if you like to slide in or out by the nut, it might be something to consider for someone. The piece of wood that was used on the back of the one I received is unexpectedly pretty. I got lucky. The top has nice strait grain. The neck is ugly. It's constructed in a few pieces and mine doesn't remotely match. One side appears to have had a patch of tear out or something, and Yamaha filled it really nicely with filler, but the filler is darker than the neck wood and adds to the kind of sloppy franken-neck look. Again, not a deal breaker. I can't feel a difference, and they have to keep costs down. When I got it, it sounded a little "stuffy." After playing it daily since I got it, the wood seems to have opened up a bit on all tones except the low A, which still sounds the same. If it does open up, this instrument is pretty impressive sounding for the money in my opinion. Someone said in another review the thing is built like a tank. I agree. It's not a delicate feeling instrument. It seems pretty well constructed until the fret wire though. Overall it's been fun to play. It's the perfect size. I left sheerness blank in the star rating. Not sure how that applies to a guitalele or any stringed instrument? Thickness doesn't really apply either, but I rated it 4 because the wood is thick. I might update this review in the future if anything changes, but I'd probably get another one if something happens to mine.

reviews.title: decent, doesn't need to be tuned up a full 4th to sound OK
reviews.body: Mahalo used to make a similar product for less than half the price, so this guy seems a little overpriced to me – but since the Mahalo seems to be discontinued, there's no real competitor, and this hardly breaks the bank. It has entirely acceptable playability, sound, intontation, etc. I especially like to play it like a mandolin, flat-picking single lines, but of course it can play full-chord accompaniments, sounding just like a ukulele but lower. Travels fine, though one thing to note about the classic camp-singalong use is that the nylon strings are suuuuuper sensitive to temperature changes, so it's a bit frustrating playing it outdoors in chilly air next to a hot campfire – you might need to invest in a steel-string alternative if you can't abide that. You *can* tune it to standard guitar tuning (E2, A2, D3, ...), which is useful if you want to use it for, say, composing on the go and not get confused about which key you're in – but down there the strings sound like garbage and don't stay in tune. The recommended tuning is up a 4th, which I find a bit high, since you can't even play G2 (de facto a lot of things you play on guitars tend to be in keys like G, D, C ...). One solution is to use the recommended tuning but with "drop G" (lowest string = G2), which sounds fine. But you also can just tune the whole thing a major 3rd higher than a guitar (major 2nd lower than the recommended tuning), rather than a 4th (so: G2, C3, F3 ....) which IMHO sounds just as good and stays in tune just as well. (I just personally keep getting confused by the mental arithmetic that requires – what you expect to be a G major chord is actually Bb major ... etc.)

reviews.title: I take mine everywhere
reviews.body: I love this thing. I tied a strap to it with some shoe strings, I slap it on my back, get on my bike. I take it with me when I go hiking, to school, to the beach, or anywhere really. The tuning on it is ADGCEA which would be equal to as if you had a capo on a regular guitar's 5th fret, which means that you can play the same chord shapes as a regular guitar, the notes will just be higher. As far as quality goes, I'm pretty happy with it. Some people said the strings that they got were no good, but I've had mine for about 3 months now and I have no complaints. The strings are very sensitive though. They bend very easily, so sometimes the chords played sound good and other times they might sound a little off. I see as a very delicate instrument.. when I press down my fingers for chords I press them straight down and make sure I'm not bending them. A;so, because they bend easily, it can go out of tune pretty easily too. I tune mine often, to make sure they are good to go. I have always tuned my normal guitars by ear, however I find that it is harder to do with the guitarlele, so I use a tuner usually. Visually I have no complaints, the wood and finish are nice, the neck has good action and feel, although a small part of me wishes that they had some artwork around the soundhole. As for sound quality, I love it.. the higher strings/notes do stand out more in a way, and definitely have the ukulele sound, but if you play gently enough it creates a nice balance. The resonance is beautiful. It has a very warm, mellow sound. It's pretty loud for it's size too. And it is so versatile, you can play Spanish style chords like Em and Am which sounds awesome (Onda Vaga uses a uke, perfect example, youtube them), .. you can emulate a mandolin to an extent.. I'm not saying it sounds exactly like a mandolin since it obviously can't replicate the resonant-sound of the double layered strings, but it does have the high notes from the strings that at least sound somewhat similar to a mandolin, if you want to cover a song with one. Or you can just play regular songs, normal chord shapes, even powerchords sound good. It's just like guitar. Just tuned to much higher notes. If you know music theory, you can do a lot with this little guitar. I even have used a capo on mine and it sounds good, although when I put it too high up the fret spaces are so small it's hard to make the chord shapes ;-) Before I saw the guitarlele I was looking at rogue instruments because they sell cheap mandolins and ukuleles. I checked out reviews of their instruments on youtube and they had some mixed reviews.. they didn't seem like very good quality. I saw someone mention the guitarlele on the comments, and when I looked it up I knew it was the 'travel' instrument I wanted. 100 bucks, for a completely unique Yamaha brand instrument? You can't go wrong. Yamaha aren't the super-high end guitars, but my bigger acoustic is a yamaha and I don't have any complaints about that one either (a friend gave it to me to replace my epiphone acoustic which I need to get a new saddle for). I hope this review was helpful. If you get one, enjoy it. I know I enjoy mine. I've even started buying other travel instruments like a melodica and a Buffalo Drum.. so yeah. Enjoy!!

reviews.title: Here is the "real deal" review on this Guitalele
reviews.body: I've been playing, and writing music since 1984. I play a myriad of instruments and currently, I write and record commercially licensed music under BMI, Inc. My Wife bought this instrument for me for a holiday gift, but I wanted to check it out before it gets wrapped.. just in case of damage. I am glad that I did. I also know how to setup and do maintenance on both electronic and acoustic instruments. The good things about this instrument: This instrument sounds really good, as it seems to be structurally sound. I do not see any cracks in the body or missing glue around the neck joint. The strings are nice wrapped around to tuning pags. The open faced tuners and gears seem to be of a higher quality than others that I have seen. The bad things about this instrument: The bridge saddle is WAY too high. I have no issues in regards to setting up a bridge saddle, but I expected Yamaha to be a "bit more" on the quality control side of things and at least have the saddle to a more "normal" height. The fretboard and body of this instrument was "very" dry. I used some Music Nomad f-one oil on the fretboard and some of the body as it needed it "badly". The thing that was VERY surprising to me, is there were run-offs / rough spots in the back and sides of the instrument. For a more inexpensive instrument from a no-name company.. I could see that. .but for the price and the Yamaha name.. again.. VERY SURPRISING. I'm also having some issues in regards to getting a partial from Amazon for some reason, but I have amplified that further up the chain on the Amazon side. Other things to think about: I was able to tune this to a standard guitar tuning, that is very possible. The neck is "wide" just like a classical guitar. A lot of people think this is a hybrid instrument of an acoustic guitar and a baritone ukulele. It's really a cross between an Classical Guitar and a baritone ukulele. Conclusion: I am sure that I will have a really awesome time opening this on Christmas day and setting up the saddle on the bridge. And I can probably buff out the rough spots in the finish.. but buying this really changed my mind in regards to Yamaha quality control. UPDATE: I was able to take off a lot of material from the saddle, and lowered the strings, so the playability is better, but I still am a bit suprised in regards to the rough spots in the finish. The instrument should be priced in the $50.00 USD mark. Other than that, it does make a nice portable instrument in regards to classical guitar or baritone ukulele. - Tom

reviews.title: A Delightful Addition to the Collection!
reviews.body: This little guy is so much fun! I love playing the ukulele, but sometimes it can be a little frustrating. With only four strings, uke chords often end up in awkward inversions, having a chord tone other than the tonic as the lowest note. By adding two strings to the bass side, you can always have the inversion you want. For uke players the chords will be a little more complex with two additional strings to deal with. Also, in strumming the "uke sound" you'll need to get the hang of not hitting the bottom two strings. But it's all worth the effort and makes for a more "musically complete" sound. For uke players aspiring to play guitar, this is a great bridge. I think guitarists will find it fun as well. The chords are all familiar but will sound a fourth up. Guitarists who are familiar with using a capo won't have any problem with this. Videos online show how to restring the instrument so it can play down in guitar range, but I think it's more fun as a "super uke!" I like the sunburst style and mahogany back and sides. It has a nice, warm uke-y tone. I'm glad I got it!

reviews.title: A nice little guitar for the price
reviews.body: At this price level I had low expectations, but having respect for the Yamaha brand I took a chance and ordered the guitar, half expecting to send it back it it proved a disappointment. It didn’t disappoint at all. As an experienced player of various full size acoustic guitars I must admit this little guitar is surprisingly well made and pleasant to play for such an economy price. TBH I didn’t buy it for myself, it was supposed to be an alternative instrument for my Ukelele playing partner to progress to. She didn’t like it, because two extra strings aid a step to far for her. Ah we’ll never mind I tried. Also I hope to use it to teach guitar to my 8 year old grandchild but haven’t introduced it to him yet. The body size is ideal for him, and the classical type nylon strings should be easier for him. However the neck width is about the same as a full size guitar and flat rather than radiused, which is not ideal for small hands. Also due to the necessarily short neck the tuning cannot be standard EADGBE like a full size so that’s an obstacle to learning the fretboard for later progression to a full size guitar when he’s older.

reviews.title: Mucho mejor de lo que me esperaba
reviews.body: La verdad es que había leído mucho de este producto antes de comprarlo y, una vez lo he recibido, me ha sorprendido gratamente. Las calidades de la madera son muy muy buenas, la acción de las cuerdas es correcta y el sonido acorde a la dimensión de la caja del instrumento. Llevo años tocando la guitarra y quería ésta para estar en casa tranquilo en el sofá. La afinación en La no es un problema. La puedes afinar con un afinador de click en modo cromático. Mantiene la afinación muy bien desde el principio y las cuerdas venían nuevas, para nada oxidadas y no se estropean con los trastes como decían algunos. La funda es mucho mejor de lo que yo esperaba con un ligero grosor y un asa. El problema que dice la gente de que la afinación es diferente no es ningún problema. Puedes tocar las mismas canciones pero suenan un poco más agudas, pero ningún problema. Antes de comprar el guitalele prueba con tu guitarra con una cejilla en el quinto traste y así te haces una idea de cómo suena el guitalele. Así que muy muy satisfecho con la compra.
reviews.body_en: The truth is that I had read a lot about this product before purchasing it and, once I received it, I was pleasantly surprised. The qualities of the wood are very very good, the action of the strings is correct and the sound corresponds to the size of the instrument's case. I've been playing the guitar for years and I wanted this one to be at home quiet on the couch. A tuning is not a problem. You can tune it with a click tuner in chromatic mode. It maintains the tuning very well from the beginning and the strings came new, not rusty at all and they are not damaged by the frets as some said. The case is much better than I expected with a slight thickness and a handle. The problem that people say about the tuning being different is not a problem at all. You can play the same songs but they sound a little higher, but no problem. Before buying the guitalele, try your guitar with a capo on the fifth fret so you can get an idea of ​​what the guitalele sounds like. So very very satisfied with the purchase.

reviews.title: Poor quality with misaligned/mis-spaced frets.
reviews.body: ***Update I am changing my one-star review to five-stars. I wrote my original review complaining of the poor quality, but especially fret placement. The company reached out to me and refunded our money. That is impressive. I appreciate a company that is willing to stand behind their product. Hopefully only our guitar had poor fret placement. Other than that and the poor string quality, the guitar is nice. Again, maybe we just had bad luck. Original review: The guitar looks nice upon opening it. It appeared to be of good quality. However, we have only had problems since then. First, the strings are cheap. They break easily. They did include a replacement set, but we are already through most of those as well. Further, our guitar teacher stated that the frets are off so it will be out of tune the further down you go on the frets. We took it into a guitar repair shop who confirmed the issue. The frets are spaced improperly. They tried to file some parts down to make it the best they could. That was another 50 dollars. Conclusion, this guitar looks nice but that is about it. If you are seriously looking to learn how to play the guitar then I suggest paying a little more to get a good guitar. We paid almost 100 dollars for this, and more since to replace strings and fix the frets in an attempt to optimize it the best we could. Paying more upfront for a good working guitar with correct fret placement is the best thing to do. I guess we will know better next time. Don't waste your money unless you are looking for a decoration for your room.

reviews.title: Bad Quality
reviews.body: I bought this guitar a little over a month ago. At first, I noticed a few blemishes along with the tuning peg being rusty and paid no mind. The very first time I tuned, I noticed it making pop sound for a few tuning keys and was anxious the guitar was gonna break but didn’t think much about it. I only played it a few times and picked it back up a week ago… As I tuned it again, the crack and pop sound continue to be made by the guitar, it seems to always make these sound when I tuned and the pin bridge got stuck. I could not get it back out and it broke. I’m afraid the guitar is not well built and although I considered getting parts of it refurbished at a store, I believe it would cost over than the guitar’s worth to get it all fixed. Everytime I tuned this guitar, I always get that anxiety that the crack sound is going to snap the guitar. I’m hoping to get even the slightest help over this. Please reach out, I am truly bummed about this.

reviews.title: It’s not worth it
reviews.body: Review – Fender FA-25N Nylon (3/4) This guitar is very disappointing unless you’re buying it strictly for a small child. If you have slightly wider fingers, chord shapes are uncomfortable right away. The neck feels narrow, and even basic chords like C major are awkward and frustrating to play. The biggest issue is the extremely high action. The strings sit very high off the fretboard, making the guitar hard to play and tiring on the fingers. It’s obvious this is done at the factory to avoid fret buzz, but it completely kills playability. The guitar does not feel inviting to play at all. The instrument is lightweight, and the body doesn’t look poorly assembled, but build quality alone doesn’t make a good musical experience. Comfort and playability matter — and this guitar fails there. Yes, it’s cheap, but the overall playing experience is bad. If you have any prior musical experience or basic expectations, this guitar is not worth it. Conclusion: Only suitable for a young beginner with small hands. Otherwise, I do not recommend it. I’m very disappointed and would not buy this model again.

reviews.title: Increíble guitarra para estudiantes
reviews.body: La Fender FA25N es una excelente opción para estudiantes, niños y jóvenes que buscan iniciarse en el mundo de la música. Con un tamaño 3/4, esta guitarra es perfecta para aquellos que buscan una instrumento más pequeño y manejable. *Comodidades* La FA25N es muy cómoda de tocar, gracias a su tamaño compacto y su mástil estrecho. Los trastes son suaves y fáciles de presionar, lo que la hace ideal para aquellos que están empezando a aprender. La guitarra también viene con una acción baja, lo que facilita la ejecución de acordes y notas. *Sonido* El sonido de la FA25N es sorprendentemente bueno para una guitarra de su tamaño y construcción(laminada). La combinación de la tapa de abeto y el cuerpo de nato produce un sonido cálido y equilibrado, con una buena respuesta en las frecuencias bajas y medias. Aunque no es una guitarra para profesionales, la FA25N es perfecta para practicar y tocar en casa o en pequeños grupos. *Acabados* La FA25N viene en un acabado natural hermoso, que muestra la belleza del abeto y el nato. El acabado es suave y brillante, y la guitarra tiene un aspecto muy atractivo. *Tamaño* Es importante tener en cuenta que la FA25N es una guitarra de tamaño 3/4, lo que la hace ideal para estudiantes, niños y jóvenes. Sin embargo, para adultos con manos grandes o que buscan una guitarra más grande, esta guitarra puede ser un poco pequeña. *Conclusión* En resumen, la Fender FA25N es una excelente opción para aquellos que buscan una guitarra para principiantes. Su tamaño compacto, comodidad y sonido hacen que sea perfecta para estudiantes, niños y jóvenes. Aunque puede ser un poco pequeña para adultos, es una excelente opción para aquellos que buscan una guitarra para practicar en casa o para regalar a un joven músico.
reviews.body_en: The Fender FA25N is an excellent option for students, children and young people looking to get started in the world of music. With a 3/4 size, this guitar is perfect for those looking for a smaller, more manageable instrument. *Comforts* The FA25N is very comfortable to play, thanks to its compact size and narrow neck. The frets are smooth and easy to press, making it ideal for those just starting to learn. The guitar also comes with a low action, making it easier to play chords and notes. *Sound* The sound of the FA25N is surprisingly good for a guitar of its size and (laminate) construction. The combination of the spruce top and nato body produces a warm and balanced sound, with good response in the low and mid frequencies. Although it is not a guitar for professionals, the FA25N is perfect for practicing and playing at home or in small groups. *Finishes* The FA25N comes in a beautiful natural finish, showcasing the beauty of spruce and nato. The finish is smooth and shiny, and the guitar has a very attractive appearance. *Size* It is important to note that the FA25N is a 3/4 size guitar, making it ideal for students, children and youth. However, for adults with large hands or looking for a larger guitar, this guitar may be a little small. *Conclusion* In summary, the Fender FA25N is a great option for those looking for a beginner guitar. Its compact size, comfort and sound make it perfect for students, children and young people. Although it may be a little small for adults, it is a great option for those looking for a guitar to practice at home or to give as a gift to a young musician.

reviews.title: I found my instrument
reviews.body: I was going to try and wait a week or two before writing a review for this, but I just couldn’t help myself. One other thing I’ll add before I start is unlike other reviewers, I haven’t had all the best brand Guitars. I’ve had electric and acoustic guitars, Bass guitars, and Ukuleles of various sizes - all at the $250 or less range. So with that… I love this instrument. This is the closest thing I’ve ever had to a “deluxe guitar”. I’ve purchased boxes in this range before and thought “yeah, okay, this’ll do.” This is the first time I’ve thought “okay this is what I’m talking about!” First off, this box keeps in tune. Not only thought but the tuning pegs are tight and seem to snap into tune pretty easily. I walk around the house and sit it up against all kinds of surfaces and don’t have to worry about knocking it out of tune. Next and just as important, it seems this guitar has raised frets and low action. I saw a few reviews and YouTube comments that made me think this was going to be hard to play and have high action, but this is perfect! I’m not worried about going to get a setup any time soon. The neck shape does seem to make fretting easier as well. This box was built with a lot of thought and a lot of love. I most recently played baritone ukulele, and even at 6’0 with relatively big hands, a dreadnought style guitar is too cumbersome for me. This thing could be great for a smaller person or kid, but it’s also very comfortable for me. Lastly but not least, the sound! I will say that when played with a pick or my nails it doesn’t produce a bad sound, but I wouldn’t say that’s the guitars strong suit. It’s kind of high and thin. BUT if you either strum this with your thumb and fingers or (even better) finger style pluck, this thing sounds gorgeous. It’s warm and resonant with lots of emotion. I’ve tried hammer ons, pull offs. Slides, bends, slides into bends, it all sounds clean, full, and resonant. I’m a beginner player, but I can see how I’m really going to be expressing myself with this box soon. If I had to gripe about anything at all, the bridge is just a little rough and grainy. Like not enough to give me a splinter, but not totally smooth. The rest of the body and guitar feels so nice and high quality to me. So yeah besides maybe not being the best guitar for pick-exclusive playing, and it might not have any electronics or bells and whistles, I feel like a wizard who found his wand with this guitar. Happy playing y’all! Ps, the little treats added in the box were a cute touch. 🙂

reviews.title: Excellent for beginners to intermediate guitarists
reviews.body: I appreciated the price for this guitar. Seems solidly made and electronics are well done - no glitches so far. I like the composition of woods and the resulting sound is clear, can be loud if you want it that way. The imbedded tuner is handy as heck, and the action on the fret board is remarkably low making it fairly easy to play, bend notes, and move quickly. HOWEVER - I do not like the finish on the sounding board. It looks like it is dusty or dirty all the time as a result. Because it comes without a pick guard - the finish is getting scratched. The tuners do not move smoothly and so tuning becomes an issue when needed. And when playing through and amp - it is easy to over power the amp and get some pretty crappy sound as a result. This guitar plays beautifully as an acoustic - just use some caution when plugging in as the sound is easily distorted. Major drawback - comes without a case! I am glad I bought it - love the cutaway - good guitar.

reviews.title: Excellent Value for a Young Classical Guitarist
reviews.body: For context, I purchased this guitar for my children. They had been using hand-me-down classical guitars for their lessons, and as they’ve started taking their playing more seriously, it was time for an upgrade. I’ve been playing guitar since I was 10, so I’ve owned and played quite a few classical guitars over the past 30 years. This one genuinely surprised me. The value for the money is excellent. It plays very well, feels solidly put together, and doesn’t have the frustrating quirks you often find with less expensive guitars. If you’re purchasing this for a child or a newer player, I think it’s a no-brainer. It’s an affordable instrument that they can actually enjoy learning and progressing on. The included gig bag is pretty basic—just the standard inexpensive nylon zippered bag—so I don’t expect it to last forever, but it does the job of getting the guitar from one place to another. Overall, this has been an excellent purchase and exceeded my expectations for the price.

reviews.title: Sounds amazing!
reviews.body: This brings plays very nicely. I bought the Vangoa 12 string from Amazon and was very disappointed so I replaced it with this Ibanez. The Vangoa did have a nice matte black finish but the tuners were garbage. This Ibanez has a satin neck and glossy body finish. Does have some sharp fret ends that can be fixed with some minor sanding. Tuners hold time nicely even though 12 strings are notoriously difficult to keep in tune. For estethic reasons I changed the tuners to bronze. The action after was great up to the 12th fret but too high afterwards so I did take out bridge saddle and sand it from the bottom end (approximately 1mm) to lower the overall action. There is a spare saddle included incase you need it. Worked out well afterwards. Overall would highly recommend if you’re looking play Pink Floyd Wish You Were Here or Bon Jovi songs lol at home but if you something more professional for recording then I would recommend something better.

The ONLY complaint is that the strings it comes with are very cheap and don't sound good. We swapped them for D'Addario strings and it played so much better. reviews.title: Not bad at all.
reviews.body: I have to say that I am impressed. While I must admit that I'm a beginner at guitar (I'm a former drummer that can no longer play due to health issues), I learned a lot about guitars from an old band mate. This beginner guitar sounds nice, and is of a better size for me to learn on. I have an old acoustic, but the body is far too large for me. This guitar arrived a little over an hour ago. No nicks, dings, or cracks on it. Checked the screws on the tuning machines, everything was good. Since the headstock is more of a classical style than a regular acoustic, I took off the steel strings that came on the guitar and replaced them with classical strings (nylon - medium tension). While it's going to take at least a few days for the nylon strings to stretch out enough before they stay in tune, I did get it tuned up for a bit and played a few chords. The guitar sounds wonderful, with a good bit of volume. I think I'll enjoy learning on this guitar. If you decide to get this guitar and go with nylon strings (which you should), unless you go with 'ball end' strings, you might have to look up how to 'tie' the nylon strings onto the guitar, as some nylon strings that you can get will not come with a ball end. I had helped do this on a guitar decades ago, but needed a refresher course, and found the information online easily enough. The reason I say you should use nylon strings is because they require less tension than the normal steel strings. Since this guitar does *not* have a truss rod, you want to go with strings that do not need as much tension. Using steel strings can cause problems with the bridge piece (breaking or coming off), the neck (warping), and the tuning pegs. You might be able to get away with using light or super light tension steel strings, but that's your choice. I'm sticking with the nylon strings. They bring out the sound that I want from this guitar. They're also easier to learn with as a beginner, as they don't hurt your fingertips as much. Yes, it will take longer to build up the callouses on the fingertips, but hey...less pain when learning can be a good thing. But again, for an inexpensive guitar, this one is a good deal. As with any instrument, if you're not sure if you, or the person you get it for, are going to maintain interest in learning the instrument...going with an inexpensive instrument like this is always the best idea. As for the other bits that come in this package...the picks are good, the case is good enough to keep dust off the guitar, the strap is not all that great, and the tuner is pretty much garbage because the battery cover does not want to stay on (I have another one just like it, and it has the same problem), and the pitch pipe is 'meh'. The main thing you want in this package is the guitar. Just get some better strings, a good tuner (I have a 'Snark' that wasn't expensive), and a decent guitar strap...and you're set.

reviews.title: Mediocre Beginner Guitar - Fit for Learning the Basics of Guitar Playing
reviews.body: This guitar is good for deciding if you want to commit to learning guitar. The strings and everything work just fine, so one can learn fingerstyle playing and chords, however, the strings are rather buzzy, and in addition with a high action guitar such as this, it is harder on the fingers to play. I used this guitar frequently for about 7 months before deciding that I would like to upgrade to an actual name brand guitar (like Fender, Ibanez, or Rogue). When I would put a regular capo on any fret of the guitar, the low E bass note would become flat, however, with no capo, the string would perform just fine. I went to a guitar center to ask about it, and they hadn't even heard of this brand of guitar. Final Verdict: Yes, the guitar is good value of money if you are looking to see if a guitar would be the right pursuit for you. Looks-wise, the guitar looks nice with a mix of basic and elegant. However, I'd only recommend buying this guitar if you are looking to see if guitar is the right fit for you. If you are looking to buy a guitar that will last you a while, you are better off looking elsewhere as this guitar is better for a trial run rather than a long-term commitment.

reviews.title: Amongst the good, the better and the best...
reviews.body: I have books 1, 2 and 3 but have not finished them. After I started working through book 1 (one) I purchase an additional set or version that combines books 1, 2 and 3 for my 16 year old grandson and sent it to him to read and study. He is self taught and I felt it is written or presented in a way that a person of any age could and would enjoy the learning process as it is presented in the books. Praise for what I have read and worked through is well deserved. It has a sequence and explanation that is way more sensible to me than what I have read in other books. When I pick back up and resume going through the book I do not have to go back and review because of the way the material is presented. Once it is taught, it does not require unnecessary repetition. That is rare and eliminates frustration. There are clear explanations and I am not left with having to do research as to what something means. I recommend purchasing book 1 and giving it a try. Complete it and you will want to continue with the subsequent books. These reviews are about books that are intended to lead us to learning how to play guitar and hopefully enjoy it. Good luck.

reviews.title: Become a better guitar player
reviews.body: I am a beginner guitar student. Over the years I have purchased several guitar books that promised to make guitar learning easy and fun. Those books are still sitting in my closet. Back in March 2024 I purchased all three books 'NO BULL Guitar For Beginners.' I am still working on the exercises in Book One. This book teaches you the basic chords, chord progressions, and strumming. To support your learning process, you also have online videos which further support the learning process. If you want to learn how to play acoustic guitar, I highly recommend you look at purchasing James Shipway's three book series. Volumes two and three further help you on your journey from beginner to becoming an intermediate player.

reviews.title: “No Bull” Won’t Leave You Cowed
reviews.body: I am a raw beginner, but I’m finding this book to be helpful for two reasons: The explanations are clear; moreover, the author understands the hurdles that all newbies encounter (sore fingers, difficulty stretching the hand for shapes like the C and G chords, trouble memorizing shapes), and makes a special effort to be encouraging. Like most people, I want to rush into being good at anything new I try. The author says it’s OK, even preferable, to slow down, to take one’s time, to enjoy the journey. Consequently, I look forward to my thirty minutes’ practice every evening, and I am making progress. Highly recommended.

reviews.reviewer_name: College Guy trying to be helpful :)
reviews.title: UPDATED 3/6/2022: READ ME! Not as bad as people say! people just love to complain.
reviews.body: READ THIS IF YOU'RE CONSIDERING BUYING THIS GUITAR!!! I bought this used - very good for 45 bucks about a year ago. I probably would not pay full price, as much as I love it. That being said, IT IS NOT JUNK GIVE IT TIME! I swear half the people leaving negative reviews have no idea how guitars work. I am a full grown adult guitar player, and I've been playing since high school. I'm in college now, and I needed something small and light to travel with. I DON'T USE THIS AS MY EVERYDAY GUITAR! I reach for this guy if I'm messing around with chords, my fingers hurt from my metal strings, or I'm just trying to relax. It's great to practice on, but not so much if you're trying to actually play in front of people. Nylons aren't meant to be used like metal stringed acoustics, they're a separate instrument! It still works for that purpose, though, you can play the same exact songs and chords. If you tune it properly it gets the job done. Great for my college dorm or throwing in the car for a camping trip cus it's super light. Great to practice on when I don't feel like lugging my full sized acoustic around. This is a decent product for the price I PAID. Being a nylon string guitar, you have to stretch the strings and tune it quite a bit (2-4 days is recommended for the strings to settle - watch a youtube tutorial on how to do it) Furthermore, the plastic strings that everyone complains about are standard on a nylon. Heck, the C40 from Yamaha, well established nylon, has the same type (but higher quality, I bet) if I recall. They do go out of tune pretty frequently, especially at the start, but it's not even that much - just retune them! The tuner works well for me, but if you don't like it, just get an app like GuitarTuna. Now, for the guitar itself, it's what I expected when I bought it for 45 bucks, barely even damaged since I got a higher quality used (or less damaged I guess) version, and I have to say, it has really grown on me. Guitars are instruments, not toys. You can't give it to a kid and expect them to learn the ins and outs. If you really want them to learn guitar, buy them a cheap acoustic like a rogue or Yamaha, a C40 is a great nylon but you could also get them a metal string, and get them lessons! Find a music store near you, it might be a bit pricey but it's the best way to learn. Originally I recommended swapping the strings, but it's not worth it to be honest. I got it back in 2021 for 45 USD used, and I love it for what I use it for. If you're dead-set on a cheap starter guitar, or you want an affordable spare, grab this but follow my advice. If you really want to learn, shell out the extra money and buy a tried and true brand. For the full price, 80 bucks is not worth it. Get a rogue for that money. Anyway, that's my rant, hope this helps! (I even bumped my review up from 4 to 5 stars - when I first wrote it, it was 1 star because I didn't understand stretching the nylon strings - IT TAKES TIME! but I genuinely love this thing!) Enjoy!
