reviews.title: Met all hopes-- Except ONE
reviews.body: I was hoping this set would be a decent guitar, but didn't really expect it to be decently made (for what it is... a youth guitar). But... the neck is perfectly straight. There's not a blemish on it. There were picks, gig bag, a pipe tuner and-- some surprise here-- an unadvertised extra set of strings. I would rate this 5 stars for "what it is"... a very low cost starter guitar. But I rate it 4 stars for a couple of general flaws: 1) The frets are not metal. They are molded into the guitar neck and PAINTED gold. That's a real shame, but for a starter guitar at this price not a deal-killer. It's for this reason along I give it 4 rather than 5 stars. 2) The gig bag is minimal of course. But the zipper broke the first time I used it. No padding, zero quality. It's meant to carry the guitar, nothing else. Had the zipper not broken it would have been fine and what is expected, but a gig bag with a broken zipper isn't of much use. I guess one can always resort to safety pins or velcro patches. Specs: * The guitar measures 31 inches from tail to tip of head, plus the strap peg on the end (yes, it has a strap peg!). Lower body is 11.5 inches wide x 2.75 inches deep. Nut is 1.5 inches wide. Nut to 18th fret is 12.25 inches. Basically-- a mid-size travel guitar similar in size to the Yamaha 6-string "Guitalele". Sound however, is quite "guitar". * The top is good-quality laminate with a resonant tone-- no dead spots (which is far more than I expected). It's not a spruce top, but the laminate is plenty resonant (far more so than many travel guitars) and has excellent sound-- amazingly so for an instrument of this class. * Tuning pegs are standard 3-to-a-set sidewinders, expected on this type of guitar. * The strap attaches to an end peg and is tie-on at the neck. STRING NOTE: I've noticed several of the negative reviews here refer to the guitar "not tuning", strings breaking, action too high, etc. While the action was pretty decent on mine, it's very common for even a quality guitar to arrive with less than desirable action (ask any guitar store). Action is fairly easy to correct by filing the bridge piece down (which is why it's detachable). When one tunes a steel-string guitar, it is imperative to tune it slowly, in steps, and allow the strings time to stretch over a period of 3-4 days. If one tries to tune it quickly strings will undoubtedly break, even on top-of-the-line guitars. Expecting a guitar to "hold a tune" when initially strung is unreasonable. All strings stretch out of tune until they hit their proper tension. Any experienced guitar player is aware of these things-- with all guitars and all brands of strings. SWITCH TO NYLON. Although this guitar comes with steel strings (even an extra set) I think it would be a shame to put that kind of tension on a neck that will most likely warp under such pressure. Despite the low cost I like an instrument to last-- and I think this will last for some time if one uses nylon strings. Because of the resonance you will still get an excellent tone. For protection, putting this in the gig bag and then retaining the triangular box for car trips can offer considerable protection (after all, the box survived shipping, yup?). There's no need to buy an expensive padded gig bag or hard shell case for a guitar that costs less than a tank of gas. Were it not for the wooden frets I'd give this guitar 5 stars. But that is a corner-cut that I don't find acceptable in anything but a plastic instrument found in the toy aisle. At the very least they could have used glued-on metal frets. Other than that, it's a decent guitar and once nylon strings are added, should work fine for a first-year student or child. It's well-worth the purchase and at least is a functional, nice-sounding guitar with decent action. I disagree with the concept of "buy a cheap guitar to see if a child will stick with it". Cheap guitars usually don't play well and so naturally the child won't like it (fortunately, this one plays pretty well). But my credo: pay more and buy a good guitar to start with (there are plenty for under $200) and then as with all things, require the child to "stick with it". No one ever regrets having learned to play an instrument, even though they may-- as kids do-- resist practice. That's where parents come in and gently guide and encourage. Go with quality. But if you can't afford or don't want to buy a quality instrument, this one will certainly suffice. It's decent.

reviews.title: A Very Nice Guitar for this Price Range
reviews.body: The guitar arrived in perfect condition (7-16-2024) packed in its gig bag and cardboard box. I chose the Cedar top. My first impression was that the finish is beautiful. I could not find a blemish or defect anywhere. The neck is arrow straight and the set up is ok; action is just a little high (about 5 mm) at the 12th fret. The fretboard top and edges are very smooth. I only found one sharp fret wire end-- on the 14th fret. The strings are ok, not the greatest. The tone is good. The gig bag has a some padding to protect the guitar if you carry it around in your car. I think it would cost close to $30 to buy it separately. The tuner is very good; I keep it clipped on the headstock since nylon strings need frequent tuning in the first couple weeks of use. The capo is "so-so", really not that great. If you use a capo a lot you might need a better one. I would say the same for the foot rest; its a little unstable but useable.. All in all, the accessory package is a really good deal! My only other complaint is that they used a black stain on the Bridge which rubbed off on the included cleaning cloth. I really had to rub it a lot to get all the stain out. I think they also used a black stain on the fretboard but it doesn't seem to rub off. I won't hesitate to give it 5 stars because it is really beautiful, sounds good, and is a great value at $169.

reviews.title: Staying in tune for almost a year
reviews.body: It will be a year next month, since I got this guitar. I average 30 minutes a day fingerstyle play. I was really pleased with the construction. The frets were well done. Only one was a little high. I did have to adjust the truss rod to eliminate some buzz on the 6th string at the 3rd fret. 3 strings required rewinding. I am really surprised how well it stays in tune. After the first week, the strings settled and has only required tuning after humidity changes in my area. The body of the guitar is well made and all the fit and finish is really quite beautiful. I work with wood as part of my trade, and an ill fitting piece stands out. This guitar is lovely and the tones are clear and strong. The sound comes out true and each open string pluck is it's own musical piece. I highly recommend this guitar!

reviews.title: Worth the purchase
reviews.body: Very pleased with this guitar. Tone is nice. Action is low (a consistent height of strings above frets) which makes the pressing of nylon strings comfortable. The action is adjustable since it has a truss rod and included allen wrench but I don't need to adjust it. Also included is a guitar case, clip-on tuner, capo, picks, extra strings, strap, cleaning cloth, and a footstool. I was surprised to see how accurate the tuner is and how easily I could tune the guitar. More surprisingly, I'm pleased with how long the guitar stays in tune. The tuner was not just for guitars. It is for chromatic, guitar, bass, violin, and Ukulele tuning. I’ve used it to tune my B-flat trumpet. Pitch range is listed at 440Hz. If you plan to hang the guitar on a wall, the width of the headstock above the nut is slightly over 2 in, so the first wall hanger I got did not fit. I ended up purchasing the Onmiwod black walnut wall hanger. It has a hook opening of 2.13 in. It works great and was easy to install.

reviews.title: Why did they raise the price?
reviews.body: I am going back to guitar after a long absence. This had twoo things you don't usually find in a less expensive guitar, a solid top and a bone nut and saddle. Both of these qualitied should improve the tone. It comes with a lot of extras including a nicely made soft case. One of the tuning peg handles was partially broken but that did not effect the guitar. I was surprised how the supplied strings maintained their tune after a couple of days. It's a nice looking guitar and seems very well made tho' I haven't heard of the brand before. I was disappointed that the punticello did not work on the 7th fret. Might be the strings. There is a slight buzz in the D string. I am frankly afraid to play around with the truss rod to adjust the action. Figured I would let the guitar "break in." Also, I am trying to get back a familiarity with a guitar so I can discover what is me and what is the guitar. Kind of disturbed at the number of people who got the guitar for free. I had to order the guitar twice because the first time it never arrived. Overall, even with the price rise, I would say it's worth the money especially as a beginner guitar.

reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised
reviews.body: I've owned several different classical guitars ranging from $150 "cheapos" up to mid-level student guitars ( Yairi CY118 and Takamini Hirade ). I can say this is a very nice guitar for what I paid for it! I've owned a couple of inexpensive Yamahas and I want to say my last model was a c40 if memory serves me and this is every bit as nice and honestly a little bit nicer than that one. Fit and finish are good, the frets are finished well with no sharp edges and it has a nice laquer job. It has a warm and balanced tone and while not the loudest guitar it's loud enough for practicing or playing in small groups if you have decent acoustics in the room. Actions nice and low over the first fret and a tad high over the 12th fret but interestingly enough its not difficult at all to play, the strings are very easy to push down and I'm not going to even tamper with it, I usually shave down my saddles to lower the action but this one won't be needing it. I went ahead and ordered a set of diadario ej45s but honestly the strings that came with it sound pretty darn good so I'm not in a hurry to change them out. It also came with the bag tuner, footrest etc. normally I don't care about stuff like that but the accessories seem like decent quality and I will use them. Overall for the price you really can't beat this instrument and if you're trying to decide between something like this or one of the Yamahas for an inexpensive guitar or for a student don't be afraid to give this one a shot, I don't think you'll be disappointed. Hope this helps.

reviews.title: You need to consider these strings!
reviews.body: Just wanted to write a quick review on these strings! I'm a huge fan of Yamaha Guitars in general, and recently bought a new FG800 in matte finish. Wonderful sound, as I believe is has a bit more open sound without the thick poly finish. Upon changing the strings to my go to, Elixir Nano PB lights, I noticed that the guitar lost a lot of what I liked about its initial sound. I searched the web and found that these are the original strings from Yamaha, and that they are coated as well. I bought a set and after installation, there's that wonderful sound again. I next swapped out the strings on my Guild DS240 sloped shoulder, and again a much improved sound! I know sound is subjective, so here's my take. These strings would be great for a player that is looking for a less high and brassy sound. These would be a combination of an Elixir and a Martin Retro string to my ears. More of an emphasis in the mids to lows, and less on the top end. The strings seem to last a long time and have a great feel to them. Will definitely be buying more.

reviews.title: I'm Impressed...
reviews.body: There is NOTHING about this stand that I dislike. I already plan to buy another one next month to put in my home studio. This one sits out by the amp and pedal board. So, obviously, the pictures show that I do not have a guitar on this particular guitar stand. That is the Korg RK100-S2 keytar. And it is a pain in the butt to place on a stand. It's odd shape makes it unstable, and the power on/off switch is right there between the two forks. Along with audio in jacks, the MIDI out, the USB port and a gain switch for a microphone. I have never heard of the CAHAYA music company before, and I wasn't sure if I wanted to get the stand for that reason alone. But, for the price, I figured that I could just leave it on the curb if it didn't work out. My main concern was needing the neck forks to be offset so much (as can be seen in the picture). I've had other stands (much more expensive) that had a kind of tongue in groove system that didn't let the neck rotate at all. That was my main concern. As you can see, no matter how screwy a position you need that neck fork to be, it can accommodate. I did have to make a slight alteration to the base forks. Again, see the picture. I used a couple of zip ties to pinch the ends of the base forks together approximately 1/2 inch. The pictures and dimensions provided by the company were at the top of the page were correct. What I didn't take into account was that my strap lock takes up about 1 inch of the bottom of the keytar. The instrument still rested easily on the base, but just barely. So I did this just to be safe. The rubber on the forks seems to be the standard stuff you will find on a lot of lower to mid-range stands. I definitely like the padding that you can find on the higher tier stands from Gator and On Stage better, but those stands come at a premium, and wouldn't have held this instrument well anyway. My concern is that this type of rubber gets tacky when it's hot, and that MIGHT damage the finish of a really nice instrument. Time will tell if it damages the finish of THIS really nice instrument, but it doesn't feel tacky at the moment, and the keytar is super stable when resting on it. Assembly was a breeze. I didn't even look at the instructions. Although, I did notice that there were both words and illustrations for anybody that needs a little help. The neck hinge is secured with a nut and bolt. And that is nice, because even some of the $80+ stands just have a squeeze kind of grip that is tight and stable, but also can be easily collapsed if hit at the right (or completely wrong) time! As for the base forks, they also secure with a nut and bolt, but there are also (2) two washers provided that allow you to tighten the base on really well, but still allows the forks to rotate into a self-leveling position when you place your instrument on it. Honestly, with the exception that I wish it had a better quality foam rubber padding, this might just be the most well engineered guitar stand that I have ever owned. It is certainly the most versatile.
reviews.body_en: There is NOTHING about this stand that I dislike. I already plan to buy another one next month to put in my home studio. This one sits out by the amp and pedal board. So, obviously, the pictures show that I do not have a guitar on this particular guitar stand. That is the Korg RK100-S2 keytar. And it is a pain in the butt to place on a stand. It's odd shape makes it unstable, and the power on/off switch is right there between the two forks. Along with audio in jacks, the MIDI out, the USB port and a gain switch for a microphone. I have never heard of the CAHAYA music company before, and I wasn't sure if I wanted to get the stand for that reason alone. But, for the price, I figured that I could just leave it on the curb if it didn't work out. My main concern was needing the neck forks to be offset so much (as can be seen in the picture). I've had other stands (much more expensive) that had a kind of tongue in groove system that didn't let the neck rotate at all. That was my main concern. As you can see, no matter how screwy a position you need that neck fork to be, it can accommodate. I did have to make a slight alteration to the base forks. Again, see the picture. I used a couple of zip ties to pinch the ends of the base forks together approximately 1/2 inch. The pictures and dimensions provided by the company were at the top of the page were correct. What I didn't take into account was that my strap lock takes up about 1 inch of the bottom of the keytar. The instrument still rested easily on the base, but just barely. So I did this just to be safe. The rubber on the forks seems to be the standard stuff you will find on a lot of lower to mid-range stands. I definitely like the padding that you can find on the higher tier stands from Gator and On Stage better, but those stands come at a premium, and wouldn't have held this instrument well anyway. My concern is that this type of rubber gets tacky when it's hot, and that MIGHT damage the finish of a really nice instrument. Time will tell if it damages the finish of THIS really nice instrument, but it doesn't feel tacky at the moment, and the keytar is super stable when resting on it. Assembly was a breeze. I didn't even look at the instructions. Although, I did notice that there were both words and illustrations for anybody that needs a little help. The neck hinge is secured with a nut and bolt. And that is nice, because even some of the $80+ stands just have a squeeze kind of grip that is tight and stable, but also can be easily collapsed if hit at the right (or completely wrong) time! As for the base forks, they also secure with a nut and bolt, but there are also (2) two washers provided that allow you to tighten the base on really well, but still allows the forks to rotate into a self-leveling position when you place your instrument on it. Honestly, with the exception that I wish it had a better quality foam rubber padding, this might just be the most well engineered guitar stand that I have ever owned. It is certainly the most versatile.

reviews.title: Decent quality at a great price.
reviews.body: This review covers two CAHAYA products: - 5 in 1 Dual Use Sheet Music Stand - Guitar Stand Floor Universal I bought them together, use them together, and have similar feedback on them, so am cross-posting this review for both products. I am an amateur, non-gigging player and have no need of (and cannot afford!) professional quality stands. However, I am tired of purchasing lower-end products that are poorly-designed and poorly manufactured using inferior materials. CAHAYA has hit the sweet spot offering decent quality stands at affordable prices. This music stand came as part of a kit including a desktop adaptor, travel bag, music clip, and sheet music folder. Personally I have little use for the folder, but it's a nice touch to include it. The desktop adaptor and clip work well when you need them. The bag is great and I use it whenever I need to quickly vacate the family room for visitors. It even accommodates my CAHAYA guitar stand. Everything (except the sheet music folder) breaks down quickly and goes into the bag in about a minute. The most important piece--the music stand itself--is well-designed and well-manufactured. Most important for me is that it easily accommodates thick three-ring binders full of music. It adjusts to any height I need, whether sitting or standing. For daily, same-location amateur use, this music stand kit is a bargain. If you expect to break it down, pack it up, throw it in a vehicle and reassemble it several times a week, you should probably go more high-end. (But if you just don't have the budget to do so, this kit can probably survive some length of pro service as long as you don't abuse it ) The CAHAYA Universal Floor Guitar Stand is similar to the music stand in terms of materials, reliability, and value: an absolute bargain for a single-location amateur. If you expect to set it up in different venues every week where it might get knocked over by a drummer stumbling toward his or her kit or by a drunk audience member, you should probably go more high-end. But this stand is light years better than some of the products that are just $10 cheaper. Some people complain that it holds the guitar too high, making it too unsteady. I was a little concerned about this at first, but I use it for a relatively heavy bass, and have never had a problem. In fact, the cradle appears to be high to accommodate the adjustable tripod legs, so it was designed this way for a reason. My only minor complaint is that you need to completely remove bolts, knobs, nuts, and washers when fully collapsing the stand. If you expect to be doing this a lot, there's a good chance you're going to drop and lose a piece at some point. Otherwise, this stand is a great solution for anybody on a budget that won't be abusing their equipment.

reviews.title: Great guitar stand! Highly recommended ....

If you've ever put put a guitar on a stand and had it tilt sideways because of the cradle or not enough support from behind then you know what I'm talking about. The CAHAYA stand is very well made, has great padding, is very stable and would be hard to knock over. The added safety buckle is a nice touch. This stand does a great job of securely holding my electric Fender Loog in place (especially after I pushed the cradle arms a little closer together. If you're a gigging musician, this would be a decent stand to have; it's portable enough and not overly heavy. For home, studio or school use, it's great! For the money (I paid $18.00), I definitely recommend this stand over the other options I've seen online and purchased in the past.

reviews.title: No reason NOT to get this guitar!
reviews.body: I received this guitar just 2 days ago. I can honestly say it's the best guitar I've ever played, although I 've never played a Martin or any other high-priced name. I wanted a guitar that has a full sound but isn't heavy like my electric Firefly. Let me break down what I like. Playability: The fingerboard is very smooth, no high frets, and ample space to play chords I hadn't played before. Happy I can play Classical Gas for the first time in about 15 years. The neck setting is perfect for me. RESONANCE: I have the Washburn hanging on my wall. I've been randomly checking the tuning as I walk by. Pleasantly discovered that the notes will "ring" for a few seconds as I leave the room. When I play the guitar, I hear strings that had always seemed muffled before.Great to hear full chords! ELECTRONICS: The tuner works easily. Just be sure to remove the plastic around the battery. The equalizer is something I'm playing with. Right now, everything is set at halfway on the dials. TUNING: Easy, smooth and holds the tuning fairly well for a new guitar. FINISH: This is a beautiful guitar that is both colorful and well finished. I only found one small clear coat blemish near the strap peg. It's nothing to get excited about. Overall, I am glad I selected this guitar. It will be great for gigs and open mics.

reviews.title: Excellent guitar and kit for a beginner, I highly recommend!
reviews.body: This is an excellent guitar, and the kit accessories round it out to a full set proper for the ideal beginner experience. I am so impressed! I am an experienced classical guitarist and I chose this for my 7 year old daughter's birthday. I felt pretty confident that the item description hit all the important points. It was well packed and arrived safe and sound. Once she opened it and we checked it all out, I was VERY happy (and so was she! this was a WOW gift). The quality of the guitar itself is excellent for a beginner. Nylon strings mean that the fingers won't be in pain, which can make a new player not want to continue practicing. This is so user friendly. It was easy to accurately tune the strings with the included tuner. (You will find that you need to tune it frequently, especially at first, which is normal). The chord chart is great, the strap, capo, picks, additional strings and gig bag are all fantastic. Getting a full kit like this is great because even a beginner needs to see the full picture of what's possible with their new instrument, and of course the gig bag means that the guitar is protected. MAJOR gift value, excellent all the way around. Another fun little part to this gift: the box that it comes in was literally taller than her, which made for some really hysterical pictures and honestly just added to the birthday fun. Most importantly, she loves the guitar. As a musician, I can say there's really nothing like getting your first proper instrument and this certainly delivered that moment for her. THANK YOU!!
